'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== ===Protection - Counterattack=== *You can protect your target from '''one''' attack during the {{A|Night}} and counterattack their attacker. You and the attacker both be dealt an indirect {{A|Powerful Attack}} by you, and will die unless either of you are healed. If multiple killers attack your target, you will die and kill one, but the other will survive and attack your target. At the same time, your target can still be protected by other {{A|Town Protective}} roles. **Your cause of death would be stated as "He/She died guarding someone." The person you kill will have the death message "He/She was killed by a {{A|Bodyguard}}." *You will counter an attack made by a {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Vampire Hunter}} (when your protected target is a {{A|Vampire}}), {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Mafioso}}, {{A|Vampire}} (attacking or converting), {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}}, {{A|Coven Leader}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}}), {{A|Potion Master}}, {{A|Medusa}} (visiting), {{A|Poisoner}} (initial visit), {{A|Pestilence}}, a {{A|Pirate}} (who wins their duel), and any {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, excluding the {{A|Arsonist}}. **If your target is attacked by the {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}} or an attacking zombie, the {{A|Necromancer}} will receive a notification that a {{A|Bodyguard}} countered their ghoul/minion. However, you will be killed protecting your target while the {{A|Necromancer}} will live. **If your target is a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Pirate}} who was attacked from visiting a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}}, you will attack the {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} and save your target. **The {{A|Coven Leader}} will only attack with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, so you will not protect your target from being {{A|Controlled}} on the first two {{A|nights}}. **Your protection acts as a one-use {{A|Powerful Defense}} for your target. That means if a fully-powered {{A|Juggernaut}} attacks your target, you and your target will die, as well as anyone who happened to visit your target that {{A|night}}. [[File:Bodyguard Poisoner protection.png|thumb|350px|The message a player receives if a {{A|Bodyguard}} protects them from the {{A|Poisoner's}} ability.]] *{{A|Pestilence}} will not be killed by your counterattack. You will die and they will survive, but your target will still live. *You cannot counter or protect your target from attacks made by the {{A|Jailor}}, the {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Town Protectives}}, an {{A|Ambusher}}, the {{A|Medusa}} (gazing at home), the {{A|Hex Master}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, and {{A|Jesters}}. *If you guard the {{A|Jailor}} and they jail an incautious {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} but they do not execute them, you will attack the {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} and save the {{A|Jailor}}. The {{A|Powerful Defense}} given in jail will '''not '''protect them from a {{A|Bodyguard's}} attack. *If there are multiple {{A|Bodyguards}} protecting the same target, the {{A|Bodyguard}} who joined the lobby first will counterattack. If there are multiple attackers, each {{A|Bodyguard}} will take out a separate attacker.  *A {{A|Bodyguard}} cannot save another {{A|Bodyguard}} who is dying to save their target. *You cannot have a {{A|Lover}} or be the {{A|VIP}} due to being a passively suicidal role. ===Bulletproof Vest=== *If you target yourself, you will use your bulletproof vest, gaining a temporary {{A|Basic Defense}}. *You may only do this once per game. *Your vest does not act like a guard; you will not counterattack any attackers. *If you use a bulletproof vest and get transported, you will still use your bulletproof vest. *If you are {{A|Controlled}} or transported into yourself, you will '''not''' use your bulletproof vest. *You will receive a message stating: "You were attacked but your bulletproof vest saved you!" if you successfully vest on the {{A|night}} that you are attacked. ===Why did my target still die?=== *You will '''not''' be able to protect your target in the following situations: **Your target was killed by the {{A|Veteran}} while on alert. **Your target was another {{A|Bodyguard}} who died in a counterattack. ***You can protect another {{A|Bodyguard}} from being attacked by a killer, but not their counterattack. Only {{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Potion Masters}}, {{A|Crusaders}}, and {{A|Guardian Angels}} can prevent a {{A|Bodyguard}} from dying in a counterattack, since those roles directly give their target {{A|Powerful Defense}} from all attacks. **Your target committed suicide (by leaving the game). **Your target was haunted by a {{A|Jester}}. **Your target was a {{A|Vigilante}} who committed suicide over shooting a {{A|Town}} member the previous {{A|Night}}. **Your target was attacked by an {{A|Ambusher}} or {{A|Crusader}}. **Your target visited the {{A|Medusa}} using a {{A|Stone Gaze}}. **Your target was attacked by another {{A|Bodyguard}}. **Your target was attacked by a {{A|Trap}}. **Your target was killed by an {{A|Arsonist's}} ignition. **Your target was killed as a result of the {{A|Hex Master's}} Final {{A|Hex}} (in which case, you would die as well). **The target was jailed and/or executed by the {{A|Jailor}}. ***If a {{A|Werewolf}} attacks a jailed target and you guard them, you will be mauled. The {{A|Werewolf}} will survive. **Your target died to {{A|Poison}}. **Your target was attacked by a {{A|Hex Master}} who wields the {{A|Necronomicon}}. **Your target was directly attacked by a fully powered {{A|Juggernaut}} (contrary to popular belief, you will not kill the {{A|Juggernaut}}). **Your target died from a broken heart in [[Game_Modes_-_Coven#Coven_Lovers|Lovers Mode]]. **Your target visited the target of a role with rampage (could be {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, or {{A|Pestilence}}). **'''Multiple''' killing roles attacked the target (you counterattack only one of them, so your target died). **If none of the above apply, yet your target still dies, at least one of the following may have occurred: ***You were {{A|Controlled}} by a {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Coven Leader}} to visit a different target. You would have received a message. ***You were [[Role block|role blocked]] by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}}. You would have received a message. ***Your target was transported with another target because of a {{A|Transporter}}. You will '''not''' know if this happens. *A {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Potion Master}} or a {{A|Guardian Angel}} can prevent you or the attacker from dying. **Being healed while counterattacking does '''not''' allow you to counter more than one attack on your target. *If a {{A|Werewolf}} attacks your target directly, you will attack the {{A|Werewolf}} but only save your own target from death. **You will only attack the {{A|Werewolf}} if your target was attacked directly by them or they visited them as a roleblocking role. *{{A|Bodyguards}} are unable to save a player from being {{A|Doused}} or ignited. ==Strategy== *On the first {{A|night}}, it is very unlikely that you will be able to do anything. Thus, it is a good idea to guard anyone who asks for "TP/LO" since if a {{A|Lookout}} watches said player, they can prove your innocence later. **Be wary when doing this though, as some {{A|Veterans}} use this to bait in evils. *The {{A|Bodyguard's}} counterattack pierces through Basic defense when someone attacks the person you guard at {{A|night}}. With this in mind, a {{A|Bodyguard}} can be critical in taking down a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Werewolf}}. *If you are attacked but your bulletproof vest saved you, do not publicly announce it because you will most likely be attacked the next {{A|night}} and there might not be a {{A|Doctor}} or a {{A|Lookout}} to be on you. Announce it to confirmed {{A|Townies}} via whispers and try to act like an {{A|Executioner}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role to avoid being targeted again. **This might backfire as {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles have {{A|Death Notes}} and might out you for being immune. This may bring suspicion on you and you might be Hanged. *The {{A|Bodyguard}} is unlike the {{A|Crusader}} in that it will only counterattack attackers, not visitors in general. Therefore, you should guard every {{A|night}}. **The only exception would be a game with at least one {{A|Vampire Hunter}} and one or more {{A|Vampires}} since you will kill attacking {{A|Vampire Hunters}}. *The {{A|Mayor}} is your priority (especially in a non-{{A|Coven}} game, as there are no other {{A|Town Protective}} roles), as only you and the {{A|Trapper}} can save them from an attack. After being revealed, they cannot be healed by {{A|Doctors}} and are extremely dangerous to killing roles, making them a primary target. Keep in mind evil roles may try to kill you first, then target the {{A|Mayor}}. **Some {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killings}} may not attempt attacking a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, so you could guard someone else, increasing the chance you take down an evil. This could be seen as gamethrowing by some people though, so be careful. *If the {{A|Mafia}} seems to be attacking people with certain names, try protecting a player with a similar name. **Likewise, if the {{A|Mafia}} are attacking in a pattern, protect a player who would be next on their hit list. **Other roles that are usually attacked if known are the {{A|Jailor}} and confirmed {{A|Town Investigative}} roles. **The defense you give your target blocks {{A|Pestilence's}} attacks, which can be used to stall someone's death. This does not kill {{A|Pestilence}}, however. *In {{A|All Any}}, you can claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} on {{A|Day 1}}, use your bulletproof vest the same {{A|Night}}, and then secretly {{A|Guard}} others. This allows for you to secretly protect others while not being a target yourself. **However, this can backfire if an {{A|Investigator}} investigates. They may assume that you are the {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Godfather}} pretending to be a {{A|Survivor}}. **The {{A|Town}} may also simply hang you because they do not need {{A|Survivors}} to win. *If you have no leads (this applies especially on {{A|Day 2}}), {{A|Guard}} the first person who talks that {{A|Day}}. Since evil roles tend to be quiet, the person you guard will most likely be a {{A|Townie}}. **Take caution doing so, as that person may be a {{A|Veteran}} or a {{A|Medusa}} baiting people. **Some {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}} also can talk first in the {{A|Day}} to act like a {{A|Townie}}. *Remember that you will become the priority of most killing roles if you are revealed, since you can kill them. Having a {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Doctor}}, a {{A|Lookout}} or even another {{A|Bodyguard}} help you is a wise idea. *Since a {{A|Werewolf}} and an {{A|Arsonist}} can go through your bulletproof vest and are at the top of your priority list, try the best you can to get them hanged. *Finding and protecting other {{A|Town Protectives}} while they guard you can prove very useful later on. If any killing roles attack your target, you will take them down. If the person you protect is a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Crusader}}, you can repeatedly protect each other no matter what you are attacked by. **Roles that mess with visits (ex. {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Witch}}), {{A|Astral}} {{A|Hex Masters}}, {{A|Ambushers}}, killing roles being healed, {{A|Arsonists}} igniting, (etc.) can disrupt this. *If you protect a player that was killed indirectly by a rampage attack, but they show up as a non-visiting role (such as a {{A|Medium}}), then that player was most likely forged by a {{A|Forger}}, and you should be wary of their {{A|Last Will}} (unless a {{A|Witch}} interferes). *It is better to prioritize trying to kill roles with defense such as a {{A|Serial Killer}}, since a {{A|Bodyguard}} killing a {{A|Mafioso}} is the equivalent to the {{A|Mafioso}} shooting the {{A|Bodyguard}} and the {{A|Bodyguard}} being a {{A|Vigilante}} shooting the {{A|Mafioso}}. Taking advantage that the {{A|Bodyguard}} deals {{A|Powerful Attacks}} is a good idea. *Another useful strategy is getting a {{A|Doctor}} to heal you while you protect them. This way, if you die protecting the {{A|Doctor}}, you will live (as they healed you). This keeps both of you alive for a nearly unbreakable chain. However, a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Pirate}} or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} can break the chain, and the chain can be broken if two attackers attack the {{A|Doctor}}, as you only can save them from one attack. **Note that this also makes the {{A|Doctor}} very susceptible to an {{A|Ambusher}} who can set up an ambush on you. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{BodyguardAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{BodyguardMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.3.2}}, {{A|Bodyguards}} were able to defend from and kill an {{A|Arsonist}} visiting their target. *There used to be a bug where the {{A|Werewolf}} would not be counter-attacked by a {{A|Bodyguard}} while jailed on a {{A|Full Moon}}. *{{A|Bodyguard}} used to be known as "BodyGuard" in-game, however this was changed. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Bodyguard's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Bodyguard.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Bodyguard's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Bodyguard Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **{{A|Werewolves}} can now be killed by a {{A|Bodyguard}} while {{A|Jailed}} when they attack the {{A|Jailor}}. **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **{{A|Arsonists}} can no longer die to a {{A|Bodyguard}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Bodyguard}} now only protects from direct attacks. **{{A|Vampires}} can no longer convert through a used vest. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Garde du corps]] [[is:Lífvörður]] [[ru:Телохранитель]] [[Category:Town Protective roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]] [[Category:Killing roles]]

Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets!}} {{Story}}}[[File:RoleIcon Doctor 2.png|thumb|100x100px|The icon that appears on the {{A|Doctor's}} Ability Coin]] ==Mechanics== ===Healing your target=== You will heal '''all''' attacks on your target caused by {{A|Town Protectives}}, a {{A|Town Killing}} role (except the {{A|Jailor}}), any {{A|Mafia Killing}} role, {{A|Serial Killers}}, {{A|Vampires}}, a {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Medusa}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, {{A|Coven Leader}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}}), {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}}, {{A|Hex Master}} ({{A|Astral}} attack), {{A|Poisoner}} (without the {{A|Necronomicon}}), a {{A|Pirate}}, and a {{A|Juggernaut}} (before their third kill). *You can heal a {{A|Bodyguard}} who was supposed to die protecting someone. This makes it so only the attacker dies. This also applies if the attacker is healed and the {{A|Bodyguard}} is not. *If you heal someone who is visited by a {{A|Werewolf}}, you will die but your target will remain alive. *You will prevent both a conversion and an attack from a {{A|Vampire}}. *If you successfully heal a target who was attacked that {{A|night}}, you will receive a message stating: "Your target was attacked last {{A|night}}!" **Your target will receive a message stating: "You were attacked but someone nursed you back to health!" ***If you {{A|Self Heal}} on the {{A|night}} you are attacked, you will receive the message above. *Healing someone gives them temporary {{A|Powerful Defense}}, so the attacker will receive an immunity message. *You can use your {{A|Self Heal}} to cure yourself of {{A|Poison}} as long as the {{A|Poisoner}} did not possess the {{A|Necronomicon}} at the time you were {{A|Poisoned}}. You will get the message, “You were cured of poison!” You '''cannot''': *Remove {{A|Poison}} from anyone if the {{A|Poisoner}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}. *Save anyone that has been attacked by an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} (a fully-powered up {{A|Juggernaut}}, an {{A|Arsonist's}} ignition, a {{A|Hex Master's}} final {{A|hex}}, a {{A|Jester's}} haunt, or a {{A|Jailor's}} execution). *Prevent someone from dying of a broken heart in {{A|Lovers Mode}}. *Prevent someone from dying by suicide methods ({{A|Vigilante}} dying from guilt, a {{A|Jester}} haunt, or leaving the game). *Heal the {{A|Mayor}} once they reveal themselves, even if you are forced into targeting them. *Remove a {{A|Frame}}, {{A|douse}}, {{A|hex}}, or the {{A|plague}} from anyone (you can prevent people from dying to the basic attack delivered by the {{A|Hex Master}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, but the victim will still be {{A|hexed}}). ===Messages=== You will be notified if your target was attacked in any way, shape, or form. *You will receive only '''one''' message, no matter how many times your target was attacked. **Your target will receive a message about being healed (only if they were attacked). They will '''not''' receive additional messages if they were healed by multiple {{A|Doctors}}. ***If your target is attacked by multiple sources simultaneously, such as a {{A|Serial Killer}} and a {{A|Mafioso}}, they will receive the same number of messages as the number of killers that attacked them. *When the {{A|Werewolf}} and {{A|Mafioso}} attack you, it is ''possible'' to receive two "Your target was attacked last night!" messages if you {{A|Self Heal}}. This is a known bug. *You will still receive the message that your target was attacked even if they were protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}} or have {{A|Basic Defense}} or {{A|Powerful Defense}}. Your target will not be notified that they were healed by a {{A|Doctor}} if the {{A|Bodyguard}} saved them unless they were attacked by another attacker ({{A|Bodyguard}} only prevents one killer's attack). *You can heal a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Jailor}} and/or the {{A|Pirate}} who role blocked an incautious {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} (on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|nights}}). *You will '''not''' see that your target was attacked if they were attacked by a {{A|Bodyguard}}. This may be a bug. *You will '''not''' see that your target was attacked if they are a {{A|Vampire}} who was attacked by a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. This may be a bug as well. *If you cure someone from {{A|poison}}, you will '''not''' receive any message, while the player you cured receives one stating "You were cured of poison!". This may be a bug. *If someone is successfully healed, their attacker will receive the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.", which is the same as if they had attacked a role with {{A|Defense}}. **This was not the case before [[Version_History - Town of Salem|Version 3.2.4]]. ==Strategy== *'''Lay low, and avoid revealing your role unless completely necessary.''' You can use your ability to secretly protect someone from death while staying under the {{A|Mafia's}} radar. Don't say '''anything''' if you healed someone the previous {{A|night}}, or if they say something along the lines of, "''Thanks Doc!''" Even whispering to your target, while it might be tempting, can be dangerous, since the {{A|Mafia}} is usually smart enough to kill whoever [[Whisper|whispered]] to someone who was healed; generally, you should only [[whisper]] to your target if you believe they are a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} and are trying to pair up with them. *'''Keep your {{A|Self Heal}} for later in the game.''' There is little chance of the {{A|Mafia}} attacking you early in the game, especially if you haven't revealed your role. However, as the game goes on, it gradually becomes more necessary to reveal your role. If you have to reveal your role, it is recommended to use your {{A|Self Heal}} that {{A|night}}, as the {{A|Doctor}} is a nuisance to the {{A|Mafia}}, as well as the {{A|Serial Killer}}. *This should go without saying, but if somebody claims {{A|Poisoned}} while the {{A|Poisoner}} doesn't have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, you should always, '''''always, '''''heal them, unless you and the rest of the town are absolutely ''certain'' they are evil. Even if the person claiming hasn't proven themselves to be a {{A|Townie}} yet, the risk just isn't worth it. There is still a big chance they are in fact a {{A|Townie}}, especially early in the game, and if you ''don't'' heal them, your {{A|Doctor}} claim will fall under immediate suspicion, as you have no true way to prove yourself. *The most important basic strategy for a {{A|Doctor}} is to ''identify confirmed {{A|Townies}}'' so you can heal them, since a {{A|Doctor}} can also accidentally heal an evildoer, potentially saving them. As an added bonus, anyone who can be publicly identified as a {{A|Townie}} is more likely to be targeted by the {{A|Mafia}}. When you lack other ideas, people to heal include: **Anyone who has voted a member of the {{A|Mafia}} up to the stand, or who provided decisive evidence to hang a member of the {{A|Mafia}} (watch for bussing). **Anyone who has been confirmed via their abilities, such as a {{A|Vigilante}} shooting an evil. *Healing a {{A|Jailor}} allows them to jail any target without fear of the target being the {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} (however, if the {{A|Werewolf}} attacks the {{A|Jailor}}, you will be attacked as well. This being said, the {{A|Jailor}} will live, which may be more important than your survival depending on the scenario). *Two {{A|Doctors}} healing each other are very difficult to kill. This combo can only be stopped by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} (redirecting one {{A|Doctor's}} heal elsewhere), a {{A|Bootlegger}} (stopping one {{A|Doctor}} from healing the other), or attacking one with an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}. **This works in a similar way with {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Crusader}}, as the {{A|Crusader}} can protect you from roles that rampage while also potentially killing an evil role. *If your target was healed, and someone was killed by a {{A|Bodyguard}} the next morning, but no {{A|Bodyguard}} died, then you almost certainly healed the {{A|Bodyguard}}. Most of the time, you should immediately whisper to them, claim to be a {{A|Doctor}}, explain what happened, and ask them to cover you for the rest of the game while you heal them. This creates a nearly unstoppable team. *Healing a {{A|Bodyguard}} allows them to kill anyone who attacks their target without them dying until you are killed. This also allows you to indirectly provide indefinite protection to a {{A|Mayor}}, who you cannot heal directly, as long as you yourself are not attacked. *A {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Bodyguard}} pair that are constantly healing/[[Bodyguard (ToS)|protecting]] each other is almost impossible to destroy. This is similar to a {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Doctor}} pair or a {{A|Crusader}}/{{A|Crusader}} pair. A killer will have a 50-50 chance of either failing to kill or being killed themselves. As long as the {{A|Doctor}} is healing the {{A|Bodyguard}}, the {{A|Bodyguard}} will recover from every successful defense. **If a {{A|Jailor}} jails either one of the pair, the person not jailed will likely be exposed to attacks. If they use their {{A|Self Heal}}/vest, they can still survive the {{A|night}}. **A {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Pirate}} can break this defense chain by redirecting or role blocking one of the pair. **If multiple killers attack the {{A|Doctor}}, the {{A|Bodyguard}} will kill one but the remaining killer will kill the {{A|Doctor}}. **A {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Pestilence}} and an {{A|Ambusher}} are able to break this defense chain by simply targeting the {{A|Bodyguard}}. **The {{A|Hex Master}}, {{A|Arsonists}} and {{A|Jesters}} are able to break this defense chain due to not being affected by {{A|Bodyguards}}. *{{A|Transporters}} can usually confirm by posting a record of who they {{A|Transported}}, but healing them after they're confirmed doesn't make as much sense as other confirmed {{A|Townies}} since they'll usually be using their ability to protect themselves afterward (unless there's a confirmed {{A|Ambusher}}). *A common misconception of a good strategy is waiting before you heal anyone right away (on the first {{A|night}}). The argument goes that you could accidentally save an evil role or run into an unexpected {{A|Veteran}}. However, this looks very suspicious and you miss the opportunity to get a {{A|Lookout}} to confirm you (if they visited the same person), as well as the fact you are more likely to heal a {{A|Townie}}. Most {{A|Town Killing}} roles will also not be able to kill on the first night, making it even less likely that you're saving an evil role from death. *You will know if your target is attacked. This can indicate their innocence in a number of ways: **If there were no attacks from the {{A|Mafia}} that {{A|night}}, it means your target may have been attacked by the {{A|Mafia}}; aside from rare shenanigans of a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}}, that would mean they're not a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, since the {{A|Mafia}} can't directly attack themselves. **If the attack looks like it was from the {{A|Werewolf}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}}, it can indicate that your target wasn't that role (but, of course, they could still be part of the {{A|Mafia}}). It can be hard to figure out if you've saved your target from becoming a {{A|Vampire}}, but that's also another potential cause for the message (and the messages are indistinguishable). *If you seem to have healed your target from a {{A|Werewolf's}} attack, yet survived yourself, this means that they weren't the {{A|Werewolf's}} primary target; in other words, it means they're a visiting role and ''visited'' the {{A|Werewolf's}} target. If the {{A|Werewolf's}} target died to the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}} in this situation, and no member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} came up dead, then it's extremely likely you've actually saved an evil role! **Of course, if you save the {{A|Werewolf's}} primary target, you will die, but the person you healed will survive. This can backfire if the {{A|Werewolf}} stayed at home, as this will give the {{A|Werewolf}} an alibi if multiple people visit them. *If there aren't any confirmed {{A|Townies}} (most commonly in the early game), it might be useful to heal the most talkative players. These players are typically targeted by the {{A|Mafia}}, as they usually are an important role that is trying to figure out who the {{A|Mafia}} are. **However, if they are an alerted {{A|Veteran}}, and you healed them because they were baiting, you will die. It can also be smart to stay on a {{A|Veteran}} to help them save their alerts, where they can be crucial end-game in a 1v1 or so. *If someone you were healing dies anyway (and the cause is something you could have healed, not suicide or an {{A|Arsonist}}), it means one of two things has happened: **First, your target may have been {{A|Transported}}. This means that your heal was redirected on to someone else, and the attack was redirected onto your target. Note that this means that your target wasn't the one who the attacker intended to kill. You can try to confirm this by asking if anyone was {{A|Transported}}; if anyone speaks up, they were probably the real target of the attack. **And second, if you selected/changed your target ''just'' as the {{A|night}} ended, it may not have reached the server in time. This is especially true for low end computers. **You could also have been controlled and redirected onto another target or role-blocked, but it would be fairly obvious as you would have gotten a message. There is a very rare bug that the control message does not show up, though. *If you're being controlled by a {{A|Witch}} every {{A|night}}, take note if your target is healed (and write what {{A|night}} it happened in your {{A|Last Will}}). After the first {{A|night}}, a {{A|Witch}} is probably making you target them, so you may be able to identify them if they're later called out by an attacker as having a defense higher than said killer's attack value. **You can also use this to call out anyone the {{A|Witch}} could be using you to heal, as they would logically heal their allies. *If you are aware of a {{A|Witch}} in-game, be careful when stating you are the {{A|Doctor}}, as doing so gives the {{A|Witch}} Powerful Defense every {{A|night}}. Under no circumstances should you reveal that you are the {{A|Doctor}} unless you ask a {{A|Transporter}} to transport you or a {{A|Lookout}} to watch you in order to bust the {{A|Witch}}. **A similar thing can apply to when there is a {{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Necromancer}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{DoctorAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{DoctorMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to [[Version_History_- Town of Salem|Version 3.2.4]], attacking a healed person would not generate an immunity message. **The healed person would still get a message saying they were healed. *The {{A|Doctor}} is the only role in the game to gain {{A|Powerful Defense}} when using their self protection, meaning they can survive a direct {{A|Werewolf}} attack whereas a {{A|Serial Killer}} would die in the same situation. *The {{A|Doctor}} is currently the only {{A|Town Protective}} to harbor no attack whatsoever. *The Doctor is the only role known to have a chance to appear in every gamemode, Classic or Coven. ==History== *[[Version_History_-_Town_of_Salem|3.2.4]] **Temporary {{A|defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *[[Version_History_-_Town_of_Salem|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Doctor's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Doctor.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Doctor's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Doctor Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History_-_Town_of_Salem|2.3.2.9706]] **Revealed {{A|Mayors}} can no longer be healed by a {{A|Doctor}} if {{A|Transported}}. **Fixed an issue where if you were {{A|poisoned}}, healed, then {{A|poisoned}} again the next {{A|night}}, you wouldn't receive a message letting you know you were {{A|poisoned}}. **Fixed an issue where if you were attacked by {{A|Medusa}}, healed, but killed by a role with a higher {{A|attack}}, you would still show up as {{A|stoned}}. *[[Version_History_-_Town_of_Salem|Town of Salem Release]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Доктор]] [[Category:Town Protective roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

The {{A|Godfather}} requires a {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}, or {{A|Witch}} to be completed. ==Strategy== *As a {{A|Consigliere}}, you are a crucial target for the {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Neutral Killings}}, {{A|Vampires}}, and the {{A|Plaguebearer}}. This is because you are one of the most useful members of the {{A|Mafia}}, as you are able to determine the '''EXACT''' role of your investigated target. You can provide a massive amount of information very quickly, threatening other roles and heavily supporting {{A|Mafia}}. You are especially useful because you can provide leads for the {{A|Mafia's}} activities at {{A|night}}. *If an {{A|Investigator}} claims that you may be a {{A|Consigliere}}, show the {{A|Town}} a role that opposes them and get that person hanged (other than your {{A|Mafia}} friends). If you find a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, such as a {{A|Serial Killer}}, proclaiming yourself as an {{A|Investigator}} on the second {{A|day}} and Hanging the {{A|Serial Killer}} can be an excellent way to make the {{A|Town}} gain trust in you. Once proven, you can lead the {{A|Town}} in Hanging {{A|Neutrals}} while the {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Mafioso}} remove some troublesome {{A|Townies}}. **Keep in mind that this might not always fool the {{A|Town}}, since they would probably expect a {{A|Mafia}} member killed. Good {{A|Town}} members are likely to notice that you're only targeting {{A|Neutrals}} and no {{A|Mafia}}. You can counter this by simply asking to buss one of your {{A|Mafia}} members. *You can claim to be an {{A|Investigator}} (if there is a {{A|Janitor}} and you found an {{A|Investigator}}, it is a good idea to kill the {{A|Investigator}} and make the {{A|Janitor}} clean him so that you can claim you're an {{A|Investigator}} without any much suspicion for the first few {{A|days}}). Also, if you have found a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or even a {{A|Town}} role that could be bad (Eg., {{A|Doctor}} can also be a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Disguiser}} when investigated), you can ask them their role, claim your investigation message, and possibly even provide false information in order to make the {{A|Town}} lose trust in what they're saying to possibly get them Hanged. **Alternatively, you could feed your {{A|Godfather}} results and allow them to claim {{A|Investigator}}. This gives the {{A|Godfather}} a better chance of surviving "Vote for Role" as {{A|Bodyguard}} (the most common {{A|Godfather}} claim) is mostly seen as suspicious. The problem with this is that another {{A|Investigator}} may see them as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Arsonist}} which will ruin the claim. Of course, the {{A|Godfather}} can simply claim {{A|Doused}} to reduce suspicion against him, but only if the role list allows for such. *Write your {{A|Last Will}} as though you were an {{A|Investigator}}. This could help you out because if you get jailed and the {{A|Jailor}} asks you to put out your {{A|Last Will}}, they will have evidence to believe that you were, in fact, an {{A|Investigator}}. Also, if the actual {{A|Investigator}} were to investigate you, it would show up as {{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Consigliere}}, or {{A|Mayor}}, since they cannot determine your exact role. *Finding potential allies is one of the {{A|Consigliere's}} best strengths. If you find a {{A|Neutral Evil}} role or the {{A|Pirate}}, you can ask them to side with the {{A|Mafia}} in exchange for the {{A|Mafia's}} assistance in satisfying their win condition (This is especially true for the {{A|Witch}}, as they cannot win with the {{A|Town}}). If you find a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Amnesiac}}, you can offer the {{A|Survivor}} the {{A|Mafia's}} protection in the Hang trials in exchange for their support (in the {{A|Amnesiac's}} case, you can ask them to remember a dead {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Mafia}} member). This can be vital in gaining the votes needed to Hang a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role or achieve victory in a kingmaker. *If you know that there is a {{A|Spy}} and you find a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or {{A|Werewolf}}, be careful when trying to get them Hanged the next {{A|day}}. A {{A|Spy}} would know if a member of the {{A|Mafia}} visited that person and would assume you are a {{A|Consigliere}}. **Also, a {{A|Spy}} could call you out for having only targets visited by the {{A|Mafia}} in your {{A|Last Will}}, but if you scramble the order of your investigations, most {{A|Spies}} should skip over you. This also works with {{A|Witch}}, if you plan to fake {{A|investigator}}. ***However, smart {{A|Spies}} will likely check your {{A|Last Will}} carefully and catch you if your {{A|Last Will}} is full of dead {{A|Townies}}, claimed {{A|Townies}} or visited {{A|Townies}}, which is why sometimes you should put your {{A|Mafia}} members into your {{A|Last Will}}. ****If you put your {{A|Mafia}} member into your {{A|Last Will}}, remember to put their claim's result, although if that {{A|Mafia}} member is Hanged, you will be placed under heavier suspicion. You can claim that your target was {{A|Disguised}} in this case. ***Alternatively, you can ask the {{A|Disguiser}} to {{A|Disguise}} you to hide {{A|Mafia}} visits from the {{A|Spy}}. *The {{A|Arsonist}} and {{A|Hex Master}} might be your worst enemy. Just because you found an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Hex Master}} result that doesn't mean they are really the {{A|Arsonist}} and/or {{A|Hex Master}}, due to the fact that {{A|doused}} and {{A|hexed}} players will appear as an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Hex Master}}, respectively. **Using this, you could report any {{A|Hex Master}} and {{A|Arsonist}} results to the {{A|Mafia}} [[Mafia Killing|killing]]. By killing off people who have been {{A|doused}} or {{A|hexed}}, you can prevent the {{A|Arsonist}} from causing any meaningful damage when they ignite, and stave off a final {{A|hex}}. If they are immune, they could be a {{A|Bodyguard}} vesting, the {{A|Arsonist}} themselves, or another role with defense. *{{A|Last Wills}}: If you keep a log of investigations in your {{A|Last Will}} that regard to an {{A|Investigator's}} results, and that person dies and they were a {{A|Town}} member, delete the name in that section and replace it with a {{A|Mafia}} member. This can make your fellow {{A|Mafia}} friend seem innocent. **Additionally, you can use the trick above to trick the town into Hanging the wrong person (finding a {{A|Jester}}, but saying they're a {{A|Serial Killer}}, or listing an {{A|Executioner}} as a {{A|Sheriff}}), so they have a better chance at Hanging a {{A|Town}} member. In the case of the {{A|Executioner}}, this tactic is golden for gaining his support, as if a living {{A|Mafia}} members points out their part in the {{A|Executioner's}} Hanging of their target, they are likely to join the {{A|Mafia}} in terms of voting. Do keep in mind though, that the {{A|Executioner}} could instantly rat you out. At the very least, the distrust created by the whisper, even if it leads to no Hanging, will waste time during the {{A|day}} and will probably have the {{A|Executioner}} drawing attention to themselves. ***Be warned about placing the names of {{A|Mafia}} members in your {{A|Last Will}} as those you have investigated in place of a dead person. Without a {{A|Disguiser}}, an experienced {{A|Spy}} can notice that said person was not visited by the {{A|Mafia}} and put two and two together. Although phenomenal {{A|Spies}} like these are rare, keep this in mind, especially in {{A|Ranked}} mode. **If someone reveals they are a {{A|Survivor}} on the first {{A|Day}}, it's a good opportunity for you to investigate them to prove their role. If they're actually a {{A|Survivor}} (or {{A|Amnesiac}} posing as a {{A|Survivor}}), you can post their investigation results to clear them of suspicion and perhaps encourage them to support the {{A|Mafia}} later on. If they're not actually a {{A|Survivor}} (ex. {{A|Neutral Killing}}), you can accuse them while posing as an {{A|Investigator}} to Hang them and gain the {{A|Town's}} trust. If they're an important {{A|Townie}} claiming {{A|Survivor}} (most likely a {{A|Mayor}}), you may be better off posting the investigation results of one of your {{A|Mafia}} friends instead while telling said {{A|Mafia}} to kill the {{A|Survivor}} claim at {{A|Night}}. ***Watch for {{A|Spies}} when doing this if you're not {{A|Disguised}}. ***If you suspect the {{A|Survivor}} claim is {{A|Medusa}}, you may instruct a {{A|Bootlegger}} to [[role block]] them while you investigate them. ***Remember that an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Hex Master}} may have decided to {{A|Douse}}/{{A|Hex}} the {{A|Survivor}} claim if they appear as such, but this is unlikely. **Make sure to always make your {{A|Last Will}} like an {{A|Investigator}} would in case you are pressed to paste it in chat. Record an {{A|Investigator}} style {{A|Last Will}} to be able to paste during the chat, but keep a log of the real results in the {{A|Notes}} so your {{A|Mafia}} friends can know what role is which. Make sure no flaws are in your {{A|Investigator}}-styled {{A|Last Will}} (e.g. writing {{A|Investigator}} results in the right order. For example, if you found a {{A|Retributionist}}, put it in your {{A|Last Will}} as {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Janitor}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, instead of something like {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Janitor}}, {{A|Medium}}), or you could be called out as a {{A|Consigliere}} by a smarter player. *When reporting results to the {{A|Town}} or the {{A|Jailor}}, always remember the investigation results an {{A|Investigator}} would see, and phrase them accordingly. Accusing someone outright of being a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or {{A|Werewolf}} when you're claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}} is a dead giveaway. *If you absolutely ''must'' get someone Hanged immediately, you might benefit from claiming something other than {{A|Investigator}}, since the Investigator results leave some wiggle-room; for instance, claiming {{A|Sheriff}} to accuse a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}}. This carries some risk of being contradicted by an {{A|Investigator}} who has investigated you previously, but if you need to Hang someone ''right away'' - for instance, if you discovered the {{A|Neutral Killing}} role last {{A|night}} and must Hang them immediately to avoid a loss - it can sometimes be a viable option. *Alternatively, another member of the {{A|Mafia}} with appropriate investigative results can use your information to make an accusation. For instance, if you identify a {{A|Serial Killer}}, then a {{A|Forger}} can claim {{A|Lookout}} and say they saw them kill someone. *If you want to accuse someone without drawing attention to yourself, you can ask the {{A|Mafioso}} to put the accusation in the {{A|Death Note}}. However, this has the drawback of revealing that the {{A|Mafia}} has a {{A|Consigliere}}, which can make it harder for you to pass as an {{A|Investigator}} later on. Another option (if the {{A|Mafia}} has missed a kill for any other reason) is to use the {{A|Death Note}} or a member of the {{A|Mafia's}} {{A|Last Will}} to accuse them of being immune. *''Always'' be sure to unambiguously identify any rival evil roles you discovered in your {{A|Last Will}}; the {{A|Town}} tends to trust a {{A|Consigliere's}} {{A|Last Will}} on those, and at that point, there's no longer any benefit to being subtle with your revelations. **If you find a {{A|Witch}}, you can put them as whatever role they claimed to protect them. If they haven't claimed a role, put them as any suitable {{A|Witch}} claim, like {{A|Survivor}}, {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Lookout}}. Alternatively, you can omit them entirely and replace them with a false accusation against someone innocent; but make sure your fellow {{A|Mafia}} know the truth beforehand so they can plan properly. *Make sure you put the investigative results in the right order in your {{A|Last Will}}. Doing so will make people more likely to believe you. Putting the roles in the wrong order, or worse, getting the investigative results completely wrong could get you Hanged easily. **While it is helpful to put the roles in the right order, you should probably not put the names in order. A smart {{A|Spy}} could notice that the order in which you investigated someone was also the order that the {{A|Mafia}} visited people, and could figure out your role if you reveal your {{A|Last There is a small risk that an alert {{A|Spy}} might notice you didn't visit some of the people on your list, but {{A|Spies}} of that caliber are rare. **On the other hand, you can use this to try and get the {{A|Town}} to Hang innocent people at little danger to yourself. Control them (e.g saying an {{A|Investigator}} is {{A|Framer}}/{{A|Vampire}}/{{A|Jester}} when you are about to get a majority) or manipulate them away from your allies by deceptively confirming them as non-{{A|Mafia}} (unless it is not possible. In that case, you have to Hang them to not get suspicion. However, try not to use this tactic because it could be seen as gamethrowing, and rather discuss it with the other members). ** Likewise, if you manage to "prove" your role as an {{A|Investigator}} and find a {{A|Town Protective}} (like a {{A|Doctor}}), you can ask them to be on you that {{A|Night}}, protecting you from harm. If you accused an evil role (like a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}}) and they decide to attack you, you can add this to the evidence of your accusation whilst potentially keeping a {{A|Town Protective}} away from the {{A|Mafia's}} next target. If the {{A|Town Protective}} is a {{A|Bodyguard}}, it's even better as they can kill most {{A|Neutral Killings}} for the {{A|Mafia's}} benefit whilst dying in the process. *Before investigating someone, you can put down in your {{A|Last Will}} that you are investigating your {{A|Mafioso}}. If the attacked target turns out to be a {{A|Veteran}} and shoots you, the {{A|Town}} will believe that your {{A|Mafioso}} is a {{A|Veteran}} by looking at the {{A|Consigliere's}} {{A|Last Will}}. Keep in mind this can backfire tremendously if the target you are visiting turns out to be a {{A|Werewolf}} staying home, so make sure your game has none of those before you attempt this tactic. *If you manage to find an important {{A|Town}} role early (like a {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}) consider not putting their results in your {{A|Last Will}} and instead replace it with another {{A|Mafia}} member entirely. The {{A|Town}} may suspect a {{A|Consigliere}} if the important role dies and will be suspicious of any {{A|Investigators}} who visited them. *If an unconfirmed {{A|Town}} member claims to be visiting someone, you may investigate who they claim who to be visiting, as a {{A|Spy}} will see a member of the {{A|Mafia}} visiting them and may accuse them, although a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} may call you out. * An extremely risky but effective claim for {{A|Consigliere}} is {{A|Lookout}}. Since you can determine exact roles, it becomes easier to predict who would visit that target. If the target is someone asking for protection for example, if you found a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}, you can say that they visited that person. This could backfire very easily, however. An {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Sheriff}} could expose you or if said {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} didn't actually visit the target you'd be found out. **This strategy can be expanded on with other people's claims. If someone who you have determined the role of claims their role and posts their {{A|Last Will}}, you can confirm this person, and confirm yourself as {{A|Lookout}}. Make sure this person is not accusing one of your fellow {{A|Mafia}} members or any other non-town role you wish to keep alive. This works best when they are simply asked role or voted up to the stand. Now that you have confirmed this person AND claimed {{A|Lookout}}, you can kill them off the next {{A|night}} as {{A|Mafia}} under the ruse that you will watch them. You can then accuse another {{A|Townie}}, who you "have found" them of being the {{A|Mafioso}}, and hopefully, get them Hanged. This should only be used if Hanging a {{A|Townie}} gives the {{A|Mafia}} majority, as it will be seen you aren't a {{A|Lookout}} unless you claim the killer was {{A|Disguised}}. *Another effective claim if you are playing in the {{A|Coven Expansion}} is to claim {{A|Tracker}} since you can determine exact roles. If you find a non-visiting role, just mark them down as ''did not visit'' and the person you tracked can confirm your claim. If you find a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role like a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Juggernaut}}, you can accuse them of visiting a target they killed. Other fake {{A|Lookout}} strategies can work with this claim with the added bonus of sharing the same {{A|Investigator}} result as the {{A|Consigliere}} so only a {{A|Sheriff}} could expose you. *It's important to keep in mind what roles you're looking for; while knowing any role is valuable, some are more important than others. ** Finding a hidden {{A|Mayor}} can mean the difference between a victory and a loss, so try to find them too, as they can counter "{{A|Mafia}} Majority" in a pinch. **Finding {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles is also vital to victory; focusing on people who are silent or who have made suspicious claims is often useful for this. *While searching for a high-priority target, like the {{A|Jailor}}, you should encourage the main {{A|Mafia Killing}} role to kill people you ''haven't'' yet investigated until you find them since that effectively lets you cross two people off the list each {{A|night}}. **Even if you found a role that seems somewhat important, like a {{A|Sheriff}}, you have to weigh telling your killer to go after them against the importance of finding the {{A|Jailor}} as quickly as possible. **Killing unknown roles will let the {{A|Mafia}} reach the point where they've identified everyone's roles twice as fast as if the Godfather simply killed every single Town you identify; once you know everyone's role, it's generally easy to win. **This works even better if you have a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer}} to prevent less-important but still-dangerous roles you've identified from influencing the game while you and the {{A|Godfather}} hunt for the Jailor. **This is especially important if you lack a {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combo, since in that situation you need to find the {{A|Jailor}} before they {{A|Jail}} your killer or the game will be lost. ===Dealing with a {{A|Consigliere}}=== *Beware of {{A|Investigator}} claims, especially if they claim to have found an important {{A|Town}} role early game, and the important Town role ends up being killed by the {{A|Mafia}} the next {{A|night}}. **{{A|Consiglieres}} will have similar strategies to {{A|Executioners}} when Hanging an immune role. ** Furthermore, if a {{A|Town Protective}} or {{A|Jailor}} ends up dead {{A|night}} 2 (role shown {{A|day}} 3), you may want to be wary of possible {{A|Consiglieres}}. They may have found that role {{A|night}} 1, then told their {{A|Mafia}} allies so they could kill them {{A|night}} 2. *** Specifically, if a {{A|Jailor}} is found dead on {{A|Day}} 3, watch out for any "{{A|Investigators}}" that found them as {{A|Spy}}, {{A|Blackmailer}}, and {{A|Jailor}} (and {{A|Guardian Angel}} in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}). They are likely a {{A|Consigliere}}. **If someone claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}} posts their will in chat, examine the order of the results given. If they are not in the correct order (e.g. {{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Arsonist}}), that player is likely a {{A|Consigliere}} who's forgotten the right order of investigative results for the person they examined. *** In most of these cases, the role they put first is the actual role of their target. *Many people do not know that {{A|doused}} targets appear as {{A|Arsonist}}, and therefore, a {{A|Consigliere}} will generally try to point and accuse out immune roles that would oppose the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Mafia}}. **This same concept applies to {{A|Hex Masters}}. *A {{A|Consigliere}} might stop posting investigation results once they become {{A|Mafioso}}, as they can no longer investigate. *A {{A|Consigliere}} is often sure and confident in their claims. They will call them out with an {{A|Investigators}} results, but instead of being reasonable about possibilities with their target's role, they might continue to say that they are an evil role, even if their claim and {{A|Last Will}} is impossible to fault. *{{A|Consiglieres}} and other evil roles are often more relaxed and confident in general, knowing that they are safer and able to defend themselves better than a {{A|Townie}}. Often times, they will not call for a {{A|Town Protective}} role, when in the same situation an {{A|Investigator}} would ask for protection. *A {{A|Consigliere's}} behavior might change throughout the match. If an {{A|Investigator}} claim is eager to help and incredibly good at Hanging evil roles at the start of a match, especially when hunting the {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles, but then becomes more silent and starts misHanging towards the end, they may be a {{A|Consigliere}} trying to hide. *A {{A|Consigliere}} will often try to take control of Hanges when their {{A|Mafia}} members are on the line, and sit back when the {{A|Town}} is Hanging someone that isn't part of the {{A|Mafia}}. If the {{A|Investigator}} claim sits back and allows the {{A|Town}} to Hang people, but suddenly takes control, it is likely that they are a {{A|Consigliere}}. *A {{A|Consigliere}} will not accuse somebody of being {{A|Mafia}}, because they already know who the {{A|Mafia}} is. Beware of {{A|Investigator}} Claims that have not found any {{A|Mafia}}, only {{A|Neutrals}}. They are likely {{A|Consigliere}}, especially when there is still a {{A|Random Mafia}} slot still open. *A {{A|Spy}} is a major nuisance for the {{A|Consigliere}}, as they can track who the {{A|Mafia}} visited. If a player claims {{A|Investigator}}, and their visits match up with the {{A|Mafia's}} visits, and that specific person had no visible actions done to them, they might instead be a {{A|Consigliere}}. **As {{A|Spy}}, you can try to ask {{A|Investigator}} claims to visit a person of your choice. If the person you asked an {{A|Investigator}} to check was shown as a person mafia visited, then the {{A|Investigator}} claim is most likely a {{A|Consigliere}}. ***However a {{A|Disguiser}} can mess with this plan by hiding the {{A|Mafia}} visits. ***A member of the {{A|Mafia}} can also visit the {{A|Investigator's}} target to paint them as a {{A|Consigliere}} to the {{A|Spy}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{ConsigliereAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{ConsigliereMessages}} ==Trivia== *According to a poll made by [http://town-of-salem.wikia.com/wiki/User:Naru2008 Naru2008], the {{A|Consigliere}} is the fifth most loved role in Town of Salem with 108 votes, and the reason being is because the users loved knowing a person's exact role at {{A|night}}. *The {{A|Consigliere's}} role icon reflects how the {{A|Consigliere}} is a "{{A|Mafia}}-{{A|Investigator|Mafia}}", with it being extremely similar to the {{A|Investigator's}} role icon. **The same applied for the old role icons before Unity ({{A|Consigliere}}: [[File:Achievement Consigliere.png|30x30px]], {{A|Investigator}}: [[File:Achievement Investigator.png|30x30px]]). *The term {{A|Consigliere}} means advisor to the mob. This word was made more famous by the movie "''The Godfather''". *{{A|Consigliere}} may be the most incorrectly pronounced role in the game. The correct way to pronounce it is "kon-sull-yair-ee".https://www.lexico.com/definition/consigliere ==History== *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Consigliere's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Consigliere.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Consigliere's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Consigliere Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.5.11.5389}} **{{A|Doused}} players now show up as an {{A|Arsonist}} to a {{A|Consigliere}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. ==References== {{Navbox Roles}} [[Category:Mafia Support roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} == Mechanics == When investigating someone, the {{A|Investigator}} receives a message which includes a target's possible roles. Below lists the possible investigative results in the game (in both Classic and the {{A|Coven Expansion}}).

{{RoleResults - Investigator}} ==Strategy== ===Surviving as an {{A|Investigator}}=== *Always consider if it's worth exposing yourself as an {{A|Investigator}} and how many players are left in the game as well as what roles are left. Once other players know you are an {{A|Investigator}}, you will become a target or some sort of priority to the {{A|Mafia}}. However, if you know that there are {{A|Town Protective}} roles, revealing yourself as an {{A|Investigator}} early and giving everyone information about suspicious evils can help the {{A|Town}} win. **Make sure to do your best not to reveal who the {{A|Townies}} are as you could end up making them a target for kill-capable {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killings}}. Remember that simply posting in your {{A|Last Will}} that someone is good may lead experienced evil players to conclude that the said person is important (e.g. you put that someone is a confirmed {{A|Townie}}). *Always investigate people who claim any roles that seem suspicious. Evil roles tend to claim roles that will usually be ignored to escape questioning. Some may pose as a victorious {{A|Executioner}} or a {{A|Jester}}. *The {{A|Investigator}} is much more powerful in {{A|Classic Mode}} due to not all the roles being available. Here is a list of all results in {{A|Classic Mode}} that reveal more than you think: {| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{A|Classic Mode}}  |- |{{InvRes1}} - '''{{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Veteran}}, or {{A|Mafioso}}''' |- |{{InvRes2}} - '''{{A|Medium}} or {{A|Retributionist}}''' |- |{{InvRes4}} - '''{{A|Spy}} or {{A|Jailor}}''' |- |{{InvRes5}} - '''{{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Executioner}}''' |- |{{InvRes6}} - '''{{A|Framer}}, {{A|Jester}}, or {{A|Framed}}''' |- |{{InvRes7}} - '''{{A|Lookout}}''' |- |{{InvRes8}} - '''{{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}} ''' |- |{{InvRes9}} - '''{{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Serial Killer}}''' |- |{{InvRes10}} - '''{{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Mayor}}''' |- |{{InvRes11}} - '''{{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Godfather}}''' |- |''All other results not listed are no different in {{A|Classic Mode}} than they are otherwise.'' |} *In {{A|Classic Mode}}, there can be only one {{A|Random Town}}. Keep this in mind if someone claims to be a role that isn't explicitly stated in the [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Roles|role list]]. *{{A|Investigator}} is also helpful in the {{A|Town Traitor}} game modes: {| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{A|Town Traitor}}  |- |{{InvRes5}} - '''{{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|disguised}} {{A|Mafia}}''' |- |{{InvRes6}} - '''{{A|Framer}} or {{A|Framed}}''' |- |{{InvRes9}} - '''{{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Disguiser}}, or {{A|disguised}} {{A|Mafia}}''' |- |{{InvRes11}} - '''{{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|disguised}} {{A|Mafia}}''' |- |''All other results not listed are no different in {{A|Town Traitor}} than they are otherwise.'' |} *{{A|Investigator}} is very useful in {{A|Town Traitor}} once you find out what the role of the {{A|Random Mafia}} is.
{| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}}  |- |{{InvResCVN1}} - '''{{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Veteran}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN2}} - '''{{A|Medium}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Necromancer}}, or {{A|Trapper}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN3}} - '''{{A|Medusa}} or {{A|Psychic}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN4}} - '''{{A|Spy}} or {{A|Jailor}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN5}} - '''{{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Poisoner}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN6}} - '''{{A|Hex Master}} or {{A|Hexed}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN7}} - '''{{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Coven Leader}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN8}} - '''{{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN9}} - '''{{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Potion Master}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN10}} - '''{{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Mayor}}, or {{A|Tracker}}''' |- |{{InvResCVN11}} - '''{{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}}''' |- |''All other results not listed are no different in {{A|Coven Expansion}} {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}} than they are otherwise.'' |} *Once again, {{A|Investigator}} is very useful in the {{A|Coven Expansion}} {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}} game mode if you find out what the role of the {{A|Random Coven}} is. *If there is a {{A|Sheriff}}, find each other and work together. During the {{A|day}}, discuss with each other about who you are both going to visit. At {{A|night}}, both of you choose the same person. For example, if the {{A|Sheriff}}'s investigation says your target is ''seems innocent'' and yours says that they are a ''{{InvRes1}}'', that person is either a {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Veteran}}, or {{A|disguised}} member of the {{A|Mafia}} (assuming no other roles intervene, such as a {{A|Transporter}}). **However, this can backfire as a {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Witch}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Jailor}} can interrupt your plan. Also, if you both visit a {{A|Veteran}} on alert, both of you will die. A {{A|Blackmailer}} can also use your information to help the {{A|Mafia}}. * Because there may be a {{A|Consigliere}} in the game, the {{A|Mafia}} can try to trick real {{A|Investigators}} to make {{A|Townies}} think you are {{A|Consigliere}} instead. To avoid this, make sure you wrote your {{A|Last Will}} properly and in the exact order of your investigation result. Writing investigation results in a different order may lead other {{A|Townies}} to think you are a poorly-played {{A|Consigliere}}. *'''Write the best {{A|Last Will}} you can.''' You can make or break a game depending on your {{A|Last Will}}. Consider leaving out important roles though as the {{A|Mafia}} will probably target them the second they see your {{A|Last Will}} in a way such as a {{A|Janitor}}'s cleaning (or when you die). * If you receive a result with possible good and bad roles, try to ask what their role is. For example, if you received something like ''{{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Forger}}, or {{A|Witch}}'', ask the person their role. If they say a role you didn't get, (e.g. that they are a {{A|Medium}}), they might be a {{A|Forger}} or {{A|Witch}} trying to keep suspicion off of themselves. *You should write down any claims people make about their roles, and investigate them later; catching someone lying about their role is an easy way to determine that they're evil. *Ask the person you investigated for their role without posting your results. This is useful as evils don't always claim inside their investigative results and you can catch them lying. *Be very careful if there's an {{A|Arsonist}}. A significant push against them can put you under a lot of suspicion as a {{A|Consigliere}} or {{A|Witch}}, '''especially''' if the suspected {{A|Arsonist}} claims they were controlled by a {{A|Witch}}, as {{A|Witch}} ascertains '''exact''' roles regardless of their target being {{A|Framed}} or {{A|doused}}. **On the other hand, an {{A|Arsonist}} can mean the difference between a {{A|Town}} win with you being dead, or everyone being dead and an {{A|Arsonist}} victory. You should determine the worth of your own life by comparison to an {{A|Arsonist}}, especially if another role can kill them at {{A|night}} instead (i.e. {{A|Jailor}}). === Dealing with {{A|Investigator}} Results=== *The first thing you need to know is that you need to keep up with the updates. For example, a player who last played in 2015 would be confused about the new changes and will ask questions to the town, which will be a giveaway to evil roles that this player is an {{A|Investigator}}. *If you find a {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} on the first {{A|night}}, you should tell the {{A|Town}} about it. You might be called an{{A|Executioner}}, however revealing yourself too late as a {{A|Town Investigative}} generally makes you look way more suspicious. If you manage to hang the evil player you found, the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} will often try to attack you that {{A|night}}, so ask for a {{A|Town Protective}} role to be on you. **If you do decide to wait and you only write your results in your {{A|Last Will}}, a {{A|Janitor}} can be your downfall since they wipe out {{A|Last Wills}}, revealing them only to the {{A|Mafia}}. If this is a threat to you, try to find ''good'' roles. Finding a {{A|Spy}} or a {{A|Town Protective}} and [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] your findings to them will allow the {{A|Town}} to retain your findings even after you are {{A|Cleaned}} (if the person you [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to is trusted by the other {{A|Townies}}). This works especially well with the {{A|Jailor}}; an informed {{A|Jailor}} is a lethal one. * In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, {{A|Investigator}} results tend to be much broader due to the added roles, therefore making it harder to deduce what specific role your target may be. **Again, you can work with a {{A|Sheriff}} to see if your target is evil or not. *Another big threat are {{A|Disguisers}} as they are, most likely, randomly disguising {{A|Mafia}} members as people, and the fact that if they do in fact random {{A|disguise}}, their investigative results shift to that of who they {{A|disguised}} as. If you suspect someone as being a {{A|disguised}} member of the {{A|Mafia}}, it is recommended to check them two {{A|nights}} in a row. If their results change and they weren't {{A|Transported}}, they are most likely a {{A|disguised}} member of the {{A|Mafia}}. *Remember to record the roles people have "claimed" in your {{A|Last Will}}, not just what you discover through your investigation; catching lies is one of your main roles. Under most circumstances, {{A|Town}} members have no reason to lie about their roles. *Someone appeared to be a ''"{{InvRes1}}"''? Take account if there were any deaths by a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Veteran}}. If there weren't, the person is most likely a {{A|Mafioso}}, {{A|Ambusher}}, or a {{A|Vigilante}} who decided to only shoot people with enough proof (which is common). ** If there were any deaths from an {{A|Ambusher}}, this will make them even more suspicious. ** Most games (like {{A|Classic Mode}} and {{A|Ranked Practice}}) only have one {{A|Town Killing}}, so if there is a known {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Veteran}}, it's easy to see the {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Ambusher}}. ***However, keep in mind that they can still be a legitimate {{A|Town Killing}} from a {{A|Random Town}} spot. **If there's no {{A|Mafioso}} in the [[graveyard]], and the {{A|Godfather}} dies, investigate that player again. If their results don't change, they're probably a {{A|Townie}}. If they show up as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Arsonist}}, they are most likely a {{A|Mafioso}} promoted to a {{A|Godfather}}, but there is always the chance that they were {{A|doused}} if an {{A|Arsonist}} is in the game. *If someone is shown as ''"{{InvRes6}}"'', remember that they might be {{A|Framed}}. If you're unsure, you can visit them later to see if you acquire the same result. **However, know that sometimes the {{A|Framer}} might frame the same person throughout the entire game. If you do think that they are {{A|Framed}}, tell a {{A|Lookout}} to check him and see if anyone visits him, as you check him again or ask a {{A|Spy}} if they have been visited by the {{A|Mafia}} on {{A|nights}} before you investigated them (keep in mind a {{A|Disguiser}} can mess with both the {{A|Lookout}} and {{A|Spy}} results by simply disguising the {{A|Framer}}). **{{A|Framed}} people always come up as suspicious to a {{A|Sheriff}}. Therefore, if a {{A|Sheriff}} investigates someone and finds them not suspicious ''the same {{A|night}}'' that you investigate them and receive a result of "{{InvRes6}}", then they must be a {{A|Vampire}} or {{A|Jester}}; they couldn't have been {{A|Framed}}. **If it's impossible for there to be a {{A|Framer}}, it is dangerous for the {{A|Town}} to hang them, since they might be a {{A|Jester}}. However, a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} can bypass this by executing or shooting them; provided it's impossible for there to be a {{A|Framer}}, there's no risk of them being a {{A|Town}} member. ** In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, this result becomes even riskier with the addition of {{A|Hex Master}}, who can {{A|hex}} people and have them permanently appear as this result for the remainder of the game. If you suspect that someone is {{A|Hexed}}, ask a {{A|Spy}} if they have been visited by a member of the {{A|Coven}}. This could have been a visit by a {{A|Potion Master}} healing their {{A|Hex Master}} but this is unlikely due to the {{A|Potion Master}} having other priority things to do. You can also request for a {{A|Sheriff}} to investigate them after the {{A|Coven Leader}} dies, as if the {{A|Hex Master}} gains the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they will become detection immune to the {{A|Sheriff}} and will be outed as a {{A|Hex Master}} since they now "seem innocent". Keep in mind they can still be a {{A|Jester}} that simply remained unhexed throughout the game. *If someone has come up as ''"{{InvRes3}}"'', and has started to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to seemingly random people, investigate the people they [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to. It could be an {{A|Amnesiac}} unknowingly leading you to the people they are planning to join later. *If someone claims {{A|Survivor}}, you can investigate them to catch them trying to escape suspicion easily to the end. If someone claims {{A|Survivor}} but comes up with {{A|Bodyguard}}/{{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Arsonist}}/{{A|Crusader}}, they are likely a {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Arsonist}} trying to hide their {{A|Basic Defense}} (however, it is possible that they are {{A|doused}}). *If your target was purged by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, all {{A|douses}} will wear off, giving you more accurate investigation results and signaling that they did not have {{A|doused}} investigation results. However they could still be {{A|Framed}}, since a {{A|Guardian Angel}} cannot remove {{A|Frames}}. *If someone claims and posts their {{A|Last Will}}, '''check the order''' of the results. If they are not in the correct order (e.g. {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Hex Master}}, or {{A|Jester}}) that player is most likely a {{A|Consigliere}} who forgot the order of investigation results for people they have investigated. ==Fake-Claiming {{A|Investigator}}== *{{A|Investigator}} can be a relatively easy role to fake-claim (in terms of difficulty to fake, it is comparable to {{A|Lookout}}), as many {{A|Townies}} will out themselves and their role to throw suspicion onto someone else or even have someone hanged. It is an especially powerful fake-claim as well because people expect evils to claim easier fake-claims, and you can throw suspicion onto someone claiming {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Medium}}, or another hard-to-prove, easy-to-claim role, and in some cases, force miss-hanges. *Claiming that most of your targets are {{A|doused}} is a viable strategy. The {{A|Town}} will be distracted on finding the {{A|Arsonist}} that may or may not exist, and you can have an excuse as to why you have plenty of people's investigation results wrong. **If there is a {{A|Neutral Killing}} other than {{A|Arsonist}} confirmed in this game, do not use this strategy. *If someone announces "X is suspicious" in a binary fashion, they are probably a {{A|Sheriff}} or an {{A|Executioner}} fake-claiming {{A|Sheriff}}. Pay attention to people [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] a lot and asking for roles as this is common behavior for {{A|Investigators}} trying to narrow down results (you may use this strategy to your advantage if you prove yourself as {{A|Investigator}} - claim you are narrowing down investigative results, and they will most likely go along with it). Silent players are most likely the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or a {{A|Neutral}} role trying to stay under the radar, but they may be just a player who is normally silent. *Another useful tool for {{A|Investigator}} fake-claims is when {{A|Townies}} out themselves as their role to try and have someone hanged. If the hang is not successful, or suspicion is cast on them for [[bussing]], you can "confirm" their claim. A problem with this is that when the person dies and their role was false, you may be outed as a fake. *Great help for fake {{A|Investigator}} claims that aren't a {{A|Consigliere}} is a {{A|Mayor}} revealing. Claiming to have investigated them before they revealed puts a confirmed bit of information into your {{A|Last Will}} which nobody can claim is false. *One way to fake claim as {{A|Investigator}} is by using the [[graveyard]]. Use the [[graveyard]] to observe their roles and scramble up when you investigated them so you can have investigated them on different {{A|nights}} when they were alive. Of course, smart {{A|Townies}} will see that your {{A|Last Will}} lists only dead {{A|Townies}} and may call you out. Another way of doing this is through a mix of [[graveyard]] and claims. When someone claims, it normally is in their investigative result, so you should be safe there. But if you are not sure, just list them as {{A|Framed}}, {{A|Hexed}} or {{A|doused}}. *If you aren't sure on what to put for a certain player's role (e.g.: you were asked to investigate player X to prove yourself), put in the {{A|Framed}} results (''"{{InvResCVN6}}"''). You can then pretend they were {{A|Framed}}, which can buy you another {{A|day}} if there is no {{A|Spy}}. If you are asked to investigate them again you can pretend the "{{A|Framer}}" is framing whoever you are asked to investigate so you can't prove yourself to the {{A|Town}}. Similar strategies can be used for {{A|hexes}}, {{A|douses}}, and {{A|disguises}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{InvestigatorAchievements}} ==Trivia== *Prior to [[Version_History - Town of Salem|Version 1.5.11.5389]], there were different investigative results.
