'''{{A|Juggernaut}} '''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== [[File:JailorSKDeath.png|thumb|262x262px|Death message received when the {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Jails}} and does not {{A|Execute}} a {{A|Serial Killer}}.]] *The {{A|Jailor}} is a {{A|Unique}} Role. There can only be one {{A|Jailor}} in a match. *Neither you nor the {{A|Mayor}} can be an {{A|Executioner's}} target. *You {{A|Roleblock}} your target and override [[Role block Immunity|Role Block Immunity]]. *{{A|Executing}} your target deals them an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}. *You can talk with your target at {{A|Night}}, and you'll be called {{Amne|Jailor|Jailor}} at {{A|Night}}. *Targets are given {{A|Powerful Defense}} for the {{A|Night}}. ==='''Jailing a target'''=== [[File:Jailor Death Note.png|thumb|361x361px|An example of a {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Death Note}} ]] [[File:RoleIcon Executioner.png|thumb|100x100px|{{A|Jailor}} {{A|Execute}} icon]] Jail a target for the upcoming {{A|Night}} by clicking on the "{{A|Jail}} " button next to the player's names on the player list during the {{A|Day}}. * All outsider visitors are notified that their target was {{A|Jailed}} and their ability will fail; however, they still visit their target. The {{A|Jailee}} will not be notified of any of these visits except for attackers, being {{A|Transported}}, being {{A|Roleblocked}}, or being [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]]. * A {{A|Bodyguard}} visiting your target will not retaliate if the target is attacked. *If you {{A|Jail}} a {{A|Serial Killer}} (that isn't Cautious), {{A|Werewolf}} (during a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}), or {{A|Pestilence}} and don't {{A|Execute}} them, they will attack you even if they leave the game. A {{A|Bodyguard}} can save you from both an attacking {{A|Serial Killer}} and a {{A|Werewolf}}. **If you do {{A|Execute}} a {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Werewolf}}, they will not attack you. **If a {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Serial Killer}} attacks you, you will receive a different message: "You were killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}} you {{A|Jailed}}." ***There is an achievement you receive the first time you {{A|Jail}} but do not {{A|Execute}} an incautious {{A|Serial Killer}}. **{{A|Jailing}} {{A|Pestilence}} will give you a different message: "You {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Pestilence}} and were obliterated. Flummery!". This occurs whether you {{A|Execute}} them or not as your attack cannot kill {{A|Pestilence}}. *If a dead {{A|Medium}} seances you, you will listen and talk to both the {{A|Medium}} and the other player at the same time. The {{A|Jailee}} cannot hear the {{A|Medium}} but can see your end of the conversation. If a dead {{A|Medium}} seances the {{A|Jailee}}, the {{A|Jailee}} will likewise listen and talk to both you and {{A|Medium}}. You will not see the {{A|Medium's}} messages but can see the {{A|Jailee's}} end of the conversation. *Whoever you have {{A|Jailed}} will still be able to hear anyone they can usually hear at {{A|Night}} ; {{A|Vampires}} and members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} will hear their respective chats, a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} will still hear the {{A|Vampires}} they listen in to, and a {{A|Medium}} will still be able to hear the dead. However, the other {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Vampires}}, or the dead will not be able to see the {{A|Jailee's}} messages. **If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Mafia}} and {{A|Jail|Mafia}} a player, the {{A|Mafia}} will hear you and you will hear them along with the {{A|Jailee}}. The {{A|Mafia}}, however, will not hear the {{A|Jailee}} (also applies for a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Coven}}). *If a {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampire}}, or {{A|Coven}} member is {{A|Jailed}}, the rest of their team will see that they were {{A|Jailed}}, as a message will appear stating: "(Player) was hauled off to {{A|Jail}}". **If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Mafia}}, the {{A|Mafia}} will receive this notification even if you don't {{A|Jail}} a {{A|Mafia}} member. (also applies for a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Coven}}). ==='''{{A|Executing}} a target'''=== {{A|Execute}} your prisoner by using the {{A|Night}} ability button. You have three {{A|Executions}}. *You cannot {{A|Execute}} your target on the first {{A|Night}}. *If you decide to {{A|Execute}}, your prisoner will receive the notification "The jailor has decided to {{A|Execute}} you.". *If you cancel your {{A|Execution}}, your prisoner will receive the notification "The jailor has changed his mind.". *You are unable to {{A|Execute}} your target if you are {{A|Roleblocked}} by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Pirate}}. **Due to a bug, you can still press the {{A|Execute}} button if you are being {{A|pirated}} (which your prisoner will see), but the {{A|Execution}} will not go through. *If a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} controls you into targeting someone other than your prisoner, you will be unable to {{A|Execute}} them. **If they control you into your target, however, you are forced to {{A|Execute}} them, unless it is the first {{A|Night}}. *If you {{A|Execute}} a {{A|Townie}}, a message (''"You have slain a town member so you can't attack again."'') will be shown to you every time you {{A|Jail}} a person. You will lose your remaining {{A|Executions}} as well. **If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Mafia}} or a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Jailor|Coven}}, you will never lose your {{A|Executions}} unless you use all 3 of them. *If you {{A|Execute}} your {{A|Jailee}} and a {{A|Guardian Angel}} watches over them, your {{A|Execution}} will fail and you will lose one {{A|Execution}}. The same occurs if you attempt to {{A|Execute}} {{A|Pestilence}}, though in this case you will be dead. **If a {{A|Serial Killer}} (non-Cautious) manages to survive your {{A|Execution}} (meaning you were {{A|Roleblocked}}, controlled away from your target, or your target was protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}), they will still kill you. **If you execute a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} who was protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, the {{A|Werewolf}} will '''not''' attack you or anyone, which may be a bug. But they will still kill you if you get {{A|Roleblocked}} or controlled away. **If you {{A|Execute}} a {{A|Townie}} who was protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, you will still lose '''all''' your {{A|Executions}} even if they survived. This is most likely a bug as well. *You have a {{A|Death Note}} that can explain why you {{A|Executed}} your {{A|Jailed}} person based on their claim and actions. The reasons are below: **No reason specified. **They are known to be an evildoer. **Their confession was contradictory. **They are possessed and talking nonsense. **They are too quiet or won't respond to questioning. **They are an outsider that might turn against us. **I'm using my own discretion. *You are able to place a check mark on any of these reasons. By default, "No reason specified" will be checked, and it is impossible to have all of them un-checked. ==Strategy== *'''Keep track of your {{A|Jailed}} targets in your {{A|Last Will}} ''' and write their names in your {{A|Last Will}} before the {{A|Night}} begins. If you {{A|Jail}} the {{A|Werewolf}} during a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} and die, the {{A|Town}} will be able to know the {{A|Werewolf's}} possible identity. This also applies to {{A|Pestilence}}. **This won't work against a {{A|Serial Killer}}, as if you {{A|Jail}} a {{A|Serial Killer}} your {{A|Last Will}} will be erased. *'''Avoid {{A|Jailing}} other {{A|Jailor}} claims if they claimed {{A|Day 1}}. ''' {{A|Serial Killers}} may claim {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Night}} one to have the {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Jail}} them, with the {{A|Jailor}} unable to {{A|Execute}} them. This strategy is however extremely risky for the {{A|Serial Killer}}, as they will more likely be called out immediately. However, feel free to {{A|Execute}} them the next {{A|Night}}. *'''Write down any claimed roles in your {{A|Last Will}} immediately''' before the {{A|Night}} ends, in case you die that {{A|Night}}. *'''If you reveal yourself''', make sure that any {{A|Town}} roles that can protect you are doing so, since you are the highest priority target for nearly all evils. This includes {{A|Doctors}} and {{A|Bodyguards}} protecting you, as well as indirect methods such as a {{A|Transporter}} moving you (which makes you difficult to hit) and a {{A|Lookout}} watching you to find who visits you. If anyone else claims to be the {{A|Jailor}}, they are lying since your role is {{A|Unique}}, so {{A|Jail}} and {{A|Execute}} them without having to reveal or risk being haunted by a {{A|Jester}}. *'''Take a neutral stance on your prisoner''', do not be too trusting, but do not be too eager to {{A|Execute}}. Stay level-headed, and don't make rash decisions. Try to be polite -- an unhappy prisoner may be overly defensive and angry. If you don't {{A|Execute}} an evil role, not only do they live for a {{A|Night}} but now the {{A|Town}} may believe they have some credibility because the {{A|Jailor}} believed them. Even worse, you may die from a {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Werewolf}}. However, killing a {{A|Townie}} will result in the loss of all your remaining {{A|Executions}} and your effectiveness as {{A|Jailor}}. Keep yourself composed, and make rational decisions based on fact. *'''Collect information from everyone,''' as this can help find true info for {{A|Townies}} and sort out people who are evil, thus allowing you to {{A|Execute}} them. Try {{A|Jailing}} [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisperers]], talkative people, or anyone looking suspicious. *When you {{A|Jail}} someone, '''make sure to ask for their role.''' If the {{A|Jailed}} target claims a role, ask for their {{A|Last Will}} unless it's {{A|Night 1}}. You will collect information from an {{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Spy}} and can immediately find fake {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, or {{A|Lookout}} claims if they claim they moved or {{A|Roleblocked}} you or one of your {{A|Jailed}} targets. Your target will be notified when you decide to {{A|Execute}} them. {{A|Executing}} first can make many evil roles panic and give wrong information. Have all the information you can, no matter what role they claim. Most evil roles will have a role with somewhat credible information in their {{A|Last Will}}. However, the information may be something you know to be false. {{A|Execute}} all of these people. *'''Consider using a code word in the event of a {{A|Medium}} claim.''' Every {{A|Night}} you {{A|Jail}} a player, tell them a code word unless they claim {{A|Medium}}. Once a player you previously {{A|Jailed}} is killed, they can tell any living {{A|Mediums}} what the code word was, instantly confirming the {{A|Medium}} and outing all other {{A|Medium}} claims as evil. **Of course, this strategy can be flawed, if both the dead player and the {{A|Medium}} claim are {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, or {{A|Vampires}}, they could have discussed the code on a {{A|Night}} they weren't {{A|Jailed}}. *Keep track of {{A|Mafia Killing}}. '''If no one is killed, there is a chance your target is a kill-capable member of the {{A|Mafia}}.''' Beware that if the {{A|Mafia}} have both a {{A|Mafioso}} and a {{A|Godfather}} alive, you will be unable to prevent them from killing by {{A|Jailing}} either one of them. However, if you have {{A|Jailed}} the {{A|Mafioso}}, their {{A|Death Note}} will change from the {{A|Mafioso's}} to the {{A|Godfather's}}, which you can use as evidence to out the {{A|Mafioso}}. Many times, the {{A|Mafia}} will not kill in order to have the {{A|Jailor}} believe that the last person they had {{A|Jailed}} is a killing role so that the {{A|Jailor}} would re-jail and {{A|Execute}} or hang that prisoner. *If you {{A|Execute}} someone, be sure to mark down the specified reason in your {{A|Death Note}}, and optionally include it in your {{A|Last Will}}. *'''If the {{A|Mayor}} reveals themselves''', you can {{A|Jail}} them in case a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or the {{A|Mafia}} targets them, since a revealed {{A|Mayor}} is a high priority to those roles due to the increased voting power. Note that if you both are revealed, a {{A|Witch}} could force you to {{A|Execute}} the {{A|Mayor}}, or you might just be killed instead. On the other hand, you could instead have a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}} for the {{A|Mayor}}. {{A|Trapper}} is also acceptable, but because their {{A|Traps}} take time to build and can be triggered by anyone, it is less optimal. Also note that {{A|Doctors}} cannot heal a revealed {{A|Mayor}}. **You may want to consider revealing yourself to the {{A|Mayor}}, or any other confirmed {{A|Town}} roles that you trust. This is especially useful if you can reveal yourself to a Confirmed {{A|Town Investigative}} role, so that during the {{A|Day}} you can communicate via [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] and together figure out who to {{A|Jail}} and {{A|Execute}} without the {{A|Town}} or any evils interfering. However, do not use this strategy on anyone who you are not certain is {{A|Town}}, as you may well be selling your identity any evil role that would benefit from you dying. ***However, remember that the {{A|Mayor}} cannot be whispered to, so be careful about telling the {{A|Mayor}} your role or try revealing to them before they reveal. You can also reveal yourself to the {{A|Mayor}} while {{A|Jailing}} them, protecting them and baiting an evil role into wasting a kill. **If you have had someone who claimed that they were a {{A|Town Protective}} aside from {{A|Doctor}} and a revealed {{A|Mayor}} dies, feel free to {{A|Jail}} them out of suspicion. You have a good chance to have {{A|Jailed}} an evil role. *You are not {{A|Control Immune}} or {{A|Roleblock Immune}}. Never state who you are if there is a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Bootlegger}} in game. *The {{A|Jailor}} can act as a protective role, as their prisoner is granted Powerful Defense. The {{A|Jailor}} can use this to the {{A|Town's}} advantage by {{A|Jailing}} those who need to be protected, such as a revealed {{A|Mayor}}. **This Powerful Defense will not protect the {{A|Jailed}} player from being killed by a {{A|Bodyguard's}} counter-attack if they are a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} and you don't {{A|Execute}} them. **Remember that a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} can control you into {{A|Executing}} the {{A|Mayor}} and throwing the game a whole different direction. *Do not {{A|Execute}} someone solely for claiming a role a previous target claimed. Doing so is a good way to not only kill a {{A|Townie}}, but also to lose your remaining {{A|Executions}} which makes you not much of a threat to anyone you {{A|Jail}}. Rather, have a confirmed {{A|Town Investigative}} role investigate both targets. {{A|Execute}} the one who has lied. Remember - it's okay to defer {{A|Executions}}! Keep in mind that if you {{A|Jail}} two people and they both claim the same role, the first person isn't always telling the truth! *There is no such thing as a confirmed {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Jester}} (with the extremely rare exception of one who has been investigated by a confirmed {{A|Investigator}}, while {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Hex Master}}, {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, and {{A|Poisoner}} do not fit into the role list) You should strongly consider {{A|Executing}} any {{A|Neutral Evil}} claims you see, as the {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}, or any {{A|Neutral Killing}} role will often try to claim to be an {{A|Executioner}} to explain their Basic Defense. Remember that these roles are evil; they have goals that directly interfere with the {{A|Town's}}. *If there is anyone claiming to be a successful {{A|Executioner}} and you are playing a mode with a few evil roles, such as {{A|Ranked}}, {{A|Execute}} them that {{A|Night}}. They may be an evil faking an {{A|Executioner}} after randomly accusing and hanging someone and being lucky seeing they are {{A|Town}}, or they could actually be a successful {{A|Executioner}}. Either way, you remove an evil role or an {{A|Executioner}}, which has Basic Defense and can side with evils. *Be wary of people who claim {{A|Neutral}} roles, as these can be an evil role. However, keep in mind that they could be telling the truth. {{A|Survivors}} sometimes betray the {{A|Town}}, so keep this in mind. However, if you {{A|Execute}} a role like a {{A|Survivor}}, you may have wasted an {{A|Execution}} that could have been used against a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or the {{A|Coven}}. *Never say what your targets have claimed during the {{A|Day}} because you will attract unwanted attention by the evil roles. *{{A|Mafia}} and evil {{A|Neutral}} roles tend to claim {{A|Town}} roles that are easy to fake, such as {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Sheriff}}. This goes for everyone you {{A|Jail}}, but always ask for their wills. *'''If you manage to {{A|Jail}} the only {{A|Mafia Killing}} role while you know other {{A|Mafia}} roles exist''', you should keep them alive, continually {{A|Jailing}} them, while the {{A|Town}} safely finds the remaining members of the {{A|Mafia}}. Do not use this if there is a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, since they can kill you at any time. Keep in mind that a {{A|Witch}} may have teamed up with the {{A|Mafia}} and they might know who the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role is and could easily force you to {{A|Execute}} the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role before everyone finds the remaining members of the {{A|Mafia}}. *One tactic is to hit the {{A|Execute}} button at the start of the interrogation to put more pressure on their targets and then release the {{A|Execute}} button if the target has satisfied your tests. You should not use this tactic if you have a low-end computer prone to freezing as you will not be able to take back your decision for the rest of the {{A|Night}}, risking the loss of all your {{A|Executions}}. *Sometimes, you might want to be cautious about what you write in your {{A|Last Will}} ; reporting claims for important roles like {{A|Town Killings}} and {{A|Investigators}} could expose them to the {{A|Mafia}}. Generally, though, you should write as much as possible, since preserving information will help the {{A|Town}} more than it helps the {{A|Mafia}}. **Some {{A|Jailors}} like to put in their {{A|Last Will}} the alignment their prisoners claimed instead of the role. This has no real advantages because if they actually are evil, they take more claim space from you. However, the exception to this is {{A|Town Killing}}. This helps prevent a {{A|Witch}} from controlling the {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot a {{A|Townie}} with no risk because now they could visit a {{A|Veteran}} and be killed. Since {{A|Town Killing}} roles occupy the same role slot and have the same {{A|Investigator}} results, this doesn't change the information you give to the {{A|Town}} too much. *If you {{A|Jail}} someone who claims to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, consider telling them who you've {{A|Jailed}} (but not the roles they've claimed, unless you trust them completely), and of course, seize the list of who they've {{A|Roleblocked}}. Since you're both role-blockers, this lets you narrow down who to {{A|Jail}} to prevent the {{A|Mafia}} from killing. If the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is actually an evil role, most likely a {{A|Bootlegger}}, the list of who you've {{A|Jailed}} is generally not hugely useful to them. *On {{A|Day 1}} (or any {{A|Day}} with no leads), {{A|Jail}} someone you think might be killed that {{A|Night}} based on their name or actions. You can gather information, while also possibly protecting someone. *TwoPercentSkimm's "Aggressive Jailor" tactic may work, as it forces someone to claim or else face death. (For those unaware, immediately ask for role and count down from 3 to 1, hitting the {{A|Execute}} button immediately after you say 1. You can still change your mind however.) **Be careful, however, as you may end up {{A|Executing}} an innocent {{A|Townie}} or find yourself on the wrong end of a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf's}} stick should you fall for their claim. ***To avoid this, keep a list of claims in your {{A|Last Will}}. Look for claims that don't make sense (such as multiple unique {{A|Townies}}) *A good way of finding out if someone is evil is telling them you are a random person's name. If they die by {{A|Mafia}}, they are most likely evil. This can backfire if the random person you claimed to be is actually a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. **A similar tactic for {{A|Investigator}} and {{A|Sheriff}} claims is to act like you are suspicious (claiming that you think {your username} is suspicious) and asking them to investigate them the next {{A|Night}} for proof. 2 {{A|Nights}} later, if they have not already posted their results, {{A|Jail}} them again and ask for results. If these results are not accurate, {{A|Execute}}. ***Note that {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Disguisers}}, {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven Leaders}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, and {{A|Bootleggers}} can throw this strategy off by giving the claimer a justifiable reason for an inaccurate will. *If your target claims to be a {{A|Town Protective}} role, it's a good idea to tell them your name and order them to protect you every {{A|Night}}, threatening to have them hanged via your {{A|Last Will}} if you die. The only way this can be exploited is if the {{A|Town Protective}} claim is a member of the {{A|Mafia}} that has a {{A|Forger}} or {{A|Janitor}}. They can kill you without revealing that you should have been protected. *There is no reason to keep any non-{{A|Town}} role claims alive except for {{A|Amnesiac}}. This includes {{A|Survivor}} claims. You would need an {{A|Investigator}} to investigate them, or you could eliminate the non-{{A|Town}} roles and save the {{A|Investigator}} a precious {{A|Night}}. However, keep in mind some {{A|Survivor}} claims are actual {{A|Survivors}} trying to make sure they live, so you could be killing off a potential ally. This doesn't prevent them from siding with an evil faction, however. **However, keep in mind that {{A|Amnesiacs}} can remember evil roles, but you can {{A|Jail}} and {{A|Execute}} them quickly once they've remembered an evil role. **Also keep in mind that other {{A|Neutral}} roles, such as the aforementioned {{A|Survivor}} and the {{A|Jester}} role, might be considered a waste of an {{A|Execution}}. It would be wise to take into account the pros and cons of {{A|Executing}} these Neutral roles and act accordingly to your current situation. *In All Any or Coven All Any, be wary of {{A|Mayor}} claims if there is a {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. Often, these roles will claim to be {{A|Town}} roles that you would be very hesitant to {{A|Execute}}, allowing them to kill you that {{A|Night}} instead. This especially applies later in the game, when a {{A|Mayor}} should have revealed and a {{A|Spy}} should have shared their information. It is still not generally worth {{A|Executing}} them; if they actually are telling the truth, you lose an important {{A|Townie}} and your {{A|Executions}}. Always keep your {{A|Last Will}} updated just in case. *If you know who the {{A|Serial Killer}} is but you have run out of {{A|Executions}}, choosing whether or not to {{A|Jail}} them becomes difficult. In {{A|Jailing}} them, you will most likely die but will protect other {{A|Town}} for an extra {{A|Night}}. In not {{A|Jailing}} them, you leave them loose to kill someone else, possibly even you. **A similar case is true on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}} with {{A|Werewolves}}. In {{A|Jailing}} them, you kill yourself, but you also kill anyone visiting you because of the {{A|Werewolf's}} rampage, unlike with the {{A|Serial Killer}} . ***A similar case is also true for {{A|Pestilence}}, but is the case on all {{A|Nights}} and regardless of whether or not you have {{A|Executions}}, as {{A|Pestilence}} is the only role you can not {{A|Execute}}. ****Of course though, you can easily avoid death by being healed by a {{A|Doctor}} should they still be alive at this point. However, in the case of a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}, or {{A|Pestilence}}, the {{A|Doctor}} will die. **This is not the case for {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, the {{A|Juggernaut}}, or {{A|Neutral Chaos}} roles other than {{A|Pestilence}}, as they will not attack you if {{A|Jailed}}. {{A|Arsonists}} will know your identity if you {{A|Jail}} them however. *Unlike most roles, you can freely focus on people who are talkative {{A|Day 1}}, since you won't die if they're a {{A|Veteran}} trying to bait people in; this can both protect talkative {{A|Townies}} who are targeted by the {{A|Mafia}} and can let you press evil roles who are pretending to be a {{A|Veteran}} to deflect attention. *If there is a revealed {{A|Mayor}} and you have revealed yourself as the {{A|Jailor}}, consider saying something along the lines of, "I'll {{A|Jail}} the {{A|Mayor}} tonight." but {{A|Jail}} a different player. This could keep them safe while you interrogate other players. **However, if there is more than one member of the {{A|Mafia}} still alive, this could be dangerous (especially if both the {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Mafioso}} are still alive), as they will be notified that one of their teammates was {{A|Jailed}} instead of the {{A|Mayor}} and may attack them anyways. ***In this case, it is optimal to have a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}} stay on the {{A|Mayor}}. {{A|Trapper}} is also usable but is less optimal, as {{A|Traps}} take time to build and can be triggered by anyone. *If someone claims to be the {{A|Veteran}} in {{A|Jail}}, has not made said claim publicly yet, and has not shot anyone yet, you might want to put them as {{A|Vigilante}} in your {{A|Last Will}} with their permission. If you die and people see the {{A|Vigilante}} claim, many evil roles will attack them, so the {{A|Veteran}} can kill them with their alert the next {{A|Night}}. If you did this, the {{A|Veteran}} should continue on with their claim of being a {{A|Vigilante}} to prevent suspicion until they shoot and kill someone. **This strategy can also work with other important {{A|Town}} roles, such as {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Retributionist}}, but these can be uncovered by {{A|Investigators}} or many other methods of finding evils. *Although your status as the most powerful member of the {{A|Town}} may make you want to conceal your role as much as possible, it's often valuable for you to reveal at a key moment, especially late in the game when it seems like it's the {{A|Town's}} last chance to win. **Because it's unique, talks to people at {{A|Night}}, and can easily {{A|Execute}} anyone who claims it falsely, {{A|Jailor}} is almost impossible to fake. {{A|Town}} members will almost always believe you without question, and you can easily prove it if anyone doubts you. **It is common for {{A|Jailors}} to reveal themselves on the first {{A|Day}}, and this strategy has its benefits and its drawbacks. This is known as the Jailor Meta'''™''' and is common in the middle levels of {{A|Ranked}}. ***It benefits {{A|Town}} by giving them a confirmed townie to work with, such as by having {{A|Town Investigatives}} whisper you their wills. Since {{A|Town}} knows you are important, {{A|Town Protectives}} and {{A|Lookouts}} will often target you. {{A|Lookouts}} also give an opportunity for {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and {{A|Spies}} to confirm themselves by targeting you the first {{A|Night}}. This will also prevent dying {{A|Night 1}} and allowing any {{A|Janitors}} from claiming your role and leading the {{A|Town}} in this case. ***It hurts {{A|Town}} by revealing an important Townie. Any {{A|Townies}} whispering their wills can be uncovered by {{A|Blackmailers}} and picked off by the {{A|Mafia}} or used in fake {{A|Last Wills}}. While it does give you some protection from the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Serial Killers}}, it leaves you open to {{A|Arsonists}} and {{A|Jesters}}. {{A|Bootleggers}} and {{A|Witches}} will prevent you from ever using your {{A|Executions}} unless there's a {{A|Transporter}}. If you have a {{A|Werewolf}}, they can wreak havoc by targeting you {{A|Night 2}}, killing any {{A|Town Protectives}} and {{A|Lookouts}} on you, or you if there are no {{A|Town Protectives}} on you. If you have a {{A|Bodyguard}}, this will kill the {{A|Werewolf}}, but doing so still paves a path for {{A|Mafia}} to kill you. **Late in the game, you have a huge amount of information from the people you've {{A|Jailed}}, which you can rapidly put together with the rest of the {{A|Last Will}} to determine who to hang/{{A|Execute}}. **Your list of claims from your prisoners can pressure people into revealing their roles or help confirm certain {{A|Townies}}. Plus, you are essentially a confirmed {{A|Town}} since claiming {{A|Jailor}} will usually have the claimer {{A|Executed}} (unless there's a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Witch}}), and the {{A|Town}} won't hesitate to follow your lead. Use the trials during the {{A|Day}} to gain more claims from roles and don't hesitate to {{A|Execute}} any claim that feels suspicious or is a confirmed evil. ***If there are {{A|Town Protective}} claims, you can publicly order them to protect you. If you are killed, they will be outed as a fake and should be hanged. However, a {{A|Bootlegger}} can {{A|Roleblock}} them to put pressure on them the next {{A|Day}}. ***If you've {{A|Jailed}} a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Vigilante}}, or {{A|Veteran}} claim, say you are someone else. If that person shows up dead the next {{A|Day}}, you know they were a fake. Be careful, because if they're {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampire}}, or {{A|Coven}} and you claim you are one of their teammates, they'll know you're a liar. ***When putting together a plan, consider who (and how many) people could be lying to you. Your goal should be to find a set of commands you can give to the {{A|Town}} that will collectively leave the fake claims with no viable options. **If the role list has a limited amount of a specific {{A|Alignments}}, and more people claim roles that fit into said {{A|Alignment}} (ie. 3 people claim {{A|Sheriff}}), this does '''''NOT''''' mean the last person that claimed a role in said {{A|Alignment}} is guilty. Instead, you should take into consideration what info they have revealed so far. {{A|Jail}} the person that has revealed the least amount of information, and try to obtain some more information out of them. *Once you run out of {{A|Executions}}, your remaining abilities can be used either as a {{A|Roleblock}} or as protection for a revealed {{A|Mayor}}. This can help town by protecting a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or by keeping a {{A|Mafia Killing}} at bay. This can also be used to find the last {{A|Mafia Killing}} : if the {{A|Mafia}} doesn't kill one {{A|Night}}, its possible the person you {{A|Jailed}} was the last {{A|Mafia Killing}}. This is mostly useless for {{A|Neutral Killing}}, however, as {{A|Serial Killers}} will attack you, {{A|Werewolves}} will attack you if they can, {{A|Arsonists}} will usually choose not to ignite anyway, and you'll be {{A|Doused}} from {{A|Jailing}} them. {{A|Juggernauts}} are an exception, as it is usually safe to {{A|Jail}} them. *If somebody is unresponsive, it might be a good idea to simply write it down in your {{A|Last Will}} that the player wasn’t talking rather than {{A|Executing}} them. The next {{A|Day}}, take note of what happened during the {{A|Night}} and how they react to being {{A|Jailed}}, if they even react at all. This can help you make the choice of whether or not to {{A|Jail}} them again. ==Suspicious Claims== *Pay attention to the {{A|Investigator}} list; many evils will claim the corresponding good roles on their list in case an {{A|Investigator}} reveals their result. *{{A|Doctor}} is a common claim for {{A|Serial Killers}} and {{A|Potion Masters}} due to it fitting in their investigative result. If someone claims this, be sure to try and get a trusted {{A|Sheriff}} to investigate them and help you out if you're suspicious of either claim. *{{A|Bodyguard}} is commonly claimed by the {{A|Godfather}} as well as the {{A|Arsonist}} because it fits into their investigative result, and also helps them explain their immunity with their one vest. *{{A|Vigilante}} is a common claim from the {{A|Mafioso}} because it fits into their investigative result and allows them to accuse others of immunity. *A {{A|Mafioso}} will sometimes also claim {{A|Veteran}}, which likewise fits their result; the claim is occasionally used by {{A|Jester}} (or by anyone who has clearly been caught in a lie while claiming a valuable role) to explain their behavior. Some evils may be more reluctant to claim {{A|Veteran}} due to its uniqueness, but you can't depend on this. *{{A|Jester}} is a popular claim for evils. You should kill any {{A|Jester}} claims you see, unless {{A|Executing}} said {{A|Jester}} results in you not having enough {{A|Executions}} later on. *{{A|Bootleggers}} will often claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. Few other roles are likely to do so, as {{A|Tavern Keepers}} are easily confirmable. If there is a {{A|Spy}}, check the {{A|Mafia}} visits. If they align with your prisoner's will, they are more likely evil. Keep in mind of competent {{A|Disguisers}} as they can hide {{A|Mafia}} visits. *{{A|Consiglieres}} will usually claim {{A|Investigator}}. Be suspicious of an '{{A|Investigator}} ' who only catches non-{{A|Mafia}}. An '{{A|Investigator}} ' who knows a non-{{A|Mafia}} target's ''exact'' role is almost certainly a {{A|Consigliere}}. They could also be a {{A|Jester}} faking, but you should still {{A|Execute}}. *{{A|Hypnotists}} are tough due to their results being legitimate and only somewhat disprovable by {{A|Spies}}. They usually claim {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Transporter}}, or {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. Refer to the role list in order to catch them, and keep track of all wills given to you. *{{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Doctor}}, and {{A|Investigator}} are all important roles that are easy to fake and are thus very commonly claimed by evils. Ask for their {{A|Last Wills}}, and write it down in yours. *{{A|Executioner}} is also a common claim for evils. They are hoping that the {{A|Jailor}} or the town would ignore them because the {{A|Neutral Evil}} would less likely reveal themselves. You should also kill any {{A|Executioner}} claims as well. You shouldn't kill all of these claims since you only have 3 {{A|Executions}}, but if someone claims one of these roles, keep an eye on them throughout the game. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{JailorAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{JailorMessages}} ==Trivia== [[File:ToS Unity Being Jailed|thumb|330x330px|Animation upon being {{A|Jailed}} ]][[File:ToS Unity Being Released From Jail|thumb|330x330px|Animation upon being released from {{A|Jail}} ]] *If you are killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}} on the first {{A|Night}}, there is only a ~52% chance that you have {{A|Jailed}} them. Of course, everyone will know whether you {{A|Jailed}} them or not, as your {{A|Last Will}} will be covered in blood if you did. *Prior to [[Version_History - Town of Salem|Version A.0.1.8]], the {{A|Jailor}} was not a {{A|Unique}} role. *Prior to [[Version_History - Town of Salem|Version 2.0]], {{A|Jailors}} had {{A|Death Notes}} in the same form as any other killing role. This allowed them to be easily confirmed by revealing who they are in their {{A|Death Note}}. *Prior to [[Version_History - Town of Salem|Version 2.10]], {{A|Jailors}} had no {{A|Death Note}}. They are now the only {{A|Town Killing}} role with a {{A|Death Note}} and the only role with a different style of {{A|Death Note}}. *There is currently a bug where a dead player can still receive a message of them being hauled off to {{A|Jail}}. *According to a poll made by [http://town-of-salem.wikia.com/wiki/User:LevinSnakesRise LevinSnakesRise], the {{A|Jailor}} is the most loved role in Town of Salem which had 541 votes, the main reasoning because they can lead the {{A|Town}} to victory. *The {{A|Jailor}} is considered the most powerful {{A|Town}} role. It is the only {{A|Town}} role with a {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} as well as being the only role in the entire game which can override role block immunity and stop almost all visits on a target. *The {{A|Jailor}} is one of four roles that have a {{A|Day}} ability, the other being the {{A|Mayor}}, {{A|Pirate}} and a dead {{A|Medium}}. *The {{A|Jailor}} is one of the two {{A|Town}} roles that can talk at {{A|Night}}, the other being a {{A|Medium}}. *The {{A|Jailor}} is essentially a combination of all the {{A|Town}} sub-alignments; {{A|Town Investigative}} (with it's ability to talk at {{A|Night}}), {{A|Town Killing}}, (killing ability) {{A|Town Protective}} (giving {{A|Powerful Defense}}), and {{A|Town Support}} (role blocking). *If your prisoner did not die, and you chose to {{A|Execute}} them, you were possibly {{A|Roleblocked}} or {{A|Controlled}} off your target. You will know if this happens. **In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, your prisoner could have been protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}. You will know if this happens the next {{A|Day}}. ***Your prisoner could have also been {{A|Pestilence}}. You will also know if this happens, since the {{A|Jailor}} receives a special message upon being killed by a {{A|Pestilence}} in {{A|Jail}}. ****There was a bug where if {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Pestilence}}, their cause of death would appear to be obliterated by {{A|Pestilence}} twice. [[File:Screenshot 2020-05-07 at 3.20.21 PM.png|thumb|right|Bug]] *The {{A|Jailor}} is the only role in the game that is present in all non-{{A|Coven Expansion}} [[Game_Modes (ToS)|game modes]], excluding {{A|All Any}}. ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.4]] **Fixed bug when {{A|Jailor}} was killed by {{A|Jailing}} {{A|Pestilence}}. **Server no longer attempts to send {{A|Execution}} message to a {{A|Jailed}} player that has left the game. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.3]] **Added a {{A|Jailed}} screen overlay when you are {{A|Jailed}}. **Removed the click sound that played when the {{A|Jailor's}} {{A|Death Note}} was displayed. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.1.14]] **Added {{A|Jailor}} (no {{A|Executions}} remaining) vs. {{A|Coven Leader}} [[stalemate]] detector. **Added {{A|Hex Master}} vs. {{A|Jailor}} (no {{A|Executions}} remaining) [[stalemate]] detector. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.5.12200]] **{{A|Jailor}} is now shown with yellow text instead of grey text when talking in {{A|Jail}}. **The {{A|Jailor's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Jailor.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Jailor's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Jailor Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.3.10958]] **Fixed a bug where a {{A|Serial Killer}} who has been {{A|Executed}} by a {{A|Jailor}} would still see a message regarding them attacking the {{A|Jailor}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.1.10655]] **{{A|Werewolves}} can now be killed by a {{A|Bodyguard}} while {{A|Jailed}} when they attack the {{A|Jailor}}. **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.4.0.10404]] **{{A|Mafioso}} no longer sees target's {{A|Defense}} being too high while the target was {{A|Jailed}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.3.2.9706]] **{{A|Jailor}} {{A|Death Notes}} can no longer be spoofed. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.1.0.7320]] **Added the {{A|Jailor's}} {{A|Death Note}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.0]] **{{A|Jailors}} no longer have a {{A|Death Note}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|1.5.8.4235]] **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Jailor}} as a target. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|Alpha 0.1.8]] **{{A|Jailor}} is now {{A|Unique}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|Town of Salem Release]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Geôlier]] [[ru:Тюремщик]] [[Category:Town Killing roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Role blocking]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Defense]] [[Category:Unstoppable Attack]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

Selecting yourself will {{A|Ignite}} all {{A|Doused}} players, dealing an Unstoppable attack to each of them. * You will automatically {{A|Douse}} any players who visit you during the {{A|Night}}. This happens even if you are [[roleblocked]] or dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}. If you are {{A|jailed}} you will passively {{A|Douse}} the {{A|Jailor}}. Using this, you can identify who visited you, by looking at who got {{A|Doused}}. * Players will not know if they are {{A|Doused}} unless they are another {{A|Arsonist}}. * All {{A|Doused}} players will show up as "{{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Arsonist}} (plus {{A|Crusader}} in the {{A|Coven Expansion}})" to {{A|Investigators}}, while {{A|Consiglieres}} see all {{A|Doused}} players as an {{A|Arsonist}}, similar to a {{A|Hex Master's}} {{A|hex}}. **{{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven Leaders}} and {{A|Potion Masters}} are not affected by your {{A|Douse}}. They will still receive the true role of their target. *Since {{A|Sheriffs}} cannot find you anyway due to your [[Detection Immunity]], they are not affected by your {{A|Douse}} either. They will still receive the normal result of their target. *If you choose no action at {{A|Night}} you will clean gasoline off of yourself. This happens even if you're not {{A|Doused}}. If you select this option, you will not be able to be {{A|Ignited}} and you will not be {{A|Doused}} anymore. This is useful if there are other {{A|Arsonists}} in the game or you were transported/controlled into dousing yourself. ==Side Notes== *A {{A|Guardian Angel}} can purge the gasoline from a {{A|Doused}} target. **If a player is purged the same {{A|Night}} you {{A|Ignite}}, they will survive. This is due to the {{A|Guardian Angel}} having a [[Attributes (ToS)|Priority]] of 2, higher than the {{A|Ignition's}} 5. **If a {{A|Guardian Angel}} purges one of your {{A|Doused}} targets, the {{A|Doused}} icon next to their number will immediately disappear when the night ends. ***The {{A|Doused}} icon will also immediately disappear if your target is a fellow {{A|Arsonist}} who cleaned the gasoline off themself. *{{A|Jailors}} can prevent you from {{A|Dousing}} their targets, although they cannot prevent their targets from being {{A|Ignited}}. **Due to a visual bug, you will still see a {{A|Doused}} icon on {{A|jailed}} players even though they weren't actually {{A|Doused}}. *{{A|Spies}} can catch you getting {{A|Doused}} or cleaning yourself of gasoline with their {{A|bugging}} ability. *A {{A|Veteran}} will be {{A|Doused}} even if on alert, although you yourself will be killed. *If another {{A|Arsonist}} is in the game, {{A|Igniting}} your targets will {{A|Ignite}} all of ''their ''targets as well. *No {{A|Town Protective}} roles have an effect on your {{A|Douse}}, and cannot affect you when {{A|Igniting}} either. **A {{A|Crusader}} will still attack you, but you will not die due to your {{A|Basic Defense}}. *An {{A|Arsonist}} can and will {{A|Ignite}} themselves if they are {{A|Doused}} through the means of {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, or other {{A|Arsonists}}, unless they take the time to clean themselves off. *Due to the passive {{A|Douse}} mechanic, most roles that have [[Attributes (ToS)|Priority]] 3 or higher can get instantly {{A|Ignited}} when they visit an {{A|Arsonist}} who chooses to incinerate their targets, despite these roles never having been {{A|Doused}} on a previous night. Some of these roles include {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Bodyguard}} (but '''not''' {{A|Doctor}}), {{A|Crusader}}''',''' {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Jailor}} (in multiple {{A|Arsonist}} games), {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Framer}} and other {{A|Arsonists}}. ==Strategies== As an {{A|Arsonist}}, you are a massive threat to all opposing factions, as you break through all common forms of {{A|Defense}}, can not be detected, and can not be killed by ''any'' forms of protection, such as a {{A|Bodyguard}}. You also permanently change the investigative results of all targets you have {{A|Doused}}, making you a headache for an {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Consigliere}}. Therefore, most factions will try to kill you as they have no way of knowing who is and who isn't {{A|Doused}}. ===Who to Douse=== *Your ideal situation is to reach the end of the game with as many people as possible {{A|Doused}}. Therefore, your goal is to figure out ''who is likely to live until the end of the game'' and Douse said people, avoiding the ones who are likely to die by other means. Somebody just revealed themselves as the {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Doctor}} or another important {{A|Town}} role? Chances are this player will be dead the following {{A|day}} without you intervening. *Dousing people who are quiet has a lot of advantages. They're often evil roles, (who tend to live longer) and they're less likely to attract the attention of other killers. **If you find a good lead that somebody is a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, or {{A|Vampires}} it's best to Douse them because members of their respective faction cannot hurt each other (Apart from the use of a {{A|Transporter}} or (mostly in the {{A|Mafia's}} case) {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}); this means they generally tend to live longer and tend to be people you need to kill yourself. *You don't need to {{A|Douse}} ''absolutely'' everyone; {{A|Arsonists}} will automatically win in a 1v1 against any members of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Serial Killers}}, {{A|Vampires}}, {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, and a {{A|Jailor}} with no executions. However, multiple other roles are required to be killed by you in order to win: **A {{A|Werewolf}} can maul you and win if you haven't {{A|Doused}} them yet and a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} is coming next. They could also cause a draw by killing you when a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} is coming even though you {{A|Doused}} them. Your only chance is to have them {{A|Doused}} beforehand, and {{A|Ignite}} them on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}.[[File:Arsonist_Promo.png|thumb|The {{A|Arsonist}} Character Promo]] ***If you do not find the {{A|Werewolf}} by {{A|Night}} 4, you will most likely lose, since every {{A|Night}} after that is a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. **A {{A|Mayor}} can easily Hang you with their voting power when the {{A|day}} comes around. **A {{A|Veteran}} with alerts left is a risk for you, and a mind duel between the two of you will determine the winner. **A {{A|Jailor}} with executions won't even give you a chance to Douse him, let alone {{A|Ignite}} him. **A {{A|Hex Master's}} final attack can prove your demise if you do not have them {{A|Doused}}. If you end up in a 1v1 situation, you will most likely lose, since the {{A|Hex Master}} only needs one {{A|Night}} to {{A|Hex}} and kill you, while you need two {{A|Nights}} to {{A|Douse}} and {{A|Ignite}} them. **A {{A|Medusa}} with {{A|Stone Gazes}} left or a {{A|Necronomicon}} can easily break through your defense. You'd rarely end up in a 1v1 situation before {{A|Night}} three, which means she'll have the {{A|Necronomicon}} and guarantee you not winning. **A {{A|Necromancer}} could prevent you from winning if the right roles are in the graveyard and haven't been used yet, such as a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} or {{A|Pestilence}}. **A {{A|Plaguebearer}} can infect you and become {{A|Pestilence}} before you can kill them, dooming you for death. If they're already {{A|Pestilence}}, you lose. Your only hope is to leave one person alive to Hang them and choose their fate. **{{A|Juggernauts}} pose major threats to you. As their abilities increase, their threat to you also increases. Their attacks will always kill you, meaning you must find a way to incinerate or Hang them early on. *In particular, while you need the {{A|Mayor}} dead to win, you may want to avoid dousing them yourself in the hope that someone else will kill him for you as he's likely to be protected by {{A|Lookouts}} or {{A|Transporters}}. *The {{A|Survivor}} and the {{A|Witch}} can win together with you, so avoid dousing them unless you think an evil role is claiming them. Likewise, dousing a {{A|Jester}} is pointless because they're trying to die anyway; dousing an {{A|Executioner}} is also pointless because their goal doesn't conflict with yours either. If you're certain you've identified any of these roles, don't bother dousing them. Avoid dousing {{A|Witches}} in particular as it's important because they can prevent you from {{A|Igniting}} if they identify you. **However, remember that evil roles often claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} or pretend to be a {{A|Jester}} or {{A|Executioner}}. The last thing you want is to {{A|Ignite}} your {{A|Doused}} targets, only to find that you're alone with a {{A|Werewolf}} who kills you the next {{A|Night}}, or that the {{A|Jester}} and {{A|Survivor}} you spared are actually members of the {{A|Mafia}} who proceed to Hang you. Additionally, remember that {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Jesters}}, {{A|Executioners}}, and {{A|Witches}} might vote unpredictably; if you {{A|Ignite}} with one member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Townie}} left and a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Neutral Evil}}, you run the risk of the swing vote turning against you and Hanging you. **The {{A|Arsonist}} can be a big threat to {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}}, {{A|Witches}} and {{A|Executioners}}, so these roles might Hang you even if the fact of you being known as an {{A|Arsonist}} is revealed. This is because a {{A|Survivor}} and {{A|Executioner}} know that your attack goes through {{A|Basic (Defense)}} and {{A|Powerful Defense}}, and may Hang you if they believe you {{A|Doused}} them. An {{A|Amnesiac}} may Hang you so they are able to remember your role, and a {{A|Witch}} may want to side with another rival faction or evil role, also note that it is near impossible for {{A|Witches}} to win with you since they are {{A|Doused}} upon visiting you. If they are showing any of these plans, your best bet to survive is to Douse (if you haven't already) them and {{A|Ignite}}. You may lose a possible ally, but it's better than dying right off the bat. Remember that you should only kill these roles as the last resort as they can't do as much harm to you as other ones. **However, if an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers your role and wins, you also win. *Trying to bait people into visiting you can be a good way to get a lot of players {{A|Doused}}. Asking for {{A|Town Protective}} roles on you can work well. **You may also use this to get an idea of what roles certain people are, for instance, If you are [[roleblocked]], anyone who is {{A|Doused}} who you didn't directly visit is either a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}}. If you are attacked, whoever is {{A|Doused}} that {{A|Night}} who you didn't visit is almost guaranteed to be a killing role, such as a {{A|Mafioso}}. You can use this information to give yourself a viable {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} claim. ***Once you are falsely confirmed as an important {{A|Town Investigative}} role, you can ask for a {{A|Town Protective}} role to protect you, which will Douse them. *While not foolproof, it is possible to not {{A|Douse}} anyone until very late game. This prevents you from being killed or exposed by {{A|Veterans}}, {{A|Jailors}}, and {{A|Lookouts}} (but it also leaves you open to {{A|Spies}}). If you are certain all {{A|Town Investigative}} roles are dead, then you can claim a role before dousing. You must find a happy medium between remaining completely silent and talking too much. ===When to {{A|Ignite}}=== *Ideally, you only want to {{A|Ignite}} when it would win you the game; this means leaving you with only one other person alive, at most. {{A|Igniting}} too early has several disadvantages: **It wastes a chance to Douse, slowing down your ultimate victory. **It reduces the number of people who could be the {{A|Arsonist}}, making you easier to find. Depending on who's left, they might even identify you instantly, especially if an {{A|Investigator}} has previously investigated you. **Another disadvantage to {{A|Igniting}} too early is that it exposes {{A|Last Wills}}. Since {{A|Townies}}' {{A|Last Wills}} provide confirmed evidence, it's to your advantage to avoid making them appear. On the other hand, remember that very few {{A|Last Wills}} are likely to outright expose you; you are immune to {{A|Sheriffs}} and only an {{A|Investigator}} can see you directly, but you are functionally indistinguishable from a {{A|Bodyguard}}. **An early {{A|Ignition}} also incontrovertibly confirms the presence of an {{A|Arsonist}}, which is generally very bad for you - if you were investigated prior your result becomes more suspicious, and the town will become more aggressive about Hanging anyone who potentially has {{A|Night}} immunity, both of which are common ways for {{A|Arsonists}} to lose. **If you are {{A|Doused}} by another {{A|Arsonist}}, wait a {{A|Night}} and stay idle. Doing so will clean the gasoline off of you, making you unable to be {{A|Ignited}} and also revealing yourself to the other {{A|Arsonist}}. However, this could backfire if a {{A|Spy}} bugs you. This will confirm you as {{A|Arsonist}} as no other role gets this message. *It can occasionally be worth {{A|Igniting}} early if you have a number of dangerous threats {{A|Doused}} (such as the entire {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Vampires}}, the {{A|Werewolf}}, and so on). Try to figure out who will be left after your {{A|Ignition}}, and determine if they'll be able to catch you before you can Douse and {{A|Ignite}} the remaining targets; weigh the risk of being killed by the threats you've already {{A|Doused}} vs. the risk of being caught by the people you haven't {{A|Doused}} yet. *In [[Game Modes - Coven#Coven Ranked|Ranked]] games, it is sometimes to your advantage to {{A|Ignite}} the {{A|Jailor}} if you can be sure of avoiding the {{A|Lookout}} (in particular, note if ​​​​​​people [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to the {{A|Jailor}}, and if multiple {{A|Town Investigative}} roles have claimed). *When there are multiple {{A|Arsonists}}, it is generally a bad idea to {{A|Ignite}} early. Resist your impatience and go slowly - multiple {{A|Arsonists}} have a huge advantage and {{A|Igniting}} early on generally throws it away in one manner or another. **The only reason an {{A|Arsonist}} would want to {{A|Ignite}} early is to eliminate someone who they absolutely have to kill off before they are caught. However, when you know for a fact that there are multiple {{A|Arsonists}}, the risk of being caught decreases sharply - the remaining one can just {{A|Ignite}} to wrap up the game. **Early {{A|Ignites}} risk burning your fellow {{A|Arsonist}} (or yourself, if you're {{A|Doused}}) before you've identified each other. The longer you wait, the more likely you'll find each other. **Every {{A|Ignite}} wastes a {{A|Night}}. Even with the risk of dousing the same people, it generally isn't worth it to {{A|Ignite}} until you think it will win you the game. **{{A|Arsonists}} are fairly difficult to find. {{A|Igniting}} early narrows down your identities. **The number of people who die in an early {{A|Ignition}} with multiple {{A|Arsonists}} will let the town know what they're up against, which generally makes you more vulnerable, especially because there are only going to be a few candidates left. **Only a few roles pose a direct threat to {{A|Arsonists}}; only {{A|Ignite}} if you're sure you're targeting them. If you ''fail'' to Douse Investigators, you're increasing the chance that they'll find you. Blind {{A|Ignites}} don't help you, even with multiple {{A|Arsonists}}. **That said, with multiple {{A|Arsonists}}, it's often tricky to figure out whether your {{A|Ignition}} will win you the game or not. Don't wait ''too'' long, and don't be shy about {{A|Igniting}} if you're confident it will give you a plurality. **Also, if another {{A|Arsonist}} is hanged, it can be a good idea to {{A|Ignite}} that {{A|Night}}, as you don't know how many people are {{A|doused}}, and you may waste time by re-{{A|dousing}} someone the other {{A|Arsonist}} doused. *In modes where multiple {{A|Arsonists}} are possible, some people {{A|Ignite}} on the first {{A|Night}} in order to see if another {{A|Arsonist}} is present. This is generally a terrible idea for several reasons: **You're informing the Town that there are multiple {{A|Arsonists}}, too; this knowledge is generally far more useful to them than to you. They might also find one of your teammates outright due to the ignition's kills and Hang them, turning this from terrible move into a throw. **You risk burning yourself if another {{A|Arsonist}} {{A|Doused}} you that {{A|Night}}. **If there are no other {{A|Arsonists}}, you waste a precious {{A|Night}} and accomplish nothing. **If the ''are'' other {{A|Arsonists}}, it can give you people to ally with later in the game, but {{A|Igniting}} on the first {{A|Night}} can waste a {{A|Night}} of dousing someone who may turn out important for other factions later in the game. ===Threats=== *Even though you have {{A|Basic Defense}}, {{A|Night}} killers like the {{A|Serial Killer}} and {{A|Mafia}} are still the greatest threat to you. Most of the time, all it takes is one hit from one and a {{A|Death Note}} outing you to put you on trial. If you are hit, you need to have a strategy to deal with the accusation; note that there is no strategy that works reliably. **You can claim you were {{A|Transported}}, but most of the time the {{A|Town}} will expect a {{A|Transporter}} to come forward to confirm this, which means it is not a reliable strategy. **You can claim {{A|Survivor}} (or imply that you're an {{A|Executioner}}), but this is unlikely to save you after you've been accused; it's better used as an early claim to avoid being attacked in the first place. **You can claim you were healed by a {{A|Doctor}} ({{A|Doctors}} are less likely to reveal than {{A|Transporters}}, and the {{A|Town}} won't expect it). But be warned that a {{A|Doctor}} not revealing to healing might be suspicious, also note that since {{VH|Version 3.2.4}}, the messages for healing and having {{A|Defense}} have been generalized, thus meaning that players might be more suspicious of people who a {{A|Doctor}} healed if no one backs them up. **You can claim that you're a {{A|Bodyguard}}, but since they only have one bulletproof vest (and therefore the chance of it being hit is low, especially if you haven't been publicly revealed as a {{A|Bodyguard}} earlier), this rarely works. A {{A|Death Note}} can leave you hanging in the case you claimed this, however. ** You can simply say that your accuser is lying, especially if it's a {{A|Death Note}} from an evil role. However, the {{A|Town}} usually accepts accusations of people having any form of {{A|Defense}}, and based on the circumstances hanging you would prove better in the long run. *** You can deny that you are immune and that a {{A|Consigliere}} must have revealed you to be an important {{A|Town}} role, and that the {{A|Mafia}} is attempting to kill you off. Note that you will probably have to claim an actually important Town role while making this argument (especially since, with your role already known to the Mafia, you would have no reason to keep hiding it.) ** If there is someone else that the {{A|Town}} regards as suspicious, it is good to focus attention on them and off of yourself. Most of the time the {{A|Town}} will not pay attention to {{A|Death Note}}, but when they do it is important to shift focus away, and putting it on someone who is already considered possibly evil is a great way to make people forget about you. Try not to make it too obvious though. Remember to use commenting to drown out the smart {{A|Townies}} who've brought up your immunity. *Certain roles like {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Bootleggers}}, {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven Leaders}} and {{A|Jailors}} can prevent you from dousing people and {{A|Igniting}}, even if they only find you very late in the game. It can sometimes be worth an early {{A|Ignition}} to kill them. **The {{A|Jailor}} can also, of course, execute you. It's important to have a claim ready for if you're {{A|jailed}}; {{A|Bodyguard}} is a logical claim since it's the {{A|Town}} entry in your investigative result, but since you share it with the {{A|Godfather}} and since it's such a convenient claim, it may make the {{A|Jailor}} suspicious of you, especially if the Town already knows an {{A|Arsonist}} is present. Other roles with easy-to-fake {{A|Last Wills}}, such as the {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Medium}}, and {{A|Doctor}}, are all decent claims as well provided you're not worried about {{A|Investigators}}. You can claim {{A|Doused}} if an {{A|Investigator}} comes to falsify your out-of-result claims. **A {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} is essentially forced to control you every {{A|Night}} if they find you to prevent their death from incineration. If they know a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Medusa}}, they will very likely force you to visit them to keep themselves alive. It is imperative to find and Hang them before they find you. *The {{A|Hex Master}} is a dangerous threat since they are characteristically you but with a team. If they have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they can {{A|Hex}} you without risk of being {{A|Doused}} from visiting you. Make sure to find and Hang them, because if they've {{A|Hexed}} too many people or you end up in a 1v1 with them not {{A|Doused}}, they can auto-win for the {{A|Coven}}. *{{A|Consiglieres}} can be a threat since they can identify you if not many people have been {{A|Doused}}. They could also alert the {{A|Town}} in a {{A|Death Note}}, and instruct any {{A|Bootleggers}} to [[role block]] you. However, they can be thrown off if they investigate someone who has been {{A|Doused}} themselves because they will apprehend the {{A|Arsonist}} result and might go for them. However they may ask the {{A|Mafia}} to attack their targets to check for immunity instead. *{{A|Investigators}} are no longer that dangerous to you, because all {{A|Doused}} targets show up as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}} to them, preventing suspicion to you. Still, though, your investigative result is still suspicious, especially if it's the beginning of the game or you have just {{A|Ignited}} (since not many people have been {{A|Doused}}). If you are accused by one, you could claim to be {{A|Doused}} yourself. This makes it especially important to {{A|Ignite}} only when it would win you the game; claiming to be {{A|Doused}} and still being alive after your {{A|Ignition}} makes it obvious that you were lying. *The {{A|Werewolf}} can ignore your {{A|Basic Defense}} and can catch you by targeting people who haven't yet been {{A|Doused}}. Of course, if you ''know'' who the {{A|Werewolf}} is, you can often have them Hanged or Douse them on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. *The {{A|Vampires}} are a threat because they can both identify you by failing to convert you, and can identify you by process of elimination if they take over much of the {{A|Town}}. They're one of the reasons it's a bad idea to {{A|Ignite}} early since even if you thought the non-{{A|Doused}} targets were harmless {{A|Doctors}} and {{A|Sheriffs}}, you might find yourself surrounded by {{A|Vampires}} who will immediately deduce your identity. *{{A|Transporters}} are dangerous because they can prevent you from {{A|Dousing}} your intended target, and they can even make you {{A|Douse}} yourself. Unlike the {{A|Hex Master|ToS}}, you can at least figure out that your target was swapped because the {{A|Doused}} effect icon will correctly appear on the player you ended up targeting. Keep in mind that a {{A|Transporter}} can't keep you from {{A|Igniting}}. *The revealed {{A|Mayor}} can kill you one-on-one, and can force you to claim a role; but since they're also a major target for the {{A|Mafia}} (and will often prioritize them over you, especially if they haven't personally been {{A|Doused}}), they're often not your first concern. Additionally, one advantage of having a confirmed {{A|Mayor}} is that you can easily Douse them as only the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Transporter}} can stop you. *The {{A|Veteran}} is an obvious threat in which they can kill you if you try to Douse them; worse, your usual strategy of waiting for the {{A|Mafia}} or the {{A|Serial Killer}} to kill them for you might not work here, since the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Serial Killer}} want to save the confirmed {{A|Veteran}} for last as well (and that means they're probably going to hit ''you'' first). And worst of all, you don't automatically win a 1 v 1 against a {{A|Veteran}}, so you need to eliminate them somehow. Your best options are to wait and hope someone else takes a potshot at them despite the risk or to eventually Douse them near the end and hope they wasted their alerts. *The {{A|Town Protective}} roles, {{A|Spy}}, {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Vampire Hunter}} , and {{A|Medium}} are usually not threats to you. The {{A|Spy}} can bug and see your {{A|Douse}}/cleaning messages, the {{A|Medium}} can bring back logic and information from the dead, and a {{A|Vigilante}} can discover your {{A|Basic Defense}} with a potshot, but these are not normally major threats compared to the above. If you're reasonably certain that everyone you haven't {{A|Doused}} is one of these roles (plus unaffiliated {{A|Neutrals}}), then it might be worth {{A|Igniting}} early, since unless you screw up, a {{A|Town}} composed only of these roles will have a lot of trouble catching you. *{{A|Pestilence}} is a major problem for you since you will need help from others to Hang them. Your best bet is usually to hold off on visiting or {{A|Igniting}} once the Horseman has been revealed - visiting risks dying to {{A|Pestilence's}} rampage or by visiting them directly, while {{A|Ignition}} risks leaving you alone with the Horseman since they are immune to '''ALL''' attacks, including your {{A|Ignition}}. Given how quickly they kill, and how difficult they can be to find, you will usually need all the time you can have and can't afford to cut things faster by {{A|Igniting}}. Even if you believe your {{A|Ignition}} would leave three people alive, and even if you trust the last person to side with you, there's a risk {{A|Pestilence}} could kill the last person that {{A|Night}} - plus, by {{A|Igniting}} down to three people, you confirm yourself as non-{{A|Town}}, whereas otherwise, you can potentially have them to Hang {{A|Pestilence}} without them realizing it will lead to your victory. ===What to Claim=== The {{A|Arsonist}} is a powerful role, but dousing many people could be a waste if you're just going to be Hanged (or executed) anyway. There are ways your role could be revealed like investigation, but you need to have a backup story if you are investigated, a role, of course, is the most believable, there are claims that could potentially fool other players if used correctly. *One option is to claim to be a {{A|Survivor}}, which explains your {{A|Basic Defense}}; this is more likely to have you Hanged if people are being killed by a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, because {{A|Survivor}} is a common claim for {{A|Neutral Killing}}, whom all factions want dead. If you do claim to be a {{A|Survivor}}, it's important to do it early, ''before'' you are attacked; claiming it after you're accused of having a higher {{A|Defense}} value than the attacker's {{A|Attack}} value will almost certainly have you Hanged since the {{A|Town}} has no real reason to keep a {{A|Survivor}} alive. *Another option is to imply that you're an {{A|Executioner}}; accuse someone at random, and (assuming they're {{A|Town}}) thank the {{A|Town}} after they're Hanged. You can even just thank the {{A|Town}} after a random Hang of any innocent {{A|Townie}}. This will both divert attention and explain your {{A|Basic Defense}}. You can also explain your investigative results by claiming you were {{A|Transported}}. This is believable as {{A|Transporters}} often {{A|Transport}} themselves with roles with a {{A|Defense}} value to ward off suspicion or claim you might be {{A|Doused}}. However, it carries several risks; you may be executed by a {{A|Jailor}} or Hanged by a vengeful {{A|Town}}, and {{A|Investigators}} and {{A|Consiglieres}} can still identify you. You may also claim {{A|Doused}}, however, if you decide to {{A|Ignite}} after claiming {{A|Doused}}, then it proves you weren’t {{A|Doused}}. Also, if you delay on dousing to reinforce your disguise, you may find the {{A|Town}} turning their suspicion back to you, with no real way of ending things quickly. *If you're going to claim a {{A|Town}} role, {{A|Bodyguard}} is the logical choice. Aside from that, you can almost always fake a {{A|Last Will}} to improve your chances of people believing you. However, claiming to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} after a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or confirmed {{A|Townie}} died can be extremely suspicious, since the {{A|Town}} will wonder why you weren't protecting them. You can even claim to have to use your vest if attacked, but this forces you to stay with the fact you have already used your vest. If you are attacked again, there's nothing you can conclude overall other than hope you aren't outed. **However, {{A|Bodyguards}} and {{A|Arsonists}} share investigation results, and {{A|Bodyguard}} is a common {{A|Arsonist}} (and {{A|Godfather}}) claim. Claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} may raise suspicion and may cause you to be Hanged. **You don't have to claim {{A|Bodyguard}}, as you can claim that you were {{A|Doused}} as cover. *Claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}} with a {{A|Last Will}} that shows everyone you {{A|Doused}} as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}} can work well, as you can also claim you were {{A|Doused}} yourself. However, you can be busted by a {{A|Lookout}} who notices the shift between everyone that has been {{A|Doused}}. This works in situations where you need to claim a role and fast, otherwise you would be Hanged. **However, this has a downside of revealing who was {{A|Doused}}, which can create many other problems for you, like people panicking and making you the top threat. To counter this, change some names to quiet people to create more confusion and less panicking. *Claiming to be a {{A|Witch}} with only {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral}} roles alive can help your chance of survival. However, if no one has been controlled, the {{A|Neutral Evil}} slot is taken by {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Jester}}, or you have {{A|Ignited}}, then this will not work. If you claim to be a {{A|Witch}} in a 1 v 1 v 1 scenario, you can cause the {{A|Mafia}}, or any other {{A|Neutral}} role to Hang the last remaining opponent, thus winning all other match-ups. However, experienced killers will ask who you have controlled and their exact roles, so be wary. This works best if you haven't {{A|Doused}}. *If an {{A|Investigator}} lets out your investigation result and attracts suspicion to you or if you're directly accused by one, you can claim any believable {{A|Town}} role and then claim you must've been {{A|Doused}} and thus, framed. Although this tactic does not always work and the {{A|Town}} wouldn't usually believe you, it's more effective in the start of the game or mid-game when there's a good number of people that could possibly be {{A|Doused}} and the {{A|Town}} doesn't have their suspicions confirmed or fully locked on to you. **Careful, though, if another {{A|Arsonist}} {{A|Ignites}} and people remember you claimed {{A|Doused}}, you will be cast under extreme suspicion from the {{A|Town}} causing you to likely be Hanged. *Claiming {{A|Investigator}} dramatically decreases suspicion—listing down {{A|Doused}} targets will convince players that you're really an investigator, and other {{A|Investigators}} can no longer be a threat to you, for you can claim that you are {{A|Doused}} as well. Additionally, {{A|Investigator}} is hardly ever a role claimed by evil roles. *If you feel more comfortable in a {{A|Coven}} match claiming within your investigation results, {{A|Crusader}} is also viable. People expect this as an {{A|Arsonist}} claim less, as they are usually more accustomed to Classic. **However, you have to pick players that haven't been visited on the {{A|Night}} you claim to have protected them, or else players can call you out on your fake {{A|Last Will}}. This makes it as suspicious as a {{A|Lookout}} claim with "no visits" every {{A|Night}}. *Claiming a powerful {{A|Town}} role such as {{A|Mayor}} can give you an extra {{A|Night}} to {{A|Ignite}}. This is a high risk, high reward - if you do this, be sure you are ready to {{A|Ignite}} the next {{A|day}}. *You can also claim you were {{A|Doused}} to the {{A|Town}} anytime; they'll assume you're just a bad {{A|Jester}}, and they'll leave you alone. Note this can go awry as they'll either try to kill you at {{A|Night}} or end up Hanging you instead. ==Playing against {{A|Arsonists}}== *If multiple people are showing up as an {{A|Arsonist's}} result, then they might be {{A|Doused}} themselves. To use this tactic, you will need to refer to the role list and your gut to find out who is {{A|Doused}} and who isn't, since you will have no way of knowing otherwise. **Anyone who contains the investigative result of the {{A|Arsonist}} and is still alive after an {{A|Ignition}} can be an {{A|Arsonist}} themselves. *If you are an {{A|Investigator}} and a {{A|Lookout}} has died with the name of a visitor that visited one of your previous targets, it may be worth checking the same target again. If they show up as a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}} instead of the result you had previously, they have been {{A|Doused}} and the person in the {{A|Lookout}} will is more likely the {{A|Arsonist}}. *If you are a {{A|Jailor}}, take your claims ''very seriously''. Someone that is {{A|Doused}} has a completely different investigation result, and talks with their claim. If they were shown to be {{A|Doused}}, think about their claim and the role list. The {{A|Arsonist}} might have {{A|Doused}} a {{A|Bootlegger}} who claims {{A|Tavern Keeper}} in {{A|Jail}}, and you not executing that {{A|Bootlegger}} gives the {{A|Mafia}} another chance. Depending on the role list, sometimes you might have to go with your gut feeling and execute that person. *As a {{A|Consigliere}}, if you find a possible {{A|Arsonist}} it's best to out them in the {{A|Death Note}} of any {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles to put suspicion on them. If they turned out to be a {{A|Doused}} target, their credibility decreases and you can kill them if they turn out to be an important role to kill. *As a {{A|Coven Leader}}, if you have a {{A|Medusa}} with {{A|Stone Gazes}} left, you can control the {{A|Arsonist}} into her gaze to eliminate the problem entirely. Doing this with a {{A|Veteran}} can have a similar effect. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{ArsonistAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{ArsonistMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.11.5389}}, {{A|Doused}} targets would be notified that they were {{A|Doused}}. {{A|Doused}} targets would also keep their investigative results and would not be changed into the current {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or {{A|Crusader}} result. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.3.2.9706}} {{A|Arsonists}} would be killed by {{A|Bodyguards}} and {{A|Trappers}} protecting their target. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.6}}, {{A|Arsonists}} would not {{A|Douse}} visitors. *According to a poll made by [https://town-of-salem.fandom.com/wiki/User:LevinSnakesRise LevinSnakesRise], the {{A|Arsonist}} is the third most hated role in Town of Salem with 171 votes, saying the role was too slow and was boring for taking too long to kill anyone (Similar to {{A|Framer}}). Also note that this poll is outdated, as the {{A|Arsonist}} role has received multiple buffs after this poll. *The {{A|Arsonist}} is the only {{A|Neutral Killing}} outside the {{A|Coven Expansion}} to have permanent [[Detection Immunity]]. *The {{A|Arsonist}} is one of two roles to have 2 [[Avatars (ToS)|skins]], the other being the {{A|Vigilante}}. *Paradoxically, it is often good for other {{A|Neutral Killings}} for the {{A|Town}} to suspect an {{A|Arsonist}}. Simply not killing as a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} is a good way for {{A|Investigators}} to not suspect your results. *Some players mistakenly believe that a {{A|Arsonist's}} {{A|Douse}} will make you appear to be an {{A|Arsonist}} to a {{A|Sheriff}} (and therefore appear Innocent). However this is not the case so don't fall for this. ==Gallery== ApocalypseArsonist.png|Alternate Avatar ==History== *{{VH|3.3.1}} **Fixed issue with {{A|Arsonist}} passive {{A|Douses}} not working on {{A|Investigator}} and {{A|Juggernaut}} in some scenarios. *{{VH|3.2.5}} **{{A|Arsonist}} now passively {{A|Douses}} anyone that visits them. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate {{A|Doused}} players for the {{A|Arsonist}} ([[File:SpecialLabel Doused.png|30x30px]]). **The {{A|Arsonist's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Arsonist.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Arsonist's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Arsonist Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **{{A|Arsonists}} can no longer die to a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trapper}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Arsonist}} now has passive {{A|Ignition}}. *{{VH|1.5.11.5389}} **Non-{{A|Arsonist}} players no longer receive the message "You were Doused in gas!" when {{A|Doused}}. **The {{A|Arsonist}} now fools an {{A|Investigator}}. **The {{A|Arsonist}} now fools a {{A|Consigliere}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Pyromane]] [[it:Incendiario]] [[es:Incendiario]] [[de:Brandstifter]] [[pl:Podpalacz]] [[ru:Поджигатель]] [[tr:Kundakçı]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Neutral Killing roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Unstoppable Attack]] [[Category:Astral]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
