'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |mustkill=Given Target (via Hang) }} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You will receive a target at the start of the game. Kill your target via [[Hanging (ToS)|Hanging]] to win. **Your target will always start the game as a {{A|Townie}}. **Your target cannot be the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}. **You must Hang your target while being alive. ***If you die after Hanging your target, you will still win (with the exception of leaving the game). **If your target is converted into a {{A|Vampire}}, you will still remain as an {{A|Executioner}} with the same target. **If you leave the game after you get your target Hanged, you will '''not''' win. **Multiple {{A|Executioners}} and/or {{A|Guardian Angels}} may share the same target.{{LabelTarget}} *You have {{A|Basic Defense}}. *If your target dies during the {{A|night}}, you will turn into a {{A|Jester}}. ==Strategy== *Pay close attention to the {{A|Last Wills}} and claims of others in order to determine just what the holes in the {{A|Town's}} knowledge of your target are. If a {{A|Sheriff}} says your target is not suspicious, you can still claim to be an {{A|Investigator}}. Accuse them and say that you investigated your said target and the investigative results that showed up for you were {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}}. If an {{A|Investigator}} lists them as having a result that includes a possible evil role, accuse them of that role (e.g. if they claim to be a {{A|Doctor}}, claim to be a {{A|Lookout}} and accuse them of visiting someone who was killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}}, since {{A|Doctors}} and {{A|Serial Killers}} are part of the same investigative result). Occasionally, there will be an error or coincidence in a {{A|Last Will}} that you can use to push an accusation against your target, such as them being visited by the {{A|Mafia}} in a {{A|Spy}} {{A|Last Will}} on a {{A|night}} when the {{A|Mafia}} didn't kill anyone. Note that while being the last person visited by a dead {{A|Investigator}} is not an indication of anything, many inexperienced {{A|Townies}} can still be swayed by it in [[Classic Mode|Classic]]. *Another strategy is to wait until about {{A|day}} 3. Then claim {{A|Investigator}} and accuse your target. Try to get them on the stand but also try to get them to vote innocent. If you are able to convince them to vote innocent, stall long enough for the {{A|day}} to end, then ask the {{A|Jailor}} to jail and execute your target. If he does, you will turn into a {{A|Jester}} that {{A|night}} and the role of the innocent {{A|Town}} member will appear, giving yourself enough suspicion to be Hanged. The downside is that the {{A|Jailor}} might not jail your target, giving them enough time to prove themselves and Hang you, denying your victory, or if experienced players see that you were a clever {{A|Executioner}} turned {{A|Jester}} and simply call you out. *If people figure out you are the {{A|Executioner}} and put you on trial, say something along the lines of, "Okay, you got me. I'm the {{A|Executioner}}." Hopefully, they will think that you're a {{A|Jester}} and are trying to get yourself Hanged. Most people will then vote innocent. Thus, you will be off the hook and survive. However, this will probably backfire in some cases as many {{A|Serial Killers}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, {{A|Godfathers}}, and other roles with {{A|Basic Defense}} may claim it. *If you are pressured to claim a role, you may just tell the truth, side with the majority and before the majority wins, ask for your target to be Hanged. You may also say you can be an extra vote so they can focus on Hanging the true evil roles while your target gets Hanged near the end of the game. Note that this may not work if you are jailed, depending on the {{A|Jailor}}. *If a {{A|Townie}} finds a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, you may want to quickly side with them and try to counter whatever the accuser might be saying, then whisper to the member of the {{A|Mafia}} about how you saved them, and you want to side with them, and to do so, they must help with Hanging your target. *Wait until later in the game, especially if not many evils are dead. The {{A|Town}} will get desperate and should have a better chance of believing your claim. However, this could backfire as they might know who the other {{A|Townies}} are due to the process of elimination and might Hang you instead even if there are bigger targets. *As it says in the description, use everything you can to get them Hanged, starting with the accusation. After you accuse your target, make them claim their role and use other possible roles they could be and use that to your advantage. Do this by taking what they claim and accuse them of being a similar, evil role. For example, if they claimed {{A|Investigator}} and they posted their {{A|Last Will}}, try to make them look like a {{A|Consigliere}} or {{A|Witch}}. This is extremely effective if they defended an evil role. *You can claim to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} that role blocked your target and was attacked and healed, then claim they are the {{A|Serial Killer}}. This strategy is uncommon and even some more experienced players might believe it. It works especially well if your target is a {{A|Doctor}}. *If you're playing a game mode such as [[Classic Mode]] where roles are heavily limited, you can claim the same role as your target to throw suspicion on them. The downside, of course, is that you could be Hanged instead. However, the risk might be lower than you think, since if the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} have discovered that you're an {{A|Executioner}} (e.g. By trying to kill you and discovering that you have {{A|Basic Defense}}) they will almost certainly side with you, meaning that you only need to split the {{A|Town}} a bit in order to win. This naturally won't work if they claim a role that can be easily confirmed. It works best if your target happens to be a {{A|Sheriff}}, since any {{A|Investigators}} who examined you will have seen a {{A|Sheriff}} as one of your possible results. Another advantage to doing this is that if your target dies, you will simultaneously be thrown into suspicion and will become a {{A|Jester}}. *Sometimes, remaining silent and voting your target on {{A|day}} 2 can get everybody else to vote for them. This is unlikely to work in ranked, as it is a random vote and may bring suspicion upon you. *If you become a {{A|Jester}}, start following the strategies on the {{A|Jester}} page. However, note that there are some {{A|Jester}} strategies unique to playing an {{A|Executioner}} which start before you actually change roles. In particular, you have the advantage of having {{A|Basic Defense}} (which is generally limited to evil roles, and therefore extremely suspicious should the {{A|Town}} learn about it. Keep in mind, however, that once you turn into a {{A|Jester}}, you will lose your {{A|Basic Defense}}). **If it becomes impossible to get your target Hanged, especially if it's because they confirmed themselves as a {{A|Townie}} in Ranked, it can be advantageous to start planning your {{A|Jester}} strategy even before they die. Your target is, after all, likely to die quickly after being revealed, especially if they are an important {{A|Town}} role. **If it seems like your target is going to get killed at {{A|night}}, then try to lure people into attacking you so they'll see your {{A|Basic Defense}}. If you're lucky, by the time your {{A|Basic Defense}} is revealed, your target will be dead and you'll be a {{A|Jester}}. This carries some risks (you might be Hanged before your target is killed, you could be executed by the {{A|Jailor}}, or attacked by roles with at least a {{A|Powerful Attack}}), but since the {{A|Town}} almost always accepts defense as a reason to Hang someone, it can be extremely effective when it works. **If you do end up accused as a result of your {{A|Basic Defense}} after you've already turned into a {{A|Jester}}, claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} (which is a common claim for evil roles to explain their {{A|Defense}}, although be wary that {{A|Survivor}} cannot appear in classic) or say that you're a {{A|Doctor}} and healed yourself or a {{A|Bodyguard}} who used their self vest (which may make you look like a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Arsonist}} but you should try to claim this late and unconvincingly, as its possible the {{A|town}} might believe your claim). **Avoid voting up possible members of the {{A|Mafia}} in general. This is unlikely to get you Hanged instantly, but it will keep you under suspicion, which can be valuable if you later turn into a {{A|Jester}}. **If you think it's easier to win as a {{A|Jester}}, or if your target gets confirmed, a good strategy is just to remain silent until your target dies. You have {{A|Basic Defense}}, so it shouldn't be difficult to survive unless you're called out as immune. *If your target has been quiet the whole game, suggest a random Hang and vote him. Others might side with you, since quiet roles tend to be evil, like an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Werewolf}}. **Remember that important {{A|Town}} roles usually remain silent, too. If your target claims an easily confirmable role, such as {{A|Veteran}} on the stand, the {{A|Town}} will likely pardon them and put you up instead. **If it doesn't seem like the {{A|Town}} is going to random Hang, bring up that they were silent. If it's later in the game, people will find this a reason to Hang someone. *If you're lucky enough, sometimes your target will say something suspicious or act suspiciously. Even if it is only a single sentence, dwell on it, and do your best to make their actions look as suspicious or evil as possible. *Sometimes claiming something so bizarre or out of the ordinary is the deciding factor to get your target Hanged. Be creative, but make sure it is possible at the same time. If a {{A|Medium}} is dead, say that the {{A|Medium}} used their seance on you and told you that your target was evil. *The dead appear as more credible sources. Accuse your target of being guilty, on accounts that the dead told you so. *If your target is a {{A|Lookout}} and they accuse someone of killing someone, ask them if anyone else visited them. If they say no, then say they are an {{A|Executioner}} and you also visited the target. Players may believe you and Hang your target. *If someone died the previous {{A|night}} by an {{A|Ambusher}}, you can claim to be a {{A|Medium}} and tell the town that your target is the {{A|Ambusher}}. **Another {{A|Medium}} can ruin your play, though, so make sure you are the only {{A|Medium}} claim before performing this tactic. *If your target is a {{A|Transporter}} who killed a {{A|Mafia}} member, you claim to be a {{A|Medium}} or a {{A|Spy}} who saw a double visit and accuse them of being a {{A|Forger}}. *Sometimes you don't even have to accuse your target, especially in modes with confirmed role lists, like [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]] or [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Classic_Mode|Classic Mode]]. Simply getting your target up on the stand, either through luck, pushing for the {{A|Town}} to vote for roles, claiming they are too quiet or not quiet enough, then counterclaiming their role claim, can get them Hanged. *Claims made early (such as on {{A|day}} 2) are very suspicious to the other players, as this is obvious {{A|Executioner}} behavior. The longer you can go without your target dying or being confirmed {{A|Town}}, the more "helpful" your claim will be. *It's usually a bad idea to accuse someone on the same {{A|day}} the {{A|Town}} already has a lead. If an {{A|Investigator}} comes forward with information, or if the {{A|Town}} is determined to Hang someone for other reasons, they may simply ignore you. **However, there is one advantage to accusing at the same time as someone else: If the genuine {{A|Investigator}} accused a {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} member, that person, and their allies, will usually leap at the chance to push the {{A|Town's}} attention on to someone else. Therefore, especially when you think the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} is near a majority, it can be worthwhile to contradict a genuine accusation against them with a false one of your own in hopes of allying with them. This tends to be less effective when the {{A|Investigator}} accused a {{A|Serial Killer}} or other {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, since they're not going to have any allies to help. *A good tactic is to wait (normally about halfway through discussion time) and see if the {{A|Town}} has any leads that {{A|day}}. If they don't, all the attention will be focused on you, giving you more time to prove why your target is guilty. Remember that even if the {{A|Town}} is silent, you shouldn't reveal on {{A|day 2}} unless you're aiming to get the [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]]. *If you start accusing your target too early, many players will quickly assume you are an {{A|Executioner}}. Once this happens, it will become far more difficult to Hang your target. However, the longer you wait, the higher the chance of your target being proven innocent or being killed in the {{A|night}}. *Waiting just until the end of discussion leaves people less time to question your story. However, waiting too late won't give them enough time to vote. *This isn't foolproof, but you can accuse the person of something completely random that doesn't exist or something that does exist but isn't a common term. For example "______ is buddying!" *Whisper to your target to ask his/her role, then tell the {{A|Town}} that he/she is lying by inventing proof. *If your target is not Hanged the {{A|day}} you claim that they are evil, an {{A|Investigator}} will likely investigate you or your target and see that you are lying. It is crucial to get them Hanged the {{A|day}} that you claim they are an evil role, or you have a very low chance of winning as an {{A|Executioner}}, unless the {{A|Mafia}} has majority vote and decides not to risk killing your target at {{A|night}} for the fear of being a {{A|Veteran}} or a {{A|Transporter}}. In that case, your only hope is usually only if your target gets killed at {{A|night}} and you win as a {{A|Jester}}. *If you didn't manage to get your target Hanged that same {{A|day}}, a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} who believed you might kill the {{A|Townie}}, causing you to be an obvious {{A|Executioner}} that turned into a {{A|Jester}}. *In the worst case scenario, your target could be a {{A|Townie}} who is proven early in the game. If this is the case, the best you can do is hope that your target dies so that you can become a {{A|Jester}}, or wait until evil roles have majority and you can convince them to give you a free win. *{{A|Achievements}} are a surprisingly compelling argument. If you claim to do something having to do with an {{A|Achievement}}, especially if you can remember the name of the {{A|Achievement}}, it can convince {{A|Townies}} that you are not lying. *Using {{A|Achievements}} also appeals to the previously mentioned sympathy psychology. For example, claiming to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Investigator}} on {{A|day 1}} and asking to be witched to yourself "for the {{A|Achievement}}", then claiming that you were actually {{A|Lookout}}, was witched to yourself, and that your target visited you is a good claim. Beware that if your target has info or {{A|day}} abilities a {{A|Witch}} would not have ({{A|Lookout}} with valid information, {{A|Transporter}}), then this can backfire on you. **Another example would be to say "I transported myself with (Player) and got the "Stop Hitting Yourself" achievement!". This would immediately accuse the Player of being a killer with {{A|defense}}. *In [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]], You can claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and say, "I have role blocked (your target) and there isn't any {{A|Mafia}} kills!" or, "I am a {{A|Transporter}}, I have transported myself with (your target), and got the "Stop Hittin' Yourself!" {{A|Achievement}} for making (your target) attack themselves!" *Another idea is to wait until your target has claimed a role, then counterclaim by saying you are that role. For example, if your target is a {{A|Bodyguard}}, and they claim it, you should counter-claim with a [[Last Will (ToS)|will]], hoping to get them Hanged. *Your overall way of winning is having a propelling argument, so you need a good enough number of people to believe you. An {{A|Executioner's}} best hope for winning is the {{A|Town}}. *Be detailed in your accusations. One of the telltale signs of a bad {{A|Executioner}} is when they make an accusation without the details that a normal {{A|Townie}} making the same accusation would give - a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} claim who says the target is "bad" but fails to reveal exactly what result they got, for instance, just saying "(Player) is suspicious!". Always keep a fake will to back up your claims. *In [[Rainbow Mode]], your target will always be the {{A|Veteran}}, as you occupy the {{A|Any}} slot and the {{A|Jailor}} cannot be your target. Usually, you can just come out as an {{A|Executioner}} and tell other players who the {{A|Veteran}} is, and they will be happy to [[Hanging (ToS)|Hang]] them. *In the unlikely event a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is killed by role blocking a {{A|Serial Killer}}, you can ask the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} to taunt the person they blocked, and then taunt your target. **Of course, if your target has already been taunted, the ability to taunt won't be available until the next {{A|day}}, and by then the {{A|Town}} might have already forgotten. **This strategy generally useless in higher levels of play, as smart {{A|Townies}} will point out that that a dead player's taunt cannot be seen by living players. ***On the other hand, if a {{A|Bootlegger}} was the one to visit the {{A|Serial Killer}}, you can ask the {{A|Mafia}} to taunt the {{A|Serial Killer}} instead and then semi-swiftly taunt your target before the {{A|Mafia}} outs the real {{A|Serial Killer}} (but not so fast that it must be fake). Since at least a {{A|Mafioso}} should still be alive (provided they didn't die the same {{A|Night}}), this will hold more weight in the argument. Even if they beat you to the punch, it still might prove beneficial to let them have the taunt, as the {{A|Serial Killer}} will likely be eliminated and you will remain safe to try another strategy. * If your target claims to be a {{A|Sheriff}}, and found you suspicious (meaning you were {{A|Framed}} or {{A|Hexed}}), you could argue that your role is something evil that would not normally be found suspicious like {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Plaguebearer}}; then proceed to accuse your target of being a {{A|Werewolf}} or some other role faking {{A|Sheriff}}. As long as the role you claim is not more dangerous than the one you accuse your target of being, players may decide to let you live long enough to have your target executed before you die. ===Siding with the {{A|Mafia}}=== *In expansion to finding two potential suspects. You may confirm the identity of a member of the {{A|Mafia}} by asking them in a whisper (However, exposing you to the risk that you are incorrect) and tell them that you will contribute to their votes. During the {{A|day}}, you may figure out that particular member in addition to your target, stating that they claimed a specific role on a specific {{A|day}} (stating a particular {{A|day}} will be more credible) and state it late during the [[Discussion]] phase, leaving little time for others to question your story. If you are lucky, that member of the {{A|Mafia}} will have falsely claimed the role you specified, making it seem like you have found two of the {{A|Mafia}} rather than only one. It will be more difficult for the {{A|Town}} to Hang the true member of the {{A|Mafia}} and it will be easier for you to Hang your target with additional votes. *If you have found an inconsistency with two people stating the same role, and you are sure that one of them is a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. you may whisper one of them stating that you are the {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Arsonist}} and to tell them that you will give them an extra vote. If you have picked the incorrect player, you may whisper the other player and tell them to kill your target, saying that they are a member of the {{A|Town}}, and that you will actually give them more votes. With luck, the player that you incorrectly whispered will call you out the next {{A|day}}, but by then you will have reverted to a {{A|Jester}}. *If the {{A|Town}} finds a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, you may want to quickly side with them and try to counter whatever the accuser might be saying, then whisper to the member about how you saved them, and you want to side with them, and to do so, they must help with Hanging your target. *Although risky, if you spot a player who seems to be blackmailed, you could try whispering to them and send a message to the {{A|Blackmailer}} that you’re the {{A|Executioner}} and want to join them, this is very risky though and if the {{A|Blackmailer}} dies, the person you’re whispering to puts it in their will, or a lookout is still alive, you will almost certainly be outed. **Alternatively you could try faking {{A|Executioner}} and doing this, as being “revealed” would divert a lot of attention from you, this is also risky however and generally not recommended. *Remember, if the game ever reaches a point where your vote and the {{A|Mafia's}} vote combined outnumbers the {{A|Town's}}, you can immediately declare your role and ask the {{A|Mafia}} to vote for your target. Unless there's a hidden {{A|Mayor}}, the {{A|Town}} won't be able to do anything about it, and both you and the {{A|Mafia}} will win. **This also applies for {{A|Vampires}} and the {{A|Coven}}, however the {{A|Vampires}} may not be as eager to help if one of their teammates is your target. *If your target is a confirmed {{A|Veteran}}, siding with the {{A|Mafia}} is your most likely way to win. The {{A|Town}} is unlikely to Hang a confirmed {{A|Veteran}}, but the {{A|Mafia}} is probably going to want to Hang them rather than risk hitting an alert, so all you have to is survive until the {{A|Mafia}} reaches a majority. ===Revealing your role=== *If you believe evil roles have the majority of votes (or will have one, counting your vote), you can simply declare your role as an {{A|Executioner}} and ask them to Hang your target. They will normally listen to you and give you the win, unless they see you as a possible threat. *Remember, you are still a {{A|Neutral}}, even if it is {{A|Neutral Evil}}. If you risk trying to side with the {{A|Town}}, and try to help them, and then later in the game ask to Hang your target, there is a chance the {{A|Town}} will listen to you. However, this depends on the {{A|Town}} and how they react; whether they kindly listen and since they have the clear win Hang one of their own willingly, or refuse and Hang you instead. However, you may also be left in the dust helping the {{A|Town}} but your target not being Hanged. Do not count on this working- they may not believe you and Hang you instead. **'''Note: This isn't a good strategy to use in [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]] games, since experienced players may Hang an {{A|Executioner}} regardless.''' ===Claiming a role=== *Voting for your target "randomly" sometimes works. However, your accusation is more effective with a suitable cover story. Therefore, coming up with the best role to claim in a specific scenario, and making the ideal type of accusation increases your chances that the {{A|Town}} Hanges your target. ===={{A|Town Investigative}}==== *Simply claiming on the second {{A|day}} that "I'm the {{A|Lookout}}/{{A|Sheriff}}/{{A|Investigator}} and [target] visited someone who died/is suspicious/not suspicious, could be {{A|Godfather}}" can work surprisingly well, especially in {{A|All Any}} modes. *Pay attention to the details of what exactly your role learns. If you're claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}}, you should list a set of possible roles; if you claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}}, you need to accuse your target of being suspicious, and so on. Details that match what an actual member of your claimed role would see will make people more likely to believe you, while vague accusations that someone is evil or accusations that are more specific than your claimed role can determine are more likely to get you spotted as an {{A|Executioner}}. ===={{A|Lookout}}==== *If someone is being controlled by a {{A|Witch}}, [[Role block|role blocked]] or blackmailed for several turns and publicly complains about it, claim that you "looked" at them and "saw" your target visiting them, therefore accusing your target of being a {{A|Witch}}, {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer}}. The damaged person will jump on any lead to end their suffering, so you will have at least one supporter. *When attempting to get your target Hanged, it is more credible to figure out two potential suspects, especially if one is a confirmed role. For example, you may pose as a {{A|Lookout}} and claim that two particular people (one being your target) visited someone who had died on a particular {{A|night}} and also state that the player who is not your target is some confirmed role other then {{A|Jailor}} (especially if their role was not explicitly stated and they did, in fact, visit the dead player), making it easier for you to Hang your target. It is also a good idea to write a false {{A|Last Will}}, in case you are questioned about your role, giving players less time to think about whether to Hang your target. *The danger in claiming a {{A|Lookout}}, of course, is that anyone who ''actually'' visited the person you say you watched that {{A|night}} will immediately know you're lying. Likewise, if you name more than one possibility, any {{A|Townie}} you name who didn't visit them that {{A|night}} will know you're lying. On the other hand, claiming {{A|Lookout}} and naming someone as a visitor is one of the few ways to accuse someone with total certainty on {{A|day}} 2, since a {{A|Sheriff's}} target may have been framed and {{A|Investigators}} usually show more than one possibility. **You could bluff and threaten to "reveal" the numbers of the players who visited a victim unless they state the reason for their visit. Chances are very likely a {{A|Mafia}} member will give a false reason, but at least one person should speak to make the statement more convincing. Then, if your target has '''not''' spoken up, accuse your target of having visited and not claiming a role. If your target '''did''' visit the victim, just push them in a one-for-one situation. *If your target was cleaned as well, claim that 2 people visited, one being your target, and one being a random person. Do not be eager to Hang your target, since it will make you an obvious {{A|Executioner}}, but let someone else do the voting first. You can also say, "It doesn't matter who we Hang first." to make people vote for your target or the other person. This is a 50% chance that your target will be Hanged, if any Hangings happen for your accused. If the other person turns to be a {{A|Mafia Killing}} or {{A|Janitor}}, however, your target will be hanged for sure! (But in this scenario, it is nearly certain your target will be a target of {{A|Town Killing}}) *On the first {{A|day}}, if you plan on claiming {{A|Lookout}}, claim {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and ask to be witched into yourself for the achievement. On the second {{A|day}}, "reveal" that you are actually a {{A|Lookout}} and you saw your target visit you. People will assume they are the {{A|Witch}}. **Remembering the achievement names makes your case more compelling. If you claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, ask for 'I Look Good!', and if you claim {{A|Investigator}}, ask for 'Who am I?'. ===={{A|Investigator}}==== *Claiming that your target is a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}} or {{A|Jester}} is a bit dicey (since they can claim to have been framed). On the other hand, it's less likely to get you hanged in retribution, since you have a legitimate excuse for an error even in the eyes of your victim. It also means that if your target happens to have been framed before, your results will match those of any previous {{A|Investigators}} who looked at them that {{A|night}}; and if the {{A|Mafia}} is smart, they'll continue to frame them going forward. Also claiming "{{A|Jester}} support" is an easy way to fool the {{A|Town}} into thinking that they're helping a {{A|Jester}}. *If your target has claimed a role, claiming any investigative result that doesn't match that one can get them hanged, though you risk being contradicted by actual {{A|Investigators}}. *{{A|Investigator}} is a difficult role to write fake {{A|Last Wills}} for, since you have to identify one person per {{A|day}} and could be found out if you get anyone wrong. On the other hand, this also means that a fake {{A|Investigator}} will tends to be more convincing. *Claim to be an {{A|Investigator}} and pretend to "investigate" people by asking them for their roles the next {{A|day}}, claiming {{A|Investigator}}. If they seem like a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, side with them, telling them that you are the {{A|Executioner}}. Tell them who your target is, and make sure that they won't kill your target. If they're {{A|Town}}, write what the investigative result for their role would be in your will (do the same for members of the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles too). A little later in the game, ask your target for their role. When they tell you their role, announce to the {{A|Town}}, "Hang [your target]." When they ask you why, say, "I'm {{A|Investigator}} and they came up as [investigative result-anything except {{A|Framer}}/{{A|Vampire}}/{{A|Jester}} because they could claim to have been framed] but they claimed [something different that's not in the result]." Post your {{A|Last Will}} as "proof" if they ask you for it. However, be wary that if you do this too early, people may suspect you of being an {{A|Executioner}}. Also, you won't have enough results to use as "proof" that you are an {{A|Investigator}}. *Claiming that your target came up as a {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Disguiser}}, or {{A|Serial Killer}} and there's a high possibility that they are a {{A|Disguiser}} may persuade most players to Hang them, especially if there's no {{A|Neutral Killing}} (which means {{A|Town}} has to kill all {{A|Mafia}} by themselves to win). This method will not work in modes which don't have a spot for a {{A|Disguiser}} role (such as Classic) and has a low chance of working in modes where {{A|Disguiser}} rarely appears ([[Rainbow Mode]], most [[Custom Mode]]/[[Coven Custom]] setups). The best place for it is [[All Any]] and [[Coven All Any]]. *Claiming that you investigated your target one {{A|night}}, and that you investigated them the next {{A|night}} and a different result came up may work. The {{A|Town}} may think that your target is a {{A|Disguiser}}. However, this may not work, as most {{A|Disguisers}} will keep disguising as one target until they die. Also, an actual {{A|Investigator}} may prove you wrong. *{{A|Investigator}} accusations should be tailored towards the evils that the town is currently searching for. For instance, if they're trying to find the {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Poisoner}}, accusing someone of being {{A|Sheriff}} / {{A|Executioner}} / {{A|Werewolf}} / {{A|Poisoner}} is more effective and it's particularly effective if both are present; if there's an active {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Necromancer}}, you could accuse someone of being a {{A|Medium}} / {{A|Janitor}} / {{A|Retributionist}} / {{A|Necromancer}} / {{A|Trapper}}. Often, {{A|Investigator}} accusations are more effective if you wait until it's clear who the evils are and then accuse someone of something that matches them, especially if it's at the point in the game where the {{A|Town}} is starting to get desperate. *A useful move as fake {{A|Investigator}} would be to claim your target came up as {{A|Tavern Keeper}}/{{A|Bootlegger}}/{{A|Transporter}}/{{A|Hypnotist}}, and they claimed something else. {{A|Mafia}} should immediately know you're lying (as the only non-{{A|Town}} roles available are {{A|Mafia}} roles), and the {{A|Town}} might believe your argument as {{A|Hypnotist}} can also fake {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, or {{A|Witch}} (along with {{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Trapper}}, {{A|Poisoner}}, and {{A|Guardian Angel}} in {{A|Coven Expansion}}). There is one significant risk though: if your target ends up completely cleared of suspicion (either a {{A|Sheriff}} or a real {{A|Investigator}} can out the truth), people will know you're lying. To evade this possibility, wait until later in the game so you have enough time to build your {{A|Last Will}} '''and''' hope evils have majority or the {{A|Town}} is desperate. ===={{A|Sheriff}}==== *Claiming to be a {{A|Sheriff}} can work if there are still {{A|Town Investigative}} roles in play who have not yet in some way been revealed to the {{A|Town}}. The {{A|Sheriff}} can accurately pinpoint any non-{{A|Godfather}} {{A|Mafia}} as well as the {{A|Serial Killer}}. Claim your target is either and that you have investigated them. This is especially easy in [[Game Modes (ToS)#All_Any|All Any]], where the {{A|Mafia}} may be numerous and the {{A|Town}} is not aware of what roles are in play and is thus more likely to follow your presumed authority. If you fail to get them hanged on the {{A|day}} of your 'reveal', your {{A|Defense}} will protect you from any killing roles now targeting you. During the next {{A|day}}, you may try to fake another interrogation by claiming another {{A|Town}} member came up as innocent, then stress to hang your target. *Avoid accusing someone on {{A|day}} 2 as many people will see you as an {{A|Executioner}} and ignore you. Instead, bring up your lead on {{A|day}} 3 in order to make your claim more believable. *One benefit to claiming {{A|Sheriff}} is that if an {{A|Investigator}} investigates you after you accuse your target, you will come up as a {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Executioner}}, or {{A|Werewolf}}, which will help sell your story and gain an additional vote. This may not work if a {{A|Framer}} decides to frame you or if the {{A|Investigator}} realizes that you still may be {{A|Executioner}} or even a {{A|Werewolf}}. *The {{A|Sheriff}} is easy to write a fake {{A|Last Will}} for. You can declare anyone you like to be non-suspicious and you're unlikely to be immediately contradicted (since any {{A|Townies}} who knew they were {{A|Mafia}} probably would have come forward already.) Posting detailed fake {{A|Last Wills}} may help convince skeptical {{A|Investigators}}. It does carry some risk of being caught in a lie by a {{A|Lookout}}, but few {{A|Lookouts}} are alert and clever enough to immediately notice the contradiction. *When claiming {{A|Sheriff}}, remember to stay calm and not use caps when accusing someone. This way, the {{A|Town}} is more likely to believe you as {{A|Sheriff}} instead of an eager {{A|Executioner}} looking to Hang their target. *The biggest disadvantage to claiming {{A|Sheriff}} is that it's, by far, the most common strategy {{A|Executioners}} use; this tends to mean it gets more scrutiny than other accusations. ===={{A|Spy}}==== *Claiming {{A|Spy}} is generally not a bad idea, especially in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. This is because when you accuse your target and post fake visits, the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} will most likely see you as an {{A|Executioner}} and may help you get your target Hanged, so you'll only have to convince a couple {{A|Town}} that your target is evil. It's even better if both are present in modes such as [[Coven Custom]] or [[Coven All Any]], as if both factions push your target, you may not have to convince any {{A|Town}} at all. **Note that they may also see you as a {{A|Neutral Killing}} or {{A|Plaguebearer}} attempting to pose as an {{A|Executioner}} and may simply out you in a {{A|Death Note}}, or, in the case of the {{A|Coven}}, kill you outright. *As the {{A|Spy}}, you know who {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visits. If they were no {{A|Mafia}} deaths, you can claim {{A|Spy}} and say that {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} visited your target and didn't die, accusing your target of having {{A|Defense}} (i.e. {{A|Serial Killer}}) This is a good strategy since {{A|Spy}} always gets results. You can be counterclaimed by an actual {{A|Spy}} saying that {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} didn't visit your target or a {{A|Town Protective}} saying that they protected your target and they weren't attacked. You also may be asked to provide a will of who the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} visited and who you bugged and what happened to them. *Another potential option, particularly if no one can contradict it, is to claim that your target is frequently being visited by the {{A|Mafia}}. This can give the appearance that there might be a {{A|Disguiser}} and that your target is constantly being visited by them. This has two added benefits, as not only do you appear more legitimate and helpful for finding specific roles for the {{A|Town}}, but the chance of you being argued as the {{A|Executioner}} can still be explained as a {{A|Framer}} could also be visiting your target. *You can also claim that you saw your target clean the gas off of themselves or gotten doused. Since {{A|Arsonist}} is the only role that cleans the gas off of themselves or gets a notification of being doused, you're accusing your target of being an {{A|Arsonist}}. A {{A|Tracker}}/{{A|Lookout}} can counterclaim you saying that you didn't visit your target, or a {{A|Investigator}} saying that your target isn't anything but {{A|Bodyguard}}/{{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Arsonist}}/{{A|Crusader}}. You can also be counterclaimed by a {{A|Spy}} who bugged your target, but that is rare. *It is also possible to claim your target was attacked but was immune, which accuses your target of being a {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Coven Leader}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, {{A|Plaguebearer}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, or another {{A|Executioner}}. Evils might recognize you as an {{A|Executioner}} and might even write in their {{A|Death Notes}} that your target was immune, helping your target get Hanged, although most evils will believe you to be a {{A|Spy}} and might attack you instead, exposing your {{A|Basic Defense}}. *As a {{A|Spy}}, you know what notifications your target gets. For example, if you bugged a {{A|Doctor}} who healed an attacked target, you will know. Using this knowledge, you can use this to counter-claim your target. For example, if your target is a {{A|Bodyguard}} who used their vest to protect against an attack, you can claim to bug him and say that he is immune, and didn't use a vest to survive. This can be counter-claimed by a {{A|Tracker}}/{{A|Lookout}} saying that you didn't visit your target, or a {{A|Spy}} who bugged your target saying that you're lying. *You can claim that you bugged your target and they were controlled by a {{A|Witch}} and did not say anything up to that point (since they obviously can't claim witched) and trick the {{A|Town}} into hanging them (although do note that you'll have to include a full {{A|Spy}} will. If you see another Spy will, copy it, or if you're the only claim, fake it enough to convince the {{A|Town}}. Additionally, the {{A|Mafia}} will obviously know you're lying, and could potentially help you hang your target). ===={{A|Psychic}}==== *Claiming {{A|Psychic}} can be much more effective than it seems at first. As a phony {{A|Psychic}}, you can only reveal that your target is one of three possible evils, and only after odd {{A|nights}}, but there are a number of ways to turn this to your advantage. **Naming a {{A|Town}} member who died that {{A|night}} as one of the three potential evils immediately narrows it down to two (and isn't particularly uncommon, so few people will grow suspicious). **If you're desperate, and two {{A|Town}} members died on an odd-numbered {{A|night}}, you can even name both of them alongside your target, but this is implausible enough that most {{A|Townies}} will grow suspicious. **You can use your even-numbered {{A|nights}} to do the reverse and imply other people you named are good, especially by using the same trick mentioned above - name two people, one an evil who died that {{A|night}}, and the other one of the three people who you named previously. **Claiming to be a {{A|Psychic}} gives you the ability to avoid directly stating the conclusion that your target is evil. Even when you've falsified results that leave no other option, it's often best to let other people realize that themselves if possible. Pretending you didn't realize that your visions collectively imply your target is evil both makes you look less like an {{A|Executioner}} and will let any other {{A|Town}} members who spot it feel clever, which can lead to them being more committed to getting your target Hanged than if you just dropped the solution on them. **People have a tendency to grow suspicious of anyone who appears in two "evil" {{A|Psychic}} results, even if there's still other options in each {{A|night}}. This can get your target Hanged even if you don't actively try to narrow the possibilities down to one person. *Claiming {{A|Psychic}} has a number of other advantages: **A {{A|Psychic}}, like an {{A|Executioner}}, is non-visiting; therefore, you can't be caught by {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Trappers}}, {{A|Trackers}}, and {{A|Jailors}} who notice you didn't visit your target when you claimed to, or by {{A|Transporters}} who might 'helpfully' reveal your target was transported. **It's more common for genuine {{A|Psychics}} to reveal their results on {{A|day}} 2 (and every {{A|day}} thereafter). Therefore, people are less likely to get suspicious when you do so when compared to {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Investigators}} and the like. **A {{A|Psychic}} ''always'' receives results. People tend to be suspicious of a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Lookout}} who claims to have gotten lucky on the first {{A|night}}, but there's no reason to be suspicious of a {{A|Psychic}} - and while your phony results will form an unlikely coincidence that rapidly implies someone is evil, this is harder for people to recognize. **Frequently, random events can end up helping you - if one of the other people you named dies or gets confirmed, your target will look extremely suspicious. **When you only have two people who could be evil (having named a third person who died the {{A|night}} before), those two are often going to be compelled to try and vote against each other, making it more likely that your target will be Hanged. Additionally, while your target can't be a {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}, the other person potentially could be. **Any evils who ''are'' in the results you named will be motivated to push the guilt on to someone else, like your target, and if they're part of an evil team, everyone else on their team is likely to help. **When you screw up, it's often easier to explain - it's extremely unlikely for ''none'' of your targets to be evil. Even when your efforts to get your target Hanged fail on a particular {{A|night}}, you'll often be free to keep going with more visions on later {{A|nights}}, whereas other claims will tend to make you look like an obvious {{A|Executioner}}. **If your target dies at {{A|night}}, it will often end up making you look suspicious by contradicting your visions, and since {{A|Psychic}} is a more indirect way of accusing them, people may not realize you're an {{A|Executioner}} who has now become a {{A|Jester}}. Even if you don't look suspicious immediately, your phony {{A|Psychic}} results will usually get contradicted eventually, making the backup plan of getting Hanged as a {{A|Jester}} much easier. **{{A|Psychic}} is also a role that is usually trusted by the {{A|Town}}, even though it is a fairly easy role to fake and often claimed by evils, which makes your job all the much easier. *However, there are a few disadvantages to consider, too: **{{A|Psychic}} is not in your investigative results, so being investigated will most likely have you called out, and possibly Hanged. **If one of the other people you name coincidentally ''does'' happen to be evil, and gets exposed as such, you'll be sent back to square one. This does carry some advantage (it makes you look like a genuine {{A|Psychic}}), but can delay your goal of getting your target Hanged. **{{A|Psychic}} is generally slightly slower than other methods of accusing. Unless you make an extremely implausible claim or get very lucky in terms of how the {{A|Town}} reacts to your vision, it's not likely that you'll get your target Hanged on {{A|day}} 2. **If there is a confirmed {{A|Medusa}} in the game and you have already claimed, or are about to claim, you will immediately be put under massive suspicion by the other {{A|Townies}}, as {{A|Psychic}} is a common {{A|Medusa}} claim. Use this strategy with caution. **To use a {{A|Psychic}} claim effectively, you usually have to reveal on {{A|day}} 2, then continuously state results and take center stage every {{A|day}} thereafter until your target is Hanged. This can make you a target for killing roles, and while your immunity protects you from some of them, it won't protect you from a {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Pirate}}, or other attacker with strength greater than Basic. ***This can ''sometimes'' work to your advantage. If your immunity is hit after you publicly claimed to be a {{A|Psychic}}, your attacker may conclude that you're an {{A|Executioner}} and work to help you. On the other hand, they might conclude you're a rival killer and expose you to the {{A|Town}}. ***It can also result in you getting role blocked, which puts you in a bind. If you were role blocked by a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can freely keep revealing results without saying anything about it (although a {{A|Spy}} who kept an eye on you might realize something is up). If you were role blocked by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, however, stating that you got results that {{A|night}} will out you as a fake. Someone role blocking a {{A|Psychic}} claim is ''probably'' a {{A|Bootlegger}}, but it's hard to be certain. ===={{A|Tracker}}==== *Claiming that you are a {{A|Tracker}} that followed your target to the house of a player who died the {{A|night}} before can work if there are still {{A|Town Investigative}} roles in play that have not yet been revealed. Another thing that could be problematic is if someone points out that there was more than one visitor at the said murdered person's house. *You should customize your accusation to what evils are in play. For instance, if someone claims to have been dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}, state that you tracked your target last {{A|night}} and that they visited the dueled player. *Similarly, if someone has made it clear that they have been repeatedly [[controlled]], [[Role block|role blocked]] or blackmailed, you can state that you tracked your target and you saw them visit the controlled/role blocked/blackmailed person over the course of one or more {{A|nights}}, thereby accusing your target of being the {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Bootlegger}}/{{A|Blackmailer}}. The damaged person will usually jump on any lead to end their suffering, so you'll have at least one supporter. *If there are no deaths one {{A|day}}, and in the morning someone goes "Thanks Doc!", say that you followed your target and that they visited the healed person, thereby accusing them of being the killing role. The actual killing role that attacked the healed person will help place suspicion onto your target do divert attention off of them and onto the unsuspecting {{A|Townie}}. *If an {{A|Investigator}} announces to the {{A|Town}} that a player showed up as a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Jester}} or {{A|Hex Master}}, use this to your advantage and accuse your target of visiting the person the {{A|Investigator}} is posting results about. Accuse them of being the {{A|Framer}} attempting to frame an innocent {{A|Townie}}. If the person the {{A|Investigator}} investigated is actually a {{A|Framer}},{{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Plaguebearer}} or a {{A|Jester}}, they will happily side with you and accuse your target of being a {{A|Framer}}, as for the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Vampires}}, it helps to push a Hang on a {{A|Townie}}, whereas if it is a {{A|Jester}}, it helps draw suspicion onto them, and if it is a {{A|Plaguebearer}} they will want to divert suspicion onto your target to gain another {{A|night}} to infect people. *If your target has publicly claimed any non-visiting {{A|Town}} role, you can announce that they are lying as you tracked them last {{A|night}} and that they in fact visited someone. This works amazingly if your target claims to be a {{A|Medium}} but you claim that you tracked them to a cleaned player, accusing them of being the {{A|Janitor}}. Since {{A|Medium}} is a common claim for {{A|Janitors}} avoiding suspicion, your target will be under immense suspicion. *If someone was turned to stone by the {{A|Medusa}} before {{A|night}} 3, you can say that you tracked the player to your target, thereby accusing your target of being the {{A|Medusa}}. This plan will backfire if someone actually visited your target the {{A|night}} you claimed you tracked and wasn't turned to stone. This plan might also not work if it is known that the {{A|Medusa}} is the last {{A|Coven}} member alive and that they possess the {{A|Necronomicon}}, as the {{A|Town}} might think that the {{A|Medusa}} visited the person specifically to turn them to stone. *Be careful when saying that you tracked a player. If a {{A|Lookout}} was watching the person you claim your target visited and didn't see them visit, they will out you as an {{A|Executioner}}. This also works if they watched your target and did not see you visit them. They will know that you are an {{A|Executioner}} fake-claiming {{A|Tracker}}. *If a {{A|Necromancer}} seems to be present, you can claim that you saw your target visit a dead person; the only roles to do so are {{A|Necromancers}} and {{A|Retributionist}}, and {{A|Retributionists}} are generally obvious when they act. Therefore, this allows you to accuse your target of being the {{A|Necromancer}}. **If the {{A|Necromancer}} clearly acted last {{A|night}}, claim your target visited someone who would have produced that result - such as the dead {{A|Serial Killer}} if there was a {{A|Serial Killer}} attack that {{A|night}}. Otherwise, claim they visited a dead person whose role wouldn't produce any obvious result (such as a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Town Protective}}). **This accusation has the advantage of reducing the risk of being caught in a lie by a {{A|Lookout}}, since naturally they can't have watched the dead person. ===={{A|Transporter}}==== *You can use a {{A|Transporter}} claim to misdirect other accusations at your target. For instance, if a {{A|Sheriff}} accuses someone of being {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, you can claim {{A|Transporter}} and say that you transported the accused Mafia member with your target. *You can also use this to redirect an accusation of immunity in {{A|Death Notes}}. *The original target of the accusation will usually be happy to support your claim that they were transported, since it lets them avoid suspicion, but there is still some risk (if they were actually {{A|Town}}, they may speak up and say they weren't transported despite the cost to themselves). *Your target will obviously know they weren't transported, but their protests normally won't mean much (since naturally that's what a guilty person would say). *One advantage to this strategy is that it works on {{A|days}} when someone else made an accusation, when you'd usually want to avoid making your play. *Another advantage is that the spontaneous nature of your reveal and the large amount that will be going on (between the accuser, the original target, yourself, and your target) means that the {{A|Town}} will rarely think to ask for the detailed {{A|Transporter}} will that you would normally be expected to provide when claiming {{A|Transporter}}. *Most of the time, this trick guarantees at least one supporter for your accusation (the person who was originally accused); and if they're actually {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, it will tend to get you the support of the rest of their faction as well, who will be eager to push for a misHang in order to protect their buddy. ===={{A|Medium}}==== *If all {{A|Town Investigatives}} are dead, you can claim to be a {{A|Medium}}. Say that a dead {{A|Town Investigative}} role has told you that your target is a {{A|Mafia}} member or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}. This could just about work as two {{A|Mediums}} cannot see each other in the dead chat. Alternatively, if a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Jailor}} was killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}}, you can claim they told you they were visiting/jailing your target when they died; or you can claim that the {{A|Jailor}} told you the target claimed a role that now clearly causes a contradiction. Of course, if there actually is another {{A|Medium}}, they may accuse you of not being correct on what the dead said. *Also remember that for all {{A|Medium}}-based accusations, you're operating by filling in a blank in the {{A|Last Will}} of a dead player. This is easy if they left a blank or incomplete {{A|Last Will}}, and your claims will be vastly stronger if their entry indicates that they were investigating, distracting, or jailing your target the {{A|night}} they died; but it can be tricky if they left a detailed will and never examined your target. *Generally speaking, a {{A|Medium}} claim is strongest when exactly one {{A|night}} has passed since an {{A|Town Investigative}} died (especially if their will says they were going to investigate your target). After all, an Investigative with valuable information would usually pass it on as soon as they could, and a {{A|Medium}} would usually reveal it at the first opportunity. *You can also relay false accusations from dead evils accusing your target of being a rival killer - especially from a dead {{A|Consigliere}}, but an accusation of immunity from a dead killer can also be effective, especially if they failed to kill on their final {{A|night}}. This carries some risk that the {{A|Town}} will refuse to believe the words of a dead non-{{A|Town}}, but generally speaking such accusations are taken seriously. *You can also fake forgeries, cleanings or stonings to accuse your target based on what the dead "say". ===={{A|Retributionist}}==== *If multiple {{A|Town Investigative}} roles have died, you can claim to have resurrected one and saw that your target was found doing something that would solidify them as an evil role, see other strategies for {{A|Town Investigative}} roles such as saying you used a {{A|Sheriff}} and they came up as suspicious, or that they visited a player the {{A|night}} they died. *You don't always need to wait for Investigative roles to die, you can claim to have role blocked them with a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} on a {{A|night}} where there was no mafia kill that {{A|night}}, or that you shot them with a {{A|Vigilante}} and they had defense. *This has the benefit of seeming a little less suspicious and making you sound less like an {{A|Executioner}} as an {{A|Executioner}} would have to wait for specific roles to die before making a play, which would not only rely on specific circumstances, it would leave their target open to attacks, turning them into {{A|Jester}} before they would be able to make an accusation against their target. *Do note that this is still a flaw in this plan as it requires you to wait, which leaves killing roles ample time to kill your target. It is also dependent on certain roles dying, so you should only attempt this claim if you think the corpses available are useful for your accusation. *This is also a [[Unique Role]], meaning a real {{A|Retributionist}} will almost certainly counter-claim you, making you sound far less credible and making it far less likely for your target to be Hanged *If your target is a {{A|Retributionist}}, you can counter-claim them, similarly to the prior situation. The {{A|town}} will likely be torn on who to Hang, however you actively counter-claiming them can give you some more credibility. ===={{A|Vigilante}}==== *If multiple {{A|Town Killing}} roles are alive, you can claim to be a {{A|Vigilante}} and say that you shot your target only to discover that they had {{A|Defense}}, which is common among the enemies of the {{A|Town}}. *Remember, a {{A|Vigilante}} cannot shoot {{A|night}} 1, so you absolutely cannot make this accusation until {{A|day}} 3 at the earliest. Even then, a Vigilante who shot at the first opportunity is going to seem a bit suspicious. *This strategy generally requires that you come up with a justification for why you shot them (they were too silent, for instance); if you can't come up with an explanation for why you shot them, the {{A|Town}} may grow suspicious. However, it could be possible to claim a mis-click that you did not notice, which could convince the {{A|Town}} to Hang the target anyway, or at least relieve some suspicion. *Another risk to this is that the {{A|Town}} may assume you're actually an evil killing role yourself, since such roles often claim {{A|Vigilante}} to make immediate accusations. You should particularly avoid this strategy if an evil killer missed their kill last {{A|night}}, since it will look like you're them. *{{A|Vampires}} also frequently use this strategy to make accusations against people they failed to turn, so it's not a good idea in a game with {{A|Vampires}}. ===={{A|Jailor}}==== *An '''EXTREMELY''' risky strategy is to claim that you are the {{A|Jailor}}. If one {{A|day}} there were no {{A|Mafia}} kills, claim that you jailed your target, but that you want to conserve your executions for other evil roles. Alternatively, you could claim that your target claimed an impossible role in jail but that you cannot execute them because you keep being role blocked or witched, implying that your target is a member of the {{A|Mafia}} but a {{A|Bootlegger}} or a {{A|Witch}} is preventing you from executing them, then ask the {{A|Town}} to Hang them. *This strategy should only ever be used as either a last resort if no other claim will work, or if you have a grand master plan to use this strategy from the beginning of the game; otherwise, the real {{A|Jailor}} will easily counter-claim you if it seems your Hang is likely to work, and execute you at {{A|night}} if it doesn't. *However, you could claim {{A|Jailor}} at the very start of the game before the first {{A|Day}} is up, and set up your strategy accordingly: **If you are jailed, tell the real {{A|Jailor}} that you only lied to inform them you are some significant role that is safe to not act on the first {{A|Night}}, such as {{A|Vampire Hunter}} or {{A|Retributionist}}, and adjust your plan accordingly. **If you are '''not''' jailed, this will almost certainly mean there is no {{A|Jailor}} in the game and you can utilize any strategy you need. *Usually, this is only a viable strategy when the game mode means that the presence of the {{A|Jailor}} is uncertain, such as in [[All Any]] or in specific [[Custom Setups (Classic)|Custom Setups]]. *You could also use it if you believe the {{A|Jailor}} has been cleaned by a {{A|Janitor}} or stoned by a {{A|Medusa}}, but be careful, since if you've concluded this, other people may have as well. *There are many ways this could backfire. If there is actually a {{A|Jailor}}, they will jail and execute you immediately. They might also call you out during the {{A|day}}. Also, many {{A|Townies}} will doubt your {{A|Jailor}} claim if no one has claimed to have been jailed recently, or if you produce a fake {{A|Jailor}} will that is called out on during the {{A|day}}. **To avoid this, claim {{A|Jailor}} on the first day to see if there is a {{A|Jailor}} (who should jail you anyways) or not. Make sure to deceive according to if there is a {{A|Jailor}} (in which case, lie about being a necessary role that needs to wait a {{A|Night}} to act) or not (in which case, use whatever strategy you think best). *Never ever claim to be the {{A|Jailor}} and that you have jailed your target, and then proceed to accuse them of being a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}, as the {{A|Townies}} will immediately call your bluff, as all three of the aforementioned evil roles kill the {{A|Jailor}} if jailed and not executed. **Though, if you think you can get away with it, you could lie about being healed after the {{A|Serial Killer}} attacked you, but it won't work with {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}. *The only advantage that claiming {{A|Jailor}} as an {{A|Executioner}} brings is that this claim will be so unexpected, that many {{A|Townies}} might believe it on the basis of how extremely rare an evil role claims to be the {{A|Jailor}}, and so will believe your claim and Hang your target. ===={{A|Veteran}}==== *If your target claims to be the {{A|Veteran}}, counter-claim them. Use anything you can to your advantage to "prove" how your target's claim is false and that they are an evil masquerading as the {{A|Veteran}}. Calling out even the tiniest of things that hinder your target's argument could be enough to convince the {{A|Town}} to Hang them. *If they don't have a {{A|Last Will}} and they respond with, "Why would I keep a will as {{A|Veteran}}?", call them out on this by saying that this, "proves" that they are evil. *You could still claim to be the {{A|Veteran}}, even if your target does not claim {{A|Veteran}}. If there is a {{A|Town Killing}} dead in the graveyard, and multiple {{A|Town Killing}} roles are unlikely, and your target is claiming to be the {{A|Random Town}}, say that they cannot be the {{A|Random Town}} because you are the {{A|Veteran}} and so you fill the {{A|Random Town}} slot. ===={{A|Tavern Keeper}}==== *If the {{A|Mafia}} fails to kill anyone on a particular {{A|night}}, you can claim to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and say that you distracted your target that {{A|night}}. This will generally only work if there is no {{A|Mafioso}}, though you could try and claim that both the {{A|Mafioso}} and the {{A|Godfather}} were blocked or that the {{A|Mafioso}} failed to vote. *Note that if the number of available roles are limited to the point where there's only one possible {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and no {{A|Bootlegger}} (which can happen fairly easily in [[Game Modes (ToS)#Classic_Mode|Classic Mode]], if the {{A|Random Town}} is known), then anyone who was actually distracted by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} will know you're lying; however, they will hopefully be {{A|Mafia}} members, who will keep quiet. *If there's a second {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, they may pipe up with whoever they distracted (since even if they believe you're a second {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, anyone who was role blocked that {{A|night}} is a possible suspect.) Similarly, the {{A|Jailor}} might think whoever they jailed was responsible. However, if you make the accusation first, you can generally push at least a fairly large amount of suspicion onto your target without coming under scrutiny yourself; using {{A|Tavern Keeper}} to implicate someone has the advantage of being relatively rare and obscure, so few people are likely to immediately suspect you of being an {{A|Executioner}}. *If there is a {{A|Serial Killer}} in the game, you could claim to have role blocked your target and was attacked and healed by a {{A|Doctor}}. You need to convince the {{A|Town}} that the {{A|Serial Killer}} was not using their Cautious ability. If a previous {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}} has died this way, and their will was covered in blood, this may work even more. ===={{A|Crusader}}==== *If your target claims to be a visiting role, claim that your target's {{A|Last Will}} is false because you visited the same person as they did on a certain {{A|night}} and so you would of killed them had they really visited your target, as the {{A|Crusader}} kills a visitor to their target at random. Claim that therefore, your target is lying as they couldn't have visited the same target as you on the same {{A|night}} and survived. This works even better if your target also claims to be a {{A|Town Protective}} as it will appear that you are the {{A|Town Protective}} and that they are lying. *This plan will backfire however if multiple people visited the person you said you guarded and no one died to a {{A|Crusader}}. Also, the real {{A|Crusader}} might call you out. ===={{A|Trapper}}==== *If your target claims to be a visiting role, claim that your target's {{A|Last Will}} is false because you constructed a trap at the same person's house on the same {{A|night}} they claimed to have visited. Claim that since a {{A|Trapper's}} traps trigger regardless of the alignment of the visitor, but that your traps weren't triggered, your target is lying about visiting them on that {{A|night}}. This works even better if your target also claims to be a {{A|Town Protective}} role, as you can claim to be the true {{A|Town Protective}} and expose their "false will". *This plan will backfire however if multiple people visited the person you said you constructed a trap at and none of them triggered a trap. Also, the real {{A|Trapper}} might call you out. ===={{A|Consigliere}}==== *A risky strategy is to claim to be a {{A|Consigliere}} and have found a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role. This will work better if multiple {{A|Neutral Killings}} exist. *However, you might be Hanged first, and you may attract suspicion, since few actual {{A|Consiglieres}} would publicly claim the role when alternatives exist. Experienced {{A|Townies}} may also see through your act as an {{A|Executioner}}, and a {{A|Jailor}} may choose to jail and execute you. ===={{A|Godfather}}==== *This strategy mainly revolves around you being called out for being immune at {{A|night}}. If the {{A|Serial Killer}} attacks you at {{A|night}} and outs your immunity in a {{A|Death Note}} the following {{A|day}}, you could theoretically claim to be the {{A|Godfather}}, but that your {{A|Mafia}} teammates have discovered that your target is the {{A|Serial Killer}} (other immune roles work fine). Emphasize how Hanging the {{A|Serial Killer}} first is preferable to Hanging you first, and it may just work. However, this is ultimately a 50/50 on who gets voted first, and you will almost certainly die the following {{A|night}} by the {{A|Jailor's}} hand for claiming to be the {{A|Godfather}}. *The effectiveness of this strategy is increased if a {{A|Consigliere}} is confirmed to be in the game, either through deduction or because it is on the role list. You can claim that your {{A|Consigliere}} found them as the {{A|Serial Killer}}. This strategy could also work if there are multiple evildoers present. For instance, if multiple {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles are in the game, you could accuse your target of being any of them if you get called out for being immune. ===={{A|Witch}}==== *Another risky strategy is to claim {{A|Witch}} and say you have found a killer (your target). Since Hanging you is less important than Hanging a killer, you may be successful. *As is the case with {{A|Consigliere}}, you may be Hanged first or attacked by the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}}. *This strategy works best when you've been identified as evil and are facing a potential Hang; it's implausible that a Witch would suddenly out themselves for no reason, but it's reasonable that they'd throw another evil under the bus late in the game in hopes of surviving long enough to win with another evil. *The best lie to give in this situation is to claim you found your target to be an {{A|Arsonist}}, as the {{A|Witch}} will find '''exact''' roles regardless if your target is {{A|Framed}}/{{A|Disguised}}/{{A|Doused}}, and will result in your target being far more likely to be executed since {{A|Arsonist}} is a dangerous role and the {{A|Witch}} would be {{A|Doused}} anyways, so there is a legitimate reason for the {{A|Witch}} to out themselves. ===={{A|Pirate}}==== *Another risky strategy is to claim that you are a {{A|Pirate}}. Say that you dueled your target and won the duel, but that they didn't die, thus accusing your target of being a role with {{A|Defense}}. *Note that this will only work on inexperienced {{A|Townies}}, as any experienced player will immediately call you out with the fact that the {{A|Pirate}} attack is Powerful, and so would kill even a role with {{A|Defense}}. ===={{A|Vampire}}==== *If you feel like {{A|Vampires}} are starting to take over the game, you can say out loud that you are a {{A|Vampire}} and you found (insert your target's name) immune to bite. Be careful though, since if your target happens to be a {{A|Town}} member converted to a {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Vampires}} may try to get rid of you as a potential threat. *Another threat would be if there was a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} who decides to check to see if you are a {{A|Vampire}}. The next {{A|day}}, the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} will say that you are not a {{A|Vampire}}. This could be a threat if a {{A|Mayor}} reveals themselves or there are enough non-{{A|Vampires}} to vote you up. ===={{A|Vampire Hunter}}==== *The reverse is that you can claim {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, and that {{A|Vampires}} said in chat to bite someone, (who you visited the next {{A|night}},) and that person did not die, meaning that the person the {{A|Vampires}} "visited" was immune. *As with the above, this only works when {{A|Vampires}} are confirmed to exist. *An actual {{A|Vampire Hunter}} might call you out because they didn't hear the {{A|Vampires}} say they would bite your target, and some players might point out that some {{A|Vampires}} try to trick {{A|Vampire Hunters}} into thinking they bit someone who wasn't bit. *A real {{A|Vampire}} may even call you out, but this would be very rare, as a {{A|Vampire}} would not want to reveal their own identity. *This is most likely the rarest and least used tactic, as {{A|Vampires}} are impossible in all game modes except for [[Game Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom Mode]], [[Rapid_Mode#Rapid_Mode|Rapid Mode]], and [[Game Modes (ToS)#All_Any|All Any]]. Only use this tactic in those three areas, and only in Custom or Rapid if {{A|Vampires}} are confirmed to exist. ===After winning=== {{A|Executioner}} has the ability to win before the game ends and live to see one faction take victory, similarly to a {{A|Pirate}}. This means you are a confirmed {{A|Executioner}}, but because you already have your victory, you most likely will be left alone. You can even keep your {{A|Basic Defense}}, so while you no longer need to try and win, there is still much you can do. *Perhaps the most useful thing you can do is outright side with another faction based on how well they play or other motives. They may remember you in other games and you can use this time you were an {{A|Executioner}} and sided with them to get them to side with you in the future. *Some people tend to Hang or execute confirmed {{A|Executioners}} on the off-chance that they're an evil role (e.g. {{A|Werewolf}}) claiming {{A|Executioner}} in the hopes of being ignored. If this happens, it doesn't hurt you, since you've already Hanged your target and don't need to live to win. *While you have already won the game, don't upset or annoy other players to the point of it being reportable. Stay calm and organized, and choose the side you want to win later on if the situation comes up. **If you manage to get your target Hanged and want to make the game a little more interesting, don't claim {{A|Executioner}} success after you win. You might still be attacked by the {{A|Mafia}} or even have accusations thrown at you to divert attention from others onto yourself and keep the game spicy. Don't worry about dying, though--as aforementioned, you win after you successfully Hang your target, regardless of if you live to the end of the game. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{ExecutionerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{ExecutionerMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 0.8.1}}, a {{A|Mayor}} could be an {{A|Executioner's}} target. *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.3.0}}, a {{A|Spy}} could be an {{A|Executioner's}} target. **{{A|Spies}} could once again become an {{A|Executioner's}} target in {{VH|Version 1.5.0}}, due to {{A|Blackmailers}} receiving the ability to read whispers. *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.8}}, a {{A|Jailor}} could be an {{A|Executioner's}} target. ==History== *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate the {{A|Executioner's}} target for the {{A|Executioner}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_GenericTarget.png|30x30px]]). **The {{A|Executioner's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Executioner.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Executioner's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Executioner Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.5.8.4235}} **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Jailor}} as a target. **{{A|Executioner}} can now have {{A|Spy}} as a target. *{{VH|1.3.0}} **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Spy}} as a target. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Mayor}} as a target. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Палач]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Neutral Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
