'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''|goal = Kill anyone that will not submit to the {{A|Mafia}}.}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can choose a target to attack each night. Your decision overrides whatever choice is made by the {{A|Mafioso}} (if one is alive). **If you are {{A|Roleblocked}}, then the {{A|Mafioso}} will attack his own target. If the {{A|Mafioso}} did not pick or was {{A|Roleblocked}} also, no one will be attacked. **If your {{A|Mafioso}} is role blocked, dead, or does not exist, '''you''' will attack the target. *If there is a {{A|Mafioso}} (and they are not {{A|Roleblocked}} that night), then they will kill the target for you. Only the person who does the actual killing will: **Be visible by to any {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Trackers}}, {{A|Spies}}, or {{A|Trappers}} visiting the target. **Be attacked by any {{A|Town Protectives}}, rampages, alerts, and/or {{A|Stone Gazes}} at that location. **Receive a message if the target has defense or was {{A|Jailed}}. Note that if the {{A|Mafioso}} does the attacking, the {{A|Godfather}} will ''not'' receive said message for ordering an attack on the target in question. **Be able to leave a {{A|Death Note}} behind for the {{A|Town}} to see in the morning. *Both you and the {{A|Mafioso's}} kill/death message appear as "a member of the {{A|Mafia}}", meaning [[Role block|Role Blockers]] (most notably the {{A|Jailor}}) cannot determine if they {{A|Roleblocked}} either of you. *If a {{A|Mafioso}} is alive when you die, the {{A|Mafioso}} will be promoted to the {{A|Godfather}}. *If there is no {{A|Mafioso}} when you die, whichever member of the {{A|Mafia}} joins the lobby first will be promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}}. They will ''not'' be able to become a {{A|Godfather}} unless an {{A|Amnesiac}} becomes the {{A|Godfather}} and dies. *If your {{A|Mafioso}} is {{A|controlled}} , they will still kill your target and not that of the {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}. *You have {{A|Basic Defense}} and [[Detection Immunity]]. *You can talk with the other members of the {{A|Mafia}} at night. ==Strategy== As the leader of the {{A|Mafia}}, it is important for you to give orders to the {{A|Mafia}} and to make the most use out of all of their abilities. It is also important to listen to the other members of the {{A|Mafia}} and make use of any information that they give you. *If you are pressed to [[Role Claims Guide|claim]] a {{A|Town}} role, the most obvious choice is {{A|Bodyguard}} if, of course, you don't own {{A|Coven Expansion}}, since that's the only {{A|Town}} role in your investigative result. However, a lot of people find that claim suspicious for many reasons, so don't be surprised if they do not believe you. You can also claim as the {{A|Executioner}} and state a false target. You can choose your target as an active {{A|Sheriff}} or one of your members of the {{A|Mafia}} as a target. If you can't choose anyone as your target and the {{A|Investigator}} found you are lying, just say that you were {{A|doused}} by an {{A|Arsonist}} and claim to be the {{A|Sheriff}} and prepare your {{A|Last Will}} because {{A|Sheriff}} is easy to pretend. You can try to also claim {{A|doused}}, and state a different false claim. **Be cautious about claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} unnecessarily; the {{A|Town}} also knows it's your most obvious choice (and it's also the obvious choice for {{A|Arsonists}}). During late or even early game, a desperate or aggressive {{A|Town}} might hang you for claiming it if they have no other leads. **Claiming to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} is also difficult if an important confirmed {{A|Town}} role like the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}} has died at night, since the {{A|Town}} would wonder why you weren't protecting them. In this situation, you can try to claim that you were role-blocked by a {{A|Bootlegger}}. **If another {{A|Town Protective}} is killed, especially if they are a {{A|Bodyguard}} themselves, you may be hanged or killed due to the much lower chance of there being another {{A|Bodyguard}}. **You can also claim to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} and have another member of the {{A|Mafia}} (which can be a {{A|Disguiser}}) claim {{A|Doctor}}. Then every {{A|day}} you can say that you will protect the {{A|Doctor}} tonight and they will heal you tonight. You can also use messages during the day such as "Thanks, Doc!" or "Thanks BG!" to further mislead the {{A|Town}}. This strategy is very hard to disprove because the {{A|Investigator}} will also see you as a {{A|Bodyguard}} and the {{A|Disguiser}} as a {{A|Doctor}}, even if he does not {{A|disguise}} himself or you as anyone (or if he {{A|disguises}} as a {{A|Doctor}} or you as a {{A|Bodyguard}}). You will also have an alibi to why you did not protect the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}} if they died that night. You can even have the {{A|Spy}} confirm you by the {{A|Mafia}} visits made by the {{A|Disguiser}}. **When claiming to be {{A|Doused}}, be aware that if an {{A|Arsonist}} ignites, you will likely be hanged under suspicion of being an {{A|Arsonist}} (unless a {{A|Guardian Angel}} interferes). **Sometimes, it can be advantageous to claim {{A|Arsonist}} since some {{A|Townies}} prefer to keep {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles alive if the {{A|Mafia}} is nearing majority. It can also be used to deter roles like {{A|Pirates}} or {{A|Witches}} from targeting you or to sway a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Executioner}} to your side. *A potential strategy with the {{A|Mafia}} is to have one of them claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} saying another member of the {{A|Mafia}} (usually one that's not important, like a {{A|Framer}}) came up as suspicious. This has some benefits: First, the accusing member of the {{A|Mafia}} usually becomes a "confirmed" {{A|Townie}}, so the member of the {{A|Mafia}} that claimed to be a {{A|Sheriff}} has a viable defense. However, this can cause more harm than benefit as someone can call them out through information. It can also lead to the member of the {{A|Mafia's}} death from a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role if it's a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}}. This is called [[bussing]], and is a very effective strategy if pulled off. *'''Always''' select a target, since your {{A|Mafioso}} might get {{A|Roleblocked}} or controlled that night. *Try having {{A|Townies}} hanged by putting roles you want to dispose of as having some form of Defense, even if they don't. The {{A|Town}} almost always listens to {{A|Death Notes}} claiming someone has [[immunity]], especially if they don't have any leads during the day. This is a great way to eliminate {{A|Townies}} and other opposing forces. You can also try to frame {{A|Townies}} this way. Claiming to attack them and saying their defense is too high. Watch out for {{A|Spies}} when doing this, as they can easily disprove the {{A|Death Note}} unless one of your {{A|Mafia}} members visited them. **If the {{A|Mafia}} found a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role and you want to keep them alive for just a moment, you can place their name in your {{A|Death Note}} so that you can reveal them when your {{A|Mafioso}} is killed or {{A|Roleblocked}}. If the {{A|Mafioso}} is also using {{A|Death Notes}}, copy it's information and add your important info alongside it. *Try claiming to be an {{A|Executioner}} and tell the {{A|Town}} you will side them if they help you hang your target. That might explain your {{A|Basic Defense}} and keep people off your case for a while. Of course, this could backfire if there is a {{A|Jailor}} who chooses to execute you, or if you unknowingly claim that your target is the {{A|Jailor}} or someone who is confirmed to not be a {{A|Townie}}. *Deception is your greatest power. Use it to throw a {{A|Town Investigative}} off your scent. *You do not visit when commanding a {{A|Mafioso}}. This can be used as a {{A|Psychic}}, {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Executioner}} claim. **However, if your {{A|Mafioso}} dies or is {{A|Roleblocked}}, you could be caught by a {{A|Tracker}} or {{A|Lookout}}. *If a member of the {{A|Mafia}} is not following your orders or acting dangerously (voting against fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}} when not necessary, refusing to hang non-{{A|Mafia}} members when their vote is key), claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} the next day and accuse that person of being suspicious. This might sound like [[gamethrowing]], but it confirms you as a {{A|Townie}}, and the threat can be neutralized. This is called [[bussing]]. *Occasionally, when facing a {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Vampire}}, or {{A|Serial Killer}}, it can be useful for you to bait them into attacking you in order to protect other members of the {{A|Mafia}}. This is generally only a viable strategy when you just need one more night or when you already have at least a plurality, since you'll out yourself as a role with {{A|Defense}} in the process. Also, if you're going to bait by making yourself appear to be evil (generally necessary to bait a {{A|Vigilante}}), ensure that the {{A|Jailor}} is dead. *Remember, while you are generally considered the leader, do not try to be too bossy. The other members of the {{A|Mafia}} may not listen to you if you act rude. Also, remember that other members of the {{A|Mafia}} may know more than you, such as a {{A|Consigliere}} or {{A|Blackmailer}} finding an important {{A|Town}} role. *If you are attacked, act natural. Most {{A|Godfathers}} will not say anything during the day if they were attacked. A few carefully worded lies can keep you from the gallows. **If you where shot by a {{A|Vigilante}}, you can claim that you're a {{A|Bodyguard}} and used your bulletproof vest. Claiming to have been healed by a {{A|Doctor}} can sometimes work too, though if a {{A|Doctor}} dies and kept track of who he healed, this could backfire without a {{A|Forger}}. A {{A|Doctor's}} heal still produces a message of {{A|Defense}}, but there must be an explanation for why a {{A|Doctor}} had any reason to heal you. Claiming to be a {{A|Survivor}} rarely works, since the {{A|Town}} has little reason not to hang a {{A|Survivor}} who has fallen under suspicion, and may even assume them to be a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Arsonist}} (if there is a possibility of a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role). {{A|Survivor}} is also impossible to claim in {{A|Ranked}}, so reserve it for {{A|All Any}}. ***Conversely, you can claim to be a {{A|Veteran}} who alerted and claim that the {{A|Vigilante}} is faking. However this carries several risks, as not only can a real {{A|Veteran}} counter-claim you, you may get called out by anyone else who visited you. Therefore, you should only use this if the {{A|Mafia}} has hit a plurality. ***If the {{A|Vigilante}} is not confirmed and you know who they are, you can quickly counterclaim {{A|Vigilante}} and accuse the real one of having {{A|Defense}} before they even start accusing you. Getting the {{A|Vigilante}} hanged or, ideally,{{A|executed}} will buy the {{A|Mafia}} more time to get majority. *You could try and claim to be a {{A|Vigilante}} on Day 2 and that you attacked one of the members in your {{A|Mafia}} but they were immune. Keep telling the {{A|Town}} to hang them. The {{A|Town}} will realize that a {{A|Vigilante}} can't shoot on Night 1 and assume you are an {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Jester}} and that the person you called out is your target. This strategy helps you in several ways: **An {{A|Executioner}} has {{A|Basic Defense}}, giving credit to your claim since you have {{A|Basic Defense}} as the {{A|Godfather}}. **The member of the {{A|Mafia}} you called out will be considered a {{A|Townie}} ('''Note:''' if you are outed as {{A|Godfather}} somehow, and people find out your role, then experienced {{A|Townies}} might think your that "target" is also a member of the {{A|Mafia}} since this is a common strategy called "[[bussing]]".) **You've also now removed suspicion from yourself and another member of the {{A|Mafia}} since most people will ignore an {{A|Executioner}} or a {{A|Jester}} once they've been revealed. Of course, this requires the cooperation of the other member of the {{A|Mafia}}. In some cases, however, they'll think you're ratting them out and tell the {{A|Town}} you're the {{A|Godfather}} or that you're a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. You obviously don't want this to happen, since it crumbles the alibi you're trying to build. **'''NOTE: '''do not try this in {{A|Ranked}}, you will quickly be hanged or {{A|executed}} if you pretend to be a non-{{A|Town}} role in a competitive [[Game Modes (ToS)|game mode]]. *Try to have a non-member of the {{A|Mafia}} hanged as early as possible. If it works and they are {{A|Town}}, you can claim to be an {{A|Executioner}} and you will work with the {{A|Town}}. If it doesn't work, try to hang them all game; the {{A|Town}} will say you are a bad {{A|Executioner}}. If the {{A|Townie}} you tried to have hanged dies, the {{A|Town}} will not hang you out of fear that you have turned into a {{A|Jester}}. **Although claiming {{A|Executioner}} often works well, it can work out badly as {{A|Jailors}} often execute people who they believe to be an {{A|Executioner}} or who claim/act like one in case they are a role with [[Keyword System|Defense]] faking. They could also hang you, although this is less likely as they may suspect you of being a {{A|Jester}}. *One of the quickest ways to lead to downfall for the {{A|Mafia}} are {{A|Death Notes}} - if the {{A|Mafioso}} is {{A|Roleblocked}} and you kill someone, leaving a entirely different {{A|Death Note}}, then the {{A|Town}} will know that either the {{A|Death Note}} has been changed or, more likely, the person writing it wasn't the same person as the one writing the other {{A|Death Note}}. The easiest way to avoid this is for the {{A|Godfather}} to copy the {{A|Death Note}} of their {{A|Mafioso}}, so that the {{A|Town}} has no idea when one of them has been {{A|Roleblocked}}. *If your {{A|Mafioso}} is {{A|Jailed}}, it can be somewhat risky when choosing a target to kill since attacking an alerting {{A|Veteran}} or a target guarded by a {{A|Bodyguard}} will kill you and put pressure on the {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Mafioso}} the next day. ===Dealing with {{A|Townies}}/{{A|Neutrals}}/{{A|Coven}}=== '''Dealing with an {{A|Investigator}}''': If you are concerned that you may be visited by an {{A|Investigator}}, claim {{A|Bodyguard}} when pressed to claim a result, since that is the only {{A|Town}} role in your investigative results, and it is very hard to disprove. You can even claim to have used your bulletproof vest if someone calls you out as having a higher defense value than their attack value. Of course, {{A|Bodyguard}} isn't always the most plausible claim. but if you were investigated, it is the only thing you can do. If there is an {{A|Arsonist}} or you are playing {{A|All Any}}, claim you might be doused. '''Dealing with a {{A|Sheriff}}:''' A {{A|Sheriff}} cannot find you, but they can find and call out the other {{A|Mafia}} members to the {{A|Town}}. You can claim any {{A|Town}} role or any role with [[Detection Immunity]] ({{A|Neutral Benigns}} are the best choice if you can't claim a {{A|Town}} role). After that, make up a fake yet well-written {{A|Last Will}} if needed. However, if there is evidence mounting against you, there is little you can do. '''Dealing with a {{A|Jailor}}''': Like all evil roles, you should have a claim ready for, if and when you are {{A|Jailed}}. *The most obvious and sometimes only claim is {{A|Bodyguard}} (unless you are playing the {{A|Coven Expansion}}), especially if the {{A|Jailor}} has {{A|Jailed}} an {{A|Investigator}} before. *Alternatively, you can simply claim some other role, such as {{A|Sheriff}} or some other role which will be drawn up for easily, and hope that the {{A|Jailor}} hasn't yet cross-referenced your role with the {{A|Investigator}}. You may be in trouble if their {{A|Last Will}} is exposed to the {{A|Investigator}}, but it's preferable to delay the issue and hope you can win before then than to be executed immediately by a suspicious {{A|Jailor}}. *If all hope is lost, and the {{A|Jailor}} has decided to execute you, remember that the {{A|Jailor}} can still be [[Roleblock|role blocked]] by a {{A|Bootlegger}} or [[controlled]] by a {{A|Witch}} that has teamed up with you. '''Dealing with the {{A|Mayor}}''': Once a {{A|Mayor}} has been revealed, it's a war between you and him in terms of commanding your faction, as both of you are the leader of your respective alignments. Being the {{A|Godfather}} , you know the identity of all the fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}} and can easily communicate with them at night. However, the {{A|Mayor}} faces many difficulties related to these two aspects due to his inability to send or receive whispers and the lack of privacy from belligerent roles during the day. These are the {{A|Mayor's}} biggest pitfalls, which you can use to your advantage. Trying to kill the {{A|Mayor}} immediately after they've revealed is risky, as a {{A|Bodyguard}} could be protecting them. However, {{A|Blackmailers}} are completely unaffected by {{A|Bodyguards}}. A blackmailed {{A|Mayor}} is unable to reason with {{A|Neutral}} roles, instruct other {{A|Townies}}, or reply to them. Thus, the blackmailed {{A|Mayor}} is effectively stripped of all his powers except for the triple vote he has. This tactic has its flaws, too; However, as the {{A|Mayor}} could be protected by a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Transporter}}. A {{A|Lookout}} will be able to call out your {{A|Blackmailer}} if they are present, but this gives you some opportunity. If you have a {{A|Disguiser}}, you can tell them to {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Blackmailer}} to deceive the {{A|Lookout}} into hanging a {{A|Townie}}.

In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, a {{A|Crusader}} can protect the {{A|Mayor}} and kill your {{A|Blackmailer}} or {{A|Mafioso}}, and prevent your attack, so target them first. '''Dealing with a {{A|Survivor}}''': You can [[whisper]] and try to convince them that the {{A|Mafia}} has a better chance of winning than the {{A|Town}}. In return, you can promise that you will not attack them. In the best case, the {{A|Survivor}} will help you hang the {{A|Town}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles in late game; in the worst scenario, they will simply rat you out to the next {{A|Townie}} they see. '''Dealing with a {{A|Witch}}''': The {{A|Mafia}} can win with {{A|Witches}} and it is very common for them to work together, but an ill-informed {{A|Witch}} can cause serious problems for you. If you or a member of the {{A|Mafia}} are repeatedly being controlled by the {{A|Witch}}, it may be a good time to identify the {{A|Witch}} as quickly as possible as they could make you kill your members of the {{A|Mafia}}. '''Dealing with a {{A|Coven Leader}}''': The {{A|Coven Leader}} is a big danger to the {{A|Mafia}} as they can make you kill members of the {{A|Mafia}} or make you or your {{A|Mafioso}} visit the {{A|Medusa}}. Before night 3, you can kill the {{A|Coven Leader}} before they gain their defense, so find and target them early. '''Dealing with a {{A|Medusa}}''': You can kill her at the right time when she doesn't use her Stone Gaze. Your {{A|Bootlegger}} can also role-block her, allowing you to kill her safely; unlike the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Medusa}} is ''not'' immune to being role-blocked. '''Dealing with a {{A|Necromancer}}''': The threat the {{A|Necromancer}} presents depends on what is in the graveyard. To mitigate the threat, use the {{A|Janitor}} and the {{A|Forger}} to thwart their kill potential. You can also have the {{A|Forger}} forge a killing role as a {{A|Town Protective}} role to trick them into killing members of the {{A|Coven}}. '''Dealing with a {{A|Hex Master}}''': Like the {{A|Arsonist}}, they are a silent killer that can thwart your {{A|Consigliere's}} results and can kill all the {{A|Mafia}} if left unchecked. However, unlike the {{A|Arsonist}}, they do not have defense. Try attacking players that show up as {{A|Hex Master}} to the {{A|Consigliere}} as you'll likely hit the {{A|Hex Master}} doing this. '''Dealing with a {{A|Potion Master}}''': Unlike the other {{A|Coven}}, the {{A|Potion Master}} is less of a threat and more of a nuisance, as like a {{A|Doctor}}, they can prevent your attacks from killing members of the {{A|Coven}}, and like the {{A|Consigliere}}, they can directly find the mafia even if {{A|Doused}}. If you suspect that a {{A|Potion Master}} healed the target you attacked, attack them again. Since the {{A|Potion Master}} usually has a 3-day cooldown between potions, you can kill your original target without much interruption. '''Dealing with a {{A|Poisoner}}''': Generally speaking, if there's a {{A|Doctor}} in the game, the {{A|Poisoner}} is virtually a non-threat to the {{A|Mafia}} as the {{A|Poisoner}} serves as a mere distraction for the {{A|Doctor}} as you kill higher priority targets. If someone claims {{A|Poisoned}} on the same night the {{A|Poisoner}} died, tell the {{A|Ambusher}} to target them. '''Dealing with a {{A|Serial Killer}}''': A major obstacle in the way of {{A|Mafia's}} victory is the {{A|Serial Killer}}. The {{A|Serial Killer}} is a wildcard that can make or break the {{A|Mafia}}. Using {{A|Mafia}} role strategies listed below can stop a {{A|Serial Killer}}. However, as {{A|Godfather}}, there is little you can do to get rid of the {{A|Serial Killer}} due to their [[Keyword System|Basic]] Defense. One small strategy that can assist your victory against {{A|Serial Killers}} is to pretend that you are {{A|Town}} and to bait the {{A|Serial Killer}} to attack you. When the day comes, say that you were attacked but you were healed by a {{A|Doctor}} ({{A|Serial Killers}} usually can't accuse you of being the {{A|Godfather}} without revealing themselves in the same round as their attack, but they may do so in their next {{A|Death Note}}, so make sure to dispose of them as soon as possible after being attacked). Because of the {{A|Serial Killer's}} [[Keyword System|Basic]] Defense and the fact that {{A|Serial Killers}} win over any member of the {{A|Mafia}} vs {{A|Serial Killer}} situation, hanging a {{A|Serial Killer}} when there is a small group is vital for a win. A more risky strategy can be done once you find out the {{A|Serial Killer}} due to their [[Keyword System|Basic]] Defense. Claim to be a {{A|Witch}} and you have been controlling the {{A|Serial Killer}}. Proceed to convince the {{A|Town}} on how hanging you would not benefit over hanging the {{A|Serial Killer}}. You could also try saying you will side with the {{A|Mafia}}. It is also possible to claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} after finding the {{A|Serial Killer}}, then accuse the {{A|Serial Killer}} of being the {{A|Serial Killer}}. If you succeed, the added perk of the {{A|Town's}} trust is gained. '''Dealing with a Rogue {{A|Neutral}}''': Sometimes {{A|Serial Killers}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, the {{A|Werewolf}} and the {{A|Juggernaut}} will admit that they are a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, recognizing they're going to lose, and instead side with the {{A|Town}}, meaning they will only attack players the {{A|Town}} tells them to. Essentially, it is considered [[gamethrowing]] to help the {{A|Town}} win, and they will target you and members of the {{A|Mafia}} first. Although this is challenging to counter, since it deals with fighting someone suicidal, there are several ways to keep your team intact. If you have a {{A|Blackmailer}}, you should obviously continue to blackmail that killer and convince the {{A|Town}} to hang them. If you have a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can [[role block]] an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Juggernaut}} constantly. It is also possible to simply remind the {{A|Town}} that they are [[gamethrowing]] by not hanging an enemy. ===In Conjunction with {{A|Mafia}} Roles=== While it may be tempting to micromanage the {{A|Mafia}} and give orders to everyone, it is generally smart to listen to your members for advice and info before giving orders to the members in your faction: *{{A|Mafioso}}: Make sure your {{A|Mafioso}} is choosing a target every night in case you are {{A|Roleblocked}}, and listen for feedback on whether they received a message notifying them of said target having a form of {{A|Defense}} if their attack was unsuccessful. Also, make sure they leave any important information you want to reveal to the {{A|Town}} in their {{A|Death Note}}. **If there's an active {{A|Forger}} or {{A|Janitor}}, make sure your {{A|Mafioso}} is choosing the same target as you to utilize the most efficient usage of their abilities and to ensure they don't waste a forgery or cleaning if you are {{A|Roleblocked}}. **If the role-list does not show a guaranteed {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combo or a {{A|Forger}} forged someone as a {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Godfather}}, you can ask a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or the {{A|Jailor}} to jail/[[Role block|roleblock]] you. Since the {{A|Town}} does not know what {{A|Mafia}} role someone died to (except {{A|Ambusher}}), you can generally clear yourself from suspicion of being the {{A|Godfather}} if played well. **Since your {{A|Mafioso}} cannot be controlled when you command them, consider having your {{A|Mafioso}} claim {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Investigator}}. Doing this can help bait a {{A|Witch}} into targeting your {{A|Mafioso}}, which can be a major help for the {{A|Witch}} trying to find the {{A|Mafia}} to team up without disrupting the rest of the {{A|Mafia}}. *{{A|Consigliere}}: If the {{A|Consigliere}} tells you their results each night, use that to determine who to kill. If they tell you to kill a certain target, listen to them, cause they'll usually tell you that they're an important role (like a {{A|Mayor}}). If they discover a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, you can out them in a {{A|Death Note}}, though sometimes it can be more beneficial for the {{A|Consigliere}} to accuse them publicly while claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}}, gaining the {{A|Town's}} trust. **A competent {{A|Consigliere}} usually tells you what role their results showed the next day (via whispers) or night. Remember, though, that you can't deduce anything about someone they visited the night they were killed (since they wouldn't have had a chance to say anything). **As a general rule, you should keep track of who the {{A|Consigliere}} visits, and avoid killing people the {{A|Consigliere}} has visited and and didn't tell you to kill. In addition, this has the added advantage of rapidly reaching a point where the {{A|Mafia}} knows every role. **For the same reason, when the {{A|Consigliere}} reveals a weak role like a {{A|Survivor}}, consider passing over them for now and killing targets with unknown roles instead. This will increase your chance of finding more important roles like the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} early on. **Conversely, if the {{A|Consigliere}} has investigated most of the other roles and told you only {{A|Town}} roles, any {{A|Neutral Killing}} role you're searching for is probably among the people they haven't visited. *{{A|Blackmailer}}: Coordinate with a {{A|Blackmailer}} to silence dangerous {{A|Townies}} without revealing their {{A|Last Wills}}. If you suspect someone is a {{A|Town Investigative}}, blackmail them every night instead of killing them. While you ''can'' also try to have blackmailed targets hanged, be warned that this is a fairly obvious gambit and will often attract suspicion to you, especially once it becomes clear that the person you accused was blackmailed. Remember, ask the {{A|Blackmailer}} for information on whispers but any competent {{A|Blackmailer}} would tell you if there was important information without being prompted. *{{A|Bootlegger}}: Similar to the {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, use your {{A|Bootlegger's}} distraction abilities to stop pesky {{A|Town Investigative}} roles from revealing your {{A|Mafia's}} identities and to suppress dangerous killing roles. If there is a single {{A|Town Protective}} role protecting someone, (like a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mayor}}) you can tell the {{A|Bootlegger}} to distract them as you kill the {{A|Town Protective's}} target. This has the added bonus of drawing suspicion on the protective role the {{A|Bootlegger}} {{A|Roleblocked}}. As a last resort, tell your {{A|Bootlegger}} to [[role block]] the {{A|Werewolf}} if need be, and put the {{A|Werewolf's}} name in their {{A|Last Will}}. *{{A|Disguiser}}: Communication with your {{A|Disguiser}} is key to pull off successful plays. If other members of your {{A|Mafia}} fall under suspicion, and other {{A|Townies}} have claimed certain roles, you may need to tell your {{A|Disguiser}} to disguise them in order to keep the other {{A|Mafia}} members alive, and instead put suspicion on other {{A|Townies}}. *{{A|Forger}}: Communicate with the {{A|Forger}} to rewrite dangerous info of {{A|Town Investigatives}}. If someone claims a unique role like a {{A|Veteran}}, you can have the {{A|Forger}} forge a silent {{A|Townie}} to draw suspicion on the claim. You can alternatively have the {{A|Forger}} forge someone as {{A|Jester}}, {{A|Witch}} or even a role with defense (provided they left the game) to further deceive the town. You can even have the {{A|Forger}} forge a {{A|Mafia}}-known {{A|Vigilante}} as a {{A|Town Protective}} role to trick the {{A|Retributionist}} or {{A|Necromancer}} into killing their teammates. *{{A|Janitor}}: You should team up with the {{A|Janitor}} for the most efficient usage of their abilities. A cleaned {{A|Townie}} can make it easier to lie about roles and can thwart an {{A|Investigator's}} {{A|Last Will}} logs. Since the {{A|Janitor's}} cleaning is obvious, you can order them around somewhat more directly than most roles; but you might want to be a bit circumspect out of courtesy to them if it's not clear they'll want to clean and they haven't yet outed their presence by cleaning previously. *{{A|Ambusher}}: Similar to the {{A|Crusader}}, command the {{A|Ambusher}} to kill pesky {{A|Town Protective}} roles protecting higher-priority {{A|Town}} roles. You can also command the {{A|Ambusher}} to target the same person as another member of the {{A|Mafia}} (like a {{A|Bootlegger}}) to kill potentially dangerous {{A|Town}} roles like a {{A|Lookout}} or a {{A|Spy}}. Beware of {{A|Mediums}} or multiple non-{{A|Mafia}} visitors as they can reveal the {{A|Ambusher}}. *{{A|Hypnotist}}: The {{A|Hypnotist}} is a wildcard to the {{A|Mafia}}, which means you can utilize their abilities in some ways. You can have the {{A|Hypnotist}} claim {{A|Doctor}} and send a fake {{A|Heal}} message in case you are {{A|Jailed}} without a {{A|Mafioso}}. You can also have them use the {{A|Crusader}} protect message to pass off your {{A|Crusader}} claim. *{{A|Framer}}: Generally speaking, let the {{A|Framer}} do their thing unless you need someone specifically to be {{A|Framed}} to give you a slight advantage. {{MafiaKillTable}} ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{GodfatherAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{GodfatherMessages}} ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} tracking {{A|Godfather}} bug. **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} detecting {{A|Godfather}} visiting victim when {{A|Godfather}} orders {{A|Mafioso}} to kill the victim. **Fixed incorrect {{A|Tracker}} results when {{A|Mafioso}} picks one victim but {{A|Godfather}} chooses another. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Godfather's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Godfather.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Godfather's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Godfather Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **Attackers will now get "Your target is immune" message when attacking {{A|Werewolf}} on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|nights}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Крёстный Отец]] [[Category:Mafia Killing roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Framer}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon = Framer[[File:RoleIcon Framer.png|thumb|left|100px]] |alignment = {{A|Mafia Deception}} |attributes = Attack: None Defense: None |type = Manipulation

'''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''

They must be a {{A|Framer}}! |summary = You are a skilled counterfeiter who manipulates information. |abilities = Choose someone to Frame at Night. |attributestext = If your target is investigated they will appear suspicious.
If there are no kill capable {{A|Mafia}} roles left you will become a {{A|Mafioso}}. |goal = Kill anyone that will not submit to the {{A|Mafia}}. |winwith = '''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}'''
'''{{A|Witch}}''' |mustkill = '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Vampires}}'''
'''{{A|Arsonist}}'''
'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Coven}}'''
'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can choose a target to {{A|Frame}} each {{A|Night}}. {{A|Framing}} a target will show them as suspicious until they are investigated. Your {{A|Frames}} take priority over an {{A|Arsonist}} {{A|Douse}}. *{{A|Framed}} targets will show up as "suspicious" to the {{A|Sheriff}}. *{{A|Framed}} targets will appear to be a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Jester}} (and {{A|Hex Master}}, if playing with the {{A|Coven Expansion}}) to an {{A|Investigator}}. *Upon turning into a {{A|Mafioso}}, previous {{A|Frames}} will remain on the target. ==Strategy== *A strategy to use before the {{A|Night}} phase starts is to say a player is suspicious, and request for a {{A|Town Investigative}} role to check that person. However, an experienced player may realize you could be a {{A|Framer}}, and might call you out on it. **Since players are {{A|Framed}} until investigated, this strategy is not recommended, unless you expect the {{A|Town Investigatives}} to check them numerous times to confirm they are not {{A|Framed}}. *If accused, a possible strategy is to tell the truth about your role, especially if someone whispers you to ask. Most people will brush you off as a bad {{A|Jester}} trying to be hanged and some people may even step up in your defense if you draw too much attention. You don't have to make a clever lie as long as {{A|Investigators}} and {{A|Sheriffs}} suspect that you've been {{A|Framed}} the next {{A|Night}}, allowing you to survive longer. **Try not to press too hard when doing this. Telling the {{A|Town}} directly "You want to hang me!" is the best strategy. Do not be too annoying, as spamming is against the rules, but reinforce the point every {{A|Day}} by repeating that you're a {{A|Framer}} and act annoyed that {{A|Town}} is not doing their duty to hang you. Do this until people are annoyed at you and believe you are a ''confirmed'' {{A|Jester}}. **'''This strategy has a downside''': You could be executed by a {{A|Jailor}} or shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} since killing {{A|Jesters}} is a natural method for these roles. Telling a {{A|Jailor}} you are a {{A|Framer}} will almost guarantee your execution. You could also be attacked by a member of the {{A|Coven}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}. *Your job in the {{A|Mafia}} is to be the "middleman" between the {{A|Mafia}} because you know that if people investigate you, you have a valid reason to say you were {{A|Framed}}. This works even better if there is a {{A|Disguiser}} who visited you the previous {{A|Night}} as any {{A|Spy}} in the game will confirm that you were {{A|Framed}}. *Never keep a {{A|Last Will}} as to who you have actually {{A|Framed}} because this may prove the innocence of those that you {{A|Framed}} and give a clue as to who is {{A|Mafia}} by narrowing down suspects. However, you can write down that you have {{A|Framed}} other members of the {{A|Mafia}} and other fake evidence to mislead the town even upon death. **If you MUST keep track of who you actually {{A|Framed}}, write it in the {{A|Notes}}, as unlike {{A|Last Wills}}, anything written in the {{A|Notes}} won't be revealed to the town. *A possible strategy is not to do anything at {{A|Night}}. While it may seem like this is a waste of your abilities, {{A|Framer}} alone is not very powerful. By not doing anything, you can trick the {{A|Spy}} that there is less {{A|Mafia}}, and if your {{A|Mafia Killing}} is roleblocked or jailed, you can move and trick the {{A|Spy}} that a player has basic defense (bonus if you have another {{A|Framer}} visiting to count as a double visit). However, this may not work in tight role lists, and some {{A|Mafia}} members could expect you to Frame every {{A|Night}}. If someone is confused as to why you aren't doing anything, be sure to explain your reasoning. This strategy can also be used to prevent a death by {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Veteran}} and keep you alive until you become a {{A|Mafioso}}. *While claiming {{A|Town Protective}} or {{A|Spy}} might seem dumb, your visits can cover them up for you. If a {{A|Jailor}} asks for {{A|Town Protective}} and a {{A|Lookout}} on them, you can either claim to be a {{A|Doctor}} that was visiting your target to heal them, or a {{A|Spy}} who was bugging the {{A|Jailor}}, and the {{A|Lookout}} can cover it up for you. **If there is an actual {{A|Spy}} in the game, you can still visit the {{A|Jailor}} to prevent a {{A|Lookout}} from confirming all the visitors as not a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. **Of course, if a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} role blocked the {{A|Jailor}} and you're claiming {{A|Spy}}, things could take a bad turn, as the {{A|Jailor}} would likely call you out for not seeing the role block. ===Who to Frame=== *It's best that you {{A|Frame}} people with names that stick out the most as {{A|Town Investigative}} roles tend to investigate said players first, letting your {{A|Frames}} take effect faster, and in some cases, make the accuser look like an {{A|Executioner}}! *Players that talk {{A|Day}} 1 are often a good target, because it makes them stick out to {{A|Town Investigative}} roles. **Watch for {{A|Veterans}} who are baiting. *Roles that ask for {{A|Town Protective}} roles to be on them but don't claim {{A|Jailor}} are a good first pick, but you should only do this the first {{A|Night}}. **This works especially well if they talk the first {{A|Day}}. **However, some {{A|Town Investigatives}} actually avoid people who talk for fear of them being a {{A|Veteran}}. *Framing people that are number one, number eight, or number fifteen on the player's list is a good idea too as they also tend to be investigated first. *Try framing {{A|Vampire Hunter}} claims. If an {{A|Investigator}} checks them, they will probably think they are a {{A|Vampire}} and accuse them. **However, a {{A|Sheriff}} that checks the target will not assume the target is a {{A|Vampire}}, since they will appear suspicious. The silver-lining is that the {{A|Sheriff}} may accuse them as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} instead. *If people are suspicious of a particular person, there's a good chance that people will investigate them. It's also a good chance for you to {{A|Frame}} them. Be wary though, as a {{A|Lookout}} may be one of these investigative roles and see you visit this person, so try to {{A|Frame}} them a Day before they become suspicious. *Since {{A|Framers}} don't die to {{A|Traps}}, a {{A|Framer}} may check for {{A|Lookouts}} or {{A|Trappers}} on a confirmed {{A|Town}} target such as a revealed {{A|Mayor}}. *If {{A|Spies}} don't exist or are dead, consider framing each {{A|Night}}. Most {{A|Sheriffs}} and {{A|Investigators}} will check a different person every {{A|Night}}. Since your {{A|Frames}} last until the player is investigated (even if you die or get promoted), they are almost guaranteed to investigate those you {{A|Framed}}. *Framing a {{A|Mafia}}-known {{A|Jester}} could possibly have them hanged, killing a {{A|Townie}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} in the process. Plus, if the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} decides to kill them, they've wasted a shot or execution. *Remember, sometimes it isn't necessary to {{A|Frame}} someone every {{A|Night}}. Framing on a {{A|Full Moon}} risks being killed by the {{A|Werewolf}}; framing on any {{A|Night}} risks visiting the {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Medusa}}. Worst of all, whenever you {{A|Frame}} ''anyone'', you confirm to every {{A|Spy}} in the game that your target is not a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, accomplishing the exact opposite of your goal. **If there's a {{A|Disguiser}}, you can ask them to {{A|Disguise}} you to hide your visits to mitigate the {{A|Spy}} risk. **Fortunately, if you {{A|Frame}} someone who asks for '''TP/LO''' on {{A|Day}} 1, you can prevent a {{A|Lookout}} using a {{A|Spy}} from confirming all visitors as not a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. Additionally, you may not even be seen by the {{A|Lookout}} at all, since players who ask for {{A|Town Protectives}} and {{A|Lookouts}} usually have more than 3 visitors. *You could ask another {{A|Mafia}} member to [[Common_Player_Behaviors#Bussing|bus]] you to "confirm" themselves if you believe you are useless, however, higher level players will suspect you if you don't put up a good defense as being {{A|Framed}}. *Since visiting a target confirms them as non-{{A|Mafia}} to every {{A|Spy}} in the game (unless there's a {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Transporter}}, or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}), consider framing people who are being killed by the {{A|Mafia}}. By doing this, you can trick the {{A|Spy}} that the dead {{A|Townie}} was forged, causing them to call out and discredit the info in the {{A|Last Will}}. You can also do this to hide the real {{A|Forger's}} visits within your visits. **If a {{A|Spy}} asks a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} to role block a certain person (that's not a member of the {{A|Mafia}}), you can move and visit the same target as the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} to make them appear as a {{A|Bootlegger}} to the {{A|Spy}}. If they're role blocking a {{A|Mafia}} teammate, try asking a {{A|Witch}} to control you into visiting the {{A|Tavern Keeper's}} target. ***You can also do this to a {{A|Transporter}} as well to make them look like a {{A|Hypnotist}}. If they make the {{A|Mafia}} kill another {{A|Mafia}} member, provided you visit the same target as the main {{A|Mafia}} killer (or all {{A|Spies}} are dead beforehand), you can make it appear that there's a {{A|Forger}}-{{A|Hypnotist}} combo. *Consider only visiting if you're sure it will give the {{A|Mafia}} an advantage, especially in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. Your ability is ''extremely'' weak; your chance of your {{A|Frames}} having an actual effect is tiny, and there are countless ways things can go wrong: *If there is a living {{A|Spy}} in the game, it is basically impossible for you to successfully {{A|Frame}} anyone since they can immediately speak up and reveal your target was visited by the {{A|Mafia}} if a {{A|Sheriff}} calls one of your targets suspicious; in that case, randomly visiting is not only counterproductive but actively hurts your team, especially if a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} sees you visit someone and they cross-reference their information with a {{A|Spy}}. *Visiting exposes you to a {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Crusaders}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, a {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Medusa}}, {{A|Juggernaut}} and {{A|Pestilence}}; it spreads the plague for a {{A|Plaguebearer}} as well. The damage that these can do vastly outweighs the minimal impact your visits have... *There may not be a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} in the game at all, especially in the {{A|Coven Expansion}} In that case, your visits accomplish nothing beyond exposing you. On top of that, your ability is only partially effective against an {{A|Investigator}}, since they'll know the {{A|Framed}} result is suspicious. *As of {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, however, your ability is slightly more powerful since now your {{A|Frames}} are permanent until investigated. If you {{A|Frame}} the right people, it can buy the {{A|Mafia}} some extra {{A|Days}}, especially if you get promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}} and/or are the last {{A|Mafia}} member overall. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{FramerAchievements}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, {{A|Frames}} would last only one {{A|Night}}, whether they were investigated or not. *If an {{A|Investigator}} finds a "''{{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, or {{A|Jester}}'' (+''{{A|Hex Master}}'' in the {{A|Coven Expansion}})" result during {{A|Night}} one in a {{A|Ranked}} game, the chance of them really being a {{A|Framer}} is ~33% (25% in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}). This assumes, however, that the {{A|Jailor}} jails a target and a {{A|Framer}} {{A|Frames}} someone. **However, remember that with 9 options for the one {{A|Random Mafia}} role, a {{A|Framer}} only has a ~11% chance of appearing in {{A|Ranked}} in the first place. *According to a poll made by [[User:LevinSnakesRise|LevinSnakesRise]], the {{A|Framer}} is the second most hated role in Town of Salem with 263 votes, for the reasoning that it was too slow and boring (similar to {{A|Arsonist}}). Other comments were that you had to be extremely lucky for the role to be effective at all and that it was underpowered and needed a buff (keep in mind that this poll is somewhat outdated, as {{A|Framer}} has received buffs since then). ==History== *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Frames}} will now last until an investigative role targets the {{A|Framed}} player instead of only the {{A|Night}} the player is {{A|Framed}}. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Framer's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Framer.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Framer's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Framer Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Клеветник]] [[Category:Mafia Deception roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}}{{Story}} == Mechanics == * You may choose to {{A|Blackmail}} someone each {{A|Night}}, preventing them from speaking that {{A|Day}}. ** You can also read private [[Whisper|whispers]]. * When a {{A|Blackmailed}} target tries to speak, they will simply receive a message saying: "'''You are {{A|Blackmailed}}.'''" and no one will be able to see their original message or their attempt of speaking. * When a {{A|Blackmailed}} target tries to [[whisper]], they will simply receive a message saying: "You cannot chat or whisper while {{A|Blackmailed}}." and no one will be able to see their original message or their attempt of [[whispering]]. * If the {{A|Blackmailed}} target is voted to go on trial during the [[Phases#Defense|Defense]] phase, the {{A|Blackmailed}} target's message will be changed to "I am {{Amne|blackmailed}}.". They will then be unable to say that message again whilst still on trial. * Your target is also unable to [[whisper]], but they can still be whispered to. * If you visit a {{A|Veteran}} on alert and you are killed, they will still be {{A|Blackmailed}} the next {{A|Day}}. * A {{A|Blackmailed}} {{A|Mayor}} can still reveal that {{A|Day}}. * You cannot {{A|Blackmail}} a target that was jailed that {{A|Night}}. You will be notified that your visit failed and the jailed person will know that someone tried to {{A|Blackmail}} them. * You can't affect your target's ability to write in their {{A|Last Will}} and {{A|Death Note}}. * You can't affect your target's ability to vote and unvote someone. * You are still able to read [[whispers]] when dead. == Strategy == * As a {{A|Blackmailer}}, your role in the {{A|Mafia}} is to silence a confirmed {{A|Townie}} or a person who is accusing a member of the {{A|Mafia}} to make them stop accusing them. ** However, despite having the ability to {{A|Blackmail}}, your alternative role is to also serve as an eavesdropper, gaining important information from [[whispers]] during the {{A|Day}} to provide leads for the {{A|Mafia's}} activities at {{A|Night}}. * You may also play as a {{A|Spy}} entirely, passing on at {{A|Day}} who gets killed, forged, framed, cleaned or investigated to gain the {{A|Town's}} trust. If you see someone get visited but not killed, use that against them by calling them out as immune and get them [[Hanged]] to easily gain majority while still killing off the remaining {{A|Town}} or threatening {{A|Neutrals}}. Usually. when you use this strategy, you should not {{A|Blackmail}} people. You will be immediately called out as suspicious if you {{A|Blackmail}} anyone. ** You can also use this against other {{A|Spy}} claims. {{A|Blackmail}} someone and accuse any {{A|Spy}} claims of being the {{A|Blackmailer}}. Be careful with this strategy as it may get you immediately killed if town realizes you were lying. ** As the {{A|Spy}} can now bug people's houses and know what notifications their target had received, you can exploit your knowledge of what the other members of the {{A|Mafia}} are. Don't do this every {{A|Day}}, but every once in a while, you can claim you bugged the house of someone who was transported, attacked or roleblocked by the {{A|Bootlegger}}. Often times, players will announce that they were {{A|Transported}}, controlled, roleblocked, etc. You could claim you bugged them and claim you saw this happen. Have a look at the bugging messages and think of ways you could deceive the other players into thinking you're really the {{A|Spy}}, but don't overdo it. They could get on to you after a while. You could also ask for protection and distract the {{A|Lookout}} by watching you. ** Feel free to take the opportunity to give false information to the {{A|Town}}. You can be very manipulative with this role. This can confuse the {{A|Town}}, and even cause them to not suspect actual members of the {{A|Mafia}}. However, don't make it blatantly obvious that you are indeed giving false information. You will have to be careful when manipulating the {{A|Town}} in order not to get caught. Also, any other {{A|Spies}} in the game may call your out for lying about who the {{A|Mafia}} visited at {{A|Night}}. ** (Note: As of {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6537}}, this strategy is less effective as you can no longer easily "confirm" yourself as a {{A|Spy}} since {{A|Spies}} can no longer read [[whispers]]). *** This strategy is also much less effective in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, since you do not know who the {{A|Coven}} visit, unless someone claims {{A|Poisoned}} or controlled. * In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, you can alternatively claim {{A|Guardian Angel}} and state who's your target since the {{A|Town}} normally leaves {{A|Guardian Angels}} alone. If your "target" dies, the {{A|Town}} will assume you've become a {{A|Survivor}} if you've made the correct claims to explain why you did not protect them (e.g [[Role blocking|role blocked]]). Note that if you choose a {{A|Mafia}} member as your "target", you risk outing your {{A|Mafia}} friend if you die and your role is revealed. * Your second ability allows you to collect valuable information for the {{A|Mafia}} via [[whispers]], this can help by finding someone's role or to discover what actions some {{A|Townies}} are planning, use this to help the {{A|Mafia}} find and take down a potentially dangerous target like a {{A|Lookout}} or strengthen your claims if someone asks you for your role and {{A|Last Will}}. ** If anyone attempts to collect roles via [[whispers]], you can tell this to the {{A|Mafia}} so they can plan their operations more accurately now that the roles of the {{A|Townies}} have been revealed. You can also harvest info from whispers by {{A|Town Investigative}} roles, the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mediums}} and use them to your advantage. ** If someone reveals their {{A|Last Will}} and role via [[whispers]], you can tell the {{A|Forger}} their will so they can write down exactly the correct order their {{A|Last Will}} follows to help a {{A|Mafia}} member escape suspicion or even frame someone. ** If there are {{A|Vampires}} or {{A|Coven}} in the game, you find them by their [[whispers]] if they decide to try and coordinate via [[whispers]]. Of course the {{A|Coven}} can simply use the {{A|Coven Chat}} to go around this problem, but the {{A|Vampires}} can't utilize their {{A|Vampire chat}} as effectively due to the potential existence of a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. You can do this to find other {{A|Neutrals}} as well if they attempt to coordinate via [[whispers]]. ** Use [[whispers]] to your advantage! If you find out who the {{A|Jailor}} is jailing through [[whispers]] or by convincing them to jail a {{A|Mafia}}-known {{A|Townie}}, you can then ask a {{A|Witch}} who has teamed up with you to control the {{A|Jailor}} into the person they're jailing to force an execution, making the {{A|Jailor}} lose their executions. * You can claim {{A|Investigator}} if a lot of people are [[whispering]] their roles to an important {{A|Townie}}, such as the {{A|Jailor}}. "Investigate" anyone [[whispering]] to someone else their roles and post the investigative results of their claim. Additionally, your {{A|Mafia}} visits do not match up to your fake visits so a {{A|Spy}} cannot bust you. ** This can backfire if one of your targets dies and happens to be another role, or if a {{A|Tracker}} tracks you and sees you visit no one/the person you {{A|Blackmailed}} INSTEAD of the target you "investigated". You can claim that your target was transported or forged in some of these cases. * If you or the {{A|Consigliere}} finds a {{A|Town Investigative}} or {{A|Town Support}} role, it can be useful to {{A|Blackmail}} them rather than killing them instantly, as they can reveal crucial information in their {{A|Last Will}}. {{A|Spies}} should especially be {{A|Blackmailed}} as soon as possible. ** This strategy can backfire if the person you {{A|Blackmail}} either dies to something like a {{A|Veteran}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role or they are jailed and can speak the next {{A|Day}}. * Continue to {{A|Blackmail}} the same person for a few {{A|Nights}}, then casually ask why they have been so quiet, and it will put suspicion on them. This only works when the person hasn't been giving signals about being {{A|Blackmailed}}; additionally, be warned that this will tend to call attention to you - if it later becomes clear they were {{A|Blackmailed}}, smart players will immediately be suspicious of anyone who pointed out that they were silent. For this reason, it might be best to wait and hope that a {{A|Townie}} notices their silence on their own. ** {{A|Blackmailing}} the same person repeatedly has a few risks; if they're a {{A|Veteran}}, they'll easily kill you, while if they signal that they were {{A|Blackmailed}}, a {{A|Lookout}} (or, worse, the {{A|Werewolf}}) may catch you {{A|Blackmailing}} them the next {{A|Night}}. On the other hand, like any member of the {{A|Mafia}} who visits the same person repeatedly, it has the advantage that you avoid revealing multiple people as non-{{A|Mafia}} to a {{A|Spy}}, although smart {{A|Spies}} will easily notice that the person has been role blocked or {{A|Blackmailed}} for a few {{A|Nights}} straight, therefore exposing a {{A|Blackmailer's}} existence. * {{A|Blackmailing}} the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Town Investigative}} can be good at making them less effective. Be careful of {{A|Blackmailing}} a revealed {{A|Mayor}} as there could be a {{A|Lookout}} watching him, and without a {{A|Disguise}}, you will be called out by the {{A|Lookout}} due to the {{A|Mayor's}} signal of being {{A|Blackmailed}}. * {{A|Neutrals}} such as the {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}} and the {{A|Arsonist}} will have no defense for their actions if they are {{A|Blackmailed}}, so if you want to get rid of them, {{A|Blackmail}} them as soon as possible and accuse them. * If you are [[Role blocking|role blocked]] or your target dies in the same {{A|Night}}, you or another member of the {{A|Mafia}} may act as if they have been {{A|Blackmailed}} (you may also simply choose not to {{A|Blackmail}} anyone for a {{A|Night}}). However, this carries the danger of a {{A|Spy}} calling you out, thus getting you [[Hanged]]. Only use this if there is no {{A|Spy}} in game or there's a {{A|Disguiser}}. * Try to {{A|Blackmail}} people who are accusing a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or are chatty. The {{A|Town}} may forget what they said and go on to other things if you {{A|Blackmail}} them for a few {{A|Nights}} or if they die. ** However, if you {{A|Blackmail}} someone accusing a {{A|Mafia}} member, it will confirm their suspicions. Alternatively, you can use this strategy to frame someone outside of the {{A|Mafia}}. * If you think you may be put on trial the next {{A|Day}}, a good strategy is to not {{A|Blackmail}} anyone that {{A|Night}} and instead pretend you are {{A|Blackmailed}} yourself. Again, this carries a risk of a {{A|Spy}} calling you out. However, if you have a {{A|Bootlegger}} on your side, getting your {{A|Bootlegger}} to role block the {{A|Spy}} (providing you know who the {{A|Spy}} is) to prevent the {{A|Spy}} from checking whether you were actually visited by the {{A|Mafia}}. You can also have a {{A|Disguiser}} visit you to make it appear that a member of the {{A|Mafia}} visited you to a {{A|Spy}}. Be careful with this strategy as it can make you look very suspicious. * If you have a {{A|Bootlegger}}, try targeting the same target as them. It is usually effective and can create a misHang against someone (e.g a {{A|Sheriff}} that is role blocked cannot do their {{A|Night}} action and if they are {{A|Blackmailed}}, they cannot state that they were role blocked). * {{A|Blackmailing}} people every {{A|Night}} isn't necessarily a good plan; when the {{A|Town}} realizes that people are being {{A|Blackmailed}}, it becomes much harder for you to claim {{A|Spy}}, and they're likely to be more cautious with [[whispers]]. * Another possible strategy, especially with four members of the {{A|Mafia}} in a {{A|Ranked}} or {{A|Ranked Practice}} game, is to simply ''not {{A|Blackmail}} at all.'' Considering the {{A|Blackmailer's}} main ability is not as useful as that of other {{A|Mafia}} members early game, this is not just a viable strategy but a powerful one. The main reason is that your ability to read [[whispers]] is generally more powerful and it may allow you to collect more information from someone than a {{A|Consigliere}} would (especially if there's an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Hex Master}} in the game). The other reason being that if you're called up to the stand, this makes a {{A|Spy}} claim much more plausible. If it becomes clear there is an active {{A|Blackmailer}}, many {{A|Townies}} will [[Hang]] {{A|Spy}} claims right on the spot. This requires the cooperation of the other members of the {{A|Mafia}}, especially in {{A|Ranked Practice}}, by not having them reveal the existence of a {{A|Blackmailer}} to a real {{A|Spy}}. ** A strategy is to pretend to be {{A|Blackmailed}} yourself. If the {{A|Mafia}} is struggling mid-game, provided that there is no {{A|Spy}} (or you had a {{A|Disguiser}} disguise you), you can remain completely silent and signal to other players that you are '{{A|Blackmailed}}' by voting and canceling two times. This will mess up their suspicions, but be careful not to overdo it. Discuss with the {{A|Mafia}} to let different members act {{A|Blackmailed}} on different {{A|Days}}. Do be warned that if a faking {{A|Mafia}} member is [[Hanged]] or killed it will immediately draw suspicion on the others. This strategy works better if you haven't {{A|Blackmailed}} the previous {{A|Night}}. This strategy is not as effective as it once was, since most players in {{A|Ranked Practice}} and {{A|Ranked}} are used to immediately suspecting anyone that claims to be {{A|Blackmailed}}, as it is a popular defense for {{A|Blackmailers}} on trial. ** Be careful when {{A|Blackmailing}} people over and over again in the {{A|Coven Expansion}} as a {{A|Crusader}} can protect your target and can kill you. ** One particularly interesting, if not outright chaotic, strategy is to claim you are the {{A|Jailor}} in an {{A|All Any}} match. Since {{A|Jailor}} won't be a guaranteed role '''and''' it is a [[Unique Role]], the chances of your position being questioned is not likely. Even if a {{A|Jailor}} does exist, chances are they will jail you and, in turn, out the fact that there is a known {{A|Jailor}} that most evils will want to keep a watch on and find. If a {{A|Jailor}} does '''not''' exist, don't {{A|Blackmail}} anyone so no one questions your legitimacy; thus you can read whispers without people being suspicious of a {{A|Blackmailer}}, and you will likely end up having a legitimate protection on your side in terms of the {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}. Even better, should you die at {{A|Night}} (most likely due to a {{A|Witch}} controlling a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Serial Killer}}), chances are that the {{A|Town}} will go after someone who claimed to be protecting you at {{A|Night}}. This is useful if a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} gets roleblocked or converted into a {{A|Vampire}} '''or''' a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Arsonist}} claimed to protect you to prove their role. *** In the event a {{A|Jailor}} '''does''' exist and they jailed you, claim you wanted to guide them into you as something useful to a {{A|Jailor}} (i.e. {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, or {{A|Vampire Hunter}}). This could give you a few more Days to keep you alive, even if your cover gets blown. * You continue to hear [[whispers]] after death. While this is rarely useful, it can be used to out mutual enemies to the {{A|Medium}} or to trick them by lying about a [[whisper]]'s content. * At times, a {{A|Jailor}} will [[whisper]] a {{A|Town Protective}} claim to protect them. They will often put in their will afterward that if they die, to kill the {{A|Town Protective}} claim for lying. If you have a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can stop the {{A|Town Protective}} from doing their job and also getting a [[Hang]] off, saying that they didn't protect the {{A|Jailor}}. This can be done with many important {{A|Town}} roles other than the {{A|Jailor}} as well. == Dealing with {{A|Blackmailers}} == * If you are a {{A|Townie}} and suspect someone of being {{A|Blackmailed}}, use this simple test to determine whether or not the target was {{A|Blackmailed}}: ask the suspected person to vote and cancel the vote of someone twice if they are {{A|Blackmailed}}. Most people will appreciate you for checking. * Even if nobody asks you and you are {{A|Blackmailed}}, voting and un-voting the same person anyway will get the attention of the {{A|Town}} and they will know that there is a {{A|Blackmailer}} in game. The earlier the {{A|Town}} knows about the {{A|Blackmailer's}} presence, the earlier they can stop [[whispering]] important information. * If it's proven that someone was {{A|Blackmailed}}, ask the {{A|Jailor}} to jail them. The {{A|Jailor}} will collect information from this person and will prevent the {{A|Blackmailer}} doing their work. It may even save the game since {{A|Blackmailers}} usually {{A|Blackmail}} people with important things to say. * If a {{A|Townie}} [[whispers]] you their role claim and an {{A|Investigator}} [[whispers]] you that {{A|Townie's}} investigation results, they may be a {{A|Blackmailer}} who is pretending to be an {{A|Investigator}}. You should call them out if said {{A|Townie}} dies and they pretended to be another role. * If it turns out that someone was {{A|Blackmailed}}, be suspicious of anyone who accused them or who pointed out how silent they were; inexperienced {{A|Blackmailers}} will often accuse the person they {{A|Blackmailed}}. In particular, if someone claims to be {{A|Blackmailed}} on the stand, anyone who tries to dispute that or suggests that they are faking should be seen as ''extremely suspicious''; it is extraordinarily rare for non-{{A|Mafia}} roles to fake being {{A|Blackmailed}} (due to the high risk of being outed by a {{A|Spy}}). You should almost always vote innocent on people who say they were {{A|Blackmailed}} on the stand, and investigate, role block, or even vote up the person who accused them to demand their role. ** {{A|Blackmailers}} will often invent new "rules" about how {{A|Blackmailing}} and the {{A|Blackmailed}} message works to try and cast suspicion on the person they've been {{A|Blackmailing}} (for instance, complaining that they said they were {{A|Blackmailed}} too many or too few times, or too quickly/too slow). Turn it around and look at it from the other direction; falsely claiming to be {{A|Blackmailed}} is an ''extremely'' rare and risky strategy, one that has few benefits and which can be easily discounted by a {{A|Spy}}, while {{A|Blackmailers}} trying to get their targets [[Hanged]] is extremely common. Therefore, any claim that someone who is acting {{A|Blackmailed}} is "faking it" should be seen as extremely suspicious, especially if it comes from their main accuser. ** Note however, that a {{A|Disguiser}} can mess the {{A|Mafia}} visits for the {{A|Spy}} and legitimize the {{A|Blackmailer's}} claim that someone is "faking it" by disguising the {{A|Blackmailer}}. They may also be able to have a {{A|Mafia}} member falsely claim {{A|Blackmailed}} to halt [[whispers]] and put any {{A|Spy}} claims under suspicion. ** You can possibly throw a {{A|Blackmailer}} off guard by [[whispering]] to a a {{A|Spy}} test. A foolish, gullible, or inexperienced {{A|Blackmailer}} may tell the town the correct code. It's a dead giveaway since {{A|Spies}} can no longer read [[whispers]], and with proof, you can promptly [[Hang]] the {{A|Blackmailer}}. == [[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]] == {{BlackmailerAchievements}} == [[Messages (ToS)|Messages]] == {{BlackmailerMessages}} == Trivia == * Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.0.3431}}, {{A|Blackmailers}} could not hear private messages. * Since the release of {{VH|Version 2.0.0.0.6537}}, it's more difficult for {{A|Blackmailers}} to claim to be a {{A|Spy}}, as {{A|Spies}} can't hear [[whispers]] anymore. * As of {{VH|Version 2.5.1}}, people who are {{A|Blackmailed}} can only say "I am blackmailed." once while on trial. * If someone was {{A|Blackmailed}} the {{A|Day}} the game ends, they will no longer be {{A|Blackmailed}}. * When [[whispering]] as a {{A|Blackmailer}}, your own [[whisper]] will be shown twice, as when you [[whisper]], your [[Abilities (ToS)|Ability]] to read [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] will activate, causing you to see the [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] you sent from your own perspective (seen as "To [Name]") and once from a {{A|Blackmailer's}} perspective (seen as "From [Your name] to [Target's name]"). This might be a bug. == History == * {{VH|2.5.5.12200}} ** The {{A|Blackmailer's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement_Blackmailer.png|30x30px]]. ** Added {{A|Blackmailer's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon_Blackmailer_Circled.png|30x30px]]). * {{VH|2.5.1.10655}} ** {{A|Blackmailed}} players can now only say "I am blackmailed." once on trial. * {{VH|1.5.0.3431}} ** {{A|Blackmailer}} can now see [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]]. * {{VH|Town of Salem Release}} ** Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Шантажист]] [[uk:Blackmailer]] [[Category:Mafia Support roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

They must be a {{A|Bootlegger}}. |summary = You are a beautiful dancer working for organized crime. |abilities = Distract someone each night. |attributestext = [[Role blocking|Sharing a drink]] blocks your target from using their role's night ability.
If there are no kill capable {{A|Mafia}} roles left you will become a {{A|Mafioso}}.
