'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You may choose to {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} a target each {{A|Night}}, which prevents them from using their {{A|Night}} ability. **You may {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} someone who left the game the same {{A|Day}}/{{A|Night}}. This can be used for tricking {{A|Spies}}. **You cannot be {{A|Roleblocked (Bootlegger)}}. *If you role block a {{A|Serial Killer}} (that isn't Cautious), or a {{A|Werewolf}} (during a {{A|Full Moon}}), they will attack you. **If said roles are {{A|Jailed}}, your visit will fail and they will not attack you. They will however be notified that someone tried to {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} them while in jail. **You will know exactly if you {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} a {{A|Serial Killer}} or not. You will ''not ''know if you directly {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} a {{A|Werewolf}}, you will only know that you were attacked by one. The {{A|Werewolf}} themselves however will know. **A {{A|Bodyguard}} can counter-attack both of these roles if they protected you. ***{{A|Serial Killers}} will still attack their intended target. *There are multiple roles that are [[Role block Immunity|immune]] to your {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} (such as the {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, and {{A|Pestilence}}). *If a {{A|Pirate}} duels you, you will still be able to {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} someone because you are {{A|Roleblock Immune}}. *If there are no kill capable {{A|Mafia}} roles left, you will always be the first {{A|Mafia}} member to be promoted to {{A|Mafioso}}. ==Strategy== *As a {{A|Bootlegger}}, your job is to cause as much trouble as possible to the {{A|Town}}, {{A|Coven}} and {{A|Neutrals}} without getting caught. You are also the {{A|Mafia's}} last line of defense if there is an {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Sheriff}} roaming around. While {{A|Doctors}} and {{A|Bodyguards}} protect an {{A|Investigator}} from harm, they do not protect the {{A|Investigator}} from being {{A|Roleblocked (Bootlegger)}}, making you a key role to the {{A|Mafia}}. *As you are a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, you should avoid a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}-style list of everyone you've role blocked in your {{A|Last Will}}, as it reveals who the non-{{A|Mafia}} are. However, since you die if you role block a {{A|Werewolf}}, you may want to write down just the ''last'' person you role blocked; that way, if you die to a {{A|Werewolf}}, you will likely get them Hanged. As an added bonus, even if the {{A|Werewolf}} is not your target and happens to target you at random, you may get an innocent {{A|Townie}} Hanged anyway! But if you want to hide who is the {{A|Werewolf}}, when you {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} someone, don't write the last person you role blocked in your {{A|Last Will}}. This strategy will make the {{A|Town}} unaware of who is the {{A|Werewolf}}, and the members of the {{A|Mafia}} will still know who you had visited last {{A|Night}}. You can do this to the {{A|Veteran}} as well. *It is one of your highest priorities to find and role block {{A|Town Investigative}} roles, as doing this makes their job completely useless. Another high priority is to role block the {{A|Town Protective}} roles so that the {{A|Mafia}} may kill without interruption (You can also do this to the {{A|Potion Master}} and {{A|Guardian Angel}} as well). The next high priority is other killing roles (but avoid the {{A|Veteran}} on alert, the {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, {{A|Serial Killers}}, and {{A|Pestilence}} as you'll die upon visiting them) so that the members of the {{A|Mafia}} may not die at {{A|Night}} (ie. if a member of the {{A|Mafia}} is jailed, you can role block the {{A|Jailor}} so they can't execute said member of the {{A|Mafia}}. Be careful if there is a {{A|Spy}} in-game as they can easily call out the existence of a {{A|Bootlegger}} if you do role block the {{A|Jailor}}). You can also do this to prevent a non-factional {{A|Neutral}} role (like a {{A|Jester}}) from dying at {{A|Night}}, encouraging them to side with the {{A|Mafia}}. Also, role blocking a {{A|Spy}} prevents them from seeing who the {{A|Mafia}} had visited that {{A|Night}} which may sometimes be important. Finding the {{A|Arsonist}} and stopping them from possibly dousing/igniting members of the {{A|Mafia}} can lead you to an easy victory (however, it's might be in the {{A|Mafia's}} interest to let him douse other players thus throwing off an {{A|Investigator}}. This is especially true early game) The same applies to {{A|Juggernauts}} as unlike the {{A|Werewolf}}, they do not rampage at home regardless if they were role blocked or not, allowing you to permanently shut them down at any time. *As a {{A|Bootlegger}}, always try to work with the other {{A|Mafia Support}} roles in the game. The {{A|Consigliere}} or {{A|Blackmailer}} may find an important role in the game for you to role block, such as a {{A|Town Investigative}}/{{A|Town Protective}} role, a {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Jailor}}, youngest {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, or even a {{A|Medusa}} that is not immune to your roleblocks and will be able to be killed safely. *Being a {{A|Bootlegger}} is the easiest role to cover up since you can claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, although sometimes this is tricky, since {{A|Town Support}} and {{A|Random Town}} roles could all be claimed and confirmed. Since the effects of your actions are noticeable to the rest of the {{A|Town}} without killing them, it may be possible to claim that you are a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} if someone asks your role, and list the people you've blocked the past few {{A|Nights}} (players can say, "Yes, I was role blocked.") Doing so may help you win over the {{A|Town's}} favor and secure your position in the role-list, especially near the end of the game. You may even prove your role by publicly promising to role block a particular person the next {{A|Night}}. But if you are planning to role block a confirmed {{A|Vigilante}}, don't claim to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, because then questions will arise when the {{A|Vigilante}} says he's been continuously being role blocked when he wants to shoot somebody (unless there's a {{A|Hypnotist}} using the controlled message on him to help your claim). **You can also claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and pretend role block one of your {{A|Mafia}} members (especially one accused of being a {{A|Mafia Killing}}) to ‘confirm’ both (more info listed belowM). **Unlike a {{A|Hypnotist}}, your {{A|Tavern Keeper}} claim cannot be disproven by {{A|Roleblock (Bootlegger)}} immune roles or roles that produce obvious results at {{A|Night}}. **If you are claiming {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, you should not role block ''any'' confirmed {{A|Town}} unless you absolutely need to. Since a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} would be role blocking suspicious people, doing so could make people believe you are a {{A|Bootlegger}} instead. **If you want to claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, see if there is a {{A|Spy}} and {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Spy}} is your worst enemy when claiming {{A|Tavern Keeper}} because they know your {{A|Mafia}} visits and can report them to the {{A|Town}}. Of course this is negated with a simple {{A|Disguise}}. ***You can also scramble your role blocks in your last will so a {{A|Spy}} doesn't suspect you, however a smart townie might notice they were roleblocked on a different {{A|Night}} and you will likely be Hanged.  **While being a {{A|Bootlegger}} may be easy to fake as a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, remember the fact that you still retain the attributes of a normal {{A|Tavern Keeper}} as well. This means that you will still die if you role block a {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}. However, this can be useful to the {{A|Mafia}}, as they now are aware of said person being evil, especially if your {{A|Last Will}} gets bloodied the next day. *Watch out for {{A|Lookouts}} on roles like the {{A|Jailor}}. They can easily call you out as a {{A|Bootlegger}}. Make sure to prioritize these roles to kill first or have a {{A|Disguise}} to divert suspicion onto another {{A|Townie}}. *If the {{A|Mafia}} is planning on killing a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Doctor}}, then it may be a good idea to role block the {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Doctor}} to prevent them from using their temporary self protections to ensure their death (Doing this to a {{A|Survivor}} can have a similar effect). You cannot prevent a {{A|Veteran}} from using their self protections since {{A|Veterans}} are [[Role block Immunity|Role block Immune]] and will kill both you and the {{A|Mafia}} role attacking the {{A|Veteran}}. **You can also do this to {{A|Survivor}} claims to test for {{A|Night}} immunity. If you suspect the claim is a {{A|Werewolf}}, test them on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. *If you're facing {{A|Vampires}}, you want to identify and continuously role block the youngest {{A|Vampire}}. The easiest way to do this is to identify a likely {{A|Townie}}, someone who is definitely not a {{A|Vampire}} yet and then role block them repeatedly; ideally, the {{A|Vampires}} will eventually bite them, at which point you'll be able to keep them from biting again. **However, if you do not know or cannot find who the youngest {{A|Vampire}} is, you could be wasting your role block on a useless person, especially a {{A|Vampire}} that is not the youngest. Keep this in mind when you could be role blocking a far more dangerous target. **If the {{A|Ambusher}} killed a {{A|Vampire}} and their target survived the {{A|Night}}, there is decent chance that their target has been converted. It would be a good idea to roleblock the {{A|Ambusher's}} original target as they could be the newly converted {{A|Vampire}} if they weren't killed, and you'll be able to keep the {{A|Vampires}} from biting again. If they're an immune role, you can still role block them to prevent a potential {{A|Arsonist}} from igniting. *The {{A|Coven}} is more vulnerable to [[Role block|role blocks]] in general, since they produce obvious deaths/messages unlike the {{A|Vampires}}. If you find a member of the {{A|Coven}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}} or a {{A|Poisoner}} from role-blocking them, you can then either use public accusation to get them Hanged, or ask the other {{A|Mafia}} to kill them. **Unlike a {{A|Veteran}}, a {{A|Medusa}} is not immune to your role blocks, and will be unable to kill you (or anyone else) if you visit them. Therefore, you can role block them to allow the {{A|Mafia}} to kill them safely (the same applies for a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}). ***A {{A|Consigliere}} can safely search for the {{A|Medusa}} with your assistance. This also applies to {{A|Survivor}} claims you suspect to be {{A|Medusa}}. ** Keep in mind that the {{A|Coven Leader}} and the {{A|Necromancer}} are both immune to your roleblocks. *MA viable strategy is to claim to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, then write in your {{A|Last Will}} that you have role blocked members of the {{A|Mafia}}. Then, those members of the {{A|Mafia}} can "confirm" you to be a true {{A|Tavern Keeper}} by saying that they were role blocked. Additionally, if you die and your {{A|Last Will}} is revealed, the {{A|Town}} might think the people you role blocked were also {{A|Town}} (since you can't role block members of the {{A|Mafia}}). Be wary of this as this strategy is commonly used and people may suspect you as a {{A|Bootlegger}}. **Another way of performing this is if the {{A|Mafia}} does not kill for the {{A|Night}}, and you role block someone, claim they are the {{A|Godfather}} who got {{A|Roleblocked (Bootlegger)}}. if the {{A|Town}} thinks you are a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, you might just divert the blame onto a {{A|Townie}}. *If you want to claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, it may be a good idea to not randomly role block early. *Claiming {{A|Tavern Keeper}} could be dangerous as if a confirmed townie asks you to role block a fellow {{A|Mafia}} member. You could be easily outed as evil as you cannot role block them. Of course, your other {{A|Mafia}} member can claim role blocked in order to lower suspicion on them and you, but if they die, you will look very suspicious to the {{A|Town}}. **You may also get outed by a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} when they see you didn't visit your other {{A|Mafia}} member, which is why you take some caution when deciding to claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. *Another viable strategy is if you don't want to claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is claiming {{A|Spy}}, since you know who the {{A|Mafia}} visits and you can fake an accurate bug result by claiming to have bugged the person you {{A|roleblocked}}. If the {{A|Jailor}} meta is in play, you can role block the {{A|Jailor}} {{A|Night 1}} and claim to have seen the {{A|roleblock}} in your bug result. **Of course, this can backfire if anything else happened to the {{A|Jailor}} (ie. other roleblocks, controls), as they'll call you out for not seeing the other messages. **Do not try this in {{A|Coven All Any}}, there are {{A|Coven}} visits you will not be able to detect. *You can also claim {{A|Transporter}} since this also fits in your {{A|Investigator}} results. You can strengthen your claim with a {{A|Forger}} or a {{A|Hypnotist}} collaborating with you which may be important to take away a possible {{A|Town Support}} claim space needed to get a {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Retributionist}} Hanged. *In {{A|Coven All Any}}, it is a good idea to claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, as the only {{A|Town}} roles who can detect you ({{A|Sheriffs}} and {{A|Spies}}) are unlikely to spawn. In addition, you can {{A|Roleblock}} non-{{A|Mafia}} members who didn't claim, which will make {{A|Town}} trust you if they end up being the {{A|Coven}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{BootleggerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{BootleggerMessages}} ==Trivia== *{{A|Bootlegger}} is the only role to have an exact duplicate of its role in another faction. *The {{A|Bootlegger's}} old icon ([[File:Achievement Consort.png|30x30px]]) (when it was still known as {{A|Consort}}) reflected how the {{A|Bootlegger}} is an {{A|Escort|Mafia}}, with it being extremely similar to the {{A|Escort's}} old icon ([[File:Achievement Escort.png|30x30px]]). *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6537}}, a {{A|Serial Killer}} would attack a {{A|Consort}} for [[Role block|role blocking]] them even if they were {{A|Jailed}} and/or executed. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.11}} **Role renamed to {{A|Bootlegger}} **Updated {{A|Bootlegger's}} icon to a placeholder ([[File:RoleIcon Bootlegger.png|30x30px]]), previous icon was ([[File:RoleIcon Consort.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Reanimated {{A|Ambusher}} will no longer attack roles that attempted to visit but were {{A|Roleblocked (Bootlegger)}}. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} incorrectly seeing someone visiting when {{A|Roleblocked (Bootlegger)}}. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Consort's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Consort.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Consort's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Consort Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced as {{A|Consort}}. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Супруга]] [[Category:Mafia Support roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Role blocking]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Roleblock Immune]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You may {{A|Disguise}} any living member of the {{A|Mafia}}, as a living, non-{{A|Mafia}} target. This will cause {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Investigators}}, {{A|Lookouts}}, and {{A|Spies}} to receive incorrect results. **The {{A|Sheriff}} will be fooled by a {{A|Disguiser's}} {{A|Disguise}}; the {{A|Sheriff}} will see the {{A|Disguised}} {{A|Mafia}} member as innocent or suspicious depending on the role of the {{A|Mimic}} target. **An {{A|Investigator}} will see the {{A|Disguised}} {{A|Mafia}} member's investigative result as the investigative result of the specific role they were {{A|Disguised}} as. For instance, disguising someone as a {{A|Sheriff}} will change their investigative results to that of the {{A|Sheriff}} for the {{A|night}}. **A {{A|Lookout}} will see {{A|Disguiser}}'s second target visit the player they were watching, instead of the {{A|Disguised}} {{A|Mafia}} member who actually performed the visit. For example, if the {{A|Mafioso}} visits Player A, and a {{A|Lookout}} is watching Player A, but a {{A|Disguiser}} has {{A|Disguised}} the {{A|Mafioso}} as Player B, the {{A|Lookout}} will see Player B visit their target instead of the {{A|Mafioso}}. *** When you {{A|Disguise}} yourself as someone and a {{A|Lookout}} is watching you, the {{A|Lookout}} will see your {{A|Mimic}} target visit you instead of seeing you visit yourself. However, a {{A|Lookout}} will still see your name when watching the player you {{A|Disguised}} yourself as. The latter may be a bug. **A {{A|Spy}} will not see the visits of a {{A|Mafia}} member {{A|Disguised}} as a non-{{A|Mafia}} member. ***You will hide your own visits from from the {{A|Spy}} when you {{A|Disguise}} yourself. ***If a {{A|Mafia}} member is {{A|Disguised}} as a {{A|Coven}} member, the {{A|Spy}} will '''not''' see the visit as a {{A|Mafia}} visit nor a {{A|Coven}} visit. *You have an unlimited amount of {{A|Disguises}}. **You will not receive a message confirming your {{A|Disguise}} has succeeded. **You will not receive a message stating which role you have {{A|Disguised}} a {{A|Mafia}} member as. **You can {{A|Mimic}} any non-{{A|Mafia}} role. **You cannot {{A|Disguise}} a {{A|Mafia}} member as a target that has been {{A|Jailed}}. **You can {{A|Disguise}} a {{A|Mafia}} member as a target that has left the game before the {{A|Night}} ends (and vice versa). **The second target does not need to die in order to {{A|Disguise}} as them. **Neither targets will get a notification about being visited by a {{A|Disguiser}}. *If a {{A|Consigliere}} ends up targeting a {{A|Disguised}} player, the {{A|Consigliere}} will not be fooled. The {{A|Consigliere}} will see the {{A|Disguised}} player as their real role. *Someone who is {{A|Doused}}/{{A|Hexed}} and {{A|Disguised}} as someone will still appear under the {{A|Arsonist's}}/{{A|Hex Master's}} investigative result to the {{A|Investigator}}. *If you get {{A|controlled}}, the {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} will only change your first target. Your second target stays the same. **If you choose no action at night, the {{A|controller}} cannot force you to visit anyone (so it might be wise to stay home on the second {{A|Night}} if you suspect that a {{A|Coven Leader}} might {{A|control}} you into {{A|Medusa}}). ==Strategy== ===Deciding who to {{A|Disguise}}=== *In the beginning, if you decide to {{A|Disguise}}, you should consider what {{A|Mafia}} member needs your {{A|Disguise}} the most, as some of your {{A|Mafia's}} abilities are nullified by a {{A|Spy}}, and they could call out your {{A|Mafia}} for having visits that match {{A|Mafia}} visits. **If you are unsure which {{A|Mafia}} member to {{A|Disguise}}, it's almost always best to {{A|Disguise}} yourself when you lack other plans. Not only will this protect you from a prying {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}}, but this will also hide both your visits from the {{A|Spy}}, allowing you to freely use your ability without being called out by a {{A|Spy}}. *Later in the game, as more roles are known, you might be able to {{A|Disguise}} your {{A|Mafia}} to help support their claims to an {{A|Investigator}}. **For example, if you originally {{A|Disguise}} someone as a {{A|Sheriff}}, and later find an {{A|Executioner}}, you can use the {{A|Executioner}} as an alternative should the {{A|Sheriff}} somehow die. **It is recommended to tell the {{A|Mafia}} to not kill certain targets so you can {{A|Disguise}} them to match their claim if an {{A|Investigator}} is roaming around. *Your {{A|Disguises}} are a powerful tool to negate the info of {{A|Town Investigatives}}, use them to throw a suspicious {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} off the {{A|Mafia's}} scent. **If there's a {{A|Sheriff}}, you may need to {{A|Disguise}} one of your {{A|Mafia}} teammates to make them appear as innocent to the {{A|Sheriff}}. If there's a {{A|Spy}} in-game, you will need to {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Janitor}} in particular as their target to "spoof" the visits and prevent the {{A|Spy}} from seeing any anomalies in the {{A|Mafia}} visits (ex. Player C died to {{A|Mafia}}, but the {{A|Spy}} did not see the {{A|Mafia}} visit Player C). *A risky play you can make is to ask a {{A|Lookout}} to watch you while you {{A|Disguise}} yourself as someone who claimed a non-visiting role (like a {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Retributionist}}). If a {{A|Lookout}} does watch you, they'll see the {{A|Medium}} "visit" you, which can lead to the {{A|Lookout}} accusing the {{A|Medium}} claim, causing confusion within the {{A|Town}} and potentially getting 3 {{A|Townies}} killed. **More experienced, smarter players, however, will probably not fall for this trick, and will be certain that you're a {{A|Disguiser}} trying to exonerate themselves. *Unlike a {{A|Transporter}}, you can {{A|Disguise}} yourself even if a {{A|Crusader}} is protecting you. This is because you do not swap a targets visitors like the {{A|Transporter}} does, allowing the {{A|Crusader}} to protect you and not someone else. The result is the {{A|Crusader}} attacking the {{A|Disguiser}} they are protecting. You can use this to help "confirm" yourself to the {{A|Town}}, fake the existence of an immune role, or solidify a {{A|Town Protective}} pair. *Your visits are seen by {{A|Spies}} (Unless you {{A|Disguised}} yourself), you can use this to your advantage and {{A|Disguise}} other {{A|Mafia}} members to make it harder for the {{A|Spies}} to find the {{A|Mafia}} by process of elimination. **You can also have the {{A|Mafia}} member you {{A|Disguised}} claim role blocked, blackmailed, or {{A|Framed}} even if the role associated with the ability does not exist in the game since the {{A|Spy}} will see your visit on the {{A|Mafia}} member. ***However, this can backfire if the {{A|Spy}} bugged the {{A|Mafia}} member claiming blackmailed or role blocked so consider the risk proceeding with this strategy. ****This risk is negated if the {{A|Mafia}} member you visited is jailed, as they can claim attempted blackmailed or role blocked in jail, and the {{A|Spy}} cannot disprove this with their bugs. **Since you visit 2 targets, you can {{A|Disguise}} a {{A|Mafia}} member as the {{A|Mafia's}} kill target to make it appear to a {{A|Spy}} that the target was forged, while at the same time protecting your teammates. You can also {{A|Disguise}} them as someone who asks for '''TP/LO''' on {{A|Day}} 1 as well to prevent a {{A|Lookout}} and {{A|Spy}} from confirming any visitors. ***If a {{A|Mafia}} member has disconnected (left the game), you can still {{A|Disguise}} them to trick the {{A|Spy}}, making them believe that it's a {{A|Forger}} game and there's actually no dead {{A|Mafia}}. *If your existence has been exposed by {{A|Spies}}, you can ask a {{A|Witch}} who has teamed up with you to control you into disguising a non-{{A|Mafia}} since she can only control your first target and not your second target (similar to a {{A|Witch}}). If played correctly, this will trick the {{A|Spy}} into calling out non-{{A|Mafia}} by seeing the visits, which may be valuable for misHanges. You can do this with a {{A|Transporter}} as well. ====Working with {{A|Mafia Deception}}==== *{{A|Spies}} are the biggest threat to a {{A|Forger}} and {{A|Framer}}, since they can easily discredit their efforts by seeing the {{A|Mafia}} visits. Use your {{A|Disguises}} to hide their visits from the {{A|Spy}} so their work isn't easily discovered by them. *The {{A|Hypnotist}} is a special case where it depends on what they are claiming. It is recommended to not {{A|Disguise}} them if they are claiming {{A|Doctor}} and having the {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles not attack to support their claim to a {{A|Spy}}. Otherwise, feel free to {{A|Disguise}} them as needed. *The {{A|Janitor}} and other {{A|Disguisers}} are generally a lower priority for your {{A|Disguises}} since the other {{A|Disguisers}} can easily protect themselves, and your role's existence may be exposed by a {{A|Spy}} if you {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Janitor}} as anything other than their {{A|Cleaned}} target. ====Working with {{A|Mafia Killing}}==== *If all the {{A|Town Protectives}} and {{A|Spies}} are dead, you can {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Mafioso}} and tell them to attack certain key roles like the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Mayor}}, or a confirmed {{A|Townie}}. If there is a {{A|Lookout}} watching them, they'll likely tell the town to Hang the person you {{A|Disguised}} the {{A|Mafioso}} as, which will often result in the {{A|Lookout}} getting killed at night by {{A|Town Killing}}, which will severely hurt the {{A|Town}}. **If there is a {{A|Spy}} in the game, however, it is a bad idea to {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Mafioso}}, especially during early game. If the {{A|Mafioso}} kills someone, and the {{A|Spy}} doesn't see that person get visited by the {{A|Mafia}}, this will confirm the existence of a {{A|Disguiser}} and the {{A|Spy}} will know that one of the players visited by {{A|Mafia}} is the {{A|Mafioso}}. This is why in a {{A|Spy}} game, you should generally {{A|Disguise}} the {{A|Mafioso}} '''only''' as whoever they are killing (however, this will make the {{A|Lookout}} think that you are the {{A|Mafia Killing}}). *Disguising the {{A|Godfather}} is generally only useful if the {{A|Mafioso}} is Jailed, roleblocked, or simply does not exist. The {{A|Godfather}} does not visit if the {{A|Mafioso}} is available and the {{A|Lookout}} may catch the {{A|Mafioso}} or worse, the {{A|Spy}} might discover the presence of a {{A|Disguiser}} and catch the {{A|Godfather}} if they see an abnormal visit count. Keep this in mind, especially in ranked. If the {{A|Mafioso}} is jailed or dead, refer to the {{A|Mafioso}} section. *The {{A|Ambusher}} only really needs your {{A|Disguises}} if they want to hide their visits from the {{A|Spy}} and to be protected from {{A|Sheriffs}} and {{A|Investigators}}, since their kills may expose the {{A|Disguiser's}} presence to a {{A|Spy}} if they kill someone, provided the victim kept an accurate will. Of course, you can claim the victim was controlled in this case. **Contrary to popular belief, the {{A|Disguiser}} cannot change the {{A|Ambusher's}} name to any visitor, as they will always see the {{A|Ambusher}} prepare an ambush and not the person you {{A|Disguised}} the {{A|Ambusher}} as. ====Working with {{A|Mafia Support}}==== *As you cannot tell what role you are disguising someone as, a {{A|Consigliere}} or a {{A|Blackmailer}} can help by finding {{A|Town}} roles that aren't important enough to kill but have investigative results full of {{A|Town}} roles for you to {{A|Disguise}} your {{A|Mafia}} as. *Since your {{A|Disguises}} hide {{A|Mafia}} visits from the {{A|Spy}}, feel free to {{A|Disguise}} any of the {{A|Mafia Support}} roles so their claims aren't exposed by a {{A|Spy}} for having matching {{A|Mafia}} visits. **For example, if the {{A|Consigliere}} decides to claim {{A|Investigator}}, you can {{A|Disguise}} them so they don't have to scramble their wills as much. The same applies for a {{A|Bootlegger}} claiming {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. *If the {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer}} has an important role pinned down, you can {{A|Disguise}} them to protect them from a {{A|Lookout}} seeking to find the {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer}}. **In addition, disguising the {{A|Blackmailer}} can lead to a {{A|Spy}} calling out that the blackmailed victim is "faking" by looking at the {{A|Mafia}} visits. ====Working with {{A|Town Investigative}}==== *{{A|Town Investigative}} roles might leave behind important information on who to {{A|Disguise}} as. An {{A|Investigator}} can give you a list of possible roles when they show their wills, and a {{A|Lookout}} might reveal {{A|Town Protectives}} being on important {{A|Town}} roles. ==Dealing with {{A|Disguisers}}== Successfully dealing with {{A|Disguisers}} is tricky, as they can not only fool investigative roles into believing they are a {{A|Townie}}, they can make other {{A|Mafia}} members appear innocent as well. *{{A|Sheriffs}} and {{A|Investigators}} can be completely thrown off with their results, but this gives them some opportunity. If a player they investigated turns out to actually be a {{A|Mafia}} member upon their death, anyone who supported the claim of that person could possibly be a {{A|Mafia}} member themselves. *{{A|Lookouts}} are harmed by a {{A|Disguiser}} heavily, as they can completely disregard the result of the name the {{A|Lookout}} receives that {{A|night}}. However, if the person they saw visiting the target was not the person who actually did, it not only confirms the presence of a {{A|Disguiser}}, but the person they saw is more likely not {{A|Mafia}} themselves. **In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, {{A|Trackers}} are not harmed at all when tracking a {{A|Disguiser}}. If you see someone visit two targets, call them out, especially if they claim {{A|Doctor}}. If they turn out to be a {{A|Disguiser}}, you can bust another {{A|Mafia}} member as well since one of the {{A|Disguiser's}} targets has to be {{A|Mafia}} unless they {{A|Disguised}} themselves or a {{A|Coven Leader}}/{{A|Transporter}} interferes. *Look for claims! Once {{A|Townies}} begin dying off, the role list will become more filled and slots will be taken up. If someone is claiming to be an investigative role when all possible slots for investigative roles have been taken, regardless of whether they have matching results or seem innocent, they are evil. **Bear in mind the {{A|Mafia}} may keep some {{A|Townies}} alive for {{A|Disguise}} targets and to put suspicion on them. **This strategy is useless if the dead {{A|Townies}} are {{A|Cleaned}}, {{A|Stoned}}, ''forged'' or you're playing {{A|All Any}}. *Although {{A|Spies}} can have their results discredited, most people visited by {{A|Mafia}} members will not be {{A|Mafia}} members themselves. Once a {{A|Disguiser}} has been exposed, use the {{A|Mafia}} visits to whittle down the confirmability of players to weed out the {{A|Mafia}} members in the process. {{A|Disguisers}} can only {{A|Disguise}} one other {{A|Mafia}} member at a time; use it to your advantage. **In games with a guaranteed {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Mafioso}} at the start, like [[Game Modes (ToS)|Ranked]], if a {{A|Spy}} sees that four people were visited by the {{A|Mafia}}, then it usually means that one of them is the {{A|Godfather}} that the {{A|Disguiser}} targeted (since there is no visit from the {{A|Godfather}} to hide if the {{A|Mafioso}} is alive and not {{A|roleblocked}}). ***Seeing four {{A|Mafia}} visits as {{A|Spy}} in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Ranked]] can also suggest that the {{A|Disguiser}} was unable to hide a {{A|Mafia}} visit because one of their targets was {{A|Jailed}} (and thus the {{A|Disguise}} failed), which would still mean that one of the people visited by {{A|Mafia}} is most likely a {{A|Disguised}} {{A|Mafia}} member. ***Keep in mind that a {{A|Transporter}} or a {{A|Witch}} can manipulate the {{A|Disguiser}} into visiting two non-{{A|Mafia}} members, which can also result in the {{A|Spy}} seeing four visits if the other {{A|Mafia}} members also visit someone. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{DisguiserAchievements}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.9}}, a {{A|Disguiser}} would trade bodies, names, and placement on the [[Maps (ToS)|Village]], but not {{A|Last Wills}}. They could only do this 3 times and required the targeted player to die. This caused some great confusion and was very easy to bypass (by writing your name in your will), and some people used this ability to get other people banned. **The {{A|Disguiser}} would also receive a message "You have successfully Disguised yourself!" when they target a player who died the same {{A|Night}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, a {{A|Disguiser}} could only {{A|Disguise}} themselves as other living players, affecting only an {{A|Investigator}}. Upon the death of the {{A|Disguiser}} the same {{A|night}} or if they are Hanged the following {{A|day}}, they would instead appear as the role of the person they {{A|Disguised}} as. Now the {{A|Forger}} has the ability to change roles upon death instead. **There used to be a glitch where if a {{A|Disguiser}} had {{A|Disguised}} themselves as a {{A|Medium}}, they would have a nonfunctioning seance button after death. **Several other roles, such as {{A|Witch}} and {{A|Necromancer}}, can select two targets, but only visit one of their targets, usually their first target. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.0}} **The {{A|Disguiser}} can no longer fake their role upon death. **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now {{A|Disguise}} any {{A|Mafia}} member rather than only the {{A|Disguiser}} themselves. **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now change {{A|Lookout}} results to show the {{A|Mafia}} visit as being a visit from another player being {{A|Disguised}} as. **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now change {{A|Sheriff}} results to show the {{A|Disguised}} with the results of whatever role the {{A|Disguised}} was {{A|Disguised}} as. **The {{A|Disguiser}} now being able to visit {{A|Mafia}} members also means that the {{A|Spy}} now sees {{A|Disguiser}} visiting their own {{A|Mafia}} members. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Disguiser's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Disguiser.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Disguiser's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Disguiser Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.5.9.4557}} **The {{A|Disguiser}} can no longer trade player possession for up to 3 times. **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now {{A|Disguise}} as other players, stealing their {{A|Investigator}} results. If they die the same {{A|night}} or the following {{A|day}} (via [[Hanging (ToS)|Hanging]]), the role they {{A|Disguised}} as is shown instead of "{{A|Disguiser}}". *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Маскировщик]] [[Category:Mafia Deception roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{Amne|(Amne)|Amnesiac}} |alignment={{A|Neutral Benign}} |avatar=[[File:Forgetful Freddy.png|150px]] |actionother= Select a dead player in the graveyard. You will remember their exact role. You may not select {{A|Stoned}} or {{A|Cleaned}} players. |investigator = '''Classic Results'''

'''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvResCVN3}}. |consigliere= Your target does not remember their role. They must be an {{A|Amnesiac}}. |goal= Remember who you were and complete that role's goal. |summary=You are a trauma patient that does not remember who they were. |winswith= Team and allies of chosen target. |mustkill= Enemies of chosen target. }} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *At {{A|night}}, you may select a dead player's role from the [[graveyard]] to remember yourself as. You will always become the true role of your target, despite any {{A|Forger}} changes. *When choosing a player to remember, the players will appear alphabetically, not in the order in which they died.[[File:Example Amnesiac Remember.png|thumb|300x300px|An example of remembering a role ({{A|Consigliere}}).]] **This ability is assumed to be {{A|Astral}} since {{A|Tracker}} cannot see the {{A|Amnesiacs}} visit the dead player, and they will not die to a dead {{A|Pestilence}}, unlike the {{A|Necromancer}}. ***However, you can still die to a {{A|Werewolf's}} {{A|Rampage}} if a {{A|Coven Leader}}/{{A|Witch}} controls you to a {{A|Werewolf's}} target. *The role you remembered will be announced for everyone to see at the start of the following {{A|day}}. *If multiple {{A|Amnesiacs}} choose to remember any [[Unique Role]], the {{A|Amnesiac}} who joined the lobby first will succeed, while the others will fail. *You are unable to select roles of players who have been {{A|cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|stoned}} by a {{A|Medusa}}. *If you are killed the same {{A|night}} you attempt to remember a role with a defense value, you will still die as an {{A|Amnesiac}} due to your low priority. *If you remember yourself as the {{A|Godfather}} when all {{A|Mafia}} members are dead, you will instead remember yourself as a {{A|Mafioso}} and the {{A|Town}} will see this. If there's at least one {{A|Mafia}} member alive, then you will become the {{A|Godfather}}, as long as that only {{A|Mafia}} member isn't another {{A|Godfather}}. **Even after you successfully become {{A|Godfather}}, you can still get "promoted" to {{A|Mafioso}} after the current {{A|Mafioso}} dies. Due to a bug, the game does not see the {{A|Amnesiac}}-turned-{{A|Godfather}} as a kill capable {{A|Mafia}} role. *If you remember yourself as the {{A|Coven Leader}} when there's one or more {{A|Coven}} members alive, you are guaranteed to inherit the {{A|Necronomicon}} once the member who currently possesses it dies. *If you remember yourself as {{A|Pestilence}}, you will instead remember yourself as a {{A|Plaguebearer}} and the {{A|Town}} will see this. However, you will become {{A|Pestilence}} the following {{A|night}}. **{{A|Pestilence}} will not attack you if you attempt to remember their role, since you remembering a role isn't considered a visit. *Although {{A|Amnesiacs}} are seen as innocent to the {{A|Sheriff}}, if you remember yourself as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} (not the {{A|Godfather}}), {{A|Coven}} (without the {{A|Necronomicon}}), a {{A|Serial Killer}}, or a {{A|Werewolf}} (on a {{A|Full Moon}}), you will be seen as suspicious by them. *If you are role blocked or controlled into someone who did not die, you will be unable to remember a role. *Being controlled into yourself announces to the {{A|Town}} that an {{A|Amnesiac}} has remembered being an {{A|Amnesiac}}. **If you are controlled into someone who died the same {{A|Night}}, you will will be forced to become that players role. ==Strategy== *Revealing as an {{A|Amnesiac}} early in the game is risky. It might prevent you from becoming a target if you join the winning team, but it eliminates your anonymity (and most of the fun) if you choose an evil role. Note: If you reveal and announce you will claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}} the next {{A|night}}, you are almost guaranteed a win, if you indeed become a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}}. **The only threats that would visit you are the {{A|Vampires}}, since they usually want to convert you to join their faction, thus preventing you from being an extra vote to another faction, as well as allowing you to win while dead. Of course, {{A|Vampires}} can be blocked through your vest. *Try not to talk too much or make yourself a target before you pick a role. You do not want {{A|Investigators}} finding out who you are if you are picking an evil role; nor do you want to be killed by the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} at the {{A|night}} before or, worse, the {{A|night}} you choose a role to remember that you were like. *If you reveal that you are an {{A|Amnesiac}} to one team, it would be in your best interest to earn their trust and protection by remembering that you were like a role that places you on their side. If you do reveal and remember an opposing role, like the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, you place yourself at a great risk of getting killed. *If you survive long enough, you can remember that you were like an {{A|Arsonist}} the last {{A|night}} of the game and win in the following stalemate, since the {{A|Arsonist}} wins in a stalemate versus most roles, namely: the {{A|Godfather}}, the {{A|Serial Killer}} and the {{A|Jailor}} (if he has no executions left). This is especially successful if you play the rest of the game with a benign attitude, remaining neutral, appearing to be A.F.K (Away From Keyboard), being discovered and keeping it neutral, making the {{A|Town}} believe you are a {{A|Survivor}}, etc. *If your role is known and there is a living {{A|Town Protective}}, you could choose to become one too and let the other protect you. Be careful, though! If somebody says they are a {{A|Town Protective}} role but are lying, they can easily kill you or gain free protection away from the {{A|Town}}. *In games with {{A|Plaguebearer}}/{{A|Pestilence}}, you can claim {{A|Survivor}} and team up with another evil such as a {{A|Serial Killer}}. When the game is nearing its end, and after the {{A|Plaguebearer}}/{{A|Pestilence}} has died, and you're certain that everyone else besides you two are going to die, remember {{A|Plaguebearer}}/{{A|Pestilence}} and steal the win. Note that this strategy can be switched up, for instance; remembering a {{A|Juggernaut}}, {{A|Arsonist}} (as previously stated), or a {{A|Werewolf}}, depending on the people left in the game and who has died. *'''{{A|Survivor}}''': Outside forces such as {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Investigator}} may threaten you to join their side if they find out you're {{A|Amnesiac}}. Try to claim to be a {{A|Survivor}}, if possible, but if there's only one {{A|Neutral Benign}} role and then, if you pick your role, it will be obvious that you are {{A|Amnesiac}}. Even worse, the {{A|Town}} might Hang you because they thought there was already another {{A|Neutral Benign}}. Note that most {{A|Jailors}} might execute {{A|Survivor}} claims especially if the claim is not convincing, or if the {{A|Jailor}} is aggressive. *Not all {{A|Amnesiac}} strategies involve claiming another role to stay hidden. Simply claiming {{A|Amnesiac}} {{A|day}} 1 and promising to remember {{A|Neutral Benign}} can ensure that evils ignore you. **If you want to try this, don't say you will remember {{A|Town}}. This can lure {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} onto you and can get you killed. This also applies to promising to remember other alignments other than {{A|Neutral Benign}}, since the {{A|Town}} can simply Hang you. *If the game seems like it will end soon, but there is no clear winning team, don't try and wait another {{A|night}}. If the game ends and you haven't picked a side yet, you don't win despite staying alive. Even if everyone but the {{A|Amnesiacs}} die, you will still lose. *If there are ''multiple'' {{A|Amnesiacs}} in the game and one of the others gets outed, you can take advantage of this by remembering that you were like an evil role yourself, which will likely get them Hanged (and increase your chance of winning as a member of the {{A|Mafia}}.) Be careful though, the person that was getting called out could be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or your future ally. *You have the ability to near-perfectly confirm yourself as any role by announcing what you intend to recall the {{A|day}} before you remember that you were like a role. This works best if you're about to recall an uncontroversial role like {{A|Survivor}}, but you can also use it to confirm yourself as a {{A|Witch}} to an entirely evil {{A|Town}}. There is one risk when doing this; another {{A|Amnesiac}} may remember a different role and get you Hanged or killed at {{A|night}}. **This strategy may also be used by other roles (typically evils) to buy them a {{A|day}} and saying they were roleblocked when {{A|Town}} does not see the message for remembering as an {{A|Amnesiac}}. *One particular strategy is to claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} {{A|day}} 1. Then, hope a {{A|Jester}} dies early on so that you can remember that you were like it. The {{A|Town}} will remember that you had claimed to be a {{A|Survivor}}, and hopefully Hang you, giving you the win. **An aggressive {{A|Jailor}} can disrupt this strategy however, since they can decide to execute you since you are an outsider of the {{A|Town}}. *Any attributes of your new role will take effect starting the following {{A|day}}; e.g. you will not see the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, or {{A|Vampire}} windows until the {{A|night's}} deaths are called out, and you will not have Defense, will not see {{A|Mafia}} visits as a {{A|Spy}} and will not clean any {{A|Arsonist's}} gas until the '''next''' {{A|night}}. Fortunately, you will still be able to get achievements for remembering that you were like certain roles, e.g. I Am Who I Am (see [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]]). **If you win, it will only count as an {{A|Amnesiac}} win for your achievements, but you are able to gain achievements for your new role. *When possible, you should choose your role based on whichever side you think will win the game based on its current situation. That said, sometimes you're forced to pick a side without much to go on, or to choose whether you want to join the one available in the graveyard; in that case, it can be useful to take the role list for your current game mode into consideration. **In {{A|All Any}}, the {{A|Mafia}} has a higher chance to appear, but it's important to pay attention and try to figure out how many there are - if you see one in the graveyard, they could have as many as 3 left, or as few as 1 (or even 0, if the one dead {{A|Mafia}} is their killer.) {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles also have a higher chance in {{A|All Any}}, especially if there are multiples of the same type, and the immunity is worth more due to the higher number of kills per {{A|night}}. **In {{A|Coven All Any}}, you're often better off waiting a bit longer than in other modes, since a large number of [[Factions (ToS)|factions]] and killers makes it hard to predict who will have the advantage after the first few {{A|nights}}. {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles are worth even more than in normal {{A|All Any}}, since a large number of different [[Factions (ToS)|factions]] of killers makes their immunity so valuable; but make certain no [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] has an overwhelming advantage first. ==Selecting Your Role== *If a [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] knows you're an {{A|Amnesiac}} and you join an opposing [[Factions (ToS)|faction]], expect to be Hanged or killed quite quickly. It's best to get a plan at the beginning at what you want to become before you take action and claim. *You cannot select roles that were {{A|Cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Stoned}} by a {{A|Medusa}}. *You can choose to remember that you were like a dead {{A|Amnesiac}}. The first time you do this, you will earn an [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]]. This can be used as a means of confirming your role as an {{A|Amnesiac}} without permanently turning into another role, as it will be announced the following {{A|day}}. *If you choose to become an {{A|Executioner}}, your target will be one of the currently living {{A|Townies}}, except for the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}. If there are no {{A|Townies}} alive, or if only a {{A|Mayor}} and/or {{A|Jailor}} exists, you will automatically become a {{A|Jester}}. The town will see you have become an {{A|Executioner}}. *If you choose to become a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, your target will be anyone who is still alive. If your target dies the same {{A|night}}, you will automatically become a {{A|Survivor}} instead. In this case, the other players will be notified that you turned into a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, not a {{A|Survivor}}. *If you remember yourself as a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} when all {{A|Vampires}} have been killed, you will remain that way until the rest of the game unless another {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers themselves as a {{A|Vampire}}, and dies before converting. *If you choose to remember that you were a {{A|Juggernaut}}, you will start at the level that the previous {{A|Juggernaut}} was at. *It may be tempting to simply wait for a role you want and recall that. While this option is one of the most fun parts of playing {{A|Amnesiac}}, remember that your desired role may not be in the game or may not die. *One strategy for {{A|Amnesiacs}} is to wait until later in the game, then become a role with the team that seems to be winning. This will add another vote for the team you choose (i.e: {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Town}}, etc.), which will boost your chances of winning, and allow you to appeal to that side if they try to Hang you. The downside to this is that you risk being killed before then. (since, unlike {{A|Town}} and {{A|Mafia}}, you can't win while dead.) *If you are being threatened into remembering that you were like a {{A|Mafia}} role by the {{A|Mafia}} that has identified you using a {{A|Consigliere}}, you can remember that you were like a {{A|Town}} role with the ability to protect itself, such as a {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, or {{A|Transporter}}, and call them out. Doing this has the added advantage that exposing a member of the {{A|Mafia}} will increase your chances of winning as {{A|Town}}; however, make sure the {{A|Town}} can still win before joining them. *When you've been exposed as an {{A|Amnesiac}} to the {{A|Town}}, your options are more limited; remembering that you were like an evil role in this situation is likely to get you Hanged. Remembering that you were like a role capable of protecting itself (especially {{A|Transporter}}, which can protect itself indefinitely) is still a good idea. *Remembering that you were a role like an {{A|Executioner}} is effective when you're certain the {{A|Town}} no longer has a majority; you can simply reveal and try to get the evils to Hang your new target with you. However, there are some warnings. If the game has devolved into two competing evil [[Factions (ToS)|factions]], they may not be eager to Hang a {{A|Townie}} (since they need to defeat each other.) Additionally, if the {{A|Town}} has been ''entirely'' eliminated (by {{A|Vampires}}, for instance), you might become a {{A|Jester}} instead. *Remembering that you were like a {{A|Witch}} is also a good choice if you think the {{A|Town}} no longer has a majority; simply remember that you were like a {{A|Witch}} and announce your choice. *Similarly, remembering that you were like a {{A|Survivor}} (often announcing you will do so the {{A|day}} before you do, so there's no risk of confusion) will usually guarantee a victory. Some {{A|Townies}} might choose to Hang you out of fear that you'll side against them, and there is a slim risk of being bitten by a {{A|Vampire}}, but for the most part, nobody will have a reason to bother you and you'll coast to victory. Remembering that you were like a {{A|Survivor}} may also be your only hope of winning when (as is often the case) the rest of the graveyard is entirely filled with the losing side. *Remembering that you were like a {{A|Jester}} is very risky (since the {{A|Town}} will be alerted to the existence of a {{A|Jester}}), but it may be a good idea if, for whatever reason, it seems like you're about to get Hanged. Additionally, while it's a risky choice, it's sometimes your only option for victory when facing a victorious majority who has no non-[[Unique Role|unique roles]] in the graveyard. If facing a {{A|Mafia}} team who hasn't lost anyone, for instance, you could remember that you were like a {{A|Jester}} and try to appear to be a {{A|Veteran}} so they Hang you rather than killing you at {{A|night}}. One advantage to this is that anyone else on the losing side who catches on is likely to help you get voted up, since they'll want the {{A|Mafia}} to Hang you as well; for instance, if you start acting like a {{A|Veteran}}, a real {{A|Veteran}} will likely realize you're the {{A|Jester}} and could start acting like a {{A|Jester}} to support you. **However, if you let the {{A|Mafia}} know about your plan, you can tell them that you'll haunt a {{A|Town}} member. This has a high chance of working. **If you have a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, you’re even more at risk due to the fact that they are working against your goal - remember, they win when you survive, not when you win. Not only are they likely to work to defend you, they can also block you from being hung with their protections. Only remember {{A|Jester}} when you have a {{A|Guardian Angel}} if you’re sure you can get hung the day you remember {{A|Jester}}. *You could try and be a confirmed {{A|Townie}}; demand that you get protection and will remember that you were like a {{A|Town}} role, remember that you were like that role, then direct everyone. Unlike a {{A|Mayor}}, you can get healed by a {{A|Doctor}} and can get whispered to. However, the {{A|Town}} might be reluctant to listen to you. *If it is nearing the end of the game with you not remembering that you were like a role yet and it looks like one [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] might get a perfect {{V|Victory}} (meaning their [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] gets no deaths at the end of the game), you could reveal yourself as an {{A|Amnesiac}} and ask that to Hang one of their own [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] members so you could join in on their victory. However, don't rely on this strategy as the team might want to keep their perfect victory. If there is a {{A|Neutral}} role that can win the game with the [[Factions (ToS)|faction]], remember that you were like that role instead of asking that someone of the winning [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] to be Hanged (For example, {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Witch}} if {{A|Mafia}} is going to have a perfect victory). *In some custom cases, remembering to be a {{A|vampire}} after all {{A|vampires}} are dead can advance you gain two advantages; The fact that the maximum {{A|Vampire}} cap has been increased, or that every {{A|Vampire Hunter}} has been converted to a {{A|Vigilante}} and is uncertain of who to shoot. Especially good in role lists with no {{A|Town}}. |} ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{AmnesiacAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{AmnesiacMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.1.0}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} were able to win without remembering a role if they survived to the end. **{{A|Amnesiacs}} had their own {{V|Victory}} screen before this update. [[File:AmnesiacWins.png|thumb|right|200px|{{A|Amnesiac's}} old {{V|Victory}} screen]] *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.10}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} could remember {{A|cleaned}} roles as long as they weren't [[Unique Role|unique]]. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} were not able to remember any [[Unique roles]], such as a {{A|Werewolf}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.4}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} were not able to remember any [[Unique]] {{A|Town}} roles, such as {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}. This was because previous to this, the {{A|Retributionist}} was able to permanently revive these roles; resulting in the two unique roles existing in the same game. *You can surpass the limit of 4 members of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, and {{A|Vampires}} if multiple {{A|Amnesiacs}} remember as them. *There was a bug where you were unable to remember a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} due to the game registering them as a [[Unique Role|unique role]]. *The {{A|Amnesiac}} is the one of two roles whose ability won't take effect the {{A|night}} they are killed the other being the {{A|Plaguebearer}} on the same {{A|night}} they {{A|infect}} everyone. *The {{A|Amnesiac}} suffers from retrograde amnesia, based on their lore. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} can now remember [[Unique]] {{A|Town}} roles. *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} remembering dead {{A|Coven}} can now receive the {{A|Necronomicon}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} can now remember [[Unique]] non-{{A|Town}} roles. *{{VH|1.5.10.4747}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} can no longer remember {{A|Cleaned}} players. *{{VH|1.1.0}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} now needs to remember a role to qualify for winning. Before that, if an {{A|Amnesiac}} was the last player alive, the victory screen would be [[File:AmnesiacWins.png|100x100px]]. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Amnésique]] [[it:Amnesiac]] [[uk:Amnesiac]] [[es:Amnésico]] [[de:Amnesiac]] [[pl:Amnezję]] [[ru:Потерявший память]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Benign roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''

They must be a {{A|Forger}}.. |summary = You are a crooked lawyer that replaces documents. |abilities = Choose a person and rewrite their last will at Night. |attributestext = If your target dies their last will is replaced with your forgery and their role will be shown as the role you select to forge.
You may only perform 2 forgeries. |goal = Kill anyone that will not submit to the {{A|Mafia}}. |winwith = '''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}'''
'''{{A|Witch}}''' |mustkill = '''{{A|Town}}'''

'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''
