'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== [[File:LastWillForge.jpg.jpg|thumb|253x253px|{{A|Forger's}} {{A|Last Will}} GUI when forging a player.]]You may choose a non-{{A|Mafia}} target to forge each {{A|Night}}, replacing their {{A|Last Will}} and [[role]] shown in the [[graveyard]] with your selection. *You have two {{A|Forgeries}}. **If you visit a {{A|Jailed}} player, you will ''not'' lose a {{A|Forgery}}. **If your target does not die the same {{A|Night}} you target them, you will lose a {{A|Forgery}}. *Your target has to die in any way the same {{A|Night}} you {{A|Forge}} them in order for your {{A|Forge}} to take effect. **You are supposed to be able to visit and successfully {{A|Forge}} players who disconnected (left the game). But note that {{A|Forging}} leavers is currently bugged as of a recent small update in August 2026. *Your {{A|Forge}} and your own {{A|Last Will}} are two '''separate''' notes. *If you successfully {{A|Forge}} someone, but did not type any character (excluding spaces) in their {{A|Last Will}}, their {{A|Last Will}} is removed. *If you and a {{A|Janitor}} visit the same target that successfully died, your forgery will not appear, since they will appear as {{A|Cleaned}}. **If you and a {{A|Janitor}} visit the same target that successfully died, the {{A|Janitor}} will still know the true [[role]] of their target and their true {{A|Last Will}}. *If the {{A|Medusa}} visits your target or your target visits the Stone Gazing {{A|Medusa}} and dies, your forgery will not appear, since they will appear as {{A|Stoned}}. *If you and at least one other {{A|Forger}} visit the same target that successfully died, then the {{A|Forger}} who selected first will have their forged {{A|Last Will}} and [[role]] shown. *An {{A|Amnesiac}} will remember the true [[role]] of their target. *The {{A|Retributionist}} or {{A|Necromancer}} will use the true [[role]] of their target. **The {{A|Retributionist}} will be unable to use the corpse of a forged non-visiting or non-{{A|Town}} [[role]], even if their true [[role]] is a visiting {{A|Town}} [[role]]. **The {{A|Necromancer}} will be unable to use the corpse of a forged non-visiting [[role]], even if their true [[role]] is a visiting [[role]]. **A {{A|Trapper}} who witnesses a forged corpse visiting will see the true [[role]] of the corpse. This can result in a {{A|Trapper}} witnessing a {{A|Mayor}} visiting, despite not having any visiting mechanics. *If your target is a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Jailor}}, or {{A|Pirate}} that dies from visiting a non-Cautious {{A|Serial Killer}}, their {{A|Last Will}} will still be shown as bloody, however you will change their [[role]]. *If the {{A|Night}} ends without you saving your forgery, their [[role]] will default to {{A|Forger}}. **If you save your forgery and do not select a [[role]], their [[role]] will default to {{A|Ambusher}}. This is because {{A|Ambusher}} is the first role in alphabetical order. *If your target is the [[Game Modes (ToS)#Town%20Traitor|Town Traitor]] who successfully dies, their forged [[role]] will always show as red in the [[graveyard]]. *A {{A|Spy}}, {{A|Lookout}}, or {{A|Tracker}} can witness your visits. A {{A|Spy}} can only determine who you visited, not your identity. **A {{A|Disguiser}} can hide your identity/visit from both a {{A|Lookout}} and a {{A|Spy}} simply by {{A|disguising}} you. ==Strategy== *After running out of forgeries, you are still useful to the {{A|Mafia}}, either as a vote or becoming a {{A|Mafioso}} later. **You may allow the {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}} to out you as {{A|Mafia}} and "confirm" themselves as {{A|Town}}, as you are not able to do anything else. *Considering the investigative results of {{A|Forger}}, another viable strategy would be to claim {{A|Lookout}} and out a member of {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} to "confirm" yourself as {{A|Town}}, this is easier to pull off with a {{A|Consigliere}} on {{A|Mafia}}, as you will be able to find {{A|Neutral Killings}} easier. *If someone that the {{A|Mafia}} will kill but have produced their {{A|Last Will}} and accused a {{A|Mafia}} member, forge their {{A|Last Will}} to look exactly how they wrote it. Change the result so it gets the {{A|Mafia}} member off scot-free. Be wary that a {{A|Spy}} can bust your efforts without a {{A|Disguise}}. *Forging someone as a [[Unique Role]] (besides {{A|Mayor}}) such as a {{A|Veteran}}, can get the real {{A|Veteran}} hanged. *If someone hasn't talked after {{A|Day}} 2, and there is no {{A|Blackmailer}}, or the {{A|Blackmailer}} hasn't been revealed, you can forge them as a {{A|Sheriff}}. In their {{A|Last Will}} you can put someone as suspicious, and that they were blackmailed. This can cause {{A|Town}} to mishang, but it may also confirm the existence of a {{A|Forger}} in the process. *A similar strategy is to claim {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. On {{A|Day}} 2, you can forge someone as {{A|Vampire}}, and modify their {{A|Last Will}} to a {{A|Sheriff's}}. Forge their {{A|Last Will}} and put someone as suspicious, and make it appear as if they raged and quit when they got bitten (if they left the game). This helps confirm yourself as {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, and may cause a mishang. ===Who to Forge=== *Anyone who may have important information against the {{A|Mafia}} in their {{A|Last Will}} is a good target: Similar to the {{A|Janitor}}, this information will never reach the public, unless there is a {{A|Medium}}. Even then, some {{A|Mediums}} won't realize or recognize this information. **However, unlike a {{A|Janitor}}, if you forge someone's {{A|Last Will}} and role, you do not get their real {{A|Last Will}} and role, and the {{A|Mafia}} also loses that information, which might have been useful to find a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role. Remember this if you have both a {{A|Janitor}} and a {{A|Forger}} and have a target with dangerous info. *If someone called out one of your {{A|Mafia}} companions, you can forge their {{A|Last Will}} and their [[role]] to something like a {{A|Jester}} to make the {{A|Town}} believe it was a bluff. *If there are any known {{A|Amnesiacs}}, forge someone as a {{A|Townie}}. If the {{A|Amnesiac}} reveals themselves, stating that they will remember your forged role, but becomes an evil role instead, they are very likely to get hanged. **If a {{A|Transporter}} was involved and got a {{A|Mafia}} member killed (since both the kill and forge are transported), this can result in a new {{A|Mafia}} member getting hanged. *If you don't know any priority targets, consider how many forgeries you have left and how many more you might need: **Early in the game, few people will have acquired dangerous information, so your forgery may be pointless unless you want to deny claim space for the {{A|Town}}. **Keep at least 1 forgery in case someone appears to have dangerous information, how little it may be. **Don't hoard your forgeries for too long; if you die or get promoted, your remaining forgeries are wasted. ===What to Write=== *Try to prepare your forgery at least a {{A|Night}} in advance. It may be helpful to copy and paste a generic {{A|Last Will}} that you wrote ahead of time on your {{A|Notes}}, then add some key details. You can only edit your forged {{A|Last Will}} during the {{A|Night}}, which gives you little time to make it as believable as possible. *Customize your forgery's visit list according to the [[role]] you change them to (e.g. an {{A|Investigator's}} {{A|Last Will}} should contain hints at other people's roles.) *If an important {{A|Townie}} reveals their {{A|Last Will}} to the {{A|Town}} in an effort to get one of your own {{A|Mafia}} members hanged, but the {{A|Town}} focuses on hanging someone else, write down exactly the correct order their {{A|Last Will}} follows if the {{A|Mafia}} can easily kill and forge them. If you need time, write the fake {{A|Last Will}} in your own {{A|Last Will}} to prepare. If there is incriminating evidence against a {{A|Mafia}} member, such as an {{A|Investigator}} finding a different result than one claimed, change that result to match the role that the {{A|Mafia}} member claimed. It can also work with a {{A|Sheriff}}. This works especially well if the target who is forged has been confirmed, as one look at the "unchanged" {{A|Last Will}} shows that the claimed role fits in the investigative results. Often, such a minor change can have a large effect, since anyone viewing the {{A|Last Will}} can't know if they were forged, and it allows your {{A|Mafia}} member to escape some heat. Unless there is a {{A|Spy}} who noticed a double visit or a {{A|Medium}} who revealed the forgery, you pretty much get off scot-free. Some good examples would follow like this: **''{{A|Investigator}}'' **''N1: John Hathorne: {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Forger}}, or {{A|Witch}} (or'' {{A|Juggernaut}} and{{A|Coven Leader}} in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}) **''N2: Giles Corey: {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}} (and'' {{A|Crusader}} in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}) ***''Giles Corey is the {{A|Mafia}} member who claimed {{A|Sheriff}}, so you would modify the {{A|Last Will}} to appear as shown, but change the result to {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Executioner}}, or {{A|Werewolf}} (and'' {{A|Poisoner}} ''in the'' {{A|Coven Expansion}}''.)'' **''{{A|Sheriff}}'' **''N1: John Hathorne: Seems innocent'' **''N2: Ann Sears: Seems innocent'' **''N3: Giles Corey: Suspicious'' ***You change the "Suspicious" part to "Seems innocent" to follow the order written to look less suspicious. *You can prepare your forgeries at any time during of the {{A|Day}} or {{A|Night}}, '''BUT '''beware of a {{A|Town Investigative}} role or a confirmed {{A|Vigilante}}. They may suspect you for being too quiet for too long. *If there is a {{A|Retributionist}} in the game, you can forge a {{A|Vigilante}} as a {{A|Town Protective}} role to trick the {{A|Retributionist}} into accidentally killing a key role like a {{A|Mayor}}, {{A|Jailor}}, or a confirmed {{A|Townie}}. This strategy also works with {{A|Necromancers}}. *Don't copy and paste your fake {{A|Last Will}} after you have finished your forgery. This is a common mistake as {{A|Forger}}, and it will make the {{A|Mafia}} member you tried to make look innocent instead look suspicious. However, you can use this to frame another player. *If you don't know your target's role, and don't know what to forge them as, you can try one of the following: **Write fake Nightly visits. The majority of roles have a {{A|Night}} ability, so the false information can confuse the {{A|Town}}. **Explicitly frame someone as being evil (any role that the {{A|Town}} must kill). Even without evidence, you may get this person hanged or shot. **If your target [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispered]] with someone, fake the contents of those [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] in your forgery. You can manipulate suspicion on their [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] companion this way. If you have a {{A|Blackmailer}}, it's even better as you may get someone's role from the whisper and make your forgery more convincing. **If you aren't sure you can make the forgery believable or don't have enough time, leave the forgery blank or almost blank. Many players don't keep a proper {{A|Last Will}}, the {{A|Town}} will believe that was the case. **Blanking out their {{A|Last Will}} can be a good idea if they have not revealed their {{A|Last Will}} in the chat, as you will erase all information in said {{A|Last Will}}. This is extremely useful if the {{A|Last Will}} belongs to the {{A|Sheriff}} or the {{A|Investigator}}, and if they have a lot of dangerous info, the {{A|Town}} will lose a lot of information. However, it usually becomes obvious that a {{A|Forger}} was involved, and the {{A|Town}} may suspect any {{A|Lookout}} claims. **You can make a fake {{A|Last Will}} for any player who the {{A|Mafia}} hasn't killed to make it look like they are the {{A|Forger}} who accidentally put their real {{A|Last Will}} this will usually frame them as the {{A|Forger}} and can usually get them hanged. **If you have a {{A|Consigliere}} that tells you the role of the soon-to-be deceased, the forgery becomes much more convincing, but usually will only work with non-{{A|Town Investigative}} roles, people will wonder why a {{A|Spy}}, {{A|Lookout}}, or {{A|Investigator}} has no information several {{A|Nights}} in the game, so this works better with a {{A|Blackmailer}}, as they can tell you the contents of someone's {{A|Last Will}} in whispers if they reveal it and allow you to forge as needed. **If the role list of your game has an {{A|Any}} slot, then you can forge someone as a {{A|Vampire}} or {{A|Vampire Hunter}} to throw suspicion on confirmed {{A|Townies}} even if {{A|Vampires}} aren't in the game. **If you're playing in a game where {{A|Coven}} roles are possible, you can forge someone on {{A|Night 2}} as a {{A|Coven Leader}}/{{A|Potion Master}} who found an evil role to frame another player. The main downside is that this will confirm your existence to the {{A|Coven}} (if they exist). **You can forge them as a {{A|Mafioso}}. In [[Game Modes (ToS)|Game Modes]] such as {{A|Ranked}} or {{A|Ranked Practice}} where there is a guaranteed {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combo, provided the real {{A|Mafioso}} doesn't die before the {{A|Godfather}}, you can trick any {{A|Tavern Keepers}} in the game into randomly [[roleblocked|roleblocking]] since the "{{A|Mafioso}}" is dead. If played correctly, this can disrupt the {{A|Town}} by a large margin and may even cause the {{A|Tavern Keepers}} to get hanged under suspicion of being {{A|Bootleggers}}. **You can try forging them as a {{A|Jester}}. This works well in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Game Modes]] such as {{A|Ranked}} or {{A|Ranked Practice}}, because there can only be one {{A|Neutral Evil}}. It can help the {{A|Mafia}} in the long run when the actual {{A|Jester}} gets hanged, because important roles such as {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Mayor}} might vote guilty, thinking that the {{A|Jester}} is already dead. This works well even if there is ''no'' {{A|Jester}}, because that means that {{A|Executioners}} will most likely side with you for helping them. This also works if you forge them as a {{A|Witch}}. **You can also forge them as an {{A|Executioner}} (Although this will confirm the existence of a {{A|Forger}}. if it's a {{A|Mafia}} kill). You can forge someone as an {{A|Executioner}} and write that their target was a certain {{A|Townie}} in order to frame them as {{A|Mafioso}}. Even better if the {{A|Townie}} you framed happens to be the real {{A|Executioner's}} target. **If a player has just left the game, then you can reliably forge them as a role with defense without the {{A|Town}} questioning it (Unless there's a {{A|Spy}}). **You have an easier time claiming {{A|Transporter}}, since you can forge players as members of the {{A|Mafia}}. However, some smart {{A|Townies}} may notice they weren't transported and call you out, so this works better with a {{A|Hypnotist}} working alongside you. ===Forging Specific Roles=== *'''{{A|Sheriff}}''': Forging a {{A|Sheriff}} is always a good idea since you can confirm your own members of the {{A|Mafia}} or frame someone as being seen as suspicious. *'''{{A|Investigator}}''': If a member of the {{A|Mafia}} is claiming outside of their own Investigative results, forge the {{A|Last Will}} of an {{A|Investigator}} to make them look like the role they are claiming or that someone else is claiming outside of their own Investigative results. *'''{{A|Lookout}}''': You can forge a {{A|Lookout}} {{A|Last Will}} to cover up {{A|Mafia}} visits, claim that a member of the {{A|Mafia}} visited someone they are claiming they did, or to claim an innocent townie visited a player the {{A|Night}} they died or someone who they didn't visit to cause a mishang on them. *'''{{A|Tracker}}''': Same idea as {{A|Lookout}}. *'''{{A|Spy}}''': You can forge to cover up {{A|Mafia}} visits, you should also claim that members of the {{A|Mafia}} were visited by the {{A|Mafia}} and put a caption saying "Not {{A|Mafia}}, Visited by Maf:" so people think that the {{A|Mafia}} members are innocent, since {{A|Mafia}} are likely not able to visit another member of {{A|Mafia}}, this is a very effective way to make them look confirmed if you can pull it off. *'''{{A|Jailor}}''': If there is a role that can't be claimed anymore, say someone claimed this role, even if they claim another role they will be seen as even more suspicious. You can also claim that someone who said they were jailed wasn't, or if a member of the {{A|Mafia}} needs to claim a different role than the one they said to the {{A|Jailor}}. *'''{{A|Psychic}}''': You should replace the mention of any members of the {{A|Mafia}} in an evil vision with any other player. {{A|Psychic}} {{A|Last Wills}} are very long and most {{A|Townies}} won't realize any changes in one. *'''{{A|Vigilante}}''': You can claim that they shot a target with defense. Since no {{A|Town}} roles generally have defense this can get a mishang on the target, this is especially great if the {{A|Vigilante}} dies from guilt upon shooting a {{A|Townie}} since people won't think the {{A|Last Will}} is forged since it wasn't a {{A|Mafia}} kill. *'''{{A|Tavern Keeper}}''': If you have a solo {{A|Mafia Killing}}, you can forge a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} {{A|Last Will}} to make it look like they [[roleblocked]] them. Add a notice saying "anyone I have [[roleblocked]] is likely not a {{A|Mafia Killing}} role" so people are more likely to notice this, and also for extra confirmability. *'''{{A|Mayor}}''': Usually, {{A|Mayor}} {{A|Last Wills}} include claims. Thus you should say that an innocent {{A|townie}} claimed a role that isn't possible anymore, people are obviously trusting of a {{A|Mayor}} and you can get a mis-hang on that player relatively effectively. **Be sure you don't change the role if the {{A|Mayor}} has revealed, set it to {{A|Mayor}} to avoid confirming your existence. *'''{{A|Medium}}''': Since it is the only role that gains information ''before ''the end of the {{A|Night}}, forging their {{A|Last Will}} and saying fake information like a dead {{A|Sheriff}} found an innocent {{A|Townie}} as suspicious, a {{A|Cleaned}} target having a different role than what their real role is or just that the dead players think that someone is evil can be very effective. **While forging someone as {{A|Medium}} you can also add some fake [[Chat (ToS)|dead chat]] messages that make it look like you are a {{A|Medium}} as well, if that's what you wish to claim. Make sure you also have those fake [[Chat (ToS)|dead chat]] messages in your own {{A|Last Will}}. *'''{{A|Retributionist}}''': Forging the {{A|Last Will}} of a {{A|Retributionist}} and using almost any strategy mentioned before can work and people will be less suspicious of a {{A|Forger}}. You can have a {{A|Blackmailer}} [[Blackmailer|blackmail]] the {{A|Retributionist}} or say that they were [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]] since a good {{A|Retributionist}} would share this info with other players. *'''{{A|Executioner}}''': If they have left the game, an effective strategy is to forge their and claim that their target is a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, since an {{A|Executioners}} target is always a {{A|Townie}}, you can confirm that they are innocent when they really aren't, this also means that the {{A|Executioner}} can't attest to whether or not this is true even if there is a {{A|Medium}}. **You can forge '''anyone''' who left the game to appear as an {{A|Executioner}} who's "target" is a {{A|Mafia}} member. ***Your existence however, may be confirmed if they left {{A|Day}} 1 almost immediately, since they could not possibly have time to write a {{A|Last Will}}. **'''DO NOT''' forge someone who the {{A|Mafia}} killed as an {{A|Executioner}} and make their {{A|Last Will}} say that their target was a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. The {{A|Executioner}} has {{A|Basic Defense}}, making them immune to the {{A|Mafia's}} attack, so most {{A|Townies}} will be able to put together that they were forged, exposing the member of the {{A|Mafia}} that you put in their {{A|Last Will}}. ***You can alternatively do this to cause a mishang by forging the person the {{A|Mafia}} kills {{A|Night}} 1 as an {{A|Executioner}} and claiming that a random person who isn't a {{A|Mafia}} member is their target, although remember that this uses one of your forgeries, and also exposes the fact that you exist. *'''{{A|Witch}}''': If they are going to be killed at {{A|Night}} and you fear they might have the names of the {{A|Mafia}} in their {{A|Last Will}}, forge their {{A|Last Will}} so that the {{A|Mafia}} aren't completely outed, alternatively, list {{A|Townies}} as members of the {{A|Mafia}} or the {{A|Neutral Killing}} to try to get them hanged. **In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, this can also work for a {{A|Coven Leader}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, and, to a certain extent, {{A|Necromancer}}. This is because the {{A|Witch}} cannot exist in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, and all of these roles oppose the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}}, hence why it would make sense for them to expose them in their {{A|Last Will}}. *'''{{A|Vampire}}''': A risky but very effective strategy is to forge a {{A|Vampires}} {{A|Last Will}} to make it look like they have a record of who they have bitten. This is a strangely common mistake by many beginner players and can get anyone mentioned in that {{A|Last Will}} hanged or shot. ===What to Claim=== If you are ever accused of being a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, it will most likely come from one of these roles. While you don't have much to defend yourself, there are a few options you have to deflect suspicion off of yourself. *'''Claim a role that fits with your investigation results: '''You can claim to be a {{A|Lookout}} and provide a fake {{A|Last Will}} to prove your innocence. If it fits in the role list, your chances of surviving on trial will be higher. If you have a member of the {{A|Mafia}} claiming to be a visiting role, you can use them to try to confirm them and yourself. If there is a confirmed {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}, or even better, a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Consigliere}} claiming {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Investigator}} you can use their visits for your fake {{A|Last Will}} so its not just filled with "No Visits". *'''Claim you were {{A|Transported}}. '''This is another obvious way out, but it can work if there aren't a lot of dead roles. If there's a confirmed {{A|Transporter}} and you get called out for it, you will have no chance of surviving past that point, unless you somehow manage to convince the there is another {{A|Transporter}} or that they're lying. However, you have some wiggle room if you had forged a {{A|Mafia}} kill as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} the previous {{A|Night}} or two. *'''Claim your accuser is lying. '''This will only work early in the game, and if you only have one accuser. Claiming your accuser is an Evil role, or better yet, a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, and delaying as to not be hanged can work massively in your favor. If you are investigated or interrogated, you can even claim to be framed or one of the roles in your investigation result so the suspicion on you fades. '''Dealing with a Role Call: '''These are often just before you reach a majority of the roles, so the longevity of your claim isn't as much of a concern. These can also happen early on. *'''Claim outside your investigative results. '''If it's near the end and your team has killed the enemies, feel free to claim anything. Claiming something with a non-suspicious investigative results is one of your best shots. *'''Claim inside your results. '''If you want to play it safe, you can claim to be a {{A|Lookout}} using the strategies above. ===Roles Not To Forge=== While funny to see pop up, all you really do by forging a target as one of these roles is confirm with certainty the existence of a {{A|Forger}} in the game. Only do this if you know that your team will win the following {{A|Day}}. *'''{{A|Pestilence}}:''' If a {{A|Plaguebearer}} has not yet transformed into {{A|Pestilence}}, this will confirm your existence. Even if {{A|Pestilence}} exists, {{A|Pestilence}} cannot die during the {{A|Night}}, unless they leave the game. **However, forging someone who left the game as {{A|Pestilence}} may be a good strategy to trick the {{A|Town}} into thinking that the {{A|Pestilence}} is dead, which could be devastating should they visit {{A|Pestilence}} or their target. ***Just be aware that someone dying to {{A|Pestilence}} the same Night will end up revealing that the person you forged wasn't actually {{A|Pestilence}}. *'''Impossible roles:''' For example, forging someone as a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} in {{A|Town Traitor}}. {{A|Vampire Hunters}} cannot exist in this game mode, and therefore confirms the existence of a {{A|Forger}}. *'''Roles with {{A|Basic Defense}}:''' The only {{A|Mafia}} role that could possibly "kill" a player with {{A|Basic Defense}} is the {{A|Forger}}. However, this downside is negated if that player leaves the game, dies from higher value attacks (such as an {{A|Arsonist's}} ignition), or dies from a {{A|Veteran}} (if said role can visit). *'''{{A|Witch}} (in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}):''' While you can forge someone as a {{A|Witch}} in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, this will confirm the existence of a {{A|Forger}}. since {{A|Witch}} is impossible in all [[Game Modes - Coven|Coven Game Modes]]. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{ForgerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{ForgerMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, {{A|Forgers}} could only modify the {{A|Last Wills}} of others players upon their deaths. They also had 3 forgeries. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.1}}, {{A|Forgers}} could forge someone as invalid "roles". This included: {{V|Alignments}} (such as {{A|Random Mafia}} or {{A|Any}}), as well as {{A|Stoned}}.[[File:Forger achievement.png|thumb|right|75px|{{A|Forger's}} achievement and statistic icon]] *When looking at in-game [[statistics]] or {{V|achievements}}, the {{A|Forger}} is one of two roles (the other being the {{A|Tavern Keeper}}) that has their icon different from the actual role icon found during gameplay. It appears to be facing the other way. *Paradoxically, it is often good for a {{A|Mafia}} who lacks a {{A|Forger}} for the {{A|Town}} to suspect a {{A|Forger}} Simply visiting the {{A|Mafia's}} kill target as a non-{{A|Janitor}} {{A|Random Mafia}} is a good way to get {{A|Spies}} to discredit someone's {{A|Last Will}}. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.2}} **Fixed issue when {{A|Forger}} was promoted to {{A|Mafioso}} that could result in a disconnection. *{{VH|3.3.1}} **Copying and pasting should now work in forged {{A|Last Wills}} on the web version. **Fixed issue where roles that were forged as and died as {{A|Medium}} saw "Seance" buttons during the {{A|Day}}. **Fixed issue where you could forge players as invalid roles. These included {{V|alignments}} such as {{A|Any}}, {{A|Random Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Benign}}, as well as {{A|Stoned}} and en-US:GUI_ROLE_201 (which would show up as {{A|Stoned}}). *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Forger}} can now select a role to forge as. **{{A|Forger}} now only has 2 uses instead of 3. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Forger's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Forger.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Forger's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Forger Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.2.0}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Фальсификатор]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Mafia Deception roles]] [[Category:Last Will modifiers]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Hex Master}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{CovenInfobox ||nameandicon = Hex Master[[File:RoleIcon HexMaster.png|thumb|left|100px]]
(HM) |alignment = {{A|Coven Evil}} |avatar = [[File:Hex Master Avatar.png|150px]] |attributes = [[Detection Immunity]] (with the {{A|Necronomicon}})
Attack: Unstoppable (Final Hex) or Basic ({{A|Necronomicon}})

[[Unique Role]]
Can inherit the {{A|Necronomicon}} on {{A|Night 3}} |type = Manipulation
Killing
Unique |priority = 3 (Hexing target)
6 (final attack) |uses = |investigator = '''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Jester}}, or {{A|Hex Master}}. |consigliere = Your target is versed in the ways of Hexes. They must be the {{A|Hex Master}}. |summary = You are a spell slinger with a proficiency for Hexes and curses. |abilities = You may choose to Hex a player each night. |attributestext = With the {{A|Necronomicon}} you gain Astral and Basic attacks.
Players are still Hexed when you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}. |goal = Kill all who would oppose the {{A|Coven}}. }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== [[File:SpecialLabel_Hexed.png|alt=|thumb|The icon that appears next to {{A|Hexed}} players in the player list]]The {{A|Hex Master}} is a role with the ability to {{A|Hex}} one player each night. When all the non-{{A|Coven}} players left alive have been {{A|Hexed}}, all {{A|Hexed}} players will die in an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}. *If you die the same night you use your {{A|Final Hex}}, the wipeout will still occur. *You will still use your {{A|Final Hex}} even if you are {{A|Roleblocked}}. *A {{A|Necromancer}} can trigger a {{A|Final Hex}} if they reanimate your body to {{A|Hex}} the final non-{{A|Coven}} member. *It is not required to {{A|Hex}} the {{A|Town Traitor}} for your final {{A|Hex}} to go off. *{{A|Hexing}} a player ''cannot ''be intercepted by a {{A|Bodyguard}}. If you visit a {{A|Trapped}} target, you will trigger a {{A|Trap}} but not die from it. *The {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} will not trigger {{A|Veteran}} alerts. *If a {{A|Coven}} member ends up {{A|Hexed}} due to a {{A|Transporter}} or formerly being an {{A|Amnesiac}}, they will die to your large attack. *Players are not told that they are {{A|Hexed}} until it kills them. *{{A|Hexed}} players will appear as suspicious to the {{A|Sheriff}}. They will also show up under the {{A|Hex Master's}} results to an {{A|Investigator}} and {{A|Consigliere}}. *With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, your targets will not only be {{A|Hexed}} but will also be dealt a {{A|Basic Attack}}. In addition to this, your ability becomes {{A|Astral}}, meaning your ability will no longer be considered a visit. **For example, you will not die to a {{A|Werewolf}} that attacks your target; your attack will ignore a {{A|Bodyguard's}} guarding, nor will a {{A|Lookout}} detect your visit. **Even with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, your attacks still {{A|Hex}} people; you can use this to kill people who have a form of defense (whether temporary or permanent), provided you {{A|Hex}} everyone else. **You will always be the first {{A|Coven}} member to inherit the {{A|Necronomicon}} once the {{A|Coven Leader}} dies/if there is no {{A|Coven Leader}}. This may be a bug. ==Strategy== *Claiming {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Sheriff}} is a good idea because {{A|Hexed}} targets have their investigation results changed to yours. Listing your {{A|Hexed}} targets and then claiming that they were/are {{A|Hexed}} can be a good idea. Be wary of experienced players as they may notice that all your results are of {{A|Hexed}} people and call you out for it. You may wish to mix in a few other results as well, and only use {{A|Hexed}} results when you cannot fill up your {{A|Last Will}}. **You can also claim anything you want because your {{A|Hexed}} targets have the same investigation results as you, and you will look {{A|Hexed}} to an investigative role. ***But beware, as {{A|Spies}} will notice that the {{A|Coven}} hasn't visited you unless the {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Potion Master}} interferes. Also, if you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, the {{A|Sheriff}} will find you to be not suspicious, which is what shouldn't appear if you are {{A|Hexed}}. ***If there is also a {{A|Potion Master}}, you should communicate with them about the players they've revealed, and add that into your Investigator will. *Claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} is also a good strategy because you can get away with saying that {{A|Bodyguard}} can't intercept the {{A|Hex Master's}} attacks. Since it is the only {{A|Town Protective}} role that will not do anything to you (regardless if you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}), it makes a good fake claim. **Be mindful that a {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Tracker}}, or {{A|Trapper}} can see that you didn't visit as you claim. *Acting like a {{A|Jester}} when you obtain the {{A|Necronomicon}} is not a bad idea. You share the same investigative results as a {{A|Jester}}, appear innocent just like a {{A|Jester}} does, and will not appear to visit anyone. **This can backfire if a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} chooses to kill you, or the {{A|Town}} wants to give you the win. *Don't go up or down the list starting from top or bottom, as these players are often targeted by other killing roles, or worse, protected by a {{A|Crusader}}. Picking random people with a name that doesn't stand out means you'll be able to win much easier. You rely on your targets surviving in order to cast the final spell. *Keep track of the people you have {{A|Hexed}} and share it with the {{A|Coven}} members. Kill the ones who are not {{A|Hexed}} to end the game quickly. *As the rest of the {{A|Coven}} are also capable of killing, ask your {{A|Coven}} to not attack the people you've {{A|Hexed}} in order to not perform any useless work. Conversely, avoid Hexing people that the rest of the {{A|Coven}} is likely to want to kill before the endgame. *When choosing who to {{A|Hex}}, some {{A|Arsonist}} strategies may be relevant since the roles are similar in changing investigative results and being able to deal an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} to all affected targets. **Unlike an {{A|Arsonist}}, you ''must'' Hex all non-{{A|Coven}} for your final {{A|Hex}} to go off. Therefore, it often makes sense to Hex confirmed {{A|Survivors}} and {{A|Jesters}}, at least if the {{A|Town}} seems unlikely to kill them for you. This also includes {{A|Pirates}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}}, {{A|Executioners}}, and {{A|Guardian Angels}}. *Choose people who you think will live the longest. Remember, when every living non-{{A|Coven}} player becomes {{A|Hexed}}, an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} happens, purging the rest of the players in the late game. Even if there are 3 people that oppose you, if you guessed that they were going to live until the end of the game and {{A|Hexed}} them earlier, you could still finish them off, which would ensure your victory. *Bear in mind that your {{A|Hex}} will not kill {{A|Pestilence}}, as it has {{A|Invincible Defense}}. You will die if you target him without the {{A|Necronomicon}} or without a form of protection. **The only situation where it makes sense to deliberately Hex {{A|Pestilence}} is if you have everyone else {{A|Hexed}} and are certain there will be enough {{A|Coven}} left to hang him the next morning since even though it won't kill him, Hexing him is still a requirement to set off your Hexes on everyone else; if you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, you can even Hex him without dying yourself since you will have an {{A|Astral}} attack. *Use {{A|Astral}} to your advantage. Being {{A|Astral}} means you do not have to worry about being killed by the {{A|Town Protectives}}, roles that rampage, the {{A|Ambusher}} or be busted by {{A|Lookouts}} or {{A|Trackers}}. You can even safely attack a {{A|Veteran}}; if they don't {{A|Alert}}, they'll die, and if they do, you'll survive and they will be {{A|Hexed}}. *Just because you ''can'' kill people once you have the {{A|Necronomicon}} doesn't necessarily mean you ''should''; you can still Hex people with protection instead. If the {{A|Town}} seems directionless and passive, it can make more sense to target rival night immune killers instead of people you can kill immediately and either rely on other {{A|Coven}} to kill the rest or hope that the rival killers will take them out for you. *It's best to keep your role under the radar, as once the town knows a {{A|Hex Master}}, finding you will be one of their top priorities. The best way to stay hidden is to keep your fellow {{A|Coven}} alive as well. Bear in mind this strategy is completely useless if the role list completely shows your role. *A {{A|Necromancer}} can help you Hex people if you are an {{A|Amnesiac}} that remembered {{A|Hex Master}}. The previous {{A|Hex Master}}(s) body can be reanimated to Hex someone. *If you are an {{A|Amnesiac}} who remembered {{A|Hex Master}}, it is important to find out who has already been {{A|Hexed}}. Try asking your new {{A|Coven}} teammates. *Your Hexes, along with being gateways for an Unstoppable attack, also function as permanent {{A|Frames}}. Use this to your advantage, as you should try Hexing people who are likely to be checked by a {{A|Sheriff}} or an {{A|Investigator}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{HexMasterAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{HexMasterMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Hex Master}} is the only {{A|Coven}} role that can directly kill a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role other than the {{A|Medusa}}. *According to the game's [[Official Town of Salem Stories|lore], the {{A|Hex Master's}} name is Helena. She is based on Fuji Musume (The Wisteria Maiden). *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.4}}, the {{A|Hex Master}} must have survived the night in order to perform their final Hex on all non-{{A|Coven}} players. *The symbol of the {{A|Hex Master's}} Hexes resemble the “文” (bun) character in Kanji, symbolizing theatre performance arts. ==History== *[[Version History (ToS)|3.2.4]] **{{A|Hex Master}} can now deal their {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} if they {{A|Hex}} their final target the same {{A|night}} the {{A|Hex Master}} dies. **Temporary {{A|defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *[[Version History (ToS)|3.2.3]] **Fixed a very complicated {{A|Trapper}}-{{A|Hex Master}} interaction that could result in a player dying to a {{A|trap}} that should have previously triggered. *[[Version History (ToS)|3.1.14]] **Added {{A|Hex Master}} vs. {{A|Jailor}} (no executions remaining) [[stalemate]] detector. *[[Version History (ToS)|2.5.5.12200]] **Added a label to visually indicate {{A|Hexed}} players for the {{A|Hex Master}} ([[File:SpecialLabel Hexed.png|30x30px]]). **The {{A|Hex Master's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Hex Master.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Hex Master's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Hex Master Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version History (ToS)|2.5.1.10655]] **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *[[Version History - Town of Salem|2.0.0.6582]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Колдун]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Coven roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:Unstoppable+ Attack]] [[Category:Astral]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can choose someone other than yourself to protect each night, granting them a temporary {{A|Powerful Defense}} from all attacks. You will deal a {{A|Basic Attack}} to one random visitor to your target, '''even if your target is not attacked.''' *If your target is attacked, the message "You were attacked but someone protected you!" will appear to them. You will receive the message "Your target was attacked last night!" *Your divine protection extends to all attacks; including a {{A|Bodyguard}} dying to protect their target, or your target being killed by any role that attacks visitors (such as {{A|Veterans}} and {{A|Medusa}}). This is similar in ability to the {{A|Doctor's}} heal. **Your protection does NOT cure {{A|Poison}}. **You will not attack {{A|Vampires}} or any Astral visitors, including attacking ones (most notably the {{A|Hex Master}}). *You will not get a message saying your target was attacked if you save a {{A|Bodyguard}} who successfully protected someone (this is a bug). *Your ability will fail if your target was {{A|Jailed}}, however, due to a bug, you will still get a message about your target having been attacked if someone tried to attack them in {{A|Jail}}. ==Strategy== *You can protect someone who asks for a {{A|Crusader}} on them, but you shouldn't protect someone who asks for a {{A|Town Protective}} on them, unless all other {{A|Town Protective}} roles are dead. You may accidentally kill another {{A|Town Protective}} role. Be cautious, as {{A|Medusas}} often bait {{A|Town Protective}} and {{A|Town Investigative}} roles this way. If someone asks for {{A|Crusader}} on them, if the role list allows for multiple, you may want to claim so that you don't die that night to another {{A|Crusader}}. *Protecting a confirmed {{A|Townie}} with little or no chance of a {{A|Lookout}} is often a good idea as there is little reason for another player besides an evil one to visit the said {{A|Townie}}. However, if another {{A|Town Protective}} visits the confirmed {{A|Townie}}, you will kill them. *Protecting a player that left the same {{A|Day}}/{{A|Night}} can kill any {{A|Ambushers}}, {{A|Forgers}}, and {{A|Janitors}} visiting them. Do note that if the player is targeted by an {{A|Ambusher}}, you will die with them if you are attacked or are the only non-{{A|Mafia}} visitor. *More often than not, you should ''not'' protect early in the game as there is a high chance of killing a fellow {{A|Townie}}. An exception would be if the majority of players are evil, such as in {{A|Coven}} [[Custom Mode|Custom]]. *If you are nearing the end of a game or evils have the majority, protect a player every night. You need evils to be dead at this point and they have a high chance of visiting your target. Make sure you're not out in the open, have another {{A|Town Protective}} on you. *Unlike a {{A|Doctor}}, you are able to provide direct protection to a revealed {{A|Mayor}} independently, assuming you are not roleblocked. In a game with no other {{A|Town Protectives}}, you are free to protect them every night without limitations. **This has many other benefits as well, such as the you being able to kill {{A|Blackmailers}}, {{A|Hex Masters}}, and {{A|Pirates}} attempting to visit the {{A|Mayor}} as well as attackers. **Unlike an {{A|Ambusher}}, you do not attack {{A|Vampires}}, but you do prevent their attacks/conversions. **If you do this strategy, either insure you are the only {{A|Town Protective}} left or openly claim. If you don't get the word out, there is a high chance that you will end up killing a {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, or another {{A|Crusader}} that had the same idea as you. *In a VIP mode game, protect the VIP every night. This way, you can prevent the VIP from dying. Players are often conscious that the VIP will be protected by a {{A|Crusader}} and would rather not visit him. Typically, the {{A|Crusader}} will openly claim on Day 1. **If there are multiple {{A|Crusader}} claims, protect the VIP/each other in the order you claimed to prevent multiple {{A|Crusader}} deaths. First claim goes on the VIP, second claim goes on the first claim, etc. *If there is another confirmed {{A|Crusader}} in the game, make sure never to have both of you protecting a target at the same time. Whisper to each other who you are going to protect. You both have the possibility of killing each other if both of you visit the same target. *Watch out for people that might claim {{A|Crusader}} on Day 1 because they may be a {{A|Medusa}} trying to bait {{A|Town Protective}} roles. *As a last resort, you are able to cancel out with an {{A|Ambusher}} if you both visit the same target. This is usually more than a fair trade, however; as the {{A|Mafia}} losing a killer outweighs losing a {{A|Townie}} in most circumstances (unless evils have majority and you're the only killing {{A|Town}} role overall). *As you are able to attack ''all'' visitors and not just attackers, if someone is being blackmailed, controlled, or roleblocked repeatedly, you might want to consider protecting that target. You have a high chance of killing a {{A|Blackmailer}}, {{A|Consort}}, or {{A|Coven Leader}}. **Keep in mind, however; after the {{A|Coven Leader}} receives the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they will be able to survive your Basic Attacks; but you will still protect your target from being drained. **You will also not be able to kill roles with defense, such as {{A|Arsonists}}. **You may accidentally kill a {{A|Lookout}} seeking to bust said roles or if your target is actually evil, you might be freeing them up to kill someone. *Be extremely cautious about protecting a {{A|Mayor}} early on, since it's very likely other {{A|Town}} will protect him as well. Make sure to communicate to your fellow {{A|Townies}} to decide who to protect. *A {{A|Crusader}} can pair up with a {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}} or another {{A|Crusader}} to make both of you nearly invulnerable, in much the same way that a {{A|Doctor}} can pair up with a {{A|Bodyguard}}. You cannot maintain persistent invulnerability with a {{A|Bodyguard}}, since you can be killed by either Astral Attacks or the {{A|Ambusher}}/{{A|Werewolf}}, but it can still be a useful strategy to ensure that evils lose someone if they attack either of you. The only major threat to these combos are {{A|Arsonists}}, so make sure to rid of them first. *Unlike a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Doctor}}, you do not have a self-heal or bulletproof vest available to protect yourself from harm. Therefore, if you are relatively sure there are no other {{A|Town Protectives}}, you should be wary of revealing yourself too early. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{CrusaderAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{CrusaderMessages}} ==Trivia== *Lots of players have joked that the {{A|Crusader}} is essentially a green {{A|Ambusher|Town}}, with its ability to attack a random visitor to its target being very similar to the latter's. **However, {{A|Ambushers}} cannot attack {{A|Mafia}} members, while you '''can''' attack {{A|Townies}}. *The {{A|Crusader}} is the only {{A|Town Protective}} equipped with a {{A|Basic Attack}}. **It is also the only one with the potential to kill non-attacking roles. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.4}} **Removed {{A|Crusader}}-specific {{A|Hypnotist}} message option from [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic Town of Salem]]. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Crusader's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Crusader.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Crusader's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Crusader Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Крестоносец]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Town Protective roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]] [[Category:Killing roles]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |avatar=|actionother=Attack one visitor and reveal name to all visitors|actionnone=}}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can choose to lie in wait at someone's house each {{A|night}}. You will deal a {{A|Basic Attack}} to ONE random visitor. **Other {{A|Mafia}} roles cannot be attacked. **However, the {{A|Ambusher}} is able to attack the {{A|Town Traitor}}. *All visitors to your target will learn your name (even if {{A|Disguised}}). The message is: '''"You saw [Ambusher] prepare an ambush while visiting your target."''' **Therefore, {{A|Mediums}} can prove to be a major threat. *All visitors who visit your target will learn your name, even if they don't die. If two or more people visit your target, at least one other person will know your name, since the {{A|Ambusher}} can only kill one of them. *When all other {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles die, you will be promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}}. *You cannot select yourself or another {{A|Mafia}} member to lie in wait at their/your house. *Your visit is passive, meaning you will not be attacked by any {{A|Bodyguards}} or {{A|Traps}} protecting the player you attack. ==Strategy== *As an {{A|Ambusher}}, your goal is to kill off {{A|Town Protective}} roles and {{A|Lookouts}} to open them up for the {{A|Mafia}} to kill directly. This means you should focus on people who you know won't be visited twice but at least once. This can open them up for the {{A|Mafia}} to kill later. Two kills per night can be a major help, especially if the {{A|Mafia}} needs the majority as quickly as possible to win. *Target important confirmed {{A|Townies}}. The {{A|Town}} would likely protect them allowing you to be able to kill them. This will always help with big hindrances such as {{A|Lookouts}} and {{A|Town Protective}} roles. **If you know that the {{A|Doctor}} is healing a {{A|Town}} role, visit the person that they are healing. You will kill the {{A|Doctor}} and leave the {{A|Townie}} vulnerable. This is also a recommended strategy with {{A|Bodyguards}}. *You only kill one visitor to your target and you are revealed to all visitors, so be careful who you ambush. Randomly choosing a target early on is not a good idea, as it reveals your name and likely won't have a huge impact on the {{A|Town}}. **It is usually smart to ambush people who are usually quiet as you may hit a {{A|Town Investigative}}. *Targeting an early {{A|Mayor}} reveal may be tempting, remember that they often have multiple visitors, which risks exposing you (also applies to "'''TP/LO'''" callers). *Targeting a player that left the same {{A|Day}}/{{A|Night}} is generally pointless aside from tricking {{A|Spies}}, as you'll generally have a better chance of ambushing someone by targeting another player. The only exception to this is if a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Forger}} decides to visit that player and you want to protect them from a potential {{A|Crusader}}. *You should also try to target the possible targets of {{A|Town Investigatives}}. Waiting around a suspicious {{A|Townie}} or possible {{A|Neutral Killing}} can take them out. Try visiting a person who has been accused of "being suspicious". This will most likely guarantee a hit against a {{A|Town Investigative}} role but still be careful of those being extremely suspicious as they, most likely, will be visited by more than one person, giving away your role. Beware, because {{A|Werewolves}} also use this tactic. *If someone claims to have visited your target, but you didn't attack any visitors, that player could be an {{A|Executioner}}, a {{A|Neutral Benign}}, or a rival evil role. You should reveal this to the {{A|Mafia}} at {{A|Night}} to decide what action to take against them. *If there's a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} roaming around and you lack a {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combo, predicting who they'll role block next and ambushing them can take out a dangerous role that can guarantee a loss if they find your killer. *You are the only {{A|Mafia Killing}} role that can kill a {{A|Transporter}} with little risk. By placing an ambush on the the {{A|Transporter's}} house, you can deny them the ability to protect themselves, and they'll be killed by you if they try to transport themselves. However, the {{A|Transporter}} can be useful for messing up the {{A|Town Investigative}} roles, so try to weigh the benefits and risks before ambushing them. **If a known {{A|Survivor}} claims to have been transported the day after they reveal, consider targeting the {{A|Survivor}}. There's a very high chance that the {{A|Transporter}} will transport them again to act as a "human shield" and you'll be able to kill them without the risk of the {{A|Transporter}} swapping the {{A|Survivor}} with a {{A|Mafia}} member. You may also have an easier time encouraging the {{A|Survivor}} to side with the {{A|Mafia}} later on by doing this, if they are indeed a {{A|Survivor}}. **Make sure to note if the existence of any {{A|Mediums}} are in play, as they will certainly reveal you provided you kill the {{A|Transporter}}. *You are also the only killing role (aside from a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, {{A|Vampire}}, or {{A|Serial Killer}}) that cannot kill or harm your own teammates by any means. A {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, {{A|Transporter}}, and even a {{A|Necromancer}} cannot force you to attack fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}}. **Since you cannot attack your own {{A|Mafia}} teammates (unlike a {{A|Crusader}}), consider targeting the same person as the {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer}}. If they currently have that player pinned down, you may kill a {{A|Spy}} or more importantly, a {{A|Lookout}} that decided to visit the {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Blackmailer's}} target. *You can also try to attack the same target as the {{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Mafioso}} if you suspect that someone might also visit that target. You may kill a {{A|Lookout}} or a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} doing this. Keep in mind however, that the same target may have multiple visitors, exposing you. *If somebody claims poisoned, you should always consider if it's worth it to ambush them. If there is a {{A|Doctor}} in the game, they are more than likely to visit that poisoned target. However, when you or one of your {{A|Mafia}} friends gets poisoned, you might need that {{A|Doctor}}. If the target claims poisoned on the same night the {{A|Poisoner}} died, however, it is usually safe to ambush them, as the {{A|Poisoner}} can no longer cause any harm to your team (unless there is a {{A|Necromancer}}). When the {{A|Poisoner}} obtains the {{A|Necronomicon}}, this all becomes obsolete, as the {{A|Doctor}} can't heal their targets anymore and won't waste their time trying to do so. *If you are dealing with {{A|Vampires}} or {{A|Coven}} members, you can single-handedly take them out yourself if you know who they would go for. {{A|Vampires}} want to go for open targets to convert, and the {{A|Coven}} wants to kill off or investigate roles that may do them harm. Waiting around these targets can take them out with the added bonus of their teammates not knowing who the {{A|Ambusher}} is (unlike the {{A|Medusa}}) provided that there are no other visitors when you kill them. **If you manage to kill a {{A|Vampire}}, have the {{A|Mafia}} attack/{{A|Roleblock|Mafia}} your original target the next night. If they weren't killed, there is a high chance of them being a new {{A|Vampire}} themselves! However, they can also be an immune role, so place their name in your {{A|Last Will}} or {{A|Death Note}} to out them and divert attention in such cases. *If you don't really know who you should ambush, consider visiting the same person over and over again. You are more likely to hit someone if you stick to one player, as at some point, someone will probably decide to visit that player. *If one of your {{A|Neutral}} allies has fallen under suspicion, you can use this to your advantage and target your {{A|Neutral}} ally. You can kill a {{A|Town Investigative}} visiting them, or even a {{A|Vigilante}} who decided to shoot them by doing this. Do note however that you do not grant your target {{A|Powerful Defense}}, meaning you cannot save your {{A|Neutral}} friend if they're attacked. **If you are paired up with a {{A|Witch}}, you can simply choose to lie in wait outside the {{A|Witch's}} house while they control some {{A|Townies}} into visiting them, allowing you to kill reliably, similar to how the {{A|Coven Leader}} controls {{A|Townies}} into visiting the {{A|Medusa}}. If there is a risk of the controlled player being a killing role, you can simply have the {{A|Witch}} control them into someone else while you target the {{A|Witch's}} second target. **You become more of a pseudo-protective role when paired with a {{A|Witch}}, as they can control you into visiting your {{A|Mafia}} teammates. If a member of the {{A|Mafia}} has fallen under minor suspicion, you can ask the {{A|Witch}} to control you into visiting that {{A|Mafia}} member to ambush a suspicious {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}}. It also has the added bonus of potentially clearing your {{A|Mafia}} friend since {{A|Ambushers}} normally cannot visit members of the {{A|Mafia}}. ***This has some extra caveats, if the {{A|Mafia}} has their only kill-capable {{A|Mafia}} role locked down by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, you can ask the {{A|Witch}} to control you into visiting the {{A|Tavern Keeper's}} target to kill the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and free up the {{A|Mafia's}} main killing role. *Although rare, if you're in a case where the {{A|Mafia}} is stuck against a {{A|Bodyguard}}/{{A|Doctor}} combo, you can break it as {{A|Bodyguards}} only protect from direct attacks. Just simply place an ambush on the {{A|Bodyguard}}. You'll kill the {{A|Doctor}} and leave the {{A|Bodyguard}} vulnerable. *Be careful around people who are baiting. It may be tempting to want to go on someone who seems to be acting strange, but even if they aren't a {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Medusa}}, or a baiting {{A|Pestilence}}/{{A|Werewolf}}, they are more likely to be visited by multiple people, and thus your identity may be revealed. *If needed, you can cancel with a {{A|Crusader}} to kill each other, although this is a last resort. It is almost always better to have the {{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Mafioso}} kill them. *Your passive visits allows you to safely trigger {{A|Traps}} to allow the {{A|Mafia}} to kill without risk. In addition, if you visit the {{A|Trapper's}} target on the {{A|Night}} they {{A|Trap}} them, not only will you waste their {{A|Trap}}, but you'll kill the {{A|Trapper}} visiting them as well. *If there is a {{A|Medium}} in the game, tell the {{A|Blackmailer}} to repeatedly {{A|Blackmail}} them if you manage to kill someone. This will prevent your identity from being revealed by the {{A|Medium}}, their {{A|Last Will}} or most importantly, from their séance; rendering them unable to reveal you. You can also take advantage of this and try to ambush anyone visiting the {{A|Medium}} to kill a {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Spy}}, or even a {{A|Transporter}} visiting the {{A|Blackmailed}} {{A|Medium}}. Do note however, that this can backfire if the {{A|Blackmailer}} was role blocked, the {{A|Medium}} was jailed, or another {{A|Medium}} exists. **If you don't have a {{A|Blackmailer}}, a good alternative is a {{A|Janitor}} or a {{A|Forger}}. You can have the {{A|Mafia}} to kill and {{A|clean}}/{{A|forge}} the {{A|Medium}}. Doing so will prevent your identity from being revealed if someone saw you and died. However, they may still séance a player and tell them about the {{A|Ambusher}}, but it will give you an extra day.  **A {{A|Bootlegger}} will not hinder the {{A|Medium}} at all, as their {{A|Night}} ability is passive. **Even if a {{A|Disguiser}} {{A|Disguised}} you as someone else, the visitors will still learn your name. *Be aware that if you end up attacking an immune role, there is a high chance of your identity being revealed in a {{A|Death Note}}. **{{A|Hex Masters}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}} or {{A|Guardian Angels}} will have the {{A|Astral}} property, and you cannot ambush them. *When claiming a role, try to claim a {{A|Town Protective}} role or a non-visiting role as it gives you more credibility than something like a {{A|Town Investigative}} where you cannot do much to prove yourself. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{AmbusherAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{AmbusherMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6501}}, {{A|Ambushers}} would be killed by {{A|Bodyguards}} and {{A|Trappers}} protecting their targets. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, the {{A|Ambusher}} was restricted to the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *In the [[Public Test Realm]] before the {{A|Coven Expansion}} was released, the {{A|Ambusher}} was able to ambush its own {{A|Mafia}} members and only had three uses. *The {{A|Ambusher}} is the only {{A|Mafia Killing}} added since the release of the game. *If a {{A|Necromancer}} uses a dead player (or {{A|Retributionist}}) on the {{A|Ambusher's}} target, the dead player would receive the {{A|Ambusher's}} name despite being dead. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Ambusher}} is now available in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic Town of Salem]]. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". **Reanimated {{A|Ambusher}} will no longer attack roles that attempted to visit but were {{A|Roleblocked}}. **Added message "You ambushed someone who visited your target last night!". *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Ambusher's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Ambusher.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Ambusher's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Ambusher Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Ambusher}} now has passive visits. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Партизан]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Mafia Killing roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}}[[File:Hypnotist Messages.png|thumb|222x222px|alt=|{{A|Hypnotist}} messages in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}]] {{Story}} == Mechanics == *You may hypnotize one player each {{A|night}}, giving them a false message once the {{A|Night}} ends. **If you don't choose a message, you cannot be {{A|controlled}} into visiting anyone. *A {{A|Spy}} who bugs your target will receive the message you planted. {{HypnotistAbilityMessages}} == Strategy == *You are a wildcard to your team, with the ability to manipulate messages people receive. This can help with claiming specific roles, though that isn't to say if you select the wrong message, your presence is revealed. *Claiming to be a {{A|Doctor}} may not be a bad idea - if you hypnotize someone to think that they were attacked but healed, they will most likely say something along the lines of, "Thanks, {{A|Doctor}}," the next morning. [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|Whispering]] them saying, "You're welcome," will make them feel indebted to you and more likely to support your claim if you are accused. Another way to gain the trust of who you "heal" is by [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] them a message a close friend would say. Some examples are: "I don't think so!", or "Not today!". This will make them see you as more friendly, and more like they have some connection with you. **Even if they don't make any mention of being healed, whispering that you know they were healed will likely make them view you as a confirmed Townie. *If your only {{A|Mafia Killing}} is {{A|Jailed}} or being {{A|Roleblocked}}, you can use the attack & protected messages to fake {{A|Mafia}} attacks and reduce suspicion against them. This is particularly useful in the situation where the {{A|Godfather}} is {{A|Jailed}} without a {{A|Mafioso}}, as your "protection" messages can cover for the lack of killing, and the {{A|Spy}} can cover for you by seeing the {{A|Mafia}} visits (and the message if they happened to bug your target). This will prevent the {{A|Mafia}} from being paralyzed in a pinch, and perhaps save the game if the {{A|Town}} believes the message. *While claiming to be a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} may seem like a stupid idea because you cannot directly {{A|Roleblock}} someone, your hypnosis can cover that for you. This is reinforced by the fact that most people claim they were {{A|Roleblocked}}. ** Be wary of {{A|Serial Killers}}, however, as anyone who {{A|Roleblocks}} them will die (unless they choose to be Cautious). Although they can hardly call you out on it, a smart {{A|Serial Killer}} will know you are a {{A|Hypnotist}} and attack you. **Additionally, remember that if you send a fake {{A|Roleblocking}} message to someone whose ability produces obvious results (such as most investigative roles), they'll immediately know there's a {{A|Hypnotist}}. **Finally, a {{A|Spy}} can easily call you out, and (although they will accuse you of being a {{A|Bootlegger}}) you will likely be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. *{{A|Investigators}} limit your claim-space down to a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}. If you choose random people to hypnotize into believing they were {{A|Roleblocked}}], and can disprove your claim, you may be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] easily. In this case, {{A|Transporter}} is a decent claim if there are no {{A|Spies}} around. *Claiming {{A|Transporter}} can be a good idea if you claim that you {{A|Transported}} someone that was killed or claim to have been {{A|Transported}} yourself. Usually, the {{A|Town}} will have no idea this was the work of a {{A|Hypnotist}}. It works even better if your target freely shares they were {{A|Transported}}. **Keep in mind that much like role-blocks, you cannot produce a "Someone tried to {{A|Transport}} you but you were in {{A|Jail}}." message, as your ability will fail when targeting a {{A|Jailed}} player. This means that a {{A|Transporter}} producing this message is ultimately confirmed as not {{A|Hypnotist}}. ***You can also use this to your advantage, by telling a {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Mafia}} member to claim they received this message, will help prove your claim as legitimate. Smart {{A|Townies}} might realize that both of you are lying, but by the time that happens it will probably be too late for the {{A|Town}}. **If your {{A|Last Will}} consists of only {{A|Transporting}} one person with yourself, or dead people, you may be suspected as a {{A|Hypnotist}}. You can have another {{A|Mafia}} member claim {{A|Transported}} to justify your claims a bit. **Your {{A|Transporter}} claim can be strengthened if you have a {{A|Forger}} or another {{A|Hypnotist}}, as the {{A|Forger}} can fake {{A|Mafia}} attacking themselves by forging targets as {{A|Mafia}}, and the {{A|Hypnotist}} can add that extra {{A|Transport}} message needed to "confirm" yourself as a {{A|Transporter}}. **However, a {{A|Spy}} can discredit you fairly easily if they realize many of your targets match {{A|Mafia}} visits without a {{A|Disguiser}}. They will immediately call out the other {{A|Mafia}} members that supported you once you are killed. *You can use your hypnotism to eliminate claim-space that a {{A|Town}} member needs in order to get them [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] - for instance, making it appear that there's a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Tavern Keeper}} occupying {{A|Town Support}} so people won't believe a {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Retributionist}} (especially if a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Necromancer}} is in game) claim. When using your ability in this way, try to target someone talkative and trusted so they'll volunteer the falsified information on their own, or {{A|Town}} members whose votes you particularly need to hang the victim (like a {{A|Mayor}}). *Making roles think they were controlled by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} can be useful as it can disrupt the {{A|Town's}} focus or reveal roles that are hiding under the radar, such as a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Mayor}}. **With a {{A|Disguise}}, using the controlled message on a {{A|Jailor}} who claims {{A|Day}} 1 can place all visitors under suspicion even with {{A|Spies}} around. **Unfortunately, using this on roles that are given information at {{A|night}} will ultimately reveal your presence. You can circumvent this with a {{A|Bootlegger}}. ***In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, doing this after {{A|night 3}} or with the {{A|Coven Leader}} dead will also reveal your presence unless you can convince the {{A|Town}} the dead {{A|Coven Leader}} was ''forged'' (before {{A|Night 3}}). **Posing as a {{A|Witch}}, you can also use your hypnotism to try to trick a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role you found into confessing their role to you. If they do, you can either immediately out them to the {{A|Town}}, or work with them and tell them to attack certain targets for the {{A|Mafia's}} benefit, ''then'' hang them once they've served their purpose. *In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, you can manipulate {{A|Guardian Angels}} using your {{A|Necronomicon}} {{A|poison}} message; most {{A|Guardian Angels}} will immediately protect their target when they claim to be {{A|poisoned}}. This can be used to waste a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} protections to get their target killed sooner. Make sure that there's a {{A|Guardian Angel}} present first, or it will be obvious there's a {{A|Hypnotist}} when the target fails to die to {{A|poison}}. **If it's {{A|Night 3}} or later and there is a confirmed {{A|Coven Leader}} in-game, smart {{A|Townies}} will realize the presence of a {{A|Hypnotist}} if a {{A|Spy}} bugged the hypnotized target or by simply asking if the message contained ''"unless you are cured!"'', since the {{A|Poisoner}} cannot possibly have the {{A|Necronomicon}}. Don't use the message from{{A|Night}} 3 onwards if the {{A|Coven Leader}} is not dead yet, or the target will realize they have been hypnotized. **If you still want to make it appear that there's a {{A|Poisoner}} in game, use the "poisoned but healed" message. This can also work to fake the existence of a {{A|Necromancer}} as well if there's a dead {{A|Poisoner}} (real or forged). *Sending a {{A|poison}} message and no follow-up (and other bizarre messages) can sometimes be useful for discrediting people; while the {{A|Town}} might realize there's a {{A|Hypnotist}}, they may also assume that someone making nonsensical claims is a {{A|Jester}}. *Your {{A|Bodyguard}} message might seem useless at first (because the {{A|Town}} will immediately be suspicious at the lack of a corpse for both the {{A|Bodyguard}} and the attacker), but if there's an potential {{A|Necromancer}} to make an attack that leaves no attacker's corpse, the {{A|Bodyguard}} message can sometimes be utilized by claiming to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} who was saved by a {{A|Doctor}}. Better yet, you can have another {{A|Mafia}} member pretend to be the {{A|Doctor}} who healed you ([[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] you as soon as the next {{A|day}} begins), which will discourage other evils from attacking either of you. The catch is that you risk outing two {{A|Mafia}} members if either of you gets caught. If you think it's too risky to use a {{A|Bodyguard}} message, you can use a {{A|Trapper}} message instead. **You can also use this to have another {{A|Mafia}} claim {{A|Doctor}} and accuse someone of being the attacker, but only do this if you know for certain that your team will gain majority by doing this. **You can also claim to be a {{A|Retributionist}} using a dead {{A|Bodyguard}}. In this case, you can tell the main {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles to not attack to help support your claim, and the {{A|Spy}} can cover for you by seeing the {{A|Mafia}} visits or even seeing the message with their bug. If the {{A|Doctor}} happens to save someone that night, they might think they saved the {{A|Mafia Killing}}. ***Under the right circumstances, you can also make your target believe that you used the dead {{A|Bodyguard}} to save them from {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}}. ***Keep in mind that the {{A|Retributionist}} is an [[Unique Role|unique role]] and they will likely call you out if one exists. *Remember, you can manufacture false claims for ''anyone'' in the {{A|Mafia}}, not merely yourself; you can also prepare them, share them in the {{A|Mafia chat}}, and have whoever needs them use them when pressed. It's a good idea to prepare an excuse or two for other {{A|Mafia}} members in advance, using messages to prepare things that anyone can claim if pressed. **When manufacturing fake claims for the entire {{A|mafia}}, roles that only produce occasional messages (such as {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}) are more useful than ones that would be expected to produce them every {{A|night}} (like {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}). You can still fake 'noisy' roles by making most of your visits be to dead people, but it's more risky, and other {{A|Mafia}} members are unlikely to prepare the detailed fake {{A|Last Will}} this requires - whereas "if you get in trouble, claim {{A|Doctor}} and say you healed this player" is much easier to remember and fall back on. **You can also do this if the {{A|Godfather}} (and any member of the {{A|Mafia}}) decides to claim {{A|Crusader}} and they can claim that they attacked an immune role. If there's a {{A|Spy}}, you should have your {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}} not attack to help support said {{A|Crusader}} claim, as any {{A|Spy}} bugging your target will see your {{A|Crusader}} protect message and see the {{A|Mafia}} visited said person and failed to kill, thus legitimizing said {{A|Crusader}} claim. **If you suspect that a {{A|Tracker}} is tracking the {{A|Disguiser}}, you can ask them to {{A|Disguise}} you as your target while you hypnotize your target into believing that they were transported. Since a {{A|Transporter}} is the only other role aside from a {{A|Disguiser}} that can be seen by a {{A|Tracker}} visiting two targets, you can help "confirm" the {{A|Disguiser}} by claiming transported if a {{A|Tracker}} tracks the {{A|Disguiser}}. **You can ask a {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot the {{A|Godfather}} while you use a heal/protect message on the {{A|Vigilante}}. This will allow the {{A|Godfather}} to claim {{A|Veteran}} who shot someone, and the {{A|Vigilante}} can confirm their claim by your message. Of course, this will backfire if the {{A|Vigilante}} was role-blocked, visited by an actual {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Crusader}}, or simply chose not to shoot. This can also backfire if the {{A|Godfather}} has multiple visitors or was jailed on the night the {{A|Vigilante}} shoots them, so consider the benefits and risks before attempting this strategy. **When using messages to set up fake claims, it's useful to send them to people who are unlikely to die (and who the {{A|Mafia}} isn't going to want to kill for a while), such as {{A|Survivors}} - after all, if the person who received your message dies, it's going to be wasted. Be cautious about relying on {{A|Jesters}}, since they may lie about your messages in order to get killed themselves. *The wide variety of messages available to the {{A|Hypnotist}} means that {{A|Town}} members rarely suspect any one of them. Convoluted or unlikely claims (such as a {{A|Bodyguard}} who was healed or a {{A|Doctor}} who happened to heal someone) are actually more likely to be accepted, since a {{A|Hypnotist}} making those claims is even more rare. Fantastic claims are also more likely to make an ''impact'' on the {{A|Town}}, whereas common ones might simply be ignored. *If you can identify the {{A|Jailor}}, sending him a message that he was attacked and nursed back to health can make him suspect whoever he {{A|Jailed}} that {{A|night}} of being a {{A|Serial Killer}}. Sending that message to a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} can have a similar effect. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{HypnotistAchievements}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, the {{A|Hypnotist}} was exclusive to the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *The {{A|Hypnotist}} (initially named [https://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/viewtopic.php?f=51&t=23521 Drug Dealer]) was made by Kirize12 and added into the game as a result of the [https://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/viewtopic.php?f=27&t=118494 Testing Grounds]. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.12}} **If a {{A|Hypnotist}} "poisons" someone it will now send the correct message depending on the {{A|Coven}} having the {{A|Necronomicon}}. On {{A|Night 1}} and {{A|Night 2}} it will say "will die tomorrow unless cured", after that it will just say "you will die tomorrow!". **If a {{A|Hypnotist}} "roleblocks" someone the message will change accordingly if the target is roleblock immune or not. If the target is Roleblock Immune, they will get the "Someone tried to role block you but you are immune". instead. *{{VH|3.3.4}} **Removed {{A|Crusader}}-specific {{A|Hypnotist}} message option from [[Game_Modes (ToS)|Classic Town of Salem]]. *{{VH|3.3.1}} **Removed {{A|Coven Expansion}}-specific {{A|Hypnotist}} message options from [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic Town of Salem]]. *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Hypnotist}} is now available in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic Town of Salem]]. **For non-mobile platforms, fixed the size of the {{A|Hypnotist's}} menu. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Hypnotist's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Hypnotist.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Hypnotist's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Hypnotist Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Гипнотизёр]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Mafia Deception roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Guardian Angel}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |}{{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Guardian Angel}}[[File:RoleIcon GuardianAngel.png|thumb|left|100px]] |alignment={{A|Neutral Benign}} |avatar=[[File:Uriel.png|150px]] |attributes=[[Detection Immunity]]

Non-Unique |priority=2 |restrictions=2 uses |actionother=Protect target |investigator='''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvResCVN4}}. |consigliere=Your target is watching over someone. They must be a {{A|Guardian Angel}}. |summary=You are an Angel whose only goal is the protection of your charge. |abilities=Keep your target alive. |attributestext=Your target is XXXXXXX.

Twice a game you may Heal and Purge your target. This may be done from the grave. Watching over a player ignores Jail. |goal=Keep your target alive until the end of the game. |winwith={{A|Town}}
