{{A|Juggernaut}} |mustkill=N/A (target must live) }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *Twice a game you may "{{A|Protect}}" your target, which {{A|Heals}} and {{A|Purges}} them. *The {{A|Guardian Angel}} may find their target in their role card in the "Attributes" section.{{LabelTarget}} *An {{A|Executioner}}, {{A|Jester}}, or another {{A|Guardian Angel}} ''cannot ''be the target of a {{A|Guardian Angel}} for them to protect. **However, if the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target happens to be an {{A|Amnesiac}}, they can remember themselves as any of those roles. This can result in conflicting win conditions where a {{A|Guardian Angel}} may be forced to keep a {{A|Jester}} alive, despite the {{A|Jester}} wanting to be hanged! *Multiple {{A|Guardian Angels}} may share the same target. *A {{A|Guardian Angel}} and {{A|Executioner}} may share the same target. *During the {{A|Night}}, the {{A|Guardian Angel}} may select to protect their target. **A {{A|Guardian Angel}} can watch over their target '''even when dead'''. **The {{A|Guardian Angel's}} protection can stop multiple attacks on the target. **The {{A|Guardian Angel's}} protection can prevent a {{A|Jailor}} execution and an {{A|Arsonist}} ignition on their target. ***They cannot, however, prevent a {{A|Jester}} haunt, the Unstoppable attack from a {{A|Hex Master}}, an attack from a fully powered-up {{A|Juggernaut}}, or a {{A|Vigilante's}} death from guilt after having shot a {{A|Town}} member. **The target being protected will receive a notification at the end of the {{A|Night}} stating, "The {{A|Guardian Angel}} was watching over you!" **At the start of the next {{A|day}}, the entire town will see the following message: "The {{A|Guardian Angel}} has protected [target's name].". The target will not be able to be voted up to trial during the voting phase that {{A|day}}. **Players who attack a protected target will receive no notification, just like when attacking a {{A|Witch}} with their mystical barrier (however, {{A|Witches}} cannot appear in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}) or someone healed by a {{A|Potion Master}}. ***A protected target who was attacked will receive the following message: "You were attacked but the {{A|Guardian Angel}} saved you!". ***The {{A|Guardian Angel}} will also be notified of an attack on their target, similar to a {{A|Doctor}}. [[File:SpecialLabel_GuardianAngel.png|alt=|thumb|The icon that appears next to a player protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}} in the player list]] *The {{A|Guardian Angel's}} protection also purges the target, removing certain negative effects, including an {{A|Arsonist's}} {{A|Douse}} and a {{A|Poisoner's}} {{A|Poison}} (even if they have the {{A|Necronomicon}}). A target who is doused and protected on the same {{A|Night}} will end up not being doused. {{A|Poison}} will be removed regardless of whether you heal your target on the {{A|Night}} they were {{A|Poisoned}} or the {{A|Night}} they would die. *A {{A|Guardian Angel}} will not remove the effects of {{A|Framer's}} {{A|Frame}}, a {{A|Hex Master's}} {{A|Hex}}, or a {{A|Plaguebearer's}} {{A|Infection}} on a player. *If the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target dies at {{A|Night}}, the {{A|Guardian Angel}} will become a {{A|Survivor}} with no vests. *If the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target is hanged, they do not become a {{A|Survivor}} until the next {{A|day}}. If the game ends on the same {{A|day}} their target is hanged, they lose. *If the {{A|Guardian Angel}} is controlled, they will use a protection on their target, no matter who they were controlled into. *If the {{A|Guardian Angel}} is [[Role block|role blocked,]] they will '''NOT''' use a protection on their target. *The {{A|Guardian Angel}} will die when bitten by a {{A|Vampire}} instead of being converted. *Passively suicidal roles, including {{A|Bodyguard}} and {{A|Vigilante}}, can be a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target. *The {{A|Guardian Angel's}} visit is Astral, meaning it is not affected by roles that kill via visits, such as the {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Ambusher}}, or {{A|Medusa}}. *The {{A|Guardian Angel}} '''can '''have the {{A|VIP}} as their target in {{A|VIP}} mode. *No matter how the game ends, whether the {{A|Guardian Angel}} is alive or not, if their target survives until the end of the game the {{A|Guardian Angel}} will always win regardless if their target also wins the game or not. ==Strategy== *If you die (even on {{A|Night 1}}), '''DO NOT LEAVE THE GAME'''. You can still use your abilities while you are dead, and you can still win. *If your goal is to keep your target alive as long as possible, you may not want to watch over them on {{A|Night 1}}. This will tell the {{A|Town}} that there is a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, which they can work around if they wanted to kill the certain person to make you {{A|Survivor}} and/or prevent scenarios where that target is guilty but cannot be voted, and it wastes one of your ability uses. There is also a very low chance that your target will be killed by an evil force, so it would be pointless to protect your target then. **In addition, your target could be an evil role themselves, making it far less likely that they will be targeted or harmed, including factions, removal abilities, immunity, healing, etc. **It would expose your target. Factions opposing your target will plot to kill them immediately before you could even protect them. It would be hard to predict when someone will try to kill your target. *On the other hand, if your goal is to ''win'' as fast as possible, watching over your target {{A|Night 1}} is a viable strategy: **It immediately confirms to the Town that there's a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, making it much more likely that you'll be believed later on if you have to claim your role. **It reduces the claim-space available to evils, making the game end sooner and helping you win (whether your target dies or not.) **Sometimes, the fact that they're a confirmed {{A|Guardian Angel}} protecting your target may help them live longer, since killers may be less likely to randomly target them if there's a chance you could use the second protection that {{A|Night}}. It also provides near-absolute protection from a {{A|Poisoner}}, who will have little reason to waste a {{A|Night}} poisoning your target when they know you'll just heal them, and reduces chances of being {{A|Doused}} and {{A|Poisoned}} due to the idea that the {{A|Guardian Angel}} can remove both. **If your target dies, you lose all your protections and become a {{A|Survivor}} with no vests - and no way to prove yourself. You're in a much better position if you used one of your protections prior to this since you've proven that there was a {{A|Guardian Angel}} in the game. **An extremely effective strategy to keep yourself alive and known to the {{A|Town}} is to claim {{A|Guardian Angel}} on the first {{A|day}}, then protect your target. You will confirm yourself easily, and even if your target is evil, they will most likely hang your target and force you to become a {{A|Survivor}}. It confirms yourself and makes you less of a target since you can win with any faction once you become a {{A|Survivor}}. **Do note that if you are an annoyance to a faction, you can be easily killed as you have no way to defend yourself, so try to be neutral until late game, when having a {{A|Survivor}} on your side is crucial to avoiding being hanged. *Communicate with your target to find out their role so that you can work together with your target. The role that they have can also change when to use your ability. **For example, if your target is a role with temporary defense (a {{A|Bodyguard}}, a {{A|veteran}}, a {{A|doctor}}, or a {{A|Survivor}}, make sure not to waste any protections by communicating to your target when you will use your protections and when they should protect themselves. The only times you should use your protections even though they have some form of defense that {{A|Night}}, is if you think a {{A|Werewolf}}, an {{A|Arsonist}}, a {{A|Pestilence}} or a {{A|Jailor}} might kill them that {{A|Night}}, or if they have been {{A|Poisoned}}. *As with the {{A|Survivor}}, you want to get the game done as quickly as possible with your target ending up as a victor. Make choices that speed up the game faster. This way, your target will have a higher chance of surviving. *If suspicion is ever thrown on your target, protect them, and spend the {{A|day}} defending them, as well as watching over them. Protect them the following {{A|Night}}, as they will also be given hang immunity. **Watching over your target reveals that you are a {{A|Guardian Angel}} and are a threat, so killing your target to make you a {{A|Survivor}} gains a higher priority. **If a {{A|Jailor}} is present and alive, and you have an evil target, try to paint the accuser as an {{A|Executioner}} in order to have the {{A|Jailor}} execute them to waste their executions. This is a last-minute strategy; if your team does not have majority, and you fail to use or are unable to use a protection, your target will most likely be hanged. **If a {{A|Jailor}} is not present, simply counterclaim the accuser and try to get them hanged. Work with your evil target, perhaps even whisper them to inform them of your role if it's safe -- their faction will see you as an asset towards achieving a majority. **Consider fake claiming a role to save your target. Most players are aware that a {{A|Guardian Angel}} will say anything to save their target, so they disregard comments from known {{A|Guardian Angels}}. If they do not know your true role, then your verbal defense has more merit. ***Posting fake results for an accuser and causing chaos may very well divert enough attention from your target to give you the chance to protect them at {{A|Night}}. Note this may result in your own death, but dying is not necessarily a problem. *If there is a {{A|Medium}} after you have died, convince them to protect your target. The extra help can allow your target to last longer in the game. *A hanged {{A|Jester}} is quite a dangerous threat to your goal, as they can kill your target regardless of your protections if your target did not vote innocent. If you are dead, you can try to convince them to not haunt your target, but there is little you can do to protect your target. **An alternative is to have your target vote innocent while you vote guilty on a possible {{A|Jester}}. Your guilty vote neutralizes your target's innocent vote if the {{A|Town}} or your target's team wants that player to be hanged, not affecting the results of the trial. This will keep your target save from a haunt if they do turn out to be a {{A|Jester}}. *Whispering {{A|Survivor}} claims, even when you haven't claimed, is a good way to form a block of voters: the {{A|Survivor}} will immediately have at least 2 potential allies, and even if they are a fake claim, they have little reason to kill you except to get rid of your voting power. *You can still win if your target loses in the event of a [[draw]]. Depending on what roles are alive, if you do not have any other way of keeping your target alive other than going for a draw, it is much better to go for the draw instead of letting your target die, as it aligns with your goal and you will still win the game. *Hanging your target intentionally is gamethrowing, even if you want to become a {{A|Survivor}}. *You should always try to keep yourself alive as long as possible and make as many allies as you can. If you die, you have no possibility of becoming a {{A|Survivor}} when your target dies. Confirm your role and then ally with your target's faction. This can help your target's faction win late game if you are able to stay alive. ==Dealing with {{A|Guardian Angels}}== *When a {{A|Guardian Angel}} is protecting a person of an opposing role/faction, try to trick the {{A|Guardian Angel}} into using their ability at the wrong time so that you can waste their protections and get their target killed easier. **Keep in mind that killing the {{A|Guardian Angel}} does not always work, as the {{A|Guardian Angel}} can still use their ability from the grave. *If you are a {{A|Coven Leader}}, you can force the {{A|Guardian Angel}} to use their charges by controlling them (into anyone). The same applies for a {{A|Necromancer}}, as using a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} corpse will force them to use their charges. Do not do this if the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target is one of your own. *If you are a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can prevent the {{A|Guardian Angel}} from protecting their target by [[Role block|role blocking]] them allowing the {{A|Mafia}} to kill/hang their target without interruption. The same applies for other [[Role block|role blockers]]. *If you are a {{A|Hypnotist}}, you can hypnotize the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target with the poisoned message to trick them that they are poisoned. The {{A|Guardian Angel}} might be fooled into using a protection early. **Remember that smart players might notice that they could've been hypnotized. *As a hanged {{A|Jester}}, you have free reign on the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target as your haunt bypasses their protections on said target. *You can force a {{A|Guardian Angel}} to join and help the {{A|Town}} as a {{A|Mayor}}. Your hanging power can force them to help you out if they become a {{A|Survivor}}. **On the other hand, if a {{A|Guardian Angel}} is protecting a killer and {{A|Town}} has a slim majority, you must hang the {{A|Guardian Angel}} to help with your chances of winning as it gets rid of one of the opposing roles helping votes. *Always remember that if a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target dies, they become a {{A|Survivor}} with no vests; in practice, this means they can win with anyone. Even if a {{A|Guardian Angel}} is opposing you, killing their target will sometimes give them the opportunity to switch sides. However, the {{A|Guardian Angel}} turned {{A|Survivor}} may have vested interest against you for killing their target which may be detrimental for you in a kingmaker scenario. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{GuardianAngelAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{GuardianAngelMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.1.5}}, {{A|Guardian Angels}} could not be added more than once in custom role lists despite not being a [[Unique role]]. *In-game, the Uriel [[Avatars (ToS)|avatar]] is referred to as female, despite its gender being male in Biblical texts. *Contrary to popular belief, your Purges do not remove {{A|Hexes}} as they are based off of {{A|Frames}} and not {{A|Douses}}. ==History== *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate the {{A|Guardian Angel's}} target for the {{A|Guardian Angel}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_GenericTarget.png|30x30px]]). **Added a label to visually indicate players protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_GuardianAngel.png|30x30px]]). **The {{A|Guardian Angel's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Guardian Angel.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Guardian Angel's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Guardian Angel Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.1.5.7426}} **Fixed a bug where {{A|Guardian Angel}} could not be added more than once in [[Coven Custom]] role lists despite not being a [[Unique role]]. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Ангел-хранитель]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Benign roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Defense]] [[Category:Astral]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets!}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== * The {{A|Mayor}} is a [[unique role]], meaning there can never be more than one {{A|Mayor}} in a match. *Click on the "{{A|Reveal (Mayor)}}" button during the {{A|Day}} to reveal yourself as the {{A|Mayor}} to all players. **Once revealed, your vote will count for three. These three votes refer to both the [[Phases#Voting|Voting]] and the [[Phases#Judgement|Judgement]] phases. ** You cannot be healed by a {{A|Doctor}} once you reveal yourself, making a {{A|Poisoner}} a dangerous threat. {{A|Bodyguards}}, {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Crusaders}}, {{A|Trappers}}, {{A|Guardian Angels}}, and the {{A|Jailor}} can still protect you, however. ** You cannot [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to other players or be [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispered]] to once you reveal yourself. If you attempt to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, you will receive a message saying "You can't [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a revealed {{A|Mayor}}.". A revealed {{A|Mayor}} attempting to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to someone will receive the message "You can't [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] once you have revealed as the {{A|Mayor}}!". *Neither you nor the {{A|Jailor}} can be an {{A|Executioner's}} target. * You are the only role who can win in a 1 vs. 1 against {{A|Pestilence}}, due to you having your vote count as three and, therefore, being able to hang them. **Furthermore, you are also able to win a 1 vs. 1 against any other evil role as well, provided they don't kill you first. *If you are converted into a {{A|Vampire}} while revealed, you will still show up as a revealed {{A|Mayor}}. However, you lose your extra votes and regain the ability to whisper or be whispered to. **If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Mayor|Mafia}}, you will still show up as "{{A|Mayor}}" (green) when revealing. If you die however, you will instead be shown as "{{A|Mayor|Mafia}}" (red) in the [[graveyard]] (applies similarly for a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Mayor|Coven}}). ==Strategy == ===Deciding to Reveal=== [[File:Unity Mayor Reveal.png|thumb|right|350px|Example picture of someone revealing as {{A|Mayor}}. Notice the text color is different than any other types of chat.]] *Some players discourage revealing {{A|day}} 1, since it makes you an immediate target. In fact, some people consider it [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Non-Reportable_Actions|gamethrowing]], when it's not. However, while it has disadvantages, it also has several advantages: **It allows the {{A|Jailor}} to jail you on the first {{A|night}} and identify themselves to you so you can work together while protecting you and possibly baiting the evil-doers into wasting their kill. **It lets any {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Investigators}}, and {{A|Vampire Hunters}} know not to waste time on you, narrowing down their search and increasing the chance that they will find evils. The {{A|night}} a {{A|Sheriff}} wastes investigating you because you failed to reveal may be the difference between victory and defeat. **It gives {{A|Bodyguards}}, {{A|Transporters}}, and {{A|Lookouts}} a guaranteed {{A|Town}} member to protect early in the game, and can bait an evil role into getting caught by them. Since the {{A|Mayor}} attracts a lot of visits, it also helps the {{A|Lookout}} identify and verify later {{A|Bodyguard}} claims, or prove themselves to a {{A|Jailor}} who jailed you. **It gives you the opportunity to confirm or deny {{A|Transporter}} claims, just simply ask a {{A|Transporter}} to transport you while having the {{A|Jailor}} jail you, since a real {{A|Transporter}} will produce a message to the jailee, while a {{A|Hypnotist}} cannot. **It allows the {{A|Town}} to immediately discount later {{A|Bodyguard}} claims if you get killed or bitten, since a real {{A|Bodyguard}} would have prevented it from happening. **While it makes you a target, remember that you were a target to begin with because the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} already know everyone but themselves is an enemy. Letting other {{A|Town}} members know you're on their side (even when they're making decisions early on in the game) will usually gain you more than what you would lose, since you instantly become a confirmed {{A|Townie}} and can use it to your advantage. **Remember that all else aside, ''if you die without revealing, your role was wasted''. Dying without revealing is the worst possible outcome. Even if the impact isn't obvious to you, every {{A|night}} you're revealed for is another {{A|night}} where the {{A|Town}} gets to make slightly more informed decisions. It also allows them to not waste a {{A|night}} investigating you or protecting the wrong person. ** You instantly narrow down possible suspects and fill the role-list, giving you easier and viable targets to hang, especially in games with large amounts of evil roles, like the {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Coven}} and some troublesome {{A|Neutrals}} if there are multiple of them. This is also crucial late game as you have great influence and allow the {{A|Town}} to be more confident in their decisions. ** One factor you should consider when deciding whether to reveal is how many {{A|Town}} there are and whether the evils are one or many factions. In modes like {{A|Ranked}}, where there are few factions and many {{A|Town}}, it makes sense to reveal early or even {{A|Day}} 1. In a mode like {{A|Coven}} All Any, you might benefit from laying low in hopes that the evils will target each other. ***On the other hand, smart evils in those modes are often more concerned about rival killers than they are about a {{A|Mayor}}, and may ignore you to focus on finding and killing an enemy faction. **In the {{A|Coven}} expansion, {{A|Crusaders}} are another thing to consider; if you reveal D1 and all the {{A|Town's}} {{A|Town Protectives}} and/or {{A|Lookouts}} pile onto you, there's a high risk of a {{A|Crusader}} killing another {{A|Town}} member. * You should always reveal when a {{A|Town Investigative}} calls you out or there is suspicion circling you. **Scenario: If an {{A|Investigator}} calls you out, thinking you are a {{A|Consigliere}}, you can always avoid being hanged by revealing, but if there's no {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Jailor}}, you'll probably be killed the next {{A|night}}. This can be a nightmare if you're not ready for revealing or you will be dead tomorrow, but always reveal. If you don't reveal yourself you may be killed by a {{A|Vigilante}} who assumes you're a {{A|Consigliere}}. *If the role list contains some {{A|Town Protective}} roles, you could consider revealing on {{A|Day 1}} or {{A|Day 2}}. This way, you either bait killing roles into attacking you, wasting their kill for that {{A|night}}, or you scare them off because there is a high chance that you are protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}. After that, you can effectively lead the {{A|Town}} until you are eventually taken out. Don't forget to include a "hang list" with your suspects in your {{A|Last Will}} to help the {{A|Town}}, even after your death. **Consider a {{A|day}} 1 Reveal. The {{A|Jailor}} does not yet possess their execution power yet, and the {{A|Werewolf}} will not be active. This guarantees your survival until {{A|day}} 2, as the {{A|Jailor}} saves you from all danger (including an {{A|Arsonist}} as their visit will fail). Be sure to ask the {{A|Jailor}} his identity, as since you are revealed, he will not lie (unless he's [[gamethrowing|game-throwing]] - in that case, report said person). Also, seeing that you are jailed {{A|night}} 1 will spook many evil roles into not attacking you until all {{A|Town Protective}} roles and the {{A|Jailor}} are dead. **On the first {{A|night}} after your reveal, if you don't think there is a {{A|Jailor}} around and you survive the {{A|night}}, say something around the lines of "Thanks {{A|Jailor}} for protecting me." The killing roles won't attack you as often since they don't want to attack you while you are jailed and waste a potential kill. *When you reveal at about {{A|day}} 4 or 5, someone usually has to be hanged in order for the {{A|Town}} to win (unless it's a {{A|Mafia}} majority). When you reveal, there are usually fewer than 10 players left alive, so do a large amount of deduction. It's much easier to do when there are fewer players giving roles to you. This allows you to cross out possible roles from the players already dead in the graveyard. *If you are one of the last {{A|Town}} roles left (preferably with a {{A|Town Protective}} or {{A|Transporter}}) and they need 3 votes in order to vote someone up, then reveal and hang your suspect. Then ask the {{A|Bodyguard}} (if there is one) to protect you (or {{A|Jailor}} to jail you) and slowly eliminate the remaining baddies. **Being able to hang a person single-handedly in the game makes it especially important to keep track of the clues, because your game is practically over if you're hang the wrong person. This can make it worthwhile to copy-and-paste {{A|Last Wills}} to the chat so that they can be read completely later on. *Accusing a known {{A|Neutral Benign}} role and voting innocent can be helpful later in the game. The {{A|Mafia}} tends to vote guilty because they think the {{A|Town}} will also vote guilty because they are not {{A|Town}}. However, this strategy may not work if the {{A|Neutral Benign}} is a claimed {{A|Survivor}}, as the {{A|Mafia}} often protect {{A|Survivors}} to gain more votes later in the game. *If you reveal especially early in the game, do not be swayed by a bandwagon, as you might be helping an {{A|Executioner}} win the game or either end up hanging the wrong person instead. *It may be tempting to try and play a "surprise {{A|Mayor}}", revealing unexpectedly to swing the game at the last minute when all seems lost. While these are dramatic and memorable moments, it's generally a poor strategy to aim for that deliberately unless you have no other option: ** You are very likely to get attacked and killed before the endgame, since {{A|Town Protectives}} will see no reason to focus on you if you haven't given a role yet. **Until you reveal, you provide no real benefit to the {{A|Town}}. This means that by waiting for a big dramatic reveal, you're costing the {{A|Town}} a slot that could have been filled with a more productive role - with a high risk that you'll die before the end and get no payoff. **Games often don't end with a one-vs-one standoff where a stealthy {{A|Mayor}} can make a difference. If your stalling and indecision about revealing leads to a situation with two or more {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} against you, or a three-way split with more than one evil, you're only going to possibly be able to hang one of them and will then lose the game. **Essentially, if possible, you're better off using your clout to push the {{A|Town}} forward and your ability to reveal to remove yourself from the list of suspects so the {{A|Town}} can win while it still has the advantage, rather than deliberately trying to reach a situation where the {{A|Town}} is almost defeated just so you can dramatically save the {{A|day}}. *If you ''must'' go for a clutch ending, though (for instance, because there simply aren't enough {{A|Town}} left), you have a number of options. These should only be done when you have no other option - they are not good strategies for general usage (you do not reveal as {{A|Mayor}} in these cases). **Claiming {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Executioner}} (or pretending to be a {{A|Jester}}) can convince evils to target other people (hopefully each other.) This shouldn't be done if there's a {{A|Vigilante}} present. While you can reveal if someone calls you out, you can't reveal if a {{A|Vigilante}} shoots you, and they will end up killing themselves out of guilt, potentially giving the {{A|Mafia}} an edge by quickly eliminating two powerful {{A|Town}} roles. You can always [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to the {{A|Vigilante}} your actual role, as to ensure this won't happen. ***Claiming {{A|Medium}} might also be helpful if you're planning on a stealth reveal and get asked for a role. Medium is generally considered a weak role by the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}}, so you're more likely to be left alone, but it's also a {{A|Town}} role, giving {{A|Vigilantes}} a reason not to shoot you. It also has the additional advantage of being the same alignment as your real role, so you're more credible and less likely to get counterclaimed. However, keep in mind a real {{A|Medium}} may call you out. **In order to pull off a clutch victory, you need to avoid a situation where you get killed immediately after revealing and hanging. If you can break a three-way split between a {{A|Plaguebearer}} and another evil when the next {{A|night}} is when they transform into {{A|Pestilence}}, for instance, the horseman won't be able to attack and you can hang them the next {{A|day}}. **If you have a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Transporter}}, or {{A|Crusader}}, they can often buy you the time you need to hang other roles. [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|Whisper]] them early on if you know their identity, then reveal to avoid drawing attention to them. However, be wary of {{A|Blackmailers}}. ===Voting for roles=== *While voting for roles is a viable strategy even without a {{A|Mayor}}, the {{A|Mayor's}} power makes it easier and more reliable. To do it, the {{A|Mayor}} reveals early on and votes up players who have not yet claimed a role, focusing on people who seem suspicious; he then votes innocent on anyone who makes a remotely credible role claim. This forces evil roles to make claims that can potentially be falsified. *Additionally, this produces voting records that can potentially reveal what sides people are on; many {{A|Mafia}} members have been caught due to a reluctance to vote up fellow {{A|Mafia}}. Conversely, if someone helps you vote up a {{A|Mafia}} member, they are less likely to be {{A|Mafia}} themselves. * One risk is that you may force valuable {{A|Town}} roles to reveal; this has to be weighed against the value of the information you gain. **Realize that revealing (especially in a group) is safer than it may seem. Evils are often reluctant to immediately exploit the knowledge they gain from this, since {{A|Town Protective}} roles can protect important role claims such as {{A|Jailor}}. **Additionally, this information is revealed to other {{A|Town}}, not just to the {{A|Mafia}}; that allows {{A|Town Protectives}}, {{A|Town Investigatives}}, and {{A|Town Killing}} roles to make more informed decisions - {{A|Town Investigatives}} and, if necessary, {{A|Town Killing}} roles can focus on people with weak claims, while {{A|Town Protectives}} can focus on ones with strong or valuable ones. This often benefits the {{A|Town}} by far more than they lose in revealing their roles to the {{A|Mafia}}. **Finally, if you are reluctant to reveal your role, remember, as a general rule, ''the {{A|Mafia}}/''{{A|Coven}} ''already knows you are not {{A|Mafia}}''/{{A|Coven}}; revealing more information benefits the {{A|Town}} (who needs information to hang and win) than it benefits the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} (who wins by default if they just kill a {{A|Townie}} every {{A|night}}, without needing any information at all to do it). Hiding from the evil-doers is not a viable long-term strategy. *Another serious risk is that a {{A|Jester}} can benefit from this by refusing to claim to get themselves hanged; for this reason, a common tactic is to order {{A|Vigilante}} claims to shoot likely {{A|Jesters}} instead, proving them while eliminating an evil role. * You can only vote up three people a {{A|day}}. While it's rare for the {{A|Town}} to need this many, this does prevent you from prolonging the {{A|day}} indefinitely and getting claims from absolutely everyone. For this reason, it's also a good idea to encourage people to reveal before they're voted up. *If you plan on pursuing this strategy, it may be a good idea to reveal {{A|day}} 1 and ask the {{A|Jailor}} to jail you so they can identify themselves; this avoids the risk of demanding that one of the most valuable {{A|Town}} roles claim publicly. *Realize that voting for roles is a controversial strategy; some people may object or refuse to cooperate purely because of this. That said, the people who protest most loudly about it being "random" should be seen as suspicious - most evils prefer a passive {{A|Town}} to one that hunts for them aggressively. ===Keeping Yourself Alive=== *Asking for protection from a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Jailor}} after being revealed can keep you from being attacked, even if you are actually vulnerable. Also if in jail, be sure to get the identity of the {{A|Jailor}} so you can get to work with them and know one person's role for certain. Be warned that if the {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} knows that you were jailed, they can force the {{A|Jailor}} to execute you, wasting their executions along with your death. *If you are jailed, always try to make a good plan and consolidate claims with the {{A|Jailor}}. A {{A|Mayor}} and {{A|Jailor}} are very strong together and will bring chaos upon the evil roles. *Be wary of the {{A|Werewolf}} since when you reveal, since a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Lookout}} and/or the {{A|Jailor}} will try to look after you. You are an easy target for the {{A|Werewolf}}, due to their ability to kill everyone who visits you. You shouldn't have to worry about the {{A|Werewolf}} if there's a {{A|Bodyguard}}. It's recommended to reveal when you are confident that there is no {{A|Werewolf}} or when the {{A|Werewolf}} is dead. *Late in the game, if you are an un-revealed {{A|Mayor}} and the only other roles left are multiple conflicting evils ({{A|Mafia}} vs {{A|Neutral Evils}}), a possible claim is {{A|Witch}}, if the remaining players don't communicate. This allows you to wait for the other players to kill each other off so you can reveal and end the game with an instant hang. The advantage of the {{A|Witch}} claim over the {{A|Survivor}} claim is that you won't be attacked in order to check for {{A|Defense}}, which sometimes happens to check {{A|Survivor}} claims. The disadvantage is that the other players could communicate with each other to disprove your {{A|Witch}} claim, as no one has been controlled. If, however, there actually is a {{A|Witch}}, this disadvantage could be negated. *If you don't plan to reveal early on, claim {{A|Survivor}} (if the role list allows you to do so). If the killing roles think you are a {{A|Survivor}}, they won't attack you, ensuring your {{A|night}} survival. This might be useful to get near the end of the game where you can reveal and hang players alone, thanks to your voting power. **Careful with this strategy, as a {{A|Jailor}} may execute you because they execute {{A|Survivors}}, since it's a role usually claimed by many evil roles such as a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}}, or if the {{A|Jailor}} thinks {{A|Survivors}} are more likely to help the {{A|Mafia}} win. Also, watch out for a {{A|Vigilante}}, they tend to shoot {{A|Survivor}} claims for the same reason. **This can also backfire with trying to keep killing roles away from you, as they might test your "{{A|Defense}}", or the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} could get a {{A|Consigliere}}/{{A|Potion Master}} to investigate you just in case. *A revealed {{A|Mayor}} has an extremely hard time hiding the fact that they were bitten by a {{A|Vampire}}: ** You will only have one vote, instead of three. For this reason, if you get bitten, you should avoid voting as much as possible. ** You will be able to send and receive [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]], which allows anyone to discover that you are a {{A|Vampire}} at any time simply by trying to send you one. **These facts can be used to your advantage if the only enemy facing the {{A|Town}} is {{A|Vampires}}; you can reveal, then immediately remind the {{A|Town}} of the ways to detect if you've been bitten. This will discourage {{A|Vampires}} from wasting one of their limited bites on you while allowing you to use your three votes to aggressively demand roles and force people to give information confirming that they haven't been bitten. *If there is a {{A|Mafia}} member left in the round with an {{A|Arsonist}}, hang the member of the {{A|Mafia}}. Hanging the {{A|Mafia}} prevents you from being killed and having the {{A|Arsonist}} win the game over the {{A|Mafia}} via stalemate. If you luckily haven't been doused yet, hang the {{A|Arsonist}} to prevent an ignition, allowing you to gain a solo {{A|Town}} win. **A similar case is true for a {{A|Serial Killer}} left with a {{A|Vampire}}, in this case, hang the {{A|Serial Killer}}, then hang the {{A|Vampire}} to prevent a conversion if they're a new {{A|Vampire}}. *If aiming for the [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]] "Faith in the Town", try to act like a {{A|Jester}}, then reveal the day after you got voted innocent. However be careful, as this may lure {{A|Vigilantes}} into killing you. It might be easier for you to admit to the town that you are aiming for the achievement in Classic or All Any mode if you are on stand. But keep in mind that you would have to reveal immediately after getting off from the stand since the town would expect you to do so. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{MayorAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{MayorMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.0.3431}}, a revealed {{A|Mayor}} was able to send and receive [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]]. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.4}} (when the {{A|Retributionist}} was able to permanently resurrect dead {{A|Townies}}), if you were killed before revealing as {{A|Mayor}} and then resurrected by a {{A|Retributionist}}, you would have had 3 votes as if you had revealed. However, this would not count as revealing, thus allowing you to easily obtain the Incognito achievement without hindering the town. (See [[Achievements (ToS)#Mayor|Achievements]]) * The {{A|Mayor}} is the only role able to potentially win against any evil role in a 1v1 standoff, due to having 3 votes when revealed. * The {{A|Mayor}} is one of four roles that have a {{A|Day}} ability, the others being the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Pirate}}, and a dead {{A|Medium}}. ==History== *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.3.11]] **Fixed {{A|Mayor}} extending the TT hunt by a day in Town Traitor *{{VH|3.3.0}} ** For a {{A|Transporter}}, when {{A|Transporting}} a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, the second target buttons are no longer improperly labeled "Reveal". *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} ** The {{A|Mayor's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Mayor.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Mayor's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Mayor Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **Revealed {{A|Mayors}} can no longer be healed by a {{A|Doctor}} if {{A|Transported}}. *{{VH|1.5.0.3431}} **{{A|Mayor}} can no longer [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] or be [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispered]] to after revealing. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Mayor}} as a target. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Maire]] [[ja:市長]] [[pl:Burmistrz]] [[ru:Мэр]] __FORCETOC__ [[Category:Town Support roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *The {{A|Retributionist}} is a {{A|Unique}} Role; there can never be more than one alive at a time. *You may resurrect one dead {{A|Town}} role per {{A|Night}} and use their ability on another player. You will receive the results your resurrected corpse otherwise would have (e.g. using a {{A|Sheriff}} to determine if someone is suspicious or not).{{LabelRot}} **You will visit your first target in the [[graveyard]]. A {{A|Tracker}} can see you visiting the target you choose to resurrect. This is able to confirm you as a {{A|Retributionist}} if there is no {{A|Necromancer}}. ===Resurrecting a target=== *You can resurrect a dead {{A|Townie}} during the {{A|Night}}. There are some restrictions: **Your target ''must'' be a {{A|Townie}}. **Your target died '''before''' the current {{A|Night}} (either via [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]] or during a previous {{A|Night}}). **Your target was not {{A|Cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}}. **Your target was not {{A|Stoned}} by {{A|Medusa}}. *The corpse performs the second visit, not you. The corpse itself is then subjective to anything a normal player would be. A {{A|Lookout}} can see the dead player visiting their target, and a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trap}} from a {{A|Trapper}} will respond against your resurrected player. Likewise, a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}} rampage at your second target's location will not harm you. *If both you and a {{A|Necromancer}} target the same player on the same {{A|Night}}, only one of you will be able to use the corpse, while the other player will fail and receive a message that the corpse is missing from the [[graveyard]]. Whoever gets to use the corpse that {{A|Night}} is decided at random. The other will still be able to use the same corpse on a future {{A|Night}}. *Players who have left the game can still be used. *You have [[Roleblock Immunity]] and [[Control Immunity]], meaning that you will be able to control a corpse even if a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} targets you. ** You do, however, get roleblocked by the {{A|Pirate}} (this is a bug). *Unlike the {{A|Necromancer}}, you can use corpses on yourself. *There is an ongoing bug that sometimes causes reanimated corpses to ignore {{A|transportation}}. *There is an inconsistent bug that sometimes causes reanimated corpses to be invisible to {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Trappers}} and even {{A|Spies}}. This has been happening ever since the [[Version History - Town of Salem|QoL patch]] on October 20th, 2024. *A {{A|Psychic}}, {{A|Trapper}}, {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Mayor}}, {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Transporter}}, or another {{A|Retributionist}} (if you were an {{A|Amnesiac}}) cannot be resurrected. {| class="article-table mw-collapsible" !Role !Usable? !Effects !Strategy     |- |{{A|Town Investigative}} |{{Y}}(except {{A|Psychic}}) |Causes the corpse to perform their ability on the target, which will be noticed by {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Trappers}}, or a {{A|Veteran}} on alert. If the second target is a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, they will visit but not heal the second target. |You can use it to heal yourself or a confirmed {{A|Town}} member. |- |{{A|Trapper}} |{{N}} | | |- |Non-{{A|Townies}} |{{N}} | | |} ==Strategy== A {{A|Retributionist}} somewhat serves as a mirror to the {{A|Necromancer}}, as you work for the {{A|Town}} using your abilities. You are limited with your uses, as you can only control {{A|Town}} roles. This can either be very useful or very useless depending on the {{A|Town}} roles who die. *{{A|Town Investigative}} roles such as the {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} can be used at any time to learn the results of other players. {{A|Lookouts}} can be used to watch important {{A|Town}} roles and keep you safe from any possible {{A|Ambushers}} or {{A|Werewolves}} who may target that {{A|Townie}}. {{A|Trackers}} can give you a quick way to determine someone's claim. *Using a {{A|Spy}} can be used to confirm a player as a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}, or to catch evils claiming to be roleblocked, or that are seen with incriminating bug information such as having {{A|defense}}, being immune to role blocks, and in the case of a possible {{A|Arsonist}}, getting doused or cleaning gasoline from themselves. *If a {{A|Bodyguard}} dies whilst protecting a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, you might want to protect them again. The chances of a second {{A|Bodyguard}} is unlikely and the {{A|Mayor}} might be attacked again so this can slip up members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} by doing this. *Using a {{A|Bodyguard}} is usually preferable to a {{A|Doctor}} since the {{A|Bodyguard}} can take down an attacker, but the {{A|Doctor}} can save a player from multiple attacks. If you think a player will be attacked by multiple parties you should use a {{A|Doctor}} over a {{A|Bodyguard}}. A {{A|Crusader}} however can attack a possible attacker and keeps the target safe from all attacks against them (especially if they're a revealed {{A|Mayor}}), so they may be more useful. *Always try and save {{A|Town Protective}} corpses until you are confident a player will be attacked. You only have one use on every corpse and shouldn't waste it. *{{A|Vigilantes}} are your only reliable killing role and can be used to prove whether someone is evil or not depending on who you shoot. You can also determine if your target has a form of defense, but be careful to not confuse it with another {{A|Town Protective}} role protecting them instead. *A {{A|Vampire Hunter}} can be used if you believe that {{A|Vampires}} are still at large. If a player is accused, you can stake them to check, preferably on a {{A|Night}} {{A|Vampires}} can't convert them. *{{A|Tavern Keepers}} can prevent possible {{A|Mafia Killing}} and especially {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles from killing during the {{A|Night}}. However, a {{A|Serial Killer}} cannot be stopped from killing. *Coordinate with a {{A|Trapper}} about who they trapped so you don't accidentally set off any of their traps with your corpses as you will not only screw over the {{A|Trapper}}, players will think you are actually a {{A|Necromancer}}. *{{A|Medusas}} and {{A|Janitors}} are trouble, as they prevent you from using certain corpses as they clean out their victim’s roles. {{A|Janitors}} especially can make your {{A|Retributionist}} claim more suspicious due to their presence in your investigative result. {{A|Vampires}} are also a nuisance as you are unable to use the {{A|Townies}} they convert. *You will always use the true ability of the dead {{A|Townie}} if they are indeed a {{A|Townie}}. {{A|Forgers}} can be a dangerous threat; they can deny you corpses to use if they forge someone as a non-{{A|Town}} or non-visiting role, make your claim look suspicious by forging someone as a {{A|Retributionist}} since the role is unique, or even trick you into accidentally killing important {{A|Town}} roles (like a {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}) by forging a {{A|Vigilante}} as a {{A|Town Protective}} role. **If you try to use a non-town role forged as a {{A|Town Investigative}}, they won't produce any results. Use this to help discover the existence of a {{A|Forger}}. *If you are torn about whether or not to vote guilty on a player or are considering abstaining, you might want to vote guilty instead. If the [[hanged]] turns out to be a {{A|Townie}} and not evil, you can use their corpse the same {{A|Night}}, but you may be seen as suspicious for guilting a {{A|Town}} member so this is '''''not '''''justification to vote guilty on players who you aren't suspicious of. *You are one of the few {{A|Town}} roles that still win or draw in a 1v1 or 2v1 against a solo {{A|Mafia}} or even the {{A|Neutral Killing}} depending on what roles have died. **If there is a dead {{A|Vigilante}}, you can still draw against a solo {{A|Mafioso}} or any {{A|Coven}} member minus the {{A|Coven Leader}} (and sometimes {{A|Necromancer}}). You can also pull the victory this way if the {{A|Town}} holds a 2-1 majority. **{{A|Doctors}} can stall out the game for a couple of {{A|Nights}} which can cause draws, which are usually preferable to losses, especially since in {{A|Ranked}} games, as players will not lose any [[Elo]] incase of a draw. Be mindful that you will not be awarded a Draw if a non-factional role complete their win condition. **If there is a dead {{A|Bodyguard}} corpse you can win against all {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles, {{A|Serial Killer}} {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Juggernaut}} (with less than three kills), {{A|Vampire}} and all {{A|Coven}} roles with the {{A|Necronomicon}} except a {{A|Hex Master}} and {{A|Necromancer}}. If there are multiple {{A|Bodyguards}}, you can win against multiple separate attacks, but not more than one attack in the same {{A|Night}}. **If there is a dead {{A|Crusader}}, you can win against a solo {{A|Mafioso}} or all members of the {{A|Coven}} except the {{A|Coven Leader}}, {{A|Necromancer}}, and {{A|Hex Master}}. **If there is a dead {{A|Vampire Hunter}} and only one alive {{A|Vampire}}, you can win with the {{A|Town}} only if the {{A|Vampire}} cannot bite a target the same {{A|Night}}, otherwise you will be converted and instead win the game as a {{A|Vampire}}. **You are one of the few roles who can deal with roles that use the Rampage ability, such as {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}. Your corpse performs their ability on your target, which also results in your corpse visiting them and taking any damage you otherwise would've received. Against {{A|Pestilence}} specifically, if enough {{A|Town Protective}} roles are in the [[graveyard]] you could potentially force a draw for the {{A|Town}} over a loss. ==={{A|Retributionist}} vs. Evil Role=== Below is a list of possible draws or victories for the {{A|Retributionist}} when alone against a single evil role. *Do note that some of these outcomes are only possible with multiple corpses. {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed wikitable" !Role!!Corpse(s)!!Result  |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Mafioso}} |{{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, or {{A|Vigilante}}||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Godfather}} |{{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, or {{A|Crusaders}}||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=1|{{A|Arsonist}} |{{A|Tavern Keepers}}||Draw |- |rowspan=3|{{A|Juggernaut}} |{{A|Tavern Keepers}}||Draw |- |{{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Doctors}} or {{A|Crusaders}}
(before 3rd kill)||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}}

(after a conversion)||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Coven Leader}} |{{A|Doctors}} or {{A|Crusaders}}||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=1|{{A|Hex Master}} |{{A|Tavern Keepers}} or {{A|Vigilante}}||Draw |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Medusa}} |{{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, or {{A|Vigilante}}||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Necromancer}} |{{A|Bodyguards}}, {{A|Doctors}}, or {{A|Crusaders}} (if rival has {{A|Powerful Attack}} or {{A|Basic Attack}})||Draw |- |{{A|Vigilante}} (if rival has {{A|Unstoppable Attack}})||Draw |- |rowspan=3|{{A|Poisoner}} |{{A|Tavern Keepers}}||Draw |- |{{A|Vigilante}} (if {{A|Retributionist}} is {{A|Poisoned}})||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Crusader}} or {{A|Vigilante}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |rowspan=2|{{A|Potion Master}} |{{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, or {{A|Vigilante}}||Draw |- |{{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}}||{{A|Town}} wins |- |} ===Proving your role=== *Due to the changes in the {{A|Retributionist}} role, it is now much harder to confirm yourself, and it is a much easier claim for evils. There are, however, a few strategies you can use. *Using a {{A|Vigilante}} is one way to do this since you will create an obvious result, however, this is risky and can cost a valuable {{A|Townie}}, so only do this if you know that your target is evil. **If a player tries to claim your role, use a dead {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot them. Your role is [[Unique Role|unique]], so there cannot be a second one. ***Announce that you counterclaim {{A|Retributionist}} and that you will use a dead {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot them if they do not show proof of another role, as you risk accidentally shooting an unrevealed {{A|Mayor}} that is trying to lay low. ***Additionally, in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, your counterclaim might be a {{A|Necromancer}}. If they reanimate the same {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot you, there is a very high chance that not only you will be killed, but you also will not be able to shoot them. Once your role is revealed the {{A|Town}} should piece together that the player you said you were going to shoot is a {{A|Necromancer}}, but it will still cost your life. *Using a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} to [[roleblock]] a player can confirm you as a {{A|Retributionist}}, since this leaves a clear message behind. You should whisper in advance to make sure your target knows you will [[roleblock]] them, so they can confirm you later. **You should only do this to a confirmed {{A|Townie}} who will not act that {{A|Night}} (such as a {{A|Medium}}) or a role that is no longer useful (such as a {{A|Sheriff}} in a {{A|Vampire}} game) or a role that is [[Roleblock Immune]]. **Do note that if you roleblock an evil role, they can accuse you and you could get [[hanged]]. **You could still be accused of being {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Hypnotist}}, so this isn't foolproof. ***One strategy is to roleblock a confirmed {{A|Veteran}} who will alert that Night, as this will trigger their alert message and confirm you aren't lying. *Resurrecting an {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Lookout}} to see find information that is confirmed by other players can help you become confirmed, or if you use a {{A|Sheriff}} and find someone as suspicious. *Successfully using a {{A|Bodyguard}} and protecting someone can confirm you, but a {{A|Necromancer}} could easily put your claim under suspicion. *If a {{A|Lookout}} sees a dead player visit another player, this will confirm your existence unless you are playing in a gamemode with a possible {{A|Necromancer}}. **A {{A|Lookout}} can fully confirm you as {{A|Retributionist}} if they watch you while you make a dead player visit you, as {{A|Necromancers}} cannot target themselves with corpses. *If a {{A|Tracker}} sees you visit, they can confirm you as a {{A|Retributionist}} or {{A|Necromancer}}. *A {{A|Spy}} can help clear any suspicions of being a {{A|Necromancer}} by noting that no Coven members visited the corpses you used. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{RetributionistAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{RetributionistMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to [[Version History - Town of Salem|Version 3.2.4]], the {{A|Retributionist}} was able to revive a dead {{A|Townie}}, bringing them back to life permanently. This was most likely changed since some players felt the role was too powerful (especially in the Town Traitor gamemode and Ranked) and wasn't fun to play as or against. **Also prior to [[Version History - Town of Salem|Version 3.2.4]], the {{A|Retributionist|Mafia}} was previously unable to be a {{A|Town Traitor}} in {{A|Town Traitor}} [[Game Modes (ToS)|Game Modes]]. ==History== *[[Version History - Town of Salem|3.3.11]] **Fixed {{A|Retributionist}} not being Control Immune when controlled by a {{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Witch}}. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **The {{A|Retributionist}} can no longer revive players. **The {{A|Retributionist}} can now resurrect certain {{A|Town}} roles once per game to use their ability on a living player. **{{A|Retributionist}} uses in-place secondary targeting rather than a slide-out secondary menu. **{{A|Retributionist}} can now be a {{A|Retributionist|Mafia}} in {{A|Town Traitor}} and a {{A|Retributionist|Coven}} in {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}}. **Removed sound effect for when a player is revived. **Removed message "You have 1 resurrection left.". **Removed message "You have 0 resurrections left.". **Removed message "You have been resurrected by a {{A|Retributionist}}!". **Removed message "(Player) has been resurrected!". **Removed message "(Player) was brought back to life!" (seen in the middle of the screen). *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Retributionist's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Retributionist.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Retributionist's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Retributionist Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.5.10.4972}} **Added a sound effect for when a player is revived. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[Category:Town Support roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Roleblock Immune]] [[Category:Control Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

They must be a {{A|Sheriff}}. |summary = You are the law enforcer of the town forced into hiding from threat of murder. |abilities = Interrogate one person each night for suspicious activity. |attributestext = You will know if your target is suspicious. |winwith = '''{{A|Town}}'''

Members of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} with a {{A|Disguise}}/{{A|Necronomicon}} also cannot be found. *Anyone who has been {{A|Framed}}/{{A|Hexed}} will show up as suspicious. *Anyone who has been {{A|Doused}} will still appear as their normal result. {| class="article-table" border="1" !Investigation Message !Possible [[Roles (ToS)|Roles]] |- ! style="width:35%;" rowspan="10"|You cannot find evidence of wrongdoing. Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets! |All {{A|Townies}} (including the {{A|Town Traitor}} and {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}}) |- |All {{A|Neutral Benign}} |- |All {{A|Neutral Evil}} |- |All {{A|Neutral Chaos}} |- |{{A|Godfather}} |- |{{A|Arsonist}} |- |{{A|Werewolf}} during a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} |- |{{A|Juggernaut}} |- |A member of the {{A|Coven}} wielding the {{A|Necronomicon}} |- |A {{A|Mafia}} member {{A|disguised}} as any of the above roles |- ! rowspan="8" style="width:35%;" |Your target is suspicious or framed! |- |All members of the {{A|Mafia}} except the {{A|Godfather}}, unless they are {{A|disguised}} as an ''"innocent"'' role |- |Anyone {{A|Framed}} by a {{A|Framer}} |- |All members of the {{A|Coven}} unless they wield the {{A|Necronomicon}} |- |Anyone {{A|Hexed}} by the {{A|Hex Master}} |- |{{A|Serial Killer}} |- |{{A|Werewolf}} during a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} |- |Anyone {{A|disguised}} as any of the above roles |} ==Strategy== ===Working with Investigators=== *Unlike the {{A|Investigator}}, you can only directly determine whether your target is suspicious or not, and not their possible roles. Sharing information and discussing with the {{A|Investigator}} will allow you to narrow the pool of suspects: **If the {{A|Investigator}} finds a possibly suspicious role (e.g. a {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Serial Killer}} (or {{A|Potion Master}}), you '''should''' interrogate that person if there are signs of {{A|Coven}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}} **If the {{A|Investigator}} finds a certain {{A|Townie}} (by process of elimination), you will '''not''' need to interrogate that person, since they are confirmed and you would waste a {{A|Night}}. **If the {{A|Investigator}} finds a full [[Detection Immunity|detection immune]] investigative result (e.g. a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Arsonist}} (or {{A|Crusader}}), you will '''not''' need to interrogate that person either because, just like above, they will all appear the same. ***However, if there's a potential {{A|Arsonist}} in the game, you may need to interrogate the players the {{A|Investigator}} found as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Arsonist}} (or {{A|Crusader}}) as they could be a {{A|Doused}} {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} member or a {{A|Serial Killer}}. **If the {{A|Investigator}} finds a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Jester}} (or {{A|Hex Master}}), you should have some doubt in your interrogation results. If they show up as "innocent", they are one of those roles, and a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} should kill them; otherwise your target was likely {{A|Framed}} or {{A|Hexed}}. ===Suspicious players=== *If you're lucky enough to find a suspicious target early in the game, you should almost always reveal it immediately. Some people are afraid to reveal it because they might be called an {{A|Executioner}}, and some people will mistakenly advise you to wait because of this; however, there are numerous reasons why revealing vital information at the first possible opportunity is virtually always the right strategy: **If you don't post your information, you risk being {{A|Cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}}, {{A|Forged}} by a {{A|Forger}}, {{A|Stoned}} by {{A|Medusa}}, or {{A|Blackmailed}} forever by a {{A|Blackmailer}}, causing your information to be most likely lost forever, (unless there is a {{A|Medium}} in the case you are killed). **Generally speaking, the {{A|Town's}} majority decreases with every passing {{A|Day}}. Therefore, it is going to be easier for the {{A|Mafia}} to convince people to ignore you on {{A|Day 4}} than it would have on {{A|Day 2}}. **Even if you fail to convince the {{A|Town}} to hang someone you found immediately, you can still gain information based on how people react - people who help you try to hang a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} are probably not members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, while people who try to aggressively cast doubt on you or push suspicion elsewhere are themselves suspicious. This can be used to guide your investigations on later {{A|Nights}}, gathering information that will help the {{A|Town}} trust you. **You are unlikely to be attacked by the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} immediately after accusing one of their members because it would confirm your accusation and because you're likely to be protected. **Even if you fail to convince enough {{A|Townies}} to hang someone, the information you revealed still helps them behave more intelligently; a {{A|Vigilante}} who takes a potshot, for instance, is more likely to shoot at someone you accused, while {{A|Tavern Keepers}} are more likely to [[role block|roleblock]] them and {{A|Town Protectives}} are less likely to protect them. **Your accusations will not become more credible simply by waiting. {{A|Executioners}} often choose to accuse on either {{A|Day}} 3 or {{A|Day}} 4. Being called an {{A|Executioner}} reduces your chances of being believed, but in the long run, the {{A|Town}} benefits by having that information out there as soon as possible. On top of this, if you're asked to produce your complete {{A|Last Will}} and reveal you've been sitting on important information for several {{A|Nights}}, the {{A|Town}} is likely to treat you even more skeptically. **If you wait, there is a risk that the person you found could die to another cause. While that means they're gone, it's generally a wasted opportunity - it means you lost the chance to confirm yourself and to force their fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} to risk going on the record failing to vote up their partner. **There may be people who can confirm aspects of your accusation; for instance, a {{A|Tracker}} or {{A|Lookout}} who saw you visit will know that you're not an {{A|Executioner}}. They won't know to back you up unless you speak up. ===Detection Immunity roles=== *When you need to convince the {{A|Town}} that you're a {{A|Sheriff}} and not an {{A|Executioner}}, remember to report your visits every {{A|Night}} - after your role has been revealed, there's no reason not to share all information immediately, and even naming people as innocent will earn you a bit more trust. *If you suspect a player of being the {{A|Werewolf}}, remember to check them on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. Otherwise, they will appear as "innocent". *A less-used strategy is to coordinate with the {{A|Spy}}, as they can usually provide confirmed non-members of the {{A|Mafia}} by who the {{A|Mafia}} visits and therefore, you might want to ignore interrogating these people since they could have [[Detection Immunity]]. One example is the {{A|Arsonist}}. ===False Information=== *'''Be careful''', as multiple evil roles have [[Detection Immunity]], such as the {{A|Godfather}}, so they will appear as "innocent". Beware of whom you trust! **At any given time, there can only be one {{A|Godfather}}. Therefore, when a {{A|Godfather}} dies, anyone you investigated up until (and including) that {{A|Night}} who came up as innocent cannot be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. Note that they could still be an {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Witch}}, or {{A|Vampire}}; and people you investigate ''after'' the {{A|Godfather's}} death could be a {{A|Mafioso}} who has been promoted to {{A|Godfather}}. They could also be a {{A|Coven}} member with the {{A|Necronomicon}} or even a {{A|disguised}} {{A|Mafia}} member. *'''Be careful''', as {{A|Framed}} players will appear to be suspicious, so never be too quick to judge who is evil or not. If you aren't sure, check the same person the next {{A|Night}} (although this might not be worth it, it is usually better to gain new information that {{A|Night}} instead of doing a re-check, unless there is a confirmed {{A|Framer}}, such as in classic mode). If the {{A|Framer}} does not {{A|frame}} the same target again, your results will change. There are some {{A|Framers}} that will {{A|frame}} the same target for a few {{A|Nights}} in a row, so it's very hard to know if your information is true or not. However, in {{A|Ranked}}, if the {{A|Random Mafia}} slot is known to not be a {{A|Framer}}, it is safe to accuse anyone that shows up as suspicious. Keep in mind that it may be a good idea to ask a confirmed {{A|Spy}} who the {{A|Mafia}} visited, as they will usually be able to see who the {{A|Mafia}} might have {{A|Framed}}. Beware of {{A|Disguisers}}, as they can hide who the {{A|Framer}} visits from the {{A|Spy}} while also giving them credibility if they claim {{A|Framed}}. **A {{A|Hex Master}} is even more dangerous to you, as {{A|Hexed}} targets will permanently appear to be suspicious. You can ask a confirmed {{A|Spy}} who the {{A|Coven}} visited to help clear them and potentially find the {{A|Hex Master}} in this case (Keep in mind the {{A|Potion Master}} can visit the {{A|Hex Master}} to give them credibility if they claim {{A|Hexed}}). If someone claims to be {{A|Hexed}}, you may want to interrogate them just in case, if they appear as "innocent", then you'll know for certain the person you checked was the {{A|Hex Master}}. If a {{A|Guardian Angel}} purges their target, you can interrogate the person the following night to prove them; however, they can still be {{A|Framed}}. *If a {{A|Transporter}} {{A|Transports}} your target, you will interrogate someone else entirely without you knowing! If the {{A|Transporter}} reveals their {{A|Last Will}}, you will know who you interrogated that {{A|Night}} instead and can prove them as an evil role. However, if you see that your target says they were {{A|Transported}} the next {{A|Day}}, then don't trust the information that you have been given as it is most likely false. *If a {{A|Disguiser}} disguises your target, you will most likely find the person you interrogated to be "innocent". If the {{A|Disguiser}} dies or gets revealed, you may have to interrogate your previous targets again for more accurate results. *Be careful, as many evil roles tend to claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}}, so if you are pressed to claim a role, you could be hanged regardless of what you say by an aggressive {{A|Town}}. Be sure to have a well-written {{A|Last Will}} to improve your odds of survival, but there is no guarantee. *If you are certain the only roles left are [[Detection Immunity|Detection Immune]] roles, such as the {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Arsonist}}, don't give up! If people trust you, you can direct the {{A|Town}}. It is safe to not visit anyone though (unless there's a {{A|Doctor}} protecting you) because you might run into a {{A|Veteran}} who's on alert (if there's any). Alternatively, you could try and bait them into attacking you so that they waste a {{A|Night}} going for someone useless. Even if all of the above do not happen, you still count as a vote and possibly save the {{A|Town}} from being the minority. ===Identifying Fake Claims=== *{{A|Sheriff}} is very easy to claim, and as such is a suspicious claim unless confirmed. They may seem like an {{A|Executioner}} when outing your results, and many evils, such as the {{A|Werewolf}}, claim this role. It has a very easy {{A|Last Will}} to set up, and you can usually tell when someone is most likely fake when they are asked for their role, they claim {{A|Sheriff}}, and then show a {{A|Last Will}} with only innocent results. Usually, if someone out loud says something along the lines of, "Bob is suspicious!" in a blunt fashion with no evidence, and then a bunch of people start agreeing for no reason, they're all most likely evil. A {{A|Last Will}} that hasn't found an evil role by {{A|Day}} 5 is more likely an evil role themselves, although they can be an unlucky {{A|Sheriff}}. *Another way to identify fake results by a {{A|Sheriff}}, or any {{A|Town Investigative}} by any means is to look at their {{A|Last Will}}, and see if any results are unknown. If that {{A|Town Investigative}} role provided new information, it's usually a good chance that they are not evil. However, if their results are all dependent on things that the {{A|Town}} already knew, such as a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or if someone is on the stand and their {{A|Last Will}} consists entirely (or mostly) of dead people (who have had their roles revealed), such useless information is usually a sign of an evil. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{SheriffAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{SheriffMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to [[Version History (ToS)|Version 2.5.1.10655]], the {{A|Sheriff}} could differentiate between a target being a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, a member of the {{A|Coven}}, a {{A|Serial Killer}}, and a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. All of these roles now appear as "suspicious". *Prior to [[Version History (ToS)|Version 2.5.2.10840]], {{A|Sheriffs}} would receive the message "Your target is not suspicious." when interrogating an innocent target, which was replaced with more flavor text, appearing as "You cannot find evidence of wrongdoing. Your target seems innocent." as the two were easily mixed up. {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed wikitable" !Investigation Message !Possible [[Roles (ToS)|Roles]]  |- !Your target is not suspicious. | All {{A|Townies}}
