'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *Choose to attack a player each {{A|Night}}, dealing them a {{A|Basic Attack}}. *You will automatically attack any player who attempts to {{A|roleblock}} you during the {{A|Night}} along with your original intended target. Their {{A|Last Wills}} will be "bloodied" and no one will be able to read them. [[File:LastwillSK.png|thumb|A {{A|Last Will}} covered in blood by a {{A|Serial Killer}}]] **You may use your '''{{A|Cautious}}''' ability during the {{A|Night}} to instead only attack your intended target, and not attack any roleblockers who visit you. **A {{A|Janitor}} may clean blood from a bloody {{A|Last Will}}. They will receive the {{A|Last Will}} and role in this case. *You have {{A|Roleblock Immunity}} against {{A|Bootleggers}} and {{A|Tavern Keepers}} '''only'''. You will attack them and your intended target if you do not choose to be '''{{A|Cautious}}'''. If you are {{A|roleblocked}} while '''{{A|Cautious}}''', you will receive the message: ''Someone tried to role block you, but you are immune!'' **{{A|Jailors}} and {{A|Pirates}} will indirectly roleblock you, meaning you will be forced to attack them, and you cannot select a target when roleblocked by them. However, you can spare both the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Pirate}} if you use your '''{{A|Cautious}}''' ability. *You will automatically win in a 1v1 [[Victory (ToS)|stalemate]] against a {{A|Transporter}}, the {{A|Godfather}} and the {{A|Coven Leader}}. ==Strategy== As a fast-killing {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, you are a major target for all other factions due to your ability to kill. If played correctly, you can strategically eliminate any rivals in your path while staying undetected at the same time. However, any claims relating to a {{A|Serial Killer}} are usually hanged if they weren't previously revealed, and you will always be hanged quicker if other rival factions don't have a majority (e.g {{A|Town}} vs {{A|Mafia}} early or middle game) ===Dealing with accusations=== *Always try to deflect the blame off yourself onto another person so the fact that someone accused you of being {{A|Serial Killer}} is forgotten. Keep in mind that this does not always work and may even add fuel to the fire, having you hanged. *Also, be smart when trying to claim a role if you are {{A|Serial Killer}}. Look at the role list and the graveyard frequently in case someone with the role you're claiming dies, or an {{A|Investigator}} has a {{A|Last Will}} with you in it. *Whispering a confirmed {{A|Townie}} about your role and suspicions of someone can be in your favor for deception since no one else can see the whisper, other than the {{A|Blackmailer}}. The {{A|Townie}} you [[Whisper|whispered]] will likely suspect you to be an {{A|Investigator}} trying to hide from threats. If they believe there is nothing suspicious about the whisper, eventually they can be your potential ally when it comes to another {{A|Town}} accusation, which depends on your fake role claim and suspicions. However, this does not always work with more experienced players. If you think or know there is an alive {{A|Blackmailer}} be cautious about what you say, as you could be heard by one of your biggest rivals. *If somebody other than you is accused of being a {{A|Serial Killer}}, use it as an advantage. Keep them alive, and kill whoever is accusing them of being the {{A|Serial Killer}}. By doing this, the {{A|Town}} will think they are the {{A|Serial Killer}}, and go for them instead of you. However, this could backfire and people may think the {{A|Serial Killer}} is framing them. Be aware of a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Doctor}}, as they could potentially predict the {{A|Serial Killer's}} victim. *If you are suspected, write in your {{A|Death Note}} that you are the {{A|Serial Killer}}, ''but in the third person'' (e.g, "Jack is the {{A|Serial Killer}}" if your name is Jack). Point out in the chat that you are being framed. It might work, especially with less experienced players, but tends to put lots of suspicions on your back. *Another way to deflect suspicion is to say in your {{A|Death Note}} that you will kill yourself ''but in the third person'', e.g, "Jack will die toNight" if your name is Jack. Point it out; you will probably be {{A|Healed}}. If you are {{A|Jailed}}, you are best off being {{A|Cautious}} (to avoid killing the {{A|Jailor}}) and claiming you were attacked in jail unless you are certain that there is no {{A|Medium}}. *A good way to deflect suspicion is to pretend to be a {{A|Jester}}. Keep in mind this won't work in [[Classic Mode]] if both the {{A|Jester}} and {{A|Executioner}} have been killed, or if in [[Custom Mode]] or {{A|Rapid Mode}}, there are certain role settings. Along with these, a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} may just shoot/execute you instead to lower the majority vote. *A very risky strategy to play as a fake {{A|Doctor}} claim: Being {{A|Cautious}} every {{A|Night}}, not killing, Could fool the {{A|Town}} into thinking there is an {{A|Arsonist}} and making {{A|Bodyguard}} claims more suspicious. Late-game, start killing to sway votes in your favor. Doing this is very risky because {{A|Sheriffs}} interrogating you, or {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} attacking you will easily end your game. *Another way to deflect suspicion is to act like an {{A|Executioner}} and aggressively accuse one person (ideally, someone you think is actually {{A|Town}}.) This does have drawbacks: the {{A|Town}} could decide to hang you or the {{A|Jailor}} could execute you. Accidentally accusing an actual member of the {{A|Mafia}} has some benefits (the {{A|Town}} might believe you and protect you), but carries the risk that the {{A|Mafia}} will try to kill you and discover your {{A|Basic Defense}}. Also note that while ''implying'' you're an {{A|Executioner}} can help, you should avoid actively claiming to be an {{A|Executioner}} in response to an accusation. At that point, it's unlikely to help, since the {{A|Town}} has no reason not to hang an {{A|Executioner}}. You can also claim you are an {{A|Executioner}} after at least one person has died, but it works better when multiple people have died. Simply say your target was already hanged, and so you win either way, and offer to side with them by giving the {{A|Town}} an extra vote. The {{A|Mafia}} won't want to waste a kill on you, either. This might not work on experienced players, though. *Being called out for having strong {{A|defense}} is one of the most frequent ways for a {{A|Serial Killer}} to lose, so it helps to have a strategy for it. One advantage you have is that if you were hit by the {{A|Mafia}}, you'll have at least one turn to prepare before they can out you in a {{A|Death Note}}. Some important notes:[[File:Tutorial Guide.png|thumb|The promotional image for the {{A|Serial Killer}}]] **You can pretend to be an {{A|Executioner}}, but as noted above, this works best if you imply it ''before'' you're accused, and it carries a risk of being hanged. Be careful who you make your target, though, as you carry the risk of accusing the {{A|Jailor}} (who will immediately jail and kill you) or the {{A|Sheriff}} (who will interrogate you and find out you are suspicious). Successfully hanging a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral}} will also immediately solidify the fact that you are not an {{A|Executioner}}. **You can claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} and say you used your bulletproof vest. However, {{A|Survivors}} are non-{{A|Town}}, so you may simply be hanged anyway. Also, note that claiming to be a {{A|Survivor}} is commonly used, so the {{A|Town}} may not believe you. Beware of {{A|Investigators}}, {{A|Consiglieres}}, and {{A|Sheriffs}}, as they will immediately know and there is a high probability of them telling the {{A|Town}}. This also helps the {{A|Mafia}} in the case of a {{A|Consigliere}}, as the {{A|Mafia}} now has one person that the {{A|Town}} trusts. **You can claim to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} and say you used your bulletproof vest. However, you can only say this once. Also, since {{A|Bodyguard}} is a common claim for the {{A|Godfather}} and the {{A|Arsonist}}, an aggressive {{A|Town}} could hang you. **You can claim you were healed by a {{A|Doctor}} or you can claim to be a {{A|Doctor}} who self-healed. **You can claim you were {{A|Transported}} by a {{A|Transporter}}. However, since active {{A|Transporters}} are very obvious, this works only if other people have been transported, too. If you're going to do it, announce you were {{A|Transported}} as soon as the {{A|Day}} begins. **You can simply deny having been attacked in the first place. If possible, you can argue that the {{A|Mafia}} is lying in the {{A|Death Note}} and that the {{A|Mafia Killing}} might have actually been {{A|roleblocked}} or {{A|jailed}} that {{A|Night}}. **Remember, you may not be accused. If you don't, you can just play normally, but don't rush too ahead of yourself. Doing something like claiming {{A|Doctor}} and saying you healed yourself ''before'' anyone accuses you is a dead giveaway to most experienced players and can have you hanged unnecessarily. Players might ask you to heal them the following {{A|Night}}, so make sure to have some excuse. **A strategy used often in many games is to write two {{A|Last Wills}} on your own. Write one for your fake role, and one below for your real one. Claim the fake role and show the fake one for proof. *Always try to keep the accusation as quiet as possible. If it doesn't come to many {{A|Townies}}, you may be able to last longer. So if someone accuses you, try to do something like you didn't see them ask. This may cause them to start asking more and you may have to give them a claim. ===Who to kill=== Being a {{A|Serial Killer}} you have to be careful who you decide to kill each {{A|Night}}, since you don't know who a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Doctor}} might be protecting. You also want to avoid targeting the same person as the {{A|Jailor}} or other killers, which would waste your kill. Don't use any sort of order or predictable system to pick your targets, and avoid picking 'obvious' targets unless it's absolutely necessary. You could also not kill until near the end of the game to catch the {{A|Town}} off-guard. Using that strategy is risky, however, since the {{A|Town}} could figure you out. *[[Name|Names]] that seem rather normal or have a very low chance of being picked on are the best targets. *Picking victims from the middle is a good choice, as {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Sheriffs}}, and {{A|Investigators}}, sometimes go from bottom to top or top to bottom. It might depend on whether the player is good or not, but you'll hardly know that early game. *{{A|Investigators}} and {{A|Sheriffs}} tend to open the {{A|Day}} by saying things like "any leads?". Killing them first is a good strategy. However, they might be a {{A|Veteran}} trying to lure you in. If they're {{A|Mafia}} trying to blend in, however, it doesn't matter much. **As a {{A|Serial Killer}}, you sort of have a love-hate relationship with the {{A|Sheriff}}. They can easily call you out, so it might seem like a great idea to kill them off first, but remember: the {{A|Sheriff}} can also catch members of the {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Coven}} or even the {{A|Werewolf}}, all of which you need to dispose of in order to win the game. Therefore, you should always consider if it's worth killing the {{A|Sheriff}} off or not. If there are multiple undiscovered members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, you may want to allow him to live for a little longer, as long as you're not in any danger of being caught yourself. *Going off of the above, assuming you don't know any more roles, killing the first person to talk every {{A|Day}} is surprisingly effective, but {{A|Investigators}} might stay quiet until they have found a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}. Be warned this is a common strategy, so {{A|Bodyguards}}, {{A|Doctors}} or even a {{A|Lookout}} may figure it out. You can do First Person Talking, Last Person Talking to try and throw them off. Experienced players can normally pick up on patterns though. The next couple of {{A|Nights}}, you could use the same strategy to kill, and also be patient if you choose to. Being patient and unsuspecting can be extremely hard to do, as you can be suspected at any given moment when someone realizes you aren't talking, and so on. Being patient rewards you with some information about different roles, as listed below in the "How to find a role" guide. Sometimes, people would flat out say their roles or give hints which reveal who they are. *However, the most important strategy is to try to balance the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Mafia}} ratios. You should be making decisions under the assumption that the {{A|Mafia}} too wants to take care of core {{A|Town}} roles. If one faction becomes too powerful, the other will fall quickly, and so will you. You should also try to figure out how good the players are, which is a skill that will come with experience. If someone shows signs of being an unskilled {{A|Townies}} (like pushing for a random hang), keep them around. They can confuse the {{A|Town}}. On the other hand, be on the lookout for skilled players. One way to do this is by reading votes. If someone is put on the stand and hanged with very little evidence and they turn out to be innocent, target people who vote innocent or abstain. *Try to figure as many of the people's roles out, so that you know who you should kill first and find out possible {{A|Town Protective}} roles. Don't constantly ask what the roles of people are out in public, just piece together information to find out (elimination, how they are acting etc.)  ===Using your '''{{A|Cautious}}''' ability=== Unlike the {{A|Werewolf}}, your {{A|Cautious}} ability allows you to spare {{A|roleblockers}} and only attack your intended target. Do note however, that unlike other roleblock immune roles, {{A|Pirates}} will prevent you from killing your intended target and regardless if you chose to be {{A|Cautious}} or not, a {{A|Pirate}} that wins the duel will kill you and live. {{A|Jailors}} are a much more direct threat to you, so target them if you can. *{{A|Tavern Keepers}} generally pose very little threat to you even if you decide to not use your {{A|Cautious}} ability. This is because their {{A|Last Wills}} become covered in blood and are unreadable and you can use them for extra kills per {{A|Night}}. The only reason you should be using your {{A|Cautious}} ability for {{A|Tavern Keepers}} is if they announce who they're going to roleblock, are protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}, or a {{A|Medium}} exists. *{{A|Bootleggers}} are slightly more of a threat since their death from visiting you will reveal your role to the {{A|Mafia}} (since they know who the {{A|Bootlegger}} visited), in which they can draw the {{A|Town's}} attention to you (either by using {{A|Death Notes}} or public accusation) to get you hanged. Even if the {{A|Mafia}} wants to keep you alive at the moment, a {{A|Spy}} would see the {{A|Mafia}} visit on you, and you might be accused by the {{A|Town}} instead. You should keep your {{A|Cautious}} ability active if you suspect a {{A|Bootlegger}} exists, unless you're convinced that a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} changed the {{A|Bootlegger's}} target (and there is no {{A|Spy}}). *{{A|Jailors}} still pose the largest threat to you. If you are jailed, consider if it's worth attacking them, as anyone who visits you will know you were the jailed {{A|Serial Killer}}, and a {{A|Bodyguard}} protecting the {{A|Jailor}} will kill you. If you are going for the "no kill" strategy, then the {{A|Jailor}} poses a little less of a threat, since they wouldn't know that the person they jailed was the {{A|Serial Killer}}. *{{A|Pirates}} pose a considerable threat, as they can disregard your {{A|Basic Defense}} with their {{A|Powerful Attack}}. Similar to the {{A|Veteran}}, you can choose to "throw caution to the wind" and kill the {{A|Pirate}}. Unlike the {{A|Veteran}} however, you will not attack the {{A|Pirate}} if you lose the duel. You can still choose to spare the {{A|Pirate}} by going {{A|Cautious}}. ===Priority Targets=== Keep your ''priorities ''in mind. You have to think about the possibilities of which any of the threatening roles may find you. If the {{A|Town}} has been narrowed to a handful of people, it's good to keep track of which one has a bigger chance at discovering your motive. After killing the one with the bigger chance, you could continue on killing until you are met with another role that could discover you. *{{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}}: These are, by a large margin, the most serious threat you face, and eliminating them should take near-absolute priority over anything else. This is because they can cause you to lose in several ways (and these are the most common ways {{A|Serial Killers}} lose) **First, the {{A|Mafia}} can attack every {{A|Night}}, and if they hit your immunity you can be exposed at any time by the {{A|Mafia's}} {{A|Death Note}} and will probably be shortly hanged. **Second, if the {{A|Coven}} identifies you, the {{A|Coven Leader}} can use you to attack their targets for them and be a meat shield for any {{A|Bodyguards}} and {{A|Traps}}. **Third, near the end of the game, if too many members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} are left alive and will know your identity since they know their teammates, they will hang you with higher priority than the remaining {{A|Town}}. **Even if they ''don't'' know your identity, you will eventually be outed to the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} by process of elimination (since, unlike the {{A|Town}}, they automatically know their own numbers); even if other non-{{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} exist, these factions have a substantial advantage in identifying you, since they can eliminate their own members from consideration. The {{A|Consigliere}} and the {{A|Potion Master}} can also identify you directly, and do it without a trace. **On top of this, both factions have roles with immunity; you generally must get these people hanged in order to win. If you reach the late game without having eliminated the {{A|Godfather}} (and their {{A|Mafioso}}) or {{A|Coven Leader}} (once they have the {{A|Necronomicon}}), you will probably lose, draw, or be forced to rely on a kingmaker. You cannot kill these roles directly, but it is worth intentionally seeking them out when attacking, since once you've found them by hitting their immunity you can out them to the town in a {{A|Death Note}} in order to get them hanged. **For the most part, you should not intentionally leave these factions alive in hopes that they will kill the {{A|Town}} for you - this is usually a terrible idea; the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} are vastly more dangerous to you. **The only caveat is that unless the {{A|Mafia}} is about to reach a majority, killing ''one'' of them may not slow them down much, so you might prioritize other roles early on; but as a group, eliminating the {{A|Mafia}} as soon as possible is crucial to your victory and needs to be an overriding priority. ***However, be wary of not going {{A|Cautious}} when there's a {{A|Bootlegger}} afoot as their death from visiting you (signified by a bloody {{A|Last Will}}) will unambiguously reveal your role to the {{A|Mafia}}. **The {{A|Coven}} are more individually dangerous, with most of them having some way to kill or identify you, and should therefore be prioritized if you have to choose. ***The {{A|Coven}} become even more dangerous with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, since the holder of the {{A|Necronomicon}} can attack you, and will reveal your [[Attribute#Basic_Defense|Defense]], unless they are a {{A|Medusa}} (in this case, you will die). *{{A|Vampire}}: Vampires are a threat for the same reasons as the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}}, but slightly less so because they only attack (and therefore can only detect your {{A|Basic Defense}}) once a {{A|Night}}. Nonetheless, their ability to multiply and spread undetected can make them a dangerous foe later on. If you know there are multiple {{A|Vampires}}, make sure to kill them off as soon as possible. It is often in your best interest to keep any known {{A|Vampire Hunters}} alive, since they are harmless and can kill {{A|Vampires}} for you. *{{A|Jailor}}: A {{A|Jailor}} is a high priority target; they can execute you, which bypasses your Basic defense. If the {{A|Jailor}} told the {{A|Town}} the previous {{A|Day}} they would jail you, then die from you and get their {{A|Last Will}} bloodied, you will most likely die. If they are not protected by any {{A|Town Protectives}}, taking them out when not jailed should always be a priority. *{{A|Town Investigative}}, {{A|Consigliere}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}, and {{A|Blackmailer}}: A {{A|Sheriff}} could quickly call you out as suspicious, and an {{A|Investigator}} will put your name into their {{A|Last Will}} as {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Disguiser}}/{{A|Serial Killer}}/{{A|Potion Master}}, which narrows your claims, and if a known {{A|Serial Killer}} is about, especially in an uncertain role list, you may be hanged without much preparation. A {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} may witness you killing another important {{A|Townie}}, outing you with no cover if there are no other visitors. {{A|Psychics}}, although they cannot find you directly, are oftentimes immediately trusted, meaning you run the risk of being hanged if you're in their {{A|Last Will}} in an evil result. However, the {{A|Psychic}} is somewhat less dangerous if you manage to be put into a good vision; it's easy evidence to pretend you're a {{A|Town}} member, and if you're lucky enough to have a 2 evil player result you can avoid being hanged if you're last. A {{A|Consigliere}} will gladly reveal you to the {{A|Town}}, directly posing as an {{A|Investigator}} or through a {{A|Death Note}}, as it will allow them to be protected by the {{A|Town}}, believing them to be an {{A|Investigator}}. The {{A|Blackmailer}} can deduce your identity from your whispers. A {{A|Spy}} could find out that the {{A|Mafia}} visited you and you didn't die, which could hint to you having a form of [[Defense]]. The {{A|Potion Master}}, if you are either revealed or attacked, will be eager to call you out as you share their investigative results, meaning if there's an {{A|Investigator}} in the game they could potentially be hung under suspicion of being you. The {{A|Coven Leader}}, after controlling you, will also be very happy to call you out to the {{A|Town}} to gain confirmed {{A|Townie}} status if they found a better killing role, like a {{A|Werewolf}}. *Other {{A|Neutral Killings}}: They have a higher Defense value than your Attack value, so just try to be subtle when accusing them of being that role. That means not just flat out saying "This person is a {{A|Werewolf}}!". Instead, try asking for their role. If you are planning on flat out calling them out for their role, make sure to pose as a {{A|Town Investigative}} role to gain the trust of the {{A|Town}}. For an {{A|Arsonist's}} case, if you know who the {{A|Arsonist}} is, wait a {{A|Day}} after attacking to ask their role. They might be able to kill some people for you unless they want to go solo, then they might flat out reveal you. Another viable strategy is to call them out via {{A|Death Note}}, by writing that your target has defense and to hang them. *{{A|Town Protective}} roles: If any {{A|Town Investigative}} roles are revealed, they will often protect them, making you either waste an attack or possibly be killed. As long as a {{A|Town Protective}} is alive, any {{A|Town Investigative}} or posing {{A|Consigliere}}/{{A|Potion Master}} can safely call you out during the {{A|Day}} without fear of being immediately killed the next {{A|Night}}. The {{A|Trapper}} and the {{A|Bodyguard}} can take care of you directly with their protection, so go for them first. *{{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Bootleggers}}, and {{A|Pirates}}: While {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and {{A|Bootleggers}}, when not using your {{A|Cautious}} ability, cannot directly out you with their {{A|Last Will}}, {{A|Pirates}} still can and may be a threat. If you cannot side with a {{A|Pirate}}, killing them may prove to be a good choice. The {{A|Mafia}} would also know who the {{A|Bootlegger}} visited however, and can out you in a {{A|Death Note}} or {{A|Last Will}} if they can. *{{A|Vigilante}}: If they attack you, they will often tell the {{A|Town}} immediately to hang you, knowing you have a higher Defense value than their Attack value. If this happens, see above on how to deal with accusations of having a higher Defense value than an attacker's Attack value; however, the fact that they can accuse you to your face complicates things. Claiming to have been healed by a {{A|Doctor}} is even less likely to work against a {{A|Vigilante}}, since the {{A|Town}} would expect a real {{A|Doctor}} to immediately step forward and confirm your claim. If the {{A|Vigilante}} isn't confirmed, you can also couple your defense with a counter-accusation that they're {{A|Mafia}} (which may even be true). For instance, claim you're a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} who vested, then ask why they attacked you, and suggest that they may actually be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. People often don't trust unproven {{A|Vigilante}} claims, so saying they're a {{A|Mafioso}} could buy you some time. *Other {{A|Townies}}, while not nearly as dangerous as other roles, can be dangerous if they receive information (e.g. the {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Mayor}}) from more important targets. Also, their numbers contribute to hanging you once you are accused. ===Finding Certain Roles=== ====Finding {{A|Townies}}==== *{{A|Investigator}}: **They will often ask something along the lines of, "Has anyone been {{A|Transported}}?" to see if their results will be compromised or not. **They tend to send a lot of whispers (either to people who came up in a mainly {{A|Town}} result, or demanding that people with suspicious results claim a role). **The most obvious sign is when they flat out accuse someone of being a combination of any or 3 possible roles. However, note that when someone is ''obviously'' an {{A|Investigator}}, they're very likely to be protected. *{{A|Doctor}}: **Your main way of dealing with {{A|Doctors}} is to try and avoid choosing people they're likely to heal. If you need to kill one, though, look for quiet people. {{A|Doctors}} normally do their best not to reveal their role to anyone except proven or provable {{A|Townies}}, such as the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Mayor}} and {{A|Spy}}. **If you know a proven {{A|Townie}}, watch for them [[whispering]] to the {{A|Doctor}} requesting for a heal that {{A|Night}}. Do not attempt to kill them the following {{A|Night}}, as you will waste a {{A|Night}} going to kill someone when there's a {{A|Doctor}} planning to visit. *{{A|Lookout}}: **{{A|Lookouts}} will often ask questions about the less obvious visiting roles, such as whether anyone was witched or role blocked, since this helps judge who their visits are and what role they are. **At most times, they would outright say that you went to a victim's house. The {{A|Town}} would usually believe them, and you have no complete route of escape through this. However, you can kill them first once they reveal hints. **After the first {{A|Night}} or so, {{A|Lookouts}} would give away information to the {{A|Townies}} or to {{A|Investigators}}/{{A|Sheriffs}}. The usual are "Person D visited Person A." or "Person B was visited by Person G." {{A|Lookouts}} can be eliminated first, as they have a bigger chance at discovering who you killed through watching. If they have not revealed themselves, then continue to figure out the rest of the {{A|Town Investigative}} roles or stick with the strategy. ====Finding members of the {{A|Mafia}}==== *The {{A|Godfather}} has a higher Defense value than your Attack value, making them easily identifiable at {{A|Night}}, but the rest of the {{A|Mafia}} may not be so obvious. *Watch the conversations during Discussion Time, and see who is talking to who the most. *If a person is accused, and suddenly 2 or 3 people that hadn't been talking suddenly step up to his defense, that could indicate to you who the {{A|Mafia}} are, as they can be usually silent during discussion time. *If someone initiates a random hang, keep an eye on supporters. The {{A|Mafia}} usually shows up after 3 or 4 votes to make sure the person will be put on trial. However, if voting flows slowly, it's a good sign the voted person is a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. *Guilty and Innocent votes can tell a lot. {{A|Mafia}} sometimes tend to vote guilty on everyone except their own. If a known {{A|Mafia}} is about to be hung, watch to see who votes innocent or abstains. They could be {{A|Mafia}}. However, smart {{A|Mafia}} players will vote guilty to not seem suspicious. *Sometimes, you may not want to write in your {{A|Death Note}} that the {{A|Godfather}} had a higher Defense value than your Attack value until the {{A|Mafioso}} is dead. If the {{A|Godfather}} dies, the {{A|Mafioso}} will take their place, making them have a higher Defense value than your Attack value as well, which can further delay your kills. *The {{A|Ambusher}} is completely harmless to you and can be easily identified if they try to kill you. If you see them prepare an ambush while killing your target, you can place their name in your {{A|Death Note}} on the same {{A|Night}} you saw the {{A|Ambusher}} to draw the {{A|Town's}} attention to them to get them hanged. *People who talk a lot and seem to be trying too hard to act like a {{A|Townie}} could be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or another rival evil, but they could be a {{A|Jester}} or a talkative person in general. *Anyone who did not vote against a confirmed {{A|Mafia}} might be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. *Anybody who seems confident, too confident, may be the {{A|Mafia}}. They know who's doing most of the killing, so they may be overly cocky or talkative.  *Watch voting patterns. {{A|Mafia}} members may not vote at all, or will only vote {{A|Town}} and not their team. ===Dealing with Other Roles (Classic)=== *{{A|Jailor}}: When the {{A|Serial Killer}} is jailed, not executed, and not {{A|Cautious}}, they will kill the {{A|Jailor}} at the end of the {{A|Night}}. If there is an alive {{A|Medium}}, you are probably screwed, and just have to hope that they didn't have enough time to write in their {{A|Last Will}} if neither of them are AFK. *{{A|Investigator}}: Once you've been {{A|Investigated}}, you have little choice but to claim {{A|Doctor}} (you could also claim to have been {{A|Transported}}, but this is unlikely to hold up for long.) It might also help, instead of telling {{A|Town}} directly that you are a {{A|Doctor}}, to whisper it to the {{A|Investigator}} so it seems that you are trying to conceal your identity, and of course, that you are really a {{A|Doctor}}. Producing a fake {{A|Last Will}} of people you've healed can sometimes help convince people, but ultimately, anyone who claims {{A|Doctor}} has to face constant suspicion of being a Serial Killer, so it's best to avoid publicly claiming the role for as long as possible. *{{A|Sheriff}}: Many {{A|Executioners}} will claim their target to be a {{A|Serial Killer}}. You can therefore accuse the {{A|Sheriff}} of being an {{A|Executioner}}. An {{A|Investigator}} will not be able to differentiate between the two roles. If a {{A|Sheriff}} finds you, then your best bet would be to drag out the conversation so that the {{A|Day}} ends. At {{A|Night}}, your strategy may be to either take a big risk and attack them, if the {{A|Doctor}} and/or the {{A|Bodyguard}} are dead, or you can attack someone else that was supporting the {{A|Sheriff's}} argument against you, to try and weaken their defense, and hope that the {{A|Mafia}} attempts to kill the {{A|Sheriff}}. Do ''not'' claim {{A|Doctor}} when facing a {{A|Sheriff}}. It serves no purpose (a {{A|Sheriff}}, unlike an {{A|Investigator}}, can't confuse the two) and only makes you look like a panicking {{A|Serial Killer}}. Note, however, that killing the {{A|Sheriff}} or their supporters may incriminate you, since they will be known as a {{A|Townie}} when they die. *{{A|Tavern Keeper}} and {{A|Bootlegger}}: If these roles role block you, you will attack them automatically along with your intended target. This can be a problem if there is a {{A|Medium}}; {{A|Tavern Keepers}} usually will tell them. However {{A|Bootleggers}} may not (but you may still be revealed in the {{A|Mafia's}} {{A|Death Note}} the next {{A|Night}}). The basic strategies beyond that are similar to the {{A|Jailor}}. You need to convince the {{A|Town}} that they were attacked coincidentally. Note that they, like the {{A|Jailor}}, will receive a special message saying that they were killed by the person they visited. *{{A|Consigliere}}: If a {{A|Consigliere}} dies and they put your name down as the {{A|Serial Killer}}, you could be in trouble. You could claim the {{A|Consigliere}} would be lying to have {{A|Townies}} hanged, but if a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role is hanged due to the {{A|Consigliere's}} {{A|Last Will}}, you might be highly suspected. Do not claim {{A|Doctor}} after claiming the {{A|Consigliere}} lied, as you will be put under pressure by others as they attempt to coax you to reveal. *The easiest way to deal with {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Investigators}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and the {{A|Jailor}}, is to avoid coming to their attention in the first place. Try to act like {{A|Town}}: vote in reasonable ways, talk a bit but not too much, and so on. Most {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Investigators}}, {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and the {{A|Jailor}} will be focusing more on finding the {{A|Mafia}} than on you, and will be guiding their actions based on who seems the most suspicious in that regard. You want to aggressively hunt the {{A|Mafia}} in a way that averts their suspicion, without being so aggressive that you are attacked by the {{A|Mafia}} yourself (and outed as having a higher Defense value than their Attack value.) *{{A|Medium}}: If you killed a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Jailor}}, or {{A|Pirate}}, while you will leave their will unreadable, they will also know who you are, while the {{A|Bootlegger}} and {{A|Pirate}} might not out you and you can maybe claim that they are framing you, the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Tavern Keeper}} will almost certainly out you as a {{A|Serial Killer}} to the {{A|Medium}}, while it's possible to claim the {{A|Medium}} is lying, this usually will only buy you one {{A|Night}} *{{A|Witch}}: Normally this isn't a problem. {{A|Witches}} and {{A|Serial Killers}} can win together and can be an excellent team if they work together. Normally, a {{A|Witch}} will discover you are {{A|Serial Killer}} before you know who they are, so don't be alarmed if a stranger suddenly whispers to you asking you about your role. If there is a {{A|Veteran}}, however, a {{A|Witch}} sending you blindly after a target isn't the best way to stay alive. Do your best to convince the {{A|Witch}} to be on your side, before the {{A|Mafia}} convinces them. *{{A|Spy}}: Another way you can be found out is by the {{A|Spy}}. The {{A|Spy}}, while seemingly not a threat to the {{A|Serial Killer}}, can be if you are attacked by the {{A|Mafia}}, as the {{A|Spy}} will see that you were visited, and when he notices there were no {{A|Mafia}} kills and that you are not dead, he will suspect you of having a higher Defense value than the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role's Attack value. A good way to maneuver around this is to pretend to be [[Blackmailer|blackmailed.]] If you say nothing and the {{A|Spy}} thinks that you're [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]], you may buy yourself some time before the {{A|Spy}} reveals their findings to the {{A|Town}} and you are hanged. Pretending to be [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]] when attacked by the {{A|Mafia}} may also help find who the {{A|Spy}} is, as often they will often ask you (via [[whispering]]) to you something along the lines of, "What happened to you?" **However, this can backfire if the {{A|Spy}} bugged you the same Night, as they'll know you're a liar (Since they can see you getting attacked and not dying). **Your claim may be less believable if the {{A|Spy}} saw you get visited twice and/or the {{A|Random Mafia}} are confirmed as not a {{A|Blackmailer}}. *{{A|Veteran}}: A major threat to {{A|Serial Killers}} is the {{A|Veteran}} who ignores {{A|Basic Defense}} if they choose to go on alert. They should be left alone if possible. **If you and a {{A|Veteran}} are the only two players left alive, or you suspect the other is a {{A|Veteran}}, then it is often wise to wait until the last possible {{A|Night}} to kill them. They will likely waste any alerts they have left immediately after it is just you two. By waiting, you increase your chances of the {{A|Veteran}} having no alerts left. Some {{A|Veterans}} may be aware of this tactic and wait, but it is unlikely. *{{A|Mafia}}: The {{A|Mafia}} will be your major contenders in the battle for supremacy over the {{A|Town}}. The best strategy for {{A|Serial Killers}} is to remove them as quickly as possible after identifying them using the strategies above. **Taking out the {{A|Mafia}} by themselves is easy, but a {{A|Godfather}} may be trouble. **Hanging is the most efficient means, but also killers that ignore {{A|Basic Defense}} such as the {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, {{A|Jesters}}, and the {{A|Werewolf}} can effectively kill them. **If only the {{A|Godfather}} and a {{A|Serial Killer}} remain alive, the {{A|Serial Killer}} will win, so keeping to the shadows and deception is your best bet when dealing with the {{A|Mafia}}. *{{A|Arsonist}}: The {{A|Arsonist}} is able to kill targets with {{A|Basic Defense}}. This makes {{A|Serial Killer}} and {{A|Arsonists}} natural enemies, despite their similar neutral views on the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Mafia}}. {{A|Arsonists}} should be eliminated early on using whatever method works best since they will win if only a {{A|Serial Killer}} and an {{A|Arsonist}} are alive. *{{A|Neutral}}: Although it can be risky, if you can ally yourself with a {{A|Survivor}} or a {{A|Witch}} (as above), they can give you the support of a regular team of {{A|Mafia}}. The {{A|Witch}} can throw the {{A|Town}} off, and the {{A|Survivor}} can do as they please, then near the end of the game vote for you only, giving you the win. However, some {{A|Survivor}} want to win with the {{A|Town}} or the {{A|Mafia}}, and when you whisper them to help you, they might flat out reveal you to gain trust and not be killed, as considering you most likely don't have a team they are safe in calling you out. *{{A|Werewolf}}: Like the {{A|Arsonist}}, the {{A|Werewolf}} is able to ignore {{A|Basic Defense}}. On non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}, you are safe from them, but on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, you are in danger. Either the {{A|Werewolf}} could attack you directly, or you could visit someone who was attacked directly, so you are in trouble no matter what you do. If you find a target with a higher Defense value than your Attack value when there is an active {{A|Werewolf}}, mention it in your {{A|Death Note}} and accuse them. They can be another role with {{A|Basic Defense}}, however. ==={{A|Death Note}}=== The {{A|Serial Killer}} is a role that has enormous power in shaping how the game is played. Your {{A|Death Note}} can be an important way to communicate with other players anonymously, because the {{A|Serial Killer's}} {{A|Death Note}} is never taken lightly. After finding an immune role, you can put their name in your {{A|Death Note}}. *A simple usage of your {{A|Death Note}} is to tell the {{A|Town}} that you're going to kill a certain player, so if any {{A|Town Protective}} roles are alive, they will target them instead of your target. However, experienced players might see the double bluff, leave them alone, and go for someone else instead. Saying things that can relate to your "target" in your {{A|Death Note}}, however, can bring the {{A|Town Protectives}} to actually go for that person. *Write the names of the people who you found to have a higher Defense value than your Attack value, so the {{A|Town}} suspects them. More advanced players can write down names of random {{A|Townies}} and claim that they have a higher Defense value than their Attack value, but this needs to be done carefully. **Also, if you suspect one of your targets to be healed, you could write in your {{A|Death Note}} that they had a higher Defense value than your Attack value. Then, claiming that they were healed by a {{A|Doctor}} could have them hanged by more experienced players. However, if the {{A|Doctor}} speaks up and says they healed said target that "had a higher Defense value than your Attack value", your target will most likely be acquitted and give the {{A|Town}} another person to trust. **This should not be done immediately if there are multiple {{A|Serial Killers}}, as you can end up killing someone you are allied with. *If you're in All Any, or another mode where there can be multiple {{A|Serial Killers}}, you can communicate with other {{A|Serial Killers}} in your {{A|Death Note}}. This is helpful if it is very late in the game with multiple people claiming {{A|Serial Killer}} when there are only two confirmed {{A|Serial Killers}}, or for coordinating kills.  **If you're attacked and another {{A|Serial Killer}} has seemingly missed a kill (or only killed a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}/{{A|Bootlegger}} who {{A|Roleblocked}}] them), state that they attacked you in your {{A|Death Note}} to make it clear to the other {{A|Serial Killer}} that you're the {{A|Serial Killer}} they attacked. ===Concerning {{A|Doctor}} Claims=== As the game becomes more advanced along with the players, it is harder to run away with claiming {{A|Doctor}} as a {{A|Serial Killer}}. If you do plan on claiming {{A|Doctor}} and you are attacked at {{A|Night}} (especially {{A|Night}} 1), claiming to have been {{A|Transported}} might work well for you. Also, try to let the {{A|Mafia}} live for a little while, especially if there is too much {{A|Town}} for you to kill alone. In general, you may talk a lot and distract people's attention to finding {{A|Mafia}} or other {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles. Above all else, ''avoid claiming to be a {{A|Doctor}} unnecessarily''. Real {{A|Doctors}} are reluctant to reveal, both because they're such high-priority targets, and because they know they have no way to confirm even if they wanted to. If you seem unduly eager to tell the {{A|Town}} that you're a {{A|Doctor}}, it will likely have you hanged. Also, do not claim {{A|Doctor}} in a game with a confirmed {{A|Poisoner}}, or people will start becoming suspicious when people are claiming to be poisoned and dying to poison. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{SerialKillerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{SerialKillerMessages}} ==Trivia== [[File:Screenshot_2020-05-11_at_2.39.52_PM.png|thumb|When the {{A|Jailor}} killed the {{A|Serial Killer}}. (720p)]] * Prior to {{VH|Version 2.5.3.1095}}, an executed {{A|Serial Killer}} would still receive a message regarding them attacking the {{A|Jailor}}. The {{A|Jailor}} would not receive a message stating that they were attacked from jailing a {{A|Serial Killer}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.5}}, {{A|Serial Killers}} did not have a {{A|Cautious}} ability, and were always forced to attack any players who roleblocked them. **Also prior to this version, {{A|Last Wills}} would not be bloodified when killing someone because of {{A|Roleblocking}} you. *In the now-removed [[Tutorial]], you were guided by a {{A|Serial Killer}}, and your first role was the {{A|Serial Killer}}. *In the Achievements list, the {{A|Serial Killer's}} role color is incorrect. This is likely a bug. *If you win a duel against a {{A|Pirate}}, you will see a message that tells you you attacked the {{A|Pirate}}: "You attacked the {{A|Pirate}} for {{A|Roleblocking}} you. The scallywag!" *The {{A|Serial Killer}} is the only {{A|Neutral Killing}} role that deals {{A|Basic Attacks}}. *The {{A|Serial Killer}} is the only role in the game that is seen as ''suspicious'' at '''ALL''' points in the game. **This means that unlike the {{A|Mafia}} (who can be {{A|disguised}} as an ''innocent role'' or be the {{A|Godfather}}), the {{A|Coven}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}}), or the {{A|Werewolf}} (on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}); the {{A|Serial Killer}} will always be seen as ''suspicious'' to a {{A|Sheriff}}. **As a {{A|Serial Killer}}, the '''only''' way to be seen as ''innocent'' to a {{A|Sheriff}} without being {{A|transported}} is if a {{A|Disguiser}} was {{A|controlled}} into you while trying to {{A|disguise}} a {{A|Mafia}} member as an ''innocent role'', which is extremely rare. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.6}} **Fixed incorrect color on killed by {{A|Serial Killer}} announcement. *{{VH|3.3.3}} **The [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom]] Lobby role summary for {{A|Serial Killer}} has been updated to mention their {{A|Cautious}} ability. *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Janitors}} can now read Bloody {{A|Last Wills}} from their {{A|Cleaned}} victims. **{{A|Cautious}} button will no longer activate for interaction at {{A|Night}} if the {{A|Serial Killer}} is dead. *{{VH|3.2.6}} **{{A|Cautious}} ability will no longer activate at {{A|Night}} if the {{A|Serial Killer}} is dead. *{{VH|3.2.5}} **The {{A|Serial Killer}} now attacks their intended target along with any players who {{A|Roleblock}} them (excluding {{A|Jailors}} and {{A|Pirates}}). **Added "{{A|Cautious}}" ability. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Lightened the hue of the {{A|Serial Killer}} blue role color. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Serial Killer's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Serial Killer.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Serial Killer's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Serial Killer Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.3.10958}} **Fixed a bug where a {{A|Serial Killer}} who has been executed by a {{A|Jailor}} would still see a message regarding them attacking the {{A|Jailor}}. *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **Attackers will now get "Your target is immune" message when attacking {{A|Werewolf}} on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Серийный Убийца]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Killing roles]] [[Category:Last Will modifiers]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |mustkill=Yourself (via [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging|hanging]]) }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You win if you are [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging|hanged]] during the {{A|Day}}, and you can ''only'' win by doing so. Upon being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging|hanged]], all players in the game (including the {{A|Jester}}) will see the message "''The jester will get his revenge from the grave!". **This means if you are killed during the {{A|Night}} (any way other than by [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging (ToS)|hanging]]), you automatically lose the game. **If you survive until the end of the game, you lose. **If you leave, you will always lose, even if you completed your win condition. *You can choose to haunt one of your guilty or abstaining voters the {{A|Night}} after being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging|hanged]]. **If you do not choose anyone or deselect your target, the game will randomly choose among the guilty and/or abstaining voters. You cannot haunt someone else the next {{A|Night}}. **Your haunt ignores all forms of {{A|Defense}} except {{A|Invincible Defense}}, meaning all {{A|Town Protective}} roles, {{A|Jailors}}, {{A|Guardian Angels}}, and the {{A|Potion Master}} cannot prevent your haunt. ***The only role in the game being able to survive your haunt is {{A|Pestilence}}. You will not receive a message stating that {{A|Pestilence}} survived your haunt. **Your haunt is not affected by {{A|Transporters}}. You will always {{A|attack}} your target (if you choose one). **If you leave the game before choosing a target or before the {{A|Night}} ends, no one will be haunted. *The stalemate detector will not end the game on the {{A|Day}} you are [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging|hanged]], since you can break any stalemate by your haunt. ==Strategy== *The {{A|Jester}} can be a fun role to play as, trying to deceive the {{A|Town}} to hang you and being able to hurt them in revenge. However, it is still a violation of the rules to abuse the chat by spamming or acting unsportsmanlike to be hanged, and this can result in punishment, such as a ban. **Making various people angry is a common strategy. However, it has to be done carefully in order to make people hang you, whether or not they believe you are a {{A|Jester}}. **Contrary to popular belief, being rude or obnoxious in chat does not help your chances of being hanged. Most of the time, you'll end up either being killed at {{A|Night}}, reported, and/or ignored. What's more, it's possible people will determine you are a {{A|Jester}} based on these actions, and you'll lose. *As a {{A|Jester}}, the greatest threats to you are usually the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Vigilantes}}. You want to try to look suspicious such that you'll be voted for and hanged, but if those roles determine you're not a {{A|Townie}}, they can attack and kill you at {{A|Night}}, denying your {{V|Victory}}. The easiest way to minimize this risk is to try and be hanged the same {{A|Day}} you make yourself look suspicious. However, if you can't do that, you'll have to strike a balancing act between setting up later suspicions that will have you hanged, but not looking so suspicious that the {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} kill you the next {{A|Night}}. **When pursuing strategies that take longer than a single {{A|Day}}, you should have a plan ready in case you are {{A|Jailed}} - an explanation you can give to the {{A|Jailor}} for the way you've been behaving that way will make you look like a {{A|Townie}}, ideally coupled with a fake {{A|Last Will}}. A decent claim is {{A|Veteran}}, as they can also act loud or annoying if they are baiting. It is theoretically possible to confess to being a {{A|Jester}} and try to side with them, but most {{A|Jailors}} will execute {{A|Jester}} claims without hesitation. **Another possibility is to start this strategy on a {{A|Day}} where the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} thinks another player is a {{A|Jester}}, or is choosing to kill another player at {{A|Night}} for any reason. This way, you'll probably be safe for that {{A|Night}}, since those killing roles will be occupied. *Stay normal, do not be too contributive or you will end up killed by the {{A|Mafia}}. Do not be too suspicious or you will be shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} or executed by the {{A|Jailor}}. *Especially in {{A|Ranked}} and [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Ranked_Practice|Ranked Practice]], just stay silent like a normal evil and do what you would do and pretend to be a {{A|Townie}}. The {{A|Town}} will at some point eliminate people who are not {{A|Townies}}, including you, which not many players can defend against. Just play along and let them figure out that you are not a {{A|Townie}}, and they will most likely hang you. **In contrast, one of the best things that can happen to you is being {{A|Jailed}} on {{A|Night 1}} or when the {{A|Jailor}} has no executions left. Pretending to be AFK (away from keyboard), and then claiming in chat that you didn't think you were going to be {{A|Jailed}} on {{A|Night 1}} will cast a lot of suspicion on yourself. *Timing is tricky for the {{A|Jester}}: **The longer you wait before you begin raising suspicion against you, the more likely you are to be hanged. The {{A|Town}} is generally more desperate near the end and may be more likely to hang people without concrete evidence, especially if the {{A|Investigator}} is dead. There are also fewer people to trick, making it easier to have the necessary votes to be put on trial. If you wait quite a bit, people can also become desperate to all vote guilty so that you can kill one, like if there's 3 immune roles all on a different side. ***On the other hand, the longer you wait, the more likely you are to be killed at {{A|Night}} or to have information about you revealed by a {{A|Witch}}, {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Investigator}}, or {{A|Consigliere}}/{{A|Potion Master}}, limiting your options. **Remember that if the game ends while you're still alive, you lose. Therefore, while you want to be hanged as quickly as possible, you also want to avoid doing anything that could bring the game to an end. You should generally avoid voting people up unless you think it will help you be hanged. Additionally, voting up (or voting guilty on) a member of the {{A|Mafia}} will make the {{A|Town}} less likely to suspect you of being a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, making it harder for you to be hanged; even worse, it makes the {{A|Mafia}} more likely to kill you at Night. *If a {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Coven Leader}} find you, they may leave you alone, or try to help you: **If a {{A|Witch}} has also found the {{A|Mafia}} and has communication with them, they may control you to visit a target that the {{A|Mafia}} killed to make you look suspicious if a {{A|Lookout}} spots you. **A {{A|Coven Leader}} can also do the same, but it is easier for them since they have a [[Factions (ToS)|faction]]. They can control you into the target of a {{A|Potion Master}} or {{A|Poisoner}}. This applies with {{A|Trackers}} too in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *Contrary to the aim of being a {{A|Jester}}, pretending to defend yourself can make you appear as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}}. If you claim to be a {{A|Lookout}} and the real {{A|Lookout}} calls you out, continue to try and defend your claim, which can make people hang you anyway, under the logic of "If you are really the {{A|Lookout}}, hang the other player tomorrow". It is normally your best bet to defend your claim, but never actually give any evidence and instead just say the {{A|Town}} is dumb for hanging you. This can make the {{A|Town}} angry by defending your claim without providing any actual evidence. **The inverse also works, by claiming a role that a {{A|Townie}} has claimed while on trial. When they are revealed to actually be that role via hanging, the {{A|Town}} will very likely hang you the next {{A|Day}}, out of bitterness. This will almost always work, unless an {{A|Investigator}} identifies you as a {{A|Jester}} during the {{A|Night}} and survives to report it the next {{A|Day}}. However, you also run the risk of being shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} or executed by the {{A|Jailor}}. *If you mess up as a {{A|Jester}}, it can be very difficult to gain your win, as {{A|Investigators}} will likely try to investigate you, and a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} may kill you. When you ''do'' think you've been investigated, your options vary based on who investigated you; if it was a {{A|Sheriff}}, you need to seem to be a role with [[Detection Immunity]] (such as an {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Witch}}, {{A|Vampire}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or perhaps a {{A|Werewolf}} if the {{A|Sheriff}} interrogated you on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}). If it was an {{A|Investigator}}, you'll need to try and pass as a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Hex Master}}, or {{A|Vampire}}, unless you can convince the {{A|Investigator}} that you were {{A|framed}}/{{A|hexed}} and are a {{A|Neutral}} role that will pose a threat to {{A|Town}}. *If you end up on the stand, but aren't sure you'll be hanged, try acting angry or frustrated. A good way to accomplish this is by swearing in chat. *A good claim for {{A|jester}} would be {{A|mayor}} as people would likely want you to reveal yourself to prove it. You can use this strategy during early game and people will suspect you as you can’t prove your claim. As stated above, keep trying to back up your claim without ‘revealing’ yourself. You can have yourself hanged very early for this, but it is good to remember that {{A|Town Killings}} may kill you during the {{A|Night}} instead and hang someone else that is suspicious during the {{A|Day}}. *If you are {{A|Framed}}/{{A|Hexed}}, use it to your advantage. The {{A|Sheriff}} will see you as suspicious. It doesn't help you if an {{A|Investigator}} investigates you, since you are in the {{A|Framer}} and {{A|Hex Master's}} investigation result anyway. *If you think you are {{A|doused}}, use it to your advantage. The {{A|Investigator}} will see you as a ''{{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or {{A|Crusader}}'', and the {{A|Consigliere}} will see you as an {{A|Arsonist}}. If there is a known {{A|Arsonist}} in your game, claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} could put a good amount of suspicion on you during the {{A|Day}}. *If you are lucky enough to be at the gallows, try to play dumb, but not making it obvious that you're aiming for suicide. Try claiming a role from a dead {{A|Townie}} and give false information. This could help, but could also ruin your chance if you fail. *If you are an {{A|Executioner}} and know that there is a high chance of your target being killed at {{A|Night}} (such as if all the {{A|Town Protective}} roles are dead), try to have somebody to attack you. Hopefully, you will turn into a {{A|Jester}} and the attacker's {{A|Death Note}} will reveal your Basic defense. This could be your key to victory. *Claiming to be an {{A|Executioner}} is a terrible strategy. {{A|Executioners}} get ignored by the town, shot by Vigilantes or executed in Jail. Worst of all, you may get "lucky" and find a real evil, turning you into a "confirmed Townie" - cursed to never get hanged. *Remember that as a {{A|Jester}}, you want to appear to be an evil role ''trying'' to appear to be a {{A|Townie}} (but who makes one or two mistakes that could have you hanged). Alternatively, nobody would waste their {{A|Night}} visiting you as well as nobody wanting to vote you up, basically leaving you alone. *Many strategies for the {{A|Jester}} depend on claiming a role. However, claiming a suspicious role out of the blue can make you look like a {{A|Jester}}. Evil roles are rarely eager to make a fake claim, since it exposes them to being disproved. Therefore, you need to create a situation where claiming your fake role makes sense. One option is simply to call for a role-call, and hesitate before "revealing" your fake role claim when people ask you to claim first. *An interesting tactic is to claim that you are an evil role, and that you hate it. This works especially well when {{A|Death Notes}} that have been revealed hint at disliking that role, or if a {{A|Death Note}} hints at greatly disliking the player killed, saying something along the lines of, "They deserved to die." which almost always arouses suspicion. In most scenarios, {{A|Death Notes}} are often a bit troll-y, and show a bit of personality. A good tactic is trying to mimic the personality revealed in the {{A|Death Note}}, or use snip-its of the {{A|Death Notes}}, arousing suspicion about why you said the same thing. Similarly, if a {{A|Death Note}} is simply using emoticons (such as :), =), xP, :/), try using whatever repeated emoticon they used as often as possible (without spamming, of course). Such cases where the {{A|Death Note}} accompanies your plan, however, are rare to come by, in addition to the tactic being almost always useless against more experienced players, so don't always rely on it. *In a game with only one {{A|Neutral Evil}} slot, you can claim to have been controlled {{A|Night 1}}. "Controlled" claims tend to be believed by even relatively experienced players. Be aware that, however, if there are no other claims of being controlled as the game continues, experienced players would be more suspicious of you being a {{A|Jester}}. *If an {{A|Arsonist}} is in the game, and you have been questioned, it would be a good idea to claim a role that fits in the {{A|Arsonist}} result, such as a {{A|Bodyguard}}. You will most likely be hanged right off the bat. The same applies for claiming {{A|Doctor}} with a {{A|Serial Killer}} in game. *If you are considering making a play, make sure the {{A|Town}} has no other leads before you try to be hanged. If the {{A|Town}} has other leads, they may focus on someone else and not you. Being the center of attention is important, but don't make it too obvious. **Adding on to this, if you make a move too early in the {{A|Day}}, it increases the chance of people realizing that you're {{A|Jester}}, but if you wait too long, the {{A|Town}} won't have enough time to vote. *There is a risky way to be hanged that could either have you imminently hanged or almost forever disbelieved. You could on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}} claim to be {{A|Sheriff}} and that you JUST interrogated someone the {{A|Night}} before (A.K.A. on the non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}) and that they are a {{A|Werewolf}}. Half the time they will say something like "That's not how {{A|Sheriff}} works" and that's how you know you did it, but other times they will call you out as an {{A|Executioner}}. If you're going to do this try doing it {{A|Day 2}} since it will be even less believable. *If you are {{A|Jailed}}, you should make a plausible-sounding claim (since you don't want to be executed), but one that will put you in trouble after the {{A|Jailor}} dies. Any [[Unique Role|unique role]] is good for this tactic, especially {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Mayor}}. **If you are {{A|Jailed}} ''after'' making a play to be hanged - that is, after making yourself appear evil - your situation is trickier. In this case, you have to come up with some sort of explanation for your actions that makes you look like a {{A|Townie}}. If you claimed an implausible but powerful {{A|Town}} role (ie. saying that you were a {{A|Jailor}} yourself), saying that you're actually a {{A|Veteran}} trying to bait people sometimes works. **You should only tell the {{A|Jailor}} that you are a {{A|Jester}} if you know they've lost their executions. You can also do this if you are certain their situation is so desperate, that they'll be willing to try and work with you to trick the {{A|Mafia}} or other enemies of the {{A|Town}} into hanging you. **If the {{A|Jailor}} ''has'' lost their executions (or run out of them), and the {{A|Town}} is at risk of losing their majority, it's usually safe to confess to them and offer to work with them; just ask who they want you to haunt and most will be willing to help you have hanged in hopes of salvaging a victory. This strategy is considerably more risky with a {{A|Vigilante}} in the game. ***Note that, from a moral standpoint, {{A|Neutral Evils}} should never side with the {{A|Town}} unless they risk to lose the game. The objective of a {{A|Neutral Evil}} is to damage the {{A|Town}} as much as possible, and thus they should not side with the {{A|Town}} unless their win is in jeopardy. ===Chat=== ====Make a "mistake"==== *Many strategies for the {{A|Jester}} rely on acting like an evil role who makes a mistake of some sort, such as claiming {{A|Investigator}} and listing an exact role (which makes you look like a {{A|Consigliere}}), similarly, you could accuse some one of being a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role and post the {{A|Consigliere's}} result. You can also make up a random result yourself (such as {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Survivor}}) if you truly want to look like a {{A|Consigliere}}. *To pull off this kind of strategy successfully, your "mistake" has to be suitable for your level of play; for example, in {{A|Classic Mode}}, it might make sense to claim a role that doesn't exist (which a very new player might make), whereas in {{A|Ranked}}, it needs to be a mistake that even relatively experienced players might make. If your mistake is too implausible, you'll be spotted as a {{A|Jester}}, whereas if it's too sophisticated, the other players might not notice it. ====Use an older version of the game==== *Sometimes {{A|Jesters}} are hanged for saying things like "Thomas Danforth appeared as {{A|Mafia}} to me! I'm {{A|Sheriff}}!" This could still backfire, especially in {{A|Ranked}} games, as they already expect for you to have the [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]], as it is very easy to achieve. *This applies to claiming {{A|doused}} as well, as only {{A|Arsonists}} can see whether they were {{A|doused}}. **Keep in mind these updates happened a long, long while ago, and most {{A|Townies}} may recognize this strategy and reveal you as a {{A|Jester}}. ====“# is dying on {{A|Night 1}}” or “# will die the next {{A|Night}}”==== *A tactic that seems to work sometimes is to claim a specific player is dying on the first {{A|Night}}. This rarely works with more experienced players, mostly because the {{A|Mafia}} will be reluctant to go after an obviously named target due to fear of running into {{A|Town Protective}} roles. *You can also try and ask for roles by [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]], and if the player doesn't reveal their role, tell them that they are going to die the next {{A|Night}}. This has a chance to lead the [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispered]] {{A|Townie}} to freak out and call you out. However, this strategy is very risky to use, as you can become a target of the {{A|Investigator}}. ====Failed Whisper==== *Another strategy is to make it seem like you're [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] to someone. Only {{A|Blackmailers}} can see others' [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] - this may cause them to assume you are a {{A|Blackmailer}} and push to hang you. ====# is immune==== *Claim someone has Basic/Powerful defense and accuse them. People will wonder how you "knew" that they had Basic/Powerful defense and hang you. It would help to claim being a {{A|Vigilante}} when there is no chance of one being alive, or in-game. If it's {{A|Day 2}}, you can say that you shot them last {{A|Night}} (since {{A|Vigilantes}} can't shoot on {{A|Night 1}}). Alternatively, even when a {{A|Vigilante}} is a theoretically plausible claim, you'll often come under suspicion if there was no credible reason for you to shoot your target. This may lead players to the conclusion that you are the {{A|Jester}}, however. ====Claim a {{A|Neutral Benign}} role==== *Claim that you are a {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Amnesiac}} and maintain that claim throughout the game. The earlier you claim it, the better; even if it is as early as {{A|Day 1}}. Without conclusive evidence or any leads, the {{A|Town}} is likely to hang you, especially if you claim {{A|Survivor}}, since you are everyone's ally. This is even more helpful if a {{A|Neutral Benign}} role dies or a real {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers their role. The only flaw in this is aggressive {{A|Jailors}} and {{A|Vigilantes}}, or an {{A|Investigator}} who discovers you are the {{A|Jester}} (you can claim {{A|Framed}}/{{A|Hexed}} in this case). This tactic only works in non-Classic queues, as {{A|Neutral Benign}} roles are no longer in Classic queues. *Another great strategy, specially in chaos gamemodes, is to claim {{A|Guardian Angel}} right at the beginning of the game, whisper to someone at random pretending to be their {{A|Guardian Angel}} and simply wait. Killing roles won't want to kill you since they gain nothing by killing a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, because they can protect even when dead, and as time passes the {{A|Town}} will grow suspicious of you as real {{A|Guardian Angels}} tend to protect as early as they can to confirm themselves. If the person you whispered dies even better because they will most likely have typed in their will that you claimed to be their {{A|Guardian Angel}} and asked for protection but died anyways. ====Act like an evil role's ally==== *If an evil role (especially a member of the {{A|Mafia}}) is discovered, give a flawed explanation as to why the player is innocent. Vote innocent on them if they are put on trial, and if the role is killed, stay quiet. If the evil role does manage to survive, tell them that you are the {{A|Jester}} and that you are on their side. The {{A|Town}} can detect you as a {{A|Jester}} if you act overly suspicious, so use this within reason. *Also, if you act like the {{A|Mafia's}} ally, the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles are more likely to keep you alive, to transfer suspicion from them to you. ====Obviously fake {{A|Last Will}}==== *A few {{A|Nights}} in advance, Write a fake "{{A|Last Will}}" that seems like a certain role could have written it. However, make sure the {{A|Last Will}} has loopholes in it. Some examples are: **Writing the {{A|Last Will}} one {{A|Night}} ahead - If it is {{A|Day 5}}, write a {{A|Last Will}} that goes up to {{A|Night 6}}. **Impossible mechanic - Claim you shot someone as a {{A|Vigilante}} on {{A|Night 1}}, give an investigation result that is not possible, (such as {{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Retributionist}}/{{A|Sheriff}}) **Suspicious visits - Whenever someone is killed, write in your {{A|Last Will}} you visited the victim that same {{A|Night}}. This works amazingly well if you claim to be a {{A|Doctor}} and write that you "visited" the victims of a {{A|Serial Killer}}. **False information - Give false investigation results about players who are still alive. Since your "targets" receive messages if they were [[role blocked]]/{{A|Transported}}, they will call you out for lying. ***Claiming {{A|Escort}} is a more obvious {{A|Jester}} play, because everyone knows that it has been renamed to {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. **Typed {{A|Last Will}} - Write a {{A|Last Will}} that looks like it was hastily typed. You may also claim that you are playing on a Mobile device, therefore not being able to copy & paste. *Once you have your {{A|Last Will}}, use another strategy to make yourself suspicious, and hopefully place yourself on trial. To paste: hold Cmd+V) ===={{A|Mafia}} having the Majority==== *Being quiet the whole game and saying something on the lines of, "Alright, the {{A|Mafia}} has the majority, let's hang [name]" when the {{A|Town}} has a slight majority or when a {{A|Mayor}} exists can have you hanged. **This can also work if neither side has majority and you suspect there is an unrevealed {{A|Mayor}}. Chances are the {{A|Mayor}} will reveal themselves and hang you. **This also applies to {{A|Vampires}} and {{A|Coven}}. ====[[Unique Role|Unique role]]==== *A great strategy is claiming a [[Unique Role|unique role]] or a role that cannot possibly be alive. Try not to be too obvious by claiming to be a {{A|Mayor}} or sometimes a {{A|Jailor}}, and you will only have to say it once early on. Later, when more roles die, the {{A|Town}} may remember your suspicious claim and hang you. However, claiming a [[Unique Role|unique role]] may end up with your death at the hands of an evil or end up causing the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot you if you aren't hanged after the {{A|Town}} sees your mistake. Use this strategy with caution. *Claiming a role such as a {{A|Retributionist}} is a good idea, as it can be hard to fully confirm yourself, and if purposefully mess up your will, you may be hanged. Claiming {{A|Veteran}} is also good, especially if it is not confirmed that there is a {{A|Veteran}} in the game. As said above, however, you must use this strategy carefully. *Claiming a [[Unique Role|unique role]] that is ''definitely'' in the game (such as claiming {{A|Veteran}} after people have died to a {{A|Veteran}}) can also work well, since it can bait the real one into counter-claiming you and having you hanged. *If you do plan to claim to be the {{A|Mayor}}, you would normally want to be hanged that {{A|Day}}, or killing roles would usually attack you, granting you a loss. Normally, claiming to be a {{A|Mayor}} and asking people to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] their roles to you is an effective strategy to have yourself hanged, especially if they suspect you are an evil role. They will suspect you, asking for you to "reveal yourself". At this point, you must tread carefully, because if you slip up and be too obvious, they will not hang you. ====Accusing a known {{A|Town Investigative}} role==== *Accusing a known {{A|Town Investigative}} role is a quick way to be hanged. Most people will listen to the {{A|Investigator's}} word over yours, and you will be hanged. ====Accusing a dead player==== *Accusing a dead player puts suspicion on you, especially if you format yourself to appear like a {{A|Consigliere}} by accusing somebody based off of investigation results alone. ====Fake {{A|Executioner}}==== *If you've never played like an {{A|Executioner}} as {{A|Jester}}, then you're in for some fun. Claim things like {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Investigator}}, or {{A|Lookout}} and then push on somebody, which can make you seem like an {{A|Executioner}}. Most of the time the player you are targeting will be hanged. Since it's so common for an {{A|Executioner}} to announce their triumph, this may cast suspicion onto you. Saying things such as: "oops" or "def framed guys". *This tactic is very risky, but if you are in a game without a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}}, then it is quite safe, as you may be hanged the next {{A|Day}}. ====# has revealed themselves as the {{A|Mayor}}!==== *By typing, "has revealed themselves as the {{A|Mayor}}!" may make people suspect you of being an evil role pretending to be {{A|Mayor}} and hang you. However, this tactic could be seen as a joke or obvious {{A|Jester}} behavior due to the obvious coloring of the letters when the {{A|Mayor}} reveals. As such, this tactic should be only be used in special situations where the players are inexperienced, but not inexperienced enough to fall for this, or if another {{A|Jester}} is dead. This should only be attempted if you are sure you can run away with it, otherwise it will confirm you as a {{A|Jester}} without a doubt, and you could be seeing a {{A|Jailor's}} execution or a {{A|Vigilante's}} bullet soon. Also, the real {{A|Mayor}} may still use this strategy to act like a {{A|Jester}}, so this strategy may not let you be hanged at all. ====Keep [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]]==== *Constant whispering tends to attract attention; [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] with someone and then being evasive about what you were saying can sometimes have you hanged. Try to constantly [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] with one player, further increasing suspicions. Be careful, however, as you may be accidentally [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] to a killing role who wants to go unnoticed. *However, this carries a risk of being killed by the {{A|Mafia}}, who may assume you're an {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Spy}} talking to someone you've confirmed as a {{A|Townie}}. ====Acting inexperienced==== *If you act inexperienced, you can ask for help on some aspect of the game that makes you appear to be an evil role. For instance: **You can ask what the "[[Death Note (ToS)|bloody note]]" is, which is by your {{A|Last Will}}, and claim you've never seen it before. **Similarly, you can act confused about your role and ask how to play it, implying that you are an evil role. **Or you can ask about the people who talk at {{A|Night}}, implying you're a member of the {{A|Mafia}} confused by seeing the {{A|Mafia}} chat. **Claiming {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} without anyone asking you may make you appear to be an inexperienced {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}}. **You can also say "I think I killed #, is that what clicking on the buttons next to their name does?" **You can pretend to not know how to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]]. However, this will only work if you be obnoxious about it, otherwise people will assume you are inexperienced. ***While using this strategy, don't whisper unless told how to do so. Most beginners don't know how to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]]. *Note that these strategies are only likely to work in {{A|Classic Mode}}. For example, playing this strategy in {{A|Ranked}} will almost certainly result in you being called out as {{A|Jester}}. ====I was {{A|Doused}}==== *If there is an {{A|Arsonist}} in the game it might be wise to say you were {{A|doused}}. You could easily be called out as a bad {{A|Jester}}, though, as an update that removed players being able to see if they are doused and this might make you appear as if you are trying to trick newer players to veterans. ====Staying silent, misspelling "I am [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]]."==== *During the {{A|Day}}, don't say anything.
