For example, "I am Blackmailed/I am blackmailed,/I got bm'd/vI am blackmailed (the v is there as if it is copy pasting), or saying it more than once. Make sure to type it without the period. Once somebody sees the error, you will almost definitely be hanged as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} trying to fake your way out of punishment. Works best if someone else seems like they are [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]], since it will make the {{A|Town}} more suspicious. ====Saying suspicious messages==== *If the {{A|Town}} is in a very bad state, you can offer to start "random hanging". This can bring heavy suspicion on you, and the remaining {{A|Town}} will want to have you hanged. The {{A|Mafia}} will also know that you're not in the {{A|Mafia}} and think you're a {{A|Neutral}} role against them desperately attempting to prevent them from gaining majority, and they will vote guilty. ====Claiming you were attacked==== *Evil roles with Basic defense usually give some explaining on as to how they survived an attack. Therefore, on a {{A|Night}} evil roles failed to kill, you could claim you were attacked but survived. Most likely, the {{A|Town}} will ask how you survived, allowing you to claim that you vested as a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Survivor}}, or you could claim you self healed as a {{A|Doctor}}. If you play it poorly, you might be hanged. The downside is a {{A|Spy}} can ''easily'' disprove the {{A|Mafia}} attacked you, or if no {{A|Neutral Killing}} exist or are alive, and you may be avoided instead. ====Be annoying==== *Another {{A|Jester}} strategy is to be annoying. However, do not spam the chat or be mean to people, as this will usually result in you being ignored, reported, or killed at {{A|Night}}. *Claiming to be new, by asking, "WHAT DOES THE BLOODY/RED/OTHER NOTE DO?" each {{A|Day}} in chat, "OH GOD, I THINK I KILLED #, IS THAT WHAT CLICKING ON THE BUTTON BESIDE THEIR NAME DOES?" or other messages of the sort can/will eventually wear down the {{A|Town}} to the point where they'll hang you, however this can have its downsides with the {{A|Town}} ignoring you or a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} killing you before you are hanged. Smart {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles will see that you're a {{A|Jester}} or someone new, and thus a waste of a {{A|Night}}. **Note that an all-caps message will be blocked if you post it right after another one, so make sure to alternate with all-caps and partially-caps. *If you really want to annoy people, bring up controversial topics like sports or movies. However, like other {{A|Jester}} strategies this could simply result in you being killed at {{A|Night}}. ===={{A|Vigilante}} {{A|Day 2}}==== *Pretending that you shot somebody that was immune on {{A|Night 1}} makes you look like a killing role that found an enemy role. Whoever you 'target' as the player you shot will be the first to cast suspicion. There is still more of a chance than not that you will be called out as a {{A|Jester}}. **This strategy will work better if there's no {{A|Mafia}} kill on {{A|Night 1}}. ====[[Role block|Role blocked]]==== *If no one dies on any given {{A|Day}}, you can claim [[Role block|role blocked]]. While many people will suspect you as {{A|Jester}}, you will still likely be hanged. ====Voting against the {{A|Town}}==== *If someone is pushed up on the stand, and is guaranteed to be voted guilty or innocent, voting against the {{A|Town}} will cast suspicion on you. They will question why you voted guilty on a {{A|Townie}} that is innocent, or why you voted innocent on an evil role that is guilty. Though some people may pick up that you are {{A|Jester}}, you are likely to be hanged either the same {{A|Day}} or the next. ==== Claim to be a Killing Role ==== * On the first {{A|Day}} (as in the pregame {{A|Day}}), simply claim you're an evil killing role, and you will prove it in your {{A|Death Note}} on the first {{A|Night}}. Chances are, either the {{A|Mafia}} and/or the {{A|Serial Killer}} will likely put something in their {{A|Death Note}} to evade suspicion. Keep in mind, this can backfire in a few capacities: ** No one puts anything in their {{A|Death Note}} or they attack a role with {{A|Night}}-immunity. ** You end up {{A|Jailed}} on the first {{A|Night}}, and some {{A|Death Note}} clearly indicates you. ** The {{A|Town}} may just correctly believe you're a {{A|Jester}} and ignore you, leaving you open to be killed by any killing role, as {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Vigilante}} can both kill you with no repercussions, and no reasonable {{A|Townie}} would try such a stunt. ====Actually playing as {{A|Jester}}==== *Many rookie players would expect that a {{A|Town}} would obviously ignore a {{A|Jester}}. In reality, claiming {{A|Jester}} especially late game is a very useful way to get yourself hanged. As experienced players would expect that anybody claiming {{A|Jester}} is suspicious due to reverse psychology, regardless if they are an actual {{A|Jester}} or not. Although risky and contradictory, this will get you more likely to be hanged in a game with {{A|Neutral Killing}} or/and without {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}}. ===Behavior=== ====Staying silent==== *Try staying completely silent. When asked to speak or tell your role, say nothing and eventually you will be accused of being suspicious. The downside to doing this is you will not be suspected too much in the beginning. Occasionally, the entire {{A|Town}} will not even realize that you're there, and you'll live. Another downside to this is that killing roles may suspect you of being a high priority target such as the {{A|Jailor}}, who would rather not draw attention to themselves. This can possibly have you killed at {{A|Night}}. If put on trial, staying silent is almost a guarantee to be hanged, giving you the win. **If you are {{A|Jailed}}, create a convincing {{A|Last Will}} and post it only when you are {{A|Jailed}}, but never post your fake {{A|Last Will}} on trial. ***If you didn't have a {{A|Last Will}}, claiming [[Unique Role|unique roles]] (specifically {{A|Town Support}} because it's more convincing than {{A|Veteran}}) such as {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Retributionist}}, but don't claim {{A|Retributionist}} in a {{A|Janitor}} game since the {{A|Jailor}} can execute you. ====Telling everyone to whisper you their roles==== *During the beginning of the {{A|Day}} if the {{A|Town}} has a slight majority, yelling out to everyone to tell you their roles can have you hanged, especially if there is a {{A|Mayor}} or other confirmed {{A|Town}} role. ====Random hang==== *Try and start a random hang, then simply act either annoying or suspicious enough to have the random hang be yourself. When you have to say your defense, then simply either be silent and reply to the chat when they ask or become suspicious that you are a {{A|Jester}}. Feel free to reveal during the [[Phases#Last_Words|Last Words]] phase. If you fail to do so for one {{A|Day}}, then simply ask the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Doctor}} to heal/{{A|Jail}} you because what you said might have you killed, and that can scare off killing roles even if you aren't healed/{{A|Jailed}}. Then keep trying to do so until you are. If you are voted by some people but time runs out, then chances are that you will either be killed at {{A|Night}} or voted tomorrow. **Be careful as the {{A|Jailor}} may decide to execute you because of your suspicious nature. ====Voting innocent on a known target==== *Vote innocent when hanging a known evil target. This will make you seem suspicious, especially if the target was in the {{A|Mafia}}, etc. *When the {{A|Town}} hangs a known member of the {{A|Mafia}}, vote innocent so then you'll be suspected of being {{A|Mafia}} as well. However, this can attract unwanted {{A|Town Investigatives}} your way if you were the only one who voted innocent. This can also attract {{A|Vigilantes}} that are trigger-happy. **This strategy normally leads the {{A|Town}} to believe you are {{A|Jester}}. Be careful with how often you do that and claim to have done something along the lines of, "Sorry I, misclicked" when you are accused of being a {{A|Jester}}. This may encourage the {{A|Town}} into hanging you. ====Voting guilty/Abstaining on a confirmed {{A|Town}} role==== *If there is a confirmed {{A|Town}} role, such as {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Jailor}}, you can try to have them hanged by voting them, and voting guilty. If you aren't killed at {{A|Night}}, then you can, and might be hanged due to the suspicion. However, it is very risky, since you have a high chance of being killed at {{A|Night}}. **This works even better if a {{A|Mayor}} reveals on trial and you vote guilty. *Sometimes, abstaining on somebody that seems clearly innocent can also have you hanged, since you are expected to vote innocent as well. ====Team up==== *Team up with one side and vote with them in exchange for being hanged later, and then killing one of their enemies at {{A|Night}}. Most people will be willing to team with you for the extra vote, however, the {{A|Jailor}} is likely to execute you. Allow people to become slightly suspicious of you, then say something along the lines of: "Guys please don't hang I am {{A|Townie}} but I cannot tell you specifically what role I am." They will either become more suspicious and hang you, or think you're a {{A|Jester}}, in which case, your plan has failed. *Generally, it is better to side with the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Neutrals}} than {{A|Town}} because siding with the {{A|Town}} may make you a kill target for the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Neutrals}}. However, leave the hanging to the {{A|Townies}}, as you have a better chance to be hanged by them, than the {{A|Mafia}}, and the {{A|Serial Killer}}, as you will most likely survive the game with them, without gaining the win for yourself. *Another risky yet rewarding tactic is to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a random player on {{A|Day 2}} that you are a {{A|Jester}}, and that if they help hang you, you'll haunt someone of their choice. Offer yourself as a weapon! Generally despite the player's role, they will be more than willing to help you to their own advantage. This can be a very clever tactic because if you managed to ask help from a {{A|Mafia}} member or {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, they probably won't kill you. There are a few downfalls to this strategy, though; They may have trouble convincing people to vote you up or they might just expose you. *It might be smarter to work with the {{A|Jailor}} if you are {{A|Jailed}}. Especially if the {{A|Jailor}} has executed a {{A|Town}} member and ran out of executions, you can offer him a deal by telling the truth, and having the {{A|Jailor}} either to write it in their {{A|Last Will}} or announce it that you didn't claim a role. Most {{A|Townies}} will hang you, but it will make you suspicious if the {{A|Jailor}} has executions left, as it will make them wonder why you weren't executed. *It is usually to your advantage to signal to the {{A|Mafia}} that you are a {{A|Jester}}. This means that they're unlikely to vote guilty on you; but it also means they're likely to help you be voted up, and more importantly, it makes them less likely to kill you at {{A|Night}}. **One easy way to make the {{A|Mafia}} suspect that you're a {{A|Jester}} is to claim you were attacked on a {{A|Night}} when the {{A|Mafia}} missed their kill; the real {{A|Mafia}} will know they didn't attack you. **Another option is to claim {{A|Sheriff}} and accuse someone you're reasonably certain isn't {{A|Mafia}}, which should immediately out you as a fake (and therefore a likely {{A|Jester}} or {{A|Executioner}}) to the actual {{A|Mafia}}. Be warned that inattentive {{A|Mafia}} may fail to notice you're an obvious fake and kill you anyway. ====Strategy for other roles==== *'''Strategy for other players''': If you want the {{A|Jester}} to kill someone else, vote to put the {{A|Jester}} on trial, vote guilty (or innocent), encourage others to vote, and then change your vote to innocent at the last second. '''A {{A|Jester}} can't kill innocent voters.''' *As {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, allying with the {{A|Jester}} can be extremely valuable late game. [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|Whispering]] things to them like "I will get you hanged" or "I will try to help you be hanged" will cause the {{A|Jester}} to want to ally and vote with the {{A|Mafia}}. This is especially useful if the {{A|Jester}} is already revealed to the {{A|Town}} and has no hope of winning unless allying with the {{A|Mafia}}. Even if you end up not having them hanged, they will often appreciate the effort and vote with you anyway, so allying with a {{A|Jester}} isn't the worse idea for any {{A|Neutral}} or {{A|Mafia}} roles. **Don't rely on them not targeting you after death however. So do not vote guilty in the hopes that the {{A|Jester}} will appreciate your help and not haunt you. First of all, the {{A|Jesters}} don't care much about which side wins, so they may haunt you anyway, despite the role you played in having them hanged, or you might know them as a friend and they do the joy of having you killed. Secondly, the {{A|Jesters}} will be in contact with dead {{A|Townies}} and {{A|Mediums}} who will probably ask them to haunt you if your role has been revealed. They tend to listen to other dead people when deciding who to haunt. *'''{{A|Executioner}} turned {{A|Jester}}''': Claim that a player of an unknown role is {{A|Night}}-immune. When asked for role or evidence, give a brash, salty, or vague response that matches the grammar and style of the {{A|Serial Killer's}} previous {{A|Death Notes}} (if any). Bonus points if the {{A|Death Notes}} have even the slightest relation to your in-game name and you choose your answers based on that. Adamantly deny or affirm your guilt based on how gullible/desperate you believe the other players to be. This will cast great suspicion on you if you had been attacked before becoming a {{A|Jester}} and someone makes a claim that you are {{A|Night}}-immune, whether in the chat, {{A|Last Will}}, or {{A|Death Note}}. You could [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] if you can correctly guess the contents of a highly-suspicious one. This has a good chance of hanging you. *If you are debating whether the player on trial is a {{A|Jester}} or not, your best course of action is to vote innocent. Abstainers and those who vote guilty are the only ones at risk after a {{A|Jester}} is hanged. Generally, important {{A|Townies}} are ones who are usually told to vote innocent. ===Specific roles to claim=== ===={{A|Jester}}==== *Outright claiming to be a {{A|Jester}} may fool the {{A|Town}} into thinking you're a killing role trying to avoid being hanged. However, this rarely works and will probably have you killed at {{A|Night}}, or left alone, especially with experienced {{A|Townies}}. *A more sophisticated option is to avoid claiming {{A|Jester}} outright, but to imply it by playing a {{A|Jester}} "badly"; if you pretend to be an obvious {{A|Jester}} by using really, really basic ploys that few people would fall for, the {{A|Town}} will sometimes conclude that you're an evil role pretending to be a {{A|Jester}} to avoid being hanged and hang you. *Claiming a [[Unique Role|unique role]] that has already died or has been confirmed can set you in a prime position. *Note that any strategy where you appear to be a {{A|Jester}} carries a very high risk of being shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} or executed by a {{A|Jailor}}, since killing possible {{A|Jesters}} is normally considered part of their job. Therefore, this works best when you've confirmed that no {{A|Town Killing}} roles remain. ===={{A|Lookout}}==== *After a {{A|Werewolf}} attack, you can claim {{A|Lookout}} and say that you saw someone visit the victim, accusing them of being the {{A|Werewolf}}. Normally, any actual {{A|Lookout}} who saw a {{A|Werewolf}} attack would be killed by the {{A|Werewolf}} themselves, so this can have you hanged if anyone recognizes the contradiction. *Another way to look suspicious with a {{A|Lookout}} claim is to claim {{A|Lookout}} and accuse someone of attacking a target who was {{A|cleaned}}, attacking someone who just said they were healed, or being the attacker in an attack that was obviously {{A|Transported}}. Smart players will ask why you didn't see the second visitor and conclude that you're evil or an {{A|Executioner}}. *Claiming {{A|Lookout}} is even better if an important {{A|Townie}} reveals early on. ===={{A|Tracker}}==== *You can apply similar strategies from the {{A|Lookout}}. ===={{A|Mayor}}==== *If {{A|Jailed}}, claim {{A|Mayor}}. Then explain you don't want to reveal (afraid of {{A|Mafia}} majority or some other reason). If the {{A|Jailor}} doesn't execute you, at {{A|Day}} claim a different role with 'information' against someone (preferably not the {{A|Jailor}}). Then, the {{A|Jailor}} or the {{A|Jailor's}} {{A|Last Will}} will convince people you may not be what you claim. On the stand, re-claim to be a {{A|Mayor}} but use the "[Name]: has revealed themselves as {{A|Mayor}}!" trick. This will assure your hanging. ===={{A|Spy}}==== *With the {{A|Spy's}} bugging ability, claim someone is immune using the "Someone attacked your target but their defense was too strong!" message. You could also claim they were transported or role blocked when they weren't whilst on trial. *The {{A|Town}} often requests that the {{A|Spy}} reveal themselves early. Late {{A|Spy}} claims are often hanged. *In a game with a {{A|Spy}} claim, having a will that conflicts with theirs will often lead to a hang. *There are some players in the game who make stupid mistakes. Faking a mistake could help you get hanged if {{A|Town}} observant. Claiming {{A|Spy}} with a {{A|Sheriff}} {{A|Last Will}} is a newbie mistake, but it could also be your path to victory. ===={{A|Retributionist}}==== *You can try to claim {{A|Retributionist}}, and set up a {{A|Last Will}} where you 'accidentally' resurrect the same player twice. This casts suspicion on you since {{A|Retributionist}} can only use a single body once. *If a {{A|Vigilante}} has died, you could try stating that you'll use the {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot someone likely evil, and once the next morning dawns and they see the evil still alive, you'll likely become very suspicious. *You can also claim when the {{A|Retributionist}} is dead, although this will most likely end up having you executed by the {{A|Jailor}} or shot by a {{A|Vigilante}}. It's much better to counterclaim the {{A|Retributionist}} and convince the {{A|Town}} to hang one of you. *You could try claiming {{A|Retributionist}} and state that you'll revive someone, pretending to be someone unaware ({{A|Retributionist}} no longer brings someone back to life). This does have a risk of being shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} or executed by a {{A|Jailor}}, however. ===={{A|Survivor}}==== *One strategy is to claim {{A|Survivor}} on or after {{A|Day 3}}. However, if the {{A|Town}} has no other leads, claiming on {{A|Day 1}} or 2 might still cause them to hang you immediately, knowing that you're not {{A|Town}} and suspecting that you might be an evil role using {{A|Survivor}} to explain away your Basic defense, or just saying {{A|Survivor}} because you are everyone's ally, and should not be killed by almost anyone. *Alternatively, you can claim {{A|Survivor}} at any point by saying that you used your vest to block an attack; it is common for evil roles to do this after facing an attack, knowing they'll be called out in a {{A|Death Note}} anyway. *If you're lucky enough to face any sort of accusations, claiming {{A|Survivor}} on the stand is also often a very easy way to be hanged; the {{A|Town}} will almost always hang people who claim to be a {{A|Survivor}} under pressure, since losing a {{A|Survivor}} doesn't really hurt them. *The downside to claiming to be a {{A|Survivor}} is that it very frequently attracts attention from {{A|Vigilantes}} and {{A|Jailors}}, who will know you're unlikely to be a {{A|Townie}}. *Of course, if someone counter-claims you, you will be put under huge suspicion. *If an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers an evil role, the {{A|Town}} will remember your claim and ''instantly'' hang you! ===={{A|Doctor}}==== *Claiming {{A|Doctor}} is an effective way of putting yourself under suspicion of being the {{A|Serial Killer}}, especially if you claim, on any {{A|Day}} where the {{A|Mafia}} failed to kill, that you were attacked and healed yourself; this will make it seem like you're trying to explain away your Basic/Powerful defense. *Claiming {{A|Doctor}} is even better when the {{A|Jailor}} claims {{A|Day 1}} and there is a {{A|Lookout}} in the game. However, this may backfire as {{A|Mafia}} will kill you as soon as you claim. ===={{A|Investigator}}==== *A {{A|Consigliere}} will often pretend to be an {{A|Investigator}}; and a common mistake {{A|Consiglieres}} make when doing this is to list ''exact'' roles when accusing people (since {{A|Investigators}} see mixed results instead). Therefore, you can appear to be a {{A|Consigliere}} by claiming {{A|Investigator}} and naming people's exact roles. *A different strategy, and one of pure luck, falsely give a role at Daytime. People may suspect you of an {{A|Executioner}} and hang you on the spot. However, if a {{A|Townie}} died the previous {{A|Night}}, they can suspect you of an {{A|Executioner}} turned {{A|Jester}} and keep you away from a hang. *The {{A|Investigator}} results have been changed several times in the game's existence, and if it happens again you can use the old results right after it is changed. (e.g: claiming {{A|Investigator}} and accusing someone of having a before-{{VH|1.5.0}} {{A|Investigator}} result, such as {{A|Mayor}}/{{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Vampire Hunter}}.) The more time that passes after the results are changed, the less believable this is. *Make up some investigative results! The more far fetched the better! Like, say {{A|Serial Killer}}/{{A|Werewolf}}/{{A|Arsonist}}, or {{A|Consigliere}}/{{A|Witch}}/{{A|Survivor}}. People will surely see through your flawed claim. Be warned they may realize you could be a {{A|Jester}} since the claims are obviously incorrect. *The {{A|Investigator}} list was changed again with the release of the {{A|Coven Expansion}}; in addition to letting you appear to make a mistake by using before-{{A|Coven}} investigative results, this makes an impossible result a far more plausible mistake, since the {{A|Investigator}} results in {{A|Coven}} are longer and more complicated. *If there is a confirmed {{A|Spy}} around who releases results every {{A|Day}} that includes two or more {{A|Mafia}} visits, claim {{A|Investigator}} with your results shown as to the first visits for the {{A|Mafia}}, not ''ever'' the last shown result (the last one is the {{A|Mafia Killing}}). This can make smarter {{A|Townies}} think you are a {{A|Consigliere}}, as the results directly match. You could also do it will the results of whoever the {{A|Mafia}} have killed each {{A|Night}}. ===={{A|Bodyguard}}==== *A {{A|Bodyguard}} has a very dangerous investigative result of {{A|Bodyguard}}/{{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Arsonist}}; additionally, they are hard to prove. Therefore, a {{A|Town}} hunting either of those two evil roles will likely put unexpected {{A|Bodyguard}} claims on the stand. *If pressed for a {{A|Last Will}}, you can refuse to give one, or you can give one with clear errors in it, such as saying that you protected someone the {{A|Night}} they died, or constantly failing to protect the {{A|Mayor}} or confirmed {{A|Townies}}. Claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} after a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}} died is also extremely suspicious since the {{A|Town}} will wonder why you weren't protecting them. *You can attract additional attention as a {{A|Bodyguard}} by claiming you were attacked and saying you used your bulletproof vest; since {{A|Bodyguard}} only have one bulletproof vest, it's very unlikely for them to block an attack with it, and since both the evil roles in their investigative results are immune, they frequently claim to have used a bulletproof vest in this fashion. This works best on any {{A|Night}} when the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} fails to kill anyone, though experienced members of the {{A|Mafia}} will know they didn't attack you and may assume that you're a {{A|Jester}}. *Claiming {{A|Bodyguard}} is even better when the {{A|Jailor}} claims {{A|Day 1}}. However, this may backfire as {{A|Mafia}} will kill you as soon as you claim. ===={{A|Vigilante}}==== *Claiming {{A|Vigilante}} and saying you attacked someone only to find them with {{A|Defense}} will often draw suspicion, since {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles, {{A|Serial Killers}}, and {{A|Vampires}} often claim to be a {{A|Vigilante}} when they need to immediately out someone as immune. Claiming it after the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} haven't made a kill is particularly suspicious. Implying that you are a {{A|Vampire}} by accusing someone of being "immune" like this has the added advantage that the {{A|Vampire}} is part of your investigative results. *Claiming to be a {{A|Vigilante}} on the second {{A|Day}} and saying that a certain player is immune is also a possible plan. Most players usually catch on that {{A|Vigilantes}} cannot shoot on the first {{A|Night}}, and called you out on this. Of course, some smart players may recognize this as a tactic a {{A|Jester}} would use. ===={{A|Sheriff}}==== *This strategy is pretty much based around luck, but it can work sometimes. During the {{A|Day}}, claim you are a {{A|Sheriff}} and that your "target" came up as suspicious. This can surprisingly provoke others' suspicions of you being an {{A|Executioner}}, thus you may be hanged, especially if it's early game. However, if the {{A|Townie}} you accused dies the {{A|Night}} before, you can be suspected of being an {{A|Executioner}} turned into a {{A|Jester}} and may not be hanged. Plus, if you end up actually accusing a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, you may be written off as an actual {{A|Sheriff}} and won't be hanged and rather killed at {{A|Night}} instead. *In {{A|Ranked}}, {{A|Sheriff}} claims are often given a lot of suspicion, since it's an easy {{A|Last Will}} to fake. This makes it an easy way attract attention, especially if multiple {{A|Town Investigatives}} are dead. ===={{A|Executioner}}==== *A good strategy is to act like an {{A|Executioner}}, especially a bad one; claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Investigator}}, or {{A|Lookout}} {{A|Day 2}} and say that a random player is suspicious. Ideally, everyone will think you're an {{A|Executioner}} and hang you. **However, the {{A|Jailor}} may end up {{A|Jailing}} and executing you, or a {{A|Vigilante}} will shoot you. *If they don't, and your target turns out to be {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Town}} will hopefully hang you for revenge or suspicion of lying and setting the entire {{A|Executioner}} setup from the start, though most {{A|Townies}} will not care about you later on. *You can also claim {{A|Executioner}} outright after having a {{A|Townie}} hanged; this is a frequent strategy for killers with {{A|Defense}}, so it has a good chance of having you hanged by more experienced {{A|Townies}}. *Alternatively, you can [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a {{A|Townie}} on {{A|Day 3}} or 4, "I'm {{A|Executioner}}, help me hang (confirmed {{A|Townie}}) and I'll vote with the {{A|Mafia}}." Since they are {{A|Town}}, they will freak out and tell people you are {{A|Executioner}}, which will probably have you hanged. **Note that any strategy where you pretend to be an {{A|Executioner}} has a serious drawback: If you are not hanged that {{A|Day}}, there's a huge risk that the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} will kill your "target". If they actually are {{A|Town}}, then everyone will assume you became a {{A|Jester}}, making it almost impossible to be hanged. **Additionally, the {{A|Town}} may ignore you if they think that you're a successful (or unsuccessful) {{A|Executioner}}. To avoid this, stay active in the game; talk a lot, [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]], vote frequently, etc. You want to appear to be an evil role using the {{A|Executioner}} claim as a shield. *You can also claim to be an {{A|Executioner}} with an impossible target. {{A|Executioners}} can only target {{A|Town}} (or, in some situations, a {{A|Vampire}}), and can never target a {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}; therefore, claiming {{A|Executioner}} and saying your target was a dead non-{{A|Town}} or the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}} can have you hanged under the assumption that you're a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role pretending to be an {{A|Executioner}}. *Additionally, if you claim {{A|Executioner}} if you are put on trial. This will cause many people to just hang you to kill you off. *Another good strategy is to wait a while before conjuring your fake claim. This is so that you can see who are important {{A|Townies}}, and reduce the risk of accusing the {{A|Jailor}} (who'll instantly {{A|Jail}} and execute you) or the {{A|Vigilante}} (who'll just shoot you); However, that risk is most possible if you try this on {{A|Day 2}}, so it is recommended you do this on {{A|Day 3}}-4. ===={{A|Medium}}==== *A {{A|Medium}} claim is a hard role to prove, and it can therefore work in your favor if the {{A|Town}} is desperate for a hang. If there are {{A|cleaned}} targets in the game, and claim yourself as a {{A|Medium}}, giving a little bit of evidence against so-and-so, people will suspect you of being a {{A|Janitor}} working with a {{A|Framer}}, {{A|Executioner}}, {{A|Jester}}, or {{A|Consigliere}}. **In {{A|All Any}}, claiming {{A|Medium}} on trial after being quiet for long enough will make you seem more like an {{A|Arsonist}} than anything else. This will likely get you hanged since the {{A|Town}} only has a few seconds to judge your suspicious claim. ===={{A|Amnesiac}}==== *Claiming to be an {{A|Amnesiac}} means that you'll likely be hanged if an ''actual'' {{A|Amnesiac}} later remembers an evil role. *Claiming {{A|Amnesiac}} is usually going to make you very little of a target for evils since you don't get any abilities until the {{A|Day}} after and you also won't turn into the new role which would make killing you rude. *Additionally, if you claim {{A|Amnesiac}}, the {{A|Town}} will often demand that you remember a {{A|Town}} role the next {{A|Night}}. Failing to do so may have you hanged. However, this could have you killed by an evil role trying to eliminate {{A|Town}}. *{{A|Amnesiac}} is, however, generally a bad role to claim on the stand, since the {{A|Town}} will usually give you at least one {{A|Night}} to remember a {{A|Town}} role (and you may die that {{A|Night}} or the {{A|Town}} may be distracted by another lead). ===={{A|Vampire Hunter}}==== *If there is a confirmed {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, you should claim that also. To prove your claim, the real {{A|Vampire Hunter}} might ask you whether you turned into a {{A|Vigilante}}. Answering this incorrectly or saying "yes, wait I mean no" could have you hanged. *Also claiming that you are a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} from the start of the game is a viable option too: **Claiming {{A|Town Protectives}} and {{A|Lookouts}} on you {{A|Night 1}} gets anyone who would attack you less likely to do so, specially {{A|Vampires}}. **Whether if there are or not {{A|Vampires}} it's irrelevant, just adapt your tactics according to what you think. For example, if there are no {{A|Vampires}} just insist that there are, and with time you will get eventually hanged for not telling the truth. If there are things get more interesting: keep doing like you are checking people, and if you post in your {{A|Last Will}} that you visited someone who is a {{A|Vampire}}, they will know that you are fake and will try to get rid of you or can try to play along you. But if anyone you said you checked was really not a {{A|Vampire}}, with time the {{A|Vampires}} will believe that you are indeed a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, and will vote you out when they get majority (try to vote {{A|Mafia}} members and {{A|Neutral Killings}} out make sure they do). **Beware of {{A|Investigators}}, they can get you hanged, but can also find out that you are a {{A|Jester}}. {{A|Consiglieres}}, in the other hand, can get you hanged with no risks of being killed by the {{A|Mafia}} (they should contact you by [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] you). ===={{A|Transporter}}==== *Another strategy to win as a {{A|Jester}} is to claim {{A|Transporter}}. The {{A|Town}} will then want you to prove it, or ask people if they were {{A|Transported}} previously. Should no one claim {{A|Transported}}, your claim will automatically be put under suspicion, and may have you hanged. ===={{A|Witch}}==== *If you live near the end, and especially if the {{A|Town}} believed your claim, tell the evil [[factions (ToS)|factions]] like the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killings}} that you're {{A|Witch}} and not to hang you. If you're (intentionally) not convincing enough, they will think you are a {{A|Townie}}, and you will be hanged. ===={{A|Psychic}}==== *You can claim to be a {{A|Psychic}} and mess up your results by either putting in a name twice or putting in a player that has died. Many evil roles tend to fake {{A|Psychic}} as it is easy to claim. If your {{A|Last Will}} has mistakes in it, the {{A|Town}} will be more likely to think you are an evil role trying to claim {{A|Psychic}}. ===={{A|Veteran}}==== *As a [[Unique Role|unique role]], a known {{A|Veteran}} will get most counter-claimers of that role killed; claiming it can therefore rapidly get you hanged. While [[Unique Role|unique]] claims by evils are rare in general, {{A|Veteran}} is one of the more common ones, since it's a good alternative for a {{A|Mafioso}} who is worried about {{A|Investigators}} but who doesn't want the obvious choice of {{A|Vigilante}}. *More importantly, claiming {{A|Veteran}} will discourage people from visiting you at {{A|Night}}, reducing the likelihood that you'll get killed or investigated and increasing the chance that you'll live long enough to get hanged. *{{A|Veteran}} is a particularly good claim if you think the {{A|Mafia}} is near a majority, since it means they'll be more likely to hang you rather than killing you at {{A|Night}}. ===Exploiting scumreading=== Scumreading is a common set of techniques or senses used to determine whether someone is evil or good. Purposely go along with the characteristics of an evil people had in mind could probably frame yourself to be hanged on spot. This strategy may work better at higher level play, as these are common loopholes in scum's behavior and often noticeable by experienced player, but can sometimes be unnoticed by newer players. *Taunt {{A|Town}} and make some meaningless speech when being put up on stand. For example: "Gosh! I don't understand! This is so random. Y'all gonna lose. Don't you realize that we're losing majority? {{A|Town}} is a mess. Hanging is a total salvation from this chaos. Bye.". People may find the speaker guilty as true {{A|Town}} may voice every clue they find or know constructively instead of doing manipulative speech. *Admit a role, but not showing {{A|Last Will}}. For example: "I'm {{A|Sheriff}}, and I found someone suspicious. But I'm afraid my target could be {{A|framed}}, so I decide to keep it for myself.". {{A|Last Wills}} are the most recognizable proof to innocence, and {{A|Town}} is less likely to keep information to themselves regardless of how truthful or how useful it is. *Say something that looks helpful but lack of actual content, such as: "Who should we get next?". You may need to do this a few times to be noticed. *Vote slowly, as most of the evil hesitate to push their member to the gallows. *Giving expressions like "Why me?", "(Particular role) needs to keep a [[Last Will (ToS)|will]] for what?", "Proof?", instead of showing your role and {{A|Last Will}} when you're accused, will most probably get yourself an immediate hang. *Try hard to fail a hang by constantly defend the others without revealing your role, and refuse to push them up. Act of defense can be anything, for example, Mary Warren accused James Russell, people are piling vote on John but you push vote on Mary to spread out the focus. Constant interruption can raise the sense of necessary to eliminate the doer. *Refuse to claim a role for excuse "I'll be attacked if I tell you my role". There's no reason for a {{A|Townie}} not to say their role, for, if there are more role to be known, {{A|Town}} coordinates better. *Delay response to answering question about your role, feinting a scenario where you're buying time to make up a fake identity. *Announce to be abstained or not to push vote. As VFR (Vote For Roles) is generally helpful for {{A|Town}}, not pushing vote means they could be evil. For those who abstain almost every single time, could be the one who wishes for a possible mishang. *Do not announce being [[Role block|role blocked]] or {{A|Transported}}. As [[Transporter (ToS)|transportation]] could mess up investigation process, {{A|Town}} would most probably announce it. *Defend oneself with "findings" in form of words instead in the format of {{A|Last Will}}, like: "I checked (player x) last {{A|Night}}, he is guilty! Get him too! While I found (player y) to be innocent the {{A|Night}} before. I also checked (player z) N1, he's clean". This is a cover-up for evil who doesn't have {{A|Last Will}} updated. *Write {{A|Last Will}} in a very short and unorganized manner, like using numbers instead of [[name]] or some spelling mistakes to imply that the {{A|Last Will}} is done hasty and spontaneously. ===Other claim-based Strategies=== ====Last killer role==== *Near the end of the game, if there is only one evil role left, confess that you are tired of the game running this long and that you are the last killer role. Speak convincingly and back up your claim, but do not be too desperate, lest a smart player catches on and convinces the {{A|Town}} otherwise. *If there are three players left (You, and two other killing roles or roles like {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Doctor}}; Ex: You, {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Arsonist}}) claim that you are {{A|Godfather}} and it's a tie breaker for the non-{{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Godfather}} role. The {{A|Godfather}} will assume that you are {{A|Jester}} and go with your bluff, hoping that you will haunt the {{A|Arsonist}}. ====Appearing as a {{A|Hex Master}}==== *In the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, if a confirmed {{A|Hex Master}} is in game, and they have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, try luring in {{A|Investigators}} and {{A|Sheriffs}} to check you. Since you appear in the same investigative results as the {{A|Hex Master}}, and appear innocent to the {{A|Sheriff}} (like a {{A|Hex Master}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}}), they might assume you are the {{A|Hex Master}} and hang you. **This works even better if a {{A|Tracker}} tracks you, since with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, {{A|Hex Master}} visits become {{A|Astral}}. **However, if '''you''' are {{A|Hexed}}, this will not work due to appearing suspicious to the {{A|Sheriff}} and will assume you are {{A|Hexed}}. ====Impossible Claims==== *Claiming a role that can't possibly exist in the game can have you hanged. Some possibilities include: **A [[Unique Role|unique role]] that already exists or which is taken by someone else. Avoid claiming {{A|Jailor}} in this way unless you're certain there's no {{A|Jailor}} in the game or they've executed a {{A|Townie}} since otherwise, the real {{A|Jailor}} will very likely kill you. **A role who doesn't have a spot in the current game's role list at all. **A role whose possible spots in the role list are already taken by dead or confirmed people. *Note that ''outright'' making an impossible claim is less likely to work in more experienced games, since it's such a transparently false claim that you might be immediately suspected of being a {{A|Jester}}; this works best when you can make it seem like you're claiming under pressure or if you can arrange for your claim to be shown as impossible ''after'' you make it. *If any one player can identify that you're a fake (for instance, if you claim {{A|Doctor}} when there's only one living {{A|Town Protective}}), you can rely on them to call you out; you'll also likely be hanged if and when they die. This is also why claiming a [[Unique Role|unique role]] is often effective. ===={{A|Neutral Evil}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} role==== *A trick some {{A|Neutral Evils}} or {{A|Neutral Killings}} use is to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a random player, reveal their role, and hope that they are {{A|Mafia}}. If there is a {{A|Witch}} in the game, and seeing as {{A|Witches}} usually side with {{A|Mafia}}, this may just work. However, if you [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to someone who is in touch with the {{A|Jailor}}, or are in the midst of {{A|Mayor}} games, or are not hanged the {{A|Day}} you [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]], you may be executed by the {{A|Jailor}}. ====Multiple roles==== *Whilst this strategy is not very effective against experienced players, there is a chance you can be hanged by claiming multiple roles. *If you ever end up claiming a role, either from being asked it, revealing with information, or a request to be {{A|Jailed}}, protected, or healed, the next {{A|Day}} claim something else. People will likely realize you have claimed to be several different roles and hang you for it. **However, this is a risky move, as most people will guess that you are a {{A|Jester}} by the fact that you're claiming multiple roles. This strategy is most likely to work in {{A|Classic Mode}}, although it may not even work there. *Another strategy that can be used in conjunction with this one for maximum effectiveness is to claim something easy to prove like {{A|Sheriff}} and then claim another {{A|Town}} essential role if you are counter-claimed, such as {{A|Doctor}}. You can say that you claimed {{A|Sheriff}} to avoid being killed but are actually {{A|Doctor}}. While you may actually convince some people, most people will not buy that and hang you. ====Literal joking==== *A good strategy is on {{A|Day 1}} to say something like "N1: Tommy-SUS!". Obviously, since the game has just started, the suspicion will be pinned towards you. Note that this is not recommended for {{A|Classic Mode}} since new players tend to go for anyone who speaks {{A|Day 1}}. However, experienced players will see right through the bluff and attack you. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{JesterAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{JesterMessages}} ==Trivia== [[File:Jester Burned at the Stake.png|thumb|right|Jester [[avatar]] using the Burned at the Stake [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]].]] *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.3.1}}, a {{A|Jester's}} haunting would not kill anyone if they chose no one to haunt. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0}}, a {{A|Jester}} haunt was able to be {{A|Transported}} to someone else if they '''''chose''''' someone to haunt that voted guilty. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.3.0}}, the {{A|Jester}} was only able to haunt guilty voters. *The game will choose a random player to haunt if nobody is chosen. **This does not happen if the {{A|Jester}} leaves during the {{A|Night}} or earlier. '''BEWARE:''' if you leave after you get hanged, you do not win! *Unlike any other [[Avatars (ToS)|avatars]], pairing the Jester [[Avatars (ToS)|avatar]] with the '''Burned at the Stake''' [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]] will grant a unique [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]], which shows the Jester forming an evil grin. *The Jester avatar's appearance is likely based on the character Shaco from League of Legends. *According to a poll made by [[User:LevinSnakesRise|LevinSnakesRise]], the {{A|Jester}}, with 207 votes, is the third most loved role in Town of Salem, the main reasoning being the love of causing utter chaos and fake accusing players, stirring up even more trouble. **Funnily enough, the {{A|Jester}} also came as the fourth most hated role in Town of Salem with 145 votes. The reason for that is because {{A|Jester}} was deemed as being too hard to win. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.0}} **The [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom]] Lobby role summary for {{A|Jester}} has been updated to indicate abstaining voters are also susceptible to being haunted. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Server no longer attempts to send successful hanging message to a {{A|Jester}} that has left the game. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Jester's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Jester.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Jester's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Jester Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.3.8910}} **{{A|Jester}} can now haunt abstaining voters. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Jester}} haunt can no longer be {{A|Transported}} by a {{A|Transporter}}. *{{VH|1.3.1}} **{{A|Jester}} can no longer not haunt if they do not select a target. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Шут]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Neutral Evil roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Unstoppable Attack]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Astral]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |uses=}}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can VOTE on a target to attack each night; however, if there is a {{A|Godfather}} and they VOTE on someone else, their decision will override yours, and you will attack their target instead. **If the {{A|Godfather}} picks a target, at the end of the night you will receive the notification: "The Godfather has ordered you to kill his target." **If you are {{A|roleblocked}} (or if you are dead/if there is no {{A|Mafioso}}), the {{A|Godfather}} will perform the kill personally and will be subject to the below instead. *Regardless of whether there is a {{A|Godfather}} or not, and regardless of their actions, you will do the actual killing, provided that you are alive and not role-blocked. This has the following implications; whoever does the actual killing will: **Be visible by to any {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Trackers}}, {{A|Spies}}, or {{A|Trappers}} visiting the target. **Be attacked by any {{A|Town Protectives}}, rampages, alerts, and/or {{A|Stone Gazes}} at that location. **Receive a message if the target has defense or was jailed. Note that if the {{A|Mafioso}} does the attacking, the {{A|Godfather}} will ''not'' receive said message for ordering an attack on the target in question. **Be able to leave a {{A|Death Note}} behind for the {{A|Town}} to see in the morning. *Both you and the {{A|Godfather's}} kill/death message appear as "a member of the {{A|Mafia}}", meaning {{A|Roleblockers}} (most notably the {{A|Jailor}}) cannot determine if they {{A|Roleblocked}} either of you. *If the {{A|Godfather}} dies during the game, you will be promoted to the {{A|Godfather}} rendering {{A|Basic Defense}}, {{A|Detection Immunity}}, and the final decision on who to kill. You cannot become the {{A|Godfather}} if there was none at the beginning of the game. *If you die and there is no living {{A|Godfather}}, a remaining member of the {{A|Mafia}} will be promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}}. If there are multiple {{A|Mafia}} members, whoever joined the lobby first will be promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}}. *If a {{A|Witch}} controls you, you will still attack the target of the {{A|Godfather}}. This is because the {{A|Mafioso}} only VOTEs for who to kill, allowing the {{A|Godfather's}} command to override the {{A|coven Leader's}} control, giving the {{A|Mafioso}} {{A|Control Immunity}}. *You can talk with the other members of the {{A|Mafia}} at night. [[File:Commanded&Controlled.jpg|thumb|262x262px|alt=|If the {{A|Mafioso}} is commanded by the {{A|Godfather}} and controlled by a {{A|Witch}}, the command will take precedence since the {{A|Witch}} only chooses what target the {{A|Mafioso}} votes for.]] ==Strategy== *As a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, your job is to kill anyone who would oppose the {{A|Mafia}} without being caught. *If the {{A|Godfather}} dies, you will become the new leader of the {{A|Mafia}}. So, if it appears that {{A|Godfather}} will die or be hanged soon, you should start to take control. *If there is no {{A|Godfather}}, you will lead the {{A|Mafia}} instead. Do not take coordination for granted. * Communication with the {{A|Godfather}} is of utmost importance. You should alert the {{A|Godfather}} the next night if your target has defense in order to avoid the {{A|Godfather}} repeatedly ordering you to attack the same target if you think the target has {{A|Basic Defense}}. If the target was likely a {{A|Townie}} who got healed, talk it out with the {{A|Godfather}} to see if it's worth attacking the same target again. **If you did not receive an immunity message, yet your target did not die, you have just attacked a {{A|Witch}}. Make absolutely certain to convey this to the {{A|Godfather}} the following night. * Both you and the {{A|Godfather}} should always choose a target. If one of you are {{A|Roleblocked}}, the other will attack instead. **You will know the {{A|Godfather}} was {{A|Roleblocked}} if you did not receive an order despite the {{A|Godfather}} choosing a target. *{{A|Death Notes}} can be important to discuss with the {{A|Godfather}}, as it is the {{A|Mafioso}} that gets left at the feet of the target, and not the {{A|Godfather}}. {{A|Death Notes}} revealing who has {{A|Defense}} may help the {{A|Mafia}}, and possibly the {{A|Town}}, in hanging a {{A|Neutral Evil}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} role. You can also call out someone for being immune when they aren't in hopes that the {{A|Town}} hanges them. *If the {{A|Godfather}} is jailed, make sure to attack that night to throw suspicion off of him. Nothing screams, "{{A|Mafia}}!" more than no deaths by {{A|Mafia}} when someone is jailed. *If no {{A|Mafia Killing}} roles are able to attack (jailed, away from the keyboard, etc.) claim that you were attacked and that you were healed or keep a pattern that follows the night that the {{A|Mafia}} did not attack. **Alternatively, once or twice in a game, you may want to not attack for one night, as this will bring suspicion onto whoever was jailed/role blocked, and can even have them hanged if they claim a role like {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Veteran}}. This will work even better farther into the game if a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is still alive, but this trick will usually only work once if the {{A|Town}} discovers that the player is innocent. Be careful; the downside to this trick is that you're slowing down your killing and giving the {{A|Town Investigative}} roles more time to catch you, so only do it if you're confident the confusion it will cause is worth it. You can also do this and claim that someone is immune in your {{A|Death Note}} when you didn't even attack them. *With a {{A|Death Note}}, try a different personality than how you usually type to throw off suspicion. If possible, mimic another person's personality and typing. (Spelling errors you wouldn't usually make, poor grammar if you use good grammar normally, etc.) **Another option is to not leave a {{A|Death Note}} at all, so if you are {{A|Roleblocked}}, nobody looks suspicious. It also has the advantage of not revealing anything in the {{A|Death Notes}} themselves. *Remember that if you are jailed or {{A|Roleblocked}}, the {{A|Godfather's}} {{A|Death Note}} will be shown when the target is killed, not yours. If your {{A|Death Notes}} are different in some distinct fashion, or if you don't normally change your {{A|Death Note}}, this can tip whoever {{A|Roleblocked}} you off to the fact that you're the {{A|Mafioso}}. You can avoid this by using the same {{A|Death Note}} as the {{A|Godfather}}, by both leaving it blank, or by constantly varying it. **You can also change your {{A|Death Note}} entirely after 2-3 {{A|Nights}} to trick a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} into repeatedly role blocking an important {{A|Town}} role or a {{A|Jailor}} into executing a {{A|Townie}}. *In general, if there is no {{A|Godfather}}, your main responsibility is leading the {{A|Mafia}}. If there is a {{A|Godfather}}, then work with them along with the rest of your {{A|Mafia}} team. *'''Always''' select a target, since as mentioned, your {{A|Godfather}} might be {{A|Roleblocked}} that night. *A risky strategy - on {{A|Night 1}}, write in your {{A|Death Note}} " is immune!" Smart {{A|Townies}} will recognize that the {{A|Mafioso}} could not have known that {{A|Night 1}}, and therefore be more inclined to believe you are {{A|Town}}. **Of course, this may have the opposite effect and draw unwanted attention to yourself. Consider using this to deflect suspicion onto other players. *Since games require at least one {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Godfather}} for the rest of the {{A|Mafia}} to function, you are somewhat of a disposable role. If there are three other {{A|Mafia}}, consider going aggressive if you need to try to take down a certain target. *{{A|Executioner}} is actually a fantastic claim as {{A|Mafioso}}. If you attempt to push someone really hard on Day 2, claiming a {{A|Town Investigative}} role and they end up being {{A|Town}}, you can claim that you got your {{A|Executioner}} win, and usually, the rest of the {{A|Town}} will leave you alone. However, this does come with the included risk of hypothetically pushing a member of the {{A|Coven}} or a {{A|Neutral}} role, which although may "confirm" you as a {{A|Townie}}, it would make you target for members of the {{A|Coven}} or opposing {{A|Neutrals}}, so this strategy works even better with a {{A|Consigliere}} working alongside you. The {{A|Jailor}} may also execute you because {{A|Executioners}} usually side with evil factions after securing their {{V|Victory}}. {{MafiaKillTable}} ==Role Killing Priority== In the {{A|Town}}, you are the main enemy. You will most likely not be sided with over a {{A|Neutral Killing}} if a {{A|Townie}} or {{A|Survivor}} is forced to pick between you and them in a 1 v 1 v 1 situation. Therefore, you need to know which people to kill. ==={{A|Jailor}}=== This role can kill all of the {{A|Mafia}}, including the {{A|Godfather}} unless there are four of you. This also role blocks you, making it potentially the most dangerous role to face. The {{A|Jailor}} will also be very hard to hang, and can sometimes attract the attention of {{A|Town Protective}} roles, {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Transporters}}, and roles that Rampage. Be careful of killing this role and other {{A|Town Investigative}} roles as this might out your claim, or make your claim look suspicious.  ==={{A|Tavern Keepers}} and {{A|Pirates}}=== They can either call you out or paralyze the {{A|Mafia}}. A {{A|Pirate}} is far less dangerous as they can side with you, but if they want to side with another role they could potentially call you out as a sign of alliance. ==={{A|Mayor}}=== If kept until late game, this role can potentially turn the tides on the whole {{A|Mafia}} by countering "{{A|Mafia}} Majority". Try to take them out before it's too late. ==={{A|Vigilantes}}=== These roles have the power to take out the vast majority of the {{A|Mafia}} in one fatal swoop. They are rather dangerous, but you can manage to trick them into killing themselves by hitting a {{A|Townie}}. ==={{A|Transporters}}=== They have the capability of making you attack one of your own {{A|Mafia}} members, and can easily protect themselves. They will also win against you in a 1v1 situation. To take them out, try targeting someone who you think the {{A|Transporter}} will be transporting themselves with (Like a {{A|Survivor}} claim). You can also have the {{A|Ambusher}} safely kill them for you as the {{A|Ambusher}} can turn the {{A|Transporter's}} self protection against them. ==={{A|Neutral Killing}} roles=== These roles can also take out the {{A|Mafia}}. Keep them in until the {{A|Mafia}} gains the majority vote or they start to kill the {{A|Mafia}} members. Taking out one of these roles can false confirm the accuser as {{A|Town}}. They can be valuable to double the kills per night and {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles will most likely attack enemies to the {{A|Mafia}}. All {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles have defense that the {{A|Mafia}} can't 'break'. ==={{A|Vampires}} and the {{A|Coven}}=== These are your main enemies in a battle for supremacy over the {{A|Town}}, and have a team to fall back on. They can also take out huge chunks of the {{A|Mafia}}, so take them out. Keep the balance though, as too many {{A|Townies}} can always spell trouble. These are easier to face in a Kingmaker situation, and so are less dangerous than {{A|Neutral Killing}}. ==={{A|Town Investigatives}}=== These roles can catch you red handed. The {{A|Sheriff}} may be valuable enough for mishanges if you have a {{A|Framer}}, but they can catch the {{A|Mafia}} anyways without a {{A|Disguiser}} so it's best to kill them off. {{A|Investigators}} can trap you in a box if asked to claim, so target them early. ==={{A|Town Protectives}}=== These roles can stop you from killing higher priority targets, or potentially kill you. Take them out if you think they're on an important role. ===Other {{A|Town}}=== These are either lethal or harmless depending on intelligence and information. You need them dead to win. ==={{A|Neutral Benign}} and {{A|Neutral Evil}}=== These aren't so dangerous, but they can side against you. Always keep this in mind. For {{A|Coven Expansion}} users, the {{A|Guardian Angel}} may be the only exception, as their target can be an enemy.  ==Claiming a {{A|Town}} Role== Your investigative results are: {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Mafioso}}, {{A|Pirate}}, or {{A|Ambusher}} ({{A|Pirate}} is {{A|Coven Expansion}} exclusive). ==={{A|Veteran}}=== *{{A|Veteran}} is a unique role; if there's a {{A|Veteran}} in your game, they'll likely call you out as soon as you try to claim it, and if they die you'll be immediately exposed. On the other hand, the dangers of claiming make it much more convincing if you're willing to take the risk, and you're less likely to be visited out of fear of being shot. *If you claim to be the {{A|Veteran}}, be wary of recording in your fake {{A|Last Will}} that you used alerts unless you are relatively certain that no one visited you. Having no alerts in your {{A|Last Will}} looks very sketchy, but claiming to have alerted when someone claims to have visited you is almost certain death. Claiming you are going for the Not Paranoid (win without going alert all game) {{A|Achievement}} for the {{A|Veteran}} might work, but this leaves you possibly vulnerable to rival roles coming to kill you. Some players may say that keeping a {{A|Last Will}} as a {{A|Veteran}} is not important because you do not actually gather information, or to 'not reveal whether the {{A|Veteran}} used their alerts yet', but they may want to see if any players visited you on a night that you may have alerted. *Overall, you generally may be better off not claiming {{A|Veteran}}, unless you have a {{A|Janitor}} and a {{A|Consigliere}} on your team and you time your attack just right as long as they have yet to say who they are, or if you can convince the {{A|Town}} that the dead {{A|Veteran}} was ''forged''. **Careful, {{A|Lookouts}} can catch you doing this without a {{A|Disguise}}. **This plan will automatically fail as long as at least one dead {{A|Townie}} (who was killed by a {{A|Veteran}}) outed who the real {{A|Veteran}} is in their will. ==={{Arch|Vigilante}}=== *{{A|Vigilante}} is your easiest claim, though if there's someone acting like a {{A|Jester}} or otherwise obviously evil, the {{A|Town}} might expect you to shoot them. And since it is very well known for a {{A|Mafioso}} to claim {{A|Vigilante}}, you might be hanged or executed by a {{A|Jailor}}. *If you have no {{A|Godfather}}, claiming to be a {{A|Vigilante}} can be dangerous, since a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and the {{A|Jailor}} will know that that claim indicates a possible {{A|Mafioso}} and will likely try {{A|roleblocking}} you. Claiming {{A|Veteran}} might discourage {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, but won't discourage the {{A|Jailor}}. In that situation, you should avoid claiming if at all possible, and may want to claim outside your Investigator results if necessary. *If you plan to or already have claimed to be a {{A|Vigilante}}, you should at least write a fake {{A|Last Will}} to support your claim. Keep writing each day that you have not shot anyone. Putting in some other info as to why you did not shoot that correlates to actions that happened in the course of the game will make this will much more believable. If a {{A|Vigilante}} has shot an evil role, but did not claim it, make sure to kill, clean/forge them and use their success to "Confirm" yourself as {{A|Town}}. This could backfire with a {{A|Medium}} however, and the real {{A|Vigilante}} would normally call out their shooting to confirm themselves. * A major problem for {{A|Vigilante}} claims is the fact that the {{A|Town}} may ask you to shoot someone, and failing to do so may result in being hanged. A way around this is to claim you did indeed shoot this person, claim they were immune, and hope they have {{A|Basic Defense}} to ensure your prolonged existence. You can also use this to [[bussing|buss]] the {{A|Godfather}} to confirm yourself. However, this is risky, since you may get discovered by {{A|Investigators}} who will see a different result after promotion or {{A|Tavern Keepers}} who will see no {{A|Mafia}} kill if they role-block you. ===Other Roles=== *Claiming inside your investigative results is usually a somewhat bad way to play, and other strategies may need to be adopted. Although dangerous if it backfires, you can claim something such as a {{A|Sheriff}} and throw the {{A|Random Mafia}} under the bus (if none of {{A|Town Investigative}} roles are {{A|Investigator}}) and thus be considered a "confirmed {{A|Townie}}". And in this way, you will gain the {{A|Town's}} trust. Before when you write in your {{A|Last Will}} the names of your fellow {{A|Mafia}} members, so the {{A|Town}} will believe you more and let you live, tell your {{A|Mafia}} friends to prepare their Wills and a role to claim, and experienced players will claim a better role that may help the {{A|Mafia}} more. One such example would be {{A|Investigator}} ({{A|Consigliere's}} cover), {{A|Tavern Keeper}} ({{A|Bootlegger's}} cover) or {{A|Executioner}} (Remember to say who your target is, bonus points if it's another {{A|Mafia}} member). However, this may be seen as gamethrowing, and should be discussed with the other {{A|Mafia}}. This strategy is called [[bussing]]. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{MafiosoAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{MafiosoMessages}} ==History== *{{VH|3.3.2}} **Fixed issue when {{A|Forger}} was promoted to {{A|Mafioso}} that could result in a disconnection. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. **{{A|Mafioso}} will now die to {{A|Trap}} placed on another {{A|Trapper}}. **Fixed issue where non-{{A|Mafia}} roles could be unexpectedly promoted to {{A|Mafioso}}. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} detecting {{A|Godfather}} visiting victim when {{A|Godfather}} orders {{A|Mafioso}} to kill the victim. **Fixed incorrect {{A|Tracker}} results when {{A|Mafioso}} picks one victim but {{A|Godfather}} chooses another. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} ** The {{A|Mafioso's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Mafioso.png|30x30px]]. ** Added {{A|Mafioso's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Mafioso Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.4.0.10404}} **Fixed bug where {{A|Mafioso}} would see target's {{A|defense}} being too high while the target was {{A|Jailed}}. *{{VH|1.1.1}} **No more double {{A|Mafioso}} in {{A|Ranked}}. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **Attackers will now get "Your target is immune" message when attacking {{A|Werewolf}} on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|nights}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Мафиози]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Mafia Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
