Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets!}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You may watch a person each {{A|Night}} to see who visits them. **You will only be able to recognize up to three specific people who visit your target. **You will know if more than three people visited your target, but will be unable to identify them. ***The three people you are able to recognize are selected at random. *You can see visits made (or forced by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Disguiser}}) by: **Any role that can choose a living target at {{A|Night}}. But not those that can '''only''' target themselves, even if they are witched ({{A|Survivors}} and {{A|Veterans}}). **Despite not actually visiting, some roles will be detectable by the {{A|Lookout}} if a {{A|Witch}} controls them. They include: {{A|Mediums}}, {{A|Jesters}}, {{A|Jailors}},{{A|Amnesiacs}} and the {{A|Werewolf}} on non {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}. This is because these roles still technically "visit" in their own ways, like an {{A|Amnesiac}} visiting a dead target or a dead {{A|Medium}} visiting someone who's alive to séance them. You cannot detect roles such as {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Mayor}} if they are witched, because they have no way of visiting (Unless a {{A|Disguiser}} interferes). **If a {{A|Pirate}} duels your target, you will see them visiting your target. **Any role that visits targets two players in one {{A|Night}}, like a {{A|Transporter}}/{{A|Disguiser}} will show up visiting one of their targets. *If you watch the {{A|Jailor}} and they are attacked by the {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} they jailed but did not execute, you will '''not''' see the name of the killer. (In the {{A|Werewolf}} case, you will die due to the rampaging attack). *You '''will''' be shot by a {{A|Veteran}} on alert if you choose to watch them at {{A|Night}}. *You '''will''' be stoned by a gazing {{A|Medusa}} if you choose to watch them at {{A|Night}}. *You '''will''' be obliterated by {{A|Pestilence}} if you choose to watch them or their target at {{A|Night}}. *You will die from a {{A|Werewolf}} if whoever you're watching is attacked by one. However, you will most likely know who the {{A|Werewolf}} is, which is useful to a {{A|Medium}} if there is one. **In addition, any role that only kills visitors like a {{A|Crusader}} or {{A|Ambusher}} can kill you, but you can still identify them (especially in the case of an {{A|Ambusher}}). *You will not see yourself visiting your target, but other {{A|Lookouts}} will, and you will see them. *You will not see the following roles visit your target (unless a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Disguiser}} interferes): **Any role targeting themselves with the notable exception of a {{A|Transporter}} **Any role that attacked your target visiting another (e.g. {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Werewolf}}) **{{A|Jailor}} (additionally, your visit will fail) **{{A|Godfather}} (with a {{A|Mafioso}}) **{{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} (second target) **{{A|Hex Master}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}} or final {{A|Hex}}) **{{A|Retributionist}}/{{A|Necromancer}} **{{A|Guardian Angel}} **{{A|Arsonist}} (igniting) *Due to an inconsistent bug (as of [[Version History (ToS)|Version 3.3.12]]), you will sometimes '''not''' see {{A|reanimated}} corpses visit your target. ==Strategy== *As a {{A|Lookout}}, most people won't believe your claim right away because {{A|Lookout}} is a common {{A|Executioner}} (and other evil roles) claim. Therefore, it is '''''CRUCIAL''''' to keep an updated {{A|Last Will}}. *As a {{A|Lookout}}, it's important to keep track of what's going on during the {{A|day}} to spot out potential targets for the {{A|Town}} to hang, namely the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}}, or any possible {{A|Neutral Killings}}. *A good idea if you don't have anyone you think will be targeted is to look at player names, a lot of people will target names that stick out. *While they are generally more likely to get attacked, it is not a good idea to watch people who seem loud and annoying, as they could be a {{A|Veteran}} baiting evil roles. Additionally, if it is a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, you might die from the {{A|Werewolf}} because they generally attack loud targets. *Since experienced players know that {{A|Lookouts}} will most likely hang around names that stick out, it might not be a bad idea to watch someone whose name doesn't stick out very much like "Jonathan Corwin" or "Betty Parris". *If someone visited your target at {{A|Night}} but your target did not die, you should not be too quick when telling everyone who visited since the visitor could be a fellow {{A|Townie}} such as a {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, or {{A|Investigator}}. **Then again, most {{A|Townies}} nowadays may not believe you if you wait too long to reveal yourself or your results as a {{A|Town Investigative}}. If the lobby seems to have competitive or experienced players, it may be worth posting your results right away and then asking a {{A|Town Protective}} role to be on you. *If your target mentions that they were attacked, but only one person visited them, they could be an immune role lying to seem innocent to the {{A|Town}}. Likewise, if your target is killed and they only had one visitor, either that visitor is a killing role or the target had visited a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} (if they were a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Pirate}}) that {{A|Night}}. If your target is alive but doesn't mention being {{A|roleblocked}}, {{A|transported}}, etc; the person who visited them might be a passive role, such as a {{A|Framer}} or {{A|Sheriff}}. *Keep track of who visited who and if that person says something during the {{A|day}}, such as, "I was witched last night." This way you may know what role the person who visited was. *If you are watching a target who has {{A|Defense}} get attacked, they might say nothing about it the next {{A|Day}} (since you cannot tell the difference between an attack and other visits). For example, {{A|Arsonists}}, {{A|Serial Killers}} and {{A|Godfathers}} rarely expose that they were attacked during the {{A|Night}}, so be careful and try to deduct who could be bad or good when reviewing someone's visitors. *It is important to watch a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, for several reasons: **First, this protects them. Any accusations you make against their killer will probably be believed since it's logical for a {{A|Lookout}} to watch a revealed {{A|Mayor}}; if you ''don't'' watch the {{A|Mayor}} and they die, your {{A|Lookout}} claim is unlikely to be believed. This will also allow you to identify the culprit if the {{A|Mayor}} is blackmailed by a {{A|Blackmailer}} or bitten by a {{A|Vampire}}. You can determine if the {{A|Mayor}} was bitten last {{A|Night}} by attempting to whisper to them. **Second, {{A|Mayors}} tend to attract a lot of visitors; this allows you to identify other {{A|Lookouts}}, {{A|Bodyguards}}, and {{A|Transporters}} If the {{A|Mayor}} is not blackmailed, killed, or turned into a {{A|Vampire}} (all of which tend to be obvious in one way or another), then it is fairly unlikely that any of their visitors that {{A|Night}} were evil since the other {{A|Mafia}} roles have little reason to visit them. **This information on who visited the {{A|Mayor}} may allow you to confirm your own role later on (but be cautious about revealing it unnecessarily, since it could potentially out a high-value role like the {{A|Bodyguard}}) **Be careful though, the {{A|Werewolf}} normally targets the {{A|Mayor}} because of how many people visits them. The {{A|Mafia}} may target the {{A|Mayor}} if they have a {{A|Disguiser}} or {{A|Ambusher}} and they know you're the only protection left for the {{A|Mayor}}. *If you are watching someone several {{A|Nights}} in a row and you see the same person visiting them, you might have found a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}. Try to avoid saying this to the {{A|Town}} to avoid the {{A|Mafia}} from attacking you. If your target claimed that they were attacked and saved, try to deduct who the attacker could have been by viewing their other visitors. If they are silent, though, they could also be blackmailed, so you should ask them to talk to find out. *If you see your target visiting themselves, there are only a few options for what their role could be: **They could be a {{A|Transporter}} that transported themselves with someone else. Technically, you will have been redirected to the other target, but since the {{A|Transporter}} visits both targets, you'll still see them as a visit themselves. **They could be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} who was {{A|Disguised}} as your target. If you see anyone else visit your target when this happens, it may be worth outing and questioning that visitor because they could be the {{A|Disguiser}}. **Finally, while a {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Transporter}} could make someone not on the above list self-target, in that case you would see the {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Transporter}} as a second visitor. **Therefore, if you see someone self-target as their only visitor, you have watched a {{A|Transporter}}. *{{A|Witches}} and {{A|Disguisers}} may be your worst enemy, so keep in mind if there are any of them in the game. For example, just because you saw someone visiting someone else on non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} doesn't mean that they are not the {{A|Werewolf}}, as the {{A|Werewolf}} will visit the target selected by the {{A|Witch}}, and the {{A|Disguiser}} can make it appear that the {{A|Werewolf}} visited the target. *Consider visiting someone who has been blackmailed twice (or more) in a row. The {{A|Blackmailer}} will likely return to the same player to blackmail them again the next {{A|Night}}, and if the same person is blackmailed again the next {{A|day}}, you can confirm whoever visited them as a {{A|Blackmailer}}. Note that this may not work if more than three people visit the blackmailed victim. *Sometimes, when an important role asks to be watched, you may do it if there's a high chance of them being attacked. But if they ask openly for it, then some killing roles will be scared off of attacking the said important role, leaving you free to watch others. However, this is a risky thing to do. *If you identify a {{A|Mafia Killing}} role and need to make the {{A|Town}} listen to you, one easy way to do so is to ask that a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Tavern Keeper}} target them. While this hinges on the {{A|Town}} having those roles, it costs them very little to check out one lead, so most of them will be happy to oblige. Most of the time, keeping a {{A|Mafia Killing}} {{A|Roleblocked}} or jailed is more effective than hanging them anyway, since it renders the entire {{A|Mafia}} unable to kill. Note that this is generally ineffective if there's more than 1 {{A|Mafia Killing}} or the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role was {{A|Disguised}}. *An {{A|Investigator}} may suspect you of being a {{A|Forger}}, {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, or even a {{A|Juggernaut}} once he checks you out. Prepare your {{A|Last Will}} or any other piece of proof to try and prove yourself as a {{A|Lookout}} if they start asking or accusing you. *Your results can be very effective when paired with a {{A|Spy}}. **If a {{A|Spy}} sees a {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} visit to a person on the same {{A|Night}} you're watching them, one of the people you saw visiting them must be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}. **Conversely, if a {{A|Spy}} ''doesn't'' see any {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} visits to someone you watched, anyone who visited them that {{A|Night}} is definitely not a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} respectively. Occasionally, this can be used to catch evils by process of elimination. *If your target is visited on the same {{A|Night}} that killing role kills someone else, then whoever visited them is definitely not that killer. However, remember that a member of the {{A|Mafia}} may become the killer after the fact if the current one dies. *For the most part, {{A|Mafia}} members cannot visit {{A|Mafia}}. **This has an important implication for you: Most of the time, when you see one person visiting another, at least ''one'' of the two must be non-{{A|Mafia}}; if either one is confirmed as {{A|Mafia}}, then you know the other isn't. **There is some risk that {{A|Mafia}} members can be forced to visit each other by a {{A|Witch}}, but the chance is low. **Note that a {{A|Transporter}} cannot cause problems here - your visit will ''also'' be transported, so you still know that any visitors you see tried to target your original target; absent a {{A|Witch}}, it's still impossible for both your intended target and any visitors you see to be Mafia. **A {{A|Disguiser}} '''can''' be an issue, since they can visit their own {{A|Mafia}}. If a {{A|Disguiser}} is killed, the people you saw them visit could be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}; however, they could still be the {{A|Disguiser's}} second target. *Your ability is less disrupted by {{A|Transporters}} than other {{A|Town Investigatives}}. **First, if your intended target is transported, you will probably see the {{A|Transporter}} as a visitor (since they visit both targets). **Second, since both you and all other visitors are transported, you'll still see everyone who ''intended'' to visit your original target - they'll end up at your new target along with you. **Of course, you still have to worry about {{A|Transporters}} when interpreting what happened the next morning - if the person you tried to target ends up dead, but they were transported, then you won't have seen who killed them. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{LookoutAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{LookoutMessages}} ==Trivia== *If you see that your target was visited by the same player twice on the same night, it means that one visit is real and the other visit is from someone who was {{A|disguised}} as that player. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.5}}, {{A|Lookouts}} could identity all visitors to their chosen target, rather than only 3. ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.12]] **Fixed {{A|Lookout}} seeing reanimated corpses visit twice *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.0]] **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now fool a {{A|Lookout}}. **The [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom]] Lobby role summary for {{A|Lookout}} has been updated to include a reference about the limit of identifying 3 players. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.5]] **{{A|Lookout}} now only identifies 3 of the visits, which are chosen randomly. The {{A|Lookout}} will know if more than 3 visits occurred. **Added message "More people visited your target but you couldn't identify them.". *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Lookout's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Lookout.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Lookout's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Lookout Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|Town of Salem Release]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Разведчик]] [[Category:Town Investigative roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== During the {{A|Night}}, you are able to talk with all dead players. *The dead will see any alive {{A|Mediums}} talking as "Medium". **You, as well as the dead, cannot copy your own messages into the clipboard. *You do '''not''' see other {{A|Mediums}} talking. *If you are {{A|Jailed}}, you will hear both the dead '''and''' the {{A|Jailor}}; however, only the {{A|Jailor}} will hear you, and the dead will not be able to hear you nor the {{A|Jailor}}. Once you are dead, you may target a living player by clicking the "{{A|Seance}}" button during the {{A|Day}} to talk to them for that {{A|Night}} only. *You only have 1 seance. **If multiple dead {{A|Mediums}} {{A|Seance}} the same player, the {{A|Mediums}} '''will''' hear each other. *Your target will start the {{A|Night}} with the message "A medium is talking to you!". **Multiple {{A|Mediums}} seancing the same player will generate the message as many times as there are {{A|Mediums}} seancing the player. This means that the target will also know how many {{A|Mediums}} have {{A|Seanced}} them. *The target will see any seancing {{A|Mediums}} talking as "Medium". **You, as well as the target and other seancing {{A|Mediums}}, cannot copy your own or other {{A|Medium's}} messages into the clipboard. *If your target is {{A|Jailed}}, a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}, a {{A|Vampire}}, or the {{A|Jailor}}, they will be able to talk with you and the {{A|Jailor}}, the other members of their faction, or the {{A|Jailed}} target respectively. **In these circumstances, any message the {{A|Seanced}} player sends will be shown to all players that can hear them. For instance, a {{A|Seanced}} {{A|Mafia}} member cannot talk separately with their team and the {{A|Medium}}/{{A|Mediums}} seancing them, which means that any message the {{A|Mafia}} member sends can be seen by ''both'' the {{A|Mafia}} and the {{A|Medium}}/{{A|Mediums}} seancing them. *If your target is a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, they will still hear the {{A|Vampire chat}}. *While seancing, you are still able to hear the dead, but the dead won't hear you. ==Strategy== *As a {{A|Medium}}, you are capable of many useful things: **You can relay what the dead are saying back to the living. **You can confirm other {{A|Mediums}}. **You are one of two roles ({{A|Medium}} and {{A|Janitor}}) that are able to figure out {{A|Cleaned}} roles directly. ***However, remember that evil roles can be {{A|Cleaned}} because of the {{A|Transporter}} or the {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, and they can lie about their role to throw off the {{A|Town}}. Therefore, if there is a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, there is a chance that the {{A|Cleaned}} player is evil. **You are the only role that is able to figure out the true roles of {{A|Forged}} players, as well as {{A|Stoned}} players. ***However, just like {{A|Cleaned}} roles, it is possible that they are an evil role lying. **You can get the last result of a {{A|Town Investigative}} role just before they died. **You can find if anyone had incriminating evidence against another the {{A|Night}} they died. such as a {{A|Vigilante}} who shot someone with defense. **You can find out what happened to players before they died, such as if they were {{A|Blackmailed}}, {{A|Roleblocked}}, controlled by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, etc. **You can discover who a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Pirate}} or {{A|Jailor}} visited if killed by a non-Cautious {{A|Serial Killer}} that they targeted with their abilities. While {{A|Werewolf}} and {{A|Pestilence}} have similar mechanics to the {{A|Serial Killer}}, the dead cannot confirm who they are (although they may have suspicions based on what the player said, and may be able to tell you who they targeted that {{A|Night}}). The only exception to this is {{A|Jailor}} jailing {{A|Pestilence}}, as they will know if they targeted {{A|Pestilence}}. Additionally, a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Pirate}} may lie about who the {{A|Serial Killer}} is. **If there's an {{A|Ambusher}} in the game, you can find out who they are by talking to the player who was killed by the {{A|Ambusher}}. **If there's {{A|Medusa}} in the game, you can find out who they are by talking to the player who was {{A|Stoned}} by {{A|Medusa}}. **You get the thoughts from the deceased on who they think is {{A|Town}}, {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, or {{A|Neutral}}. **You can talk to other {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} members or {{A|Neutral}} roles to possibly get some more information using your seance. ***Be careful of any dead {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} members who explicitly reveal their fellow teammates, as they may be lying to throw off the {{A|Town}}. However, if you find out that they ''are'' telling the truth, then they are eligible to be reported for gamethrowing. *By giving your name to dead {{A|Townies}} and asking them to check the names of other players that claim {{A|Medium}}, you can figure out who is actually a {{A|Medium}} or not. And remember, '''always''' state your name/position to the dead at the start of every {{A|Night}} to ensure that all new dead players will know your identity, while also removing any doubt of you having been converted to a {{A|Vampire}}. **However, this can let players communicating externally know who you are. If you can prove that they are talking outside of the game or admit to it, feel free to report them for cheating. **You can also prove yourself by getting secret information from the dead. Ask them for the contents of any [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] they sent or received so you can use it to prove yourself to whoever was at the other end, although this still leaves the possibility of you being a {{A|Blackmailer}}. A strategy that removes this flaw is to ask anyone who was {{A|Jailed}} to tell you what they discussed with the {{A|Jailor}} (or, alternatively, ask the {{A|Jailor}} what they discussed with everyone they {{A|Jailed}}), then use this to prove you're a {{A|Medium}} if necessary. ***You could even suggest that the remaining players whisper passcodes to each other; later, if a {{A|Town}} member dies, you can get their passcode from them and use it to confirm yourself. *'''Important''': Your job in the {{A|Town}} is to carry on the discussion after players die. It's beneficial having dead players discuss freely without any doubts once you're dead, as {{A|Townies}} can give you useful information. This role can potentially change who wins and who loses, so discuss wisely. *Don't always trust what a {{A|cleaned}} victim tells you since they could be a {{A|Neutral}} role, {{A|Coven}} member or possibly even a {{A|Mafia}} member trying to throw you off with false information. Ask the deceased for proof before you tell everyone that someone is guilty. The dead can still be wrong or lie. *Also, watch if a member of the {{A|Mafia}} was killed by {{A|Mafia}} as they could actually be a forged {{A|Townie}}. Like a {{A|Cleaned}} victim, they can also lie about the forgery to get a {{A|Transporter}} killed, so ask for proof before accusing someone. *You can speak to a just-hanged {{A|Jester}} and try to convince them to haunt your preferred target. While {{A|Jesters}} have no particular reason to listen to you, they often do; many of them want to have a big impact on the game and would rather haunt a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role rather than a random {{A|Townie}}. **Reverse psychology also works: if a {{A|Jester}} just got hanged, beg them not to haunt your preferred target. They may pick that target just to annoy you, but in reality, it is what you wanted. Note that this is less effective in general as a strategy. *Having two {{A|Mediums}} can be the key to success in a round. If one of them dies, they can take info from the newly dead and tell this to the other {{A|Medium}}. They can also confirm each other by the dead almost instantly, provided they say their name. **It is recommended to ask the dead every {{A|Night}} if you are both {{A|Mediums}} in order to clear any suspicion of either of you being {{A|Vampires}}. Since the dead can lie, a safer method is to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] each other a message from the dead every {{A|Day}}. *Keep in mind that none of the above matters if nobody knows you exist, so make your presence known as soon as possible at {{A|Night}}. **However, there might be some benefits to '''NOT''' revealing at Night. Particularly, by not revealing yourself at {{A|Night}} once a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} is dead, there is a chance they might inadvertently reveal their own teammates, thinking there is no danger. ===Proving yourself=== Even if you lack incriminating evidence from the dead, there are still ways to make the {{A|Town}} less doubtful of you. *The easiest way for a {{A|Medium}} to gain the trust of the {{A|Town}} is by copying and pasting messages from the dead, since it is difficult and time-consuming for an evildoer to create a fake conversation. **For the Web and Steam versions of the game, hovering your cursor over a message will allow you to copy it by clicking on the button on the right side of the message. You can then use the '''Control + V''' (or '''Command + V''' if using a Macbook) shortcut on your keyboard to paste the message in the {{A|Chat}} or in your {{A|Last Will}}. **For the Mobile version of the game, simply tapping and holding on a message will show a green progress bar. Once it disappears, you have successfully copied the message. Tapping and holding in the {{A|Chat}} box or your {{A|Last Will}} should prompt a "Paste" button. *You should repeat the dead's thoughts to the {{A|Town}} every {{A|Day}}. *Keeping an organized {{A|Last Will}} is important and makes your claim seem more legitimate. Ideally, what happens to you during the {{A|Night}} and what the dead are saying should both appear in your {{A|Last Will}}. *Below is an example of a format you can use: **''N1: Nothing'' **''N2: Controlled'' **''N3: [[Role blocked]]'' **''N4: **''Dead chat as of N4:'' **''Giles Corey: I trust Martha's claim.'' **''Jonathan Corwin: There might be an {{A|Arsonist}}.'' *In order to prevent reaching the character limit, simply delete the dead chat from your {{A|Last Will}} once you've posted it and update the {{A|Night}} number on line 5. *In the case of multiple {{A|Mediums}}, proving yourself should be an easy task, as you will both have the same messages. ====Spotting a fake {{A|Medium}}==== There are certain clues, some more subtle than others, that can help you identify if a {{A|Medium}} claim is lying. *'''Refuses to cooperate''' - While not always the case, a {{A|Medium}} that refuses to tell the {{A|Town}} information is usually evil. *'''Wrong format''' - The format of a pasted message is "(Name): (message)". The first fake example shows the usage of "-" instead of ":", the second fake example shows the usage of ";" instead of ":", and the last fake example shows two spaces between the ":" and the message. **Real message - ''Abigail Hobbs: I was controlled.'' **Faked message - ''Abigail Hobbs - I was controlled.'' **Faked message - ''Abigail Hobbs; I was controlled.'' **Faked message - ''Abigail Hobbs: I was controlled.'' *'''Dead's messages do not match with their personality/writing''' - For example, before Samuel Parris died, they always started their sentences in lowercase and often used emoticons, but, according to the {{A|Medium}}, are now talking in uppercase and without emoticons. A sudden change in writing style could be a sign of a faked message. **Real message - ''Samuel Parris: thx for the help :)'' **Faked message - ''Samuel Parris: They have to be evil!'' *'''Wrong capitalization''' - If the [[name]]'s capitalization is wrong, the message is fake. **Real message - ''John Willard: I doubt they were {{A|Framed}}.'' **Faked message - ''John willard: I doubt they were {{A|Framed}}.'' *'''Spaces between messages''' - When pasting multiple messages at once, the game does not put a space between them. **Real messages - ''Abigail Hobbs: I was controlled.John Willard: I doubt they were {{A|Framed}}.'' **Faked messages - ''Abigail Hobbs: I was controlled. John Willard: I doubt they were {{A|Framed}}.'' *'''Their own messages''' - A {{A|Medium}} cannot copy their own messages. **Real messages - ''William Phips: How was your Day?William Phips: That's good to hear'' **Faked messages - ''William Phips: How was your Day?Medium: It was fine.William Phips: That's good to hear'' ===Using your Seance=== *If you die, do not leave, even if you die {{A|Night 1}}. You are still able to speak to a living player once through your {{A|Seance}}. *Don't use your {{A|Seance}} immediately after you die. Save it until you have enough useful information and have identified a living player you trust to use it. **Do not save your {{A|Seance}} ''too'' long. Many {{A|Mediums}} end up saving it until it's too late. Remember, you have to push the {{A|Seance}} button the {{A|Day}} ''before'' the {{A|Night}} you talk with someone, and the {{A|Town}} usually needs to still have a majority the next {{A|Day}} or they won't be able to do anything with the information you provide. **Practically speaking, this means the {{A|Town}} usually needs to have at least two more {{A|Townies}} than the {{A|Mafia}} on the end of the {{A|Day}} you initiate the {{A|Seance}} (the {{A|Mafia}} will most likely kill one of the {{A|townies}}, leaving the {{A|Town}} with only one more member than the {{A|Mafia}}, allowing them to hang one), which leaves you a very narrow window to {{A|Seance}} effectively. *Using your {{A|Seance}} on any role that has the ability to speak at {{A|Night}} (e.g. a {{A|Jailor}}, or any member of the {{A|Mafia}}) can lead to a very confusing and often irritating conversation, since other players will be speaking at the same time as you, yet neither of you can see the other's messages. In most cases, it's a detriment to the player you're speaking to from beyond the grave. **You could also use your {{A|Seance}} on someone who is suspected of being {{A|Mafia}}; once the {{A|Seance}} begins, you could take note if it seems what they say is to be directed towards other players. If what they say sounds like they are conversing with other members, then you just possibly found a member yourself. The problem with this is you have no way of directly telling the {{A|town}} about this, unless another {{A|Medium}} seances. *You could try to lie to a dead {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} member or {{A|Vampire}}. You can claim that you have wasted your seance, and then after about 30 seconds, ask that player who their last team members are, or try to guess and ask if you are correct. You may have to convince that player that you've used your seance. Do note that they could still lie about it or might not even tell you anything at all. If you do manage to get information, then use your {{A|Seance}} on a trusted {{A|Town}} member and pass it to them. **In order to make it even more believable, do not talk for the entirety of a {{A|Night}}. The moment you talk, you are revealing to the dead {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} that you did not use your seance, as normally you would be talking with your target, not the dead chat. **If there are only {{A|Townies}} in the [[graveyard]], you could use this strategy as a collective once an evil role dies. Evildoers are less likely to suspect they're being fooled if multiple players are pretending that you've used your seance. *If it turns out there are two {{A|Mediums}}, you can use your {{A|Seance}} on a third trusted player once you're dead to ensure the {{A|Town}} doesn't believe the second {{A|Medium}} claim is fake. **If there are two {{A|Mediums}}, keep in mind that you get an achievement for the first time you {{A|Seance}} a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}}. If you happen to get any of these achievements, make sure to alert the other {{A|Medium}} the next {{A|Night}}. *Occasionally, if there is more than one way for the {{A|Town}} to access the living via a second {{A|Medium}} it can be useful to {{A|Seance}} someone who you think is evil and to try and get them to confess. *If you use your {{A|Seance}} on someone with useful information, always tell them to ''put it in their {{A|Last Will}} immediately''. If you've identified them as reliable {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Mafia}} probably has too, and might kill them that {{A|Night}}; if they don't write your information in their will, it might be lost. Remember: the {{A|Last Will}} only saves if you close it. *You can instruct the player you're using your {{A|Seance}} on how to use their ability in a particular way that very {{A|Night}}, such as telling a {{A|Vigilante}} who to shoot. If the dead have identified a definite member of the {{A|Mafia}}, it can be valuable to anyone you think may need a little push to do the right thing. **This can be crucial for the {{A|Veteran}}: Suppose there are 2 players left alive, the {{A|Veteran}} and the {{A|Mafioso}}. In these 1 v 1 scenarios, there is usually a lot of discussion in the [[graveyard]]. It is likely that the {{A|Mafia}} members will celebrate too early and tell the others that the {{A|Mafioso}} is attacking the {{A|Veteran}}, so you {{A|Seance}} the {{A|Veteran}} without announcing it. Your assumption was correct, so you quickly tell the {{A|Veteran}} to alert, as you can still read the dead chat while seancing. The {{A|Mafioso}} will now die to the {{A|Veteran}} and your play won the game. *If you do not have any useful information, you could {{A|Seance}} the {{A|Mafia Killing}} and tell them who to kill to try and confuse them. By saying things such as "Kill Addfire", "The {{A|Veteran}} is out of alerts, kill them", "Don't kill Carbon", or even "Octoling is in {{A|Jail}}, don’t target them", you may cause the {{A|Mafia}} to lose. **This is especially helpful in situations in the {{A|Town Traitor]}} game mode if the Traitor {{A|Medium|Mafia}} is dead, as the {{A|Mafia}} might believe that you are the Traitor giving them advice **However, keep in mind that [[Town of Salem Rules|spamming]] is discouraged significantly as you can be banned, so when using this strategy, try to use this strategy effectively while also respecting the game's rules. *Choosing to {{A|Seance}} any member of the {{A|Mafia}} after you are certain you do not have any useful information, then annoying them with useless information or repeating over and over again that a confirmed evil is actually a {{A|Townie}}, could cause the {{A|Mafia}} to get distracted and make a mistake, tipping the game in favor of the {{A|Town}}. **This strategy is frowned upon in general, so use sparingly. ==How to Help the {{A|Medium}}== *It should be simple enough to realize this, but if you die, '''DON'T LEAVE.''' The {{A|Medium}} relies on dead players being in the game to be useful. A [[Graveyard|graveyard]] with no in-game players is as good as empty to a {{A|Medium}}. *Any talk is good talk when a {{A|Medium}} is present. Keep the [[Chat (ToS)|Chat]] at {{A|Night}} lively, and post any leads or suspicions you can. It may just tip the balance of the game. *Anything that has been whispered to you that you believe is somewhat suspicious should be relayed to the {{A|Medium}} as this is the only way to tell this information to anyone. *Are you a {{A|Jester}} that just got [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]? Let the {{A|Medium}} know who you plan to target. If you happen to be targeting them, they’ll likely let you know. *Did you attack an immune role, but never got the word out? Let the {{A|Medium}} know so they can relay it to the living. *If you have managed to visit a {{A|Veteran}} and didn't get to write who you've last visited in your {{A|Last Will}}, you could relay who the {{A|Veteran}} is to a {{A|Medium}}, so that they can easily confirm the {{A|Veteran}} in case another player counter claims being the {{A|Veteran}} in order to avoid suspicion or trying to get hanged as the {{A|Jester}}. However if you're playing a {{A|Town Traitor}} gamemode, you'll need to confirm if the {{A|Medium}} can be trusted first before giving your valuable information to them *If you have managed to visit a {{A|Medusa}} or you have been the victim of an {{A|Ambusher}}, you could relay the information on who the {{A|Medusa}} and/or {{A|Ambusher}} is to the Medium in for sweet {{A|Jester}}-style revenge from the grave. *If you're playing a {{A|Town Traitor}} gamemode and you're sure that the {{A|Jailor}} is a Town Traitor, you could relay that information to the {{A|Medium}}, so that the {{A|Town}} can rest at ease knowing that they have found the Town Traitor and will take away a valuable evil member for the opposing faction. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{MediumAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{MediumMessages}} ==Trivia== *The "{{A|Medium's}} Curse" is a popular joke that {{A|Mediums}} always get killed on the first {{A|Night}} when their role is "basically useless", despite the player not having revealed their role. Players will usually refer to it whenever it occurs, but not mention it if a {{A|Medium}} stays alive for more than ~2 {{A|Days}}. If a {{A|Medium}} is one of the last alive, they might say that the "{{A|Medium}}’s Curse" has failed or finally been lifted. The {{A|Medium's}} Curse is similar to the less popular "{{A|Retributionist's}} Curse" or "{{A|Amnesiac's}} Curse". *The "Hogan Scenario" is when two {{A|Mediums}} are in the game and their miscommunication causes a snafu during the {{A|Day}}. The name comes from a character who was a second {{A|Medium}}, and the quote comes from his defense portion - "You're stupid brothers!". *The {{A|Medium}} received a buff in {{VH|Version 0.3.0}} which was released on June 10th of 2014. Prior to then, the {{A|Medium}} would use its ability in the Daytime to select one player from the [[Graveyard|graveyard]] to talk to anonymously during the {{A|Night}}. In addition, once the {{A|Medium}} was dead, they did not have a {{A|Seance}} available to communicate with the living. *According to a poll made by [[User:LevinSnakesRise|LevinSnakesRise]] the {{A|Medium}} is the most hated role in Town of Salem which had 304 votes, saying "you were just a sitting duck", waiting to be killed. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.1}} **Fixed issue where roles that were forged and died as {{A|Medium}} saw {{A|Seance}} buttons during the {{A|Day}}. *{{VH|3.3.0}} **The "Cancel Seance" button for {{A|Medium}} will no longer improperly change back to "Seance" when {{A|Night}} transition starts. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **{{A|Medium}} is now shown with blue text instead of grey text in the [[graveyard]] when talking. **The {{A|Medium's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Medium.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Medium's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Medium Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|Beta 0.3.0}} **The {{A|Medium}} no longer has the ability to select a dead player from the [[graveyard]] during the {{A|Day}} to talk to for the {{A|Night}}. **The {{A|Medium}} can now {{A|Seance}} a living player during the {{A|Day}} to talk to for the {{A|Night}} while dead. **The {{A|Medium}} can now [[Chat (ToS)|chat]] with the entire [[graveyard]] during the {{A|Night}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Медиум]] [[Category:Town Support roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE: {{Amne|Survivor}}}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Survivor}}[[File:RoleIcon Survivor.png|thumb|left|100px]]
{{Amne|(Surv)|Survivor}} |alignment={{A|Neutral Benign}} |icon=RoleIcon Amnesiac.png |actionself= Uses a bulletproof vest |abilities=Put on a bulletproof vest at night. |attributestext=Putting on a bulletproof vest gives you Basic defense.
You can only use the bulletproof vest 4 times. |summary=You are a neutral character who just wants to live. |investigator = '''Classic Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvRes3}}.

'''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvResCVN3}}. |consigliere= Your target simply wants to live. They must be a {{A|Survivor}}. |goal= Live until the end of the game. |winswith= '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven}}'''
'''{{A|Arsonists}}'''
'''{{A|Serial Killers}}'''
'''{{A|Vampires}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |mustkill=N/A }} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You have four bulletproof vests. Using one gives you {{A|Basic Defense}} for that {{A|night}}. **You will still use up your vest even if you are not attacked. **If you are [[Transporter (ToS)|transported]] or [[Witch (ToS)|con]][[Coven Leader|trolled]], you will still use your bulletproof vest on yourself. **You will not use your bulletproof vest if you are [[Role blocking|role blocked]]. *If a {{A|Vampire}} bites you, you will be converted into a {{A|Vampire}} unless you used your vest or were protected. *In the event of a draw or a wipeout, you will still win the game if you are alive. ==Strategy== {{A|Survivor}} is one of the toughest roles to play as, despite how easy the conditions might seem. Despite your only goal being to survive to the end of the game, there are numerous things that could go wrong. Evil roles might think you're a {{A|Neutral Killing}} trying to get away with a {{A|Survivor}} claim, and the {{A|Town}} doesn't have to consider your existence for their secured victory. However, being a free-willed loner also gives you the advantage of not caring who you win with. Multiple factions might want to get you to side with them as an extra vote, and the possibility of you saying out loud who you're supporting could be your demise.  ===When to use your bulletproof vest=== *If you feel your life may be at stake one {{A|night}}, be sure to wear the bulletproof vest and protect yourself. However, if you DO get attacked, you might be called out as having immunity and be drawn to suspicion. If you've claimed earlier in the game, you most likely will be passed off as a {{A|Survivor}} and be left alone. However, if you get {{A|doused}} by an {{A|Arsonist}} or mauled by a {{A|Werewolf}}, whether you use your bulletproof vest or not won't matter as your bulletproof vest does not protect you from those attacks. *The more people are left alive, the less the chance that you will get randomly targeted. If you do not plan on claiming {{A|Survivor}}, save your bulletproof vests until you feel it is too dangerous to go unprotected. If you do plan on claiming {{A|Survivor}}, feel free to use a bulletproof vest or two early to make sure you don't get killed before claiming. *A balance between looking suspicious and looking like a {{A|Townie}} should be found. Always say something {{A|day}} 1, as this will distract the {{A|Mafia}} from attacking you, thinking that you could be a {{A|Veteran}}. Say things during the chat, but try to not make accusations or say anything that makes you look intelligent or, conversely, makes you look like a childish spammer. Stay in the middle ground to avoid attention and save a few bulletproof vests. *If you don't feel safe claiming early in the game because you don't know how many {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles there are, then use your bulletproof vests more often. Usually, when you get farther in the game you will know the identities or the presence of any killing roles, and you can claim during that time. Either way safe or not, claiming right on {{A|day}} 1 and using your bulletproof vest the next two {{A|nights}} usually can prove your innocence if you are attacked by the {{A|Mafia}} to prove your worth. If you aren't attacked and there is an {{A|Investigator}} that checked you during the game that dies, you can be proved that way. *If you do claim {{A|Survivor}} on {{A|day}} 1, you might want to consider using your bulletproof vest on {{A|night}} two if you suspect there might be an aggressive {{A|Vigilante}}. {{A|Vigilantes}} can shoot {{A|Survivors}} to prove themselves to {{A|Jailors}}, or just prove their innocence anytime. ===Claiming {{A|Survivor}}=== *Choosing to claim {{A|Survivor}} has become easier after the {{A|Investigator}} results were changed, but if you choose to claim {{A|Survivor}} '''before''' being forced to by a possible {{A|Investigator}}, keep these things in mind: **Some {{A|Townies}} may consider [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]] {{A|Survivors}} because they don't trust you or they want to make sure you will not side with their enemies (If they are in risk of losing majority). **You should '''ALWAYS''' consider if you think revealing as a {{A|Survivor}} is worth it. If you really think about it, you are just a {{A|Neutral}} to the {{A|Town}}. On one hand, there is no real reason for {{A|Townies}} to [[hang]] you unless they are about to lose majority to the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}. However, on the other hand, if the {{A|Town}} doesn't have any real leads, the {{A|Townies}} may hang you since you are clearly non-{{A|Town}}. And if they don't hang you during the day, you could be executed by the {{A|Jailor}} or shot by a {{A|Vigilante}} that night, again, since you are clearly non-{{A|Town}}. Due to this factor, think about if it's really worth revealing. But you must think fast, as claiming {{A|Survivor}} later on in the game is generally more suspicious than claiming earlier. ***{{A|Survivors}} who do not claim early game, more notably on {{A|day}} 1, are often targeted by {{A|Townies}} if no other leads are present, or are the first to be chosen out of a {{A|Psychic}} will. Claiming on {{A|day}} 1 can protect you from being suspected early but it also comes with its own risks. ***If there is a {{A|Juggernaut}}, revealing on the first {{A|day}} is likely going to lead to death on the second {{A|night}} due to the fact that {{A|Survivors}} are a priority target to level up due to lack of {{A|Powerful Defense}}. With that said, if you plan on claiming early but don't feel comfortable, do it on the third {{A|day}}. If there was a {{A|Juggernaut}} kill that {{A|day}}, smart players will realize the concept behind this but can be troublesome if there weren't any. ***If {{A|Medusa}} {{A|Stoned}} someone, you may be drawn under heavier suspicion of being {{A|Medusa}} since you share their investigative results. ***A {{A|Transporter}} is a huge threat to you if you do claim {{A|Survivor}}; since they know you're not {{A|Town}} and are unlikely to be attacked, they're likely to transport you with anyone they think is {{A|Town}}, especially themselves, utilizing you as a "human shield". If there seems to be a {{A|Transporter}}, you may want to avoid revealing as a {{A|Survivor}}; or you may want to start using your bulletproof vest once you do. **The {{A|Jailor}} may execute you on suspicion of you being a {{A|Witch}}, a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role, or even a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. If you're jailed ''before'' publicly claiming a role, it's usually a bad idea to tell the {{A|Jailor}} you're a {{A|Survivor}} since, having already wasted their {{A|night}} jailing you, they have little incentive to not just execute you if you're clearly non-{{A|Town}}. In that situation, come up with a suitable {{A|Town}} role instead, ideally with a fake {{A|Last Will}}. A good claim is {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Doctor}}, since they are easy to make up {{A|Last Wills}} for. Note that this is just for when jailed -- it is generally a bad idea for {{A|Survivors}} to claim {{A|Town}} roles publicly if they can avoid it since you also need to avoid getting targeted by the {{A|Mafia}}. ***However, saying that you will side with them because they did not execute you could possibly work if there is no more claim space to tell the {{A|Jailor}}. Be careful, however, as aggressive {{A|Jailors}} could more than likely kill you instead. ***You may also beg to not be executed and vote wherever the {{A|Town}} votes, however, if you have been rude and annoying the entire game, this will probably not work. **Smart killers are likely to pass you by if they feel that they have more important targets (i.e. everyone they can't win with), and the {{A|Godfather}} may see you as a late-game voting asset. However, keep in mind that if you side with anyone other than them or if they suspect you being a {{A|Mayor}} pretending to be a {{A|Survivor}}, they may kill you. *An uncommon strategy is to pretend to be a {{A|Jester}}, because people might think you are actually a {{A|Jester}} and leave you alone for the early part of the game. This strategy is used very rarely by {{A|Survivors}}, but is common for some {{A|Neutral Killings}} or {{A|Mafia}} roles like the {{A|Godfather}}. This means it is very dangerous, as you can be executed or killed by the {{A|Town}} or other evils easily. *Occasionally, someone else may claim to be a {{A|Survivor}}. This person may be an actual second {{A|Survivor}}, a killer with {{A|Basic Defense}} or higher, a {{A|Jester}}, or even a {{A|Townie}}. **If you doubt the existence of a fellow {{A|Survivor}}, make sure to claim your role as well. If you do not, you may get [[hanged]] later, since the earlier, other claims may seem more trustworthy. **You can also choose not to challenge their claim and see what happens. If you feel adventurous, you can whisper them about being the real {{A|Survivor}} and ask them not to kill you (in case they are a killer). **If you suspect them of being a {{A|night}} killer, you can try to convince the {{A|Town}} to [[hang]] them; if you catch a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Arsonist}} this way, you can usually safely reveal that you knew they were lying because you're the ''real'' {{A|Survivor}}. This only works, of course, in role-lists where only one or two {{A|Survivors}} are possible. *If you do not want to risk being targeted because you are a {{A|Survivor}}, you can choose '''not''' to reveal yourself early. Waiting until a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} checks you are usually your best bet. When they ask during the {{A|day}}, tell them your role as quickly as possible to avoid accidental [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]]. *In {{A|All Any}}, the {{A|Town}} doesn't know how many people it has, so it's more dangerous for them to [[hang]] someone who could side with them. Additionally, in {{A|All Any}}, {{A|Jesters}} are more common, making it dangerous to [[hang]] you out of hand. *Routinely highlighting the tendency of evil roles to use {{A|Survivor}} as a scapegoat, aka the ''lampshade defense'', may dissuade evil roles and even unproven town from doing so as well as earn sympathy. Do this before anyone has the chance to call you out or even attack you. *If you have chosen not to claim on {{A|day 1}}, and the {{A|Town}} has majority and there is one {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles left, you may want to have a fake {{A|Last Will}} claiming a simple {{A|Town}} role so they don't [[hang]] you under the suspicion that you are evil. ===After Surviving an {{A|Attack}}=== *If you are attacked at {{A|night}}, and protect yourself with your bulletproof vest, your troubles aren't necessarily over; whoever attacked you is likely to reveal that you have a higher {{A|Defense}} value than their {{A|Attack}} value in their {{A|Death Note}}, which will make the {{A|Town}} suspect you to be a {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, or (if not revealed by the {{A|Mafia}}) {{A|Godfather}}. Any of these suspicions can get you [[hanged]]. *One option is to immediately reveal that you're a {{A|Survivor}} after being attacked. Claiming after being attacked is generally riskier than claiming at the start of the game since the {{A|Town}} might assume you're an evil role trying to explain your {{A|Basic Defense}}, but it still gives you better chances than claiming after you're accused. It's always best to claim earlier on unless you're in a {{A|Juggernaut}} game. *You can also wait and see; not every attacker reveals their targets having a higher {{A|Defense}} value than their {{A|Attack}} value immediately (and they may hit someone else whose {{A|Defense}} value is higher than their {{A|Attack}} value, get [[Role blocking|role blocked]], etc, preventing their next {{A|Death Note}} from getting out for a while.) Reacting too quickly might put you in more danger than just waiting quietly. *An alternative option after blocking an attack with your bulletproof vest is to act like an {{A|Executioner}}; claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} and accuse someone you think is {{A|Town}}. Your attackers are likely to be evil, and if they think you're an {{A|Executioner}}, they might not reveal you, since {{A|Executioners}} are on their side. This is risky as you could get hung as an {{A|Executioner}} or exposed by an {{A|Investigator}}, among other things. *You can also claim {{A|Bodyguard}}, since they also have a bulletproof vest; however, since they only get one, this can be a harder thing to convince the {{A|Town}}. It also violates your investigation results, and {{A|Godfathers}} and {{A|Arsonists}} also claim it. Use this only as a last resort, as a revealed {{A|Mayor}} might die anytime and people will suspect why you didn't protect them. It can also be thought of an {{A|Arsonist}} attempting to explain their defense. *Claiming you were healed might cloud the issue a bit, but be warned an active {{A|Doctor}} will claim to have not healed you, and you could be in trouble. Fortunately, you can also try to convince the {{A|Town}} that there is a secret {{A|Doctor}}, or that you are a {{A|Doctor}} yourself that self-healed getting away with a {{A|Survivor}} claim so you can live to end-game. However, {{A|Doctor}} claims tend to be attacked by Evils, so this is a bad idea. *You can also claim to have been transported, but it's usually obvious when there's an active {{A|Transporter}}, and people will generally expect the {{A|Transporter}} to step forwards and substantiate your claim anyway. *If you survive an attack from the {{A|Mafia}}, then you should not use your bulletproof vest the next {{A|night}} unless you think there is a {{A|Transporter}} or an aggressive {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}}. Since {{A|Survivors}} are not a threat to the {{A|Mafia}}, they will most likely move onto another target to try and get closer to having the majority. They won't attack you twice, as you had {{A|Basic Defense}} last attack, so doing it again is rather stupid. You may be outed in their {{A|Death Note}}, however. ===Who to side with=== *The faster the game ends, the better; you only have four bulletproof vests, and they can't protect you from everything. Therefore, you usually want to side with whoever can win the fastest. *Generally speaking, you should help vote up anyone who starts getting votes. This ends the game more quickly. Additionally, should you help vote up a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, it will usually clear you of suspicion of being part of the {{A|Mafia}}. Vote innocent if there's any risk of a {{A|Jester}}. *Helping to vote up an obvious {{A|Jester}} and then voting innocent, on the other hand, can be useful; if it works, two people will die, making the game end faster and helping you win. However, this could backfire, as voting innocent may be seen as very suspicious. *If you claim {{A|Survivor}}, the {{A|Town}} will expect you to vote with them. While the {{A|Mafia}} might kill you if you vote against them, your bulletproof vests can't protect yourself from a [[hang]]. Therefore, once you've claimed, you should usually vote with the {{A|Town}} (and use your bulletproof vest afterward) unless you're certain the {{A|Mafia}} has won. *If the {{A|Mafia}} finds you and tries to pressure you to vote with them, try to evaluate how close they are to winning. If they're likely to win immediately with your help, you should probably take it. On the other hand, if they're doing badly, you might be better off exposing whoever contacted you, then using your bulletproof vest against any retaliation ('''BUT''' beware of {{A|Consorts}}; they can prevent you from using your vests). ** Note that {{A|Mafia}} efforts to pressure you will often be a bluff. After all, while they certainly want you to vote with them, they don't ''need'' to kill you to win; even if you're aggressively working against them, your only ability is to make them waste attacks if they go after you when you use a vest. Almost everyone else in the game is a higher priority for them to kill than you are, meaning their killers' time is best spent elsewhere. A rational {{A|Mafia}} will almost never attack a confirmed {{A|Survivor}}... with the obvious caveat that not all players are rational. *Siding with the {{A|Coven}} can be easier and resembles siding with the {{A|Mafia}}. However, the {{A|Hex Master}} needs you hexed to perform their {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}, and {{A|Medusa}} can easily kill you if they have the {{A|Necronomicon}} and you seem like a threat. *If you're running low on bulletproof vests or there's a {{A|Consort}}, it becomes more dangerous to defy the {{A|Mafia}} or to vote up a confirmed (or likely) member of the {{A|Mafia}}; in that case, it might be best to sit back and hope the {{A|Town}} either fails to notice you or loses the majority and their {{A|Jailor}} before it can go after you. *Be careful claiming {{A|Survivor}} if there are {{A|Vampires}} in the game, as they may attempt to bite you to force your hand into joining them. However, they might assume that you are a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, who you share results with. *Although your bulletproof vest will save you from most attacks, it can't protect you from the {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Medusa}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, or {{A|Pestilence}} and the increased number of attacks from the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}} can make it hard to block everything. Worse, evil roles (most commonly {{A|Neutral Killings}}) sometimes claim {{A|Survivor}} to explain their {{A|Basic Defense}}, so having them in the game can lead the {{A|Town}} to [[hang]] you. Even though you can theoretically win with them, it's usually to your advantage to help track them down and [[hang]] them as soon as possible. *However, in the endgame, sometimes it can be a good idea to side with the {{A|Neutral Killing}}, so that they don't kill you. This is common for {{A|Survivors}}, as they feel a sense of solidarity for their fellow {{A|Neutrals}}. *As tempting as it may be, taking a side as a {{A|Survivor}} will only get you killed by the people on the other team. So, try not to vote a person to put on trial and if someone does get on trial, abstain as much as possible, unless the game is almost over and you can guarantee that one side will win.  ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{SurvivorAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{SurvivorMessages}} ==Trivia== *According to a poll made by [[User:LevinSnakesRise|LevinSnakesRise]], the {{A|Survivor}} is the fifth most hated role in Town of Salem, with 99 votes (2 more than {{A|Mafioso}} who had 97 votes) saying they felt like they did nothing but sit there and wait to die, or on rare occasions, win. *Some evils, more often {{A|Neutral Killing}}, {{A|Neutral Chaos}}, and factional evils, will commonly claim {{A|Survivor}} early to divert suspicion early. This strategy has become common enough where {{A|Survivors}} are often directly targeted by {{A|Townies}} due to the little risk of hanging a known non-{{A|Townie}}. *In addition, {{A|Mayor}} and {{A|Jailor}} sometimes claim {{A|Survivor}} to escape the notice of the {{A|Mafia}}. However, this means that some killers will attack {{A|Survivor}} claims. ==History== *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Survivor's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Survivor.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Survivor's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Survivor Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Vampires}} can no longer convert through a used vest. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Benign roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Detection Immune]]

Only you will see the cleaned targets[[wikipedia:Sic|[sic]]] role and last will.

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== You can choose a target to {{A|Clean}} each {{A|Night}}. Your {{A|Cleaning}} attempt will be successful if your target dies for '''any''' reason, including leaving the game. However, it is most common that the player dies by a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, as you can see who can potentially die that night.  *The cause of death will still be revealed to the {{A|Town}}, even if it is a {{A|Bodyguard}} dying by guarding someone, or a {{A|Vigilante}} dying of guilt. *Your target's role will appear as {{A|Cleaned}} in the [[Graveyard]]. *After you have successfully {{A|Cleaned}} a victim, you will receive a message about their exact role at the beginning of the next day. The following will appear as a plain message: **'You secretly know that your target's role was [Role].' **This happens even while you are dead and used by a {{A|Necromancer}} (may be a bug). **If you are promoted to {{A|Mafioso}} the same night, you ''will'' still see your target's role. *If they had a {{A|Last Will}} written, you will receive the following messages afterwards: **'You secretly know your targets[[wikipedia:Sic|[sic]]] last will.' **'Click your targets[[wikipedia:Sic|[sic]]] name in the Graveyard to view their will.' *You will be able to read your victim's original {{A|Last Will}} by clicking on their name in the [[Graveyard]]. Everybody else, including the other members of the {{A|Mafia}}, will see a blank {{A|Last Will}} instead. *You can read a {{A|Last Will}} that was covered in blood by a role-blocker attacked by a {{A|Serial Killer}} if you {{A|Cleaned}} the role-blocker. **This can be helpful in finding a {{A|Serial Killer}}, as the [[Roleblock|roleblocker]] will have written the last person they visited/jailed. *{{A|Amnesiacs}} cannot attempt to remember a {{A|cleaned}} person's role. *{{A|Retributionists}} and {{A|Necromancers}} cannot reanimate {{A|Cleaned}} targets. *If a {{A|Forger}} attempts to {{A|Forge}} your target's {{A|Last Will}}, their attempt will have no effect; your {{A|Clean}} takes priority. *If your target is also killed by {{A|Medusa}}, your {{A|Cleaning}} will take priority over their {{A|Stoning}}, they'll appear as {{A|Cleaned}} instead of {{A|Stoned}}. **You will also be able to read their {{A|Last Will}}, and you will also know their role. **This may help you find the {{A|Medusa}} if your target kept an up to date {{A|Last Will}}. ***However this won't work if your target was controlled by the {{A|Coven Leader}}, your target's target was {{A|Transported}} or if the {{A|Medusa}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}. *You have three {{A|Cleanings}}. **If you visit a {{A|Jailed}} target, you will ''not'' lose a {{A|Cleaning}}. **However, if you visit a target that did not die during the {{A|Night}}, you will lose a {{A|Cleaning}}. *Your cleans do not have any effect on an {{A|Arsonist's}} {{A|Douse}}. ==Strategy== ===Selecting Someone to Clean=== *It is very important and common to {{A|Clean}} {{A|Town Investigative}} roles because they are almost guaranteed to write something in their {{A|Last Will}} that is important to aid the {{A|Townies}} in hanging the right people. You should {{A|Clean}} them, especially if the {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Godfather}} decides to kill a known {{A|Town Investigative}}. Be aware that if you {{A|cleaned}} a {{A|Town Investigative}} role by chance on the first night, there will not be information. **You can later pretend to be one of the known {{A|Town Investigative}} roles as well. Additionally, {{A|Consiglieres}} can benefit from the information obtained, and it will often help them prioritize their investigations. **Be wary of {{A|Cleaning}} the {{A|Mafia's}} first target. Since {{A|Night}} one is when {{A|Investigators}} and {{A|Sheriffs}} will only be getting their first bit of information, if you kill one of them, their {{A|Last Will}} will not contain useful information for the {{A|Town}}. If any roles that aren't {{A|Town Investigatives}} are killed, then it doesn't matter either, as for example, the {{A|Medium}} is almost never confirmed after the first night. As the information from these {{A|Last Wills}} will not surface until much later, your cleanings may be more useful to use later on. **If a fellow member is being accused by a non-confirmed {{A|Town Investigative}} (especially from Day 3 and onward), and you are definite that they are that role, {{A|Cleaning}} them can also be beneficial; however, some players might think your fellow {{A|Mafia}} member is the {{A|Janitor}}, or at the very least, a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, due to hiding that player's information from the others. *On the other hand, in games with tighter role lists, like {{A|Ranked}}, cleaning anyone will conceal their role and make it much harder for the {{A|Town}} to determine people's roles by process of elimination; therefore, it might be a worthwhile strategy to use all your cleans as quickly as possible to be sure you free up as much claim space as you can before you die. **If the {{A|Mafia}} has two {{A|Janitors}} or a {{A|Janitor}} and a {{A|Forger}}, it's usually worth {{A|Cleaning}} or {{A|Forging}} every person who dies, since you're unlikely to run out before the end of the game. *{{A|Retributionists}} are also unable to reanimate your {{A|Cleaned}} targets. This can come in handy when dealing with {{A|Vigilantes}}, {{A|Bodyguards}}, or other important roles who can allow the {{A|Retributionist}} to swing the game in {{A|Town's}} favor . Bonus points if the {{A|Retributionist}} tries to prove themselves to a {{A|Lookout}} by reanimating the {{A|Cleaned}} role - and getting hanged when they fail'''!''' **However, this may lead the {{A|Retributionist}} to reanimate a {{A|Town Investigative}} role, like a {{A|Sheriff}} - making the {{A|Mafia's}} job all that much harder. Generally, it is still a good idea, though. *Even when you are {{A|Cleaning}} roles that seem to have no importance for the {{A|Mafia}} in their {{A|Last Will}} (such as {{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Jesters}}, {{A|Bodyguards}}, or {{A|Survivors}}), it still can be helpful to confuse the {{A|Townies}} in a situation where the role list is tight. This situation is more likely to be useful when you're likely to be hanged next day or the game would be likely to end because there are only a few players left, and you would like to use all of your three {{A|Cleanings}}. Also, if you clean a {{A|Jester}}, then you can use it to your advantage. Simply acting like a bad {{A|Jester}} will probably result in you being ignored. *If you're in doubt about when to use your cleanings, you may consider {{A|Cleaning}} a person who is leaving the game or getting disconnected ("apparently committed suicide"). Those who left the game are incapable of telling a {{A|Medium}} their true role and are usually not investigated and not watched by {{A|Lookouts}} (especially on Night 1). They are also guaranteed not to retaliate! (eg. {{A|Veteran}} and {{A|Werewolf}}). This always sheds doubt especially on semi-random role lists, as {{A|Townies}} will be unsure of the existence of that role. *You can attempt to {{A|Clean}} someone who you think might die that {{A|Night}} while the {{A|Mafia}} kills someone else. This can cause some confusion in the {{A|Town}} and can help you {{A|Clean}} immune roles or discover dangerous roles like a {{A|Serial Killer}} or the {{A|Medusa}} by looking at who the {{A|Cleaned}} player last visited. *Avoid {{A|Cleaning}} if you want to expose a role to the {{A|Town}}—i.e. a {{A|Consigliere}} has found a {{A|Vampire}} and you want the {{A|Town}} to know that {{A|Vampires}} are in the game. ===Taking advantage of your {{A|Cleanings}}=== *You know your target's role, so saying you are a {{A|Medium}} the next night and revealing their role, claiming they told it to you can support you. With this way, you can trick the {{A|Town}} by saying in the name of the dead people, for example, "The (name/role) says X is suspicious/{{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Neutral Killing}}." when X is not a part of the {{A|Mafia}}. Moreover, you can do other things to make you naturally believed as a {{A|Medium}} by becoming a messenger (i.e. if {{A|Jailor}} has executed a {{A|Townie}}, you can say "The {{A|Jailed}} {{A|Townie}} is getting mad at the {{A|Jailor}}"). **However, keep in mind that sometimes it's normal to have two or more {{A|Mediums}}, which would result to the real {{A|Medium}} calling you out as the dead people will alert the real {{A|Medium}}(s) during the night. **This strategy may have a backlash when you're standing out as a {{A|Medium}} for too long without the {{A|Mafia}} trying to kill you, especially when you have revealed a lot of "important" information publicly. The {{A|Townies}} might think you are a {{A|Janitor}} instead. Many {{A|Townies}} will rapidly hang any {{A|Medium}} claims when it becomes clear there's an active {{A|Janitor}}, helped along with the fact that {{A|Medium}} is not deemed useful to most players and {{A|Medium}} is a common claim for a {{A|Janitor}}. *Another option you can do is to pretend or role-play to be the role that you {{A|cleaned}}, especially because only you can read your target's {{A|Last Will}}. Many [[Unique Role]]s are rarely claimed due to the ease with which they can be counterclaimed; cleaning can open these up to the entire {{A|Mafia}}. In all cases, be aware that this risks getting you exposed by a {{A|Medium}} and that these claims trust the {{A|Town}} to not dig any further and demand confirmation going forwards; ''usually'' the {{A|Town}} won't ask for more confirmation once you're "confirmed", but it may happen if the game drags on or if something else calls attention to you. Regardless, when a cleaning allows them, some of the most powerful claims are ones that the {{A|Mafia}} is rarely able to make (and which therefore are less likely to face the backlash from the {{A|Town}}): *Another strategy is if you are aware of a {{A|Retributionist}} in the game, and no one else knows about it, you can kill and clean the real {{A|Retributionist}}, you can then claim that you are the {{A|Retributionist}}. And since only you can see the {{A|Retributionist's}} will, you can copy their will over, and use their results and actions to confirm yourself a little further.  **This also fits in with your investigation result, so the only thing that can really call you out is the {{A|Sheriff}}, but they most likely won't waste any time checking you after you have been "confirmed". *While it's dangerous, claiming to be the {{A|Jailor}} is sometimes plausible after cleaning the real {{A|Jailor}}, as the {{A|Town}} will frequently not bother to ask for additional confirmation, trusting the real {{A|Jailor}} to sort you out if you lied (and are unaware that the real {{A|Jailor}} is dead); you can also use previous records of who the {{A|Jailor}} jailed from their {{A|Last Will}} in order to get them to "confirm" you as the {{A|Jailor}}. However, if there is a {{A|Medium}}, they will call you out as "not {{A|Jailor}}". The only probable hope then is to pretend to be a {{A|Jester}} or try and mishang the {{A|Medium}}. *After cleaning a {{A|Jailor}}, you can use other strategies that rely on the {{A|Town's}} assumption that the {{A|Jailor}} is still alive, too. *Help your fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}} out! If a member of the {{A|Mafia}} is in trouble, tell the role of a person you {{A|cleaned}} so they can have claim-space. Of course, you won't be able to claim this role anymore, but you could save the life of another member of the {{A|Mafia}}. **Similarly, the {{A|Veteran}} is normally a dangerous role to claim because it's [[Unique Role|unique]]; but after you've {{A|cleaned}} one, it becomes incredibly easy and will discourage {{A|Investigators}} or any {{A|Town}} roles from investigating you in the future. **{{A|Transporter}} is usually a hard role to claim due to the need to produce a {{A|Last Will}} that the people who have been transported can confirm. However, it sometimes becomes available if you steal the {{A|Last Will}} of a {{A|Transporter}}; however, you need to claim said role quickly, as the {{A|Town}} may notice if "your" {{A|Last Will}} ends early. Alternatively, you can tack on entries at the end that transport you with members of the {{A|Mafia}} or with people who died; one or two {{A|Townies}} confirming the {{A|Last Will's}} transports will often be sufficient to let you pass as a {{A|Transporter}}. **In {{A|Ranked}} and other modes where roles are defined by general category, successfully cleaning a role opens up that entire category as a safe claim. For example, in {{A|Ranked}}, if the {{A|Doctor}} dies, it is usually safe to claim to be a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}. *You can find {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles based on what they claim, as you will know what is and isn't possible. **If you manage to clean a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Jailor}} who visited/jailed the {{A|Serial Killer}}, you can use their {{A|Last Will}} to your advantage. You can tell the {{A|Mafia}} to out them in a {{A|Death Note}} or publicly accuse them while claiming a {{A|Town Investigative}} role like a {{A|Sheriff}}. ***You can also use this strategy to find the {{A|Medusa}} since your cleans take priority over her stoning and you will receive the victim's {{A|Last Will}} and role. ===After you're Out of Cleanings=== *When out of cleanings, don't give up! You still contribute to the {{A|Mafia}} via voting, sharing out strategies in the {{A|Mafia}} night chat, taking advantage of the {{A|cleaned}} roles, or perhaps becoming a {{A|Mafioso}} later on. *If you've already pretended to be as {{A|Medium}} (and you're safe that there are no actual {{A|Mediums}} left), you can continue the disguising strategy or simply saying nothing "as no {{A|Townies}} are talking". However, this is not recommended and you should always be prepared with some information. It is suspicious if you are silent and have no information, even if you were a real {{A|Townie}}. *If you have no cleanings left, it can be a good idea to try and take a hit for a more important member of the {{A|Mafia}} ({{A|Godfather}}, another {{A|Janitor}} with cleanings left, a {{A|Mafioso}} or a {{A|Forger}} with forges, etc.) Try pulling attention to yourself to draw it away from others. Only do this if it is clear that another member of the {{A|Mafia}} is in danger of getting enough suspicion on them, they are hanged or killed, or if they have a more important role in the {{A|Mafia}} than you do. Keep in mind you do not need to be alive to win when the {{A|Mafia}} kills everyone. **As a role with no more night abilities, you can try and create chaos, akin to a {{A|Jester}}. *You could also let the {{A|Godfather}}, {{A|Mafioso}}, {{A|Consigliere}}, or any other {{A|Mafia}} member call you out as a {{A|Janitor}}, and then "confirm" themselves as {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} or another {{A|Town}} role. This is a form of bussing, and if pulled off, can be very helpful. However, be sure that all {{A|cleaned}} roles have been shared with the {{A|Mafia}}, otherwise the sacrifice will be for nothing and you won't gain anything out of it. ===Dealing with {{A|Janitors}}=== *A tactic to use if a {{A|Janitor}} is in game is to ask all {{A|Town Investigative}} claims to post their wills to make the {{A|Janitor}} less useful. **Even if they are outted/killed by the {{A|Mafia}}: ***You still have information from their N1 {{A|Last Will}}. ***You can start marking down {{A|Random Town}} slots. ***You can still determine who is a member of the {{A|Mafia}} by which claim lasts the longest, especially if they aren't an easily confirmable role. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{JanitorAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{JanitorMessages}} ==History== *{{VH|3.3.0}} **{{A|Janitors}} can now read Bloody {{A|Last Wills}} from their {{A|Cleaned}} victims. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Janitor's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Janitor.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Janitor's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Janitor Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|1.5.10.4747}} **{{A|Amnesiac}} can no longer remember {{A|Cleaned}} players. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Уборщик]] [[Category:Mafia Deception roles]] [[Category:Mafia roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Last Will modifiers]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
