'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You will receive the amount of {{A|Mafia}} and/or {{A|Coven}} who visit certain people each {{A|Night}}. The order is randomized. **You will also be able to see the {{A|Astral}} visit made by the {{A|Hex Master}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}} as a {{A|Coven}} visit. But you will not see the visit made by {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}}. **If a {{A|Disguiser}} {{A|Disguises}} a {{A|Mafia}} member, you will not see who that {{A|Mafia}} member visits. ***If a {{A|Mafia}} member is {{A|Disguised}} as a member of the {{A|Coven}}, their visit will '''not''' appear as a {{A|Coven}} visit. **In the {{A|Town Traitor}} [[Game Modes (ToS)|game mode]], you cannot see who the {{A|Town Traitor}} visits. The same applies for the Coven {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}} in the Coven {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}} [[Game Modes/Coven Expansion|game mode]]. *You are also able to "bug" a person each {{A|Night}}, which reveals any direct actions against them, such as attacks, {{A|Roleblocks}}, {{A|Transports}}, etc. Investigative actions are not shown, such as from a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Consigliere}}. **{{A|Spies}} who {{A|Bug}} a {{A|Hypnotist's}} target will see the false messages the {{A|Hypnotist}} sends to a player. **While tracking {{A|Mafia}} and/or {{A|Coven}} visits is not counted as a visit, {{A|Bugging}} a player counts as you visiting them. ***By that logic, {{A|Spies}} will indeed trigger the {{A|Trapper's}} {{A|trap}} if they {{A|Bug}} the trapped person. Bear this in mind when weighing the pros and cons of {{A|Bugging}}. ***{{A|Spies}} can also be attacked by a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Medusa}}, should they {{A|Bug}} them. *If you are {{A|Controlled}}, you will {{A|Bug}} the controller's target. The controller will get the {{A|Mafia}} and/or {{A|Coven}} visits along with feedback from the {{A|Bug}}. *You will not be able to see who the {{A|Coven}} and/or {{A|Mafia}} visit if you are {{A|Jailed}}. *If you are {{A|Roleblocked}}]/{{A|Jailed}} or {{A|Controlled}}, you will not receive the results of your {{A|Bug}} or the visits. *The {{A|Bug}} will fail if your target is {{A|Jailed}}. You will know that your target was {{A|Jailed}}. You will still see visits. *{{A|Transporters}} will only change your {{A|Bug}} target. If you {{A|Bug}} A, and if a {{A|transporter}} swaps A and B, you will receive {{A|Bug}} information from player B. *Your ability to see {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} visits are unaffected by {{A|Transporters}} and will always display who the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} actually visit that {{A|Night}}: if {{A|mafia}} or {{A|coven}} visits A, you will see a visit on A, and if a {{A|Transporter}} swaps A and B, you will see {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} visit B. *Due to an inconsistent bug (as of [[Version History (ToS)|Version 3.3.12]]), you sometimes '''won't''' see the visits of {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} corpses reanimated by a {{A|Necromancer}}. *If you {{A|Bug}} a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} who controlled a {{A|Doctor}} or a {{A|Crusader}} into saving someone, you will receive the message ''"Your target's target was attacked last night"'' that the controller stole from the player they {{A|Controlled}}. *If you die, you will still receive your results for that {{A|Night}}, including {{A|Bugs}} and visits, despite having the same priority as an {{A|Amnesiac}}. ===Bugging Messages=== When a {{A|Spy}} uses their {{A|Night}} ability to {{A|Bug}} someone, they'll see messages from the following list for appropriate events: {{SpyAbilityMessages}} ==Strategy== *When the {{A|Mafia}} has a {{A|Blackmailer}}, you should try to figure out why the {{A|Mafia}} is trying to keep the {{A|Blackmailed}} person quiet. Maybe they blamed the {{A|Mafia}}, and you don't have to reveal yourself as a {{A|Spy}} to point out that someone is {{A|Blackmailed}} since they will most likely vote spam if they are blackmailed. Then tell everyone what they said before they were {{A|Blackmailed}}. **Doing this does carry some risk though, as some experienced {{A|Townies}} may call you out on suspicion of being a {{A|Blackmailer}}, as {{A|Blackmailers}} will often accuse their own target, pointing out how quiet they've been. On top of that, {{A|Spy}} is a common {{A|Blackmailer}} claim, so be wary. *As a {{A|Spy}}, your {{A|Bugs}} can confirm the existence of many roles, including {{A|Arsonists}} and {{A|Serial Killers}}. Any messages that correspond to one of these roles should be pointed out to the {{A|Town}} immediately. *If a {{A|Jester}} is hanged, you should keep track of who whispered to the {{A|Jester}} before they were hanged. If the {{A|Jester}} killed a {{A|Townie}}, then there's a high chance the person is evil. *Posting daily can help, as {{A|Spy}} usually has a long {{A|Last Will}} and gives useful information for claims. This can benefit by confirming yourself and narrowing down who is evil (such as a {{A|Bootlegger}} claiming they are a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}). Your detailed {{A|Last Will}} probably won't fit if you try to post it all at once. *Always keep a detailed {{A|Last Will}}, noting down every {{A|Night's}} {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visits. While this is true for any role, the significance of a {{A|Night's}} visits often isn't obvious until later in the game. It might be tempting to summarize it into a list of who has/hasn't been visited or a possible number of {{A|Mafia}}, but knowing the precise visits and what {{A|Night}} they occurred on can be valuable for catching a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Consigliere}}, or for interpreting the {{A|Last Wills}} of other players. *If you find someone who was controlled by a {{A|Witch}} and who didn't claim that they were controlled, the player is most likely an evil role who doesn't want to out the {{A|Witch}}. **A rare strategy you could do is claim to be a {{A|Witch}} by whispering to them that you had controlled them. Most evil roles trust a {{A|Witch}} claim, so if the evil role is a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, the player may tell you who the rest of the {{A|Mafia}} are. *If someone is visited by the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, and the next {{A|Day}} another person claims to be an {{A|Investigator}} with information about them, it may indicate that they're actually an evil (possibly a {{A|Consigliere}} or {{A|Potion Master}}) using information from that visit to deduce their role. Keep in mind that if they're accusing their target of being evil or immune, that accusation ''may'' still be correct, since both the {{A|Coven}} and the {{A|Mafia}} have reasons to want to eliminate rival evils. ===Revealing=== *If you are unable to gather a lot of information, but still have some information to contribute, a good time to reveal yourself as a {{A|Spy}} is when you know there are a lot of high priority roles, as lots of other roles at this point are a higher priority to kill than the {{A|Spy}}. Otherwise, you should reveal yourself when you have some good information to contribute with, for example, if you know who one of the members of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} is. **However, you could still become a high priority target anyway as you can catch a {{A|Consigliere}}/{{A|Necromancer}} by their visits and discredit false info. *You should try to counter an unlikely {{A|Spy}} claim, as they could be a {{A|Blackmailer}}. {{A|Spy}} is a common claim for members of the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} as it is easy to fake for them. **This doesn't apply as much to certain [[Game_Modes_-_Coven#Coven_Custom|Coven Custom]] role lists or {{A|Coven All Any}}, as members of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} can only see who their own faction visits, although the actions of the {{A|Coven}} are generally more obvious. Anyone who is seen to be falsely claiming {{A|Spy}} is usually either a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Jester}}, and a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} should kill them. *In more competitive game modes such as [[Game Modes (ToS)|Ranked]], [[Game Modes (ToS)|Ranked Practice]] and [[Game Modes (ToS)|Town Traitor]], {{A|Spies}} are generally expected to reveal themselves and post their results on {{A|Day}} 2. This meta makes it harder for evils to fake-claim {{A|Spy}}, and the information you receive can help {{A|Townies}} make more informed decisions. But it is still acceptable to wait a bit before you post, as you could expose a potential {{A|Consigliere}} who wants to claim {{A|Investigator}} on their target. ==={{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} Visits=== *Make sure to keep track of who the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visit at {{A|Night}}, in most cases the visited target will '''not''' be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}. You can use this information to narrow down who could be a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}. However, a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} or a {{A|Transporter}} can make a member of the {{A|Mafia}} visit another. A {{A|Disguiser}}/{{A|Potion Master}} could also be disguising/healing a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} so watch out for this. If an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers that they were a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}, they might be among the targets too. Late game, you can also completely confirm a {{A|townie}} if all neutrals are dead by recording their visits. *Late game, it may be a good idea to look back in your will and see the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} visits. Compare them to the currently alive players, you can narrow down who is {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} by looking at visits. If you see some players that were never visited by {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, they are most likely one themselves. *If no targets are visited at all, it is very likely that the {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}} was in jail or role blocked. In modes where the number of {{A|Mafia}} can vary significantly, such as {{A|All Any}}, it can also indicate that the {{A|Mafia}} are all dead. *If a target is visited repeatedly but is not {{A|Blackmailed}} or role blocked, the {{A|Mafia}} might have a {{A|Disguiser}}. *If none of the targets die, it is possible that one of the targets was attacked and either had a higher Defense value than said attacker's Attack value or was healed by a {{A|Doctor}}. This is especially true if a target was visited by multiple members of the {{A|Mafia}} (the second being a {{A|Forger}} or {{A|Janitor}}). *Bear in mind, however, that a common mistake among novice {{A|Spies}} is to make broad assumptions based on visitations, such as assuming one or more of the targets visited has a naturally high defense or assuming that a {{A|Mafia}} member visited a {{A|Medusa}} based on the change in the number of visits. **Calling these out early on can be detrimental for two reasons: if they actually did visit a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, the {{A|Spy}} is less likely to be believed and may end up providing a valuable distraction for the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}. On the other hand, if the target was innocent and merely protected, it would expose both that innocent player and their protector. **Furthermore, now that {{A|Spy}} is easy for any {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} member to fake, these call outs can cast suspicion upon the {{A|Spy}} themselves. This can be effective if the {{A|Spy}} doesn't have a proper {{A|Last Will}}, or just calls out someone without giving the full story. This can result in a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} killing the {{A|Spy}}, dealing a huge blow to {{A|Town}} in the process. *Keep track of who the {{A|Mafia}} visit at {{A|Night}} and use the process of elimination to find who the members of the {{A|Mafia}} are. Be aware, however, that {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Witches}}, and {{A|Disguisers}} can mess with your results. *You can distinguish between {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and {{A|Bootlegger}} claims by checking to see if the people who were role-blocked were visited by the {{A|Mafia}} on those {{A|Nights}}. {{A|Bootleggers}} cannot easily lie about their visits since each one produces a message; but they can easily claim {{A|Tavern Keeper}} if you're not there to catch them or if they're {{A|Disguised}}. *Your list of visits can be extremely effective in combination with a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}}, allowing you to narrow down possible {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} members even further: **If the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} didn't visit the {{A|Lookout's}} target or whoever the {{A|Tracker's}} target visited, then those visitors cannot be {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}, respectively. **If the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} ''did'' visit that target, then it puts any visitors under suspicion. However, for the {{A|Tracker}}, remember that there may be other visitors you didn't see who could be the actual {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}. *You can also use the pattern of visits to figure out the role(s) of the {{A|Random Mafia}} member(s). **For example, if one person is visited two times, there is likely a {{A|Forger}} or {{A|Janitor}} in play. If they don't die, they may be healed or have a higher Defense value than the attacker's Attack value. {{A|Framers}} can also visit the same target to try to trick you. **If one person is visited and not killed, then visited and killed, this may point to the presence of a {{A|Consigliere}}. They would have investigated the person, shared their role, and then the {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}} would have decided to kill them. Keep this in mind especially if they are an important Town role, such as {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mayor}}, or one that could have found out members of the {{A|Mafia}}, such as {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Lookout}}. **If one person is being visited repeatedly, this could indicate a {{A|Disguiser}}, or possibly a {{A|Bootlegger}} who is intent on [[roleblocking]] one person. If the victim is claiming {{A|Roleblocked}}, it is most likely a {{A|Bootlegger}}. ***Note however, that you cannot see a {{A|Disguiser}} who has {{A|Disguised}} themselves since it hides both their visits from you. *If someone is visited once by {{A|Coven}} and did not die or claim controlled/{{A|Poisoned}}, there could be a {{A|Potion Master}} or {{A|Hex Master}}. **If the {{A|Coven}} visit a deceased target at night, you can be certain that {{A|Necromancer}} is in play. *Your abilities can be very useful for finding {{A|Pestilence}}. ** Once {{A|Pestilence}} has appeared, any further visits without an associated {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} death indicate that the person who was visited is not {{A|Pestilence}}. **Conversely, if there's a {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} death the next morning, then any visits by {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} may indicate they visited {{A|Pestilence}}, though you also have to consider the possibility that they were visited by {{A|Pestilence}} or visited {{A|Pestilence's}} target. **When {{A|Pestilence}} is active, you should stop {{A|Bugging}}, since the benefits of that half of your abilities are too minor to be worth the risk of exposing you to death to {{A|Pestilence's}} rampage or to visiting them directly. ===Bugging=== *With the 'bug' ability, you can now know if someone is lying about what happened to them. You can also find out if someone is immune or whether they were protected by a vest. *Generally speaking, you should {{A|Bug}} people who you suspect will lie about or conceal what happened to them at {{A|Night}} - in other words, potentially evil roles. There's usually little point in {{A|Bugging}} a confirmed {{A|Town}} role, who will reveal what happened to them at {{A|Night}} anyway. **However, one benefit to {{A|Bugging}} {{A|Town}} is that you can use what you see to confirm yourself. For this reason, it's sometimes useful to choose targets the way a {{A|Lookout}} would, and visit whoever you think is most likely to be visited and have an 'exciting' {{A|Night}} in general; that will give you the information you can later use to confirm that you're a {{A|Spy}}. *Remember that some of the information you can gather with {{A|Bugging}} is redundant with the information you retrieve from your ability to see {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visits: **If someone is repeatedly acting blackmailed, you could theoretically use your {{A|Bugging}} to confirm this; however, most of the time you will already know they're telling the truth due to the {{A|Mafia}} visits (unless there's a {{A|Disguiser}}). *There are a few specific messages you can see that are much more important than others and worth actively looking for by targeting people who are likely to receive them. These are: **The unique messages a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Pirate}} gets when killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}} they {{A|roleblocked}}; this will tell you with certainty that the person they targeted was a {{A|Serial Killer}}. Of course, everyone will eventually know that because they'll leave a bloody {{A|Last Will}}, however you'll know it before anyone else and you can confirm yourself as {{A|Spy}} by quickly whispering some people the message you saw in your {{A|Bug}} before the {{A|roleblocker}}'s cause of [[Death (state)|death]] is publicly revealed. **If you target a {{A|Serial Killer}} who gets {{A|roleblocked}}, you'll receive a special message telling you that they attacked their {{A|roleblocker}} (which instantly outs them as a {{A|Serial Killer}}.) For this reason, it can be useful to {{A|Bug}} possible {{A|Serial Killers}}. **If your target has {{A|Defense}}, you'll receive a message when they're attacked. For this reason, it's worth watching people you suspect of having {{A|Defense}}. ***Note that while you can make some deductions about immunity with by watching your {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visit reports on a {{A|Night}} when they fail to kill, actually {{A|Bugging}} a target lets you distinguish between bulletproof vests, healing, and persistent immunity. ****Also note that a {{A|Hypnotist}} could be sending a fake heal message to confirm themselves to you and their target if the {{A|Mafia}} fails to kill (the same applies to a lesser extent with the {{A|Potion Master}}). **If you watch an {{A|Arsonist}} who cleans themselves, you'll receive a message stating this. This is fairly rare and typically only happens in games with multiple {{A|Arsonists}}, but it's a reason to watch potential {{A|Arsonists}} in any game that seems to have more than one. Similarly, you will ''only'' receive the message that your target was doused if they are an {{A|Arsonist}} themselves. **The "{{A|Control Immunity}}" message is seen by the {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, {{A|Necromancer}}, {{A|Pirate}} and {{A|Pestilence}}. Remember that if you see it ''and'' the transportation message, an actual {{A|Transporter}} may have transported your target with themselves. Conversely, a message that your target was successfully controlled means they cannot be any role on that list. ***Note that {{A|Retributionist}} and {{A|Transporter}} will only get a "{{A|Control Immunity}}" message when they get controlled by a {{A|Witch}}, not by a {{A|Coven Leader}}. This is most likely a bug. **The "{{A|Roleblock Immunity}}" message is only seen by a few roles: {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Pirate}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}/{{A|Witch}}, and {{A|Necromancer}}. If you see it, your target is one of the roles on that list. Of course, if it was {{A|Pestilence}}, you will die unless healed. ***This can be done to try to confirm certain claims or roles that are somewhat easy to claim such as {{A|Retributionist}}. **A message that your target was successfully role-blocked means that they cannot be any of the roles with immunity, nor can they be a {{A|Serial Killer}} or (on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}) a {{A|Werewolf}} since those have unique messages. **You can tell if the target was {{A|Transported}}. This can be vital to preventing mishanges. Remember that if you see that message, it means that ''your'' target was changed by the {{A|Transporter}}, too; for instance, if you see that message and an immunity message, it means the {{A|Transporter's}} ''other'' target is immune, not the person you intended to target. Keep in mind a {{A|Hypnotist}} can generate a transport message also, potentially leading you to false conclusions. **If you manage to catch the message of: "Someone role blocked your target so they stayed at home." then it means your target is a {{A|Werewolf}}, as this is a specific message. However, you will die due to visiting them, unless you are protected in some way. **When someone you're {{A|Bugging}} is attacked, you can see whether they were saved by a vest or by permanent immunity. For this reason, it can be valuable to {{A|Bug}} {{A|Survivor}} claims; if they are attacked, you'll immediately know whether they're actually a {{A|Survivor}} or not. While the behavior of {{A|Survivors}} can be unpredictable, speaking up to confirm them or save their lives can often convince them to side with the {{A|Town}}, and will at least prevent other {{A|Town}} members from wasting time pursuing them. **The "Your target's target was attacked last night!" message is unique to the {{A|Doctor}} and {{A|Crusader}} specifically. Receiving this result means your target is either one of these roles or a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} who stole this feedback from the {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Crusader}} they controlled. **If your target is attacked by a {{A|Bodyguard}} and survives (because they were healed by a {{A|Doctor}}), you will learn this fact, which proves that your target is a killer. You should generally out them for this immediately - doing so will both spare the {{A|Doctor}} the need to step forward (if they even realize they should do so), and will confirm you to them, while catching a likely-evil role. *While your {{A|Bugging}} can be valuable, it is generally less powerful than your ability to see {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visits; additionally, it exposes you to getting killed by the {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Crusaders}}, the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Ambusher}}, the {{A|Medusa}}, the {{A|Juggernaut}}, or (on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}) the {{A|Werewolf}}. For this reason, you might consider staying home when those roles are active, especially if you don't have any clear plan in terms of what you're checking for with your {{A|Bugging}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{SpyAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{SpyMessages}} == Trivia == *It is possible for the {{A|Spy}} to see five {{A|Mafia}} visits in one {{A|Night}} because of a {{A|Disguiser}}, however this won't happen under normal circumstances because, while the {{A|Disguiser}} does visit two players, they also hide the visit of the {{A|Mafia}} member they {{A|Disguise}}. So if you see five {{A|Mafia}} visits in one {{A|Night}} and there are no{{A|Amnesiacs}} who became a {{A|Mafia}} role, one of the following things '''must''' have happened: **A {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} forced the {{A|Disguiser}} to {{A|Disguise}} someone who isn't {{A|Mafia}} (only {{A|Disguiser}}'s '''first''' target is changed) **A {{A|Transporter}} transported the {{A|Mafia}} member that the {{A|Disguiser}} meant to {{A|Disguise}} with someone who isn't {{A|Mafia}}. **{{A|Disguiser}}'s second target was {{A|Jailed}} so the {{A|Disguise}} ability failed and thus no {{A|Mafia}} visit was hidden from the {{A|Spy}}. *Contrary to popular belief, a {{A|Spy}}'s {{A|Bug}} does '''not''' detect {{A|Vampire}} conversions in [[Town of Salem|Town of Salem 1]]. *Prior to [[Version_History (ToS)|Version 2.0.0.6537]], the {{A|Spy}} and the {{A|Blackmailer}} could read [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]]. Now, only the {{A|Blackmailer}} can read [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]]. **Also prior to the same version, the {{A|Spy}} could read the {{A|Mafia chat}}. *Prior to [[Version_History (ToS)|Version 3.2.3]], {{A|Spies}} would still be able to know who the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visit, despite being dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}, which is considered a [[roleblock]]. == History == *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.3.0]] **The {{A|Disguiser}} can now fool a {{A|Spy}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.2.4]] **{{A|Spy}} now gets their ability feedback the {{A|Night}} they die. *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.2.3]] **{{A|Spy}} no longer knows who the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visit when being dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Spy's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Spy.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Spy's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Spy Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.3.8910]] **{{A|Spy}} can now die to a {{A|Veteran}} on alert. (bug fix) *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.1.0.7320]] **{{A|Spy}} can now see all actions against a player by "bugging" them at {{A|Night}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.0.0.6582]] **The {{A|Spy}} can now see who the {{A|Coven}} visit at {{A|Night}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.0.0.6537]] **The {{A|Spy}} can no longer read [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] or {{A|Night}} [[Chat (ToS)|chat]]. **Removed message "You feel that someone can hear your conversations.". **Removed message "You feel like you can speak privately.". *[[Version_History (ToS)|1.5.11.5389]] **The {{A|Mafia}} now receive this message at the start of the {{A|Night}} if there is a {{A|Spy}} alive: "You feel that someone can hear your conversations.". **The {{A|Mafia}} now receive this message at the start of the {{A|Night}} if there is no {{A|Spy}} alive: "You feel like you can speak privately.". *[[Version_History (ToS)|1.5.8.4235]] **{{A|Executioner}} can now have {{A|Spy}} as a target. *[[Version_History (ToS)|1.3.0]] **{{A|Executioner}} can no longer have {{A|Spy}} as a target. *[[Version_History (ToS)|Town of Salem Release]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Шпион]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:Town Investigative roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, your poison can no longer be Healed. |goal = Kill all who would oppose the {{A|Coven}}.}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *The {{A|Poisoner}} has the ability to {{A|poison}} someone each {{A|Night}}. Your poison deals the equivalent of a {{A|Basic Attack}} on the {{A|Night}} you poison someone, meaning anyone who has been {{A|poisoned}} without defense then gains defense the next night (like a {{A|Survivor}} self vesting or being jailed), will still die to {{A|poison}}.[[File:SpecialLabel_Poisoned.png|alt=|thumb|The icon that appears next to {{A|poisoned}} players on the player list]] **Your {{A|poison}} will only take effect the day after you {{A|poison}} your target. Anyone with Basic or higher defense on the night they're {{A|poisoned}} will not be {{A|poisoned}}. **Your {{A|Poison}} will only kill those with temporary defense. Anyone who gains permanent defense before the night they die to {{A|Poison}} (like a {{A|Mafioso}} being promoted to {{A|Godfather}}), will survive your {{A|Poison}}. *{{A|Poisoned}} players will know they were {{A|poisoned}}. **If your {{A|poisoned}} target dies from the {{A|poison}}, your target will receive a message stating "You died to poison!" *A {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Guardian Angel}}, or {{A|Potion Master}} can remove your {{A|poison}} if they protect your target. *With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, your {{A|poison}} can no longer be cured by a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Potion Master}} and will ignore their protections. However, your {{A|poison}} can still be cured by a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} purge. Your attack will ''not'' become more powerful. *If you {{A|poison}} someone with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, it will show the message "You were poisoned. You will die tomorrow!" instead of "You were poisoned. You will die tomorrow unless you are cured!". *You cannot {{A|poison}} a player who has left the game.  *{{A|Town Protective}} roles can save someone from getting {{A|poisoned}}. However they will not get a ''"target was attacked"'' message when stopping a {{A|Poisoner}}, despite the fact that {{A|poisoning}} someone is always a harmful visit. *Funnily enough, a {{A|Hypnotist}} hypnotizing you with a fake {{A|poison}} message will cause you to see an extra {{A|poison}} icon next to your number on the player list (this is a bug). ==Strategy== *Your delayed kill means that {{A|Lookouts}} will sometimes have a harder time finding you. However, smarter {{A|Lookouts}} will notice you visiting your target, so when the target claims to have been {{A|poisoned}} or when they die to {{A|Poison}} a day later, they will be suspicious of you and even call you out. *Since your kills are delayed, you can utilize this to out roles with defense in your {{A|Death Note}} on the same {{A|Night}} you {{A|Poison}} them provided your previous {{A|Poison}} killed someone that {{A|Night}}. *{{A|Doctors}} are a high-priority target; with them in play, you are virtually useless until you have the {{A|Necronomicon}} (even then, a {{A|Guardian Angel}} can still remove your {{A|Poison}}), the reason being that anyone {{A|poisoned}} can simply claim so and the {{A|Doctor}} will heal them, confirming themselves and the {{A|Doctor}} in the process. **However, you will open the door to all other players being attacked by your fellow {{A|Coven}} members, and even members of the {{A|Mafia}} or other hostile {{A|Neutrals}}, provided there are no other {{A|Town Protectives}}. **The {{A|Coven Leader}} can prevent the {{A|Doctor}} from curing {{A|Poison}} by controlling them away. *The revealed {{A|Mayor}} is very vulnerable to {{A|Poison}} as they can't be saved by a {{A|Doctor}}. Note that you might be caught by a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Crusader}} poisoning the {{A|Mayor}}, so it's wise to find them first and kill them before poisoning the {{A|Mayor}}. *Claiming to be {{A|poisoned}} has its benefits - it means the {{A|Doctor}} will heal you that night, protecting you from harm. Even if the {{A|Town}} notices you haven't died, you can simply claim to have been healed. Of course, this will not work once you get the {{A|Necronomicon}}, as healing will no longer prevent death by {{A|poison}}. **This strategy can backfire if a there is a {{A|Spy}}, as they won't see the {{A|Coven}} visit you unless a {{A|Potion Master}} interferes. *Coordinate with your fellow {{A|Coven}} members on who you should {{A|poison}}. Before {{A|Night}} 3, you are the only {{A|Coven}} member able to kill reliably and consistently (without requiring a {{A|Coven Leader}} + {{A|Medusa}} combination). **Under the rare circumstance with a {{A|Necromancer}} teammate and a dead {{A|Blackmailer}}, the {{A|Necromancer}} can blackmail the target of your {{A|poison}}, making them incapable of asking a {{A|Doctor}} to cure them. Claiming to be {{A|poisoned}} yourself the next day, while taking suspicion off you in the short term, makes you vulnerable to being called out in your victim's {{A|Last Will}} after their death unless the {{A|Necromancer}} has an available {{A|Janitor}}/{{A|Forger}} corpse. **Once another {{A|Coven}} member obtains the {{A|Necronomicon}}, communicate with them to ensure that they don't attack the same target that's {{A|Poisoned}} or is about to be {{A|Poisoned}}. This will effectively allow the {{A|Coven}} to have a consistent two kills per night. The only to this exception is if the target is someone the {{A|Coven}} ''absolutely must'' kill immediately. *If you play with a {{A|Medusa}}, you can ask them to claim {{A|poisoned}} while you don't {{A|poison}} anyone and ask the {{A|Medusa}} to stone visitors the following night. This will allow them to kill the {{A|Doctor}} and make your {{A|poison}} an actual threat; however, a {{A|Guardian Angel}} can still remove your {{A|poison}} through purging. Be warned that smarter players will notice if someone says they will visit the {{A|Medusa}} and dies from stoning the day after. *{{A|Poison}} can be used to draw away {{A|Doctors}} from their original intended target, exposing that target in the process. Utilize this with the other available {{A|Coven}} members in order to determine who is and who isn’t protected. *The {{A|Poisoner}} is very much like a {{A|Mafioso}}, except with a higher chance that your target will not die. The {{A|Necronomicon}} is like a {{A|Mafioso}} being {{A|Disguised}}, and thus the role should be treated as a {{A|Mafioso}}. **Since a {{A|Poisoner}} is a delayed {{A|Mafioso}}, you are the least powerful {{A|Coven}} member, but you are also the most kill-consistent {{A|Coven}} member (without requiring the {{A|Necronomicon}}). Use this to your advantage. ===Dealing with {{A|Poisoner}}s=== *If you are {{A|Poisoned}} as a factional role, you still have a day to strategize with others before you die to {{A|Poison}}. Unlike any other killing role, their delayed attack allows you to coordinate with allies and even get cured if there's a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}}. *As a {{A|Lookout}}, if you see someone visit your target and your target claims they were {{A|poisoned}}, you may have found the {{A|Poisoner}}. If your target dies of {{A|poison}} the next day, the player you saw is most likely the {{A|Poisoner}}. *As a {{A|Doctor}}, make sure to heal anyone claiming to be {{A|poisoned}}. Not only will it remove {{A|poison}} from them, it will protect them from any killers and confirm your claim later on. On the other hand, if the {{A|Poisoner}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}, then healing {{A|poisoned}} people is a waste of a {{A|Night}}. **However, if the person who's {{A|poisoned}} doesn't have a claim, then you shouldn't heal them, as they are likely a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. *As a killing role, targeting people who are {{A|poisoned}} is a bad idea. Not only will they likely be protected by {{A|Doctors}} or {{A|Guardian Angels}}, even if they are defenseless, they will die from {{A|poison}} anyway, wasting a kill. However, if you have a {{A|Rampage}} attack, targeting a player that claims to be {{A|poisoned}} may help you eliminate a {{A|Doctor}}. *As a {{A|Tracker}}, you can call out a {{A|Poisoner}} if you see them visiting someone who claims to be {{A|poisoned}} the next day. Beware that the player you tracked is not necessarily the {{A|Poisoner}}, they simply may have happened to visit the same target as the {{A|Poisoner}}. *As a {{A|Mayor}}, you have the largest risk of revealing yourself if a {{A|Poisoner}} is known as a {{A|Doctor}} can't heal you. Always request protection and safety of any kind, such as a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Trapper}}, or even a {{A|Crusader}} if you feel there are no more protective roles around. {{A|Lookouts}} can cover you and identify the {{A|Poisoner}}, and {{A|Transporters}} can be a good bet too. *If a known {{A|Doctor}} visits a role that has claimed to be {{A|poisoned}} and dies to a {{A|Medusa}}, there is a good chance the person who claimed they were {{A|poisoned}} is the {{A|Medusa}} (unless a {{A|Transporter}} interferes). *As a {{A|Pirate}}, you should whisper the person claiming {{A|Poisoned}}, asking them to choose the option of your choice. If there is a {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Guardian Angel}}, they will heal your {{A|Attack}} as well as the {{A|Poison}}, and if there isn't, then your victim will die anyway. Either way, this nets you a free {{A|Plunder}} at no cost to them. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{PoisonerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{PoisonerMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Poisoner}} is one of the few roles able to kill another player even after they have already died.  **Note, however, that if you change your {{A|Death Note}} after you die, those changes will not be reflected. *According to [[Official Town of Salem Stories|the game's lore]], the {{A|Poisoner's}} name is Kande. The {{A|Poisoner}}, before joining the {{A|Coven}}, used to live in a small village in Africa. *During playtesting on the [[Public Test Realm]], the {{A|Poisoner}} would come up as ''{{A|Trapper}}, {{A|Ambusher}}, {{A|Poisoner}}, or {{A|Medusa}}'' to the {{A|Investigator}}. *If you poison someone with defense the icon of being poisoned will appear by their name during the next day and night despite them not actually going to die from it. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.1.14}} **{{A|Juggernaut}} now removes {{A|Poison}} when gaining {{A|Basic Defense}}. *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Poisoner's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Poisoner.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Poisoner's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Poisoner Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **Fixed an issue where if you were {{A|poisoned}}, healed, then {{A|poisoned}} again the next {{A|night}}, you wouldn't receive a message letting you know you were {{A|poisoned}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Отравитель]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Coven roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

(PM/PMer) |alignment = {{A|Coven Evil}} |avatar = [[File:PotionMaster.png|thumb|150px]] |attributes = [[Detection Immunity]] (with the {{A|Necronomicon}})

They must be a {{A|Potion Master}}. |summary = You are an experienced alchemist with potent recipes for potions. |abilities = You may choose to use a potion on a player each Night. |attributestext = You may choose to use a Heal, reveal, or attack potion on a player.
Each potion has a three Day cooldown.
With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, your potions no longer have a cooldown. |goal = Kill all who would oppose the {{A|Coven}}.}} {{Story}} [[File:Potion Master Potions.jpg|thumb|180x180px|{{A|Potion Master's}} currently available potions and their appearance ingame.]] == Mechanics == *The {{A|Potion Master}} can select between three potions to use at {{A|Night}}: a healing potion, a revealing {{A|potion}}, and an attacking {{A|potion}}. Each of the potions has a three {{A|Day}} cooldown. **The healing potion will heal your target. The healing will be identical to a {{A|Doctor's}}; it provides {{A|Powerful Defense}} and cures {{A|Poison}}. If your target is attacked on the {{A|Night}} you heal them, they will receive the same notification as they would if they were attacked when a {{A|Doctor}} is healing them. You, however, won't receive a notification if they are attacked. Attackers will also not receive a {{A|defense}} message. **The revealing potion will reveal your target's exact role to you. You will receive the same investigative results as a {{A|Consigliere}} would. You will see their exact role despite any {{A|Frames}}, {{A|Disguises}}, {{A|Douses}}, or {{A|Hexes}} on your target. **The attacking potion will attack your target. You will deal a basic attack to your target on the same {{A|Night}} similar to a {{A|Mafioso}} and unlike the {{A|Poisoner}}. *With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, the cool-downs for the potions are removed. *You can heal fellow {{A|Coven}} members, but you cannot choose to use an investigate or attack potion on your fellow {{A|Coven}} members. You can't use potions on yourself. *A {{A|Potion Master}} can cure {{A|Poison}}, but when they do it will have the message "You were attacked but someone nursed you back to health!" to the target INSTEAD of "You were cured of poison!". This may be a bug. So be careful if you are trying to act confirmed as a smart townie could call you out. **Due to a bug, it is possible for a {{A|Potion Master}} to cure the {{A|Poison}} of a {{A|Jailed}} player (still giving their target the wrong cure message). {{RevealRoleResults - Potion Master}} == Strategy == *Normally, it is better to use a revealing potion instead of a healing or killing potion at the beginning of the game. Doing so can give you vital information about your enemies and keeps the fact that there is a {{A|Potion Master}} in the game a secret, like all other {{A|Coven}} roles, the rest of the {{A|Town}} will know exactly what role someone died to. It also makes you and your team slightly better informed when you use your killing potion the next {{A|Night}}, along with giving you time to locate any {{A|Town Protectives}} that may take you down if you attack someone. Essentially, it makes less room for mistakes in your decisions. *When you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, it might be a good idea to use a revealing potion two {{A|Nights}} in a row, and then use a killing potion on the third {{A|Night}}. This way, the rest of the {{A|Town}} will not know that you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, which could make the {{A|Town}} panic that another {{A|Coven}} role has it instead, and start focusing on finding another {{A|Coven}} role. *Use your killing potions in compliment with your revealing potions. This allows you to take out high priority targets like a {{A|Sheriff}} or the {{A|Mafioso}}. *Your healing potion is a powerful weapon to negate the attacks of {{A|Town Protectives}}. Cooperating with other {{A|Coven}} roles is essential before you heal them. The other {{A|Coven}} members may decide to attack a specific target, knowing you would back them up with a {{A|Powerful Defense}}. This is more useful when the attacking {{A|Coven}} member targets someone with {{A|Town Protectives}} on their side. If possible, you can work with another {{A|Coven}} member to "confirm" yourself as the {{A|Doctor}} if needed. *When choosing who to heal, focus on whatever {{A|Coven}} member you think is most likely to be attacked. If you're unsure who will be attacked, you should protect whoever is most valuable - a {{A|Poisoner}} is important in the early game, the {{A|Necromancer}} is valuable if they have corpses worth using, while a {{A|Hex Master}} who has almost everyone {{A|hexed}} can be vital to protecting to ensure they live until their {{A|hex}} goes off. The {{A|Medusa}} and {{A|Coven Leader}} can protect themselves, and thus are generally a lower priority. **On that note, unless you feel like you think your team can carry the rest of the game, do '''not''' heal a {{A|Medusa}} while they are {{A|Stoning}}. Their {{A|Stone Gaze}} will still {{A|Stone}} you. ***This is only useful if you want to deliberately sell yourself out as not a {{A|Coven}} member, and is generally not worth it, considering your role is not revealed to the {{A|Town}}, and your team loses a member. **Before {{A|Night 3}}, you may need to heal the {{A|Coven Leader}} since they do not have their {{A|Basic Defense}} before then to protect them from a {{A|Crusader}}/{{A|Ambusher}}. This is especially the case for {{A|Night 2}}. **If a member of the {{A|Coven}} is being dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}, it's recommended to heal them in case the {{A|Pirate}} wins the duel, as your healing potion will negate their {{A|Powerful Attack}} on that {{A|Coven}} member. ***If you so choose, you can offer to let the {{A|Pirate}} {{A|Plunder}} one of your {{A|Coven}} since you can heal them, and [[whisper]] to them what your teammate will pick. The {{A|Pirate}} will likely pick the corresponding Attack, netting them a free {{A|Plunder}} and encouraging them to side with the {{A|Coven}}. When doing this, unless they have [[Abilities (ToS)|role block immunity]], never allow the {{A|Necronomicon}} wielder to be a sacrifice to a {{A|Pirate}}. **If a {{A|Transporter}} forces a {{A|Poisoner}} to target a {{A|Coven}} member or a {{A|Neutral}} ally, you'll be able to save them as long as the {{A|Poisoner}} does not possess the {{A|Necronomicon}}. **If a {{A|Necromancer}} is reanimating {{A|Pestilence}}, you should '''definitely''' heal them as {{A|Pestilence}} will attack the {{A|Necromancer}} for visiting them even in the graveyard. The same applies for any {{A|Coven}} member visiting a suspected {{A|Veteran}} on alert or the target of a {{A|Werewolf}}. *If you find a {{A|Town Protective}} role like a {{A|Bodyguard}}, you may claim {{A|Doctor}} and pair up with them. This can help in situations when roles like {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, or a {{A|Werewolf}} are around and the {{A|Coven}} has no other way of dealing with them. **As an added bonus, if the {{A|Bodyguard}} is ever attacked, they will trust you, and vote with you against the {{A|Pestilence}} or {{A|Werewolf}}. *If you inherit the {{A|Necronomicon}}, use the revealing potion on others to find their exact role, and paste their investigative results into chat (after claiming to be the {{A|Investigator}}) to attempt to [[Hanging (ToS)|lynch]] them. Be careful, because lynching a {{A|Townie}} could result in you losing your credibility. Gain the help of others by assisting roles such as {{A|Survivor}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}}, as this will be a major help towards the end of the game. Once everybody believes you are the {{A|Investigator}}, start killing off the non-{{A|Coven}} (preferably the {{A|Mafia}} first) until you win. **However, a smart {{A|Spy}} may notice the correlation between your "findings" and the {{A|Coven's}} visits, outing you and confirming themselves in the process, so a strategy is to change the order of your results. For example, if you found someone as a member of the {{A|Mafia}} on {{A|Night 1}}, you can put this as your results for a later {{A|Night}}; however, a {{A|Tracker}} tracking you will see that your {{A|Last Will}} does not correlate to your visits. *You are essentially a mix of the {{A|Doctor}}, the {{A|Consigliere}}, and the {{A|Mafioso}}. Refer to these roles' specific pages for strategies you could adopt into your own strategy. *Do '''not '''claim {{A|Doctor}} if there is a {{A|Poisoner}}. You would be expected to heal their victim each {{A|Night}}, and you would be discovered when you can't heal every target. **Claiming {{A|Doctor}} when you have the {{A|Necronomicon}} is plausible, but will be a waste of both the {{A|Potion Master}} and the {{A|Poisoner}} as the {{A|Potion Master}} would only be able to heal the {{A|Poisoner's}} attacks. ***Additionally, when a {{A|Potion Master}} cures {{A|Poison}}, the cured target will receive "You were attacked but someone nursed you back to health!" INSTEAD of the '''real''' '''{{A|Doctor}}''' message "You were cured of poison!". Experienced players can call you out for this. ***A way around this is to have one of your team claim {{A|Poisoned}} and pretend to heal them while instead attacking a {{A|Townie}}. However, you could be outed by a {{A|Spy}} or {{A|Lookout}} who will see no visitors. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{PotionMasterAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{PotionMasterMessages}} ==Trivia== *{{A|Potion Master}} is the only role to have three different priorities since the role itself has three [[Abilities (ToS)#Night_Abilities|Night abilities]]. *According to the game's [[Official Town of Salem Stories|lore]], the {{A|Potion Master's}} name is Nikki Flamel. *In the [[Public Test Realm]], there used to be a now-scrapped {{A|Coven Support}} {{A|Alignment}}. Most notably, the only known role to fit in this {{A|Alignment}} was the {{A|Potion Master}}. *There used to be a bug that could generate two {{A|Potion Masters}} when selecting roles from the {{A|Any}} {{A|Alignment}}, happening most often in {{A|Coven All Any}}. **Unfortunately, this has been fixed. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Potion Master's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Potion Master.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Potion Master's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Potion Master Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **Multiple {{A|Potion Masters}} can no longer spawn together in {{A|Coven All Any}}. **Fixed an issue where if you were {{A|poisoned}}, healed, then {{A|poisoned}} again the next {{A|Night}}, you wouldn't receive a message letting you know you were {{A|poisoned}}. **Fixed an issue where if you were attacked by {{A|Medusa}}, healed, but killed by a role with a higher {{A|attack}}, you would still show up as {{A|stoned}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Coven roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Defense]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, you may visit players and turn them to stone. }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *The {{A|Medusa}} can select themselves to {{A|Stone Gaze}} all visitors to their home thrice each {{A|night}}. All visitors are dealt a {{A|Powerful Attack}}, and their [[role]] and {{A|Last Will}} is cleared from everyone, including the {{A|Medusa}} themselves. **They will be shown as {{A|stoned}} in the graveyard. ***{{A|Amnesiacs}} cannot attempt to remember a '''{{A|Stoned}}''' person's role. ***{{A|Retributionists}} and {{A|Necromancers}} cannot reanimate '''{{A|Stoned}}''' targets. ***If a {{A|Janitor}} cleans a {{A|stoned}} target, the target will show as {{A|cleaned}} instead. The {{A|Janitor}} will receive the role and {{A|Last Will}} in this case. *Roles that visit you will still use their action on you. (e.g a {{A|Blackmailer}} will still {{A|Blackmail}} you, a {{A|Transporter}} will still {{A|Transport}} you, and a ''killing role'' will still kill you.) *If an {{A|Arsonist}} {{A|Douses}} you, you will remain {{A|Doused}} the rest of the game, being susceptible to {{A|Ignitions}}. *If a {{A|Transporter}} {{A|Transports}} you, it will still follow through. This means whoever was intending to visit you will be saved, while anyone who was visiting the other person transported will die from you. *With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, you may directly visit players instead, dealing a {{A|Powerful Attack}} to them. **You will still clear a player's [[role]] and {{A|Last Will}} when you visit a player. **You will not receive the {{A|Necronomicon}} if there's at least one other {{A|Coven}} member alive. ==Strategy== *Like the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Medusa}} relies on visits to get kills before they get the {{A|Necronomicon}}. Refer to the {{A|Veteran}} page on how to make the most of this ability (remember that most {{A|Veteran}} strategies that have a high chance of attacking {{A|Townies}} will work better as the {{A|Medusa}}). **Unlike the {{A|Veteran}}, however, you should note that you still need to avoid being recognized as the killer afterwards. This can be a problem if you bait people since players may look back and try to figure out who the {{A|stoned}} players might have visited and why. **Using your {{A|Stone Gaze}} does '''not''' give you any type of {{A|Defense}}, so you will be killed if a killing role visits you. However, they will be {{A|stoned}} as well. **'''You can be role-blocked.''' This prevents your gaze from taking effect on the role-blocker, and anyone can safely kill you. *The {{A|Necronomicon}} allows you to visit people and turn them to stone. Use this to kill enemies with {{A|Defense}} such as the {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Neutral Killings}}. **An added benefit to directly stoning is that the {{A|Town}} may think a threat is dead when you are killed by a killer, and someone gets turned to stone. **You can still gaze at home to kill potential visitors or a {{A|Transporter}} baiting you into attacking yourself provided you still have gazes left, as they do not increase even if you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}. *The {{A|Coven Leader}} can force people to visit you, allowing you to kill reliably prior to obtaining the {{A|Necronomicon}}. **An added advantage to this is that the {{A|Coven Leader}} learns the role of the person they're sending to their doom, allowing a member of the {{A|Coven}} to use it as claim-space. **Remember, however, that you do not gain {{A|Defense}} when using your {{A|Stone Gaze}}, so they need to be careful to avoid directing potential killers to you. **You can also save your {{A|Stone Gazes}} for a later time if needed, especially if the {{A|Coven Leader}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}. *Considering the fact you can {{A|Stone Gaze}} specific people with the {{A|Necronomicon}}, consider {{A|Stone Gazing}} the first two {{A|nights}}, especially if you are the only {{A|Coven}} member on your team. *Using certain voting patterns or leading the hang on someone can lead some guaranteed {{A|Townies}} into visiting you. *If you know who is a {{A|Transporter}}, whispering them saying "role or I shoot" can bait the {{A|Transporter}} into visiting you. *Your ability to visit once you have the {{A|Necronomicon}} can sometimes be used to frame other {{A|Townies}} as the {{A|Medusa}}; if everyone ''knows'' who someone is visiting on a particular {{A|night}}, stoning the visitor might make people think the person they visited was the {{A|Medusa}}. *Once you have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, it may be recommended to start hunting for roles with defense (especially the {{A|Neutral Killings}} or {{A|Plaguebearer}}), since those roles can pose a danger in the late game. *You can ask for {{A|Town Protectives}} or {{A|Lookouts}} to protect you (this usually doesn't attract killing roles). If you were jailed, claim you were {{A|Veteran}} baiting or that you're {{A|Mayor}}. Alternatively, you can just claim you didn't want to die {{A|Night 1}}. **Using this strategy, it might also be good idea to claim {{A|Psychic}} give a fake result. Not only does it fit into your investigative result, it's also easy to fake and usually believed by the town. After this, you can ask for {{A|Town Protective}} roles to protect you the next {{A|night}}, at which point you will be able to kill them easily. Be cautious when using this strategy though, as smart townies might call you out for medusa baiting, especially if multiple people end up stoned the next {{A|night}}. *You can claim to be "{{A|Crusader}} on {{A|Jailor}}" or "{{A|Crusader}} on lead {{A|Crusader}}" to bait some {{A|Town Protectives}} into you as a suicide tactic. **An added bonus is that {{A|Tavern Keepers}} have a lower chance of role-blocking you since you are "protecting" the {{A|Jailor}}/{{A|Crusader}}. Doing this for a confirmed {{A|Townie}} (like a {{A|Mayor}}) can have a similar effect. *Claiming to be {{A|Poisoned}} might lead some potential {{A|Doctors}} into you. *Claiming {{A|Survivor}} might lead some potential {{A|Town Investigatives}} or {{A|Consiglieres}} into you. *Do '''not''' ask the {{A|Potion Master}} to heal you if you are {{A|stone Gazing}} at home as the {{A|Potion Master}} will die to your {{A|Stone Gaze}}. **You can, however, ask the {{A|Necromancer}} to use a corpse to heal/protect you as they do not visit you with their ability. ==Dealing with {{A|Medusas}}== *Dealing with the {{A|Medusa}} is very similar to dealing with a {{A|Veteran}}, but unlike the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Medusa}} is a target to the {{A|Town}} as well. When someone is {{A|stoned}}, look back to see who they might have visited; that person could be the {{A|Medusa}}. *Keep in mind who you visit on a night that someone else dies to the {{A|Medusa}}. There's a very high chance that your target is not the {{A|Medusa}} (unless a {{A|Transporter}} transported your target and another player). *Additionally, a {{A|Medium}} or a {{A|Janitor}} (who {{A|Cleaned}} a {{A|Stoned}} target) can determine who {{A|stoned}} people visited. *However, it is important to remember that once the {{A|Medusa}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they can visit offensively; after the {{A|Coven}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}, you can't automatically conclude that the person a stoning victim visited was the {{A|Medusa}} unless you're certain the {{A|Necronomicon}} is held by someone else. **A way to tell that the {{A|Necronomicon}} is held by another {{A|Coven}} member is by their unique kill message, a {{A|Poisoner's}} incurable message, or two {{A|Potion Master}} kills in a row. *Remember that the {{A|Medusa}} only has 3 {{A|Stone Gazes}}, so if you have to investigate or kill them, you have a good chance of catching them unprotected after 2-3 {{A|nights}}. **You can also {{A|Roleblock}} them as a {{A|Bootlegger}}, allowing the {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Godfather}} to kill her safely; unlike the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Medusa}} is ''not'' immune to being role-blocked. **You can safely search for the {{A|Medusa}} with the help of a confirmed {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Crusader}}. *If you get stoned before the {{A|Necronomicon}} is held by a player, '''don't leave the game.''' As long as you weren't controlled, there is a good chance the person you visited was the {{A|Medusa}} who {{A|Stone Gaze}}d that {{A|night}}. It's recommended you tell this to a {{A|Medium}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{MedusaAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{MedusaMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Medusa}} is the only {{A|Coven}} role that can directly kill a {{A|Neutral Killing}} role other than the {{A|Hex Master}}. *Unlike an {{A|Ambusher}}, {{A|Medusa}} '''CAN''' attack their visiting teammates (most notably, the {{A|Potion Master}}). *The {{A|Medusa}} is one of two guaranteed {{A|Coven}} roles in {{A|Coven Ranked}} and {{A|Coven}} {{Amne|Ranked Practice}}, the other being the {{A|Coven Leader}}. *The {{A|Medusa}} is the only {{A|Coven}} role possible in all {{A|Coven Expansion}} [[Game_Modes_-_Coven|game modes]], except for {{A|Mafia Returns}}, which lacks the {{A|Coven}} entirely. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **Dead {{A|Coven}} members will now see the {{A|Medusa}} with {{A|Necronomicon's}} targets. **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Added {{A|Medusa}} vs. {{A|Transporter}} [[stalemate]] detector. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Medusa's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Medusa.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Medusa's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Medusa Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **{{A|Medusa}} vs. {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is now a {{A|Coven}} victory. **Fixed an issue where if you were attacked by {{A|Medusa}}, healed, but killed by a role with a higher {{A|attack}}, you would still show up as {{A|stoned}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Медуза]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Coven roles]] [[Category:Last Will modifiers]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' |mustkill=N/A (two successful plunders) }} {{Story}} [[File:Pirate Duel.png|thumb|180x180px|{{A|Pirate's}} GUI when dueling a player.]] =='''Mechanics'''== *During the {{A|Day}}, you may select a player to {{A|Duel}} later that {{A|night}} by selecting the "{{A|Duel}}" button next to a player's name. *If you or your target is {{A|Jailed}}, you will be unable to {{A|Duel}} (attempt to kill) your target. You will receive a message for both scenarios: "''You were hauled off to {{A|Jail}} so you couldn't {{A|Duel}} your target."'' and ''"Your target was hauled off to jail so you couldn't {{A|Duel}} them.''". *You cannot {{A|Duel}} the same player twice in a row. *At the start of the following {{A|night}}, both you and your target will get a special menu interface to select your actions for the {{A|Duel}}. **Your options are '''''{{A|Scimitar}}''''', '''''{{A|Rapier}}''''', and '''''{{A|Pistol}}''.''' **The victim's options are '''''{{A|Sidestep}}''''', '''''{{A|Chainmail}}''''', and '''''{{A|Backpedal}}''.''' **'''''{{A|Scimitar}}''''' beats '''''{{A|Sidestep}}''''', '''''{{A|Rapier}}''''' beats '''''{{A|Chainmail}}''''', and '''''{{A|Pistol}}''''' beats '''''{{A|Backpedal}}'''''. *If you win the {{A|Duel}}, you will deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}} to your target. *If you do not choose an option, your target will not be [[roleblocked|role-blocked]] and the {{A|Duel}} will not register. *Winning the {{A|Duel}} will also kill your target, earning you 1 of the 2 plunders you need to win the game. If your target is protected by a {{A|Town Protective}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, or {{A|Guardian Angel}} and you win, your target won't die, but it counts as 1 of the 2 plunders needed, and the same is true if you died. *Your plunder is unaffected by the {{A|Transporter's}} swap, and will always (attempt to) kill the target you {{A|Dueled}}. *{{A|Dueling}} a player with a {{A|Trap}} on them will trigger the trap. If you lose the {{A|Duel}}, you will not die. If you win, however, the {{A|Trap}} will kill you and the defender will live. It is the same for a {{A|Bodyguard's}} protection. *Your target will be [[Abilities (ToS)|role-blocked]] the {{A|Night}} they are plundered. However, unlike a {{A|Jailor}}, you do not bypass any [[Abilities (ToS)|Roleblock Immunity]] they may have. Roles may still use their ability when you {{A|Duel}} them (with the exception of {{A|Retributionist}}, which is a bug). *A {{A|Serial Killer}} will be forced to attack you unless they are using their Cautious ability, but will only attack you if you lose the {{A|Duel}}. If you win the {{A|Duel}}, you will kill them and be unharmed. *Since {{A|Dueling}} is counted as a [[Abilities (ToS)|role-block]], losing a {{A|Duel}} to a {{A|Serial Killer}}, a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}, or {{A|Pestilence}} will result in your death. If you win against a {{A|Serial Killer}}, they will die and you will live, but if you {{A|Duel}} a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}, you will die even if you win, and as for {{A|Pestilence}}, they have {{A|Invincible Defense}} ({{A|Pirates}} only deal {{A|Powerful Attacks}}), so they will not even die. *When a {{A|Pirate}} dies by losing a {{A|Duel}} to a {{A|Serial Killer}}, they receive the message: "You were murdered by the {{A|Serial Killer}} you visited." *Additionally, {{A|Dueling}} a {{A|Veteran}} can, if they choose, be deadly since they can easily go on Alert which will kill you. *'''You don't need to be alive in order to win'''. If you successfully {{A|Plunder}} (kill) 2 players before you die, you will still win at the end of the game, even if you died the same {{A|night}} you got your 2nd successful {{A|Plunder}}. Unless you leave the game afterwards, you will win the game. *You do not have any kind of defense, so any means of an attack towards you is dangerous, as you are vulnerable. *If a {{A|Plaguebearer}} has {{A|infected}} you, you will {{A|infect}} the target you chose to {{A|Duel}} at the end of the {{A|day}}, rather than the {{A|night}}. However, if you {{A|Duel}} the {{A|Plaguebearer}} themselves, you will be {{A|infected}} at the end of the {{A|Night}}. *If the {{A|Pirate}} chose to duel someone but the {{A|Pirate}} got {{A|jailed}} or [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]], roles like {{A|Lookout}} and {{A|Trapper}} can still see the {{A|jailed}}/[[Death (state)|dead]] {{A|Pirate}} visit their intended target. This is a bug. *Due to a bug, if the {{A|Pirate}} chose to duel someone who just got [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] and they didn't switch to a different target, the {{A|Pirate}} will still visit that player. If the hanged player is{{A|Pestilence}}, the {{A|Pirate}} will die for visiting them. *You will die to a {{A|Vampire}} bite. {| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" color:black;border:solid 2px darkgray" ! style="color:black;" |{{A|Pirate}} {{A|Duel}} Messages  |- !If your {{A|Plundering}} fails, you will receive one of the following messages in the shown colors: |- |''Avast! Yer {{A|Scimitar's}} slash be stopped by {{A|Chainmail}}. Ye lost th' {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Arr! Yer {{A|Scimitar's}} slash be belayed by th' bilge rat's {{A|Backpedal}}. Ye lost!'' |- |''Shiver me timbers! Th' scallywag {{A|Sidestepped}} yer {{A|Rapier}}. Ye lost th' {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Blimey! Th' rapscallion {{A|Backpedaled}} away from yer {{A|Rapier}}. Ye lost th' {{A|Duel}}!'' |- !If your {{A|Plundering}} succeeds, you will receive one of the following messages instead: |- |''Yer {{A|Scimitar's}} slash could nah be {{A|Sidestepped}} by th' landlubber. Ye won th' {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Ahoy! Yer {{A|Rapier}} skewered th' scurvy dog's {{A|Chainmail}}. Ye won th' {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Yo ho ho! Th' sluggard's {{A|Backpedal}} be nah enough to stop yer shot. Ye won!'' |- !If your {{A|Dueled}} target wins, they will receive one of these messages: |- |''You {{A|Sidestepped}} out of the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Pistol}} shot. You won the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''You {{A|Sidestepped}} the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Rapier}}. You won the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Your {{A|Chainmail}} stopped the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Scimitar}} slash. You won the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''Your {{A|Chainmail}} stopped the {{A|Pirate's}} bullet. You won the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''You {{A|Backpedaled}} away from the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Rapier}} thrust.
