You won the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- !If your plundering succeeds, your target will receive one of these messages instead: |- |''You were unable to {{A|Sidestep}} the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Scimitar}} slash. You lost the {{A|Duel}}!'' |- |''The {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Rapier}} pierced your chainmail. You lost the {{A|Duel}}! '' |- |''You were unable to back away from the {{A|Pirate's}} {{A|Pistol}} shot. You lost the {{A|Duel}}!'' |} See [[Messages (ToS)#Pirate|Messages]] for all {{A|Pirate}} messages. Depending on the selected attack or defense method, the outcome will be as follows: {| class="article-table" ! !''{{A|Sidestep}}'' !''{{A|Chainmail}}'' !''{{A|Backpedal}}'' |- !''{{A|Scimitar}}'' |{{A|Pirate}} wins |Defender wins |Defender wins |- !''{{A|Rapier}}'' |Defender wins |{{A|Pirate}} wins |Defender wins |- !''{{A|Pistol}}'' |Defender wins |Defender wins |{{A|Pirate}} wins |} ===Probabilities=== The probability to win depending on the number of plundering (n) is defined as follow (for n>1) :
1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{n-1}\left(\frac23+\frac{n}{3}\right)
Demonstration
P(X>=2)=1-\left(\binom{n}{0}\times\left(\frac23\right)^{n}+\binom{n}{1}\times\left(\frac23\right)^{n-1}\times\frac13\right) =1-\left(\left(\frac23\right)^{n}+n\times\frac13\times\frac23^{n-1}\right) =1-\left(\frac23^{n-1}\left(\frac23+\frac{n}{3}\right)\right)
{| class="article-table mw-collapsible" style="text-align:center;" !Number of {{A|Plunderings}} ! % of winning  |- ! 2 |11% |- !3 |26% |- !4 |40% |- !5 |54% |- ! 6 |65% |- !7 |74% |- !8 |80% |}
It is, of course, recommended to {{A|Plunder}} every single {{A|night}} in order to have the highest chance of success. ==Strategy== *Because a {{A|Pirate}} {{A|Duel}} is considered a [[roleblock|role-block]], {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Bootleggers}}, {{A|Transporters}}, the {{A|Veteran}}, the {{A|Coven Leader}}, the {{A|Necromancer}}, and the {{A|Pestilence}} can still perform their {{A|night}} ability due to their [[Role block Immunity|role-block immunity]]. *Just like a {{A|Jailor}} who failed to Execute a player, a {{A|Pirate}} dies if they visit a non-Cautious {{A|Serial Killer}} and lost the {{A|Duel}}. On the other hand, if the {{A|Pirate}} wins the {{A|Duel}}, the {{A|Serial Killer}} won't kill them and they will kill the {{A|Serial Killer}} with their {{A|Powerful Attack}} instead. *If a {{A|Pirate}} duels a {{A|Veteran}}, they will know they're being visited by the {{A|Pirate}} due to the GUI and will be able to go on alert, killing the {{A|Pirate}}. Avoid {{A|Dueling}} a confirmed {{A|Veteran}} unless you are '''certain''' they are out of Alerts. *If you duel a {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}, you will die regardless whether you win or not, as the {{A|Werewolf}} ends up being forced to rampage at home (as {{A|Werewolves}} are not [[Abilities (ToS)|role-block]] immune). *A {{A|Pirate's}} target cannot be changed by a {{A|Transporter}}, but they can bring protective roles or even an {{A|Ambusher}} to the {{A|Pirate's}} target. This can cause odd effects like a {{A|Crusader}}/{{A|Ambusher}} killing the {{A|Pirate}} despite clicking someone else, a {{A|Doctor}} shadow-healing the {{A|Pirate's}} target, or the {{A|Bodyguard}} killing the {{A|Pirate}} with their will being wrong. A {{A|Transporter}} who does this is "stealing a heal". *Do '''not''' attempt to {{A|Duel}} anyone who has left the game. The {{A|Duel}} will not be registered to occur and you will miss out on a possible kill. *If you chose someone to {{A|Duel}} prior to the {{A|Night}}, but then instead switch to try and {{A|Duel}} against a person who then left the game, you will {{A|Duel}} the original target instead. *If the {{A|Pirate}} doesn't choose an attack, the {{A|Pirate}} will automatically lose and both {{A|Pirate}} and their victim will see no message. Therefore, you should try to avoid going AFK at {{A|night}}. *If the target doesn't choose a defense, their automatic choice depends on whether or not they have been {{A|Dueled}} since launching the game: Players {{A|Dueled}} for the first time will automatically choose {{A|Sidestep}} if no option is chosen. Players who haven't talked all game or with default names (i. e. John Hathorne) may be AFK (as if a player joins a lobby and doesn't enter a name, a random default name is given to the player), but this usually only applies to the early game. If a player has been {{A|Dueled}} before, the choice they made the last time will automatically be the choice they will make if they select no option. *A strategy you may want to try if you know the {{A|Town}} will not try to hang you (such as when there's still a {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}, or {{A|Juggernaut}} still at play), is to whisper your target and tell them an option that you won't pick. Doing so, they'll likely not pick the "losing" option for them, therefore increasing your chances of winning from 1/3 to 1/2, but they may think you're lying, and pick that option that would "lose". *Your target does not have to die for it to count as a successful {{A|Plunder}}. If you want to avoid killing people (which can be helpful in that it prolongs the game and makes you less likely to be targeted), you can focus on targets you think are likely to be healed by a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}}. *You can, in theory, side with anyone and win with them as long as you got your 2 successful {{A|Plunders}}. In practice, this rarely works out, as {{A|Town}} members won't trust you, as they know you have to kill constantly even in the absence of identified evils, while other evil teams are unlikely to reveal their entire side to you and therefore will see you as a threat. You can more easily side with {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles (especially {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}/{{A|Plaguebearer}}, as identifying them would prevent you from attacking them and dying, and you can co-operate targets), who will generally be eager for an ally. *Try to not reveal your role, as you have no defense, so you are very vulnerable, and as you deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}} and [[Abilities (ToS)|role-block]] many roles, you pose a great threat to many. *After getting 2 successful {{A|Plunders}}, you are like a {{A|Survivor}}, and can generally side with anyone and win with them. Claiming you have been a secret {{A|Survivor}} the whole time might be a good play, and you can also stop {{A|Plundering}} people as soon as you won 2 {{A|Duels}}. *Remember that {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Serial Killers}} (with Cautious disabled) and {{A|Werewolves}} (on nights with a {{A|Full Moon}}) will automatically attack you if you lose the {{A|Duel}} ({{A|Pestilence}} and {{A|Werewolf}} will attack you regardless of the result). *When {{A|Dueling}} players, you may want to try and target possible killing roles in order to prolong the game and give you more time to win. *In particular, if you target someone, they survive, and there's no kill by an existing {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} killing role the next morning, you may want to target the same person again as soon as you can, as they may be the killing role you are looking for. Conversely, if there is a kill, you may want to move on to someone else in hopes of finding and neutralizing rival killers. You should also generally skip over anyone else you know for certain is not a rival killer, such as confirmed {{A|Town}} members, anyone who has been [[Abilities (ToS)|role-blocked]] during previous {{A|Nights}} when many kills happened (which makes it unlikely for them to be a killer), or anyone whose revealed investigative results that are confirmed to be true. However, remember that you can't target the same person twice in a row, so you're not able to prevent actions from a player completely. Furthermore, you can use the player you attacked, and/or the fact they are [[Abilities (ToS)|role-blocked]], to claim some {{A|Town}} roles (such as a {{A|Town Investigative}} who discovered them). However, be warned that they will likely attempt to out you as a {{A|Pirate}}. Luckily, they have to confess themselves to do so. With some trickery, you might be able to get them, instead of you, hanged, and {{A|Town}} would believe you word if so. If you claim a {{A|Town Investigative}} role, such as a {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Tracker}}, {{A|Lookout}}, or {{A|Investigator}}, and use that to accuse them of being the killer, they may not realize you were the {{A|Pirate}} who roleblocked them. However, you risk being outed as evil if they aren't the role you thought they were and the kill was skipped for other reasons. If they are hanged and turn out to be a {{A|Town}} member, you can try to turn this mistake to your advantage by claiming to be an already-won {{A|Executioner}}. You can also expose them to distract a {{A|Town}} from hanging you. A {{A|Mafioso}}, {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Coven}} killing role is generally higher priority for the {{A|Town}} than a {{A|Pirate}}, so this can buy you another {{A|night}}. *In a pinch, if you've been unsuccessfully {{A|Dueling}} a killing role repeatedly every other {{A|night}}, you can claim {{A|Pirate}} when pressed and tell the {{A|Town}} you'll keep locking them down until you successfully kill them. Avoid revealing as a {{A|Pirate}} in this fashion unless it seems absolutely necessary, since it's unpredictable how {{A|Town}} members will react, and you lack even the {{A|Basic Defense}} needed to keep a {{A|Vigilante}} with an itchy trigger finger or some other random killer from killing you regardless of how the rest of the {{A|Town}} feels. *As a {{A|Pirate}}, you want the game to last as long as possible (since that gives you more chances to {{A|Plunder}} people successfully) unless you have already won. Therefore, you should usually try to slow down voting, and vote innocent whenever it's justifiable. *You do usually want to find and hang {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles, since they're both a threat to you and will end the game faster if unchecked, but they can also be an ally later in the game (after you won). This is another reason why it's a good idea for you to try and [[Abilities (ToS)|role-block]] rival killers when you can, as saving the life of the {{A|Town}} prevents the game from ending and gives you more time to {{A|Plunder}}. *It may be a good idea to attack someone who claims to be an {{A|Executioner}} who has successfully hanged their target, as they have already won. Some {{A|Executioners}} may even call for a {{A|Pirate}} to attack them (or sometimes {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot them) and announce which defense they'll use to proof they are not fake claiming a victory. However, this may be a {{A|Werewolf}} (or {{A|Serial Killer}}, risking the fact that they will win, or {{A|Pestilence}}, if it already has already been summoned) claiming as an already-won as {{A|Executioner}}, so be careful about attacking them on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} if you know there's a {{A|Werewolf}}. *Players with default names (i.e. John Hathorne) may have not picked a name because they are AFK. {{A|Dueling}} them and picking {{A|Scimitar}} could net you a successful {{A|Plunder}} early on in the game, due to AFK players being forced to sidestep. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{PirateAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{PirateMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.3}}, {{A|Spies}} would still be able to know who the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} visit, and {{A|Trappers}} would still build their {{A|Traps}} despite being {{A|Dueled}} by a {{A|Pirate}}, which is considered a [[roleblock|role-block]]. *The 3 options on the {{A|Pirate}} GUI are based on rock-paper-scissors. *A bug exists where if the {{A|Pirate}} has a {{A|Trap}} placed on them, {{A|Duels}} the {{A|Pestilence}} and '''wins''', while also '''being visited by''' the {{A|Pestilence}}, they will not die and receive the message "You were attacked but a {{A|Trap}} saved you!". If the {{A|Pirate}} {{A|Duels}} the {{A|Pestilence}} while having a {{A|Trap}}placed on them and '''loses''', the same night the {{A|Pestilence}} visits them, they will die. *The {{A|Pirate}} is the only {{A|Neutral Chaos}} role that is considered non-factional, allowing them to win with any faction provided they have successfully plundered 2 players (and for the other non-factional roles, if their win condition is satisfied, as all non-factional roles are {{A|Neutral}} and solo, and as long as their win condition is satisfied, they win unless they leave). *The {{A|Pirate}} can have a solo win screen if they are the last player alive, or everyone dies and the {{A|Pirate}} win condition is the only one satisfied (if no win conditions are satisfied and everyone dies, it is a draw). This is the same for other non-factional roles. You can find a game where the {{A|Pirate}} win screen pops up [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wa7mqx25WcE here]. *The {{A|Pirate}} is the only role in the game that can consistently kill a role with {{A|Basic Defense}} on the first {{A|Night}}, as all other roles that have attack values higher than {{A|Basic Attack}} cannot attack on the first night no matter what (A {{A|Jailor}} cannot execute their target even if controlled, the {{A|Juggernaut}} and the {{A|Werewolf}} cannot attack since the first night is not a {{A|Full Moon}} and other roles such as the {{A|Veteran}} rely on things that are out of your control). *There is an {{A|Achievement}} for losing 10 {{A|Duels}} called "But You Have Heard of Me". This is a reference to the film ''The Pirates of the Caribbean''. Jack Sparrow says this line to James Norrington after being called "the worst pirate he's ever heard of". *{{A|Pirate}} is 1 of only 4 roles that have a {{A|day}} ability, the others being the {{A|Mayor}}, a dead {{A|Medium}} and the {{A|Jailor}}. *According to the formula in the Probability section, it would take approximately 68 {{A|Plunders}} to have an approximately 100% (1) chance of winning. ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.11]] **Fixed {{A|Coven Leader}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}} and {{A|Transporter}} being roleblocked by {{A|Pirate}}. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trappers}} are now [[Role block|role blocked]] from building their trap by {{A|Pirates}}. **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Added victory check for {{A|Pirate}} during all dead scenario. **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} incorrectly seeing someone visiting when {{A|Dueled}}. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Pirate's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Pirate.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Pirate's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Pirate Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Пират]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Chaos roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Role blocking]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:Roleblock Immune]] [[Category:Control Immune]] [[Category:Detection Immune]]

Plaguebearer (ToS).title: Plaguebearer (ToS)
Plaguebearer (ToS).wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Plaguebearer}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Plaguebearer}}[[File:RoleIcon Plaguebearer.png|thumb|center|100px]] |alignment = {{A|Neutral Chaos}} |avatar=[[File:Plaguebearer_Avatar.png|150px]] |summary = You are an acolyte of Pestilence who spreads disease among the town. |abilities = You may choose to infect a player with the Plague each night. |investigator ='''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be an {{InvResCVN10}}. |consigliere = Your target is a carrier of disease. They must be the {{A|Plaguebearer}}. |special = [[Unique Role]] |goal = Infect all living players and become {{A|Pestilence}}. |attributestext = Players will not know they have been infected.
When all living players are infected you become {{A|Pestilence}}.|attributes = {{A|Attack}}: None
{{A|Defense}}: Basic|type = Special
Unique|winwith = '''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}'''|mustkill = '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Vampires}}'''
'''{{A|Arsonist}}'''
'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Coven}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} [[File:SpecialLabel_Plague.png|alt=|thumb|The icon that displays next to {{A|Infected}} players in the player list]] ==Mechanics== *You may choose to visit someone each night, infecting them with the {{A|plague}}. *You cannot choose people who are already {{A|Infected}}. *Anyone that visits you will become {{A|Infected}}. *Anyone who visits or is visited by an {{A|Infected}} player becomes {{A|Infected}}. *If the {{A|Jailor}} jails someone who is {{A|Infected}} and does not execute them, the {{A|Jailor}} will become {{A|Infected}}. (This also applies if the {{A|Jailor}} jails you.) *Players will not know when they have been {{A|Infected}}. *If all living players but you are {{A|Infected}}, you will become the {{A|Pestilence}} and the {{A|Town}} will be alerted the following day with a message saying "A plague has consumed the {{A|Town}}, summoning {{A|Pestilence, Horseman of the Apocalypse}}." *If you are killed on the same night everyone is {{A|Infected}}, you will not become {{A|Pestilence}}. No message alerting the {{A|Town}} will appear, and you will die. *If the last uninfected person is hanged, you will become {{A|Pestilence}} immediately after their role has been announced during the {{A|Day}}. ==Notes== *The {{A|Plaguebearer}} is a [[Unique Role]], only one may exist at a time. *If one healthy person visits an {{A|Infected}} person who visits another healthy person, the plague will spread, so it is possible to become {{A|Pestilence}} in five days or less without kills (meaning all 15 players alive). *If an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers themselves as a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, they will not have to {{A|Infect}} already {{A|Infected}} targets, and rather {{A|Infect}} the rest of the non-{{A|Infected}} people. *If an {{A|Amnesiac}} {{A|Plaguebearer}}/{{A|Pestilence}} goes on to win the game, both the {{A|Amnesiac}} and the original {{A|Plaguebearer}}/{{A|Pestilence}} will win. *If an {{A|Infected}} {{A|Necromancer}} or {{A|Retributionist}} uses someone in the [[graveyard]], their target '''will''' be {{A|Infected}}. This will not count towards becoming {{A|Pestilence}}, since they are dead (only all living players need to be infected). *If a {{A|Necromancer}} or {{A|Retributionist}} uses someone in the [[Graveyard]] on a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, then the {{A|Necromancer}} or {{A|Retributionist}} will become {{A|Infected}} along with the reanimated role, even if neither was previously {{A|Infected}}. *If someone visits you but is intercepted by a {{A|Crusader}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}, they will not be {{A|Infected}}. *A few specific roles, most notably the {{A|Investigator}}, will not become {{A|Infected}} after visiting you or an {{A|Infected}} player. Additionally, the {{A|Godfather}} will not become {{A|Infected}} killing an {{A|Infected}} player (this is a bug). *The {{A|Plaguebearer}} will not get a message about their target being in {{A|Jail}} (this is a bug). *If the last uninfected person dies during the {{A|Night}} without getting {{A|Infected}} (e.g. haunted by a {{A|Jester}}), you will not immediately become {{A|Pestilence}} at the end of that {{A|Night}}. But you will become {{A|Pestilence}} either at the end of the next {{A|Day}} if someone gets hanged or at the end of the next {{A|Night}} if no one gets hanged. ==Strategy== *Try to visit people that you know are going to have a lot of traffic, but less likely to die. For example, if someone says, "Investigate ____ tonight", you should probably {{A|Infect}} the person they are going to visit, as the {{A|Investigator}}, if visits the person, will bring the {{A|plague}} to other people when investigating them. *Try infecting names that stand out at the beginning of the game. Since you don't attack your victim, you are safe from {{A|Bodyguards}}. The {{A|Crusader}} can attack you, but due to your {{A|Basic Defense}}, you will be fine, but they know one of their unknown visitors is immune. However, if a {{A|Tracker}} follows you or a {{A|Lookout}} watches the same target you {{A|Infect}} and isn't targeted by the {{A|Crusader}}, you are in trouble. *Try to {{A|Infect}} a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or the {{A|Jailor}} because most {{A|Town Protective}} roles will be on them. Or, {{A|Infect}} a {{A|Town Protective}} that is on a confirmed {{A|Town}} member. However, since a revealed {{A|Mayor}} and the {{A|Jailor}} is a high priority to evils, they will be targeting the {{A|Town Protective}} roles (which the {{A|Plague}} also spread to), then kill the {{A|Mayor}} and {{A|Jailor}}, wasting you a night. *You will know exactly who an {{A|Infected}} {{A|Jailor}} jails, since the jailed player becomes {{A|Infected}} at the end of the {{A|Day}}. Use this to strengthen your claims. *Infecting a {{A|Transporter}} can quickly increase who becomes {{A|Infected}} due to them being able to visit two people per night. However, they might transport the same person/people, but this is still a better infection than a role like {{A|Medium}}, who only speaks with the dead. *{{A|Werewolf}} strategies work well with this role - but make sure you don't visit the same target as a {{A|Werewolf}} as you will die. *Often times, going after {{A|Town Investigative}} or {{A|Town Support}} roles (i. e. {{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Doctor}} and {{A|Sheriff}}) can spread the {{A|plague}} quickly. However, {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} would often target them, as they can be a great threat to them. *You can always go to {{A|Infect}} suspicious people, as they tend to have a lot of visiting role attraction. *If you are role blocked by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}/{{A|Bootlegger}} early in the game, you can always claim {{A|Tracker}} for an early cover-up. *As {{A|Plaguebearer}}, you usually want to participate in {{A|Town}} debates, talk and bring your help to the {{A|Town}}. If you stay silent, you will be spotted out of suspicion immediately after the {{A|Town}} receives the message stating that you turned into {{A|Pestilence}} and you will be hanged. Being active will help you claim a role easily afterward and survive until there are only a few players left, which you can finish off with your newly gained {{A|Powerful Attack}}. This does not stop another strategy of being to lay low and wait until there are 5 or fewer players alive, then start infecting. Becoming {{A|Pestilence}} should be easy because there will be only 4 or fewer people to {{A|Infect}}. Be wary that you do not wait too long, or you may be found by the {{A|Town}} and hanged, or killed by roles with a {{A|Powerful Attack}}. *{{A|Lookout}} is a good claim for this role, especially early on. You know who is {{A|Infected}}, and players spread {{A|Infection}} by visiting each other. By the same logic, {{A|Tracker}} is also a good claim. Be cautious about claiming these roles unnecessarily, as smart players will grow suspicious of you once you turn into {{A|Pestilence}}. *Early on, you want to {{A|Infect}} visiting roles so they spread the disease. Later on, you might want to target non-visiting roles yourself, especially ones that have been confirmed (and are therefore unlikely to be visited by anyone else) as they are most likely uninfected, and have low traffic and you are less likely to be seen or found. *A {{A|Veteran}} being in the game makes it unlikely that everyone will be {{A|Infected}} as long as they live, as the {{A|Veteran}} may often go on alert. The only way to pass this is to {{A|Infect}} someone who may visit the {{A|Veteran}}, or hang the {{A|Veteran}} later in the game when evils have majority. *Try to {{A|Infect}} visiting roles early, and only go for non-visiting roles if you have no one else to go for. *You can win the game without infecting everyone, as long as only you, or with the addition of {{A|Survivors}}, are alive. *Once you become {{A|Pestilence}}, the {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles (i.e. {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Serial Killer}}) are completely harmless to you, as they are most likely loners that cannot harm you at {{A|Night}} as they will be killed trying to do so. Therefore, once you do become {{A|Pestilence}}, you should focus on killing off the {{A|Town}}, {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}} and {{A|Vampires}}, as they can easily hang you during the {{A|Day}} (that is the only way {{A|Pestilence}} can die, except for leaving the game). Before that happens, however, the {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles pose a massive threat to you. The {{A|Werewolf}} and {{A|Juggernaut}} can just kill you outright, and the {{A|Serial Killer}} can still call you out for being immune. Therefore, it might be worth it to get rid these roles early on, to make sure you aren't killed at night or exposed through a {{A|Death Note}}. *You shouldn't worry as much about the {{A|Arsonist}} compared to the other {{A|Neutral Killings}}, as they most likely won't ignite before you become {{A|Pestilence}}, and {{A|Pestilence}} is immune to ignition. ==Dealing with the {{A|Plaguebearer}}== *If you are a {{A|Town Investigative}} role that is told to check upon another person's role, you might want to refrain from doing so if you know that the {{A|Town}} is vulnerable in the case of a {{A|Pestilence}} (for example, the {{A|Town}} only has the same amount of {{A|Town}} members as there are all evil roles combine). However, if you think you are already {{A|Infected}}, or if you think it is inevitable that a {{A|Pestilence}} will be coming soon, then you should continue visiting that person, as you would be helping catch {{A|Pestilence}} by narrowing down the pool of suspects. *The best way to stop {{A|Plaguebearer}} is to kill them early before they become {{A|Pestilence}}. If you are a {{A|Town Investigative}} role and you happen to find someone suspicious of being a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, it is not a bad idea to announce your suspicions of a certain person. Even then if the {{A|Plaguebearer}} becomes {{A|Pestilence}}, the whole {{A|Town}} will probably hang {{A|Pestilence}} immediately. Announcing that you found a {{A|Plaguebearer}} earlier and then having them turn into a {{A|Pestilence}} makes your claim a lot more believable than if you just revealed it to the {{A|Town}} right when the {{A|Plaguebearer}} becomes {{A|Pestilence}}. ==Becoming {{A|Pestilence, Horseman of the Apocalypse}}== *If you do manage to become {{A|Pestilence}}, you are armed with {{A|Powerful Attacks}}, {{A|Invincible Defense}}, infinite "alerts" that are always active, and a devastating Rampage ability (similar to the {{A|Werewolf}}). However, you also become everyone's top priority as you can decimate every role there is with no worry about dying at {{A|Night}}. Refer to the {{A|Pestilence}} page on strategies once you transcend. *Unfortunately, your possibly suspicious claim that you might have had before will be thrown out the window and you will become a suspect. So it is crucial to have been a positive influence on the {{A|Town}} and have a solid claim as {{A|Plaguebearer}} before the {{A|Town}} turns to you as the first suspect. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{PlaguebearerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{PlaguebearerMessages}} ==Trivia== *Before the switch to Unity, the {{A|Plaguebearer}} would receive a list of everyone who becomes {{A|Infected}} at the end of each {{A|Night}}. **The message from the list was "''(Player) has been infected with the plague.''" *The {{A|Plaguebearer}} is the only "dousing" role to not change their target's investigation results. *It is possible to become {{A|Pestilence}} without visiting anyone, however this can only happen if you are visited. *The {{A|Plaguebearer}} is the only role in the game which doesn't tell you all the ways to win, as it says you must infect everyone and become {{A|Pestilence}}, however, in the rare event that the {{A|Plaguebearer}} is the last player alive, they will win despite not infecting everybody. ==History== *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate {{A|Infected}} players for the {{A|Plaguebearer}} ([[File:SpecialLabel Plague.png|30x30px]]). **Removed message "(Player) has been infected with the plague.". **The {{A|Plaguebearer's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Plaguebearer.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Plaguebearer's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Plaguebearer Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Носитель Чумы]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Chaos roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Psychic}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|Auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Psychic}}[[File:RoleIcon Psychic.png|thumb|left|100px]] |avatar=[[File:PsychicSkinFront.png|150px]] |alignment = {{A|Town Investigative}} |attributes = Attack: None

Non-unique |priority = 4 |sheriff = You cannot find evidence of wrongdoing. Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets! |investigator = '''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvResCVN3}}. |consigliere = Your target has the sight. They must be a {{A|Psychic}}. |summary = You are a powerful seer with a gift for finding one's secrets. |abilities = Receive a vision every night. |attributestext = On odd nights you will have a vision of three players, at least one will be Evil.
On even nights you will have a vision of two players, at least one will be Good |goal = Hang every criminal and evildoer. |winwith = '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}''' |mustkill = '''{{A|Mafia}}'''

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }}{{Story}} == Mechanics == *On odd-numbered {{A|Nights}}, you will get three names, at least one of which is evil. On even-numbered {{A|Nights}}, you will get two names, at least one of which is good. *If you are {{A|Jailed}} or [[Role block|roleblocked]], you will not receive a {{A|Vision}}. *If you are controlled by a {{A|Coven Leader}}, they will receive a vision you would have otherwise received. {| class="wikitable"; !{{A|Psychic}} Result !Possible [[Roles (ToS)|Roles]] |- !rowspan=2|Appears as 'good' in visions |All {{A|Townies}} (including the {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}}) |- |{{A|Neutral Benign}} |- !rowspan=5|Appears as 'evil' in visions |All members of the {{A|Mafia}} |- |All members of the {{A|Coven}} |- |{{A|Neutral Killing}} |- |{{A|Neutral Chaos}} |- |{{A|Neutral Evil}} |} == Strategy == *Reveal early on and ask for a {{A|Crusader}} on you. Often a {{A|Crusader}} will do as asked if they are smart, and you can easily start helping the {{A|Town}} rat out suspicious people. **However, if {{A|Medusa}} killed some {{A|Townies}}, you may get [[hanged]] under suspicion of being {{A|Medusa}}. *Generally, the {{A|Psychic}} relies on the whole {{A|Town}} to be useful. Having fellow {{A|Town Investigative}} roles can help the {{A|Psychic}} even further by gaining information about the roles that are potentially evil. *Writing confirmed {{A|Townies}} in your {{A|Last Will}} may seem like a good idea, but remember that when your {{A|Last Will}} is revealed, it potentially makes them a target for killers. *Calling someone out as evil early on is generally ''not'' a good idea. One, you could end up guessing wrong and getting an innocent {{A|Townie}} [[hanged]]. Two, people could think you are an {{A|Executioner}} and ignore you. Three, a {{A|Psychic}} is a high-priority target for the {{A|Mafia}} so you will likely be dead within a few {{A|Nights}}. **However, if it is {{A|Night}} 3, a person has appeared twice, and one or two other people on those two visions have died, it is likely they are evil. Call them out, or whisper it to a confirmed {{A|Townie}}. **If there is a {{A|Medusa}}, the {{A|Town}} will often not believe a late {{A|Psychic}} claim, so you may want to claim {{A|Day}} 1 or 2, especially if there are other {{A|Psychic}} claims. *Narrow down your pool of suspects. Two of the given potential evil roles may be good, and their death may confirm their innocence. *If you receive an evil vision and find one of the players to be evil, the remaining two players are still more likely than average to be evil. This is because the player that was found to be evil could have been evil by coincidence, and was not the player referred to as the evil one out of the three. The same thing applies with good visions. **When receiving a vision on the first {{A|Night}}, there is a 27% chance of only one of the players being evil, a 54% chance of two of the players being evil, and a 19% chance of all of them being evil. *If the {{A|Town}} has no information that confirms a player as an evil role, consider voting those that appear on the odd {{A|Night}} vision. You are not compelled to [[hang]] them, but forcing them to claim is a very effective strategy. *A {{A|Jester}} will appear as evil in your vision. This means that you should be warier when deciding which people in your odd {{A|Night}} vision should be [[hanged]]. ==Playing against {{A|Psychics}}== *Since a {{A|Psychic}} claim is easy to fake, claiming {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} and saying that the {{A|Psychic}} visited them is a potential way to get rid of a trustworthy {{A|Townie}}. **If a {{A|Psychic}} claim has themselves in a vision, they are likely a {{A|Jester}} faking it or another evil role. **As a {{A|Disguiser}}, you can ask a {{A|Lookout}} to watch you while you disguise yourself as the {{A|Psychic}}. Any {{A|Lookouts}} watching you will see the "{{A|Psychic}}" visiting you and will proceed to call out the {{A|Psychic}} without needing to accuse them yourself. *Simply pointing out that the {{A|Psychic}} could be {{A|Medusa}} can have them [[hanged]]. This works better if an actual {{A|Medusa}} {{A|Stoned}} someone previously. *As a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can take away most of the {{A|Psychic}}'s effectiveness by role-blocking them on odd-numbered {{A|Nights}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{PsychicAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{PsychicMessages}} ==Trivia== *If you are the among the last 3 players in a game alive on an odd {{A|Night}}, you will receive a message saying "The town is too small to accurately find an evildoer!" **You'll also get this message when the last evil remaining is the [[Game Modes - Coven|Town Traitor]]. *If no other {{A|Townies}} or {{A|Neutral Benigns}} are alive, you will receive a message, "The town is too evil to find anyone good!" on an even {{A|Night}}. **A {{A|Coven Leader}} controlling you will '''not''' steal this message (this may be a bug). ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.11]] **Fixed {{A|Psychic}} getting the controlled message twice **Fixed {{A|Psychic}} still getting information when witched/controlled by {{A|Coven Leader}} *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.5]] **{{A|Psychic}} now receives evil visions on odd-numbered {{A|Nights}} and good visions on even-numbered {{A|Nights}}. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.3]] **Fixed {{A|Psychic}} description in game and lobby. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.2.0]] **Fixed {{A|Psychic}} description in lobby. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Psychic}}'s role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Psychic.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Psychic}}'s circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Psychic Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.3.2.9706]] **{{A|Witch}} is no longer in visions. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.0.0.6582]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Экстрасенс]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town Investigative roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Juggernaut}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Juggernaut}}[[File:RoleIcon Juggernaut.png|thumb|left|100px]]

'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *As the {{A|Juggernaut}}, you become stronger each time you kill someone. *The {{A|Juggernaut}} starts off with a {{A|Powerful Attack}} and {{A|Basic Defense}}. *The {{A|Juggernaut}} can only kill on {{A|Full Moons}} (every {{A|night}} in the game except 1 and 3) at the start. The {{A|Juggernaut}} gains up to 3 new abilities upon killing a player: **After the {{A|Juggernaut's}} first kill, they will receive a message saying "You have gained a new ability! You may now Attack every night." This allows them to {{A|Attack}} each {{A|night}} and not be restricted to {{A|Full Moons}}. **After the second kill, the message will say "You have gained a new ability! You now [[Abilities (ToS)#Night_Abilities|Rampage]] when you Attack." When the {{A|Juggernaut}} {{A|Attacks}}, anyone who visits the {{A|Juggernaut's}} target will also be dealt a {{A|Powerful Attack}} (similar to the {{A|Werewolf}} and {{A|Pestilence}}, however, you cannot [[Abilities (ToS)#Night_Abilities|rampage]] at home). **After the third kill, the message will say, "You have gained a new ability! You ignore effects that would protect a player." This means that the {{A|Juggernaut}} gains an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}, which will allow the {{A|Juggernaut}} to bypass all protective roles without dying to them, including {{A|Bodyguard}} and {{A|Trapper}}, and even {{A|Jail}}! *Due to a bug, it is sometimes possible for a {{A|Juggernaut}} with only two kills to have an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} (confirmed to bypass a {{A|Doctor}}'s heal and {{A|Jail}}) on the very night they get their third kill, as long as they kill someone with their {{A|Rampage (Juggernaut)}} ability. *Unlike most attackers, you will never receive a {{A|defense}} message if your target was protected, regardless of your power level. *A {{A|Juggernaut}} with {{A|Rampage (Juggernaut)}} gets one less ''“You attacked someone”'' message than they’re supposed to. Due to a bug, the game only counts the {{A|Rampage (Juggernaut)}} attacks, not the total amount of attacks. ==Strategy== *Your strategy should change according to the abilities you gain. For example, once you gain the {{A|Rampage (Juggernaut)}} ability, you should switch your strategy to that of a {{A|Werewolf}}. Be wary of visiting the same target as the {{A|Werewolf}}, however, as you will die from their {{A|Powerful Attack}}. *Once you gain access to an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}, you can now target anyone in the entire game and kill them (except {{A|Pestilence}}) regardless of their protection, most notably those protected by a {{A|Jailor}}. Use this to your advantage by taking out high-priority targets, such as a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, who could be relying on {{A|Jailors}} or {{A|Crusaders}} for protection. *Despite being able to kill nearly everything at certain levels, you only have {{A|Basic Defense}}. However, at full power you do not get counter-attacked by a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trapper}}. *Initially, try to avoid drawing attention to yourself. This is because the beginning of the game is when you are at your weakest, due to you only being able to Attack every {{A|Full Moon}}. Once you have started to kill more players and your power has started to increase significantly, then you can worry less about being killed at night. **Avoid starting to become more relaxed and careless as you increase in power. If the {{A|Town}} notices before that you were very silent and not participating much, but suddenly start to become more active and involved in trying to hang others, they may suspect that this newfound confidence is due to your increased power and as such may suspect you of being an evil role that is becoming cocky. More so, just stay consistent throughout the game, and be aggressive when absolutely needed. ***Once your identity is confirmed, {{A|Townies}} may even suspect that you are the {{A|Juggernaut}} who is becoming more and more comfortable as their killing power increases. Always try to blend in with the {{A|Town}} and never go through sudden shifts in personality as this may lead them to become suspicious of you. This may be a good {{A|Jester}} strategy, although it will only work with highly perceptive players. ***The {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}}, and {{A|Coven}} may also be suspicious of you if you start becoming more and more active due to your decreased fear of dying at night. They may Attack you and expose your {{A|Basic Defense}}, or a {{A|Potion Master}} / {{A|Consigliere}} may expose you outright or may possibly try to get you killed. *As the {{A|Juggernaut}}, your worst enemy is {{A|Pestilence}}. This is because they have {{A|Invincible Defense}} and a {{A|Powerful Attack}}. If you {{A|Attack}} each other while fully powered up, you will die due to your {{A|defense}} being lower than the {{A|Pestilence's}} {{A|Attack}}, even when maxed out. {{A|Pestilence}}, however, will survive. **Do note, however; there is an {{A|Achievement}} for when a maxed out {{A|Juggernaut}} Attacks {{A|Pestilence}}. If you are going for the {{A|Achievements}}, it is recommended for both to reveal yourself for it. *Helping the {{A|Town}} point out a {{A|Coven Leader}} without being too suspicious is a good idea. The {{A|Coven Leader}} can control you and make you target yourself, which would lead to killing yourself if you are on your first kill. **Remember, if you are on your second or last kill, you gain rampage ability, so the {{A|Coven Leader}} making you target yourself will result in their death. However, unlike a {{A|Werewolf}}, you do not Rampage at home when you target yourself. Therefore, you will still die from your own {{A|Attack}}. *{{A|Transporters}} are trouble, as they can make you kill yourself if they transport you with your target. Even if you have the rampage ability, you still risk the {{A|Transporter}} sacrificing themselves to end you. They can effectively force a draw between you and the {{A|Town}} if left in a 1v1 situation. *Beware of roles that can {{A|roleblock}} as like the {{A|Arsonist}}, you do not Attack {{A|[Roleblockers}}. The {{A|Pirate}} isn't as much of a direct threat unlike {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Bootleggers}}, and the {{A|Jailor}}; but they can still kill you without risk due to their {{A|Powerful Attack}}. Also, if you are roleblocked and there are no kills from the {{A|Juggernaut}} the next day, the {{A|Town}} will most likely suspect whoever is {{A|Roleblocked}} to be the {{A|Juggernaut}}. **If there is a known role blocker, you may attempt to not kill at all one night to trick {{A|Roleblockers}} into thinking whoever they {{A|Roleblocked}} was the {{A|Juggernaut}}. Do note, however, you are wasting a night kill to do this, along with a power-up. *When selecting who to kill, choose roles that are likely to be unprotected. This way, you can escape an easy kill and gain your other abilities more quickly. Try to avoid Attacking talkative people or {{A|Townies}} that are drawing attention to themselves as they could be a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Werewolf}} baiting. Always remember you only have {{A|Basic Defense}}; try going for quiet people, and avoid suspicion or being targeted by other killing roles who may have a higher Attack value. *Your priorities on who to eliminate change as you increase in power. In the beginning, you should focus on taking out {{A|Townies}} (and sometimes {{A|Survivors}}) as they are the common enemy for evils. As you gain rampaging Attacks, consider starting to eliminate members of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}}, or members of the {{A|Coven}}, as if they remain alive for too long without sustaining any casualties, you run the risk that they quickly gain a majority and hang you. Consider leaving other solo-evils such as the {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, and {{A|Plaguebearer}} alone until you have to eliminate them. This is because not only can they help kill off {{A|Townies}}, members of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}} and {{A|Coven}} members, but they also pose less of a threat to you compared to the factions. *Try to gain the support of helpful {{A|Neutral}} roles, such as any {{A|Executioners}}, {{A|Jesters}}, or {{A|Pirates}}. Their support could make all the difference if it comes down to you, them, and one member of an opposing faction. Have them on your side as they will most likely side with a {{A|Juggernaut}} over other {{A|Neutral Killings}}, {{A|Mafia}}, or {{A|Coven}}. **If someone claims a {{A|Neutral}} role, don't whisper them until they will really help you. Too early, and you might be suspected as evil. **Only kill a {{A|Neutral}} claim if there is evidence against them that they are evil. For example, an {{A|Investigator}} saying that they are something other than {{A|Survivor}} means you can Attack the {{A|Survivor}} claim. Some {{A|Survivor}} claims are {{A|Amnesiacs}} hoping to remember a fun role such as a {{A|Neutral Killing}} like {{A|Juggernaut}}. ==Dealing with {{A|Juggernauts}}== *It is best to find and hang a {{A|Juggernaut}} early in the game as the {{A|Juggernaut's}} power will increase with every kill. **If there is an early {{A|Juggernaut}} kill, try interrogating silent people. People will tend to stay silent and tend to try to live as long as possible as {{A|Juggernaut}} is a rare role. *A very simple way to deter a non-fully powered{{A|Juggernaut}} as a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trapper}} is to simply protect people that seem quiet or not worth it to protect usually. Protecting a target this way, and possibly baiting the {{A|Juggernaut}} to attack them, takes them down quickly and may provide a break for the {{A|Town}}. *As a {{A|Coven Leader}}, if you find the {{A|Juggernaut}}, you can make them kill themselves by controlling them into themselves (A similar case is true for {{A|Transporters}}). This is only recommended before they gain their rampage ability, and it might be a better idea to use them as an extension of the {{A|Coven's}} killing power. *As a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can permanently shut down the {{A|Juggernaut's}} killing power by identifying and {{A|Roleblocking}} them, giving the {{A|Mafia}} more time to gain a majority to hang them as unlike the {{A|Werewolf}}, the {{A|Juggernaut}} does not rampage at home whether or not they were {{A|Roleblocked}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{JuggernautAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{JuggernautMessages}} ==Trivia== *{{A|Juggernaut}} is the only {{A|Neutral Killing}} role who cannot attack/{{Amne|Douse}} a {{A|Jailor}} when {{A|Jailed}} and not {{A|Executed}}. *Prior to [[Version History (ToS)|Version 3.2.4]], The {{A|Juggernaut}} had an extremely low spawn rate. *Prior to [[Version History (ToS)|Version 3.2.5]], the {{A|Juggernaut}} did not have an investigative result and had to gain their Basic defense by killing two people. *A fully powered up {{A|Juggernaut}} is the only role in the game able to deal consistent {{A|Unstoppable Attacks}} directly. *The {{A|Juggernaut}} cannot be added directly in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Custom Modes]]; it can only spawn when a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, {{A|Random Neutral}}, or {{A|Any}} slot is available. *The only way to obtain a {{A|Scroll}} for the {{A|Juggernaut}} is to purchase a bundle that gives a {{A|Scroll}} for every single role as you cannot buy them in the shop. *In the older Flash version of the game, the {{A|Juggernaut}} appeared as "???" during the role spin, changing into the proper name if it was picked. It would also play a triumphant sound upon being selected. *If {{A|Pestilence}} and a fully powered up {{A|Juggernaut}} Attack each other, everyone alive will receive the notification, "''An unstoppable force meets an invincible object. The ground beneath your feet shudders!''" The {{A|Juggernaut}} will still die, though, due to their defense being insignificant against a {{A|Powerful Attack}}. **The quote is a reference to the irresistible force paradox, yet the paradox does not apply to the gameplay situation. **Receiving this notification will grant you an {{A|Achievement}}. This only works if you are in a game where it happens. ***If you are dead, the message and {{A|Achievement}} will not show up, but if you restart Town of Salem, you will have the [[Achievements (ToS)|achievement]]. This appears to be a glitch. *If a {{A|Necromancer}} uses the ability of a dead {{A|Juggernaut}}, the dead {{A|Juggernaut}} will still power up, even though they are dead. **The dead {{A|Juggernaut}} will receive a notification that they have powered up if they have not left the game. This is likely a bug. *An {{A|Amnesiac}} who remembers that they were a {{A|Juggernaut}} will keep the power level of the previous {{A|Juggernaut}} had. *There used to be a bug where the {{A|Juggernaut}} was able to kill {{A|Pestilence}} if they stayed at home. You can see the bug in a video linked [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nGswmAZ_jxw&t=14m19s here] (Timestamp: 14:19). *Upon releasing the {{A|Coven Expansion}} into the [[Public Test Realm]] for players to try for the first time, the {{A|Juggernaut}} was to be a secret. However, this secret was quickly found by the community when players had noticed {{A|Juggernaut}} {{A|Scrolls}} in the game's [[Points (ToS)|shop]]. [[BlankMediaGames]] then removed the scrolls from the game's shop, but players still discovered the role's name due to the [[Achievements (ToS)#Juggernaut|Achievements]] screen displaying the name. **The achievements were then locked until you earned an achievement regarding the {{A|Juggernaut}}. ==History== *[[Version History (ToS)|3.3.1]] **Fixed issue with {{A|Arsonist}} passive {{A|Douses}} not working on {{A|Juggernaut}} in some scenarios. *[[Version History (ToS)|3.2.5]] **The {{A|Juggernaut}} now starts the game with {{A|Basic Defense}}. **The {{A|Juggernaut}} now gains their abilities with 1 less kill required. *[[Version History (ToS)|3.2.4]] **{{A|Juggernaut}} now has much better odds to show up in games. **Temporary {{A|defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give Attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *[[Version History (ToS)|3.2.3]] **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are Attacked. *[[Version History (ToS)|3.1.14]] **{{A|Juggernaut}} now removes {{A|Poison}} when gaining {{A|Basic Defense}}. *[[Version History (ToS)|2.5.5.12200]] **No longer shows up as "???" on the Role Wheel. **Removed sound effect for when you roll {{A|Juggernaut}}. **The {{A|Juggernaut's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Juggernaut.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Juggernaut's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Juggernaut Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version History (ToS)|2.5.1.10655]] **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was Attacked" feedback. *[[Version History (ToS)|2.0.0.6582]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Джаггернаут|ru:Джаггернау]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:Unstoppable Attack]] [[Category:Rampage]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE: {{Amne|Pestilence, Horseman of the Apocalypse}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{RoleSpecificNotice|bgcolor=lightgreen|bordercolor=green|thickness=2px|text='''Please note:''' You cannot roll {{A|Pestilence}} from the role wheel. The only way to get it is by rolling {{A|Plaguebearer}} and infecting everyone.}} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Pestilence}}[[File:RoleIcon PlagueBearer 2.png|thumb|100px|left]]
(Pest) |alignment = {{A|Neutral Chaos}} |avatar=[[File:Plaguebearer_Avatar.png|150px]] |summary = You are a horseman of the apocalypse who feeds off of disease. |abilities = You may choose to Rampage at a player's house each night. |investigator ='''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be an {{InvResCVN10}}. |consigliere = Your target reeks of disease. They must be {{A|Pestilence, Horseman of the Apocalypse}}. |special = [[Unique Role]] |attributestext = You will attack anyone who visits you or your target.
You cannot be role blocked or {{A|Controlled}}.
If you are jailed you will attack the {{A|Jailor}}. |attributes = {{A|Attack}}: Powerful

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story|Plaguebearer}} ==Mechanics== *You may choose to rampage at a target's house each {{A|Night}}. You will automatically attack anyone who visits you. You are equipped with a {{A|Powerful Attack}} and an {{A|Invincible Defense}}. *Your {{A|Invincible Defense}} means you can not be killed at {{A|Night}} '''at all'''. You will bypass even the highest of attacks, such as an {{A|Arsonist}} ignition, an assault by a fully-powered up {{A|Juggernaut}}, a {{A|Jailor}} execution, a final {{A|Hex}}, a {{A|Jester}} haunt, and even dying from a broken heart (in [[Lovers Mode]]). *You are immune to any role-blocks and controls, cannot be caught by a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}} without you killing them, and you'll also be seen as innocent to a {{A|Sheriff}}. Additionally, if you are jailed, you will automatically attack the {{A|Jailor}} even if they try to execute you. *Since you only deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}}, anyone protected by any form of protection, such as from a {{A|Town Protective}}, {{A|Guardian Angel}}, or {{A|Potion Master}} will survive, though the protector (except for the {{A|Guardian Angel}}) will die if they aren't also being protected by another protective role. *The only way you can die is through being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] during the {{A|day}}, so if the whole {{A|Town}} is against you (or any other [[faction]] that has the voting majority), you will most likely die. Utilize the support of any roles that do not oppose you (i.e. {{A|Survivors}}) to keep yourself from being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. *You will still automatically attack anyone who visits you when dead. ==Strategy== *Your main threat is whichever faction is closest to the majority - usually the {{A|Town}}, but often the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, and {{A|Vampires}} during the late game. {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles (i. e. {{A|Arsonists}}) are rarely as much of a threat, since they are generally loners and cannot harm you. *Since the {{A|Town}} starts with a large majority, it's important to wear them down. It can be helpful to you if you are still a {{A|Plaguebearer}} to narrow down the numbers so that you become {{A|Pestilence}} much sooner. Upon transforming, you should still consider keeping other {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles alive to direct suspicion, let them do extra kills (since they can't kill you), and overall a better chance of winning. *However, if you are still a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, those {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles suddenly do pose a big threat to you. The {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Arsonist}}, and {{A|Juggernaut}} can easily kill you. Although the {{A|Serial Killer}} can't harm you physically, they can easily expose you for being immune to their attack. So while you can't kill as {{A|Plaguebearer}} yet, you might want to hang these roles early on to avoid getting called out or killed. **The {{A|Arsonist}} may be an exception, as by the time they ignite, you will most likely already be {{A|Pestilence}}. *Confirmed {{A|Town}} are particularly dangerous; their existence makes it easier for people to find you by process of elimination. *{{A|Vampires}}, when present, are a huge threat because their numbers are not obvious; they may be able to find you by process of elimination before you're even aware they're close. Worse, if they try to convert you the remaining {{A|Vampires}} will get a hint to your identity from the death. Fortunately, targeting most {{A|Town}} also weakens {{A|Vampires}} by denying them possible conversions. *{{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} are massive threats because they know their own members, letting them narrow down your identity. Given the huge threat you pose, it is not uncommon for {{A|Town}}, {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}}, and even {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles to end up in an informal truce, halting all visits, claiming their true role, ceasing to kill anyone else and turning on and hunting you. Don't rely on them to take each other out (or even to visit each other at all) once you have become {{A|Pestilence}}. *Keep in mind that even though you have an invincible defense, you only have a powerful attack, meaning that {{A|Town Protectives}} can still prevent you from killing protected players. Because of your rampage ability, you will kill them if they protect your target, but your original target will live (just like with the {{A|Werewolf}}). Unlike all other killing roles, you don't have to worry about {{A|Bodyguards}} since they can't kill you and will die if they protect your target, making them just a worse {{A|Doctor}} ({{A|Bodyguards}} only protect against one ''direct'' attacker). *The main role that opposes you is the {{A|Mayor}}; if you end up in a 1v1 with them they can put you up on the stand and [[Hanging (ToS)|hang]] you. Luckily, once you become {{A|Pestilence}} all the {{A|Town}} can do is delay their death. If a {{A|Mayor}} reveals, use paranoia to your favor to trick them into [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]] the {{A|Town Protectives}}, and then go for the {{A|Mayor}} themselves since there is no {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}} to protect them. Beware of {{A|Trappers}}, as they can buy the {{A|Mayor}} an extra {{A|day}} to find you even if they die. *However, since your attacks are '''NOT''' unstoppable, the {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Crusader}} combination is a relatively dangerous threat to you as the powerful defense they give each other renders them immune to all of your attacks. This applies for {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Crusader}}/{{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Doctor}} and (in extremely rare cases) {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Potion Master}} combinations. *While you can bait people into visiting you the same way a {{A|Veteran}} does, this carries a lot of risks. First, if too many people have you as their last target in their {{A|Last Will}}, the {{A|Town}} will likely realize you're {{A|Pestilence}}; secondly, knowing that {{A|Pestilence}} is present, the Town will likely view any attempt at baiting as suspicious. **However, most players will also not visit at all as soon as you evolve, unless they have an {{A|Astral}} visit, so this strategy may not work. *For the {{A|Plaguebearer}} role, {{A|Werewolf}} strategies can be commonly used, potentially even more so than {{A|Pestilence}} due to {{A|Pestilence's}} higher capacity of destruction. *When you become {{A|Pestilence}}, the entire {{A|Town}} will receive a message about your evolution, so they will most likely prioritize finding and [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]] you, as you cannot be eliminated any other way. *The message the {{A|Town}} receives is "A plague has consumed the {{A|Town}} summoning {{A|Pestilence Horseman of the Apocalypse}}!" *You can use this to your advantage by accusing people of being {{A|Pestilence}} for one reason or another, and the {{A|Town}} will probably believe you and [[Hanging (ToS)|hang]] that person, wasting a {{A|Day}} and buying yourself another {{A|Night}}. *However, back it up with fake proof and claims. Sometimes, it's also preferable to not accuse anyone and just go with the flow, as more experienced players may catch on. You also have to be careful that the information is accurate, and that you don't make yourself look suspicious in the meantime. Do try and act like a panicking {{A|Town}} member, but not to the point where you are obviously trying to mislead the rest of the {{A|Town}}. *Another option is to claim to be a {{A|Town Investigative}} role that found someone that might be {{A|Pestilence}}. This method gives your lead credibility but will put you under suspicion when the {{A|Town}} realizes you were wrong. To avoid this, remember to claim that you investigated the person you are going after '''BEFORE''' they "became" {{A|Pestilence}}. *{{A|Pestilence}} kills anyone who visits them, so claiming otherwise will make it obvious that you are lying and it might even get you [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. However, this may work as a {{A|Jester}} strategy or for a fake {{A|Jester}} claim. *Try to make suggestions during the {{A|day}} that could "help" to find {{A|Pestilence}}, but don't be too talkative. This way, you do not look suspicious during the {{A|day}}, and you can go on with your nightly killings as an unstoppable force. *One strategy you can use as {{A|Pestilence}}, or basically any other evil role, is to act as a {{A|Jester}}. The only way to be killed as {{A|Pestilence}} is to be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] (of course, except for leaving), and people want to refrain from [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]] {{A|Jesters}}. As of {{VH|version 2.3.0}}, {{A|Jesters}} can now haunt voters who abstain too, so it may be effective to keep acting like a {{A|Jester}} if you get on trial. Refer the {{A|Jester}} page for strategies regarding this. However, {{A|Town}} may be desperate too desperate in trying and find the {{A|Pestilence}}, and the {{A|Jester}} play might backfire, if the {{A|Town}} decides to take the chance and attempt to [[Hanging (ToS)|hang]] you if they feel they do not need you, or if they want to give you the win. In the latter's scenario, either try and delay your death, convince the {{A|Town}} that you're a waste of time to [[Hanging (ToS)|hang]], or accept your mistake and die. *If you don't know who to kill at {{A|Night}}, just look back on the {{A|Night}} you {{A|infected}} the most people with the plague, and go kill that player, as people could still be visiting them and you could take out a huge chunk of the {{A|Town}}. This strategy also works for the {{A|Werewolf}}. *As {{A|Pestilence}}, there is no point trying to be undercover with your kills other than when using the stay at home {{A|Werewolf}} strategy. Any {{A|Lookouts}} or {{A|Trackers}} who catch you are going to die (without a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Crusader}}), so your only threat is a {{A|Medium}}. Even then, {{A|Medium}} claims are rarely believed, so they might be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] under suspicion of being the {{A|Pestilence}}. *Start the game out strong, and as a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, try and get confirmed as a {{A|Town}} member as soon as you can. This can be done in a variety of ways, and since you can see who visited your target, {{A|Lookout}} could be a viable option. **Trying to get yourself confirmed as {{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Tracker}}, or {{A|Sheriff}} is a good idea as the {{A|Investigator}} will most likely not investigate you. However, you are considered a threat to the {{A|Mafia}} or any other evildoers so asking for a {{A|Town Protective}} when "confirmed" as a {{A|Town Investigative}} is a good idea as they will most likely attack you, finding out you are immune, blowing your cover. {{A|Executioner}} is another great claim as it gives you the immunity defense as well. *Don't kill any roles that are harmless to you, such as {{A|Survivor}}, {{A|Jester}}, {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Amnesiac}}, unless the {{A|Amnesiac}} wants to join an opposing faction. However, if these roles show signs of wanting to vote against you, do not hesitate to kill, but make sure they aren't the only ones against you. Otherwise, you could be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. *Killing {{A|Amnesiacs}} is less risky than killing the other neutral roles, as they have to remember to win and you are a one man faction. However, if you kill the {{A|Amnesiac}}, they can't carry on your win if you are [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]], so you have to be certain that you have control over the votes. *Gaining the support of roles such as {{A|Survivor}} is a big help for you, especially later in the game. They can give you extra votes, which can keep you from being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. *Remember, you can still be [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]] whenever. Claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}} or a {{A|Tracker}} is a bad claim if the {{A|Town}} is notified of you being summoned due to these roles sharing investigative results. *Since you can only die by being [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]], the {{A|Mayor}} is a serious threat to you and should generally be dealt with quickly. *The {{A|Necromancer}} and a {{A|Retributionist}} are two of the few roles that can effectively oppose you; they can use {{A|Doctor}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, and {{A|Crusader}} corpses to safely block your attacks, and can send different zombies to visit people in order to identify you (since they see how their zombies die.) Additionally, since they only visit the graveyard, their visits won't expose them to your rampage. So you should prioritize attacking {{A|Necromancers}} and {{A|Retributionists}} whenever possible. *Even though you can survive a {{A|Jailor's}} attack, you still should do what you can to not get 'executed' when in {{A|Jail}}, since a smart {{A|Jailor}} will most certainly put in their will that they attempted to execute you. ==Dealing with the {{A|Pestilence}}== *If you have identified a likely {{A|Plaguebearer}} before they transformed, finding the {{A|Pestilence}} is easy. Otherwise, while {{A|Pestilence's}} ability to kill anyone who visits him is extremely powerful, it is also his sole weakness. Carefully read the wills of anyone who died to {{A|Pestilence}}, and try to figure out who he targeted. From this, you can deduce if anyone targeted them (and died as a result). *Additionally, once {{A|Pestilence}} has transformed, any player who was visited after the announcement and who didn't immediately die cannot be {{A|Pestilence}}. This can be used to rapidly narrow down the list of possible culprits. *As a {{A|Doctor}}, try to find another {{A|Doctor}} or even a {{A|Crusader}} to pair up with them. Since {{A|Pestilence}} only deals {{A|Powerful Attacks}}, paring up with them will give you the defense needed to withstand {{A|Pestilence}}. The {{A|Doctor}}/{{A|Bodyguard}} pair, however, are not as effective since {{A|Pestilence}} can just simply attack the {{A|Bodyguard}} and kill the {{A|Doctor}} with their rampaging ability. *{{A|Pestilence}} kills both anyone who visits his target and anyone who visits himself. As a result, it is usually best to avoid unnecessary visits while {{A|Pestilence}} is active, especially if you are a member of the {{A|Mafia}} and there are few people left. ({{A|Arsonists}}, {{A|Town Protectives}}, {{A|Hex Master}} (especially with {{A|Necronomicon}}), {{A|Retributionist}} and {{A|Necromancer}} may be exceptions). *If you are a {{A|Jailor}}, in your will write "Kill" or "Execute" next to the names you execute. This way, if you die from jailing {{A|Pestilence}}, the {{A|Town}} will easily know who the {{A|Pestilence}} is. *Because {{A|Pestilence}} can only be killed by [[Hanging (ToS)|hanging]], it's usually best for killing roles to cease killing as long as {{A|Pestilence}} is active; an active {{A|Pestilence}} can reduce the population of the town extremely fast, and killing anyone (even dangerous enemies) may leave you without the votes to [[Hanging (ToS)|hang]] them. Additionally, visiting to kill while {{A|Pestilence}} is active risks exposing you to both their rampage attack and death by visiting them. *In {{A|Lovers Mode}}, {{A|Pestilence}} will not die when their lover dies. Knowing this, you can carefully look at who claimed who was their lover, and deduce if they died along with their lover or not. The {{A|Juggernaut}} will still die, because its defense cannot withstand the {{A|Pestilence}}. *There used to be a bug where the {{A|Juggernaut}} was able to kill {{A|Pestilence}} if they stayed at home. [[File:RoleIcon TownWins.png|thumb]]The {{A|Townies}} are the "good" side of [[Town of Salem]]. Their aim is to "hang every criminal and evildoer," referring to the rival factions that may harm the {{A|Town}}. These include: the {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Neutral Killing}}, {{A|Neutral Chaos}} (excluding {{A|Pirate}}), and the {{A|Witch}}, who cannot win with the {{A|Town}}. To that end, each innocent {{A|Town}} member contributes with varied abilities according to their roles and sub-alignments, which are categorized into {{A|Town Investigative}}, {{A|Town Killing}}, {{A|Town Protective}}, and {{A|Town Support}}. These sub-alignments can help the {{A|Town}} to be led to victory when working together to combine all their abilities.

Compared to the other factions, the {{A|Town's}} primary method of elimination is by hanging their opponents in trials (due to their relative size in membership), keeping the majority of votes and power in numbers, as well as the abundance of intelligence gathering roles. Using the correct information and the {{A|Townies}}' majority, the evildoers will be hanged after voting.

This doesn't mean the {{A|Townies}} lack the ability to directly kill their enemies, nor does it mean they are sitting ducks waiting to be killed should the hanging not go as smoothly as planned. The {{A|Town Killing}} and {{A|Town Protective}} roles are there precisely for this reason. But these roles most of the time can't reliably win the game for their fellow {{A|Townies}}, so active and accurate hangings are still very much desired and necessary to win games.

It is thus crucial for the {{A|Townies}} to accurately parse the truths from the lies, which their enemies will no doubt spread. It is also important for them to act and not be passive at trials before they lose their voting power to the evil-doers; as innocent {{A|Townies}} die almost every {{A|Night}}, their doom draws ever nearer.

==Strategies==
*'''{{A|Town Protective}}'''
** Try to protect the most useful players (eg, {{A|Sheriff}}, {{A|Investigator}}, {{A|Jailor}}) once you know who the {{A|Townies}} are. This is helpful as a [[Strategies|Late Game Strategy]].
** A combination of {{A|Doctors}} and {{A|Crusaders}} are nearly unstoppable to bypass as their {{A|Powerful Defense}} each role gives prevents any killing. A {{A|Doctor}}-{{A|Bodyguard}} works similarly, but the {{A|Bodyguard}} can only protect from one single direct attack. Any attacks made by the {{A|Rampage}} ability or an {{A|Ambusher}} cannot be countered.
***In addition, all of these combinations can be stopped by any role-blocking role, a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, and any role with an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}.
*'''{{A|Town Investigative}}:'''
**'''Always have evidence''' if you want someone hanged. Otherwise, you will sound like an {{A|Executioner}}.
** If possible, team up with a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}}; You can secretly find a {{A|Mafia}} member or {{A|Neutral Evil}} role, then tell your ally to kill them in a whisper without needing to reveal yourself to the {{A|Town}} (Mind the {{A|Blackmailer}}, though).
** If you have any information at all, '''DO NOT''' leave the game once you are dead as there could still be a {{A|Medium}} . If you are dead and a {{A|Medium}} is alive, they could talk to you at {{A|Night}} and you could share your info with them. They could either write the info down in their {{A|Last Will}} or tell the {{A|Town}} about it the next {{A|day}} if they survive (Just in case you die, you should always put important information in your {{A|Last Will}} as soon as you receive it). Also, even if the {{A|Medium}} is dead, The {{A|Town}} could still be provided with info. If the {{A|Medium}} hasn't used their Seance, then they could still share the info that they have received from you with a trustworthy player via the Seance. If there is no {{A|Medium}} at all, you should still be sure to ALWAYS share the info that you have with the dead players in the chat.
* '''{{A|Town Killing}}'''
** It is not recommended to random shoot as {{A|Vigilante}} unless other evil factions are quickly gaining a majority or it you have a strong suspicion a certain player is evil. Sometimes, if you have a small reason to shoot someone for any reason at all, such as their behavior, you should make sure the risk is worth it first. Even then, be careful, as if you shoot s {{A|Townie}}, you die from guilt. It's not technically [[gamethrowing]] to do so, yet it is heavily frowned upon.
** {{A|Veteran}} should save alerts and draw attention away from themselves until the situation is right. You can become a powerful role if you have 3 or 2 alerts left late in the game. Of course, this does come with the risk of the {{A|Mafia}} randomly attacking you early on. It can be a good strategy to ask for {{A|Town Protectives}} and/or {{A|Lookouts}} on you so you can save your alerts, but this can lead to {{A|Town}} thinking of you as suspicious when you claim {{A|Veteran}}.
** Since {{A|Veteran}} and {{A|Vigilante}} are in this alignment, you can take advantage of this to become more powerful.
***As {{A|Vigilante}}, you can claim {{A|Veteran}} to make {{A|Mafia}} not visit you. The downside of this is if a real {{A|Veteran}} sees your claim, they may think that you're evil and reveal to get you hanged.
***As {{A|Veteran}}, claim {{A|Vigilante}} and that you are thinking about shooting an evil role. {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} may attack you to stop you from killing, and a {{A|Witch}} will attempt to control you into shooting someone. However, some {{A|Town Protectives}} or {{A|Lookouts}} might want to protect/watch you.
***If a {{A|Vigilante}} shoots {{A|Night}} one, they were controlled by a {{A|Witch}} or a {{A|Coven Leader}}.
** {{A|Vampires}} don't confirm that a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} exists, but a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} confirms that {{A|Vampires}} exist.
* '''In General:'''
** If you think someone is evil, don't vote innocent unless there is proof that they are not.
** Try to stay on topic--unless there is no evidence--especially if everyone else is roleplaying. [[Town of Salem]] is not a chatroom, despite how fun roleplaying is. Many evil roles try to sway the topic discussed in chat to distract {{A|Townies}} and ensure their win. Also, by staying on topic, you may catch mistakes that evil people may say in chat that other people may not notice.
** If there is a {{A|Mayor}}, tell them information in chat. This will allow them to lead the {{A|Town}} to possibly hang an evil role.
** Properly prioritizing enemies is essential to victory:
*** The {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} and {{A|Vampires}} are the highest priority throughout the game, as they have the ability to collectively sway the {{A|Town's}} vote through deception and numbers.
*** Early on in the game, {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles and the {{A|Plaguebearer}} are of lower priority as they can harm the {{A|Mafia}} as well as the {{A|Town}}.
*** {{A|Witches}} generally hold a high priority, as they can cause {{A|Townies}} to die by {{A|Town Killing}}, prevent evil roles from getting killed or caught at {{A|Night}}, and free a  role blocked {{A|Mafia Killing}} role.
*** {{A|Survivors}} generally holds a low priority during the {{A|day}} and is usually best hanged if more threatening targets are unknown. 
*** Late in the game, {{A|Neutral Killing}} may be manipulated as a check to the remaining {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}, or you may be able to trick an {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Plaguebearer}} to help vote up the last {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} if the said killer is unable to kill the next {{A|Night}}. An attentive {{A|Mayor}} can outright exploit this limitation to ensure a {{A|Town}} victory.
*** While most {{A|Neutral Evil}} roles do not need to be killed in order for {{A|Town}} to win, it is often best to do so due to their freedom; they could be an extra vote against the {{A|Town}}, as the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} would be more willing to help the {{A|Neutral Evil}} win. Usually, the only reason to keep them alive is when the {{A|Town}} desperately needs one more vote, and they think they can trust that {{A|Neutral Evil}}.
** Late in the game, if you are the only {{A|Town}} member left and the two killers remaining can both kill each other, try to avoid choosing winners and hope they do just that. Roles capable of killing each other include:
***{{A|Medusa}} and any non-{{A|Coven}} role, excluding {{A|Pestilence}}.
*** {{A|Arsonist}} and {{A|Werewolf}}, although {{A|Juggernaut}} may also substitute for either.
*** {{A|Mafioso}} and any member of the {{A|Coven}}, excluding the {{A|Coven Leader}}.
*** A {{A|Vampire}} and any member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} lacking defense. Bear in mind, however, that the {{A|Vampire}} is highly likely to simply bite you, as doing so is in line with their win condition.
** While you may be ordered around by {{A|Mayor}}, {{A|Jailor}}, or some other confirmed {{A|Town}}, don't let yourself be blindly led to hanging someone you feel is pretty innocent.
* While it's good to avoid hanging blindly, don't become too fixated on requiring 'perfect' information; there are times when it's necessary for the {{A|Town}} to take a risk and hang someone simply for being suspicious or for being unconfirmed late in the game.
**Pay attention to the number of {{A|Town}} versus evils remaining. Late in the game, if the evils are likely to have a majority the next {{A|day}}, you ''must'' hang someone, even if it's just a glorified hunch with a low chance of hanging the right person. Hanging semi-blindly has risks, yes, but being too passive means the {{A|Town}} will ''definitely'' lose. It is better to have a chance of winning than a certain loss.
** Similarly, when you have a large number of confirmed town, hanging people who cannot or will not confirm themselves becomes an increasingly effective strategy.
*If someone posts their {{A|Last Will}} and you find something off about it (e.g. no name, spaces between "N1" and "[Name]", they already wrote a {{A|Night's}} results before said {{A|Night}}), it is almost certain that they have just written their {{A|Last Will}} and are lying. This tactic can also be applied to a lot of numbers written in the {{A|Last Will}}. This isn't always the case, so be sure to be cautious while using these methods.
