Mafia.title: Mafia
Mafia.wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Mafia}}}}[[File:RoleIcon_Godfather.png|thumb|right]]The {{A|Mafia}} are a [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] of evildoers that serve as the primary enemy of the {{A|Town}}. All members have one common goal: to kill anyone that will not submit to the {{A|Mafia}}. Unlike the {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Mafia}} know who each other are from the beginning of the game. Every {{A|Mafia}} member has a unique function and unique attributes, much like the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Coven}}. However, there are a few major differences in numbers, since the {{A|Town}} primarily has multiple members at a time, while the {{A|Mafia}} can only have up to 4 members, similar to the {{A|Coven}}. Unlike the {{A|Coven}} however, the {{A|Mafia}} can pose themselves as another normal {{A|Townie}} much easier. Their main intention is to eliminate every [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] opposed to them, such as the {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Vampires}}, most {{A|Neutrals}}, and the {{A|Town}}. Despite the overall advantage in numbers within the {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Mafia's}} ability to consistently kill and intercept them can quickly back them into a corner, diminish their numbers, and by redirecting or concealing information; use their own noose against them, murdering and hanging each {{A|Townie}} one-by-one, until they have the primary majority over everyone else, including the vote to hang.

Unsurprisingly, many {{A|Townies}} will try to stand in their way. A suspicious {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} can lead to their demise on the stand, and the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}} won't hesitate to take them out with their ability to kill for the {{A|Town}}. Thus, the {{A|Mafia}} must kill off the {{A|Townies}} in the {{A|Night}}, while using their deception abilities to try and trick the {{A|Town}} during the {{A|Day}}. They must also be aware at all times, as the {{A|Town}} may outsmart them and reveal important information at any time, and end the {{A|Mafia}} in {{A|Days}} .

==Strategy==
===General strategy===
*You could put your name and role in your {{A|Last Will}}, along with other {{A|Mafia}} roles with names of people who aren't members of the {{A|Mafia}}. If you die, the {{A|Town}} might think you're throwing the game and hang someone who's innocent, helping the {{A|Mafia}} win. This strategy only works against extremely inexperienced players, so [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Classic_Mode|Classic Mode]] is recommended for this play to work.
**You may be reported for game-throwing, but it isn't as long as the names that are in your will are not {{A|Mafia}}.
**It is useful to talk a lot during the {{A|Day}} because usually members of the {{A|Mafia}} are very quiet. If you talk frequently, you draw attention, and people who draw attention have 'nothing to hide'. 
*It is good to make up a role '''in advance''' in case you are asked or jailed:
**'''{{A|Jailor}}''': Try to be as convincing as possible: Depending on your performance, the {{A|Jailor}} might execute you on the spot. Also, the {{A|Jailor}} will typically execute {{A|Neutral}} roles, so acting like a {{A|Jester}} is a bad idea. 
**'''{{A|Spy}}''': If there's no {{A|Disguiser}} and if you are able to, scramble your {{A|Last Will}} so the {{A|Spy}} won't catch you visiting the same people as the {{A|Mafia}} every {{A|Night}} so easily. You can also throw in other people who fit with your claim. For example, if you're a {{A|Blackmailer}}, put down somebody who didn't talk on a {{A|Day}}. If you're a {{A|Bootlegger}}, replace one of your targets with somebody else who claimed to be [[roleblocked]], or act like you [[roleblocked]] a fellow {{A|Mafia}} member.
**'''{{A|Investigator}}''': The role you claim must match the investigation if the Investigator has already proven their role. So for example, as a {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Ambusher}}, claim to be a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Veteran}}. {{A|Veteran}} is a better claim because if the {{A|Town}} believes you are a {{A|Vigilante}}, they may ask you to shoot known members of the {{A|Mafia}} (but, beware! The {{A|Veteran}} is a [[Unique Role]], so if you claim it, you will be called out if a real {{A|Veteran}} exists). As a {{A|Bootlegger}}, claim to be an {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Transporter}}. A {{A|Consigliere}} should pick {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Tracker}}, a {{A|Blackmailer}} should claim to be a {{A|Spy}} or {{A|Guardian Angel}} (Remember to say who your target is). A {{A|Hypnotist}} should claim to be a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, a {{A|Forger}} should claim to be a {{A|Lookout}}, and a {{A|Janitor}} should claim to be a {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Trapper}}. {{A|Framers}}, {{A|Disguisers}}, and the {{A|Godfather}} are less obvious cases. Since the {{A|Framer's}} ability is to make other people appear as {{A|Framer}}/{{A|Vampire}}/{{A|Jester}}/{{A|Hex Master}}, you can claim anything (This can also work if a {{A|Hex Master}} has been confirmed to be in the town). A {{A|Disguiser}} (or {{A|Disguised}} {{A|Mafia}}) can claim to be a {{A|Doctor}} or any other role depending on what they come up as, since that hints the second target's role. However, claiming {{A|Doctor}} itself can get you executed by a {{A|Jailor}} or hanged for suspect of being a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Potion Master}}. The {{A|Godfather}} is mixed, they can either claim a role and say they have been {{A|doused}} by an {{A|Arsonist}}, or they can claim to be a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}}, although these claims generally don't work.
**'''{{A|Lookout}}''': They will know you are able to visit if they watch you visit someone. In most cases, you can refer to the strategy for {{A|Investigators}}. As a {{A|Consigliere}}, {{A|Disguiser}} or {{A|Framer}}, you should definitely claim a [[Night Ability|visiting]] role which is not noticeable (e.g. targets will know if they are [[roleblocked]] and/or [[blackmailed]], but not if they were investigated).
**'''{{A|Sheriff}}''': If you get found as suspicious; claim you might be framed, say you were transported or accuse the {{A|Sheriff}} of being an {{A|Executioner}}.
**'''{{A|Tracker}}''': If you suspect that you are being tracked as a {{A|Mafioso}}, simply don't act for that {{A|Night}}. They will see that you visited nobody, and will hopefully think you are innocent.
**'''{{A|Psychic}}''': If you are accused of coming up in an evil vision, claim a {{A|Town}} role and try to shift suspicion onto another person from the vision. Try to role block  on an odd-numbered {{A|Night}} to reduce the risk of appearing twice in another vision (or blackmail them every {{A|Night}}). If you come up twice, however, say they are an {{A|Executioner}} or a fake {{A|Psychic}} as there aren't many ways to get out of this situation.
*Work to identify your allies.
**'''{{A|Executioners}}''' want to hang a {{A|Townie}}, so it makes sense to support them; be careful about what you claim, since unlike them, you usually have to maintain plausibility even after their target is hanged and revealed as a {{A|Townie}}. If you do claim a {{A|Town Investigative}} role to support them, sometimes claiming to be a second {{A|Executioner}} with the same target after your lies are revealed can be helpful. You can identify {{A|Executioners}} by looking for people who seem to focus on accusing one target, ''especially'' if they accuse a non-member of the {{A|Mafia}} of being a member of the {{A|Mafia}}; however, be careful, since your {{A|Night}}-immune rivals like the {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, and {{A|Arsonist}} may sometimes pose as an {{A|Executioner}} to deflect attention. It's a good idea to try and get them hanged after they've hung their "target" or investigate them at {{A|Night}}, just in case.
**'''{{A|Jesters}}''' want to be hanged, which wastes the {{A|Town's}} time and (assuming all the {{A|Mafia}} votes innocent for them) can kill a {{A|Townie}}, {{A|Coven}} or a possible {{A|Neutral}} role. You can identify {{A|Jesters}} by looking for people who make claims you know to be false, such as claiming they were attacked on a {{A|Night}} you were [[roleblocked]]. It's best not to kill {{A|Jesters}}; they can distract the {{A|Town}}, {{A|Neutral Killing}}, and other evil rivals.
**'''{{A|Witches}}''' win with you, but can be very dangerous if they're targeting blindly; making contact with them is very important. {{A|Witches}} often claim to be a {{A|Lookout}}; other evil roles often do as well, but either way, it's a waste of time to attack them unless they are really a {{A|Lookout}}. You don't usually need to tell witches you are mafia, but by not telling the town you were witched, they may be more likely to help you later. Additionally, since {{A|Witches}} win with all evil roles and need to last to the end, it can sometimes be worth just calling on {{A|Witches}} to identify themselves if doing so will result in you having a majority.
**'''{{A|Survivors}}''' want to survive, if you identify them, you may try to whisper and convince them that the {{A|Mafia}} has a better chance of winning than the {{A|Town}}. In return, you can promise them the {{A|Mafia}} won't attack said {{A|Survivor}}. In the best case, the {{A|Survivor}} will help you hang the {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Coven}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles in the late game, resulting in you having a majority.
**'''{{A|Amnesiacs}}''' want to remember a role. {{A|Amnesiacs}} are always a double-edged sword; they can be an enemy or an ally to the {{A|Mafia}}. If you know who they are, keep them alive for the time being. If they remember themselves as a dead {{A|Mafia}} member, {{A|Pirate}}, {{A|Neutral Benign}}, or {{A|Neutral Evil}}, they can become a quick ally. If they become a {{A|Townie}} or {{A|Coven}}, you can take them out swiftly. Worst case scenario is if they become a {{A|Neutral Killing}} or {{A|Plaguebearer}}, but by then your team can work a claim against them to get them hanged.
**'''{{A|Guardian Angels}}''': The {{A|Guardian Angel}} seeks to ensure that their target survives until the end of the game. If the {{A|Guardian Angel}} has one of the {{A|Mafia}} as their target, then you can whisper them to strike a deal. The {{A|Mafia}} will leave them alone or even defend them if they are accused, and in return, the {{A|Guardian Angel}} works with you and helps to defend their target, who is one of your teammates. This also works if the {{A|Guardian Angel}} has any {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Neutral Evil}} roles or a {{A|Pirate}} as their target, although it does depend on whether the neutral target of the {{A|Guardian Angel}} is willing to side with the {{A|Mafia}}. However, If the {{A|Guardian Angel}} has a {{A|Town}} member, {{A|Coven}} member or a member of the {{A|Vampires}} as their target, you should eliminate them, as they are defending one of your enemies.
**'''{{A|Pirates}}''': The {{A|Pirate}} seeks to plunder two players. If you can identify who the {{A|Pirate}} is, you can whisper them, asking them not to plunder any of the {{A|Mafia}}, and in return, the {{A|Mafia}} will not attack them at {{A|Night}}. You could also try to appease the {{A|Pirate}} if they become a Kingmaker. You could use the fact that the {{A|Mafia}} left them alone all game and did not out them or attack them in order to try and get them to vote with you. Also, note that the {{A|Pirate}} may side with another [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] over the {{A|Mafia}}. If they publicly announce that they are helping a [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] other than yours during the {{A|Day}}, try to get them killed as soon as possible, either by murdering them at {{A|Night}} or convincing the {{A|Town}} to hang the {{A|Pirate}} as they can kill {{A|Townies}} and as such must be eliminated.
*Dealing with a {{A|Jailor}}:
**The {{A|Jailor}} is the most powerful {{A|Town}} role, and can single-handedly cost you the game if not dealt with, especially if you lack a {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Mafioso}} combo - in that case, having your killer jailed will result in no {{A|Mafia}} kill the next {{A|Day}}, usually getting them executed or paralyzing the entire {{A|Mafia}}. Therefore it is vital to identify and kill the {{A|Jailor}} as quickly as possible.
**Unless the {{A|Town}} screws up or you have a {{A|Consigliere}}, it may be very difficult to identify the {{A|Jailor}} directly. However, you can identify who is ''not'' the {{A|Jailor}}, and narrow your attacks down to people on that list to increase your chances of killing them.
**Sometimes, a {{A|Jailor}} will reveal {{A|Day}} 1 and ask for {{A|Town Protective}} roles and {{A|Lookouts}} to stay on them. In this case, it is very important to kill off the {{A|Town Protectives}}. {{A|Doctors}} waste you a {{A|Night}} by undoing your kill, the {{A|Trapper}}, {{A|Bodyguard}}, and {{A|Crusader}} can get you killed (as well as preventing the {{A|Jailor's}} death), and a {{A|Lookout}} can out you as the Mafia's primary killing role. A {{A|Blackmailer}} can give you targets to kill/role block to vanquish the {{A|Jailor's}} protections. An {{A|Ambusher}} can assist in killing off the {{A|Town Protectives}}, but can also be easily outed if there's more than 1 visitor. For {{A|Lookouts}}, you can either have a {{A|Disguiser}} disguise you or (provided there's no {{A|Spy}}) claim that a {{A|Disguiser}} disguised the killer as you.
**Keep track of anyone who announces that they were jailed; it's extremely unlikely that the {{A|Jailor}} would lie about this (since whoever they really jailed would either call them out or need to know their identity), so you can usually scratch them off the list of possible {{A|Jailors}}. People who talk to the {{A|Jailor}} during the {{A|Day}} are ''probably'' not the {{A|Jailor}}, either, but a few {{A|Jailors}} might lie this way to deflect evil attention.
**Keep track of other evils, likely {{A|Jesters}} and {{A|Executioners}}, and anyone else who generally don't seem to be helping the {{A|Town}}. They're probably not the {{A|Jailor}}, either.
**Keep track of anyone whose role is known, either via {{A|Consigliere}} or some other source. Before attacking a known non-{{A|Jailor}} {{A|Townie }}, consider whether it's more important to kill them or to find the {{A|Jailor}} - you might be better off focusing on unknown people instead.
**The {{A|Consigliere}} should also follow these instructions to increase their chances of identifying the {{A|Jailor}} as quickly as possible.
**It's generally a bad idea to press the {{A|Jailor}} for their identity when jailed. Even if you've convinced them you're a {{A|Town Protective}}, {{A|Jailors}} will find it suspicious - and even if they ''do'' tell you their role, if you've claimed {{A|Town Protective}}, killing them will out that as a lie when their will pops up. You may, however, be able to tell them to signal you when they trust you with some secret code word or phrase, like "shrimp".
*Dealing with Evil Rivals.
**'''{{A|Serial Killer}}''': As the {{A|Serial Killer}} is an "every-{{A|Night}}" killer, it makes it easier to play as. If you find the {{A|Serial Killer}} early-on in a match, keep them alive for a bit, as your common enemy is the {{A|Town}}. If they start killing {{A|Mafia}}, it is late game, or you are in a struggle, it's best to out them, or, in serious situations, try getting them to attack your {{A|Godfather}} (who has Basic Defense) if one is available. Claiming {{A|Sheriff}} and finding them as suspicious is also a good claim.
**'''{{A|Arsonist}}''': {{A|Arsonists}} have the power of dousing undetected, which can move onto your {{A|Mafia}} team. If you have a {{A|Godfather}}, he is useless against the {{A|Arsonist}} by himself. If you manage to find the {{A|Arsonist}}, it's best to out them as soon as possible or even better have a {{A|Bootlegger}} [[roleblock]] them, since some of your {{A|Mafia}} friends or you may be {{A|doused}}.
**'''{{A|Werewolf}}''': Dealing with a {{A|Werewolf}} can be a large struggle since it kills all its visitors, which can include your fellow members of the {{A|Mafia}}. If you find them through ways of their Defense value being higher than the {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Godfather's}} Attack value or a {{A|Consigliere}}, it's best to out them as soon as possible, especially during late game. You can also claim you are {{A|Sheriff}} and say they are suspicious during {{A|Full Moon}}.
**'''{{A|Vampire}}''': Depending on the [[Game Modes (ToS)|Game Mode]], {{A|Vampires}} can be either a large, common threat or a small threat capable of being brought down. {{A|Vampires}} can be a problem, however, due to the fact they can spread undetected and kill all your {{A|Mafia}} members besides the {{A|Godfather}}. Finding {{A|Vampires}} and killing them can improve your team's survival. If there is a known {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, without killing them or revealing your identity, you should try teaming up with them to kill any possible {{A|Vampires}}. {{A|Vampires}} can also be used to distract the {{A|Town}} or trick them into hanging confirmed {{A|Townies}} if there is suspicion they have been converted.
**'''{{A|Coven}}''': The {{A|Coven}} will be your major contenders in the battle for supremacy over the {{A|Town}}. The best strategy for the {{A|Mafia}} is to remove them as quickly as possible after identifying them, but you may try to let someone else kill (or just simply hang) the {{A|Medusa}} as she will turn your fellow members or you into stone. However, if you have a {{A|Bootlegger}}, you can [[roleblock]] the {{A|Medusa}}, and the {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Godfather}} can easily kill her. If the {{A|Consigliere}} found a member of the {{A|Coven}} (except the {{A|Hex Master}} who might have hexed other roles), it's better for the {{A|Mafia Killing}} to kill them unless the {{A|Coven Leader}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}, in which case you need to hang them.
**'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}''': The {{A|Plaguebearer}} is initially not a major concern for the {{A|Mafia}} as they cannot directly kill your teammates, and it will take them a long time to infect everyone. If you discover their identity in the game's early stages, consider leaving them alone whilst you focus on your more powerful rivals at the start, such as the {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Coven}}, and any {{A|Vampires}}. However, if the {{A|Plaguebearer}} goes undetected for a long period of time, you run the risk that he will transform into {{A|Pestilence}}. If {{A|Pestilence}} emerges, and you cannot quickly find out who it is, the {{A|Mafia}} are doomed. Therefore, if you discover the identity of the {{A|Plaguebearer}} in the middle to late game stages, or if you discover the identity of the {{A|Pestilence}}, you should out them immediately as by then they pose a serious threat.
**'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''': The {{A|Juggernaut}} is especially dangerous throughout the game, and only poses more and more of a threat the longer they survive and the more kills they earn. While you cannot kill them directly, a {{A|Bootlegger}} can permanently shut them down at any time and give you time to find a majority to hang them. However, keep in mind no {{A|Juggernaut}} will want to be constantly [[roleblocked]] throughout the game, and the {{A|Town}} can reveal your identities early on if they are not kept in check as well. Sometimes taking the risk for the {{A|Juggernaut}} to kill off enough {{A|Townies}} at the cost of your own {{A|Mafia}} members may be needed in order to hang them and secure your own victory.

===During the {{A|Day}}===
*If one of the members of the {{A|Mafia}} is being hanged and you cannot prevent it, vote guilty to avoid suspicion of being {{A|Mafia}}. This will also allow you to point out anyone who abstained or voted innocent as possible {{A|Mafia}}.
*If you recognize that an {{A|Executioner}} is trying to hang someone, and the hang vote comes, then vote innocent. This will make it seem more like you're a {{A|Townie}}. This has the potential downside of the {{A|Executioner}} siding against you, however. If the other killing roles, like {{A|Serial Killer}}, are dead, and the {{A|Town}} mob votes someone and you are sure they will vote guilty, then vote guilty as well (unless the {{A|Mafia}} vote would override guilty).
*It is important to avoid hanging a known {{A|Serial Killer}} too soon. He can help you double the deaths of {{A|Townies}}, as well as double your chances of killing any dangerous {{A|Townies}}. Try to find out who they are (by noting the people with Defense) but do not reveal it too soon. Towards the end, if many members of the {{A|Mafia}} are alive and you know who the {{A|Serial Killer}} is, you can hang them. Otherwise, if you are confident you can win without them, write down in the {{A|Death Note}} that their Defense value is higher than your Attack value and kill someone else. The {{A|Death Note}} will be visible to the {{A|Town}} and since both the {{A|Town}} and the {{A|Mafia}} want the {{A|Serial Killer}} dead, it is very likely that the {{A|Town}} will vote them up.
**Remember however to play along with the {{A|Town}}. Try to behave the same way most {{A|Townies}} do, so as not to stick out. If for example, many {{A|Town}} members are ignoring a {{A|Last Will}} that says a specific other player is the {{A|Serial Killer}}, try not to draw too much attention while pointing them in that direction. This is especially true with your own {{A|Death Notes}}. If you use the {{A|Death Note}} to reveal sensitive information to the {{A|Town}}, don't start shouting about it the next {{A|Day}} in the chat. It will make the {{A|Townies}} suspect you as the writer of that note.
**It is very important to hang all the {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles especially if there are 4 members of the {{A|Mafia}} because the {{A|Serial Killer}} and {{A|Werewolf}} can be a big threat while the {{A|Arsonist}} might burn the whole {{A|Mafia}}.
*Sometimes, enough members of the {{A|Mafia}} will stay alive that you have the '''majority''', possibly including a {{A|Witch}} or other {{A|Neutral}}. If the {{A|Town}} has no {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Jailor}}, or {{A|Mayor}} left alive, you can easily reveal yourself during the {{A|Day}} and hang the remaining {{A|Townies}} one by one (without wasting time with {{A|Veterans}}, {{A|Town Protective}}, or dangerous {{A|Town Support}} roles).
*One of you pretends to be the {{A|Sheriff}}. If someone is immune to your attack, then say that they are {{A|Neutral Killing}}. If they are, then you will receive trust from the {{A|Town}}, and won't have to worry about getting hanged. Remember that the {{A|Executioner}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Juggernaut}}, {{A|Plaguebearer}}/'''{{A|Pestilence}}''', and {{A|Arsonist}} are also immune. If you think you've identified the {{A|Werewolf}}, you can accuse them after a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, but you have to use the right accusation or the {{A|Town}} may grow suspicious. Another danger here is that whoever you attacked, they'll know they were hit by the {{A|Mafia}}, and will likely say so on the stand, which could get you hung the next {{A|Night}} (or even immediately if the {{A|Town}} cares more about hanging the {{A|Mafia}} than an immune role), which is why having a {{A|Consigliere}} search for them is advisable.
*Try to get the {{A|Jester}} hanged for an extra kill that {{A|Night}}. Just make sure the other members of the {{A|Mafia}} vote innocent.
*Sometimes, you'll find out that hanging your own teammate is the only way out. This happens when an {{A|Tavern Keeper}} (or {{A|Jailor}}) keeps role blocking the only {{A|Mafia Killing}} role that the {{A|Mafia}} has, but the votes are not enough to hang them during the {{A|Day}}. To avoid a draw, you might be forced to contribute to the voting and hanging them. 
Example: Player A, Player B, and Player C are confirmed members of {{A|Mafia}} and the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} has [[Role block|role blocked]] Player A for two days and since then, there were no {{A|Mafia}} kills. Since nobody is getting hanged, and the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} will keep [[Role block|role blocking]] Player A since they are a confirmed {{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Mafioso}}, hang them. This will make one of your teammates get promoted to a {{A|Mafioso}} and the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} will not be sure on who to [[role block]] anymore. This can only buy you some time since the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} could be lucky and [[role block]] the new {{A|Mafioso}}, but sometimes it needs to be done to avoid a stalemate.

*One risky strategy is to pretend to be an {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Jester}} and accuse a fellow member of the {{A|Mafia}}, but with some flaw in your accusation (for instance, claiming to be an {{A|Investigator}} and saying that they came up as {{A|Mafia}}, rather than listing an investigative result that an {{A|Investigator}} would receive). This can accomplish several valuable things; if the {{A|Town}} believes you're an {{A|Executioner}}, they may assume your target is a {{A|Townie}} , whereas if they believe you're a {{A|Jester}}, they may ignore you. Even better, if your target later dies and is revealed as a {{A|Mafia}}, you can use your accusation to say that you're a "confirmed" {{A|Town Investigative}}, which may get some {{A|Townies}} to listen to you despite your 'mistakes' earlier on.
*This is risky, though, since you're calling attention to two members of the {{A|Mafia}} and could get shot by a {{A|Vigilante}}, executed by a {{A|Jailor}}, or hanged by a {{A|Jester}}-unwary {{A|Town}} for making a bad accusation; alternatively, the {{A|Town}} might not notice the flaw in your accusation and hang the accused member of the {{A|Mafia}} anyway.

*If during the {{A|Day}}, you seem ''absolutely certain'' to be hanged, and a {{A|Jailor}} is still alive, consider claiming {{A|Jailor}}. This should only be done when you feel absolutely certain you'll be hanged otherwise since it usually guarantees your execution by the real {{A|Jailor}} the next {{A|Night}}; you can often be caught out if people ask who you jailed. But it has several advantages that can benefit the surviving members of the {{A|Mafia}}:
**{{A|Townies}} often reflexively vote innocent on {{A|Jailor}} claims, giving the real {{A|Jailor}} a chance to deal with them; because {{A|Jailor}} is unique and the real {{A|Jailor}} can execute fake claims in this manner, even transparently false {{A|Jailor}} claims can sometimes make the {{A|Town}} pause due to the sheer rarity of people claiming it falsely. And if the {{A|Town}} ''does'' let the real {{A|Jailor}} handle it, this forces them to waste a {{A|Night}} and an execution dealing with you, which could have otherwise been spent elsewhere. If you have a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Witch}} on your side, they can even make a guess at the real {{A|Jailor}} to save your life.
**If you do survive to the {{A|Night}} and get jailed, tell the {{A|Jailor}} that you are a {{A|Veteran}} trying to bait. Depending on the evidence against you, it may not be sufficient to save your life, but it's the most plausible explanation for why a {{A|Townie}} would falsely claim {{A|Jailor}}.
**Sometimes, the real {{A|Jailor}} might reveal to counter-claim you, exposing them to the {{A|Mafia}}.
**Since the {{A|Jailor}} is such a powerful claim, you can sometimes push to successfully hang your main accuser; this also tends to make it more likely that the real {{A|Jailor}} will speak out, exposing themselves.
**In [[All Any]], the {{A|Jailor}} might not even be present, allowing you to claim them safely; since the claim is still so risky, many {{A|Townies}} will reflexively accept it regardless of the evidence against you.
**Do not do this if you are the sole {{A|Mafia Killing}} role since it will leave the {{A|Mafia}} unable to kill that {{A|Night}}; or if you're the last surviving {{A|Mafia}} member overall, since there won't be anyone to benefit from your sacrifice.

===At {{A|Night}}===

====Choosing a target to kill====
*If someone is being accused of being {{A|Mafia}} and they are not, not killing them will waste the {{A|Town's}} time investigating them at {{A|Night}} or questioning them during the {{A|Day}}. On the other hand, killing them may redirect suspicion to the accuser. Even better, killing their ''accuser'' may increase suspicion on them; however, it risks wasting one of your kills hitting an {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Jester}}.
*If you have someone trying to hang you, don't kill them too soon. It would be too obvious. However, if you wait too long, then you might get hanged because you let that person convince the {{A|Town}} to hang you. Additionally, if they're a genuine {{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Sheriff}}, it might be better for you to simply bite the bullet and kill them as soon as possible even if it gets one of you hung rather than leaving them alive to potentially discover the rest of the {{A|Mafia}}.
*If there is a {{A|Jailor}}, you can sometimes choose not to kill anyone: it will seem like the jailed person is the {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}}. Note that there are other possibilities for this, such as hitting a target with [[Basic Defense]]
*Additionally, a strategy that sometimes works early game is by not killing at all, and having the {{A|Random Mafia}} visit, assuming that there is a {{A|Random Mafia}} at all. If there is a {{A|Spy}}, it would make it look like the person the {{A|Random Mafia}} visited was immune.
*Try killing the person who is least expected to be killed. If someone says, "I'm an {{A|Investigator}}/{{A|Sheriff}}/{{A|Doctor}}/or any {{A|Town}} role in fact", Don't kill them. The {{A|Lookout}} might catch you doing it; the {{A|Doctor}} might heal them; they may be a {{A|Veteran}} trying to lure you in, and so on; the {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Crusader}}, or {{A|Trapper}} might protect them which can result in your death; the {{A|Transporter}} might have {{A|Transported}} them.
*The {{A|Mafia}} benefits by having a complacent or distracted {{A|Town}}. Therefore, you should generally avoid killing people who obviously seem to be wasting the {{A|Town's}} time with false accusations, off-topic arguments and so on. Often, they'll turn out to be {{A|Jesters}} or {{A|Executioners}} anyway. Conversely, it's often a good idea to kill people who seem too competent or directed.
*If you get accused and people vote for you, but they don't manage to get you up to the stand, it can be dangerous to kill your accuser; but people are less likely to notice if you kill the ''voters''.
*The {{A|Town}}, the {{A|Coven}} and {{A|Vampires}} are the biggest threat to the {{A|Mafia}}. Try focusing on eliminating them first unless {{A|Neutral Killing}} and/or {{A|Pestilences}} gets in the way.
*The {{A|Jailor}} is the most dangerous member of the {{A|Town}}, so you should make it a priority to find them. One way to go about this is to skip anyone who you know ''isn't'' the {{A|Jailor}} - if you eliminate your fellow Mafia, plus anyone who has claimed another role, plus anyone who has been seen visiting or otherwise identified as a non-{{A|Jailor}} by investigators, there usually aren't many options left in the late game. For this reason, it's often also worth skipping people identified by your {{A|Consiglieres}} unless it is someone you ''absolutely must'' kill immediately.

====Using the chat====
*The {{A|Mafia's}} greatest strength is knowing their allies and being able to talk to them privately at {{A|Night}}. If someone in the {{A|Mafia}} is being accused of being {{A|Mafia}}, you can team up with the other {{A|Mafia}} to invent "proof" that they are innocent; e.g. claiming that you role blocked your {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}}, have been {{A|Healed}} by a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, having {{A|Transported}} them, etc. This will cause the remaining {{A|Townies}} to be unsure who is lying, giving you time (or possibly hanging a {{A|Townie}}) until the {{A|Town}} does not have the numbers to hang you anymore. However, this must be done with care, since if your story falls apart, you might all get revealed. If you don't feel you can defend a fellow member of the {{A|Mafia}} successfully, hang them anyways so you don't seem suspicious to the rest of the {{A|Town}}.
*If you die and the {{A|Medium}} is still alive, then tell them the names of people who are {{A|Mafia}} (but really aren't). Since you can still see the {{A|Mafia}} log when you're dead, check first to see who the {{A|Mafia}} is going to kill, and call other people as {{A|Mafia}}. But advanced and experienced players are harder to trick, as they don't trust the {{A|Mafia}}. If you name someone as {{A|Mafia}} but then they die, and it's revealed they are {{A|Town}}, then the {{A|Medium}} will likely not believe you if you give out false information again.
**You may have better luck falsely telling them that someone is a {{A|Coven}} member or {{A|Neutral Killing}} role; you can claim that they're immune or that your {{A|Consigliere}} identified them. A {{A|Medium}} is more likely to believe you on this because it would make sense for you to reveal enemies that are shared between the {{A|Mafia}} and the {{A|Town}}.
What is recommended to do while in jail if you are the only {{A|Mafia Killing}} role:
*If the {{A|Jailor}} jails you, and you are the only killing role in your team ({{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Godfather}}) then you are in trouble. When the next {{A|Day}} comes and the {{A|Jailor}} sees that the {{A|Mafia}} hasn't killed, they will jail you again and again, and even execute you if they have the power to do so. The {{A|Jailor}} will likely call you out the following {{A|Day}}. When jailed, do your usual role claim, and then, at the very beginning of the {{A|Day}}, say, "I was in jail and someone tried to attack me." This might only buy you an extra {{A|Day}} (since the {{A|Jailor}} will jail you again just to double check) but you might make the {{A|Town}} think you are not the {{A|Godfather}}/{{A|Mafioso}}. Another member of the {{A|Mafia}} can also cover for you (by saying, "Thanks, {{A|Doctor}}.", by claiming to be a {{A|Survivor}} who blocked an attack with their bulletproof vest, sending a protect message as a {{A|Hypnotist}} and so on), which may be more likely to be believed; but this is dangerous, since you're exposing another member of the {{A|Mafia}} to suspicion, and if there's clearly only one {{A|Doctor}} when you claim to have been healed, then they'll know you're lying.

==Trivia==
*Prior to {{VH|Version 1.3.0}}, the {{A|Mafia}} could start the game with 5 or more members on their team.
**However, during the offseason between Season 4 and 5 of [[Game_Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]], one of the experimental role lists included 5 {{A|Mafia}} members.
**It is still possible to have 5+ {{A|Mafia}} members, with the help of {{A|Amnesiacs}}.
*Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.0.3431}}, the {{A|Mafia}} could not be killed by a bite from a {{A|Vampire}}.
*Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6537}}, the {{A|Spy}} could read {{A|Mafia chat}} during the {{A|Night}}. This was removed due to it giving the {{A|Town}} too much of an edge against the {{A|Mafia}}.
*Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, the {{A|Hypnotist}} and the {{A|Ambusher}} were only accessible in the {{A|Coven Expansion}} DLC add-on of the game.
*Currently, the {{A|Mafia}} is the only [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] with all roles available in Classic Town of Salem.
*The {{A|Mafia}} is the only faction whose killing roles deal only {{A|Basic Attacks}}.
*The {{A|Godfather}} is the only non-{{A|Neutral}} role that has permanent {{A|Basic Defense}}.
*The {{A|Mafia}} is the only [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] without a protective role.
**Although the {{A|Hypnotist}} can produce a protect message, they cannot actually prevent someone from dying.
**In {{A|Town Traitor}} however, a {{A|Town Protective|Mafia}} is possible.
*The {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}} are similar: both have multiple diverse roles, both can talk to each other at {{A|Night}}, both know each other's identities, both die from {{A|Vampire}} bites, both seek a majority in the trials, both are main evil-doers and both collude to destroy the {{A|Town}}. They have very different strategies though.

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *The {{A|Veteran}} is a{{A|Unique}} Role: meaning there can only be one in a match. *You may choose to go on {{A|Alert}} each {{A|Night}}, three times in total. You will deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}} to all your visitors and will gain {{A|Basic Defense}} for the {{A|Night}}. **In the{{A|Town Traitor}} game mode, the {{A|Veteran}} loses their {{A|Alerts}} if the Traitor is the only evil left, unless the {{A|Veteran}} is the Traitor. *Roles that visit you will still (attempt to) use their action on you. (e.g a {{A|Blackmailer}} will still blackmail you, a {{A|Transporter}} will still transport you, and a {{A|Werewolf}} will still kill you.) **However, a {{A|Vampire}} can't convert you while on {{A|Alert}}. *You are unable to be {{A|Roleblocked}}. *A {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Coven Leader}} cannot force you to {{A|Alert}} or prevent you from doing so. *If an {{A|Arsonist}} {{A|Douses}} you, you will remain {{A|Doused}} the rest of the game, being susceptible to ignition. *If a {{A|Transporter}} {{A|Transports}} you, it will still follow through. This means whoever was intending to visit you will be saved, while anyone who was visiting the other person transported will die from you. *If a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Juggernaut}} attacks you while {{A|Alerting}} both you and the killer will die. ==Strategy== The {{A|Veteran}} can be a tricky role to master since you only have 3 {{A|Alerts}} and, during those {{A|Alerts}}, you can do more harm than good. *The {{A|Veteran}} is arguably one of the most powerful {{A|Town}} roles, with the ability to defend themselves at {{A|Night}} with a well-placed {{A|Alert}} that ignores {{A|Basic Defense}}. *As a {{A|Veteran}}, it's generally harmful to ask for {{A|Town Protectives}} or {{A|Lookouts}} to protect you, since, while this may attract evil attention, it can be harmful to the {{A|Town}}, and it will most likely get a few of the aforementioned roles killed, perhaps without making any progress at all. **What's more, the fear of a {{A|Veteran}} doing this might cause roles like the {{A|Bodyguard}} to avoid 'TP/LO' claims unless they actually claim something like {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mayor}}, which is harmful to the {{A|town}}. *The trickiest part of being a {{A|Veteran}} is anticipating if and when you will be attacked and not wasting your {{A|Alerts}} for nothing. *If you have a [[name]] that stands out or is controversial, people may try to {{A|Attack}} you early in the game. **However, keep in mind that you won't know what role you will get. You can increase your chances of getting {{A|Veteran}} by using a {{A|Veteran}} {{A|Scroll}}, but it would still not be guaranteed to roll {{A|Veteran}}. **While choosing your name, do not break the [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Reportable_Offenses|rules]]. *If you have chosen a terrible or controversial [[name]] that sticks out, you can take advantage of this fact and choose to reveal that you are the {{A|Veteran}} after the first {{A|Night}}. Use the usual tactics to get yourself targeted on {{A|Night}} 1. You can engage in role collection similar to a {{A|Mayor}} by [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] to other players stating that you're the {{A|Veteran}} at the start of the day before deaths are announced. You can then actively [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to each player in the game demanding their roles. You are completely protected by attacks for the first three {{A|nights}}, should you choose to use up all your {{A|Alerts}} at once. You will also grab a lot of attention allowing other {{A|Townies}} such as {{A|Town Investigative}} roles to become hidden among the attention you gain. This tactic heavily relies on how much trust you gain in the {{A|Town}} (for example, people will have very little faith in you if you kill a lot of {{A|Townies}} on the first {{A|Night}}). People will become more distrustful of your legitimacy as you cannot be confirmed as easily as a {{A|Veteran}}. Members of the {{A|Mafia}} will become more tempted to attack you to silence you the more initiative you take during the {{A|day}}. *If you are dueled by the {{A|Pirate}}, you can still {{A|Alert}}. This is guaranteed to take out the {{A|Pirate}}, even if you lose the duel, since you're immune to the role blocking effect of their ability. However, since they deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}} and the defense of your {{A|Alert}} only grants {{A|Basic Defense}}, it won't save you. Most of the time, killing the {{A|Pirate}} is worthwhile, but remember that they can win with the {{A|Town}}; if the {{A|town's}} situation is particularly desperate, or if you're likely to need the {{A|Alert}} later on, you may be better off leaving them alive, however, if you are a confirmed {{A|Veteran}}, then there is a possible chance that the {{A|Pirate}} is siding with evils. Additionally, if you are dueled in the late game where the {{A|Pirate}} may be a tiebreaker on the final {{A|day}}, consider writing in your {{A|Last Will}} that you spared the {{A|Pirate}} (even if you were actually out of {{A|Alerts}}) and asking them to side with the {{A|town}}. *If you {{A|Alert}} and get a message saying you were attacked, but do ''not'' get a message saying you attacked a visitor, it means you were hit by an {{A|Astral}} attack; realistically, this means a {{A|Hex Master}} with the {{A|Necronomicon}}. Note that you are still {{A|hexed}} and will still die if the final {{A|hex}} goes off! ===Prove You Are a {{A|Veteran}}=== *If you manage to kill someone, such as an {{A|Investigator}}, who wrote in their {{A|Last Will}} who they visited, you can prove that you are the {{A|Veteran}} and make your voice count for a lot during the {{A|day}}, since you are a confirmed {{A|Townie}}. In theory, this can also work as a {{A|Forger}} strategy, since you can forge a {{A|Last Will}} to make it look like this. Unfortunately, {{A|Veteran}} isn't in the {{A|Forger's}} investigative results. Even if this works, it's likely that the actual {{A|Veteran}} will get killed rather soon, and upon being confirmed as the {{A|Veteran}}, you will die shortly after. Alternatively, you can just forge a {{A|Townie}} as a {{A|Veteran}} to cast doubt on the real {{A|Veteran}}. *If your presence is unknown and you {{A|Alert}} and kill someone, you can [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to players at the start of the next {{A|day}} before deaths get announced. You can state that you are a {{A|Veteran}} and state how many players visited you. *If there is a confirmed {{A|Townie}}, [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to them the {{A|Night}} before you {{A|Alert}} to ensure that they DO NOT visit you. **If there is a {{A|Blackmailer}}, doing this will make the {{A|Mafia}} not visit you, unless the {{A|Blackmailer}} is {{A|Jailed}} before they can share their information with the {{A|Mafia}}. *Often, the fact that you are a [[Unique Role|Unique role]] is enough to prove your identity; simply claiming {{A|Veteran}} will usually be enough, provided nobody counter-claims you or a {{A|Forger}} forges someone as a {{A|Veteran}}. === Saving {{A|Alerts}} === *Think logically! Everyone has their own play style but unless you bring attention to yourself early on or have a [[name]] that stands out, you have a smaller chance of being attacked at the beginning of the game because of all the potential targets. Aside from some unlucky deaths, you'll find that saving {{A|Alerts}} in the beginning boosts your survivability later in the game when the evil roles have fewer targets to choose from and they will more likely choose you. *If your role is known, try to have 1 {{A|Alert}} left if you are locked in a 3 or 2 player [[Victory (ToS)#Stalemate|stalemate]]. Also, never abstain, as you are more likely to hang the last evildoer than to shoot them later that {{A|Night}}, as they can coax you into wasting all of your {{A|Alerts}}. *You should always try to save one {{A|Alert}} for as long as possible, for when you think you will be targeted. As a {{A|Veteran}}, you will usually be confirmed before the end of the game, especially if you reveal yourself to the {{A|Town}}. Save 1 or 2 {{A|Alerts}} until the very end of the game in case of a [[Victory (ToS)#Stalemate|stalemate]], so you can at least guarantee a draw. *Once you run out of {{A|Alerts}}, DO NOT tell the {{A|Town}} that you have ran out of {{A|Alerts}} unless you are asking to be {{A|Jailed}} to be protected or if there is a {{A|Town Protective}} that is willing to protect you. This way, you do not become a target and you can last longer into the game, helping {{A|Town}} get majority at the end of the game. A {{A|Veteran}} without {{A|Alerts}} is useless as a role, and if the {{A|Mafia}} knows that you have no {{A|Alerts}}, you are an easy target for them. **However, you can always say you're out of {{A|Alerts}} to bait evils into attacking you. ===Make Yourself a Target=== *The hardest part of baiting players is the fact that the {{A|Town}} needs opportune targets more than evils do. This is another instance of [https://wiki.mafiascum.net/index.php?title=WIFOM WIFOM] loop which ''can'' turn out either way, however, this one is statistically shifted. **Evils ''do'' want high priority targets dead, but for them, the newest high-priority target of the {{A|day}} is also a high-risk target as they can be countered by a {{A|Doctor's}} heal, spotted by a {{A|Lookout}}, killed by a {{A|Bodyguard}}, or even baited by a {{A|Veteran}}. Hitting them on a different {{A|Night}} is a statistically safer option. *The key to being a good {{A|Veteran}} is attracting maximum worry from the evil while minimizing the interest from the {{A|Town}}. **Perhaps the only general way to achieve that is being active, as well as useful during the {{A|day}} without actually making role claims and without visibly trying to look important. You are looking to appear as a {{A|Town}} member that wants to help with the investigation, but doesn't actually have anything that could help with that (which is ironic, because that's exactly who you are). Be the first to attract attention to commonly available relevant evidence. In lower skill games, highlight important information from {{A|Last Wills}} and remind {{A|Town}} of possible {{A|Neutral Evils}}. Basically, be the kind of person the {{A|Mafia}} would not want to continue to have an effect on the {{A|Town}}, but not the kind of person whose continued survival is at the top of {{A|Town Protectives}}' and {{A|Lookouts}}' priority lists. *When an opportunity arises, tell the {{A|Town}} to protect some other confirmed {{A|Townie}}, and go on {{A|Alert}}. You might take down a {{A|Mafioso}} attempting to remove a possible threat, or another {{A|Mafia}} member trying to disrupt you. *It is against the [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Reportable_Offenses|rules]] to spam, and being a {{A|Veteran}} doesn't change that. On top of that, spam acts as a distraction that prevents {{A|Town}} from having a productive discussion about figuring and hanging evil roles. This makes you much less likely to be targeted by evil, and MORE likely to be targeted by {{A|Town}}. A spamming {{A|Veteran}} is the worst possible {{A|Veteran}} you could be. *Sometimes it's a good idea to say you are an important {{A|Town}} role, such as a {{A|Town Protective}} or a {{A|Town Investigative}}. This might result in evil roles targeting you. This mostly works in the early rounds because the evil roles don't really know any information during that period and they want to get rid of important {{A|Townies}}. **Be careful, though! A {{A|Consigliere}} might investigate you, reveal your role to the {{A|Mafia}}, and write in their {{A|Last Will}} that you're lying if you decide to save your {{A|Alert}} for the {{A|Night}}. A {{A|Witch}} can also reveal your role to their allies, and then control confirmed {{A|Townies}} into visiting you. *One way of not wasting your {{A|Alerts}} for nothing is to make yourself a target for evils by saying something like "Stop role blocking me you illiterate idiots!" or "I think I know a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, but I'm gonna double-check in case of a {{A|Transporter}}." **You should use the second one just a few seconds before the {{A|day}} ends so no one has time to question you about it. Using something like the first one might make a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} come and visit you, so be careful. *If someone says "Thanks {{A|Doctor}} for healing me last {{A|Night}}!" or something similar, say "No problem!" and go on {{A|Alert}}. However, you have to have a very clear {{A|Vision}} of the evil roles' skill levels for that to work. You need to be in a game where a {{A|Doctor}} is likely to be inexperienced enough to reveal himself like that, and when one or more killers are gullible enough to fall for such a bait. *A good strategy is to speak on {{A|Day}} 1. Strangely, whoever speaks that {{A|day}} is usually visited. This may be because the killing roles believe that the louder people will soon be the ones accusing them, so they want to get rid of them first or because they have no other information to go with. Go on {{A|Alert}}, and you could get a killing role killed especially if you spoke first. However, some other {{A|Townies}} may notice it as well and visit you. *If you know of a confirmed {{A|Town Investigative}}, [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to them that you're a {{A|Veteran}}. (Generally, it's a good idea for all {{A|Town}} roles to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] their roles to confirmed {{A|Townies}}. Mind the {{A|Blackmailer}}, though, especially as a {{A|Veteran}}.) *If you are pressed to claim your role in public, it's often advantageous to claim {{A|Vigilante}} and then go on {{A|Alert}} the next {{A|Night}}. Your investigative results include both {{A|Vigilante}} and {{A|Veteran}} (so this claim is 'safe' in that it won't contradict any previous {{A|Town Investigatives}}), and since {{A|Vigilante}} is a high-profile target, claiming it will often attract the {{A|Mafia's}} attention. Additionally, the {{A|Vigilante's}} capability to kill most {{A|Mafia}} members directly makes it more dangerous than {{A|Town Protectives}} are. **This claim, unlike claiming a {{A|Town Investigative}} role, is somewhat less likely to attract any {{A|Town Protectives}} that you might hit in the crossfire. **However, claiming {{A|Vigilante}} can be particularly problematic in a game with a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}. The {{A|Town}} is afraid of {{A|Vigilantes}} being controlled by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} and might hang you. {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and {{A|Transporters}} may try to prevent you from getting controlled by visiting you, which puts them in danger of dying. ***On the plus side, this can bait a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} into visiting you on {{A|Alert}}. *Claiming ambiguous {{A|Town Killing}} can also be a somewhat smarter move for {{A|Veteran}} in general. It is well known that each one of them wants the {{A|Mafia}} to believe that they are the other one. However, the {{A|Mafia}} aren't the only ones wanting to know who the {{A|Veteran}} is, and real {{A|Town Killing}} roles aren't the only ones claiming to be {{A|Town Killing}}. There's a very thin line between ambiguity and deception here and you should be acutely aware of the ones crossing it. If someone other than you is claiming {{A|Veteran}}, you know for sure that the line has been crossed. There is very little advantage to evils from making an ambiguous {{A|Town Killing}} claim (other than sounding a bit more plausible) and they often don't think twice before claiming specific {{A|Town Killings}}. Meanwhile, a real {{A|Townie}} falsely claiming {{A|Veteran}} puts himself in a claim deadlock with you. So long as there's no risk of a {{A|Jester}} being involved, it would be a logical move for you to counter {{A|Veteran}} claims, as it's not the real {{A|Town Killing}} who gets the most out of specific {{A|Town Killing}} claims. *You may think that saying something along the lines of "I HATE THIS ROLE" in all caps will make the {{A|Mafia}} visit you with either a {{A|Consigliere}} or a {{A|Mafioso}}, but it will typically instead make {{A|Town Investigative}} roles visit you. You could end up killing several of your {{A|Townies}} in one {{A|Night}}. *While it's extremely counter-intuitive, claiming {{A|Veteran}} {{A|Day}} 1 and then {{A|Alerting}} the next {{A|Night}} is actually a viable strategy. Other {{A|Townies}} will rarely risk visiting a {{A|Veteran}} claim early on. Killers who need to eliminate you might assume you won't {{A|Alert}} right after claiming (since ''you'' would assume they're unlikely to visit you) and try to take you out early. This makes it a "safer" bait, calling attention to yourself with a lower chance of attracting {{A|Town}}. *It is possible to claim that you have no {{A|Alerts}} left while you still have one or two. This will theoretically trick the {{A|Mafia}} into thinking you are an easy target since they believe that you have no {{A|Alerts}}. Do bear in mind that they may double bluff you and avoid you anyway, under the suspicion that you are lying. *When the {{A|Jailor}} jails you, tell them you are a {{A|Veteran}}, but ask the {{A|Jailor}} to put you down as {{A|Vigilante}} or some other role that threatens the {{A|Mafia}}. This will attract attention if the {{A|Jailor's}} {{A|Last Will}} is revealed. ===What to do once you are found out=== *Once you are found out as a {{A|Veteran}}, it is highly recommended to save your {{A|Alerts}} until very late into the game, because if you are found out, it is extremely unlikely that a killing role will visit you. Saving them to the end of the game will help the {{A|Town}} greatly, especially if you end up one-on-one versus a {{A|Mafia Killing}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} role. **Many players have caught onto the above strategy, however, and will attempt to kill you the {{A|Night}} after you have been found out. If you're playing [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]] with a high [[Elo]] lobby, it will often be advantageous to {{A|Alert}} the following {{A|Night}} or to get the {{A|Town Protective}} to defend you. If the {{A|Town Protective}} is known to be a {{A|Bodyguard}}, this is one more reason for killing roles to avoid you. *If you run out of {{A|Alerts}}, '''DO NOT LEAVE THE GAME!''' You can still help the {{A|Town}} with votes, especially if you are confirmed. *Don't worry if a {{A|Spy}} said you were visited by {{A|Mafia}} and weren't attacked and didn't {{A|Alert}}. If it is a {{A|Consigliere}}, they most likely won't ask the {{A|Mafia}} to attack you. There are a lot more important roles to attack, and they might be afraid of you {{A|Alerting}}. If it isn't a {{A|Consigliere}}, then it is most likely a {{A|Framer}} or {{A|Ambusher}}, in which case the {{A|Mafia}} won't know who you are, which is good. ==={{A|Veteran}} vs Killing Role=== *In most of these scenarios you'll have only one {{A|Alert}} left. Keep in mind that the game cannot end in a draw due to no kills before {{A|Day 9}}. *Sometimes they won't risk to attack you until the very last {{A|Night}}, where it's either a draw or a win of one of the two parts, trying to make you waste any {{A|Alerts}} left. *As a {{A|Veteran}}, you can try to make the killing role speak by talking to them or voting for them. If they don't answer, they're either Away From Keyboard (AFK) or wants you to believe that, so you will not go on {{A|Alert}}. *Stay silent to make the killing role believe you won't go on {{A|Alert}}. Most of the times staying silent will make the other player doubt what to do (going on {{A|Alert}} or not/attacking or not). *You can also claim {{A|Vigilante}}, for instance, to the killing role. Just remember to act natural. If they believe you, {{A|Alert}} the next {{A|Night}}. This can work due to the {{A|Vigilante}} being helpless in this situation, and the killing role thinks they could simply attack you to win. If the killer lacks {{A|Basic Defense}}, it's even better as you can pressure them into attacking you to go for a draw. *Usually, the killer will think you are going to save your {{A|Alerts}} until the last possible {{A|Night}}. If you have two {{A|Alerts}} left, use this to your advantage. *Try to manipulate them into thinking that you have no {{A|Alerts}} left, causing them to attack you on {{A|Alert}}. *However, in certain 1 v 1 scenarios, you will always lose no matter how many {{A|Alerts}} you have left. This applies for a {{A|Werewolf}}, the {{A|Hex Master}}, {{A|Necromancer}} and {{A|Pestilence}}. ==List of Common {{A|Veteran}} Baits== {{A|Veteran}} baits (or Vet baits for short) are strategies used by {{A|Veterans}} and sometimes {{A|Medusas}} to make themselves a target and encourage killers (or {{A|Townies}} for {{A|Medusa}}) to visit them during the {{A|Night}}. The following is a list of often used {{A|Veteran}} baits: *Claiming a role: **Claiming to be a {{A|Serial Killer}} or a {{A|Vigilante}}, so a {{A|Coven Leader}}/{{A|Witch}} attempts to control you. As {{A|Veterans}} cannot be prevented from {{A|Alerting}}, there is no need to worry about being controlled. **Claiming to be a role with a day ability, like {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mayor}}, and asking how it works. Note that this tactic is especially ineffective in [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]], as players are expected to be experienced. **Claiming to be an important {{A|Town}} role, such as {{A|Jailor}}. Note that this has a high chance of attacking {{A|Townies}}. *Chat behavior: **Acting especially quiet. This can lure evils into thinking that you are a very important role in wanting to stay hidden, causing them to attack you. Try not to be too quiet, as they'll probably just list you as Away From Keyboard (AFK). **Acting notably loud and talkative. Evils generally want to eliminate more competent and active enemies, making you a target. **Saying strange or unusual things can help you lure evils, especially on {{A|Day}} one. However, try not to say anything offensive, as it may violate the [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Reportable_Offenses|rules]]. **Being annoying, enticing killers or {{A|Blackmailers}} who wish to silence you. **Naming yourself something controversial after equipping {{A|Veteran}} [[Scrolls (ToS)|scrolls]] or [[Scrolls (ToS)|lesser scrolls]]. Please avoid offensive names, because some people may get offended and/or triggered. This can also go against the [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Reportable_Offenses|rules]]. **Acting like a troll. This is especially risky, as it can go against the [[Town_of_Salem_Rules#Reportable_Offenses|rules]]. However, trolling makes you look like an useless {{A|Jester}}, leading killing roles into your trap. **Declaring you hate a particular [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] such as {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} if they are believed to be in the game. **Go against something that a killer likes. For example, if they put they like ketchup in their {{A|Death Note}}, you would then say you hate ketchup and {{A|Alert}} that {{A|Night}}. *Luring evils into attacking you: **Asking for {{A|Town Protective}} and/or {{A|Lookout}}. Note that this has a high chance of attacking {{A|Townies}} while evil killing roles choosing to kill someone else instead since they might expect a {{A|Town Protective}} to protect you. **Accusing someone of being evil so killers target you, in an attempt to frame the person you accused. **Claiming to want to leave the game without receiving a 5 minute penalty and requesting to be killed. **Claiming {{A|Vigilante}} and threatening to shoot anyone who votes guilty/innocent while someone is on trial. **Saying you don’t want to die {{A|Night}} one. Note that this has a high chance of attacking {{A|Townies}}. **Saying something first or last on {{A|Day}} one. *Tricking evils to kill you while revealed as {{A|Veteran}}: **Truthfully claiming {{A|Veteran}} but also telling the {{A|Town}} you won't {{A|Alert}} during the {{A|Night}}. Additionally, you might choose to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] this to a player you believe to be a killer. **Claiming to be out of {{A|Alerts}} and hence, that you cannot kill anyone. **Failing a [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] during the {{A|day}}, saying something suspicious like "Okay so who do we kill tonight?". Note that this has a high chance of killing {{A|Townies}}. *[[Roles (ToS)|Role]]/[[Game_Modes (ToS)|Game Mode]] specific baits: **In games with {{A|Blackmailers}}, [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a confirmed {{A|Townie}} claiming a {{A|Town Protective}} role or {{A|Lookout}}, before {{A|Alerting}}. You can pretend as if you have important information to give. **In [[Game Modes (ToS)#Rainbow_Mode|Rainbow Mode]], try claiming an evil role on the list and ask to be killed. **In [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]], try talking about your [[Elo]] or win-streak. *Act like a {{A|Jester}} **Acting like a {{A|Jester}} is a very risky strategy, as it may lure other {{A|Town Killing}} roles into killing you, especially the {{A|Vigilante}}. However, if the {{A|Mafia}} has majority, this could work. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{VeteranAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{VeteranMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to [[Version_History (ToS)|Version 2.0]], {{A|Veterans}} had {{A|Death Notes}}. This allowed them to be easily confirmed by revealing who they are in their {{A|Death Note}}. *Prior to [[Version_History (ToS)|Version 2.1.0]], {{A|Veterans}} would not lose automatically against a {{A|Werewolf}} in a 1 v 1 situation. *{{A|Veteran}} has become somewhat of a [[wikipedia:Internet meme|meme]] across social media. *The {{A|Veteran}} is the only {{A|Town}} role that is able to grant themselves {{A|Defense}} but cannot grant it to other players. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.11}} **In {{A|Town Traitor}}, non-{{A|Town Traitor}} {{A|Veterans}} loses their {{A|Alerts}} when the {{A|Town Traitor}} hunt starts. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Veteran's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Veteran.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Veteran's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Veteran Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.5.1.10655]] **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.3.8910]] **{{A|Spy}} can now die to a {{A|Veteran}} on {{A|Alert}}. ({{A|Bug}} Fix) *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.1.0.7320]] **{{A|Werewolf}} vs. {{A|Veteran}} now grants {{A|Werewolf}} the victory, even if the {{A|Veteran}} has {{A|Alerts}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.0]] **{{A|Veterans}} no longer have a {{A|Death Note}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|Beta 0.3.0]] **{{A|Veterans}} now have a {{A|Death Note}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|Town of Salem Release]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Vétéran]] [[ru:Ветеран]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Town Killing roles]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You may choose a player to {{A|Shoot}} at {{A|Night}}, dealing a basic attack to them. You cannot {{A|Shoot}} on the first {{A|Night}}. You can only {{A|Shoot}} three times. *If you kill a {{A|Town}} member, you will commit suicide the next {{A|Night}}, dealing the equivalent of an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}}. You will still commit suicide if you are {{A|Roleblocked}}, {{A|Controlled}}, or {{A|Jailed}}, and you cannot be {{A|Controlled}} to {{A|Shoot}} someone. A {{A|Transporter}} will also be unable to {{A|Transport}} your suicide. *If a {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Coven Leader}} controls you, you are forced to {{A|Shoot}} their second target, even if it is the first {{A|Night}}. You can still be {{A|Roleblocked}} from {{A|Shooting}}. You will also still commit suicide if you were controlled into {{A|Shooting}} a {{A|Townie}}. *If your target was {{A|Jailed}}, you will not lose a bullet, but your target will be notified of your attempted attack. *If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Vigilante|Mafia}} or a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Vigilante|Coven}}, you can shoot your teammates, however it is not recommended to do this unless you are going for a {{A|Town Traitor}} hunt. *You cannot be the {{A|VIP}} due to being a passively suicidal role. ===Suicide=== *If your target was {{A|cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}}, turned to stone by {{A|Medusa}}, or forged by a {{A|Forger}}, you will still commit suicide if they were a {{A|Town}} member. *If you are converted into a {{A|Vampire}} on the same {{A|Night}} you {{A|Shoot}} a {{A|Town}} member, you will not commit suicide on the following {{A|Night}}. This informs the {{A|Town}} that you were either converted or your target was non-{{A|Town}} forged as a {{A|Town}} member (You cannot be converted to a {{A|Vampire}} on the {{A|Night}} after {{A|Shooting}} a {{A|Town}} member). **Note that you will still receive the message for shooting a {{A|Townie}}, however you will not die that {{A|Night}}. [[File:Conversion Shot.png|thumb|480px]] *Suicide is considered an {{A|Unstoppable Attack}} at a priority similar to a {{A|Jester}}. This means a {{A|Town Protective}}, {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Guardian Angel}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Pirate}}, {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, or {{A|Transporter}} cannot stop you from committing suicide. *If you are a Town Traitor {{A|Vigilante|Mafia}} or a Coven Town Traitor {{A|Vigilante|Coven}}, you will never suicide from guilt, regardless of who you {{A|Shoot}}. ==Strategy== ===Selecting Who to {{A|Shoot}}=== *Like all {{A|Townies}}, the {{A|Vigilante}} works best as a team player. Communicate in whispers to known {{A|Town Investigative}} roles and the {{A|Jailor}} so that you {{A|Shoot}} only evil-doers with your bullets. **Without communicating, you can end up {{A|Shooting}} someone that was known to be a {{A|Townie}} by a {{A|Town Investigative}}, or may lose your chance to {{A|Shoot}} anyone at all if any evildoers catch wind of your identity and kill/roleblock you. *Compile a list of non-{{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} members in your {{A|Last Will}} or {{A|Notes}} so that you can be sure you do not accidentally {{A|Shoot}} a confirmed member of the {{A|Town}}. *Only {{A|Shoot}} if you are sure that your target is a non-{{A|Town}} role, it would be too risky otherwise. In many cases, you do not need to use your ability to win the game. **An exception to this would be if the {{A|Town}} is losing and needs to consider the possibility of luckily eliminating evil roles by a calculated random shot. *Even though you're on the same team, {{A|Transporters}} pose huge risks to a {{A|Vigilante}}. If you've identified someone as evil, there's a good chance a {{A|Transporter}} has, too, in which case they may be transporting your target with themselves or a confirmed {{A|Town}}. If there's a confirmed {{A|Transporter}} in your game, consider whispering them before you {{A|Shoot}} someone who looks evil so they know not to transport them that {{A|Night}}. Be wary of {{A|Blackmailers}}, though, as they could expose you to the {{A|Mafia}}. *If you are unsure of who to {{A|Shoot}}, try and think about who is acting like a {{A|Jester}}, as they might be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral}} role trying to not get hanged. Therefore you can {{A|Shoot}} them and they have a lower chance of being a {{A|Townie}}. *If you are fairly certain someone is an evil role, such as a minor bit of evidence against them or if they claimed a role that was an enemy to the {{A|Mafia}}, and they haven't been attacked,{{A|Shoot}} them, especially in cases where the {{A|Town}} ''will'' lose majority if you don't {{A|Shoot}}. It can clear up and expose false claims, along with confirming some {{A|Townies}}. **The downside is that some players may randomly {{A|Shoot}} someone, even if no evidence is against them. Even if they hit a {{A|Neutral}} or {{A|Mafia}} member, in most game-modes, there is a high chance of them killing a {{A|Townie}}. Although this is not [[gamethrowing]], it is frowned upon by most people because of the chance a {{A|Townie}} can get killed. *One simple self-confirmation strategy is to claim {{A|Vigilante}} and ask roles from everyone, similar to a {{A|Mayor}} game. You can threaten to {{A|Shoot}} players who do not claim. The downside is you may get attacked by the {{A|Mafia}}, roleblocked by a {{A|Bootlegger}}, or worse, get controlled by a {{A|Witch}} to {{A|Shoot}} a confirmed {{A|Townie}}. *Don't be afraid to {{A|Shoot}} someone who claims a {{A|Neutral}} role if you think they could be a threat for the {{A|Town}}, because a {{A|Jester}} can kill an important {{A|Town}} member via haunt, and {{A|Witches}} can throw off the {{A|Town}} from collecting valuable information. Additionally, {{A|Mafia}} members sometimes try and fake {{A|Jester}}, giving you another reason to {{A|Shoot}} any {{A|Jester}} claims. *Late in the game, you may be forced to {{A|Shoot}} somewhat more blindly, based on circumstantial evidence or someone you suspect is ''probably'' {{A|Mafia}}. This should be avoided early on, but if you're certain the {{A|Town}} is about to lose its majority anyway, then it's preferable to take a risk rather than just let the {{A|Town}} lose. In this situation, you should rely on everything that has happened up until then to try and make the best possible guess: **Usually anyone who votes a member of the {{A|Mafia}} up to the stand when there is reasonable doubt is unlikely to be a {{A|Mafia}} member themselves. ''Guilty'' votes are less meaningful because {{A|Mafia}} members are likely to vote guilty if it's clear someone can't be saved but may try to drag their feet in the hopes that they won't get voted up to begin with. **If you can eliminate almost everyone from consideration as possible {{A|Mafia}} based on those voting patterns combined with the {{A|Last Wills}} from {{A|Sheriffs}}, confirmed {{A|Town}}, and so on, you should {{A|Shoot}} whoever is left. **Generally, use common sense to select who to {{A|Shoot}}. Don't {{A|Shoot}} people who are confirmed, and look at who has a weak claim or no claim. Anybody who doesn't have a decent {{A|Last Will}} is more likely to be evil. Use all the information, even if there isn't much around to use. *If someone is ''almost'' voted up, but the vote fails, it might be worth {{A|Shooting}} them, even if the evidence against them is weak. This is because if they are actually a member of the {{A|Mafia}},{{A|Shooting}} them can turn the entire game around by casting suspicion on anyone who refused to vote for them (and giving you valuable information for your remaining shots). However, the accuser could be an {{A|Executioner}}. **This is especially applicable when the {{A|Mafia}} is near the majority. Consider the possibilities: ***It's unlikely that the {{A|Mafia}} would have risked outing themselves by aggressively trying to vote someone up on their own when they're near (but not quite at) a majority, especially since they'll shortly win naturally by killing people. Additionally, if the {{A|Mafia}} is near a majority, smart {{A|Town}} members will know they ''must'' hang someone, even if the evidence is weak. Therefore, the people voting against that person are probably not {{A|Mafia}}. ***Conversely, if the person being voted up was not {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Mafia}} (being near a majority) would have joined in as soon as the {{A|Town}} started to vote up the wrong person and easily hang them. You can point this out and usually get them off the stand with a smart {{A|Town}}. ****This is known as a 'fast vote'. ****Experienced {{A|Mafia}} members may know this and 'slow vote' the person being voted and call out the vote speed to trick the {{A|Town}}. ***Therefore, if an effort to vote someone up fails in a near-miss in the late game when the {{A|Mafia}} is near the majority, it's usually a sign that both the person being voted up and some or all of the people who refused to vote for them are part of the {{A|Mafia}}, and you should usually risk {{A|Shooting}} the person who was voted up. *When there is a {{A|Bodyguard}} around, be careful of who you {{A|Shoot}}. If you {{A|Shoot}} someone that is guarded by one, both you and the {{A|Bodyguard}} will die, and the {{A|Town}} member guarded will be left open to attack. *It is generally a bad idea to {{A|Shoot}} someone under suspicion of being a role with Basic protection or above. While you can notionally confirm their protection (and therefore out them), this carries all the risks of hitting an innocent, either due to a false accusation or a {{A|Transporter}}, with fewer benefits if you get it right. Investigations are, when possible, better left to the {{A|Town Investigatives}}. **However, it is usually worth {{A|Shooting}} someone who has ''confessed'' to being such a role or otherwise implied that's what they are, since they may be a {{A|Jester}}, or they may be another evil pretending to be an {{A|Executioner}} or {{A|Survivor}}. ===When you {{A|Shoot}} a {{A|Townie}}=== *If you make a mistake and {{A|Shoot}} a {{A|Town}} member, '''don't reveal''' who you are the next day! The {{A|Mafia}} or any {{A|Neutral Killing}} might waste a {{A|Night}} targeting you. You can also tell the {{A|Transporter}} to use you as a 'shield' for other players as you will die anyway. *If you {{A|Shoot}} a target that is {{A|cleaned}} or {{A|stoned}} (or forged as a non-{{A|Town}} role) on the same {{A|Night}} and you die of guilt, the {{A|Town}} will gain valuable info that the target was a {{A|Townie}} as you can only die of guilt from {{A|Shooting}} someone from the {{A|Town}}. *If a {{A|Pirate}} has chosen to side with {{A|Town}}, let them plunder you, since you will die regardless, and [[whisper]] to them what you will pick. The {{A|Pirate}} will likely pick the corresponding defense, netting them a free plunder. ===When your target has {{A|Defense}}=== *If you {{A|Shoot}} a player with {{A|defense}}, make sure to inform the {{A|Town}}, so they can decide whether the person is an evil role with {{A|Defense }}and hang them. No {{A|Town}} role has {{A|Defense}} except for a {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Veteran}} who uses their self-protection. **However, if your target was a {{A|Witch}} who had {{A|Basic Defense}}, it's recommended to {{A|Shoot}} them again, rather than informing the {{A|Town}} since you'll risk getting controlled into {{A|Shooting}} a {{A|Townie}} if the {{A|Town}} fails to vote up the {{A|Witch}}. ***An easy way to tell if you shot a {{A|Witch}} is to check if you got a {{A|Defense}} message. Since only a {{A|Witch}} produces no {{A|Defense}} message to an attacker, it's easy to deduce that your target is a {{A|Witch}}. *When informing the {{A|Town}} that you shot an immune player, you should also present your logic for ''why'' you shot them. If you didn't have a good reason to {{A|Shoot}} them, you may come across as a {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} trying to accuse another evil. *If somebody is accused of being a role with {{A|Defense}} like {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Godfather}}, it's sometimes a good idea to attempt to {{A|Shoot}} them. If they are immune, you will be given a message that their defense was "too strong to kill". You can then write your findings in your {{A|Last Will}} and announce it to the {{A|Town}} the next day. Be somewhat cautious about this; {{A|Shooting}} them is a bit of a "destruction test" since if the accusation is false, you have a high risk of killing a {{A|Town}} member. ===Surviving the Day Phases=== *Secrecy is the key. The {{A|Vigilante's}} {{A|Basic Attack}} makes them a threat to all evils without {{A|Defense}}, so don't reveal your identity until asked by an {{A|Investigator}} or if your target has {{A|Basic Defense}}. *If you are aware of a {{A|Witch}} in-game, be careful when stating you're a {{A|Vigilante}} as the {{A|Witch}} can control you into {{A|Shooting}} a fellow {{A|Townie}}. Under no circumstances should you reveal that you are the {{A|Vigilante}} unless you ask a {{A|Transporter}} to transport you or not to transport your target, or you know a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Jailor}} can prevent you from {{A|Shooting}} good {{A|Townies}}. **You may wish to claim {{A|Veteran}} as it is less likely that you will be targeted by evils and you have the same investigation results. ***Be wary about claiming {{A|Veteran}} if there is another one in game. You may want to whisper to the {{A|Veteran}} about your fake claim and possibly tell them to claim {{A|Vigilante}} so the {{A|Witch}} visits the wrong person and dies. *If you're going to {{A|Shoot}} anyone, you can call "Vig {{A|Shoot}} (name)!". It's an indirect call for anyone not to touch the target (especially {{A|Transporter}}). Don't tell the {{A|Town}} "'''I''' am going to {{A|Shoot}}" -- using first-person phrasing to announce intent will out you, while third-person phrasing keeps you indistinguishable from {{A|Townies}} trying to direct you. Experienced {{A|Mafia}} members may still see through the bluff and attack/roleblock you. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{VigilanteAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{VigilanteMessages}} ==Trivia== *The only game mode that {{A|Vigilante}} cannot ever appear is the Lovers [[Game Modes (ToS)|game mode]] in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *After {{A|Shooting}} a {{A|Townie}}, a {{A|Vigilante}} may appear to not commit suicide from guilt if they leave the game. *The {{A|Vigilante}} is one of two roles to have 2 [[Avatars (ToS)|skins]], the other being the {{A|Arsonist}}. *If a {{A|Vigilante}} {{A|Shoots}} a {{A|Townie}} using their last bullet, the {{A|Vigilante}} will still "put away their gun" and commit suicide even though they have no more bullets. *The cause of death message "dying of guilt" (comitting suicide after killing a townie) was changed to being "doomed for killing a townie" in [[Version History (ToS)|Version 3.3.11]]. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.6}} **Fixed a bug where {{A|Vigilante}} could not be added in [[Coven Custom]]. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Vigilante's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Vigilante.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Vigilante's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Vigilante Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **A {{A|Witch}} controlling a {{A|Vigilante}} to kill another {{A|Townie}} with only those three alive now results in a {{A|Witch}} victory over a {{A|Town}} victory. *{{VH|2.0}} **{{A|Vigilantes}} no longer have a {{A|Death Note}}. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **Attackers will now get "Your target is immune" message when attacking {{A|Werewolf}} on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|nights}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Линчеватель]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Town Killing roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
