'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *You can {{A|Transport}} two targets (including yourself) each Night. *{{A|Transporting}} a target swaps all visitors to them; for example, all visitors that visit target A will instead visit target B, and vice versa. **However, you cannot {{A|Transport}} a {{A|Guardian Angel's}} protection onto another player. **If a {{A|Jester}} is hanged, you '''cannot''' {{A|Transport}} their haunting to another player. **Your {{A|Transporting}} does not affect an {{A|Arsonist's}} igniting, all {{A|Doused}} players will still die. *You cannot be {{A|Controlled}} by a {{A|Witch}} or a {{A|Coven Leader}}. *You cannot be Roleblocked by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Pirate}}. *You cannot {{A|Transport}} the same person with themselves. *If two or more {{A|Transporters}} choose to transport the same person, whoever joined the lobby first will have their {{A|Transport}} occur first. *You '''cannot''' {{A|Transport}} the results of a {{A|Pirate}} {{A|Duel}} away from a player, however, if you know someone is likely to be protected, swapping them will cause their protector to save the {{A|Dueled}} player if the {{A|Pirate}} wins the duel. *You cannot {{A|Transport}} the {{A|Jailor's}} target, and instead your {{A|Transport}} will fail. You will receive the message "One of your targets was in jail, so you could not {{A|Transport}} them." ===Transport - Normal behavior=== You may choose two people to {{A|Transport}} each {{A|Night}}. The order of selecting who to {{A|Transport}} does not matter. *Both the people you {{A|Transported}} will receive the message, "You were {{A|Transported}} to another location." at the end of the {{A|Night}}. *Visitors, on the other hand, will ''not'' be informed that they hit the wrong target (although some, like killers, may be able to figure it out because their selected target wasn't killed.) *If your {{A|Transport}} causes a target to visit themselves, the target will use their {{A|Night}} ability on themselves (e.g. attacking, investigating, role blocking). For certain roles like {{A|Investigator}}, you will get an {{A|Achievement}} when you do this for the first time. **The only exception to this system is the {{A|Werewolf}}. If they are {{A|Transported}} into targeting themselves, they will instead rampage at home and kill all visitors, including you. ===When your {{A|Transport}} will fail=== Transporting will be ineffective in the following situations: *You cannot switch a {{A|Survivor's}} target. If they use a bulletproof vest, it will always target themselves. Any other visits to the {{A|Survivor}} will still be switched to your other target. *You cannot switch a {{A|Veteran's}} target. If they are on alert, you will be shot. They will still be {{A|Transported}} (meaning that anyone who was trying to visit your other target will die, while anyone who was trying to visit the {{A|Veteran}} will be saved). This also applies for the {{A|Medusa}} as well. *If you {{A|Transport}} a {{A|Werewolf}} who was forced to stay at home because they were role blocked or didn't pick a target, then they will still rampage at "home". You will still die because you visited the {{A|Werewolf}} when they stayed home, but if you kept an accurate {{A|Last Will}}, you may nab the {{A|Werewolf}} in the process. *You cannot {{A|Transport}} targets who are in {{A|Jail}}. When you try, you will be notified that one of your targets was {{A|Jailed}}. A {{A|Lookout}} will still see you visit your other target, and a {{A|Werewolf}} rampaging at one of their houses will maul you. The {{A|Jailed}} person will know you tried to {{A|Transport}} them. *You cannot {{A|Transport}} targets who left the game '''before''' the {{A|Night}} ends (You will receive no {{A|Transport}} message). *You cannot {{A|Transport}} a dead {{A|Medium's}} {{A|Seance}} target since their ability takes place when the {{A|Night}} begins. *You cannot {{A|Transport}} the guilt from a {{A|Vigilante}} who shot a {{A|Townie}}. The {{A|Vigilante}} will still commit suicide. However, you may {{A|Transport}} the {{A|Vigilante's}} target the {{A|Night}} before. *When Transporting a {{A|Doctor}} or {{A|Bodyguard}}, if they chose to Self Heal or Vest, they will continue to do so. {{A|Transporting}} does not force them to protect the other {{A|Transported}} target when they have chosen a self targeting ability. *Reanimated corpses (including{{A|Necromancer's ghoul}}) sometimes ignore transportation. This is most likely a bug. *Your {{A|Transport}} cannot switch the following attacks: **If your target is attacked by a {{A|Jester}} or a {{A|Pirate}}, they will still die even if you {{A|Transport}} them. **If your target is a {{A|Vigilante}} who shot a {{A|Town}} member, they will still commit suicide the following Night. **If your target role blocked a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Werewolf}} (during {{A|Full Moon}}), the killer will attack the role blocker even if you {{A|Transport}} them. **If your target visited a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Medusa}} who is using their ability, they will still be shot or {{A|Stoned}} by them. **If your target was {{A|doused}} by an {{A|Arsonist}}, they will still be ignited if the {{A|Arsonist}} chooses to ignite their targets. **If your target was {{A|hexed}} by the {{A|Hex Master}}, your {{A|Transports}} will not prevent their massive Unstoppable attack from taking place. ***However, a bug exists where the original target will appear to be {{A|Hexed}} to the {{A|Hex Master}}, instead of the new target. **If your target attacked someone who is {{A|Guarded}} by a {{A|Bodyguard}}, they will be killed even if you {{A|Transport}} them. **If your target visited a house in which a {{A|Werewolf}} rampaged at, they will be mauled even if you {{A|Transport}} them (same with {{A|Pestilence}} and {{A|Juggernaut's}} rampages.). **If your target visited someone that was visited by a {{A|Crusader}} or an {{A|Ambusher}} and they are attacked by said roles, they will die even if you {{A|Transport}} them. *If you {{A|Transport}} someone who was targeted by an {{A|Arsonist}} and/or {{A|Plaguebearer}}, these two roles will accurately see who actually ended up getting {{A|Doused}}/{{A|Infected}}. Therefore, it is often easy for an {{A|Arsonist}} to tell who their target was {{A|Transported}} with. **This is not the case for {{A|Hex Master}} and {{A|Poisoner}}, these roles will still see their specific [[Abilities (ToS)|ability]] label ({{A|Hex}}/{{A|Poison}}) on the player they intended to target. ***If you {{A|Transport}} a {{A|Poisoner}} with their target, the {{A|Poisoner}} will see two {{A|Poison}} icons on the player list: one on themself and one on the player they meant to target. ===Interaction between two {{A|Transporters}}=== *If two {{A|Transporters}} select the same person, then the outcome will depend on the order in which the {{A|Transporters}} appeared in the lobby before the game started. Let T1 and T2 be {{A|Transporters}}, and let T1 join the lobby before T2. The game will process their targets' {{A|Transportation}} thus: *# T1 marks their left target for {{A|Transportation}}; *# If T1's right target is the same as T2's right target, then T2 marks their right target for {{A|Transportation}}; *# T1 swaps whoever they marked with their right target; *# If T2 didn't mark anyone in step 2, then they mark whoever is at their right target's house; *# T2 swaps whoever is at their left target's house with the person they marked. ==Strategy== *The {{A|Transporter}} can be a very powerful role, as long as they have the right information at hand. However, they can also be a chaotic one, messing up delicate balances. **You can always act like a {{A|Town Protective}} role when all of them are dead. {{A|Transporting}} people can help save important {{A|Town}} roles late game and cause attackers to attack themselves, wasting their {{A|Night}} kill. *A {{A|Transporter}} can actually attempt to kill people who they suspect, by baiting people into visiting them during the {{A|Day}} and {{A|Transporting}} themselves with the person they want to kill. **However, a {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Veteran}}, {{A|Medusa}}, {{A|Ambusher}}, {{A|Crusader}}, {{A|Werewolf}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, or another {{A|Transporter}} can mess up this plan. *A {{A|Transporter}} is among one of the easiest roles to confirm. It is a good idea to {{A|Transport}} two people the first {{A|Night}} to avoid any {{A|Hypnotist}} claims. *{{A|Transporters}} do not have to {{A|Transport}} every {{A|Night}}, and if in a situation where {{A|Transporting}} won't yield any important result, not {{A|Transporting}} may be beneficial to avoid messing up roles like {{A|Vigilante}} and {{A|Investigator}}. ===Who to {{A|Transport}}=== *During the second half of a game, you should be able to identify which players the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} will target, such as the {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}}. {{A|Transporting}} valuable roles could save lives. If you have a decent idea of who the opposition is '''and''' who they'll target, swap one with the other so that the player attempting to kill your fellow {{A|Townie}} will target themselves or their teammate. They will only kill themselves if they are either a {{A|Mafioso}}, a {{A|Vigilante}}, or a {{A|Juggernaut}} however. *In the later part of the game, you can play a risky route if there are obviously many killers and few {{A|Townies}}. In order to implement this strategy, you must have paid attention to who is likely to be a killing role and who they have targeted to kill. Often, the {{A|Mafia}} will target the most important {{A|Town}} roles first; in this case, act like a {{A|Vigilante}} (or other important role) who doesn't know how to play the game, and {{A|Transport}} yourself with possible members of the {{A|Mafia}}. The {{A|Mafia}} will try and fail to kill the '{{A|Vigilante}}'. If the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles are killing randomly, make yourself a target (without violating the [[Town of Salem]] etiquette or rules) by inciting confusion. Claim that [insert person's name here] is evil, claim multiple roles, be vague - since there are few {{A|Townies}}, there is little reason to vote you up - in addition, you may be the {{A|Jester}}! The {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}} will often try to kill you simply to get you out of the way - {{A|Transport}} yourself out of harm's way, and attempt to kill evil roles in the process. '''NOTE:''' This will not work against the {{A|Werewolf}}, the {{A|Pestilence}}, and the {{A|Ambusher}} as these roles can still kill you even if you {{A|Transport}} yourself since these roles can attack visitors (you visit yourself when {{A|Transporting}} yourself). *{{A|Transporting}} yourself with a killer except for the {{A|Werewolf}}/{{A|Pestilence}} and {{A|Ambusher}} will make them unable to kill you, since they cannot target themselves. If they are a {{A|Vigilante}}, {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Juggernaut}}, they'll kill themselves, and if they're an {{A|Arsonist}}, they'll {{A|douse}} themselves and you unlike in prior versions of the game, as you can no longer prevent an {{A|Arsonist}} from igniting. *Arguing and fighting is pretty common in heated [[Town of Salem]] games. Consider {{A|Transporting}} both sides of an argument with each other. It is pretty common that one or the other actually is a killer, so your chances of getting a self-attack are pretty good. **Keep in mind that one of them could be {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Vigilante}}, and that {{A|Transporting}} them could cause you/them to die unintentionally. **Investigative roles such as {{A|Sheriff}} tend to visit players that argue, so avoid doing this strategy if there's somebody in the game that claims to be a role that could gather information on one of the players by visiting them. *{{A|Transporting}} an {{A|Arsonist}} with their target causes them to {{A|douse}} themselves and you, forcing them to waste a {{A|Night}} to clean themselves. *If someone claims to be a {{A|Survivor}} (regardless of credibility), you can {{A|Transport}} yourself with the claimed {{A|Survivor}} so they will act as your human shield. The risk is that they may become a target of {{A|Vigilante}} and you may get shot in his/her place. When said person complains about being {{A|Transported}} the next {{A|Day}}, stop repeating the action in the following {{A|Night}} because any evil killer may target him/her to get rid of you. **If you know someone of high suspicion, after said person complains of being {{A|Transported}}, swap him/her with that suspicious target. Hopefully, the latter will be targeted by any evil killer instead. *If you're unsure who to {{A|Transport}}, it's usually a good idea to {{A|Transport}} yourself with someone who you suspect is evil or who seems unlikely to be attacked; you'll know with absolutely certainty that one half of the {{A|Transportation}} is a {{A|Townie}}, and the other half ''may'' be evil, which means you might get the {{A|Mafia}} to attack themselves. **Don't {{A|Transport}} yourself with someone who is ''confirmed'' as evil unless you're sure there's no {{A|Vigilante}}, since this could easily get you shot. **One drawback to this is that it makes it somewhat harder for you to confirm, since you're only showing the {{A|Transported}} message to one {{A|Townie}} instead of two, and you're deliberately aiming for someone who might be evil. *Although it rarely comes up, the {{A|Transporter}} will ''win'' automatically via auto-resolve one-on-one versus a {{A|Mafioso}}, rather than losing like you might expect; this is because the {{A|Transporter}} can {{A|Transport}} themselves with the {{A|Mafioso}} indefinitely and only one member of the {{A|Mafia}} left and you've identified them, since the {{A|Mafioso}} can only kill themselves in this situation, the stalemate detector will give {{A|Town}} the win. This is not the case for the {{A|Godfather}}, as you cannot make them kill themselves thanks to their Night immunity and the {{A|Mafia}} will ''win'' instead. *A potential strategy is to claim {{A|Transporter}} {{A|Day}} 1 and {{A|Transport}} yourself with others. This way, you produce a confirmed {{A|Town}} easily and you may then demand roles. Keep in mind, however, this will make you a target later on as you have to {{A|Transport}} more important players instead of yourself. (However, players may not believe your claim immediately. In this case, be patient. At least you have a confirmed {{A|Town}}.) Bear in mind that you may be accused of being a {{A|Hypnotist}} if {{A|Mafia}} are present, and this strategy is not recommended, especially in the case of an {{A|Ambusher}}. *If there is a {{A|Hypnotist}} in the game, do not {{A|Transport}} just yourself and somebody else, as you may be accused of being a {{A|Hypnotist}}, due to having the same investigation results and the fact that only one person confirmed {{A|Transportation}}, which a {{A|Hypnotist}} can only do. Avoid this by {{A|Transporting}} players other than yourself, to confirm yourself as {{A|Transporter}}. **Bear in mind however, that you may be accused of being the second {{A|Hypnotist}} if there is one in the graveyard, so {{A|Transport}} players other than yourself to clear yourself of any further suspicion. **{{A|Hypnotists}} will also claim that they {{A|Transported}} their {{A|Mafia}} allies, so avoid {{A|Transporting}} players that aren't confirmed and acting friendly to you, as this may be seen as two or more {{A|Mafia}} members collaborating. *If an {{A|Executioner}} wins and reveals themselves, {{A|Transport}} yourself or any important {{A|Townies}} with them. Killing roles usually won't target them, and they have permanent Basic defense, meaning only a handful of {{A|Neutral}} roles can kill them. *You can use {{A|Vigilantes}} that shot a {{A|Town}} member as a meat shield since they'll die anyway. === Who not to {{A|Transport}} === *If a {{A|Townie}} asks for "TP/LO" to be on them, '''DO NOT TRANSPORT THEM!''' They are not asking for a {{A|Transporter}}; rather, they are asking for a {{A|Town Protective}} and a {{A|Lookout}} to guard and watch them in case an evil role tries to target them. If you {{A|Transport}} them, chances are you will accidentally {{A|Transport}} them with an evil role's target, which will kill them. *While it might appear that {{A|Transporting}} early is harmful, you should always {{A|Transport}} as early as possible to confirm your existence. If your actions appear to be causing chaos, for example, a {{A|Town Investigative}} is claiming to check one of your targets, you should almost always come out and clear the confusion. *'''Do not {{A|Transport}} the revealed {{A|Mayor}} or {{A|Jailor}} when {{A|Town Protective}} roles are around''', as you might {{A|Transport}} them into a target being attacked (and not protected). This results in an important {{A|Townie}} dying needlessly. *Make certain to be wary of the {{A|Veteran}}. If you attempt to {{A|Transport}} him while he is on alert, you will be shot. Additionally, everyone who visited your other target will visit the {{A|Veteran}} instead and vice-versa. *The {{A|Vigilante}} is very dangerous to you; if you've identified a role as evil, there's a good chance the {{A|Vigilante}} has, too. This means that if you {{A|Transport}} a confirmed evil role with a {{A|Townie}} (or with yourself), you could accidentally cause the {{A|Vigilante}} to shoot an innocent person. **In particular, if you suspect the {{A|Town}} has a {{A|Vigilante}}, you may want to avoid {{A|Transporting}} yourself with someone who was ''almost'' hanged the {{A|Night}} after the hang failed; {{A|Vigilantes}} often take a risk and shoot people who seemed hard to hang in hopes of identifying the entire {{A|Mafia}} based on the people who failed to vote for them. Always try to check with the {{A|Vigilante}} to make sure who they are shooting. *The {{A|Plaguebearer}} might be your worst enemy, as an {{A|Infected}} {{A|Transporter}} can help the {{A|Plaguebearer}} spread the {{A|Plague}} and evolve into {{A|Pestilence}} much sooner. Attempting to {{A|Transport}} yourself in an attempt to protect yourself when {{A|Pestilence}} is around will very likely be a death sentence for you, as you may die to their rampage attacks or by visiting them. *If it seems like a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} has the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role pinned down, be cautious about {{A|Transporting}} people, since you could accidentally {{A|Transport}} the killer and free them to kill. This is not a danger if they're being jailed by the {{A|Jailor}}, since you are unable to {{A|Transport}} someone who was jailed. *If you suspect a {{A|Crusader}} is guarding you do not {{A|Transport}} yourself as you will die to the {{A|Crusader}}. *If you reveal yourself when {{A|Random Mafia}} are not confirmed, you run the risk of dying to an {{A|Ambusher}} if you {{A|Transport}} yourself. This is because {{A|Transporting}} yourself counts as a visit to yourself, allowing the {{A|Ambusher}} to ambush you visiting yourself, so make sure the {{A|Random Mafia}} is confirmed to not have an {{A|Ambusher}} before {{A|Transporting}} yourself. **If you know someone is likely to be healed by a {{A|Doctor}}, swapping them will cause the {{A|Doctor}} to save you if the {{A|Ambusher}} attacks you. ===Gathering information=== Take notes in your {{A|Last Will}} when you witness certain things at {{A|Night}}: *If one of your targets was jailed, you will receive a message and the {{A|Transport}} will fail. If the {{A|Jailor's}} {{A|Last Will}} is lacking, your information can help. *If one of your targets is killed, you can be fairly sure your other target is '''not''' the culprit, since no killer can attack themselves. (Except the {{A|Werewolf}}, but if you {{A|Transported}} the {{A|Werewolf's}} target, you would die.) **If one of your targets is killed by the {{A|Mafia}}, your other target probably isn't a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, since the {{A|Mafia}} can't attack their own members. **In all these cases, a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}} or another {{A|Transporter}} could potentially have forced your target to attack themselves (or a member of the {{A|Mafia}} to hit a fellow member of the {{A|Mafia}}); however, it is fairly rare for these things to happen at the same time. Make sure to be wary of controlling roles that could mess up your conclusions. **However, make sure not to blindly trust this person either, as they could still be another evil role. Just because you have identified someone as "not {{A|Mafia}}" doesn't mean they couldn't still be a {{A|Serial Killer}} or an {{A|Arsonist}}. *If someone claims to be role blocked or controlled every {{A|Night}}, try {{A|Transporting}} yourself with them. You will become the target instead of them. Since you are immune to both role blocks and controls, you will know what would have happened to your target without being affected yourself. **You may especially need to do this if a {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Witch}} has the {{A|Jailor}} pinned down, as {{A|Transporting}} the {{A|Jailor}} away from the {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Witch}} will free them up to execute someone. **Obviously, don't {{A|Transport}} them if there were no kills by the {{A|Mafia}} last {{A|Night}}, since they might be the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role and {{A|Transporting}} them away from the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} might be freeing them up to kill someone. *Pay attention to who responds to a {{A|Transport}} by complaining, and who remains silent. Evil roles are more likely to remain silent, both to avoid calling attention to themselves and because they would want {{A|Sheriffs}} who investigated them to believe any altered reading they got; conversely, innocent roles are more likely to announce having been {{A|Transported}} to avoid being mistaken for an evil role they were swapped with. *Always, always, always note down all your {{A|Transports}} in your {{A|Last Will}}. If you've been publicly revealed as a {{A|Transporter}}, consider revealing them every morning, too. Generally speaking, the information is far more useful to the {{A|Town}} (who have many {{A|Investigators}} and who can correct their information once they know who was {{A|Transported}} with whom) than they are to evil roles (who have many killers, which can't be corrected after the fact). **Similarly, it is ''extremely'' important for the {{A|Transporter}} to reveal as soon as it looks like one of your {{A|Transports}} has put an innocent person under suspicion; this will not only absolve the innocent suspect, but direct the {{A|Town}} to who they should target instead... and you can protect yourself, so you lose little by revealing. Failing to reveal in that situation can have catastrophic consequences, since not only will the innocent {{A|Townie}} get hung, but the {{A|Town Investigative}} role who accused them will likely fall under suspicion. ===When to reveal=== *A less than obvious advantage to the {{A|Transporter}} is that they can prove themselves as a {{A|Townie}} relatively easily, since {{A|Transporting}} people produces so many messages, and no other role can produce the same messages (with the notable exception of a {{A|Hypnotist}}); posting your {{A|Last Will}} with a record of your {{A|Transportation}} is generally enough to get you confirmed. The ability to confirm yourself as a {{A|Townie}} whenever you want is very powerful; but don't just wait until the last moment to use it. *In addition to being easy to confirm, you have the ability (unique among other {{A|Town}} roles) to protect yourself indefinitely by {{A|Transporting}} yourself. This further increases the advantage of revealing your role, since the {{A|Mafia}} will be unable to target you (unless they have an {{A|Ambusher}}). {{A|Transporters}} can take advantage of this to play whisper games, asking people for their roles and other information. It does have the drawback that if you're defending yourself constantly, you won't be able to protect others; but you still ''can'', it's just a matter of guessing what the {{A|Mafia}} will do. *Always reveal immediately when you suspect one of your prior targets that have been {{A|Transported}} are causing innocent {{A|Townies}} to be accused, or possible guilty ones to be overlooked. *You should also consider revealing late in the game if there are already several confirmed {{A|Townies}}; this will place more pressure on the {{A|Mafia}} and make it easier for {{A|Town Investigative}} roles and {{A|Tavern Keepers}} to find them. ===Dealing with {{A|Transporters}}=== {{A|Transporters}} are particularly a nuisance to evils, as they are easily confirmed other than being accused of being a {{A|Hypnotist}} or {{A|Forger}}, and can easily make the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} attack themselves. *Be careful of who you might think the {{A|Transporter}} is going to {{A|Transport}}, for example, the {{A|Jailor}}, and do not attack them, as you will most likely be {{A|Transported}} away, never mind the {{A|Town Protectives}} on the {{A|Jailor}}. Try to outsmart the {{A|Transporter}} and target those the {{A|Transporter}} will avoid, or target the {{A|transporter's}} second target so your attack is {{A|Transported}} onto the {{A|Town}} role you want to eliminate. *If the {{A|Transporter}} is {{A|Transporting}} themselves all the time, carry on attack as normal, as you still have a chance of accidentally killing the {{A|Transporter}} rather than zero chance by targeting the {{A|Transporter}} themselves. Generally, try to think ahead of them. **If you're an {{A|Ambusher}}, you can even target them directly to kill them with no risk to yourself. The same applies for the {{A|Werewolf}} and {{A|Pestilence}}. *As {{A|Medusa}}, you can use some common {{A|Veteran}} strategies to bait the {{A|Transporter}} into {{A|Transporting}} you while {{A|Stone Gazing}}. You will also automatically win in an auto-resolve one-on-one against them. *In the first few {{A|Days}} of each game, {{A|Transporters}} are generally a low priority, as the chance of {{A|Transporting}} you onto your teammate's is low. Focus on killing them later in the Game, as they can turn the game around within killing your teammate. Bear in mind that the {{A|Transporter}} wins in a stalemate against the {{A|Mafioso}}, as they cannot be hit if they continue {{A|Transporting}} both players. *As an {{A|Executioner}}, if the {{A|Transporter}} made the {{A|Mafia}} kill one of their own members, then you can claim {{A|Medium}} and accuse your target of being a {{A|Hypnotist}} who collaborated with a {{A|Forger}}, in an attempt to get them hanged. You can also do this while claiming {{A|Spy}} as well. *It might be worth considering leaving a {{A|Transporter}} alive, as they can mess up the {{A|Town Investigative}} results, especially if there is more than one {{A|Transporter}}. Try to stay out of their way and let them interfere with others. You can always try to trick them on who you are going to attack, and work the {{A|Transporter}}’s ability to your advantage. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{TransporterAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{TransporterMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.10}}, a {{A|Transporter}} could {{A|Transport}} someone with themselves, giving them 2 {{A|Transport}} messages and for sure confirming the existence of a {{A|Transporter}} without messing up vital investigative roles. **If attempted after the fix, the action will not go through. The {{A|Transporter}} will see the following message: "''You cannot {{A|Transport}} someone with themselves. Please make another selection.''" ***Since the switch to Unity, the {{A|Transporter's}} targeting UI was changed so this message no longer appears. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6501}}, a {{A|Transporter}} could stop an {{A|Arsonist}} from incinerating their targets and could {{A|Transport}} the haunt of a {{A|Jester}} onto another player, even if they voted innocent. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.3.0}}, the {{A|Transporter}} was the only role that could be seen by a {{A|Tracker}} visiting 2 targets. ***Several other roles, such as {{A|Witch}} and {{A|Necromancer}}, can select two targets, but only visit one of their targets, usually their first target. Transporter Scroll.png|{{A|Transporter}} {{A|Scroll}}|alt=Transporter Scroll Transporter Lesser Scroll.png|[[Scrolls (ToS)|Lesser]] {{A|Transporter}} {{A|Scroll}} *When looking at {{A|Scrolls}} and [[Scrolls (ToS)#Lesser Scrolls|lesser scrolls]], the {{A|Transporter}} is the only role that has their icon different from the actual role icon found during gameplay. It appears to have a "hand-drawn" style. *The {{A|Transporter}} is derived from SC2 Mafia's Bus Driver role. *The {{A|Transporter}} was once mistaken as a {{A|Town Protective}} due to the [https://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/viewtopic.php?f=9&t=11869&p=277880&hilit=transporter+town+protective#p277880 typo] on the {{A|Transporter's}} role card. ==History== *{{VH|3.3.11}} **Fixed {{A|Transporter}} not being notified when they're controlled by a {{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Witch}} *{{VH|3.3.0}} **When {{A|Transporting}} a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, the second target buttons are no longer improperly labeled "Reveal”. *{{VH|3.2.5}} **Fixed the "{{A|Transport}}" button labels which were being populated with improper text. *{{VH|3.2.4}} **{{A|Transporter}} now uses in-place secondary targeting rather than a slide-out secondary menu. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Added {{A|Medusa}} vs. {{A|Transporter}} [[stalemate]] detector. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Transporter's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Transporter.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Transporter's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Transporter Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **Revealed {{A|Mayors}} can no longer be healed by a {{A|Doctor}} if {{A|Transported}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Jester}} haunt can no longer be {{A|Transported}} by a {{A|Transporter}}. *{{VH|1.5.10.4747}} **{{A|Transporter}} can no longer select a player to be both targets for their {{A|Transport}}. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Перевозчик]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Town Support roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Roleblock Immune]] [[Category:Control Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== ===Basics=== *Check a target each {{A|Night}}. If they are a {{A|Vampire}}, you will deal a {{A|Basic Attack}} against them. *You have {{A|Basic Defense}} against {{A|Vampires}}. *If a {{A|Vampire}} attempts to convert you, you will stake them and will not be harmed. This will happen even if you are [[roleblocked|role blocked]]. *If you attempt to stake a {{A|Vampire}} who is being protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}, both you and the {{A|Bodyguard}} will die. *If you check a person who is visited by a {{A|Vampire}}, you cannot stop a possible conversion, nor will you kill the visiting {{A|Vampire}}. *You can read the {{A|Vampire chat}} during the {{A|night}}. *There will always be at least one {{A|Vampire}} in the game if there is a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} at the beginning of the game. ===Turning into a {{A|Vigilante}}=== *Once all {{A|Vampires}} are dead, you will become a {{A|Vigilante}}. However, multiple things are changed: **You only have one bullet instead of three. **You are permanently stuck as a {{A|Vigilante}}. This means if an {{A|Amnesiac}} becomes a {{A|Vampire}} or a {{A|Necromancer}} uses a dead {{A|Vampire}} to convert someone, you will not turn back into a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. *Similar to a {{A|Plaguebearer}} or {{A|Mafioso}}, you will become a {{A|Vigilante}} during the {{A|Day}} if the last {{A|Vampire}} is [[hanged]]. ==Strategy== *If you become a {{A|Vigilante}}, follow the strategies on the {{A|Vigilante}} page, but remember that you only have one bullet. *Check down the list, and then if you end up checking everyone, check them all again. They might have been turned since you checked them, perhaps even ''as'' you were checking them. *If the {{A|Vampires}} are talking, pay attention to what they are saying. {{A|Vampires}} may lie to fool you since the worst they can generally accomplish is making you waste your visits. **If they mention that someone is immune to their bite, it's most likely true. Write it down in your {{A|Last Will}}, but remember that calling them out reveals you as well. **If the {{A|Vampires}} argue over who to convert or discuss their victims, this can often reveal who they've turned into a {{A|Vampire}}. This is a much more common mistake than you would think, since {{A|Vampires}} need to vote on who to convert. Pay attention to what they say; even if they don't name exact names, you can often figure out what they're arguing over based on context. Be wary of possible baits that the {{A|Vampires}} may say to waste your visit on checking someone. **Try to figure out talking {{A|Vampires}} by comparing their writing style to that of players during the {{A|Day}}. Pay attention to the usage of emoticons, word capitalization, spelling, ETC. **If the {{A|Vampires}} stop talking after several {{A|nights}} of discussions, it may mean that there is only one {{A|Vampire}} left or they want to trick you. **Scum reading is one of the most important things to do as this role. You have plenty of opportunities to do so, remember to take advantage of it. If words only one or two players in the match use, such as 'Lit', show up in the {{A|Vampire chat}}, try staking them. It'll often turn out they were a {{A|Vampire}}. **Try to figure out who the {{A|Vampires}} are most likely to turn, such as revealed {{A|Mayors}} without {{A|Bodyguards}} on them. ***You can whisper a revealed {{A|Mayor}} during the day to see if they have been converted. **Look over the list of people to convert on the {{A|Vampire}} page, and follow that yourself when deciding who to investigate. **{{A|Vampires}} can only convert roles without {{A|Defense}}. If you suspect someone falls into any of these categories, skip them. Even if it's not true, they're less likely to be {{A|Vampires}}, since the {{A|Vampires}} will probably have reached the same conclusion as you and avoided visiting them. **Anyone who was confirmed as a {{A|Townie}} could be possibly converted by a {{A|Vampire}}, especially if they are an important role, so leave no stone unturned. **{{A|Jesters}}, {{A|Survivors}}, and {{A|Amnesiacs}} are the only {{A|Neutral}} roles that can be converted into {{A|Vampires}}. It is generally unwise to attempt to convert these roles as they can already be the {{A|Vampire}}'s ally. Targeting players who are confirmed {{A|Townies}} is almost always the best decision. *If a revealed {{A|Mayor}} has only one vote and can whisper or is receiving whispers, this means they've been turned into a {{A|Vampire}}. (However, in this case, the {{A|Town}} will often notice and [[hang]] them for you, so you will not have to stake them) Conversely, as long as the {{A|Mayor}} has three votes, and can't send or receive whispers, they are not a {{A|Vampire}}. A good way to always be sure is attempting to whisper to the {{A|Mayor}} during each start of the day. If you successfully whisper to them, then they were converted into a {{A|Vampire}}. *Pay particular attention to the {{A|Last Wills}} of {{A|Lookouts}}. Anyone who was visited by a confirmed {{A|Vampire}} may have been converted into a {{A|Vampire}}. (And if you are ''certain'' the visit was when the visitor was already a {{A|Vampire}} and they weren't turned into a {{A|Vampire}} themselves, then they are likely evil and should be called out.) *Try and bait {{A|Vampires}} in: **"I hate my role, can a {{A|Vampire}} convert/bite me?" sometimes works, although experienced players may suspect you to be a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, in which case they are less likely to attempt to bite you. **Claiming {{A|Survivor}} or acting like a {{A|Jester}} can occasionally lure a {{A|Vampire}} into trying to bite you. However, it carries a high risk of getting you [[hanged]] by the {{A|Town}}, executed by the {{A|Jailor}}, or shot by a {{A|Vigilante}}. Therefore, this is best saved until near the end of the game when it's possible evil roles are near a majority. ***Claiming {{A|Survivor}} near the very last {{A|night}} (ideally at the very end of the {{A|Day}} when there's not enough time for you to be [[hanged]]) can sometimes swing a {{A|Town}} victory by luring the {{A|Vampires}} to convert you while making the {{A|Mafia}} ignore you and target the {{A|Vampires}} instead, hopefully turning you into a {{A|Vigilante}} in time to swing the game with your final bullet. **Claiming Medium {{A|Day 1}} and asking for dead players to not leave can lure a Vampire into trying to bite you. You appear town-aligned without sounding overly forced, unlike more suspicious {{A|Day 1}} town claim such as {{A|Investigator}} which has little reason to claim {{A|Day 1}}. **Remember that this may have the opposite effect, as an {{A|Investigator}} may visit you and 'confirm' you as a {{A|Survivor}}, which may make the {{A|Vampires}} not attempt to bite you, as you are already their ally, and they may waste a {{A|night}} biting you when you use a vest. ***A {{A|Consigliere}} may pose as an {{A|Executioner}} claiming {{A|Investigator}} to get you killed, as even if you can get rid of a huge threat to the {{A|Mafia}}, you are still a {{A|Townie}}. *A {{A|Bodyguard}} will kill you (and you will kill them) if you visit a {{A|Vampire}} they're protecting. However, in this case, whoever you were trying to stake is confirmed as a {{A|Vampire}} (since {{A|Vampire Hunters}} cannot attack non-{{A|Vampires}}). Always list your visits in your {{A|Last Will}}, especially your most recent one, so people will know who the {{A|Vampire}} is in that situation. **Unless, of course, the person that you targeted was transported, in which case the vampire is the person who they were transported with. *A {{A|Doctor}} can heal {{A|Vampires}} you tried to stake. If you get a message saying you staked a {{A|Vampire}} who visited you, but no {{A|Vampire}} shows up dead the next {{A|Day}}, it means a {{A|Doctor}} accidentally healed a {{A|Vampire}}. You may want to reveal to alert the {{A|Town}} to this, though most {{A|Doctors}} will be reluctant to reveal themselves just to expose a {{A|Vampire}}. You could also try targeting the {{A|Vampire}} again (assuming you targeted them rather than them visiting you). However, the {{A|Doctor}} may heal them a second time. **On the other hand, if you reveal that a {{A|Vampire}} has been healed, the {{A|Doctor}} is much less likely to heal them for another {{A|night}}. **Note that the {{A|Doctor}} does not get a ''"target was attacked"'' message when saving a {{A|Vampire}} from your attack, this is a bug. *When you become a {{A|Vigilante}}, consider not revealing this fact until you use your bullet. While {{A|Vampire Hunters}} are harmless to everyone but {{A|Vampires}}, {{A|Vigilantes}} present a direct threat to the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven}}, all of which will hunt for you as soon as they know your new role. You may not want to shoot right away, so it's better to lull evil roles into thinking you are still a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. However, if a {{A|Consigliere}}, {{A|Potion Master}}, or {{A|Investigator}} checked you and it became public, shoot the next {{A|night}}. *Remember that your ultimate goal is for the {{A|Town}} to win, not simply to kill the {{A|Vampires}}. This means that under some circumstances (when you need the {{A|Vampires}}' votes in order to keep the {{A|Mafia}} from getting a majority), you might be better off waiting to kill confirmed {{A|Vampires}}. *{{A|Vampires}} will occasionally try to be "merciful" by biting surviving {{A|Townies}} so everyone can win together. You can exploit this kindness to eliminate them even when outnumbered four-to-one. Since there is a maximum of four {{A|Vampires}}, they'll have to [[hang]] one of their own and reduce their numbers to three to free up a spot to convert you. If you then stake anyone other than the youngest on the {{A|night}} they attempt to convert you, you can eliminate two {{A|Vampires}} in one {{A|night}}, leaving the last one remaining without the majority needed to [[hang]] you and letting you stake them on the following {{A|night}}. Note that this requires both knowing what {{A|night}} they'll attempt to convert you and either luck or knowledge of who the youngest {{A|Vampire}} is; if you're planning to use this strategy, you might want to discreetly probe for that information. **If the existence of a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} is confirmed, whether by you killing a {{A|Vampire}} or it being guaranteed in the role list, this becomes impossible unless a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Medusa}} successfully used their ability, as they will realize that based on the graveyard, you must be the {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. ***If a player was {{A|Cleaned}} or {{A|Stoned}}, the {{A|Vampires}} are still likely to be hesitant to give mercy if your existence was previously confirmed. Having a fake claim can help, but still remains extremely difficult. *If someone claims a {{A|Town Investigative}} role and makes an accusation against someone that turns out to be incorrect, ''but'' the target is actually someone with {{A|Basic Defense}}, it is very likely that the accuser was a {{A|Vampire}} who incorrectly guessed at their target's role because they were unable to turn them with a bite. You should generally try and stake the accuser the next {{A|night}}. *If you are in the {{A|Mafia}}, it may be worth letting {{A|Vampire Hunters}} survive. After all, {{A|Vampires}} are a large threat to {{A|Mafia}}. However, you must careful not to let the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} turn into a {{A|Vigilante}} and shoot you. **If you are a {{A|Consigliere}} and find a {{A|Vampire}}, it may be beneficial in the long run to whisper the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} the name of the {{A|Vampire}}, but don’t be upfront about your role, unless you already have a solid claim as {{A|Investigator}}. *Note that {{A|Vampire Hunter}} is not a unique role; while it is somewhat rarer than other roles due to the fact that it requires {{A|Vampires}}, it's as common as any other once you know {{A|Vampires}} are present. In particular, this means that you ''shouldn't'' necessarily be suspicious of other {{A|Vampire Hunter}} claims, provided they fit the role list. **On the other hand, you can sometimes catch fake {{A|Vampire Hunters}} based on when you turn into a {{A|Vigilante}} since they should change at the same time - if there's another {{A|Vampire Hunter}} claim, try asking them if the {{A|Vampires}} are all dead yet or not. If you do change roles, and there's a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} claim you're uncertain about, try waiting to see if they say something first. *You should always try to pair up with any {{A|Lookouts}}. This can make an easy and powerful combo in finding {{A|Vampires}}. The {{A|Lookout}} should watch people who the {{A|Vampires}} are likely to convert and you can stake suspicious people. This way, if someone you suspect being a {{A|Vampire}} visit the {{A|Lookout}}’s target, it’s likely you have got two confirmed {{A|Vampires}}. *Claiming to be a {{A|Survivor}} may work to prevent the {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Neutral Killing}} from killing you, especially if an {{A|Investigator}} investigates you and publicly reveals your results. However, you may end up being killed by a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}}, as evil roles tend to claim {{A|Survivor}}, or you may be [[hanged]] by the {{A|Town}}. **If you are voted up or are {{A|Jailed}}, reveal your role. The {{A|Vampires}} will know who you are and avoid you, and also refrain from using the {{A|Vampire chat}}, but it's better than losing a {{A|Townie}}, especially one that can effectively deal with {{A|Vampires}}. In the case of a {{A|Jailor}}, it's even safer to reveal, as only the {{A|Jailor}} will know who you are. Even if they get bitten, if they choose to share it with the other {{A|Vampires}} through the {{A|Vampire chat}}, you'll be able to stake them. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{VampireHunterAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{VampireHunterMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0}}, {{A|Vampire Hunters}} had {{A|Death Notes}}. This allowed them to be easily confirmed by revealing who they are in their {{A|Death Note}}. *If an {{A|Amnesiac}} becomes a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, they will remain a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} for the rest of the game, unless another {{A|Amnesiac}} becomes a {{A|Vampire}} and dies. This may be a bug. *There was a bug where the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} was referred to as a [[unique role]] and was unable to be remembered by an {{A|Amnesiac}}. *While {{A|Jailed}}, a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} could stake any {{A|Vampires}} who attempted to convert them. *{{A|Vampire Hunter}} is commonly mistaken as a [[Unique Role]] because it requires {{A|Vampires}}, and usually only one {{A|Vampire Hunter}} appears in a {{A|Vampire}} game. *{{A|Vampires}} who have left the game are considered dead when the game decides whether or not to make you become a {{A|Vigilante}} even if the {{A|Vampire}} who left didn't actually die yet. ==History== *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.2.4]] **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *[[Version_History (ToS)|3.1.13]] **Fixed the Chat filter potentially showing misleading information to {{A|Vampire Hunters}}. **For the {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, {{A|Vampire chat}} now has a unique style. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Vampire Hunter's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Vampire Hunter.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Vampire Hunter's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Vampire Hunter Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.5.1.10655]] **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *[[Version_History (ToS)|2.0]] **{{A|Vampire Hunters}} no longer have a {{A|Death Note}}. *[[Version_History (ToS)|1.3.0]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Охотник на вампиров]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Town Killing roles]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]
