'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== ===Basics=== *You may VOTE to bite someone each {{A|Night}}. If you successfully convert someone, you must wait another {{A|Night}} before biting again. **Only {{A|Townies}} (aside from {{A|Vampire Hunter}}), {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} and {{A|Jesters}} can be converted. ***If the target is not any of these roles, or you have four (or more in the case of an {{A|Amnesiac}}) {{A|Vampires}}, they will be delivered a [[Basic Attack]] instead. **You do not have to wait a {{A|Night}} after converting a 4th member. As soon as there are 4 {{A|Vampires}} alive, the youngest {{A|Vampire}} can deal a [[Abilities (ToS)|Basic Attack]] immediately the following night. *The youngest {{A|Vampire}} will always visit the selected target for conversion. The selected target is decided at random from all targets voted on by a {{A|Vampire}}; it is not a democratic vote. For example, if two {{A|Vampires}} vote for Samuel Sewall and one {{A|Vampire}} votes for Jonathan Corwin, then Samuel Sewall has a 2/3 chance and Jonathan Corwin has a 1/3 chance to be bitten that evening. *You can only convert players that have no {{A|Defense}}. Biting members of the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Coven}}, a {{A|Witch}} (without {{A|defense}}), a {{A|Guardian Angel}}, a {{A|Pirate}}, or any roles with no {{A|defense}} after you have four or more {{A|Vampires}} alive will result in you killing them instead. In turn, you will be able to bite again in this case the next {{A|Night}}. *If you bite the {{A|Godfather}}, a {{A|Witch}} (with {{A|defense}}), or a {{A|Neutral Killing}}, they will be unharmed, but you can bite again the next {{A|Night}}. *If you attempt to convert a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, they will attack you and be unharmed. **{{A|Vampire Hunters}} will appear as targets with {{A|defense}} if you try to convert them. *'''ALL''' {{A|Vampires}} will see who was visited (and thereby bitten) by the youngest {{A|Vampire}} even if one of them was controlled by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}. **For Example, if the Vampires all voted to bite Deodat Lawson, the message "The Vampires visited Deodat Lawson last {{A|Night}}." will be shown to all {{A|Vampires}}. *{{A|Crusaders}} are unable to kill you, but will prevent your target from being converted into a {{A|Vampire}}. *{{A|Ambushers}} '''CAN''' kill you, but they cannot prevent your target from being converted into a {{A|Vampire}}. *If {{A|Vampires}} try to bite a player with {{A|defense}} that was {{A|jailed}}, the {{A|Vampires}} will still be notified about the player’s {{A|defense}} despite their ability failing because of the {{A|jail}}. This is a bug. {| class="wikitable" !Bite Effect !Affected [[Roles (ToS)|Role]] |- !rowspan="4"|Conversion |All {{A|Townies}} (when not using a form of {{A|Defense}}) except {{A|Vampire Hunter}} |- |{{A|Survivor}} when not using a vest |- |{{A|Amnesiac}} |- |{{A|Jester}} |- !rowspan="6"|Basic Attack |All members of the {{A|Mafia}} except the {{A|Godfather}} |- |All members of the {{A|Coven}}M |- |{{A|Guardian Angel}} |- |{{A|Pirate}} |- |{{A|Witch}} after they lose their {{A|Basic Defense}} |- |Any role with no {{A|Defense}} after {{A|Vampires}} have four members |- !rowspan="10"|Immune/No Effect |{{A|Veteran}} when on alert1 |- |{{A|Vampire Hunter}}1 |- |Anyone being protected by a {{A|Town Protective}}2, {{A|Jailor}}, {{A|Guardian Angel}}, or {{A|Potion Master}} |- |{{A|Bodyguard}} using their bullet-proof vest |- |{{A|Doctor}} using their self heal |- |{{A|Survivor}} using a vest |- |{{A|Witch}} while still having {{A|Basic Defense}} |- |Other {{A|Vampires}} |- |{{A|Coven Leader}} wielding the {{A|Necronomicon}} |- |Any [[Roles (ToS)|Role]] with {{A|Defense}}3 |} 1 In addition, this role will kill the youngest {{A|Vampire}}.[[File:Bat.png|thumb|The promotion picture for a {{A|Vampire}} in Bat form]] 2 If the {{A|Town Protective}} is a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|trapper}}, they will kill the youngest {{A|Vampire}}. {{A|Crusaders}} and {{A|Doctors}} will only prevent conversion along with other attacks. Other visitors can be attacked however by a {{A|Crusader}}. 3 If the immune target is {{A|Pestilence}} or a {{A|Werewolf}} staying home, they will kill the youngest {{A|Vampire}}. Other roles with {{A|Defense}} will only be notified that someone attacked them. {{A|Arsonists}} and the {{A|Plaguebearer}} will know who attacked them due to their passive ability. M A {{A|Medusa}} who is using a {{A|Stone Gaze}} on the {{A|Night}} they were bitten will die along with the youngest {{A|Vampire}} being {{A|stoned}}. ===How {{A|Vampires}} Affect Other Roles=== *A {{A|Vampire}} bite acts as a conversion. If the target cannot be converted, they will deal a {{A|Basic Attack}} to the target. The bite and conversion will fail if: **The target has {{A|Basic Defense}}/was healed by a {{A|Doctor}}. The {{A|Vampires}} will receive a notification of the target having defense. **The target was killed by another role (if conversion was possible), There is no notification for the {{A|Vampires}} in this case, except the number of {{A|Vampires}} not increasing. **The target was protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}. Additionally, the {{A|Bodyguard}} and youngest {{A|Vampire}} will attack each other. **The target was an alerted {{A|Veteran}}. Additionally, the {{A|Veteran}} will kill the youngest {{A|Vampire}}. **The target is already a {{A|Vampire}} (a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, or {{A|Transporter}} interfered). Nothing happens. ** The target was jailed by the {{A|Jailor}}. As usual, the {{A|Vampires}} will receive a message that their target was jailed. ** The youngest {{A|Vampire}} was [[Role block|role blocked]]. The {{A|Vampires}} will '''not''' see who was visited in this case. *Additionally, the following roles have special protections: **The {{A|Witch}} cannot be converted, but their mystical barrier will not function as if they had a form of {{A|Defense}} (you will not get a {{A|Defense}} message). You can use this to identify the {{A|Witch}} in {{A|Dracula's Palace}} or certain [[Custom Mode|Custom]] role-lists. **The {{A|Vampire Hunter}} cannot be converted, will not die, and will attack the {{A|Vampire}} instead. **If the target was a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or the {{A|Coven}} and lacked {{A|Basic Defense}}, they will die instead of being converted. Additionally, if it was a {{A|Medusa}} using a {{A|Stone Gaze}}, the youngest {{A|Vampire}} will die. * Visiting or being visited by a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} will cause you to die from being staked. **Visiting a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} when they are role blocked will ''not'' prevent the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} from killing the youngest {{A|Vampire}}. **Visiting the same target the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} visits on the same {{A|Night}} will ''not'' have the youngest {{A|Vampire}} nor the target killed by the {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. **If a {{A|Bodyguard}} protects a {{A|Vampire}} and that {{A|Vampire}} is visited by a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, the {{A|Bodyguard}} will kill the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} (and die in the process). Note that, provided either of them kept up-to-date {{A|Last Wills}}, this will usually make the {{A|Vampire's}} identity obvious as the {{A|Bodyguard's}} and {{A|Vampire Hunter's}} target HAS to be a {{A|Vampire}}. *If a revealed {{A|Mayor}} is converted into a {{A|Vampire}}, they may be easily exposed as their vote will only count as 1 instead of 3. A converted {{A|Mayor}} can also receive [[whispers]], and everyone else can see this. *If a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} eliminates all {{A|Vampires}}, they will turn into a {{A|Vigilante}} with 1 bullet. Should an {{A|Amnesiac}} remember that they are a {{A|Vampire}}, the {{A|Vigilante}} will not turn back into a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}. They will also be able to be converted into a {{A|Vampire}}. *An {{A|Amnesiac}} can exceed the maximum amount of 4 {{A|Vampires}} by remembering as one when 4 exist. **If there used to be 5 {{A|Vampires}} alive due to an {{A|Amnesiac}} and one of the other {{A|Vampires}} died, the living {{A|Vampires}} will still be able to convert someone and have 5 members again, despite there being 4 {{A|Vampires}} alive. *If a {{A|Vigilante}} is converted ''the same {{A|Night}}'' they shoot a {{A|Townie}}, they will ''not'' die of guilt. **However, if the {{A|Vigilante}} is bitten the {{A|Night}} ''after'' they shoot a {{A|Townie}}, they ''will'' die of guilt and will not be converted or shown as a {{A|Vampire}}. *If an {{A|Amnesiac}} is bitten by a {{A|Vampire}} the same {{A|Night}} they try to remember a role, they will become a {{A|Vampire}}. The bite has a higher priority. *If an {{A|Executioner's}} target is converted into a {{A|Vampire}}, the {{A|Executioner}} will remain as his current role with the same target, and will still win if that {{A|Vampire}} is hanged. They can technically be a help to the {{A|Town}}, ironically, since their target was originally a {{A|Townie}}. *If a member of the {{A|Mafia}} other than the {{A|Godfather}}, or a member of the {{A|Coven}} other than the {{A|Coven Leader}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}}) is bitten, they will die. This does not count as a conversion, so the {{A|Vampires}} can attack again the next {{A|Night}}. *If a {{A|Retributionist}} is converted, they will still see what corpses they used. * Strangely, if a {{A|Transporter}} forces a {{A|Vampire}} to bite another {{A|Vampire}}, there is no message for either party. The {{A|Vampire}} will not receive a message, and the bitten {{A|Vampire}} does not receive a message informing them that they were attacked. The next {{A|Night}}, the {{A|Vampires}} may bite again. *If a {{A|Vampire}} is controlled by a {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, then different things will happen depending on what {{A|Night}} it is. **If the youngest {{A|Vampire}} is controlled on a {{A|Night}} that they cannot convert others, the youngest {{A|Vampire}} can be detected by a {{A|Lookout}} and die to the {{A|Werewolf}}. If any of the other alive {{A|Vampires}} are controlled, none of the {{A|Vampires}} will be detected by the {{A|Lookout}} or die to a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Werewolf}}. **If any of the {{A|Vampires}} are controlled on a {{A|Night}} when conversion is possible, they are forced to bite their target. The youngest {{A|Vampire}} will still be the one visiting the second target. *If a {{A|Jailor}} is converted, the {{A|Jailor}} will have access to a {{A|Death Note}} as a {{A|Vampire}}. *If a {{A|Vampire}} bites a {{A|Vampire}}, whether due to {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}}/{{A|Coven Leader}}, the attacked {{A|Vampire}} will be unharmed. ==Strategy== ===Which Roles to Convert & Not to Convert=== *The most important thing is to find targets you can convert, and to avoid ones you can't. Never try to bite anyone you suspect of having permanent {{A|Defense}}, such as a {{A|Serial Killer}}. * Your highest priority are semi-confirmed {{A|Townies}} that cannot visibly confirm themselves, such as the {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Spy}}, {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Lookout}}, {{A|Doctor}}, and {{A|Bodyguard}}. They can lead remaining {{A|Townies}} to false direction. However, if your target is fully confirmed, it is not in your best interest to bite them, as they probably have {{A|Town Protective}} roles or {{A|Lookouts}} on them. Additionally, if the {{A|Lookout}} discovers that a {{A|Vampire}} visited their target (if they hanged the visiting {{A|Vampire}}), then they can instruct a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or the {{A|Jailor}} to role block the potential youngest. A similar effect can happen with an {{A|Ambusher}} and a {{A|Bootlegger}}. *Around the transition to the late game, it may be helpful to convert semi-confirmed roles such as a {{A|Transporter}}. If someone starts to ask why nobody is role blocked or transported, {{A|Vampires}} may pretend one of them has been blocked or transported.  *Consider converting an outed {{A|Jester}} who has no chance of winning, as it is unlikely that anyone will ever bother them. It would also prevent them from siding with {{A|Mafia}}, or otherwise being an absent vote as {{A|Mafia}} approaches majority. * Converting a known {{A|Amnesiac}} is a bit more risky, as people will start to question why the {{A|Amnesiac}} hasn't chosen a role, making them more likely to be hanged. The main reason to do so is if {{A|Mafia}} is approaching majority, it would prevent them from choosing a {{A|Mafia}} role, outright giving them said majority. *{{A|Town Killing}} roles, such as the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Vigilante}}, are double-edged swords. They can kill {{A|Mafia}} and/or {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles (which are enemies), but they also can kill {{A|Vampires}}. It is advisable to keep them intact until they start to suspect {{A|Vampires}}. *A {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} can help at finding enemies, and the {{A|Sheriff}} in particular is unable to find {{A|Vampires}}, so it might be best to not bite them until after most of your enemies are dead. *'''DO NOT''' convert a revealed {{A|Mayor}} unless you are sure that your team will have the majority afterwards. Their identity can be immediately re-confirmed during the day (by attempting to whisper to the {{A|Mayor}}). The {{A|Mayor's}} vote would be counted as 1 instead of 3, and the {{A|Mayor}} will be able to send and receive whispers again. Their identity can also be tested during the {{A|Night}} phase (the {{A|Doctor}} would be able to heal the previously revealed {{A|Mayor}} who is now a {{A|Vampire}}). The {{A|Vampire}}-{{A|Mayor}} will become easy pickings for any killing or role blocking role, or simply hanged. *It's advisable not to convert a known {{A|Veteran}}, as they may be on alert and the {{A|Vampires}} may lose their youngest. If you do manage it, however, the {{A|Veteran}} can become a valuable {{A|Vampire}}, as no evil wishes to visit a {{A|Veteran}}. *Try to spot and avoid the {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, as the youngest {{A|Vampire}} will be staked after visiting him. **Also try to spot and avoid roles that can't be converted. Some roles can even kill the youngest {{A|Vampire}}, such as a {{A|Werewolf}} who stayed at home, or {{A|Pestilence}}. Do not waste time converting {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}} or {{A|Jesters}} either, unless you want to make absolutely sure they will be on your side. Remember that these roles, while likely to side with you, are still wildcards. They can win with anyone, and that "anyone" doesn't have to be you. *Do not attack people who attract too much attention, such as "{{A|Jesters}}" who are acting all too obvious. They may be a {{A|Veteran}} baiting, watched by a {{A|Lookout}}, jailed by a {{A|Jailor}}, or killed. Try to predict who will not be attacked. Visiting completely silent people is not a very good idea either, as they are often enemies who have Basic or higher {{A|Defense}}. *If an {{A|Executioner}} makes their move early and it plays out badly, consider converting their target. Not only does this confirm the new {{A|Vampire}} as a {{A|Townie}}, and they can claim what ever is needed to have someone else hanged. However, if it looks like {{A|Town}} may believe the {{A|Executioner}}, or the "{{A|Executioner}}" might actually be whatever role they are claiming, your new {{A|Vampire}} might be hanged, which both outs the fact that {{A|Vampires}} exist and wastes your {{A|Night}} biting them. *Remember that whoever you convert ends up on your side. Therefore, you should try to convert people who seem alert, intelligent, and serious about the game– both to side with them and to prevent the threat of you becoming enemies. Unlike other roles, {{A|Vampires}} are permitted to choose who their teammates are. * You can bite members of the {{A|Mafia}} to kill them. Doing so doesn't count as a successful conversion, meaning you can bite again immediately the next {{A|Night}}. If you have a confirmed member of the {{A|Mafia}}, you should seriously consider biting them. Things to keep in mind: **If you have four {{A|Vampires}}, you can still bite someone, though this will only deal a {{A|Basic Attack}} Therefore, in a situation where you are dealing with 3 or 4 members of the {{A|Mafia}}, the best way to win is to convert someone else if you can, then bite the next {{A|Night}}. This way, you can kill the {{A|Mafia}} one by one as you hang them and bite them. **Sometimes, revealing one member of the {{A|Mafia}} can allow you to hang others: for instance, if someone is ''almost'' hanged, and you suspect that they're a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, you can bite them to kill them, then call for hanges on the people who wouldn't help vote them up. However some smart {{A|Townies}} may call you out as the {{A|Vampire}} who accused them. Keep this in mind, especially if there are {{A|Vampire Hunters}} around and/or the {{A|Town}} is hunting for {{A|Vampires}} in particular. **It's also important to bite the {{A|Mafia}} when there's a danger of them hitting a majority or plurality. As long as your {{A|Vampires}} haven't been exposed, you can always bite {{A|Town}} later, but if the {{A|Mafia}} gets a plurality or, worse, a majority, then it'll be too late for you to win, regardless of who you convert. **The {{A|Godfather}} can be sometimes as dangerous to the {{A|Vampires}} as a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} not only for their basic defense and kill consistency, but also having a reliable team to fall back on (unlike the {{A|Serial Killer}}). However, since they are a threat to the {{A|Town}} as well, you don't need to convince many {{A|Townies}} to hang them even if the {{A|Town}} knows about the existence of your role. There could also be a second {{A|Godfather}} after you hang the first, so keep this in mind. **If both {{A|Vampire Hunters}} and {{A|Blackmailers}} are in the game, it can be very difficult to coordinate or even communicate well with the other {{A|Vampires}}, as the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} can hear your discussions at {{A|Night}}, and the {{A|Blackmailer}} will hear your [[whispers]] during the {{A|Day}}. Since you can only kill one of these roles, consider taking out all the {{A|Blackmailers}} so you don't accidentally expose all the {{A|Vampires}} to the {{A|Mafia}}. However a dead {{A|Blackmailer}} may still give [[whispers|whisper]] info to a {{A|Medium}} and tell them about the {{A|Vampires}}, but it will give you an extra day. **{{A|Bootleggers}} and {{A|Consiglieres}} can be dangerous threats, as the {{A|Consigliere}} can investigate and discover the {{A|Vampires}} directly, and the {{A|Bootlegger}} can lock down the {{A|Vampires}} by identifying the youngest. Do not bite {{A|Townies}} who claim they've been continually role blocked as biting them will prevent the {{A|Vampires}} from biting again since the youngest will be the {{A|Townie}} that was continually role blocked. Try to find and take out these roles quickly. **If there is an {{A|Ambusher}} in the game, choosing a target to convert can be risky, since the {{A|Ambusher}} can kill the youngest and and ask the {{A|Mafia}} to attack or role-block their original target if they didn't die. Luckily, the {{A|Ambusher}} is very easy to spot as they reveal their name to all visitors. If the youngest doesn't get targeted by the {{A|Ambusher}}, you can write in your {{A|Last Will}} or say who the {{A|Ambusher}} is at {{A|Night}} if there are {{A|Vampire Hunters}} around. **It's generally better to leave {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Sheriffs}}, and {{A|Spies}} unturned until the very end. {{A|Spies}} and {{A|Sheriffs}} can only find {{A|Mafia}}, while {{A|Tavern Keepers}} are more likely to find and lock down a solo {{A|Mafioso}}/{{A|Godfather}} than they are to find your youngest (since they can easily see when a role block results in no {{A|Mafia}} kill, while there's no indication to the {{A|Town}} when they block your youngest). If the {{A|Town}} consists mainly of these, it might be best to shift your focus to the {{A|Mafia}}. **On the other hand, be cautious about deliberately biting members of the {{A|Mafia}} if the {{A|Town}} doesn't yet know {{A|Vampires}} are present, since that will alert them and may lead {{A|Investigators}} to reveal anyone who came up with a {{A|Framer}} / {{A|Vampire}} / {{A|Jester}} (/ {{A|Hex Master}}) result. Also, if there is only one {{A|Vampire}}, you should usually bite to convert, since you're in danger of losing to a random death. *Biting a {{A|Survivor}} can be useful to deny them the option of voting against you, but it's risky - if they use a vest, your {{A|Night}} will be wasted. Biting confirmed {{A|Survivors}} may give you an outlet to find out {{A|Mafia}} members and {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles, as they often whisper to {{A|Survivors}} to side with them. Before biting a {{A|Survivor}} claim, see the {{A|Town's}} attitude towards {{A|Survivors}}, because if you're in an aggressive {{A|Town}} your new {{A|Vampire}} will be hanged, shot or executed, wasting your {{A|Night}} and outing the fact your role is in the game. *A risky, but rewarding bite is biting a {{A|Psychic}} (confirmed or not), since they can still pretend to be {{A|Psychic}} while siding with the {{A|Vampires}}. {{A|Psychic}} claims can use fake good and evil results to trick the {{A|Town}}, but one downside to this is that it forces the converted to guess who is good and who is evil. A wrong guess will likely have the {{A|Psychic}} hanged. This can also be a decent method of bussing, if you are unsure of who to put in your results. *If a {{A|Guardian Angel}} is in the game, consider biting their target. If they're {{A|Town}}, you now have 2 new allies in one {{A|Night}}, and if they're in another evil faction like {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Coven}}, you'll gain a {{A|Survivor}}. Beware if you've killed their target though, as they may harbor judgement for the death of their target. *The {{A|Coven}} can easily take out your enemies, but they can also take out your team. Some of their roles can also heal, getting in the way of your conversions, and some roles have basic defense, meaning you can't directly kill them. **The {{A|Coven Leader}} can investigate your team, and prevent your bites or kill you by controlling you into a(n) immune/protected target. Once they receive the {{A|Necronomicon}} they are both invulnerable through your bites and can kill your team. They also retrieve the {{A|Necronomicon}} first; take them out quickly, as the risk outweighs the reward. **The {{A|Hex Master}} can help cover your tracks, as anyone they hex shares your investigative results. Once they receive the {{A|Necronomicon}}, however, they become much more of a threat for you, as they can attack your fellow {{A|Vampires}} ''and ''can do it without a trace. Make sure to take them out, because if they've hexed too many people they can auto-win for the {{A|Coven}}. ** The {{A|Necromancer}} isn’t as dangerous as other {{A|Coven}} members, but keep an eye on the graveyard. They make it harder to take out threats such as the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} and other killing roles, as they can bring them back for a {{A|Night}} and slaughter your team. They can also control dead {{A|Town Protectives}} into preventing your bites, and possibly killing you. With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they can get rid of your team directly. You have to judge whether they're a high priority target based on what roles are dead. **The {{A|Potion Master}} is a swiss army knife. They can reveal you, kill your teammates ''and ''heal your targets. Take them out quickly, as with the {{A|Necronomicon}} they have no limits on what they can do to your team. **The {{A|Medusa}} is only a worry if they don't have the {{A|Necronomicon}}, as they can trade their life for one of your {{A|Vampires}}. Usually, once they obtain the {{A|Necronomicon}}, they may focus on killing other targets, leaving themselves open to be killed, although they can easily target you back. **The {{A|Poisoner}} isn’t very much of a threat, as their ability is easy to negate with a {{A|Doctor}} around, and if targeted without someone to heal you, you still have a {{A|Night}} to strategize. With the {{A|Necronomicon}}, a {{A|Doctor}} can no-longer help you, so make sure that you can keep your team alive when a {{A|Poisoner}} is around. Other than that, they're not dangerous. *The {{A|Pirate}} cannot be converted, so truce with them, as they are basically an attacking {{A|Survivor}}. It's easy to make a deal with a {{A|Pirate}}, as you can regain teammates if they attack them. They can roleblock or call out your team though, so make sure you can trust them. Never allow your youngest to be a sacrifice to a {{A|Pirate}}. *If you're investigated, you might be called out or put under suspicion since there are no {{A|Town}} roles in your result. Claiming to be {{A|Framed}}, {{A|Hexed}} or pretending to be a {{A|Jester}} could work, but if it becomes clear there are many active {{A|Vampires}}, it may be too late. ===Identifying the {{A|Vampire Hunters}}=== *The {{A|Vampire Hunter}} is immune to bites and will kill a {{A|Vampire}} if either they visit one, or is visited by one. As a result, it is a high priority to find the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} before they cause any damage. *A good way of getting the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} to reveal early is to make them think there are already 2-3 {{A|Vampires}} in the game. The {{A|Vampire Hunter}} can read anonymous messages sent by the {{A|Vampires}}. On {{A|Night}} 1, create a conversation and play both ends. Talk about how crazy it is that there are already this many {{A|Vampires}} in {{A|Night}} 1. This will put pressure on the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} and they will more often than not share any suspicions they have with the {{A|Town}}, revealing their role to you. *A second method of tricking the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} into revealing his role is to mention a false name in the {{A|Night}} chat. Say something like 'Get Player X' and instead, target someone different. Not only does this portray Player X as suspicious, but also reveals the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} when they report to the town. If the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} does not report his findings and instead finds the target to be human, they might assume that this person is immune and therefore still suspicious. **However, the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} might also assume that the {{A|Vampires}} were tricking him, and not reveal himself, and also be less likely to believe the {{A|Vampires}} in the future. *If you do choose to frame a player, do not bite them, as that player may be hanged or killed by the {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Vigilante}}. *{{A|Vampire Hunters}} will use {{A|Veteran}} strategies to bait {{A|Vampires}}.  * If you are converted, it's a good idea to say that your role was something that it wasn't. This can confuse {{A|Vampire Hunters}}. ===General Tips=== *If you are alone, it is always a good idea to start up a "conversation" with yourself, especially on {{A|Night}} One. If there are any {{A|Vampire Hunters}}, the conversation may confuse them and cause their playstyle to change drastically, as they may think there are more Vampires than there actually are. This method is amazing for confusion and generally recommended. *It is important to focus on removing anything you can't convert as quickly as you can; if the {{A|Mafia}} has four people, for instance, you could attempt cooperating with the town to eliminate them or try to kill them by yourself. You will need the numbers of the {{A|Town}} or {{A|Vampires}} to hang the {{A|Godfather}} if he does not get killed. Likewise, the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} should be eliminated at all costs as soon as possible. *If you spot a {{A|Vampire Hunter}}, all {{A|Vampires}} should try to lure {{A|Town}} into eliminating him without revealing his true identity. For methods to do so, see tips for {{A|Executioner}}. **Extra caution must be taken, however, since he can simultaneously test and kill you if he suspects you're going after him. Reporting to a {{A|Mayor}} in chat or discussion with the {{A|Jailor}} is the best way to throw him into suspicion. **If you do manage to get a {{A|Vampire Hunter}} killed, immediately claim {{A|Executioner}} by thanking the {{A|Town}} for giving you a win. This will make them less likely to conclude that you're a {{A|Vampire}}. Remember, {{A|Vampire Hunters}} are ''not'' unique, so if there's a second one, they're likely to go after anyone who seemed too aggressive about killing the first. **Remember, in tight role lists, only one of you can claim {{A|Executioner}}. If the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} gets hanged, smart {{A|Townies}} could realize that all of you are {{A|Vampires}}, causing your team to get hanged. *Since {{A|Vampire Hunters}} can hear {{A|Vampires}} talking to each other at {{A|Night}}, it's recommended to keep {{A|Night}} discussions to a minimum and, if you absolutely have to, alter your writing style (that includes spelling, usage of emoticons, word capitalization, etc). ** You could attempt to trick the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} to visit someone and waste a {{A|Night}} when you’ve converted someone and say “welcome [name]” when it’s really someone else. This may not work on experienced players. **Advanced players may attempt to trick the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} into wasting their visits on non-{{A|Vampires}}. Though {{A|Vampire Hunters}} don't have to reveal to follow up on leads because you can't kill them at {{A|Night}} even if they do, and a successful trick usually isn't going to make them kill an enemy for you. ***One very advanced way of tricking the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} is typing in {{A|Vampire}} chat using another player's daily/unique chat pattern. For Example, if they Capitalize Every Beginning Letter, you can trick the VH into wasting a {{A|Night}}, if they pay attention to the chat patterns, that is. *{{A|Vampires}} could convert someone, and if the conversion was successful, a {{A|Vampire}} will accuse the youngest {{A|Vampire}} of being a {{A|Vampire}}. The youngest {{A|Vampire}} will be hanged, "confirming" a {{A|Vampire}} as a good role and throwing off the {{A|Town}}. *If your target was immune to biting, it's a good idea to write it down in your {{A|Last Will}}. As soon as you die, the suspicion may raise about the person you mentioned as immune-to-biting. This will allow you to help the town hang criminals without revealing yourself, which in turn helps the {{A|Vampires}}.  **The target may be an {{A|Executioner}}. However, unlike the {{A|Mafia}}, it's sometimes dangerous for {{A|Vampires}} to side with an {{A|Executioner}} since his target may be someone who was converted to a {{A|Vampire}}. *If you need to accuse your target immediately during the day, you can pretend to be a {{A|Vigilante}} who couldn't shoot a person at {{A|Night}} and found they were immune. However, this can be dangerous if an existing {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} have missed a kill, since the {{A|Town}} might assume you're an evil killer. Regardless of the outcome, this is likely to attract hostile attention from the {{A|Mafia}}. If your target was a {{A|Godfather}}, it is recommended to ask for protection since you are a "confirmed {{A|Town}} role". *If {{A|Vampires}} are not explicitly guaranteed in the role list and you end up as one as a result of an {{A|Any}} or {{A|Neutral Chaos}} entry, try to hide as long as possible. The only true way {{A|Town}} can learn about presence of {{A|Vampires}} is through a {{A|Vampire}} or {{A|Vampire Hunter}} dying or by you biting a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, a member of the {{A|Coven}}, or any {{A|Neutral}} without defense (besides {{A|Survivor}} not vesting, {{A|Amnesiac}}, {{A|Jester}}). If none of these things happen, the {{A|Town}} will generally be unsuspecting until it's too late to resist. An added advantage to this is that {{A|Vampire Hunter}} claims are more likely to be hanged if the {{A|Town}} doesn't believe {{A|Vampires}} are present. ** This is even more effective in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, as the {{A|Town}} may become wary of a {{A|Plaguebearer}} and begin slowing down visits to slow down the speed at which the {{A|Plaguebearer}} will become {{A|Pestilence}}. *** If there ''is actually'' a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, the {{A|Town}} will be even less likely to believe that there are {{A|Vampires}}. If they become {{A|Pestilence}}, you should continue biting unless you only have 1-2 {{A|Vampires}} left. You may die to {{A|Pestilence's}} rampage, exposing the fact that {{A|Vampires}} exist, but if your youngest dies to {{A|Pestilence}}, your target doesn't die to {{A|Pestilence}}, and they aren't converted, then you should call them out. You'll expose yourself, but at that point, there should be few players left to the point where you can win by converting everyone else. However, remember that your youngest may have been targeted by {{A|Pestilence}} directly and your target could've been a different immune role. *If a player has Basic or higher {{A|Defense}}, say it in the {{A|Night}} chat. The {{A|Vampire Hunter}} will hear this, and you can cooperate with the {{A|Town}}, getting rid of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} or {{A|Neutral Killing}} who threaten both of you. Additionally, the {{A|Vampire Hunter}} will probably say this out loud, revealing him so you can avoid him. * If there is no {{A|Vampire Hunter}} alive, it may be in your best interests to form a truce with the remaining {{A|Townies}} to vote off {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}}. Being honest with proven {{A|Townies}} and whispering them your role and the name of other {{A|Vampires}} can earn their trust, and most players will gladly take the secondary win as a {{A|Vampire}} over losing as {{A|Town}}. Do NOT let this turn into [[gamethrowing]], though. {{A|Townies}} hanging other {{A|Townies}} to get converted is against the rules. *Keeping a fake {{A|Last Will}} of your converting visits may help if there are inexperienced players in the game. This can lead to hanges against players who could be a nuisance to your team. However, if someone you bite was immune to your attack, then you should generally write their name in your {{A|Last Will}} to hopefully put suspicion on them after you die. *{{A|Vampires}} have much more leeway to lie in their {{A|Last Will}} than most other roles. Remember, your goal should be to help the {{A|Vampires}} win even after you die. Spreading confusion or getting the {{A|Town}} to focus on hanging non-{{A|Vampires}} helps with this. **You can claim to have been any role you like prior to being turned into a {{A|Vampire}}. Use this to try and get a non-{{A|Vampire}} hanged by putting together a false {{A|Last Will}} with a list of visits. Claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} and list random non-{{A|Vampires}} as {{A|Mafia}}. Claim to be a {{A|Lookout}} and say you saw a non-{{A|Vampire}} visit someone the {{A|Night}} they were murdered. Claim to be an {{A|Investigator}} and accuse someone of a suspicious role list, like {{A|Framer}}/{{A|Vampire}}/{{A|Jester}} (/ {{A|Hex Master}}). You can even claim to have been a {{A|Spy}}. **In fact, simply claiming to be whatever role you were before you were converted (Such as {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}}) is almost always the best way to claim. Continue writing your {{A|Last Will}} you wrote before you were converted and then adding in fake information might work, especially if they hang an evil written in the top of your {{A|Last Will}}. **You can accuse anyone you like of being immune. This has two benefits, since it both throws them under suspicion and makes everyone think that there are fewer {{A|Vampires}} than there really are. **Even very transparent ruses are often surprisingly effective, since if your {{A|Last Will}} implies that a non-{{A|Mafia}} is guilty of something, both the {{A|Mafia}} and the {{A|Vampires}} will use it as an excuse to hang them, and will probably only have to convince one or two {{A|Town}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{VampireAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{VampireMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Vampire}} role is based on the Cultist role from StarCraft 2 Mafia. *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.5.11.5389}}, all members of the {{A|Mafia}} were immune to {{A|Vampires}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0}}, {{A|Vampires}} were able to convert {{A|Survivors}} and {{A|Bodyguards}} through their vests. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.4}}, {{A|Vampires}} were unable to bite targets when four or more {{A|Vampires}} existed. *An {{A|Amnesiac}} that becomes a {{A|Vampire}} can exceed the 4-player limit. *{{A|Vampire}} is the only {{A|Neutral Chaos}} role that is not exclusive to the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *{{A|Vampire}} is the only {{A|Neutral}} role that can communicate with each other during the {{A|Night}}. *{{A|Vampire}} is the only role that can directly change the goal of another player.[[File:Multiple Vampires.png|thumb|A game showing that there can be more than four {{A|Vampires}} with certain role lists]] *In [[Coven Custom]], if you create a role list with 4 {{A|Vampires}}, a {{A|Plaguebearer}}, and a {{A|Pirate}}, plus any number of {{A|Neutral Chaos}}, all of those {{A|Neutral Chaos}} slots will be {{A|Vampires}}. This can exceed the 4 {{A|Vampire}} limit. **This happens because the {{A|Neutral Chaos}} [[alignment]] only has 3 roles in it: {{A|Pirate}}, {{A|Plaguebearer}}, and {{A|Vampire}}. Since {{A|Pirate}} and {{A|Plaguebearer}} are both [[unique]], the game is forced to add {{A|Vampires}} in all {{A|Neutral Chaos}} slots, exceeding the normal limit of 4 {{A|Vampires}}. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Added {{A|Tavern Keeper}} vs. {{A|Vampire}} [[stalemate]] detector. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate youngest {{A|Vampire}} for the {{A|Vampires}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_YoungestVampire.png|30x30px]]). **For {{A|Vampires}}, the youngest {{A|Vampire}} is now shown as "({{Amne|Vampire}})" instead of "({{Amne|Youngest|Vampire}})". **The {{A|Vampire's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Vampire.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Vampire's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Vampire Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.4.0.10404}} **{{A|Vampires}} are now able to vote to bite a target while there are four or more {{A|Vampires}} alive, dealing an {{A|Attack}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6501}} **{{A|Vampires}} can no longer convert through a used vest. *{{VH|1.5.0.3431}} **{{A|Vampire}} can now successfully kill {{A|Mafia}} members with no {{A|Defense}} when attempting to bite them instead of the {{A|Mafia}} member being immune and the {{A|Vampire}} receiving the message "Your target was immune to your attack!". *{{VH|1.3.0}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Вампир]]  [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Chaos roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Basic Attack]] [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Town of Salem]] [[Category:Detection Immune]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *Choose to Rampage at someone's house each {{A|Full Moon}}. You deal a Powerful attack to your target and all their visitors. *If you do not select a target, you will stay home and attack anyone who visits you. *If a {{A|Witch}} or {{A|Coven Leader}} controls you even if you stay home or not, you will attack the target of their choice. *If you attack someone who has been {{A|Jailed}}, you will deal a Powerful attack to all visitors who attempted to visit the jailed target, but not the {{A|Jailor}} or the Jailee/person being jailed. *You cannot be controlled or transported into attacking yourself, if you target yourself via controlling or transportation, you will simply stay home. *If you are jailed on a {{A|Full Moon}} and aren't executed, you will attack the {{A|Jailor}}. A {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trapper}} who is protecting the {{A|Jailor}} will attack you. *If you are [[Roleblock|roleblocked]] by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Pirate}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}, you will be forced to stay home and therefore attack them. **Unlike the {{A|Serial Killer}}, a role blocker (including the {{A|Jailor}} if they didn't execute you) will ''not'' receive a special message upon being killed by you, hence they cannot guarantee if you are a {{A|Werewolf}} or not. *You will always attack the {{A|Pirate}} if they duel you on a {{A|Full Moon}} whether they win the duel or not. *On normal{{A|Nights}}, if you are controlled, you will still visit the target chosen by the controller, meaning you will be seen by {{A|Lookouts}} and {{A|Trackers}} and can die to a {{A|Veteran}}. *You appear suspicious to {{A|Sheriffs}} on a {{A|Full Moon}}. ==Strategy== The {{A|Werewolf}} is similar to the {{A|Serial Killer}} since both usually work alone and kill targets directly, but there are major differences: *You can only kill on the {{A|Night}} of a {{A|Full Moon}}. However, you will attack all visitors to your target. You can also choose to stay home, which the {{A|Serial Killer}} cannot do, and you can kill people who visit you this way. *You deal a Powerful attack to your targets, while the {{A|Serial Killer}} only deals a Basic attack to a single target. *You cannot spare [[Roleblock|role blockers]] on a {{A|Full Moon}}, and they will prevent you from killing your original target unlike the {{A|Serial Killer}}. Additionally, you do not destroy the {{A|Last Wills}} of the offending [[Roleblock|role blockers]]. *You are truly a lone killer, while the {{A|Serial Killer}} can possibly have multiple {{A|Serial Killers}}. If you die, you will lose the game unless an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers your role. ===You should:=== *Target people the {{A|Town}} is becoming suspicious of as they will most likely be visited by a lot of people. They will often be {{A|Jailed}}, [[Role block|role blocked]], investigated or {{A|Framed}}, and are unlikely to be protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}. **{{A|Veterans}} and other roles reliant on attacking visitors make an exception here. *Try to figure out what people are doing so you can target your attacks for maximum kills. If you suspect that a {{A|Lookout}} is watching someone, an {{A|Investigator}} is investigating them, a {{A|Transporter}} is moving them, a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is blocking them, or a {{A|Blackmailer}} is repeatedly blackmailing them, attacking them can target both them and their visitors at the same time. **Some of these people will come out and announce leads (such as a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} declaring that they've role blocked someone last {{A|Night}} and will do it again after finding no kills). Others you have to infer from context. For example, if someone signals that they were blackmailed by clicking votes repeatedly, for instance, attacking them might let you kill a {{A|Blackmailer}}. *An alternate strategy is to hide throughout the game. If you claim to be an {{A|Executioner}} (preferably by legitimately trying to have someone hanged) and visit yourself every {{A|Night}}, then, assuming no one visits you, you can attack out of nowhere during endgame. This strategy will have a higher chance of working in All Any mode since roles are random. **This is unlikely to work in modes or lists with only one {{A|Neutral Evil}} and {{A|Neutral Killing}}, since you rely on the other role not to quickly expose you or be killed by any other means. *Consider staying at home. If a {{A|Doctor}} visits you, you can claim to have been attacked by the {{A|Werewolf}} and healed by the {{A|Doctor}}. You will also kill anyone attempting to investigate or attack you, which can prevent them from telling anyone what they learn unless there's a {{A|Medium}} or if they updated their {{A|Last Will}}. **Try to have a lot of attention directed at you if you're doing it. You'll most likely kill any {{A|Investigators}}, {{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Sheriffs}}, {{A|Consiglieres}} or any others visiting you. **One downside to this is that anyone who visits you might name you in their {{A|Last Will}} as the next person they're visiting. If just one person does so, you'll be alright (as they could have been the one the {{A|Werewolf}} targeted), but if multiple people do and you aren't visited by a {{A|Doctor}}, then your status as a {{A|Werewolf}} will be obvious. **Another downside is that you're not always going to kill someone that {{A|Full Moon}}. Visiting someone almost guarantees you will kill one person, if not more. *It's generally a bad strategy to act like a {{A|Jester}}, as that will make you an obvious target to the {{A|Town Killing}} roles. The {{A|Jester}} will be shot and killed, but you will appear to have a higher Defense value than said {{A|Town Killing}} role's Attack value at {{A|Night}}, which almost always leads to a hang. *Targeting a revealed {{A|Mayor}} carries some danger since a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Trapper}} can still kill you, but if you're sure there's not a {{A|Bodyguard}} in the game, it can be an effective way to target a {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Lookout}}, or anyone else visiting the {{A|Mayor}} that {{A|Night}}. *If someone accuses you, you should stay at home, as {{A|Town Investigatives}} will likely visit you that {{A|Night}} since suspicion is being cast on you. However, if the accuser is still alive, they could still lead a hang against you. *If accused, you could also attack the accuser, but this carries the risk of {{A|Town}} becoming suspicious of you from their death. Also, a {{A|Town Protective}} could also be on them. However, if the accusation isn't all that big, say, they ask for a role or start showing suspicion of you, feel free to attack them as the risk is lower. This can be harder to use in game if the {{A|Townie}} accusing is claiming a {{A|Town Investigative}} role and says your investigation result. *If you are attacked, you could be in trouble, since whoever attacked you is very likely to call you out for having a higher Defense value than the attacker's Attack value in their next {{A|Death Note}} or {{A|Last Will}}. There's no perfect way to deal with this. **One option is to immediately claim {{A|Survivor}} and say you vested. {{A|Survivor}} is a common {{A|Werewolf}} claim, and the {{A|Town}} loses little by hanging one, so this may not work, but if you're going to do it, it's better to do it before you're accused rather than after. However, this violates your investigative results. **Another option is to immediately start acting like an {{A|Executioner}}. It fits in with your investigation results and might discourage the {{A|Town}} from calling you out. It could also make the {{A|Town}} dismiss the accusation if they do, but this risks having you hung as an {{A|Executioner}} or executed by the {{A|Jailor}}. **Alternatively, you could act as an {{A|Executioner}} from the start (accuse someone {{A|day 2}}). This does risk being hung as {{A|Executioner}} or being executed by the {{A|Jailor}} but has the advantage of being a consistent claim throughout the game. However, this could potentially backfire if your target isn't {{A|Town}}. **If the next {{A|Night}} is a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, you can claim to be a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Lookout}}, accuse someone of being a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, then kill them yourself, which will both explain your Basic Defense (by making it look like you were an {{A|Executioner}}) and make people assume you've become a {{A|Jester}}, causing them to ignore you; as a side benefit, accusing someone may make people visit them, netting you additional kills. And if they ''do'' coincidentally turn out to be {{A|Mafia}}, then the {{A|Town}} is likely to believe you are what you actually claimed and ignore the {{A|Mafia's}} {{A|Death Notes}} saying you have a higher Defense value than the {{A|Mafia Killing}} role's Attack value. **A third option is just to say that whoever called you out is lying if they're likely {{A|Mafia}} or a {{A|Serial Killer}}. Unfortunately, the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Serial Killer}} have an incentive to truthfully call out rivals with a higher Defense value than their attacker's Attack value, so they tend to be believed. **Staying home reduces the risk of being called out as a role with Defense (ie. a {{A|Serial Killer}} or {{A|Vigilante}} if they try to attack you on a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} where you stay home, they'll die before they can tell anyone, {{A|Mediums}} aside), but doesn't provide protection from being outed by {{A|Vampires}} or the {{A|Mafia}} unless you're lucky enough to eliminate them entirely that {{A|Night}}. Any {{A|Survivors}} will see that you were unaffected by the attack and know to out you. *Under certain limited circumstances, it can be advantageous to claim to be a {{A|Witch}}. The {{A|Witch}} is not a target for the {{A|Mafia}} (so they're more likely to focus on someone else, possibly hanging a {{A|Survivor}} claim or an actual {{A|Witch}} in your stead) and while they're an enemy of the {{A|Town}}, they're less of a danger than your actual role. {{A|Survivor}} is such a common claim for {{A|Werewolves}} that both the {{A|Mafia}} and {{A|Town}}, when seeking a {{A|Werewolf}} with no other leads, are very likely to hang a {{A|Survivor}} claim over a {{A|Witch}} one. If it's nearing the end of the game and the {{A|Town}} needs to hang a killer immediately to win or the {{A|Mafia}} just gained a majority, claiming {{A|Witch}} can sometimes buy you the small amount of time you need to win. Note that this will not work if your Basic Defense has already been discovered (since unlike the {{A|Witch}}, attackers will receive an immunity message). Make sure you claim before you are voted up or are receiving votes because you are less likely to be put down from the stand as a {{A|Witch}} than a {{A|Survivor}}. *If you see someone who said something along the lines of, "{{A|Investigator}} or {{A|Sheriff}}, this person is very suspicious. Please check them toNight", or "{{A|Tavern Keeper}} please role block this person toNight", it is a good idea to attack that person who is going to be visited by those roles. Since they are less likely to be protected by a {{A|Bodyguard}}, watched by a {{A|Lookout}}, or healed by a {{A|Doctor}}, you might be able to kill some people, even the important {{A|Town Investigative}} or {{A|Town Support}} roles, and keep suspicion away from you for some time, unless your status is already discovered. *If you are pressed a role, {{A|Sheriff}} is usually your best bet. It fits in your investigation result and is hard to disprove. However, since {{A|Sheriff}} is such a common claim for {{A|Werewolves}} (and any other evil role), you might be hanged on the spot. Make sure to have a fake {{A|Last Will}} to back your claim up. *Generally speaking, you should focus on killing the "factions" of {{A|Vampires}} and {{A|Mafia}} more than focusing on killing {{A|Town}}, especially if they can gain a majority quickly. With a few exceptions, the {{A|Town}} is not a huge threat to you and will have trouble identifying you; but it is flatly not possible for you to win if the game comes down to you against multiple members of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} or {{A|Vampires}}. Additionally, both have a high chance of identifying you by attacking you. You should try to eradicate them as quickly as possible. **On the other hand, since only a {{A|Disguiser}}/{{A|Potion Master}} can visit other {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}} members and {{A|Vampires}} cannot visit other {{A|Vampires}}, you're more likely to have those factions as "incidental" kills if you target high-profile {{A|Town}}. ===If your target was...=== *If your target was jailed, you will kill anyone who visits your target. The target and the {{A|Jailor}} will not be affected. **This generates the message "Your target was not home, but you rampaged anyways." *If you are roleblocked on a {{A|Full Moon}} by a {{A|Tavern Keeper}}, {{A|Bootlegger}} or {{A|Pirate}}, you will stay at home and attack them instead. This can and usually will generate suspicion from the {{A|Town}} against you, provided the role blocker kept an updated will. *If your target was visited, you will attack the target and all visitors. ===Behavior with other roles=== *{{A|Serial Killers}} will rarely attack suspicious targets. If you want to kill the {{A|Serial Killer}}, try to identify them or predict who they will attack next. **Note that just like the {{A|Mafia}}, it is not a bad idea to keep the {{A|Serial Killer}} alive, until mid-game or possibly {{A|Night 4}} where a moderately large portion of the other players are dead. *Try to work with {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Pirates}}, {{A|Survivors}}, {{A|Guardian Angels}}, {{A|Amnesiacs}}, {{A|Jesters}} and {{A|Executioners}}. These are your only possible allies and can help you with votes. *You have a leg-up on the {{A|Arsonist}}: If you keep attacking targets who aren't doused, you may kill the {{A|Arsonist}} directly or indirectly. Furthermore, the {{A|Arsonist}} will usually save their incineration until the end, giving you plenty of time to kill them even if you are doused yourself. **As of the current version of [[Town of Salem]], you should try and use {{A|Investigators}}' results to figure out who isn't doused, and who is. *The {{A|Tavern Keepers}} and {{A|Bootleggers}} are dangerous to you because they force you to stay home, killing all visitors. If one visits you and puts you in their {{A|Last Will}}, you may come under suspicion and possibly be hanged. *{{A|Coven Leaders}} are dangerous to you because if they discover your identity, they can force you to attack their targets for them or force you to visit {{A|Medusa}} on a non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}. *{{A|Sheriffs}} are somewhat dangerous. If they interrogate you on a {{A|Full Moon}}, they'll see you as suspicious and will usually out you the next {{A|day}}. Checking you on either {{A|Night 1}} or {{A|Night 3}} however, nets you with some degree of confirmability since you appear as not suspicious. Smart {{A|Townies}}, however, may point out you can still be the {{A|Werewolf}} overall. *{{A|Investigators}} are moderately dangerous as well. Your {{A|Sheriff}}/{{A|Executioner}}/{{A|Werewolf}}/{{A|Poisoner}} result provides some protection, but you could be called out if all the {{A|Town Investigatives}} are revealed or if the {{A|Town}} is hunting a {{A|Werewolf}} in particular. This is because {{A|Sheriff}} is a somewhat suspicious role. *{{A|Doctors}}, {{A|Crusaders}}, {{A|Lookouts}} or {{A|Transporters}} are not very dangerous. If they heal, protect, watch, or transport your target, they will die. *A {{A|Lookout}} can be dangerous if there is a {{A|Medium}}, or if there's a {{A|Town Protective}} role that aims to save the {{A|Lookout}} from death. That way, they could inform the {{A|Town}} of who the {{A|Werewolf}} is. *A {{A|Tracker}} is dangerous, If they track you when you attack someone, they could inform the {{A|Town}} of the {{A|Werewolf's}} identity. *{{A|Veterans}} may end up killing you on chance, so attempt to identify them as soon as possible. If one is identified, consider them as the last ones to kill, to increase the likelihood that they waste their {{A|Alerts}} or be killed by someone else. If you visit an {{A|Alerting}} {{A|Veteran}}, both of you will be dealt with a powerful attack. It should also be noted that a {{A|Werewolf}} will win by default against a {{A|Veteran}} if they are the only two players alive, so it might be worth avoiding the {{A|Veteran}} altogether. *{{A|Serial Killers}} and the {{A|Mafia}} are less dangerous to you than they are to most other roles since they can't kill you at {{A|Night}}; but they can still call you out for having a higher Defense value than their Attack value, so it's worth trying to eliminate them if you can figure out who they are. If someone accuses you of having immunity, remind the {{A|Town}} that they would be taking advice from a {{A|Serial Killer}} or the {{A|Mafia}}, who doesn't have their best interests in mind. *A {{A|Bodyguard}} or a trap from a {{A|Trapper}} will not harm you if their target visited your target and died due to your Rampage ability. Other protective roles; however, will save their target as they give them Powerful defense regardless of any outside circumstances. ==Dealing with {{A|Werewolves}}== *If you visit a player and they died to the {{A|Werewolf}}, they were not the direct target of the {{A|Werewolf}}, but instead visited the {{A|Werewolf's}} target or the {{A|Werewolf}} themselves. *As a {{A|Sheriff}}, you will only see the {{A|Werewolf}} as suspicious on {{A|Full Moon}}{{A|Nights}}. Keep this in mind when you find somebody suspicious. *If there is confirmed to be a {{A|Werewolf}} in the game, it is wise to limit visits to high-profile targets on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}} in general. The {{A|Werewolf}} would attack anyone who would garner any visits, so avoid needlessly visiting targets that will already have plenty of visitors on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}. *If you do find the {{A|Werewolf}}, it might be wise to keep them alive right after a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}} in order to hang higher priority targets like a member of the {{A|Mafia}}/{{A|Coven}}, the {{A|Arsonist}}, ​​​​​​or any other evil as the {{A|Werewolf}} can't attack on Non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}. If it is a {{A|Full Moon}} however, hanging the {{A|Werewolf}} would be a smarter move. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{WerewolfAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{WerewolfMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Werewolf}} was added into the game in {{VH|Version 0.8.0}}, making it the 30th [[Roles (ToS)|role]] to enter Town of Salem. *Prior to {{VH|Version 0.8.1}}, players who attacked the {{A|Werewolf}} on a {{A|Night}} where there was a {{A|Full Moon}} would not receive a notification stating that the {{A|Werewolf}} was immune to an attack. *Prior to {{VH|Version 1.3.0}}, the {{A|Werewolf}} had no {{A|Defense}} on {{A|Nights}} where there was no {{A|Full Moon}}, which made the {{A|Werewolf}} easy to kill on odd-numbered {{A|Nights}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.1.0}}, an alive {{A|Werewolf}} would not automatically win when the only other player alive was a {{A|Veteran}}. This made it possible for the game to end in a draw if the {{A|Werewolf}} attacked on a {{A|Night}} where the {{A|Veteran}} decided to go on {{A|Alert}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.5.1.10655}}, there was a bug where a jailed {{A|Werewolf}} could attack the {{A|Jailor}} without being attacked by a {{A|Bodyguard}} who happened to visit the {{A|Jailor}} that {{A|Night}}. *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.5}}, a {{A|Full Moon}} would only occur every even {{A|Night}} in the game ({{A|Night 2}}, {{A|Night 4}}, etc). {{A|Full Moon}} now occurs on {{A|Night}} Two and then every {{A|Night}} following {{A|Night 4}}. ==History== *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Temporary {{A|Defense}} given by certain roles through game mechanics now give attackers the message "Your target's defense was too strong to kill.". *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|Attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Werewolf's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Werewolf2.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Werewolf's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Werewolf Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.1.0.7320}} **{{A|Werewolf}} vs. {{A|Veteran}} now grants {{A|Werewolf}} the victory, even if the {{A|Veteran}} has {{A|Alerts}}. *{{VH|1.3.0}} **The {{A|Werewolf}} now has permanent {{A|Basic Defense}} instead of {{A|Basic Defense}} every {{A|Full Moon}}. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.1}} **{{A|Town}} vs. {{A|Witch}} and {{A|Werewolf}} [[stalemate]] fixed. **Attackers will now get "Your target is immune" message when attacking {{A|Werewolf}} on {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}}. *{{VH|Beta 0.8.0}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Loup-garou]] [[ja:狼]] [[ru:Оборотень]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Neutral roles]] [[Category:Neutral Killing roles]] [[Category:Killing roles]] [[Category:Unique Roles]] [[Category:Basic Defense]] [[Category:Evil roles]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:Rampage]] [[Category:Suspicious]] [[Category:Detection Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

The town will only go through the Defense (and subsequent Judgement and Last Words phases) if someone is put on trial during the Voting phase, and will only go through the Last Words phase if said person is deemed guilty by the majority of players and [[hanged]].

[[Town of Salem|Town of Salem's]] [[Rapid Mode]] is a [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic Game Mode]] identical to [[Game Modes (ToS)#Custom Mode|Custom]], but with the [[#Discussion|Discussion]] and {{A|Night}} phases reduced. There is no {{A|Coven}} equivalent.

=={{A|Day}}==
[[File:Day_Theme.mp3|400px]]
*The total time of the {{A|Day}} phase in the standard [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]] will range from 75 to 721 seconds (1 minute and 15 seconds to 12 minutes and 1 second), while it will range from 45 to 691 seconds (3/4 of a minute to 11 minutes and 31 seconds) in [[Rapid Mode]].''' This is not counting the transitions between the {{A|Day}} phases and the transition into the {{A|Night}} phase.'''

===Discussion===
[[File:Discussion Theme.mp3|400px]]

*The Discussion phase in standard [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]] lasts 45 seconds, while only lasting 15 seconds in [[Rapid Mode]].

*This is the primary phase of all [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]], where the players get to discuss among themselves, reflecting on previous {{A|Days}} and {{A|Nights}}.

===Voting===
[[File:Voting Theme.mp3|400px]]

*The Voting phase lasts 30 seconds in all [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]].

*During this phase, players can vote for others to put on trial. The number of votes required to put someone on trial is a simple majority.

*Players can be put on trial 3 times in a {{A|Day}}. After the third trial, the {{A|Day}} phase immediately ends, regardless of how much time is left.
*If a player isn't sent to trial, the {{A|Day}} phase ends, and the game will transition into the {{A|Night}} phase.

===Defense===
[[File:Defense Theme.mp3|400px]]

*The {{A|Defense}} phase lasts 20 seconds in all [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]].

*The Town will only go through this phase if a player is voted up to trial during the Voting phase.

*During this phase, the player in question gives a Defense. Only this player can speak (with the exception that the town can [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to each other).

*In Town of Salem 1, {{A|Blackmailed}} players may only say "''I am blackmailed.''" once as their defense.
**Evil roles can use this as a last resort if they are not ready to [[Role Claims Guide|claim a role]].
*In both games, the players cannot repeat the phrase if they are voted up a second time.

===Judgement===

*The Judgement phase lasts 20 seconds in all [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]].

The town will only go through this phase if a player is voted up on trial during the [[Phases#Voting|Voting]] phase.

===Last Words===

*The Last Words phase lasts 7 seconds in all [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]].

*During this phase, the player in question can deliver a final statement to the town before being killed by their [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]]). Only this player can speak.

*After the player is [[hanged]] (or killed another way depending on their [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]]) their {{A|Last Will}} and [[role]] is shown, and other players may speak again. This includes {{A|Silenced}} players (due to a {{A|Bug}}). The {{A|Day}} phase then ends, and the game transitions into the {{A|Night}} phase.

*Note that spamming at any time during any phase is against the rules and could get you banned. Refer to [[Town of Salem Rules|this page]] for more info.

=={{A|Night}}==
[[File:Night Theme.mp3|400px]]

*The {{A|Night}} phase in standard [[Game Modes (ToS)|game modes]] lasts 37 seconds, and only lasts 10 seconds in [[Rapid Mode]]. '''This is not counting the transition into the {{A|Day}} phase.'''

*If there are few players left alive, it is ill-advised to visit any player during these {{A|Nights}}, as it may get you killed inadvertently.

Coven (ToS).wikitext: {{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Coven}}}} {{Coven Exclusive}}[[File:RoleIcon CovenLeader.png|thumb]]The {{A|Coven}} are a [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] exclusive to the {{A|Coven Expansion}} add-on. Being a diverse set of multiple [[roles (ToS)|roles]], all members of the {{A|Coven}} specialize in witchcraft in any way possible and have the possibility to kill anyone they desire. Knowing who their teammates are similar to the {{A|Mafia}}, they can single-handedly take out four or more innocent {{A|Townies}} in one {{A|Night}} alone, a devastating blow. They can discover the roles of their rivals and their allies, and can easily wipe out a whole {{A|Town}} in {{A|Days}} if left unchecked. Unlike the {{A|Mafia}}, the {{A|Coven}} focus more directly on killing and prohibiting their targets rather than deception. Only a few roles and the {{A|Necronomicon}} can keep the {{A|Coven}} safe from any {{A|Town Investigative}} or {{A|Town Protective}} roles, or simply being Hanged themselves by the more probable {{A|Town}} majority. Thus, the {{A|Coven}} need to kill off targets quickly, but that may create desperation for those who oppose them. Despite their massive killing power and abilities, they all can get pinned down equally by multiple roles, killing or blocking alike. Only a few {{A|Coven}} roles can bypass the lure of an {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Consort}} (they will still be roleblocked by a {{A|Pirate}}) or avoid being killed by any means necessary. The {{A|Necronomicon}} is simply a help to the {{A|Coven}}; if they are discovered, they most likely won't survive the {{A|Night}}. {{LabelNecronomicon}} For the {{A|Coven}} to emerge victorious, they must avoid detection and kill those who pose the biggest threats to them. The {{A|Town}}'s unity within themselves will try and weed out the identities of the {{A|Coven}}, while the {{A|Mafia}} would much rather put their efforts driving attention directly to them and using the support of the {{A|Town}} to burn them at the stake. If needed, the {{A|Mafia}} certainly would not refrain from using "normal means" instead and murdering each member one-by-one. The {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles, while minimal, can be toys to play with but would otherwise demolish the {{A|Coven}} if given the opportunity. The {{A|Pirate}} and {{A|Pestilence}} are less of this, and rather a large nuisance, since these roles would much rather use the {{A|Coven}} as target practice than serving an outside use. As such, the {{A|Coven}} must prioritize who must be killed and who can be spared, as given enough time, their enemies will grow in number and certainty, and will waste no time in destroying their alliance. ==List of {{A|Coven}} roles== {| class="article-table" style="margin: 0px auto; width: 75%;" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" |- ! scope="col" |Role Name ! scope="col" |Role Alignment/Category ! scope="col" |Role Description |- |{{A|Coven Leader}}[[File:RoleIcon_CovenLeader.png|thumb|100px|left]] |{{A|Coven Evil}} |You may choose to control a player and use their ability on another player. If the {{A|Coven Leader}} dies and an {{A|Amnesiac}} remembers the role of the {{A|Coven Leader}}, then they will inherit the {{A|Necronomicon}} once the member who currently possesses it dies. Whoever has the {{A|Necronomicon}} becomes [[Detection Immunity|Detection Immune]] to the {{A|Sheriff}}. ==Dealing with The {{A|Coven}}== *{{A|Coven Leaders}} usually claim {{A|Lookout}}, so be very careful with {{A|Lookout}} claims. If someone claims controlled and a {{A|Lookout}} will has them visiting another player, it's possibly a {{A|Coven Leader}} faking genuine results. *{{A|Hex Masters}} don't have any {{A|Town}}-based claim-space with their investigation results. Someone who may be claiming to be {{A|Framed}} or {{A|Hexed}}, or if they claim {{A|Jester}}, may be a {{A|Hex Master}}. Have a {{A|Vigilante}} or {{A|Jailor}} kill them, especially if they claim to be a {{A|Jester}}. *{{A|Medusas}} commonly claim during the {{A|Day}} and focus around baiting people to visit them. If someone asks for any {{A|Town Protectives}} or if they claim {{A|Psychic}}, and multiple {{V|roles}} are {{A|stoned}} the next {{A|Day}}, that person is more than likely the {{A|Medusa}}. *{{A|Necromancers}} commonly claim {{A|Medium}} or {{A|Retributionist}}. Since they visit their reanimated target, a {{A|Tracker}} can quickly spot them as a {{A|Necromancer}}, and {{A|Spies}} can confirm their existence quickly. *{{A|Poisoners}} usually claim {{A|Sheriff}}. In addition to this, their targets are often outspoken about being {{A|poisoned}}. If you are a {{A|Lookout}}, unless you want to find out who the {{A|Doctor}} is, don't watch the {{A|poisoned}} player, and watch someone who you believe it is in the best interest to {{A|poison}}. {{A|Mayors}} are often the target of {{A|poison}}.  *{{A|Potion Masters}} usually claim {{A|Doctor}}; however, they cannot heal for 2 {{A|Nights}} after healing (until they have the {{A|Necronomicon}}). If a {{A|Doctor}} claim suddenly stops healing {{A|poisoned}} players for 2 {{A|Nights}}, or the {{A|Poisoner}} isn't active for 2 {{A|Nights}}, there's a {{A|Potion Master}} afoot. =={{A|Coven}} vs {{A|Mafia}} 1v1s== In all of these scenarios, a single remaining member of the {{A|Coven}} will usually have the {{A|Necronomicon}} and will be facing against either a {{A|Mafioso}} or the {{A|Godfather}}.
