*The {{A|Coven}} is the only [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] without a roleblocker. **The {{A|Coven Leader}} and {{A|Necromancer}}, however, can force a roleblock on people with their abilities. **Additionally, in {{A|Town Traitor (Coven)}}, a Traitor {{A|Tavern Keeper|Coven}} or {{A|Jailor|Coven}} is possible. *All {{A|Coven}} roles are [[Unique Role|unique roles]]. *The {{A|Coven Leader}} is the only role that replaces another role in the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. *The {{A|Coven}} is the only faction that lacks a role with a {{A|Day}} ability/attribute. *Similar to the {{A|Mafia}}, all {{A|Coven}} members will die when bitten by a {{A|Vampire}}. *In the [[Public Test Realm]], there used to be a now-scrapped {{A|Coven Support}} {{A|Alignment}}. Most notably, the only known role to fit in this {{A|Alignment}} was the {{A|Potion Master}}. *The {{A|Coven}} is the only [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] not available in [[Game Modes (ToS)|Classic]]. It can be accessed through the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. * Since the {{A|Coven}} is very similar to {{A|Mafia}}, refer to the {{A|Mafia}} page for some strategies to adopt into your own strategies. {{Navbox Roles}} [[fr:Loup-garou]][[ja:狼]] [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

Trapper (ToS).title: Trapper (ToS)
Trapper (ToS).wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Trapper}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |} {{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Trapper}}[[File:RoleIcon Trapper.png|thumb|center|100px]] |avatar=[[File:Achievement Trapper.png]] |alignment = {{A|Town Protective}} |attributes = Ignores [[Detection Immunity]]
Attack: Powerful
Defense: None |type = Protection
Investigate
Non-unique |priority = 1 |uses = Unlimited |actionself = Remove {{A|Trap}} |actionother = Set {{A|Trap}} |investigator = '''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be a {{InvResCVN2}}. |consigliere = Your target is waiting for a big catch. They must be a {{A|Trapper}}. |summary = You are an intelligent woodsman with a knack for Traps. |abilities = You may set up a Trap at another player's house. |attributestext = {{A|Traps}} take one day to build.
{{A|Traps}} can be torn down by selecting yourself at night.
You may only have one {{A|Trap}} out at a time. |goal = Hang every criminal and evildoer. |winwith = '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}''' |mustkill = '''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Vampires}}'''
'''{{A|Arsonist}}'''
'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Coven}}'''
'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}} {{Story}} ==Mechanics== *At {{A|Night}}, you will build a {{A|Trap}} if you do not have one ready to be placed. **If you are [[roleblocked]] on the {{A|Night}} you build your {{A|Trap}}, you '''will not''' build your {{A|Trap}} that {{A|Night}}. You will have to wait one extra {{A|Night}} to place it, you will still build it if you are controlled though. *On a {{A|Night}}, when you have a {{A|Trap}} ready to be placed, you can choose someone to place your {{A|Trap}} on. *If anyone visits the person you have placed your {{A|Trap}} on, the {{A|Trap}} is triggered and reveals all roles (not names) of people that visited your target. **{{A|Traps}} will show the true role of a player meaning they are not be deceived by {{A|Disguisers}}, {{A|Framers}}, {{A|Hex Masters}} and {{A|Arsonists}}. **If your target is attacked, your {{A|Trap}} will additionally deal a {{A|Powerful Attack}} to one attacker visiting them (including {{A|Vigilantes}} and {{A|Vampire Hunters}}), and will defend against one direct {{A|attack}}. ***{{A|Traps}} only defend against one direct attacker. This means that {{A|Hex Master}} with {{A|Necronomicon}} can kill through a {{A|Trap}} without triggering it, since they are [[Attribute|astral]] and do not count as a direct attacker. This also means someone with a Trap may still die if they are attacked by multiple roles. *You may only have one {{A|Trap}} on a player at a time; you cannot build more {{A|Traps}} before the current one is triggered or {{A|Dismantled}}. **When you have a {{A|Trap}} placed on someone, you can select yourself to take it and {{A|Dismantle}} it. Dismantling the {{A|Trap}} will prevent it from being triggered that {{A|Night}} but allow you to rebuild it immediately, so you can continue to place a new {{A|Trap}} on the next {{A|Night}}. *If you are converted into a {{A|Vampire}} with a {{A|Trap}} on a target, that {{A|Trap}} will not be removed. *If you are {{A|Controlled}} by the {{A|Coven Leader}} on a {{A|Night}} you may place your {{A|Trap}}, the {{A|Trap}} will be placed on the {{A|Coven Leader's}} secondary target. You will not know upon whom the {{A|Trap}} has been placed and you may not {{A|Dismantle}} it. *You will only visit the night you place your {{A|Trap}}. If your {{A|Trap}} is not triggered the night you place it, you '''will not''' visit if it is triggered on any following night. *If {{A|Necromancer's Ghoul}} attacks someone with a {{A|Trap}} on them and no other role visits that player, you will be told that your {{A|Trap}} attacked someone without seeing any roles. This will cause the counter-attack mechanic of the {{A|Trap}} to be removed, however the {{A|Trap}} will remain on the target - this means that future attackers can safely trigger your {{A|Trap}} and kill through it. You also won't be able to {{A|Dismantle}} the trap until it is triggered. This may be a bug. *Due to an inconsistent bug (as of [[Version History - Town of Salem|Version 3.3.12]]), you will sometimes '''not''' see {{A|reanimated}} corpses trigger your {{A|Traps}}. *You '''won't''' get the feedback that says ''"Your trap attacked someone!"'' when saving someone from a {{A|Vampire}} (this is a bug). *When you save someone from a {{A|Potion Master}} or {{A|Poisoner}}, your target will see the {{A|Bodyguard}}-specific message ''"You were attacked but someone fought off your attacker!"'' (this is a bug as well). ==Strategy== *[[File:SpecialLabel Trap_Building.png|thumb|The icon that appears next to you on the player list when you are building your {{A|Trap}}]][[File:SpecialLabel Trap_Ready.png|thumb|The icon that appears next to you on the player list when your {{A|Trap}} is ready to be placed]][[File:SpecialLabel Trap.png|thumb|The icon that appears next to your {{A|Trapped}} player on the player list when your {{A|Trap}} is placed]]You must wait a {{A|Night}} to build a {{A|Trap}} to use. Therefore, strategize to be able to place {{A|Traps}} that will be effective once they are built. *Two {{A|Trappers}} setting {{A|Traps}} at each other's houses gives both of them {{A|Powerful Defense}}, enabling them to protect each other if they are attacked. The only downside is that they might be destroyed from a normal visitor. As well as this, other important {{A|Town}} roles such as a {{A|Jailor}} or {{A|Mayor}} will not be protected. *Be careful of {{A|Ambushers}}, as they can trigger your {{A|Trap}} without dying (thereby wasting it), and if you visit the same target as them when you set your Trap, they will attack you if you are the only other visitor to their target. **However this confirms that the player you attempted to {{A|Trap}} is most likely not a {{A|Mafia}} role. *Unlike most other {{A|Townies}}, you don't always want to keep an accurate {{A|Last Will}}. Your {{A|Traps}} can still kill people after you die, so misleading evil roles about where your most recent {{A|Trap}} has been placed can sometimes benefit the {{A|Town}}. However, you should still write down the roles of the people who triggered your {{A|Traps}} somewhere, in case a {{A|Medium}} asks you for information *If a non-killing role hits your {{A|Trap}}, it will be expended and reveal the roles that set it off in the process. This has a number of applications: **You can distinguish between {{A|Tavern Keeper}} and {{A|Bootlegger}} claims, along with {{A|Investigator}} and {{A|Consigliere}} claims; all it takes is one entry in their {{A|Last Will}} that hit one of your {{A|Traps}}, and you'll know who they are. **You can precisely identify people's roles in conjunction with a {{A|Lookout}} or {{A|Tracker}}. (Do be aware, however, that if a {{A|Lookout}} watches your target, they will trigger your {{A|Trap}}.) **You can determine what roles are present, narrowing down the list of possible claims. This is of great benefit to the {{A|Town}}, especially in game modes with lots of claim space (such as [[All Any]]). **You can also easily identify silent killers such as an {{A|Arsonist}}, a {{A|Hex Master}}, and the {{A|Plaguebearer}}, which would normally take the town quite a while to find without the help of an {{A|Investigator}}. *If an important {{A|Townie}} is confirmed, you should not {{A|Trap}} them if there are other {{A|Town Protective}} roles alive, as it may be triggered by a {{A|Bodyguard}} or {{A|Crusader}} and will be wasted. If you are relatively certain that you are the only {{A|Town Protective}}, you should {{A|Trap}} them. *Ideally, you should try to {{A|Trap}} important {{A|Townies}} (like a confirmed {{A|Sheriff}}) who you think won't be protected by another {{A|Town Protective}}, as the {{A|Mafia}} or any other killing role might try to attack them, having come to the same conclusion as you. This will work best if the {{A|Jailor}} and/or {{A|Mayor}} has revealed themselves, as most, if not all {{A|Town Protectives}} will be on them (Note: keep in mind that the {{A|Doctor}} cannot heal a revealed {{A|Mayor}}, so they will most likely move on to other targets as well). **In many cases, your {{A|Trap}} could be the deciding factor for a {{A|Town}} victory in a 1v1 against several roles, like the {{A|Godfather}}, a {{A|Serial Killer}} a {{A|Werewolf}}, and so on. **Be careful of {{A|Crusaders}} though, as they will usually refrain from protecting either of these as well since they might kill another {{A|Town Protective}} by accident if they do so. *You can determine if a {{A|Necromancer}} exists. If a unique role (that is non-{{A|Town}}) hits your {{A|Trap}}, and no {{A|Amnesiacs}} have remembered that role, a {{A|Necromancer}} is in the game. **Additionally, if you get the message "Your Trap attacked someone.", yet no role was mentioned along with it, then your {{A|Trap}} attacked a {{A|Necromancer's}} {{A|Ghoul}}. This also confirms that the {{A|Necromancer}} has the {{A|Necronomicon}}. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{TrapperAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{TrapperMessages}} ==Trivia== *Prior to {{VH|Version 3.2.3}}, {{A|Trappers}} could still build their {{A|Trap}} while dueled by a {{A|Pirate}}, which is considered a [[roleblock]]. *There is currently a bug where a {{A|Trapped}} target will sometimes receive the {{A|Bodyguard}} protect message '''INSTEAD''' of the {{A|Trapper}} protect message. You can see the bug in a video linked [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EW8woxFziiI&t=17m00s here]. ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.12]] **Fixed {{A|Lookout}} seeing reanimated corpses visit twice *{{VH|3.3.0}} **The {{A|Trapper's}} "Trap Set" icon will now display on the player where the {{A|Trap}} has been set, instead of on the {{A|Trapper}} themselves. *{{VH|3.2.3}} **{{A|Coven Leader}} with {{A|Necronomicon}} will now die to {{A|Trap}} placed by controlled {{A|Trapper}} on themself. **{{A|Trapper}} will no longer die to {{A|attack}} if another {{A|Trapper}} has placed a {{A|Trap}} on them. **Dual {{A|Trappers}} can now save each other if they have placed {{A|Traps}} on each other and both are attacked. **{{A|Traps}} will now be removed when a player that left enters the [[graveyard]]. **{{A|Trappers}} are now [[Role block|role blocked]] from building their Trap by {{A|Pirates}}. **{{A|Traps}} placed by a dead {{A|Trapper}} are now removed after triggering. **{{A|Mafioso}} will now die to {{A|Trap}} placed on another {{A|Trapper}}. **Fixed a very complicated {{A|Trapper}}-{{A|Hex Master}} interaction that could result in a player dying to a {{A|Trap}} that should have previously triggered. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **Added a label to visually indicate that a {{A|Trap}} is being built for the {{A|Trapper}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_Trap_Building.png|30x30px]]). **Added a label to visually indicate that a {{A|Trap}} is ready to be placed for the {{A|Trapper}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_Trap_Ready.png|30x30px]]). **Added a label to visually indicate that a {{A|Trap}} is set on a player for the {{A|Trapper}} ([[File:SpecialLabel_Trap.png|30x30px]]). **The {{A|Trapper's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Trapper.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Trapper's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Trapper Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.5.1.10655}} **Fixed {{A|Guardian Angel}} "target was attacked" feedback. *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **{{A|Arsonists}} can no longer die to a {{A|Trapper}}. *{{VH|2.0.0.6582}} **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Ловец]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town Protective roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Powerful Attack]] [[Category:Town of Salem]] [[Category:Killing roles]]

Tracker (ToS).wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Tracker}}}} {| align="center" style="background: #98301e; color: white; border: 2px solid #f6a902; width: {{{width|auto}}}%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; {{roundy|30px}}" |- |}{{Coven Exclusive}} {{Infobox Role |nameandicon={{Amne|Tracker}}[[File:RoleIcon Tracker.png|thumb|left|100px]] |alignment = {{A|Town Investigative}} |avatar = [[File:Tracker Skin.png|150px]] |attributes = Ignores {{A|Detection Immunity}}
Attack: None
Defense: None |type = Investigation
Non-unique |priority = 3 |uses = |sheriff=You cannot find evidence of wrongdoing. Your target is innocent or great at hiding secrets! |investigator = '''{{A|Coven Expansion}} Results'''
Your target could be an {{InvResCVN10}}. |consigliere = Your target is a skilled[[wikipedia:Sic|[sic]]] in the art of tracking. They must be a {{A|Tracker}}. |summary = You are a skilled tracker who will follow their prey to any destination. |abilities = Track one person at night to see who they visit. |attributestext = None. |goal = Hang every criminal and evildoer. |winwith = '''{{A|Town}}'''
'''{{A|Survivor}}''' |mustkill = '''{{A|Mafia}}'''
'''{{A|Vampires}}'''
'''{{A|Arsonist}}'''
'''{{A|Serial Killer}}'''
'''{{A|Werewolf}}'''
'''{{A|Coven}}'''
'''{{A|Plaguebearer}}'''
'''{{A|Pestilence}}'''
'''{{A|Juggernaut}}''' }}{{Story}} ==Mechanics== *The {{A|Tracker}} can select one target at {{A|Night}} to see who the target visits. *If the target does not visit anyone or has an {{A|Astral}} visit, the {{A|Tracker}} will receive no notification. *If the target does visit another player, the {{A|Tracker}} will see "Your target visited [other player's name]!" *You will not know the action used on another player if the target visits another player, unless it is revealed the next {{A|day}}, such as they were killed, {{A|Poisoned}}, etc. *If you visit a {{A|Veteran}} on alert, you will die. However, if you track someone who visits a {{A|Veteran}} on alert, you will ''not'' die. *If the {{A|Tracker}} visits a {{A|Necromancer}} or a {{A|Retributionist}} controlling a dead corpse, they will see which dead player they are visiting. **An {{A|Amnesiac}} will not visit the person whose role they are attempting to remember. *If your target visits someone who is {{A|Transported}}, you will see your target visit whoever they were {{A|Transported}} into visiting and '''not''' their original selected target. *If your target visited two people, this means your target is either a {{A|Transporter}} or a {{A|Disguiser}}. ==Strategy== *Early in the game, try to track people who barely talk. Evils have a tendency to stay silent. **Track suspicious players; this could potentially reveal that they visited a player who was killed during the {{A|Night}}. *The {{A|Tracker}} is mostly a team player that works with other roles to find out the roles of people being tracked. Try to find other {{A|Town Investigative}} and {{A|Town Protectives}} to track down evil roles that do not kill immediately. *If you know who the {{A|Doctor}} is and you think that you have tracked a {{A|Poisoner}}, then it may be a good idea to whisper who the {{A|Poisoner}} targeted. This way, the {{A|Doctor}} could heal the poisoned player. Of course, most players fake that they are poisoned so this strategy may not be useful. However, if the player is [[Blackmailer|blackmailed]], this will work as an effective backup plan. *Avoid tracking {{A|Transporter}} claims. If they transport themselves, you will not see them visit their targets, and can put suspicion on the {{A|Transporter}} until they claimed to have transported themselves. *If you track the same person each {{A|Night}} and they keep visiting different targets, try to communicate with a {{A|Sheriff}} or {{A|Investigator}} to see the target's investigation results. If the people that are being visited show up as {{A|Bodyguard}}, {{A|Godfather}}, or {{A|Arsonist}} to the {{A|Investigator}}, then the person you are tracking is an {{A|Arsonist}}. Likewise, this strategy can be used with a {{A|Sheriff}} to find out a {{A|Framer}} or {{A|Hex Master}}. If the targets that are being visited show up as suspicious to the {{A|Sheriff}}, then the person you are tracking is likely a {{A|Framer}}/{{A|Hex Master}}. *If you find a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}} and there's a confirmed {{A|Serial Killer}} kill, try tracking them. If they die the next {{A|Day}} from a {{A|Serial Killer}} and their {{A|Last Will}} was bloodied, you will know the identity of the {{A|Serial Killer}}. *Try tracking {{A|Town Protective}} claims. If they visit {{A|Medusa}} and are {{A|Stoned}} the next day, you will know the identity of {{A|Medusa}}. *Sometimes, knowing ''whether'' someone visited can be as useful as knowing ''who'' they visited. **Some hard-to-spot roles, like the {{A|Arsonist}}, {{A|Hex Master}}, and {{A|Plaguebearer}}, will usually visit every single {{A|Night}}; if you track someone and they don't visit, it's unlikely that they're one of those roles. If they suspect a {{A|Tracker}} will investigate them, they may stay home to avoid suspicion, but this is rare. **Similarly, if someone claims a non-visiting role, such as {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Survivor}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Amnesiac}}, or {{A|Psychic}} or a role that produces obvious results after a visit, like {{A|Vigilante}}, then you can check by visiting them - although again, a smart evil might stay home right after claiming one of those roles. ***Additionally, if they are the {{A|Godfather}} (with a {{A|Mafioso}}) or the {{A|Hex Master}} (with the {{A|Necronomicon}}), you will not see their visits. *Two roles can be caught visiting two people: the {{A|Transporter}} and the {{A|Disguiser}}. Therefore, in theory, if you see two visits for your target, they are definitely one of those roles; however, interpreting that they are a {{A|Transporter}} is complicated by the fact that {{A|Transporters}} often transport themselves. **If you see two visits, and they both claim to be transported, there is a {{A|Transporter}} in game, and one of them is the person you targeted, then you did ''not'' target the {{A|Transporter}} but got transported onto them. Therefore, one of the two you ''didn't'' select as your target that {{A|Night}} is the {{A|Transporter}}. **Trying to deliberately verify if someone is a {{A|Transporter}} only works if they don't self-transport (if they do, you'll get the results for their other target, and therefore probably won't see two visits). **To determine if you tracked a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Disguiser}}, ask the targeted players if they were transported. If not, the tracked player is most likely a {{A|Disguiser}}. **In the case of a {{A|Disguiser}}, one of the targets is a {{A|Mafia}} member, unless one of the targets is the {{A|Disguiser}} themselves. *Your results can be very effective when paired with a {{A|Spy}}: **If a {{A|Spy}} sees a {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} visit to a person on the same {{A|Night}} that your target visited them, your target ''may'' be a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}}. Keep in mind, however, that it's possible that there was a second visitor who was the actual evil you're looking for. **On the other hand, if a {{A|Spy}} ''doesn't'' see any {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} visits to the person your target visited, then your target is likely not a member of the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Coven}} respectively; keep track of people who are 'cleared' like this in your will. **Keep in mind the {{A|Disguiser}} can mess with the {{A|Spy}}'s results. *If your target visits on the same {{A|Night}} that a killer kills someone else, then your target was definitely not that killer. (However, keep in mind that if they're a member of the {{A|Mafia}}, they could later become the killer if the current one dies.) *If you see your target visit a dead person who is not a {{A|Town}} role, they are a {{A|Necromancer}}. *If you track a {{A|Jailor}}, you will get no results. {{A|Jailors}} do not leave their house, even if they choose to jail someone. *Remember that only a {{A|Disguiser}} can normally visit other Mafia. Unless a {{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Transporter}} is involved, when you see a {{A|Mafia}} visit another, that means the person they visited cannot be {{A|Mafia}}. *If you have visited someone who has not visited another player, they may be an {{A|Amnesiac}}, especially if they hint at being neutral or outright claim a {{A|Neutral Benign}} role. If they turn against the {{A|Town}}, there is a good chance that this is the person in question. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{TrackerAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{TrackerMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Tracker}} was added into the game as a result of the [https://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/viewtopic.php?f=27&t=118494 Testing Grounds]. ==History== *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.3.11]] **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} still getting information when witched/controlled by {{A|Coven Leader}} *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|3.1.14]] **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} incorrectly seeing someone visiting when [[Role block|role blocked]], dueled, and controlled. **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} tracking {{A|Godfather}} bug. **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} detecting {{A|Godfather}} visiting victim when {{A|Godfather}} orders {{A|Mafioso}} to kill the victim. **Fixed incorrect {{A|Tracker}} results when {{A|Mafioso}} picks one victim but {{A|Godfather}} chooses another. *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.5.5.12200]] **The {{A|Tracker}}'s role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Tracker.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Tracker}}'s circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Tracker Circled.png|30x30px]]). *[[Version_History - Town of Salem|2.0.0.6582]] **Introduced. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Следопыт]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Town Investigative roles]] [[Category:Investigative roles]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

'''{{A|Juggernaut}}'''}}{{Story|Escort}} ==Mechanics== * You may choose to {{A|Roleblock}} someone each {{A|Night}}, which prevents them from using their {{A|Night}} ability. ** [[Abilities (ToS)|Role block Immune]] roles, such as a {{A|Bootlegger}}, will not be affected. ** You cannot {{A|Roleblock}} [[roles (ToS)|roles]] with {{A|Day}} abilties, because you have a {{A|Night}} ability. ** You may {{A|Roleblock}} someone who left the game the same {{A|Day}}/{{A|Night}}. However, this is usually pointless, and is not recommended. * If you {{A|Roleblock}} a {{A|Serial Killer}}, a {{A|Werewolf}} during a {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Night}}, or {{A|Pestilence}}, they will attack you. ** This does not apply if they are jailed. ** A {{A|Serial Killer}} will only attack you if they are not Cautious. If they are Cautious, the {{A|Roleblock}} will fail, and you will live. *** When {{A|Roleblocking}} a non-Cautious {{A|Serial Killer}}, you will receive the message "You were murdered by the {{A|Serial Killer}} you visited!", and your {{A|Last Will}} will be covered in blood and unreadable. This does not apply to a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}. ****If you did not target them directly, this message will not appear, and the normal {{A|Serial Killer}} death message will appear. ** {{A|Town Protective}} roles (except {{A|Trapper}}), the {{A|Potion Master}}, and a {{A|Guardian Angel}} are capable of defending against this attack. *** However, with a {{A|Serial Killer}}, if you then die from any other cause, your {{A|Last Will}} will '''still''' be bloodied, even though the {{A|Serial Killer}} death cause does not show up. ** When {{A|Roleblocking}} a {{A|Werewolf}} or {{A|Pestilence}}, you and all other visitors to your target will be attacked. *** In the case of a {{A|Werewolf}}, they will stay home to do so. Their original target will survive, provided they do not visit the {{A|Werewolf}}. ** A {{A|Serial Killer}} and {{A|Pestilence}} will attack their original target, even if the {{A|Serial Killer}} was Cautious. * There are several roles that are [[Role block Immunity|immune]] to your {{A|Roleblock}}; {{A|Witches}}/{{A|Coven Leaders}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, {{A|Veterans}}, other {{A|Tavern Keepers}}, {{A|Transporters}}, {{A|Retributionists}}, {{A|Necromancers}}, {{A|Pirates}}, {{A|Serial Killers}}, and {{A|Bootleggers}}. * In a situation where you are alone against a single evil role, the [[Victory (ToS)|stalemate]] detector will make you lose, despite being able to prevent the other player from killing you. **{{A|Tavern Keeper}} vs {{A|Juggernaut}}, is the only exception, the game will not automatically end in this 1v1 scenario. This is most likely '''not''' intended. * If a {{A|Pirate}} duels you, you will still be able to {{A|Roleblock}} someone due to your {{A|Roleblock Immunity}}. However, you will be killed if they win. ==Strategy== * One of the main purposes of the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is to hunt for the {{A|Godfather}} (or {{A|Mafioso}} if there is none) who lacks a {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combination. If you {{A|Roleblock}} someone and there are no {{A|Mafia}} kills the following {{A|day}}, it is possible you've found the {{A|Godfather}}, at least if one out of the {{A|Mafioso}} and {{A|Godfather}} are dead or you are in a mode where the pairing is are not guaranteed to exist. Things to consider: ** If there is both a {{A|Mafioso}} and a {{A|Godfather}}, this is basically useless against the Mafia, and any lack of {{A|Mafia}} kill on a particular {{A|Night}} is probably unrelated. ** Even when there is only one {{A|Mafia Killing}}, it is not ''certain'' that you found the killer. The killer might have attacked a target with a form of defense, was Away From Keyboard (A.F.K), or have simply chosen not to attack. ** Regardless, when there is no {{A|Mafia}} kill, it is generally a good idea to {{A|Roleblock}} the same person again to double check; if {{A|Roleblocking}} the same target multiple {{A|Nights}} results in no {{A|Mafia}} kills every time, it is ''usually'' safe to assume your target is the {{A|Godfather}}. ** When you do feel you've identified the {{A|Godfather}}, you should keep {{A|Roleblocking}} him repeatedly and note this in your will (so people will know to act against them if you die somehow.) You ''may'' want to out him to the town, but doing so isn't always necessary - if you've actually found the {{A|Godfather}}, then {{A|Roleblocking}} him repeatedly will lock down the {{A|Mafia's}} main method of killing while the town searches for other Mafia members, and revealing yourself exposes you to a {{A|Witch}}. ** These same strategies apply to {{A|Coven}} roles that produce obvious deaths. It does not apply to the {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles; the {{A|Serial Killer}} and {{A|Arsonist}} produces no visible effect, while the {{A|Werewolf}} will kill you, so you cannot identify them by this method. When hunting a {{A|Poisoner}}, pay attention to if anyone announces they were {{A|Poisoned}} (and remember that the Poisoner themselves might lie and say they were {{A|Poisoned}} after you {{A|Roleblocked}} them). * If a {{A|Janitor}} has been consistently {{A|Cleaning}} the {{A|Mafia}} kills, and the {{A|Mafia}} killed last Night without {{A|Cleaning}}, then the person you {{A|Roleblocked}} is almost certainly the {{A|Janitor}}, unless they already used all three of their {{A|Cleanings}}. *In most cases, there is no reason to {{A|Roleblock}} someone multiple times unless you have some reason to believe they're evil; when you don't know who's evil, you should {{A|Roleblock}} different people each {{A|Night}} to search for a killer. Remember, however, that if the current kill capable {{A|Mafia}} role dies, a new person will inherit the role, and that could be someone you blocked before that point. It might be helpful to put a divider in your {{A|Last Will}} after the point where the kill capable {{A|Mafia}} role died as a reminder that anyone ''after'' that point can't be the new {{A|Mafioso}}. ** Even when you've identified someone as evil, most of the {{A|Mafia}} roles other than the killers are weak, so {{A|Roleblocking}} them produces only a marginal benefit. Provided there's no {{A|Mafioso}} + {{A|Godfather}} combo, your time is usually better-spent hunting for the {{A|Godfather}} rather than repeatedly {{A|Roleblocking}} someone just because you think they're evil. **However, if a {{A|Vigilante}} is revealed and there's a {{A|Witch}} in game, you may want to continually roleblock the {{A|Vigilante}} until the {{A|Witch}} is dead, to prevent the {{A|Vigilante}} from being controlled into shooting a townie. The same applies for a {{A|Jailor}} who has jailed a revealed {{A|Mayor}} or last {{A|Mafia Killing}}. * If you find the {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}} (on a {{A|Full Moon}}) or an {{A|Ambusher}} (on your target) during your hunt for killers, you will be attacked by them and probably die. Therefore, it is imperative to '''keep records in your {{A|Last Will}}'''. ** Conversely, this means that anyone you've {{A|Roleblocked}} under those circumstances without dying cannot be the {{A|Werewolf}}. This is another reason why keeping a {{A|Last Will}} of all your {{A|Roleblocks}} is important; you may also want to indicate {{A|Full Moon}} {{A|Nights}} in your will to make it more clear that those people have been cleared of that suspicion. ** You can use this to your advantage and do a process of elimination. As long as a {{A|Transporter}} or {{A|Witch}} doesn't interfere, you could make a list of suspects of being the {{A|Werewolf}} because you haven't {{A|Roleblocked}} them. ** If you die by the {{A|Serial Killer}} when you did not visit him, you will get the standard death message. If you did visit the {{A|Serial Killer}}, you will get a special message ("You were murdered by the {{A|Serial Killer}} you visited!"). Make absolutely certain to convey this to any {{A|Mediums}} the following Night. ** However, if you died to the {{A|Werewolf}} you {{A|Roleblocked}}, you will NOT get a special message; you will only know you were attacked by them. * Think hard about whether you want to {{A|Roleblock}} at random; there are several things to consider, which vary depending on game mode: **{{A|Roleblocking}} {{A|Town}} could interfere with vital abilities. ** {{A|Roleblocking}} a {{A|Serial Killer}} or (on a {{A|Full Moon}}) a {{A|Werewolf}} will get you killed. However, if you have been keeping a good will, you can possibly nab the {{A|Werewolf}} in the process. ** You can find the {{A|Godfather}} as described above, but ''only'' when there's no {{A|Mafioso}} / {{A|Godfather}} combo. Therefore, in modes like Ranked where that combination is guaranteed, you may want to start blocking at random only once one of them is dead. ** The {{A|Coven}} is more vulnerable to {{A|Roleblocks}} in general, since their kill messages are unique unlike the {{A|Godfather}} & {{A|Mafioso}}; however, most of them don't produce obvious effects until they have the {{A|Necronomicon}} and some {{A|Coven}} roles are immune to your role blocks outright, so you may want to only {{A|Roleblock}} at random once the {{A|Necronomicon}} appears and there's no {{A|Coven Leader}} or {{A|Necromancer}}, or if hunting a {{A|Poisoner}}. Hunting a {{A|Poisoner}} like this also risks {{A|Roleblocking}} a {{A|Doctor}} who would otherwise save the poisoned victim, of course. ** Random {{A|Roleblocks}} have the advantage of producing a useful will for you that other people can confirm; while you may fall under suspicion of being a {{A|Bootlegger}}, a {{A|Spy}} can generally clear you of this by noting that no Mafia members visited the people you {{A|Roleblocked}}, and even without that it's still useful to be able to avoid suspicion for all evil roles but one. * {{A|Roleblocking}} the {{A|Mafioso}} will cause the {{A|Godfather}} to attack the target himself instead of the {{A|Mafioso}}. Therefore, if you're in a game with a guaranteed {{A|Mafioso}} and {{A|Godfather}} combination, and the {{A|Godfather}} dies to a {{A|Veteran}} or {{A|Bodyguard}} before the {{A|Mafioso}} dies, then you should try {{A|Roleblocking}} your target again. If this results in no {{A|Mafia}} kills the following {{A|day}}, then ''continue {{A|Roleblocking}} whoever you blocked that {{A|Night}}'' since they are possibly the new {{A|Godfather}}. * Normally, when there is both a {{A|Godfather}} and a {{A|Mafioso}}, the {{A|Mafioso}} will leave his {{A|Death Note}} at the target, not the {{A|Godfather}}; but if you {{A|Roleblock}} the {{A|Mafioso}}, the {{A|Godfather's}} {{A|Death Note}} will be left instead. Therefore, if the {{A|Mafia's}} {{A|Death Note}} suddenly changes, it may be a hint that you have {{A|Roleblocked}} the {{A|Mafioso}}, especially if you {{A|Roleblock}} someone else and the {{A|Death Note}} changes back the next {{A|Night}}. ** Note that the {{A|Mafioso}} can frequently change his {{A|Death Note}}, so do not accuse them unless you have other proof. **This strategy is useless if the {{A|Godfather}} copies the {{A|Mafioso's}} death note or if neither of them use {{A|Death Notes}}. * If a {{A|Town Investigative}} finds a possible {{A|Mafia Killing}} role, you should {{A|Roleblock}} them to keep them from killing anyone and to confirm that they are indeed a member of the {{A|Mafia}}. * {{A|Roleblocking}} early can be useful since it confirms there is a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}}, but has the risk of preventing {{A|Townies}} from protecting and investigating other players. Generally speaking, it's a good strategy to {{A|Roleblock}} on the first {{A|Night}} in game modes where the {{A|Mafia}} is likely to have only one killer (because the benefit of {{A|Roleblocking}} that killer is high enough to outweigh the risk of disrupting a {{A|Townie}} for a {{A|Night}}, and because you want to start narrowing down who the kill capable {{A|Mafia}} role is as fast as possible); it makes considerably less sense to do so in game modes like {{A|Classic Mode}} or {{A|Ranked}} where the {{A|Mafia}} is guaranteed to start with both the {{A|Godfather}} and {{A|Mafioso}}. * Once either a {{A|Mafioso}} or {{A|Godfather}} has died, the {{A|Mafia}} can only have one kill capable {{A|Mafia}} role (unless an {{A|Amnesiac}} or {{A|Forger}} interferes); from that point on you should ''always'' {{A|Roleblock}} every {{A|Night}}. If there are no {{A|Neutral Killing}} roles, finding the last {{A|Mafia Killing}} role can often singlehandedly win the game. * When you do find and {{A|Roleblock}} the {{A|Godfather}}, it isn't necessarily a good idea to try and get him hanged immediately; that would just cause a new member of the {{A|Mafia}} to become the {{A|Mafioso}}. As long as you have him blocked, the {{A|Mafia}} can't kill (and it's unlikely you'll get ''forged'' or {{A|Cleaned}} with the {{A|Mafia}} unable to kill, so even if you do die, they'll probably get hanged when your {{A|Last Will}} is revealed). If you find the {{A|Arsonist}} or {{A|Juggernaut}}, try the same strategy. This will prevent them from killing and allow your {{A|Town Investigatives}} to safely search for the remaining criminals. ** Remember that, in this situation, if there is a {{A|Serial Killer}}, {{A|Werewolf}} or an {{A|Ambusher}} + {{A|Witch}} combo and you are confirmed, you will most likely die. In this case, you should try to hang them or at least put it very clearly in your {{A|Last Will}}. ** Also, remember that the {{A|Transporter}} has a higher priority than you and that the {{A|Witch}} can control you; these things can potentially free a {{A|Mafia Killing}} role who you thought you had pinned down. In particular, the danger of being controlled means you should never announce that you're {{A|Roleblocking}} a {{A|Mafia Killing}} role unless you intend to try and get them hanged the same {{A|day}}. *If you're playing Ranked and the {{A|Mayor}} reveals {{A|day}} 1, it's usually best to block him on {{A|Night 1}}. You are almost twice as likely to get a "bad" visit (blocking a {{A|Town Investigative}}, {{A|Town Protective}}, dying to {{A|Serial Killer}}/{{A|Ambusher}}) than to get a "good" visit (blocking a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Arsonist}}). Many of your visits will be "neutral" (blocking a {{A|Medium}}, {{A|Jester}}, {{A|Bootlegger}}, or {{A|Godfather}} while there is a {{A|Mafioso}}) that doesn't have much value either way. **One major value of role-blocking early is that you confirm that there is a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}} in the game. Most {{A|Bootleggers}} will be trying to help the {{A|Mafia}}, and anyways, they have a much higher chance of a "good" visit. Therefore, it is probably a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} that is blocking the {{A|Mayor}}, not a {{A|Bootlegger}}. **However, as soon as the {{A|Godfather}} or {{A|Mafioso}} is killed; the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} should immediately begin blocking to narrow down the suspects of who the {{A|Godfather}} is. If there was a kill when you blocked someone, you know they cannot be the {{A|Godfather}} (unless they were transported, of course). **The importance of {{A|Roleblocking}} the {{A|Mayor}} somewhat decreases as more {{A|Townies}} die, but it is still usually smart to wait until at least {{A|Night 3}} before coming off the {{A|Mayor}} (unless the {{A|Mafioso}} dies). This is because "bad" visits also have a slight increase; (roles like {{A|Town Killing}} and {{A|Werewolf}} are more likely to end up being {{A|Roleblocked}}). *You can {{A|Roleblock}} the youngest {{A|Vampire}} in order to prevent them from biting or converting someone that {{A|Night}}. It sometimes may be best to force a draw between the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Vampires}} if no other options are available. **If you are converted to a {{A|Vampire}}, you will lose your {{A|Roleblock Immunity}}. *Be very careful if you visit someone who is confirmed to be a {{A|Town}} role (like a {{A|Vigilante}}), as the {{A|Mafia}} or {{A|Serial Killer}} may try to kill them too. A {{A|Lookout}} may see you visit and you may get [[Hanging (ToS)|hanged]]. ==[[Achievements (ToS)|Achievements]]== {{TavernKeeperAchievements}} ==[[Messages (ToS)|Messages]]== {{TavernKeeperMessages}} ==Trivia== *The {{A|Tavern Keeper's}} skin ([[Avatars (ToS)|Candy]]) has a very striking resemblance to the Disney character [http://disney.wikia.com/wiki/Jessica_Rabbit Jessica Rabbit.] *Prior to {{VH|Version 2.0.0.6537}}, a {{A|Serial Killer}} would attack a {{A|Tavern Keeper}} for {{A|Roleblocking}} them even if they were jailed and/or executed. *[[File:Escort achievement.png|thumb|right|75px|{{A|Tavern Keeper's}} achievement and statistic icon]]When looking at in-game [[statistics]] or [[achievements (ToS)|achievements]], the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} is one of two roles (the other being the {{A|Forger}}) that has their icon different from the actual role icon found during gameplay. It appears to be rotated to the right. *If you are killed by the {{A|Serial Killer}} on the first {{A|day}}, there is only a ~52% chance that you have {{A|Roleblocked}} them. Of course, everyone would know whether or not you did {{A|Roleblock}} them by seeing the bloodied {{A|Last Will}}. **Proof: Let R = event {{A|Roleblocked}} {{A|Serial Killer}} {{A|Night 1}} (N1), K = event killed by {{A|Serial Killer}} N1. P(A) represents the percentage chance that an event, A, occurs. P(A|B) represents the chance that event A happens when we know that B also happens. To understand this, imagine two coins. You flip the first and it comes up as heads. Here's a sample space where possible outcomes from now on are bold - {| class="article-table" | | colspan="3" |Coin 1 |- | rowspan="3" |Coin 2 | |H |T |- |H |'''HH''' |TH |- |T |'''HT''' |TT |} Let Hx = event that coin 1 turns up heads, followed by flip x from Coin 2 HH = event heads comes up twice. We want to find P(HH|Hx). Usually, the sample space is equal to 1 and all probabilities are a fraction of 1, the sum of all probabilities, making them equal to themselves and relative to the whole sample space, but there are results in the complete sample space that we want to ignore; these are ones where coin 1 shows tails. To find P(HH|Hx), we can create a smaller sample space within the whole one which only includes results where Coin 1 shows heads, represented in bold. Now we can find P(HH) relative to the smaller sample space, where P(HH) (which is 1/4 relative to the whole sample space) becomes a fraction of 1/2, the size of the smaller sample space (set Hx) when the results have been narrowed down to occurrences within the smaller sample space. This P(HH) relative to the set Hx is equal to P(HH|Hx). P(HH|Hx) = (1/4)/(1/2) = 1/4 x 2 = '''1/2''' '''P(HH|Hx) = 1/2''' *We need to find P(R|K). Like in our example, we want to determine the size of the smaller sample space of the set K, which is equal to P(K). There are two ways that Event K can happen: *#The {{A|Tavern Keeper}} {{A|Roleblocked}} the {{A|Serial Killer}} . There is a 1/14 chance of this happening in a Classic game assuming nobody leaves the lobby. *#The {{A|Tavern Keeper}} ''did not distract the {{A|Serial Killer}} '' and the {{A|Serial Killer}} killed the {{A|Tavern Keeper}} naturally. This is 13/14 x 1/14 = 13/196 These two ways are mutually exclusive (there is no overlap between them) so that certain possibilities aren't counted twice. P(K) = 1/14 + 13/196 = 0.138 (3 dp) *P(R) as a fraction of 0.138, making it relative to the smaller sample space of set K, is equal to P(R|K). We already know that P(R) = 1/14. P(R|K) = (1/14)/0.138 = 51.85% (2 dp) ==History== *{{VH|3.3.11}} **Role renamed to {{A|Tavern Keeper}}. Some assets (i.e. Scrolls) were not updated, leaving several references to the prior role identity. **Updated {{A|Tavern Keeper's}} icon to a placeholder ([[File:RoleIcon TavernKeeper.png|30x30px]]), previous icon was ([[File:RoleIcon Escort.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|3.2.4}} **Reanimated {{A|Ambusher}} will no longer attack roles that attempted to visit but were {{A|Roleblocked}}. *{{VH|3.1.14}} **Added {{A|Escort}} vs. {{A|Vampire}} [[stalemate]] detector. **Fixed {{A|Tracker}} incorrectly seeing someone visiting when {{A|Roleblocked}}. *{{VH|2.5.5.12200}} **The {{A|Escort's}} role icon has been changed. Old one was [[File:Achievement Escort.png|30x30px]]. **Added {{A|Escort's}} circled role icon ([[File:RoleIcon Escort Circled.png|30x30px]]). *{{VH|2.3.2.9706}} **{{A|Medusa}} vs. {{A|Escort}} is now a {{A|Coven}} victory. *{{VH|Town of Salem Release}} **Introduced as {{A|Escort}}. {{Navbox Roles}} [[ru:Спутница|ru:Спутн]] [[Category:Town Support roles]] [[Category:Town roles]] [[Category:Roles]] [[Category:Role blocking]] [[Category:No Attack]] [[Category:No Defense]] [[Category:Roleblock Immune]] [[Category:Town of Salem]]

*The {{A|Fast Mode}} modifier halves the amount of time players have for discussion and voting during the {{A|Day}}.

Friends (ToS).title: Friends (ToS)
Friends (ToS).wikitext:
{{BetterImage| "Player Left Lobby" and "Invite Accepted" images with transparent background (Low Priority)}} [[File:Offlinefriendlist.png|alt=A friends list with 35 friends and all players friended offline|thumb|A friends list.]] '''Friends''' are a feature in Town of Salem. It gives you the opportunity to add players to your own party and enter a game together, as well as send private messages. The friends list can be brought up in the main menu. ==How to add a friend== Players can have up to 500 friends.

'''Sending a Request:''' #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow human figure. #Look on the top right of the screen. There should be a button with that same yellow human figure with a green + sign next to it. #Type in the '''Username''' of the person you wish to add, a.k.a. the name they log in with. #Click the "Add" button in the middle of the screen. '''Receiving a Request:''' #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow bell. :*There will also be a little pop-up notification in the bottom right of the screen. #Look on the right side of the screen. Hover over the username of the person who has added you as a friend. #Select "Accept" to become friends or select "Decline" to decline the request. :*If a request is accepted or declined, no notification is sent to the other user. ==Removing a friend== #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow human figure. #Look on the right side of the screen. Click on the friend you wish to remove. #In the chat box, look on the top left of the chat box. There should be a button with that same yellow human figure crossed out by a white /. #Click the "Ok" button in the middle of the screen. :*No notification is sent to the person who was removed as a friend. ==Best Friends== [[File:Add Best Friend.png|thumb|180px]] [[File:Remove Best Friend.png|thumb|180px]] [[File:Best Friend in List.png|thumb|180px]] #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow human figure. #Look on the right side of the screen. Click on the friend you wish to make into your best friend. #Look on the top of the menu. There will be a star button. If the star button is yellow, then they are already your best friend. #Click on the button to toggle best friendship. This will not affect how you appear on their screen. #Best friends will show before other users in the friends menu, and will have a golden name in lobbies. ==Blocking a user== #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow human figure. #Look on the right side of the screen. Click on the friend you wish to block. #Look on the top of the menu. There will be a red circle. #Click on the button to block the user. #Blocked users will be unable to send you friend requests, and will have a red name in lobbies. ==Messaging a friend== #Look on the top left of the screen. There should be a button with a yellow human figure. #Look on the right side of the screen. Click on the friend you wish to chat with. #Type your message inside the chat box, then send. Messages will appear as a notification. Upon logging out, any and all messages are removed and these conversations cannot be recovered. In addition, if a player is not online or is not at the home screen, they will not be able to receive messages. If a friend goes offline as you are chatting, you will still be unable to send them messages.  ==Light Notes== Beside your friend's name, there will be a circle with varying colors. The color of the light depends on whether your friend is present or not. *'''Green:''' ONLINE. Your friend is not in a game, invite away! *'''Purple:''' IN LOBBY. Your friend is currently in a lobby, waiting for the [[host]] or whatever they're up to. *'''Yellow:''' IN GAME. Your friend is currently in a game. *'''Dark Gray:''' AWAY. Your friend is online and not in a game, but has not done anything for a little while. *'''Gray:''' OFFLINE. Your friend is not playing Town of Salem right now.  If your friend owns the {{A|Coven Expansion}}, they will have a red moon around their circle. [[File:Friend_Coven_Online_New.png|25x25px]] == Parties == '''Parties''' allow friends to chat and enter a game together. The Host is marked with a [[File:Host_Crown_New.PNG|25x25px]] crown at the start of their name. The Host can invite people to their party, [[File:Host Crown New.PNG]] give other players their host permission, [[File:Invite_Arrow_New.png]]the permission to invite players, or [[File:Kick_X_New.png]] kick people from the party. People with invite powers have a [[File:Invite_Arrow_New.png|25x25px]] arrow at the start of their name. They can invite other players to join their party. The players invited to the party are seen in the middle of the screen. A player with a [[File:Party_Pending_Envelope.png|25x30px]] next to their name currently has a pending invite. Players with [[File:Party_env_accepted.png|25x30px]] next to their name have accepted a Party Invite and Have joined the party. Players with [[File:Party_Inv_Dec.png|25x30px]] next to their name have declined the party invite. Players with [[File:Party_Left_New.PNG|25x30px]] next to their name have either left the party or have been kicked by the party host. The Host is the person who starts the game whenever they wish. If the number of players in their party fits in an existing lobby, the Host and their party will be put in an existing lobby. If the number of players in the party exceeds the amount of free spots in an existing lobby, the party will be put in a new lobby with the party's Host as the lobby's Host. If a player who owns the {{A|Coven Expansion}} has invite permissions in a Coven party, they can only invite players with Coven to join. Attempting to invite a player who does not own it will result in a message appearing next to the invited player saying "No Coven." The invited player will not be notified that they were invited. The host of a {{A|Coven Expansion}} party can switch to Classic Mode if they want, however the host of a Classic party can only switch to a {{A|Coven Expansion}} mode if all players in the party own the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. Party members will have a {{A|Coven}} Icon next to their name if they own the {{A|Coven Expansion}}. === '''How to Create a Party''' === * Once you are logged in, select "Play" at the top of the screen. A menu will pop up. * At the bottom of this menu, select "Create a Party". You are now the Host of the party. * At the top-right of the screen you may select which game mode you would like to play with your party. * At the bottom-right of the screen you may select "Invite" to invite players to join your party. * Once you've selected players to join, select "Invite Players" at the bottom of the screen to officially send your invitations. Wait for your friends to accept the invitation. * Once ready to begin, select "Start" at the bottom-right of the screen. You and your party will be sent to a lobby to play together. == Referring a friend == [[File:Refer Box.png|thumb|350x350px]] ==='''How to refer'''=== * When a friend decides to sign up for an account, they may refer a person who told them about the game. This may only be done during the signup. ==='''Rewards for being referred'''=== * When a friend refers you and also makes a purchase using real life currency, your count for referring friends will increase. This purchase may be buying the game, purchasing in-game promotions, and so on. * If a friend has referred you before {{VH|Version 1.2.0}}, they do not have to make a purchase but rather they must complete 10 games. For more information, view the official [http://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/viewtopic.php?f=11&t=26003 Town of Salem forums].[[File:Friend Not Food Unlocked.png|alt|right|225x225px]][[File:Grim Reaper Unlocked.png|alt|right|225x225px]]

Premium players are individuals who have spent money on the game. {{Quote1|quote=When a premium user reaches 10 games played they will receive 5 referral codes that they can give to their friends. Getting Started.title: Getting Started
Getting Started.wikitext: {{BetterImage}}New to the game? This is an overview of how to get started with playing [[Town of Salem]] and what you need to know for the basics of the game! ==Starting the Game - What you should do== You need an [http://www.blankmediagames.com/phpbb/index.php account], which will work for the forum and the game, but not this wiki. If you want to make an account for this wiki, you have to make a [https://auth.fandom.com/register Fandom account]. You can log in from your browser [http://www.townofsalem.io/TownOfSalem/ here]. You can also join from Discord, however you still need an account. How to play Town of Salem on Discord: *Join a Voice Channel or DM *Press the 'Start an Activity' button *Search 'Town of Salem' *Click 'Town of Salem' to open & play *Newer to Discord Activities? Check out [https://discord.com/blog/server-activities-games-voice-watch-together Discord's blog on Discord Activities]. If you have bought the game from Steam, Steam is suggested because it is more stable and it's advertisement free. You can also buy [[Web Premium]] which will also get rid of ads and give you other bonuses too! Once in a while, an offer comes up for a very short amount of time. It offers many things for a very large discount, so it is highly encouraged to purchase it if you can. Even the {{A|Juggernaut}} {{A|Scroll}}, a {{A|Scroll}} that cannot be bought through the [[Points (ToS)|store]], is available in most of these packages! ([[Bundles (ToS)|Bundles]]) ==Main Menu - What it looks like== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" !Image !Description |- |[[File:Unity Play Button.png|center|thumb|105x51px]] |Here you can start a [[Game Modes (ToS)|new game]]. See [[#Starting a New Game (Lobby)|next section]] for more info! |- |[[File:Unity Settings.png|center|thumb|75px]] |{{A|Settings}}: Here you may view your friends, notifications, your ranked profile and [[Elo]]/Ranking, music/sound settings, or choose to log out of your account or close the game. |- |[[File:Unity Friends.png|center|thumb|75px]] |Here you can see your complete [[Friends (ToS)|friends]] list! You will see how many friends you have online and whether they are playing or not. You may add any friends with their IGN in the upper-right corner or select any friends you have to send them a message. |- |[[File:Unity Notifications.png|center|thumb|75px]] |Here you will see whether or not you have any friend requests or game invitations. |- |[[File:Unity Sound Effects.png|center|thumb|75px]] |Here you may choose to mute the in-game sound effects. |- |[[File:Unity Music Icon.png|center|thumb|75px]] |Here you may choose to mute the in-game music. |- |[[File:IconDefault.png|alt=|center|thumb|100x100px]] |[[Customization Options]]: Here you can change your [[Avatars (ToS)|avatar]], [[Pets (ToS)|pet]], [[Houses (ToS)|house]], [[Maps (ToS)|map]], [[Death Animations (ToS)|death animation]], [[Icon|Lobby icon]], and equip {{A|Scrolls}}. {{A|Scrolls}} increase your chances of getting a role, and everything else is cosmetic. |- | File:Unity Daily Brew.png File:Cauldron Gif.gif | |{{A|Daily Brew}}: Here you can earn prizes every 7 {{A|Days}} you log in, such as {{V|avatars}}, [[taunts]], {{A|Scrolls}} and more! |- |[[File:Shop_Transparent.png|center|thumb|100px]] |Shop: Here you can buy custom [[Avatars (ToS)|avatars]], {{V|houses}}, {{V|pets}}, {{A|Scrolls}}, and more with {{A|Merit Points}}, which you can earn by playing and finishing games. You can also spend {{A|Town Points}}, which is an exclusive currency used to buy certain special items only obtainable by purchasing them directly, by purchasing bundles with real currency, or rarely from {{A|Daily Brew}}. |- |[[File:Friend Referrals Icon No Background.png|alt=|center|thumb|100x100px]] |Here you may view your total used and unused referral codes that you may give out to your friends to allow them to play 5 free games. You may also purchase {{A|Scrolls}}, [[taunts]], name changes, and other premium bonuses here. |- |[[File:Achievements-Transparent.png|center|thumb|100px]] |{{A|Achievements}}: Here you can see a list of {{A|achievements}} you can earn in-game. Each one is worth {{A|Merit Points}} which you can use in the Shop to buy items you can use in the game! |- |[[File:Statistics_Transparent.png|center|thumb|101x101px]] |Here you can view your statistics for certain actions for every [[role]]! You can view how many people you shot as a {{A|Veteran}}, how many times you died to a {{A|Serial Killer}} as an {{A|Tavern Keeper}} or {{A|Bootlegger}}, and much more! |} ==Starting a New Game (Lobby)== [[File:Unity Custom List.png|left|thumb|307x307px|A [[Custom Setups (Classic)|Custom Setup]] in the [[Custom Mode|Custom]] game mode.]] You can either: *Choose a [[Game Modes (ToS)|game mode]] and press "Play Solo" or *Press "Create a Party", and you will then enter a lobby and be able to {{V|chat}} with the other players; their usernames will be listed on the top left. ([[Friends (ToS)#Parties|invite some friends]]) You then choose a [[Game Modes (ToS)|game mode]] from the upper right corner and then press "Start" to join a lobby for that gamemode with your friends. If you chose [[Custom Mode]], the first person to join the lobby will be the [[Host]] (it could even be you). The host sets up the game for everyone by choosing which [[Roles (ToS)|Roles]] should be in the game. There is a big list of Custom Setups in this wiki! ([[Custom Setups (Classic)|Classic Setups]], [[Custom Setups (Coven)|Coven Expansion Setups]]) During your first few games, It's recommended to play on the game mode [[Game Modes (ToS)#Classic_Mode|Classic]] because it is a gamemode made for beginners. After you think you got a handle on that, you can then move on to other modes such as [[Game Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom]], [[Game Modes (ToS)#Dracula's_Palace|Dracula's Palace]], [[Game Modes (ToS)#Rainbow_Mode|Rainbow]] and [[Game Modes (ToS)#All_Any]]. However, it's also recommended that you play [[Game Modes (ToS)#Custom_Mode|Custom]] so you can learn all the roles. After you have gotten the hang of the game you can try out [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked_Practice|Ranked Practice]]. It is a gamemode used by players to either play in a balanced and more competitive environment or warm up for [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]]. After 50 games, where 10 of which are [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked_Practice|Ranked Practice]], you get to play [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]], and by now, you will have known about most of the roles, so have fun! ==Before the Game== You can pick your [[name]]. It can be different for each game and doesn't have to be the same as your login name. Even your name can matter in Town of Salem! (See the [[Strategies]] page for more.) You can set a default name in your [[Customization Options|customization options]]. You can see other players and their names when they "join the {{A|Town}}." (e.g.: Deodat Lawson has joined the {{A|Town}}.) After you picked your name, you will randomly receive a [[role]]. If you own any {{A|Scrolls}} and have them equipped, you chances of getting that/those role(s) are increase by tenfold! However, it is not guaranteed that you will get that role. (Note: {{A|Scrolls}} do not work in [[Game Modes (ToS)#Ranked|Ranked]]. This is to ensure that no one can get any possible advantages.) ==During the Game== You will see a short description of your [[role]] on the top right of the screen. Some roles are more complex than others; you can read up on mechanics and strategies for your role on the wiki! You will also see your role's role card from the beginning of the game. It will also cover the mechanics of the role and its goals. You can also turn on Tips, which is a function where the game gives you tips on how to play your role properly. (Also see [[Tips and Tricks]] for some more info) Every game lasts several in-game {{A|Days}} which have several [[phases]]. *During the {{A|Day}}, you can {{V|chat}} with the other players, vote for a player to be [[hanging (ToS)|hanged]], or even use your [[Day Ability]] if you have one. *During the {{A|night}}, you can use your [[Night Ability]] if you have one. Factional roles besides {{A|Town}}, as well as the {{A|Jailor}} and {{A|Mediums}} can chat with other player(s) at {{A|night}}! When you [[Death (state)|die]], that does not always mean you lose! You should check the goal and [[Victory (ToS)|Victory]] conditions of your role before you leave. If your win conditions have not been met and you are a member of a faction (not a {{A|Neutral}} role), there is still a chance that your [[Factions (ToS)|faction]] could win. To [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to a certain player privately, type /w ''or'' /whisper ''or'' /pm (player's name or number), or click the number of the player you want to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] to and click the "Whisper" icon. This will paste this command where you may type. *In a game with players that have similar names, make sure you type exactly the name of the player you want to [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whisper]] and not another player. *These can be seen by {{A|Blackmailers}} though, so be careful. (See [[Strategies]] page for more) *Revealed {{A|Mayors}} cannot send or receive [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]]. ===On the Screen=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" !Image !Description |- |[[File:Last Will Button - Unity.png|alt=|center|thumb|69x69px]] |Edit or save changes to your {{A|Last Will}}. Your {{A|Last Will}} will be revealed to everyone when you die, unless you are {{A|Cleaned}} by a {{A|Janitor}} or {{A|Stoned}} by a {{A|Medusa}}. Additionally, a {{A|Forger}} may modify your {{A|Last Will}}, or a {{A|Serial Killer}} may bloodify your {{A|Last Will}} (if you are a [[Role block|role blocking]] role). All players have a {{A|Last Will}}. |- |[[File:Death Note Button - Unity.png|alt=|center|thumb|69x69px]] |Edit or save changes to your {{A|Death Note}}. Your {{A|Death Note}} will be revealed to everyone when the player you attacked dies. This button is only available if you are a {{A|Mafia Killing}}, {{A|Neutral Killing}}, any member of the {{A|Coven}}, a {{A|Pirate}}, or the {{A|Jailor}}. Note that the {{A|Jailor}} has a different {{A|Death Note}} layout, where you can only choose between 6 options! |- |[[File:Notes Button.png|alt=|center|thumb|69x69px]] |Edit or save changes to your {{A|Notes}}. Your {{A|Notes}} will never be revealed and can only be seen by you. It is like your own personal diary - keep track of who claimed what, who you think is suspicious, and anything else that might come in handy! All players have {{A|Notes}}. |- |[[File:Chat Log Button - Unity.png|alt=|center|thumb|69x69px]] |Open the message log. This log, in which you can scroll up or down, displays all in-game chat and messages, starting from "Choosing Names" all the way till the end of the game. If you die, this will also show dead messages since when you died. You can also filter the message log so you can highlight messages sent by a certain player, or even show messages ''only'' from that player! |- |[[File:Victory Conditions - Unity.png|alt=|center|thumb|69x69px]] |Check your {{V|Victory}} conditions. For example, if you are a {{A|Doctor}}, you win with the {{A|Town}} and {{A|Survivors}}, must kill the {{A|Mafia}}, {{A|Vampires}}, {{A|Arsonists}}, {{A|Serial Killers}}, {{A|Werewolves}}, {{A|Witches}}, {{A|Coven}}, {{A|Plaguebearers}}, {{A|Pestilence}}, and {{A|Juggernauts}}, and may spare anyone else. |- |[[File:MinimizeButton.png|alt=|center|thumb|71x71px]] |Minimize a tab ([[Graveyard]], Role List, or Role Card). |} ===Player window=== The player window appears on the lower right corner of your screen, besides player names. Whether a button appears depends on your [[role]] and the current [[Phases|phase]]. {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |- |[[File:Vote Player - Unity.png]][[File:Cancel Vote Player - Unity.png]] |During the [[Phases#Voting|Voting]] phase, vote or cancel your vote for a living player to be put on trial. You cannot vote for yourself. You also cannot vote for a player that is currently protected by a {{A|Guardian Angel}}. |- |[[File:Whisper Player - Unity.png]] |[[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|Whisper]] a player to send them a message that only you and the whispered player will see. Typing "/w", "/whisper", or "/pm" in the chat will work too. {{A|Blackmailers}} will be able to read [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispers]] too. Everyone else will see it as "Player 1 is whispering to Player 2.", unless you are playing in [[Lovers Mode]], where Lovers [[Chat (ToS)#Whispering|whispering]] eachother is completely hidden. |- |[[File:Taunt Player - Unity.png]] |[[Taunts|Taunt]] a player to make people laugh. [[Taunts]] are cosmetic items and do not affect gameplay. If a dead player uses a [[Taunts|taunt]], only other dead players and the taunted target will see the [[Taunts|taunt]]. |- |[[File:Ignore Player - Unity.png]][[File:Unignore Player - Unity.png]] |[[Chat (ToS)#Ignoring_a_player|Ignore]] a player to stop seeing their messages. Typing "/ignore" and the alternative "/unignore" in the chat will work too. It is recommended to [[Chat (ToS)#Ignoring_a_player|ignore]] a player if they are spamming. |- |[[File:Report Player - Unity.png]] |Report a player for rule-breaking behavior. See [[Town of Salem Rules|this page]] for more info. |- |[[File:Last Will Player - Unity.png]][[File:No Last Will Player - Unity.png]] |Read a dead player's {{A|Last Will}}. |- |[[File:Death Note Player - Unity.png]] |Read a dead player's {{A|Death Note}}. |- |[[File:Guard Player - Unity.png]] |During the {{A|night}}, use your [[Abilities (ToS)#Night_Abilities|night ability]] on a certain player. The targets you can choose depends on your [[role]]. The {{A|Transporter}}, {{A|Retributionist}}, {{A|Disguiser}}, {{A|Witch}}, {{A|Coven Leader}}, and {{A|Necromancer}} need to select two targets. This button won't display if you have no {{A|night}} ability, or you cannot use your ability on that {{A|night}} (e.g. {{A|Vigilante}} on {{A|night}} 1 or {{A|Werewolf}} on non-{{A|Full Moon}} {{A|night}}). The image is an example of the button a {{A|Bodyguard}} clicks in order to guard someone for the {{A|night}}. |} ==After the Game== When the game ends, you will see a [[Victory (ToS)|victory]] message. Anyone who hasn't left the game yet can now chat, dead or alive! When you decide to return to the lobby, you will see a screen showing you the usernames of everyone who played and their roles. Their username, in-game name, and role will be in a certain font color depending on their current status. {| class="article-table" border="0" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="1" style="font-style:inherit;font-weight:inherit;width:500px;" |- ! scope="col" |Color ! scope="col" |Description |- |'''White''' |The user is currently in the end-game lobby. |- |'''Grey''' |The user is still in the match. |- |'''Red''' |The user has left the end-game lobby and the match. |} Have fun! Slow Mode.title: Slow Mode
Slow Mode.wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Slow Mode}}}}
*The {{A|Slow Mode}} modifier doubles the amount of time players have for discussion and voting during the {{A|Day}}.
**{{A|Slow Mode}} does not affect the speed of the {{A|Night}} phase, with it being the same amount of time.
*No game modes currently use this modifier.
[[Category:Modifiers]]

Anomaly.title: Anomaly
Anomaly.wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:{{Amne|Anomaly}}}}
* The Anomaly modifier adds random Modifiers and Bans at the start of the game.
** {{A|Anon Players}}, {{A|No Scrolls}}, {{A|Perfect Town}}, and {{A|Slow Mode}} cannot be spawned from the {{A|Anomaly}} modifier.
* There will always be at least 1 Modifier and 1 Ban added.
* Each additional Modifier or Ban added is half as likely as the previous one.
[[Category:Modifiers]]
